2. ENGLISH 
 
You must use English in class: Do not use Korean or another language. 
You must try as best as you can to communicate all of your thoughts in English.  If you 
cannot find the correct words in English, try to find some other way to express yourself 
(description, body language, face expressions, drawing pictures, etc.).  Be creative.  
 
It is a requirement of this course that you use English in this class. 
 
 
 
3. PREPAREDNESS 
 
Be prepared for class. At a minimum, bring your notebook for note taking and file folder to 
every class. You are expected to read ahead any information, course material, pages, 
etc. your professor assigns to you. Being prepared includes by evidence of study outside 
of class; accessing and reviewing KULMS’s Announcements/Course Materials; being aware 
of due dates. 
 
One thing to get you through university is being organized and prepared for each class; 
hence the GF and file folder requirement. 
 
 
4. PARTICIPATION  
 
 Participate actively in the class.  Don’t be afraid to speak in class, and don’t worry 
about making mistakes.  
 
      It is important to remember mistakes do not matter to me at all, so please do your     
      best. 
 
 Incorrect speaking is better than no speaking. Perfect English is not necessary,  
but class participation is necessary.  It is a part of your grade.  
 
 Use your level of interest and motivation to create, expand and express your ideas, 
thoughts, feelings and questions. Even if you are not confident, you will have the chance 
to do well. Overtime, your confidence in speaking up in class will improve. 
 
 Use class time wisely and be prepared for each class.  
 
 Complete assignments thoroughly in a timely manner. 
 
Do not sleep in class. This will affect negatively on your participation grade. 
 
Involve yourself in every class activity; be positive and ready to learn and participate 
including asking questions. 
 
5. ASSIGNMENTS 
 
 Complete all assignments in a timely matter. Late assignments or projects will result in 
points deducted: 1 point for each day late including the weekends and holidays.  
 
 Copying assignments, homework or cheating on tests will automatically get you an “F/0". 
See also page 6. 
 
 Do not rehash and/or submit work (old or new) from another course/class. 
 
 
 If you are absent, make sure to contact me or ask your classmates about what you 
missed.   
 
 
 
 Submitted work must include a cover page, be paginated and include subtitles when 
necessary. Do not include the course material or lecture notes with your 
assignments. 
 
 As #4, use class time wisely and be prepared for each class and complete assignments 
thoroughly in a timely manner.

6. ABSENCES   
 
Come to class every day and on time and stay in class.  
 
 
If you are going to be absent from class for any reason, I will mark you as absent for that 
class, but I allow you 4 absences in the semester without any academic penalty.  
 
 If you will be absent for a special reason, and you wish to be excused from attending class, 
you must tell me before the class.  In addition, you can apply for an excused absence 
through the Korea University portal. It will still count as an absence, so use your free 
absences wisely.  
 
 
Just because you are absent for any reason does not absolve you of your responsibility. You 
are still responsible for content missed. 
 
 
Proper documentation must be provided for all special school-related absences: illness, 
death in the family or military. NOTE: a prescription is not valid documentation. 
 
Sleeping in class. This will affect negatively on your class attendance as well as your 
participation grade.  
 
Students missing 9 classes total will automatically receive a grade of “F”. 
 
See page 6 for more information. 
 
7. GRADES   
 
Although important to you and your GPA, learning a foreign language is not only about 
grades.  It is a skill that can be life changing for your future.  Developing good English 
language skills can open opportunities for employment and future study abroad, it can help 
you connect to the world beyond the borders of your country; and it can enhance your 
understanding of other cultures.  Please view this course as an opportunity to build your 
future, and not simply as an influence on your GPA.   
 
Furthermore, in Korea, English is often used as a measure of a person’s value in society, but 
NOT in this class.  It is a useful tool just as mathematics, critical thinking or creativity.   
The grades I assign to you are not an evaluation of you personally nor reflective of my likes 
or dislikes.  It is simply an evaluation of your performance in class tasks and activities.  
 
See page 7-8 for detailed assessments. 
 
8. TIME 
 
Be in class on time.  Students who are late are disturbing for the class and for me. Enter the 
class quietly. If you are more than 15 minutes late, I will mark you absent for that class.   
 
If you are late 3 times, I will mark you absent for one class. This will NOT count as one of 
the allowed absences in #6.

On most days, we will be using materials made available through KULMS.  Please make sure

Classrooms are sometimes arranged in rows. It is advisable to avoid sitting in the back since 
you might miss important information; it can be a sign you are shy but also a sign you’re 
trying to avoid participation or you’re not focusing or you’re disinterested in the class. 
Therefore, sit in the front or close to the front of the class. Choose a seat for a few 
weeks, so I can remember who you are including your name.  
 
Depending on the assignment, new seating arrangements maybe created.

Please use the break time BETWEEN CLASSES for getting drinks, making phone calls and 
going to the washroom.  If it is an emergency, you don’t have to ask me for permission to go 
to the washroom.  If it is not an emergency, you do not have to go. 
 
 
13. MANNERS MAKETH THE PERSON 
 
Show respect and courtesy to EVERYONE in the class.  Acknowledge people with a 
simple hi or hello, or good morning/afternoon or a nod. (Basic Communication)  
 
Please be respectful of your classmates and help me to provide a positive and encouraging 
learning environment.   
 
Use of offensive language will not be tolerated (English, Korean, etc.).  
 
Your enjoyment of this class and the development of your academic English skills depend on 
the attitude you bring to this class every day.  Please be positive, be polite and be kind. 
 
 
 
Speaking English isn’t only about fluency. It’s about being in class, doing the work, understanding, 
and following instructions and making an effort. 
 
 
 
KU’S AI POLICY 
 
 
The use of generative AI in class without basic guidelines. It may negatively impact the quality of teaching and 
learning. Common negative impacts include: 
 
(1) Violations of academic integrity, such as plagiarism and cheating. 
(2) Decline in critical thinking, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills due  
     to over-reliance on generative AI. 
(3) Acquisition of inaccurate or biased information. 
(4) Reinforcement of entrenched stereotypes.

Evaluation Method 
 
Typically, a maximum of about 40-45% of you will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”. Evaluation in this class is 
based strictly on performance, and not on English language proficiency. All parts of the evaluation system 
must be completed in an exceptional manner (above and beyond) if you want to get an “A+”.   
 
I employ rubrics where students are evaluated on organization (see below), content (see below) and 
language (see below). More criteria will be given when the projects are assigned. Many students ask for a 
word count for written assignments. My philosophy is that students should be focusing on answering the 
question and providing enough support for their answer. So concentrate on fully exploring your answer.  
This is done through research (what have others said on the topic); planning (brainstorming and outline and 
deciding on your answer), and editing (checking your work for mistakes in organization, content and 
language).

▷ 강의 개요
1. 초급한문에서 이어진 교양 한문 강좌로, 여러 문체의 한문 문장을 해독함으로써 한문 문리를 터득하
는 데 필요한 능력을 기르도록 한다. 
2. 한국과 중국의 역대 한문산문 중 문예적 가치가 높거나 문학사적 의의가 큰 작품을 선별하여 강독한
다. 이를 통해 한문산문의 구조와 특징, 문체와 내용을 알고, 변천 과정과 특징을 이해하며, 한문이라
는 중세 동아시아의 보편적 언어체계 속에 구현된 동양적 사유양상과 문예의식을 파악할 수 있다.
3. 실생활 속 한자 및 한문 관련 상식의 증진함으로써 우리말과 우리 문학에 대한 이해를 더욱 깊게 합
니다.
※ 수강생들이 ‘한문 초학자’라고 생각하고 기본 한자도 익히며 한문 수업을 진행하겠습니다.

  * 출석 15점, 쪽지시험 10점, 과제 10점, 발표 20점, 중간고사 20점, 기말고사 25점.

∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서 위치를 작가하며 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과 약속한 사항을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생들의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 학문적 지식탐구 및 미래 비전과 연결된 교과목 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 미리 교육자료 탐독하고 확인
 -정해진 수업시간에 결석, 지각, 중도 이탈 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -적극적으로 토론, 질의응답 등 수업활동에 참여
 -스스로 성실하게 작성한 과제를 제출하고 인용한 모든 자료는 변조, 왜곡 없이 표시

∙ [실험실습 안전]
 -연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분야 대상학과에 
소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 
학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수
 -신규교육(신입생 2시간), 정기교육(고위험학과 학기별 6시간, 저위험학과 학기별 3시간)
 -대상학과(부): KUPID > 지식관리 > 안전관리지식 > 연구실안전
 -포탈시스템 상단 메뉴에서 “정보생활” 클린, [안전교육(서울)] 클릭하여 안전교육 페이지 접속 (“크롬”으로 접속, 접
속 오류 시 인터넷 설정에서 “팝업 차단 해제” 설정 필요)
 -포탈 아이디가 없는 경우, 국가연구안전관리본부 연구실안전교육시스템(https://edu.labs.go.kr/) 접속하여 수강 가
능함.
 -외부기관에서 안전교육을 이수한 경우 별도의 등록절차를 통한 이수 가능
 -미이수 시 불이익: 학부생(성적열람 제한), 대학원생(출입제한)
 -문의사항: 교육문의(안전관리팀 02-3290-2763), 시스템문의(아키시스템즈 02-2664-5354)

하고 있으며 매학년도 1회 이상(학부생의 경우 총 4회 이상 이수필수)
 -수강방법 : 블랙보드(https://kulms.korea.ac.kr)에 로그인하여 수강(블랙보드 로그인 → 상단 '안내페이지' → 오른쪽

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

BUSS236: ESG 경영      
 
담당교수 
 
이재혁 (LP 617, jayrhee@korea.ac.kr) 
강의시간 
 
수요일 3:00-5:45 pm 
 
과목개요 
본 과목은 ESG 경영에 대한 이해를 바탕으로 기업의 지속 가능성을 유지/확보할 수 있는 방안에 
대해서 논의하는 것을 주요 목적으로 합니다. 기업이 수립하고 실행하는 수많은 전략의 궁극적인 
목적은 경쟁력 확보를 통한 지속가능성 증진입니다. 각종 경영환경의 변화가 초래하는 경쟁 
심화로 인해 기업의 지속가능성에 대한 우려가 높아지고 있습니다. 재무적 성과가 초라한 기업의 
지속가능성은 결코 높을 수 없습니다. 하지만 재무적 성과가 아무리 탁월해도 환경(E), 사회(S), 
지배구조(G)로 대변되는 비재무적 성과가 낮은 기업 역시 지속가능성이 높을 수는 없습니다. 이윤 
창출 과정에서 절차적 공정성과 사회적 정당성을 준수하지 않은 기업은 이해관계자들과 장기적인 
공생이 불가능하기 때문입니다. 본 과목의 주요 목적은 ESG
와 관련된 이론 및 개념, 
ESG 평가방법의 특징 및 한계, ESG 관련 최근 추세 및 대응방안과 관련된 다양한 사례 분석 등을 
통해 ESG 경영에 대해 체계적으로 학습하고 논의하는 것입니다.

시험 
이 수업에서 다루는 내용과 직간접 관련이 있는 주제나 사례에 대해서 에세이 형태, 혹은 사지선다 
형태의 시험이 실시됩니다.  
 
 
수업 참여 
 
 
모든 수업에서 진행되는 각종 토론에 대해 논리성, 직관성, 창의성 등을 기본으로 수업 참여도가 
평가됩니다.  
 
 
 
조별 프로젝트  
이 수업에서 논의된 내용을 토대로 지속가능성 증진을 위한 ESG 경영의 구체적 실천방안 도출을 
주요 목적으로 합니다. 특정기업을 선정하여 해당 기업의 비즈니스모델, 경영환경 등을 분석하여 
(1) 현재 직면하고 있거나 향후에 직면할 수 있는 ESG 관련 주요 문제점들을 파악, (2) 동일/유사 
산업에서 경쟁하고 있는 타기업의 베스트 프랙티스와 비교 분석, (3) 향후에 해당기업이 수립하고 
실행해야 하는 ESG 경영의 구체적 실천방안을 제시합니다. 이를 위해 해당기업들이 발간하는 
지속가능경영보고서 뿐만 아니라 해당기업들의 재무적/비재무적 성과, 해당기업들에 대한 
ESG 평가결과 등 객관적인 사실에 근거하여 체계적이고 통합적인 분석을 실시합니다.

GMES206 
Entertianment Effect 
 
 
Instructor: Prof. Sangwon Lee  
Office: Room 1204, Media Hall 
Email: leesangwon@korea.ac.kr 
Class Hours: Tue & Thu, 10:30 – 11:45 AM 
Office Hours: Tue & Thu, 3:00 – 4:00 PM (Walk-ins welcome). Other times are available by 
appointment via email. 
Teaching Assistant: Youngjin Lee, M.A. student (youngjinl00@korea.ac.kr) 
 
Course Description and Objectives 
This course theoretically explores the psychology of play and enjoyment manifested through 
various entertainment-based media—including dramas, films, variety shows, political 
entertainment, and social networking services. The primary goal is to understand the underlying 
mechanisms of media enjoyment through empirical research. 
The curriculum focuses on analyzing media user responses through key concepts of 
entertainment psychology, such as empathy, immersion, identification, narrative comprehension, 
and affective disposition. Rooted in psychological perspectives, this course applies traditional 
media effects theories to the context of entertainment content and provides an in-depth 
examination of the psychological influence of entertainment in the contemporary media 
environment. 
Learning Goals 
Understand the core concepts of entertainment psychology and apply them to various 
entertainment media contexts. 
Critically and deeply analyze the psychological responses and effects of media users, with a 
focus on dramas, variety shows, political entertainment, and SNS. 
Course Materials 
No required textbook. All necessary learning materials, including lecture slides and 
supplementary readings, will be provided by the instructor. Students are expected to fully 
understand the concepts covered in the lectures. 
Course Structure 
50% Lecture / 50% Group Discussion. The course meets twice a week. One session focuses on 
theoretical lectures, while the other is dedicated to discussions and activities that apply the 
concepts covered in class. 
Exams. The midterm and final exams will consist of multiple-choice questions designed to 
evaluate your understanding of the concepts covered in lectures and course materials. Specific 
details regarding the exam format will be provided prior to each exam, and a review session will 
be conducted beforehand to assist with your preparation. 
Attendance. Attendance is crucial for your learning, but flexibility is provided for personal needs. 
• 
Free Absences (Max 4): You may miss up to 4 classes for any reason (illness, 
menstruation leave, rest, etc.). These are "no-penalty" absences to use at your discretion. 
•

Classroom Digital Device Policy: No-Tech Mode 
Principle: In principle, the use of all digital devices (laptops, tablets, smartphones) is restricted.

This policy is designed as an intentional break from our screens. The goal is simple: to practice 
stepping away from digital distractions and to train ourselves to be fully present and focused 
during class.

printing costs, I recommend printing 4 or 6 slides per page. The slides will be uploaded to the

same assignment without permission), and facilitating misconduct (assisting another student’s 
academic dishonesty). Unauthorized use of materials or devices during exams or assignments, 
falsifying attendance or submissions, and proxy attendance are also considered academic 
misconduct. All forms of academic misconduct are strictly prohibited. Any student found in 
violation may receive an F for the assignment or for the course.

analysis, or original thinking required for the assignment.

- Unauthorized use of AI or use that undermines academic integrity (e.g., plagiarism, fabrication 
of information) will be treated as a violation of academic ethics. In particular, AI-generated text 
frequently contains non-existent or inaccurate information (so-called “hallucinations”).

수업 개요 
의복 구성의 기본이 되는 평면 패턴 제도를 통해 옷의 구성 원리와 구조를 익히는 기초과정으로서 스커트와 블라
우스의 변형 및 재구성을 통해 기본적인 아이템을 패턴으로 만들고 봉제하여 제작할 수 있는 능력을 습득한다. 
 
 
수업 목표 
1. 여성의 인체와 패턴의 연관성을 이해하여 패턴메이킹의 기본 구조를 이해한다. 
2.  Bodices, 블라우스, 소매, 스커트의 기본 패턴을 제작하고 이를 활용하여 다양한 디자인의 의상을 위해 패턴 응 
용력을 기른다. 
3. 표현하고자 하는 패션디자인을 실현화 할 수 있도록 패턴에 대한 기본지식과 응용력을 기른다.  
 
 
수업 원칙 
1. 출석: 모든 학생들은 정해진 시간에 출석하여야 하며 무단 결석 시에는 출석점수에서 10%씩 감점이 이루어 진
다. 3 번의 지각은 1 번의 결석과 동일하게 평가된다. 부득이하게 결석해야 할 경우에는 담당교수에게 미리 연
락을 취해야 한다. 긴급한 상황이 아닐 경우, 담당교수 의 허락 없이는 강의 도중에 나갈 수 없다. 출석 일수
의 1/3을 초과하여 결석한 경우 학점을 부여하지 않는다.  
2. 과제: 과제물은 반드시 주어진 날짜에 제출해야 하며, 늦게 제출하는 경우 과제에 부여된 점수에서 주당 10% 
씩 감점된다. 과제 제출 기한이 지난 과제물은 원칙적으로 받지 않으나, 부득이한 사정이 있을 경우 사전 허가
를 받아 늦게 제출 가능하다. 
3. 수업 유형: 대면 수업을 기본으로 하며, 오프라인 수업의 경우 마이크와 카메라가 있는 환경에서 온라인 수업을 
진행한다. 
4. Blackboard: 수강생들은 수업시간 전에 본 수업을 위해 설치된 사이트인 http://kulms.korea.ac.kr 에서 수업 관련 
공지와 자료를 확인하며, 게시된 강의 자료들을 인쇄 또는 저장하여 수업시간에 가져오도록 한다. 블랙 보드 
메뉴는 주로 다음의 용도로 사용된다: (1) 수업 관련 공지, (2) 강의 자료와 유인물, (3) 과제물 제출, (4) 토론실, 
(5) 온라인 강의 
5. 평가: 출석 및 태도(10%), 수시 과제(10%), 퀴즈(5%), 스커트(20%),  블라우스(20%), 개인 작품(35%)

study—who wish to advance their analytical and productive skills in English by applying grammar

helping them understand how English grammar is used in real-world contexts. Through various in-
class activities (individual, pair, and small group work), students will have opportunities to practice 
and apply their grammatical knowledge, improving both accuracy and fluency in English.

practical English communication.

-
Demonstrate proficiency in using a variety of grammatical structures with greater fluency.

Course Outline: Spring Semester 2026 <From Idea to Commercialization: Starting a 
Business with AI> 
Instructor: Andy Kim cyberzen@korea.ac.kr  (010-3497-3316)  
 
Course Overview: This course, "From Idea to Commercialization: Starting a Business with AI," teaches 
students how to utilize and innovate throughout the entire startup process using various generative AI tools 
such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Felo, as well as Agentic AI like Genspark, through practical cases 
and hands-on exercises. The instructor is a graduate of the Business School and an MBA scholarship graduate 
from Harvard Business School, who has served as an executive at leading global companies across 6 countries, 
including Samsung Electronics, IBM (USA), HTC (Taiwan), and Goertek Group (China). After that, he started 
his own business and currently operates a startup accelerator and business consulting service company as an 
active professional. Based on various success and investment failure cases, from early-stage investment in 
startups to directly taking companies public through corporate development, he aims to deliver practical 
knowledge and insights connected to the field. 
 
Course Objectives: This course aims to cultivate the ability to automate, enhance, and put into practice the 
startup process using generative AI and Agentic AI. In an era where the average lifespan is approaching 100 
years, entrepreneurship is no longer a matter of choice, but a matter of when and how to start a business. 
Even for students who have not decided on entrepreneurship as their career path, this course aims to help 
them internalize how entrepreneurship can be the best option as a means to achieve the economic freedom 
that everyone dreams of, through theory and case studies. As a startup accelerator, the course will share 
know-how and various techniques on how to nurture and invest in startups in actual practice, and provide 
practical solutions on how to reduce risks at all stages of entrepreneurship and execute more easily and 
quickly using more than 10 specialized AI solutions to overcome the vagueness and constraints of 
entrepreneurship itself. 
This course is designed for students who want to explore careers in the startup ecosystem, such as direct 
entrepreneurship, startup incubation, or venture capital, or who want to learn how small companies are created, 
survive, and grow, regardless of their future career path, and apply this knowledge to various fields. 
 
Grading: Attendance (10), Participation (20) + Midterm (30) + Final Team Project (40)

교과목 개요 
본 수업은 보건의료 정책 및 관리 분야에 관심 있는 학부생을 대상으로 하는 실습 중심 
교과목이다. 보건의료 분야는 공공정책, 병원경영, 제약·바이오, 건강보험, 디지털 헬스 
등 다양한 영역으로 빠르게 확장되고 있으나, 학생들이 실제 현장을 경험할 기회는 
제한적이다. 이로 인해 전공 지식을 진로와 충분히 연결하지 못하거나, 자신의 역량을 
어떤 분야에 어떻게 활용할지 탐색하기 어려운 경우가 발생한다. 이러한 간극을 
줄이고자 진로 설계·구체화와 실무 역량 개발을 핵심 목표로 삼는다.  
 
수업에서는 보건의료 관련 주요 기관·기업을 직접 방문하여 현장 중심 학습을 진행한다. 
기관/기업별로 세부 프로그램은 달라질 수 있으나, 일반적으로  
 
• 
실무 전문가의 약 1시간 강연을 통해 조직과 산업 전반에 대한 이해를 높이고  
• 
약 1시간 동안 실제 업무 프로세스와 실무 환경을 소개받으며  
• 
최근 입사자 또는 현업 종사자와의 질의응답을 통해 채용 과정, 요구 역량, 진로 
설계 등에 대해 논의하는 시간을 갖는다.  
 
이를 통해 학생들은 보건의료 분야의 실제 업무 구조와 직무별 역할을 보다 명확히 
이해하고, 자신의 전공 지식을 현실의 맥락 속에서 어떻게 활용할 수 있는지 체감하게 
된다. 궁극적으로 본 수업은 학생들이 보다 구체적인 진로 계획을 수립하고, 보건의료 
분야에서 요구되는 역량을 능동적으로 개발할 수 있도록 돕는 것을 목표로 한다.

개요
이 강의는 외국인 학부생을 대상으로 하는 <한국어고급> 강의로, 고급 수
준의 한국어를 익혀 전문적이고 추상적인 주제에 대해 정확하고 유창하게 
의사소통하는 것을 목표로 한다. 사회적 맥락에서의 과제 및 학업 활동을 
수행하는 데 필요한 의사소통 기능을 학습하고 정치, 경제, 과학, 역사와 
같은 다양한 학문 분야에 대한 지식을 공유한다. 한국어를 매개로 문화의 
다양성과 특수성을 이해하며 세상을 바라보는 시각을 넓히고 유연한 사고
를 함양한다.

선이수과목(권장)
수업운영원칙
1. 수강생은 강의에 적극적으로 참여해야 하며, 강의 내용을 이해하기 위
하여 예습과 복습을 해야 한다.  
2. 수강생은 Padlet을 통하여 강의 중 학습한 문법에 대하여 교수자의 일
대일 피드백을 받을 수 있으므로 문장 만들기 과제를 성실히 해야 한
다. 
3. 본 강의는 수강생의 한국어 능력 향상을 위한 강의이므로 발표 및 조
별활동에 반드시 적극적으로 참여해야 한다.
4. 표절 및 부정 행위 가능성을 방지하고, 평가의 공정성을 확보하기 위해 
ChatGPT를 활용한 과제 수행을 제한한다.
5. 시험은 오프라인 대면 시험으로 실시된다.
6. 형성평가(퀴즈)는 학기 중 총 3회 치른다.

Hakjoo Oh

Basic Information
• Instructor: Hakjoo Oh
– Position: Professor in Computer Science and Engineering, Korea University
– Expertise: Programming Languages, Software Engineering, Software Security
– Email: hakjoo oh@korea.ac.kr
Course overview
Compilers are software systems that bridge the gap between humans and
machines by translating programs written in a high-level programming language into a low-level
language. The goal of this course is to learn principles, techniques, and tools for compiler con-
struction. Topics include:
• Lexical analysis: lexical tokens, regular expressions, finite automata, lexical analyzer gen-
erators
• Syntax analysis: context-free grammars, top-down parsing, bottom-up parsing, parser gen-
erators
• Translation: syntax-directed translation, three address code, control flow graph, basic
blocks
• Semantic analysis: static analysis, abstract interpretation, verification, type-checking,
data-flow analysis, optimization
• Code generation: register allocation and assignments, instruction selection, machine code
generation
Course materials:
• Self-contained slides will be provided.
• Recommended Books:
– Alfred V. Aho, Monica S. Lam, Ravi Sethi, and Jeffrey D. Ullman. Compilers: Princi-
ples, Techniques, and Tools (2nd Edition).
– Andrew W. Appel. Modern Compiler Implementation in ML.

COURSE OUTLINE  
This course aims to provide a substantive overview to the technology, applications, and 
the management of IT/IS in organizations with special emphases on the strategic role and 
implications of IT and electronic business. The course is designed to provide the necessary 
frameworks, concepts and principles to guide you to understand and to effectively address 
the issues pertaining to the vast and fast growing field of IT/IS in the context of an enterprise 
and business webs.  
More specifically, the purpose of this course is three-fold: First, to introduce the concept 
and role of IT/IS in organizations; Second, to provide recent hot issues related to IT/IS; 
Finally, to develop the top-notch communication skills (both written and oral) through 
intensive rounds of writes-ups, presentation, and discussion.  
After understanding the role of IT/IS in organizations, course participants should be 
able to 1) explain how to develop and manage IT/IS; 2) appreciate the needed technologies in your 
organization; and 3) understand and discuss recent issues related to the management of information as 
corporate resources. Furthermore, through the real world case studies, you will learn how to 
deal with the specific managerial problems you may encounter in your real IT/IS 
environment. It is the premise of this course that understanding how IT/IS may be 
harnessed to create and deliver value is an essential and notable competency for twenty-first 
century managers. 
 
TEACHING APPROACH  
Appropriate lectures, readings, case studies, discussion and debate for sharing the 
knowledge and experiences of the using and managing IT/IS are required for supporting 
respective topics. Emphasis will be placed on ensuring a participative and interactive approach 
during the semester.

COURSE POLICIES 
 
· 
Course Type 
This course will be a full offline mode. 
 
· 
Copyright Law 
Materials and lectures in this course are strongly protected by Copyright Law. Materials are presented 
in an educational context for personal use and study and should not be shared, distributed, or sold in 
print - or digitally - outside the course without permission. Electronic video and/or audio recording 
is not permitted during class unless the student obtains permission from the instructor. If permission 
is granted, any distribution of the recording is prohibited. 
 
· 
Anti-graft Law 
Do not ask the instructor to change the grade unless there is a flaw in grading. Improper solicitation 
and graft for any matters are strictly prohibited by Anti-graft Law. 
 
· 
Attendance Policy 
Do not miss the class more than three times! If you have any justifiable reason to miss a class such 
as emergencies (e.g., job interview, funeral, etc.), please report at least before the class by email or by 
phone, and get the formal allowance from the instructor to minimize the deduction of your points. 
The allowed one will not be counted as absence, but as being late.  
 
· 
Expectations about preparation for class 
You are expected to come prepared to class. Preparation for a class involves downloading, reading, 
and working on the teaching material indicated in the schedule. You are strongly expected to access 
the course website for downloading and reviewing the material, which will be uploaded a few days 
before each session.  
 
· 
Peer Evaluation 
In order to exactly evaluate the degree of contribution made by team members within a team, the 
peer evaluation system will be adopted. At the end of the semester, the peer evaluation form will be 
distributed to all students. Each student should fill in the form and return it to the instructor when it 
is due. 
 
· 
Presentation Guidelines 
All teams will present two times throughout the semester. Each team member has to get involved in 
presentation at least more than one time without exception. In addition, it is not allowed to simply read 
written script for presentation. All presentation should be done in the professional manner. 
 
· 
Participation and Feedback 
This course strongly pursues a two-way communication mode between instructor and students as 
well as between students. Therefore, your strong participation is required not only to get a better 
score but also to share each other’s knowledge and experience in class. 
In terms of feedback, it is hoped that the communication process will indeed be two directional. 
Feedback is to reflect not only how well class objectives are being met, the effectiveness of the 
instructional facilitation, and the extent to which individual needs are being fulfilled, but also the 
quality of student contribution and involvement. Consequently, your oral and written feedback 
relative to questions or concerns you have, more information you need, and any evaluation you have 
of process, content, or the instructor are welcome at any time. In addition, the instructor is willing to 
provide evaluative feedback in the way of comments, advice, and resource suggestions in response to 
any submitted materials. 
 
· 
Academic Dishonesty Policy 
Dishonest academic behaviors are subject to punishment under the Undergraduate Program 
Handbook at Korea University Business School.

COURSE DESCRIPTION 
 
This course intends to introduce you to qualitative methods in sociological research. Throughout 
the semester, you will learn various qualitative methods, including in-depth personal interview, 
focus group interview, content analysis, etc. You will learn how to design, collect and analyze 
your own qualitative data of your interest in the area of sociology.  
 
 
COURSE OBJECTIVES 
 
After taking this class, students are expected to be able to: 
1. Understand and describe the characteristics of different qualitative methods 
2. Collect, interpret, analyze qualitative data  
3. Write an academic paper with qualitative research method

Textbook: Flick, U. (Ed.). (2013). The SAGE handbook of qualitative data analysis. Sage. 
Reading: There could be assigned readings (journal articles) each week. You can find the 
assigned readings via the KU library website.

meet you to discuss your progress or to clarify course assignments or requirements. Please come 
to my office hours or make an appointment.

▷ 과목개요 
 
 
This class offers lectures, presentations, and interactive mentoring sessions on Korean history and culture for 
foreign students without a Korean educational  background.  Specifically  for the Spring 2026 semester, the 
Visiting  Professor  places  a special  emphasis  on "communication"  and "mentorship."  Beyond  simple 
knowledge  transmission,  the course  is designed  to foster  a close  intellectual  relationship  between  the 
instructor and students.
(Spring 2026)
 
 
 
 
During the first half of the semester, emphasis will be given to Korean culture and how it relates to Korean 
identity  and “Korean- ness.” In the second  half, the course  will cover major periods  in Korean  history  in 
chronological order. Instead of focusing on Korea as a ‘single nation with a distinct history,’ the course will 
take a civilizational approach with attention paid to the position of Korea in the context of regional and world 
history. Through active discussion and mentoring, students will learn to view Korean history and culture as 
products  of interaction  with the rest of the world.  Major  events,  such as wars,  will be analyzed  in their 
geopolitical context, and lectures will attempt to eschew stereotypes through critical dialogue.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
▷ 학습목표 
이 강의는 한국에서의 교육 경험이 없는 학생들을 대상으로 하며, 2026학년도 1학기에는 특별히 초
빙교수(Visiting Professor)와의 '소통'과 '멘토링'을 강화하여 운영된다. 단순한 지식의 전달자로서의 
교수가 아닌, 학생들이 한국 사회와 문화를 이해하는 과정을 돕는 멘토로서의 역할을 수행하며, 강
의실 안팎에서의 활발한 상호작용을 통해 수업을 진행한다.
이 강의는 단순히 '일국사'로서의 한국학을 다루기보다는 문명학적인 관점을 택하여, 한국사를 동아
시아 지역사와 세계사의 맥락 속에서 다룰 것이다. 한국사 역시 세계사의 일부분이며 세계와 단절된 
것이 아니라 세계 속에서 발전하여 온 것이기 때문이다. 학생들은 교수와의 지속적인 문답과 멘토링
을 통해 이러한 거시적 관점을 자신의 것으로 소화하게 된다.
초반 강의에서는 정체성과 문화성 상징이라는 테마를 중심으로 문화적 정체성 형성에 대한 이론을 
강의하고, 한국학을 배우는 데 필요한 역사·정치 이론과 문화이론 전반을 소개한다. 이 강의에서는 ‘
문화’를 베네딕트 앤더슨의 ‘상상의 공동체’, 그리고 새뮤얼 헌팅턴이 사용하는 ‘문명’ 개념과 연계하
여 강의한다. 즉 상상의 공동체로서의 한국과 ‘문명’으로서의 한국을 구성하는 갖가지 상징(symbols
)들은 곧 한국문화를 구성하는 개별단위이기 때문이다. 따라서 각 강의마다 ‘테마’를 부여하여 각 시
대를 대표하는 개념을 설정하고 심도 있는 토론을 진행한다. 아울러 현재 세계 대중문화의 흐름을 
주도하고 있는 K-pop에 대한 강의를 통하여 한국 대중문화의 흐름을 파악하고 한국 현대사회와의 
관련성을 조명한다.
전반기 한국의 '기원'에 관한 강의에서는 역사기록은 물론 정치학, 고고학, 유전학, 민속학 등 인접 
학문의 이론과 학설을 적극 활용한다. 한반도와 인근 지역의 인간 집단 이동, 고고학적 유물들의 의
미, 고대인들의 유전학적 분석 등을 설명하고 또한 고대 한국인들에게 공동체적 정체성이 어떻게 형
성되었는지에 대하여 설명한다. 전쟁과 같은 중요사건(예: 고구려-수/당 전쟁, 몽골 침공, 임진왜란, 
병자호란, 일제 강점) 역시 '세계사 속의 한국'이라는 관점에서 설명이 될 것이며, 한국사가 아닌 세
계사적인 의미를 지니는 사건으로 자리매김될 것이다.
전쟁이나 정치적 격변 같은 사건들 못지않게 중요한 것은 그 사건들이 한국 역사 속에서 사회의 구
성에 미친 영향이다. 예를 들어 상인 집단이 건국한 고려와 성리학을 추종하는 신진사대부에 의하여 
건국된 조선 같은 경우, 그 상이(相異)함은 국가의 운영이나 사회 구성원들의 생활(경제적 활동, 남
녀관계 등)에 큰 영향을 미치며, 이를 자세히 들여다본다. 이러한 과정에서 상존하고 있는 (한국 관
련) 스테레오타입과 고정관념을 지양하고, 교수와의 멘토링을 통해 새로운 한국의 역사상(Historical 
Image)과 문화상(Cultural Image)을 정립하는 데 주력할 것이다.
 
Through this course, students are expected to achieve a comprehensive understanding of Korean history and 
culture.  The goal extends  beyond  the simple  transmission  of information;  we aim to provide  an array of 
diverse perspectives that encourage students to develop their own unique insights into Korea. In addition to 
interactive  in-class lectures, students will have the opportunity  to choose topics for weekly presentations, 
fostering active engagement. Furthermore, two scheduled excursions will complement the lectures, bridging 
theoretical  knowledge  with  actual,  out- of-class  experiences  to stimulate  greater  interest  and  deeper 
connection with the subject matter.

학기 전반부에는 한국 문화의 고유한 매력을 문명사적 관점에서 폭넓게 조망합니다. 특히 세계적으
로 주목받는 대중문화를 깊이 있게 들여다봄으로써, 전통과 현대가 어우러진 한국 사회를 더욱 생동
감 있게 이해할 수 있도록 이끌 것입니다. 후반부에는 고대부터 현대에 이르는 역사의 흐름을 따라
가되, 단순한 연대기적 나열은 지양합니다. 대신 각 시대의 사회적 변화를 이끈 결정적 사건들에 주
목하여, 역사의 소용돌이 속에서 한국인의 정체성이 어떻게 형성되고 변화해왔는지 여러분과 함께

또한, 이번 학기는 교실 밖에서의 생생한 경험과 소통을 특히 중요하게 생각합니다. 학기 중 예정된

불어 초빙교수와의 자유로운 멘토링과 토론 과정을 통해, 여러분이 타인의 관점을 답습하기보다 스
스로의 시선으로 한국을 해석하고 깊이 공감하는 의미 있는 시간을 만들어가기를 기대합니다.

  이 수업은 연결성(connectivity)의 관점에서 1990년대 이후 동아시아 국제관계의 전개
와 그 메커니즘을 이해하고 이를 적극적으로 활용하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 그동안의 연결
성에 대한 관심은 주로 경제 분야에 제한되어 왔다(예: 무역 및 투자, 인프라, 공급망 등). 
하지만 경제는 물론 정치·안보, 사회·문화 분야에서 한국, 중국, 일본을 비롯한 동아시아 
각국이 서로 어떻게 연결되어 있는지 종합적으로 바라봐야 할 필요가 있다.
  동아시아 국가 간 연결성을 상징적으로 보여주는 것이 국가 정상들이 합의한 ‘전략적 파
트너십(동반자관계)’이다. 각각의 전략적 파트너십은 다양한 라이프사이클(형성, 발전, 좌
절, 회복 등)을 보여준다. 동북아 국가 간 (전략적) 파트너십은 과거사 문제, 영토문제, 정
치적 대립, 미중 전략경쟁 등으로 정체와 후퇴를 거듭했다. 그에 반해 동북아-동남아 국가 
간 전략적 파트너십은 크나큰 발전을 이루었다.
  현재 동북아와 동남아를 포함한 동아시아는 하나의 정치·안보적 공간으로도 변모하고 있
다. 20~30년 후 우리는 유럽연합(EU)과 유사한 동아시아연합(EAU)에 살고 있을지도 모른
다. 갈등과 대립이 완전히 없어지지는 않겠지만 그럼에도 경제통합, 사회제도, 정치체제, 
문화코드, 가치·규범을 공유하는 공간의 출현에 대비해야 할 것이다. 서로 접촉하는 가운
데 새로운 양식이 만들어지는 ‘접변’의 시대이다.

면담시간: 강의 직후 및 이메일을 통해 수시면담
 
과목개요:
본 강좌는 서양문화와 역사에 대한 교양 차원의 이해를 돕는 것을 목표로 한다. 서양, 특히 
유럽 고유의 문화적 규범과 특징은 근대보다 전근대에 그 깊은 뿌리를 두고 있다. 본 강좌는 
절대왕정기까지를 대상으로 하되, 촘촘한 개설 지식의 전수보다 학생들이 향후 서양 근현대사
에까지 관심을 확대해갈 수 있는 동기부여와 서양사에 대한 기본적인 이해를 제공하는 데 목
표를 둔다. 방법론적으로는 역사적 사건 위주의 통사적 접근을 지양하고 그림, 건축, 문학작
품, 음악 등 문화적 재현을 하나의 입구로 삼아 서양사의 주요 이슈에 접근한다. 이를 통해 
AI 시대의 중요한 화두가 된 서양문화에 대한 이해를 도모함과 아울러 문화적 재현을 읽는 문
해력 함양에 초점을 둔다. 또한 수업에서 다루는 내용의 현대적 확장과 적용을 위해 세 차례
의 발표토론회를 통하여 시사적, 보편적 주제를 탐구한다.        
 
학습목표:    
1. 서양문화의 역사적 뿌리인 유럽사의 발전을 고대로부터 근세에 이르기까지 개관한다.
2. 서양 역사의 발전에서 중요한 시대적 특징들을 문화적 현상을 통해 이해한다.
3. 문화적 재현과 실행에 대한 이해를 심화시키고 이를 독해하는 능력을 함양한다. 
4. 개별 문화적 재현양식에 매몰되지 않고 문화적 패러다임의 변화를 역사적으로 이해하는 것
을 도모한다.
성적평가방식: 
중간고사 대체 과제(40%), 기말시험(40%), 수업참여도(20%: 출석점수 8+토론참여 3×4회), 발
표가산점(5%)에 기초하여 절대평가. 평가 기준은 총점 85점 이상 A+~A, 65점 이상 B+~B, 64
점 이하 C+~C.  
실라버스에 표기된 [발표토론] 주제 중 하나를 선택하여 과제 보고서(본문만 5장. 미주와 참고
문헌은 분량 외. 개인/팀보고서 가능. 한글파일 작성 경우에 명조체 계열 10, 줄간격 160; 워
드파일 작성 경우에 한컴바탕체 혹은 유사한 서체 10, 줄간격 1.15)를 작성. 보고서로 중간고
사를 대체. 기말시험(오픈북 테스트, 전자기기 반입 금지)은 6/11에 실시. 
수업자료: 매 수업시간 전 PPT 자료를 제공하기에, 교재를 특정하지 않으며, 『서양사 강의』

SOCI 282: Creativity and Cultural Innovation 
 
Prof. Kangsan Lee  
Office: TBA / Email: kangsanlee@korea.ac.kr 
Course Schedule: Tue/Thu 10:30-11:45pm  
 
 Location: TBA 
 
[Course Description] 
From aspiring directors refining their cinematic worlds to visionary chefs crafting novel 
dishes, creativity permeates everywhere, continuously reshaping industries. This course 
delves into the intricate facets of creativity, its evaluation, and the underlying mechanisms 
that drive both soaring success and imbalanced distributions within creative sectors. 
Students will explore diverse interpretations of creativity, delve into its valuation, and 
analyze the interplay of key factors such as market dynamics, networks, strategies, 
entrepreneurship, and technology. This course provides insights about creativity from 
disciplines such as management and organization, sociology, and entrepreneurship. The 
course unfolds in two phases: Firstly, students will focus on mastering theoretical 
foundations and analytical tools. In the second phase, they will delve into industry-specific 
topics and applications across domains like arts, fashion, music, cuisine, film and TV 
series, and NFTs. Students culminate their journey by contemplating the evolution of 
creativity in the age of big data and AI. 
 
[Teaching and Learning Methodologies] 
     Each class session will encompass comprehensive discussions on the weekly topics, 
which will be prepared in advance through memo submissions by students. Following 
these discussions, there will be a thorough lecture to elucidate the essential concepts. To 
deepen their comprehension of their chosen theoretical approaches, students will also be 
tasked with in-class presentations on their selected topics. A fundamental grasp of 
theories and concepts will be assessed through take-home midterm and final 
examinations. Furthermore, the practical application of these theories to contemporary 
cases and student-selected projects will be evaluated through individual case studies and 
presentations. This multifaceted approach to teaching and learning will provide a holistic 
understanding of the subject matter. Further detailed teaching and learning methods for 
each activity will be found below.  
 
[Graded Activities]  
 
1) Participation (15%): Students are required to submit a short response (one paragraph) 
addressing the topic of the week till Monday 11:59 pm. This weekly memo accounts 
for 15% of the final grade and serves as a platform for sharing thoughts on the 
readings and discussing key points.  
2) Topic Presentation (25%): Starting from week 9 till 13, students will be assigned to lead 
a weekly topic presentation as an individual or a group, which will contribute to 25% 
of the final grade. These presentations will involve guiding the discussion on the 
assigned topic.  
3) Take-home Final Exam (20%): The course includes a take-home final exam (20%), 
allowing students to refer to course materials and resources while answering the 
questions.  
4) Case Presentation and Report (40%): Students will be tasked with conducting a case 
presentation (20%) about a creative case using AI and submitting a corresponding 
report (20%). This assignment serves two key purposes: 
 
a) It provides an opportunity for students to apply the different approaches of 
creativity and its values to the organization they choose and hone their analytical 
skills by examining the contemporary case. 
 
b) It offers a platform for students to enhance their presentation abilities by 
delivering a formal presentation in a supportive and safe classroom environment. 
 
In the early weeks of the course, students will select one case of their interest. They 
should choose an organization/individual that they find intriguing and believe may 
hold personal or professional significance in creativity, innovation, or novelty, either 
presently or in the future. Each student will then present a case study of their 
chosen organization, which will involve analyzing how they define, apply and create 
values with creativity in their cases. However, if the number of enrolled students 
exceeds 15, the individual project will be replaced with a group project involving 2-3 
students.

Goal of PHY220(00)
In this course, students will learn classical dynamics of particles and continua. They will be exposed
to the familiar Newtonian mechanics first and Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalism afterwards.
After the course, students will be fluent in solving problems in classical mechanics and have basic
analytic skills needed in more advanced courses.
Course description
The course will follow the chapters of the main textbook (Thornton & Marion). To accommodate
the range of topics covered within a single semester, some sections addressing advanced material
that are not essential to the progression of learning will be omitted. Assignments consisting of a
few problems per chapter and all relevant example problems will be given after each chapter. All
lectures will be delivered in Korean.
Textbook
Main textbook is Classical Dynamics of Particles and Systems, 5th Edition by Stephen T. Thorn-
ton and Jerry B Marion.
Here are some references that can be helpful:
• Analytical Mechanics by Grant R. Fowles, George L. Cassiday.
• Introduction to Classical Mechanics : with problems and solutions by David Morin.
• Classical Mechanics by John R. Taylor.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

본 강의의 커리큘럼은 한문학과 학생회가 주관하는 학과답사와 연계되어 있습니다. 한문학과 소속 이외의(한문학을 제1
전공으로 하지 않는) 학생은 수강 신청 전에 반드시 교수에게 연락하여 수강 가능 여부를 상의해야 합니다.
학습 목표
본 강의는 한문학과 신입생이 처음으로 접하는 전공과목으로서
1. 문학과 고전, 한자(어)와 한문을 둘러싼 기본적인 개념과 용어를 이해한다.
2. 위의 주제와 관련되었거나 일상 및 지적 활동에서 두루 쓰이는 기초적인 한자와 한자어를 익힌다.
3. 문화유산과 일상생활에서 한자․ 한문을 발견하고 그것의 의미와 쓸모에 대해 생각해본다.
수업 자료
1. 수업 자료는 기본적으로 교수가 작성․ 준비한 것을 사용한다. 자료는 수업 전에 배포하는 텍스트
(PDF), 수업시간에 사용하고 수업 후 공유하는 PPT(PDF로 변환한 파일), 수업시간에 곁들여 볼 수 
있는 시청각 자료(이미지․ 영상 등) 등으로 구성된다.
2. 수업 및 답사활동을 위해 학생 스스로 살펴볼 참고자료(논저 ․ 영화 ․ 에세이 ․ 문학작품 등)는 필요
에 따라 별도로 제시한다.
3. 이상의 수업 자료는 주로 LMS 수업자료 게시판를 통해 배포․ 공유된다. 업로드에 대한 별도의 공지
가 없더라도 강의 전후 해당 게시판을 확인하여 수업 자료를 챙기길 바란다.
수업 방법
1. 수업은 크게 교수의 강의와 학생의 답사활동으로 구성된다.
2. 교수의 강의는 다음과 같다.
  ① 主
    ∙ ⽂學의 쓸모, 古典의 이유
    ∙ 漢字의 이력, 漢字(語)와 한국어
    ∙ 漢字· 漢⽂과 동아시아, 漢字· 漢⽂과 번역
  ② 副
    ∙ 답사활동 및 중간고사 등에 대한 피드백
    ∙ 참고자료 소개, 기타 한자· 한문과 관련된 이야기
3. 학생이 수행할 답사활동은 다음과 같다.
- 2 -
  ① 前半 학과답사(조별)
    ∙ 조 구성, 조원 간 소주제 및 역할 분담
    ∙ 발표자료 草稿 제출, 예비발표 및 보완
    ∙ 발표자료 完稿 제출, 현지발표
  ② 後半 개별답사(개인별)
    ∙ 일상생활에서 한자․ 한문을 발견하고 이를 주제로 한 지정 또는 자유 양식의 에세이 쓰기
    ∙ 발견의 범위와 대상, 에세이의 분량․ 형식 등 구체적인 사항이나 예시 등은 중간고사 이후 안내
    ∙ 우수 에세이로 선정된 경우 학기말에 간략히 발표
평가 방법
1. 수업참여는 출석을 비롯해 한 학기 동안 수강 과정 전반에서 보이는 성실성과 자발성, 成⼈으로서
의 기본적인 교양과 책임을 뜻한다. 수업 듣기는 물론 답사활동을 수행하는 과정에서 적극적인 질
의응답을 권장한다. 출석은 한 번 결석할 때마다 2점씩 감점한다. 감점은 세 번째 결석부터 적용한
다. 학교의 출석인정지침이나 일반적인 상식에 비추어 합당한 사유가 있는 결석은 예외로 한다.
2. 답사활동은 前半의 학과답사와 後半의 개별답사 각 15점씩 배점 예정이며 제반 사정에 따라 조정될 
수 있다. 학과답사는 일련의 과정(발표자료 준비, 예비발표 및 현지발표 등)이 충실히 이루어졌는지, 
본인이 조원으로서 맡은 역할을 성실히 수행하였는지 등을 평가한다. 개인별 P/F로 평가하되 우수
한 발표를 한 조에 대해서는 조원 전원에게 加點을 부여한다. 개별답사는 사유의 獨創性(스스로 발
견하고 생각하여 수행하였는지), 표현의 正確性(어휘를 본래의 의미나 문장의 맥락에 맞게 사용하였
는지, 문법에 맞지 않거나 부자연스러운 문장은 없는지), 제출의 時宜性(기한에 맞추어 제출하였는
지) 등을 기준으로 평가한다. 개인별로 상(15), 중(10), 하(5), 실격(0)으로 평가하되 우수 에세이에 
대해서는 加點을 부여한다.
3. 중간고사 및 기말고사는 각 30점씩 배점 예정이며 진도 및 기타 상황에 따라 조정될 수 있다. 수업
을 통해 학습한 내용을 얼마나 정확히 알고 있으며 그것을 논리적으로 서술할 수 있는지 평가한다. 
주요 용어의 개념에 대한 서술, 한자 및 한자어의 읽기․ 쓰기 등을 포함할 예정이다. 구체적인 사항
은 시험 전에 다시 안내한다.
4. 평가와 관련하여 다음 각 사항에 유념한다.
  ① 【실격(F) 처리의 기준】 아래의 어느 하나에 해당되는 경우 다른 평가항목의 점수와 관계없이 평
점을 F학점으로 처리한다.
    ∙ 결석 7회 이상 즉 출석 점수가 0점이 되는 경우
    ∙ 답사활동을 수행하지 않는 경우
    ∙ 중간고사 또는 기말고사에 응하지 않은 경우
    ∙ 교수의 강의 운영이나 동료의 수강에 방해되는 행위가 과도한 경우, 특히 게임이나 영상 시청 
등 최소한의 상식에서 벗어난 행위를 하는 경우 예외 없이 즉각 F학점으로 처리한다.
    ∙ 일체의 부정행위에 대해서는 不正의 輕重을 不問하고 무관용 원칙으로 일관한다. 시험 시 훔쳐
수업참여 10 + 답사활동 30 + 중간고사 및 기말고사 60 = 총점 100 + 우수 발표 및 에세이 加點
- 3 -
보기는 물론 대리 출석, 출석 체크 후 강의실 이탈, 유고결석에 대한 허위 증빙서류의 제출, 발
표나 과제에서의 윤리위반행위(기존의 논문이나 저서, 언론 기사나 칼럼, 각종 SNS, AI 등 타인
에 의해 기존하는 내용의 도용 ․ 표절 ․ 가공 ․ 윤색 ․ 짜깁기)도 명백한 부정행위이다. 하나의 평
가 항목에서 단 한 번의 부정을 범했다 하더라도, 그 시점까지 취득 ․ 누적된 다른 모든 평가항
목의 점수와 관계없이 즉각 F학점으로 처리한다.
  ② 【성적 공개의 원칙】 학기 종료 후 최종적으로 부여되는 평점을 제외하고 총점과 평점별 총점 구
간은 공개하지 않는다. 다만 필요하다고 판단되는 경우 중간고사 등 학기 중 진행되는 각 평가항
목에 대해서는 해당 평가 완료 후 채점된 답안지 또는 과제물의 개인별 열람 및 반환, 수강생 전
체 점수 공시(익명) 등의 방법을 통해 공개할 수 있다.
  ③ 【성적에 대한 異意】 성적에 대한 이의는 교수가 채점이나 합산 등에서 착오를 범한 경우 외에는 
수용하지 않으며 기타 어떠한 이유로도 성적의 수정은 불가하다. 「부정청탁 및 금품 등 수수의 금
지에 관한 법률」에 따르면 채점 상의 오류가 없음에도 성적의 상향 또는 하향을 요구하는 것은 부
정청탁에 해당되며 학생으로부터 2회 이상 부정청탁을 받은 교수는 학교에 신고 의무가 발생한다.
  ④ 【기타】 기타 평가에 대한 제반 사항은 학교의 관련 규정을 따른다.
기타
1. 본 강의의 커리큘럼은 한문학과 학생회가 주관하는 학과답사와 연계되어 있다. 한문학과 소속 이외
의(한문학을 제1전공으로 하지 않는) 학생은 본 강의의 수강을 확정하기 전에 교수에게 개별적으로 
연락하여 상의하길 바란다.
2. 본 강의는 현재의 한문학과 전공교육과정 체계에서 ‘전공선택’ 과목으로 설정되어 있으나 2학기의 
<한문독해의 첫걸음>과 함께 한문학과 1학년생에게 ‘전공필수’에 준하여 수강을 권장하는 과목이
다. <한문학과 문화유산>은 학과답사와 연계되어 있고 <한문독해의 첫걸음>은 이후 모든 전공 과목
의 기초가 되므로 한문학과 1학년생은 1학기와 2학기에 각각 이 두 과목을 수강하길 바란다.
3. 한문학과 1학년생은 첫 한 해 동안, 현대 한국어는 물론 고전 한문을 이해하는 데 필수적인 2,000
자 내외의 한자(교육부 선정 중고등학교 한문교육용 기초한자 1,800자 또는 고려대 선정 기초한자 
2,100자 등)를 가능한 모두 익히길 바란다. 기초한자에 대한 자발적인 학습과 함께 <생활한자> ․
<초급한문> 등 한자․ 한문 관련 교양 과목을 수강하는 것도 좋은 방법이 된다.
4. 한자․ 한문도 하나의 언어이다. 어떤 언어든 학습 초기에는 소리 내어 읽고 손으로 쓰는 등의 번거
롭고 원초적인 과정을 겪어야 한다. 현재 중등교육에서 한문을 필수로 가르치지 않는 탓에 한자․ 한
문은 누구에게나 어렵고 생소한 언어가 되었다. 따라서 한자․ 한문에 대한 현재의 실력보다는 그것
을 배우고자 하는 의욕과 학습 초기의 어려움을 이겨내고자 하는 의지가 요구된다.
5. 본 강의 계획은 개강 전까지 수시로 갱신된다. 학기 초를 비롯해 학기 중에도 수강생의 학습 수준 
등 기타 강의 진행 상황에 따라 강의 내용, 수업 방법, 평가 방법, 주차별 일정 등이 일부 수정될 
수 있다. 다만 변동되는 내용은 세부적인 사항에 한하며 강의 계획의 ⾻⼦는 유지된다. 강의 계획이
나 수업 내용 등에 대한 질의와 제안은 개강 전은 물론 학기 중 언제라도 가능하다.
6. 첫 시간에 한 학기 강의 계획에 대해 설명하고 수강 인원 및 수강생의 수준 등을 파악한 후 필요에 
따라 강의 계획을 일부 수정하여 확정한다. 따라서 첫 시간에 반드시 출석해야 하며 출석하지 않으
면 수강할 수 없다.

Course Structure:
English in Media has been structured for group and individual activities.  The first half of the semester will focus 
on film, with several objectives in mind.  These include, but are not limited to, improving listening 
comprehension, enhancing leadership capabilities, summarizing and connecting ideas, building vocabulary and 
expressions, learning to identify important scenes and symbols in movies, addressing cultural topics, and sharing 
views/ideas with others.  Students will write plot charts, reaction papers, and complete role sheets in preparation 
for discussion with classmates.  The second half of the semester will focus on selecting and researching a media 
topic of the student’s choosing.  Midterm and final tasks will be in the form of academic papers (midterm being a 
typical 5-paragraph academic essay (topic will involve one or more of the films from the first half of the course) 
and the final paper being a longer version (on a media topic of the student’s choosing).  There are no formal 
presentations in this class.

Texts: These will be available on campus or KULMS:
• Innovative Approaches to Cinema (8th edition, 2024)	
	
	
Blackwood, Michael
• The Way of Research: English in Media (school year 2025)	
	
Blackwood, Michael
Please do not purchase any of the above materials yet; more info will be given in class regarding these texts and 
where you might acquire them.  The films themselves will also act as reference sources; I will attempt to have the 
films available on a computer in our classroom.  Discussions will be based on film content, your own life 
experiences, and occasional referencing to the text.

Participation: 
• Active participation in class, in English, is required. All discussions, exercises, and assignments must be 
conducted in English. Participation includes attendance; arrive on time and prepared. Late arrivals and absences 
disrupt the class and will result in penalties. You are allowed up to three excused absences; ten or more absences 
(including excused) will result in a failing grade, as per Ministry of Education policy.
• Excused absences and tardies do not excuse missed work; you are responsible for catching up. Excused 
absences must be documented with official paperwork, not phone photos, and communicated promptly. Email 
all correspondence to the address provided, not through EKU email. Missed assignments receive a zero; missing 
a midterm or final may result in failing the course. It is your responsibility to ask about missed work and adhere 
to deadlines.
FYI (for your information):
• I expect English to be spoken during class.  People who speak another language will be considered absent.
• Please be aware that deadlines are final. If late work is accepted (due to an excused absence, for example), it 
will be penalized by daily increments.  Deadline extension must be granted by the professor prior to the due 
date.  Failure to complete the midterm or final, and/or a pattern of failure to complete assignments or tasks 
could result in failure of the course.  First submissions only will be graded. To ensure academic integrity and 
facilitate plagiarism checking, students are required to upload their final paper to the university website by the 
deadline, as well as to submit peer review sheets with their final paper.
• Scholarly behavior is expected: arrive on time, prepared with necessary materials, and refrain from using cell 
phones or chatting during class. Points will be deducted for lack of preparation or disruptive behavior.
• All submitted work must include your name, student number, and class code/name (EiM). Incomplete 
information or late homework will result in lost points. Homework must be submitted in class when collected; 
do not send assignments by email unless specifically instructed.
• Assignments of two or more pages must be stapled in the upper left corner (one staple per assignment), but do 
not staple multiple assignments together.
• Emails must be written professionally, not like text messages. Include your name, student number, and the 
course name, and use proper spelling, grammar, and salutations. Questions about the syllabus or grading should 
be asked early in the semester, not at the end of the semester.
• Failure to follow these guidelines will result in point deductions.
AI Usage:
• Students can use generative AI tools like ChatGPT to enhance their learning outcomes (for example, asking 
ChatGPT to check work for mistakes) and have positive educational experiences (for example, asking to explain 
terms or concepts from class that the student cannot understand themselves; however, if students use generative 
AI without basic guidelines (for example, creating answers to an assignment), it may negatively impact the 
quality of teaching and learning.
• Common negative impacts include: (1) violations of academic integrity, such as plagiarism and cheating; (2) 
decline in critical thinking, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills due to exercising the “other brain” and 
not your own; (3) acquisition of inaccurate or biased information; and (4) reinforcement of entrenched 
stereotypes.
• In short, “There is no royal road to learning” (Euclid).  If you use generative AI to do your work for you, you 
have not learned the skills you took the course to learn and so have wasted your money.
Course Outline and Goals:
• Outline:  This course is designed to stimulate students' thinking of the world around them, as well as to provide 
the chance to employ communication skills through reading, writing, listening, and speaking.  All activities are 
provided as a means to further stimulate students' thinking and to facilitate writing. Special effort has been 
taken to establish process rather than product goals.  Also, see attached week-by-week syllabus for further 
details.
• Goals:  The goals for this course include, but are not limited to, critical thinking, a willingness to explore ideas 
contrary to one's own beliefs, as well as knowing when information or data are relevant to an issue and how to 
find that information.  In addition to these general concepts, the instructor also wishes to address student 
concerns for self discovery.
How are students assessed?
• I use a range of assessment methods for the course, including story plot charts, reaction papers, role sheets, role 
group and cafe discussions, as well as an academic essay and a research paper.  There is in this course a clear 
emphasis on working with your peers to discuss ideas, and to work collaboratively to produce more individual 
confidence in speaking, listening, reading, and writing in English.
Grade Codes
Overview of grading criteria:
95-100: A+, 90-94: A, 85-89: B+, 80-84: B, 75-79: C+, 70-74: C, 65-69: D+, 60-64: D, 59 and below: F
For Grade calculation, there are 5 units, generally grouped as follows:
Unit 1: PARTICIPATION (general attendance, scholarly conduct/attitude/initiative/motivation)
Weighted score (10%)
Unit 2: SPEAKING (free-talking meetings/discussions, consultations)
Weighted score (10%)
Unit 3: WRITING [movie assignment sets (plot charts, reaction papers, & role sheets)]
Weighted score (20%)
Unit 4: MIDTERM (academic essay)
Weighted score (25%)
Unit 5: FINAL [research paper, (including in-class pre-writings)]
Weighted score (35%)
These five units are then added together, yielding a subtotal for points earned for the course, plus/minus 
attendance, relative evaluation standards, as well as other sundries.
Attendance Policy
Tardies, absences:
You are permitted up to three excused absences. For each unexcused absence beyond the third, your final course 
grade will be reduced by 1 percentage point through Participation (E.g., if you earn 87%, but have eight absences 
(three excused and five unexcused absences), then your final grade will be 82%.). Being late three times 
constitutes one absence. This follows university policy passed down from the Ministry of Education of 1/3 
absences (>10 absences) being an automatic “F”.
What is excused or unexcused?
Excused: Illness (with documentation), family emergencies, university-sponsored events, military test, etc.
Unexcused: Absences beyond the allowed number, or those without valid documentation.
Counseling Services
The KU Student Counseling Center offers help to students having trouble at university or with their feelings. 
They are very good at listening. They have one to one counseling, group counseling, and even some tests people 
can take about their lives, feelings, personality, relationships, and more. During the semester, they are open from 
Monday-Friday from 9 a.m. - 5:30 p.m (closed for lunch). They are located in the Central Plaza Room 114. Tel: 
3290-1540~1. Website: http://kuscc.korea.ac.kr (in Korean).

Syllabus Addendum	
	
	
English in Media
A Bit More Detail**
English in Media is not only the study of how we communicate visually (and audibly), it is 
also the study of our fixation on the visual medium for the last hundred or more years; by 
this I am referring specifically to the motion picture, how it influences our lives and our 
opinions, how it can incite our imagination or aggravate our fears.
With the aid of technology, students have an opportunity to review visual artifacts (the films) 
on their own, as well as to understand and analyze nuances of said artifacts.
We will study images and symbols that are all around us in the world of media today.  
Students will have opportunities to explore major academic principles with other students, 
thereby gaining confidence and skill in utilizing those principles in English.
Course Objectives
By the end of this course students will have had the opportunity to:
• be able to define key academic terms used to discuss media, specifically the role of motion 
pictures in the modern world.
• become acquainted with many of the tools to be able to recognize, define, and apply the 
basic elements of media studies used by academics today.
• be able to engage in the fundamental discussions of academic thought: defining, 
describing, elaborating, analyzing, engaging in critical thinking, etc.
• be able to analyze elements within visual communication (films, primarily, but also 
potentially extending to adverts, pictures, covers, paintings, etc.) by breaking down 
elements.
• be able to express ideas by means of collaborative study and group discussions, informal 
presentations, etc.
• increase their level of confidence in speaking both formally and informally in English 
regarding media, specifically the visual/audio communication of film.
• become acquainted with APA/MLA styles and have practice writing a research paper
Requirements
Flash Drive (USB)
Students will use this drive to save the current film for private study in their 
home as they complete assignments and exams.  It does not have to be larger 
than 10GB (the biggest film I'm considering would be around 5GB and most 
will be approximately 2GB)

The Right Attitude
Most important of all, students are expected to have a positive attitude toward 
peers, the professor, and about the films; you won't "love" every movie or 
genre that we study, and that's ok (we don't love every book we read in a 
literature class, either).  Students should have a constructive disposition and an 
open mind.  Be respectful, polite, nice, and cooperative.
Grading Rubric
Exemplary work.  Way above expectations.  Displays a perfect application of the 
concepts covered and a great command of English.  Attention to detail, extra time and a 
lot of extra effort.  Displays a professional quality.
“Very good” work, above average.  Displays extra effort, understanding of the 
concepts, and good use of English.  Work that goes beyond the minimum conditions.  
Shows experimentation and insight with fresh ideas.
Satisfactory “good” work.  All minimum conditions met.  Strong effort that displays the 
understanding and application of the concepts covered in the course.
Work that is incomplete, inappropriate, unscholarly, rushed, plagiarized, or sloppy.

Course Outline 
Applied Financial Modeling & Investment is a hands-on course designed to equip students with 
practical skills essential for a successful career in finance. The course emphasizes the application of 
Microsoft Excel to build, analyze, and interpret financial models used in real-world corporate and 
investment contexts. Unlike traditional finance courses focused primarily on theory, this course 
prioritizes interaction, participation, and experiential learning. Students are expected to engage 
actively, both voluntarily and through occasional cold calls, and to come prepared by reviewing case 
materials and background information on assigned companies. The course demands substantial 
commitment and active involvement throughout. 
Students will learn to construct comprehensive financial and accounting models from the ground up, 
perform valuation analyses, and gain an applied understanding of transaction structures such as 
Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) and Leveraged Buyouts (LBOs). In the final part of the course, 
students will apply their valuation skills to portfolio-level decisions, learning the basics of equity 
portfolio management, factor exposure, and performance evaluation. Through case studies, stock pitch 
sessions, and investment memo assignments, participants will develop the ability to craft a coherent 
investment thesis, conduct rigorous financial research, and communicate findings effectively in a 
professional context. 
All analytical work will be conducted using Microsoft Excel, and final deliverables such as 
presentations and reports will be prepared in Microsoft PowerPoint. Students will also review 
professional-level outputs, including equity research reports and investor relations materials, to 
benchmark their work against industry standards. By the end of the course, students will have 
strengthened not only their technical modeling and valuation skills, but also their strategic thinking 
and communication abilities that are essential for high-performance roles in finance, consulting, and 
investment management.

Note on Group Project Collaboration 
The default policy for group projects is that all members of a group receive the same grade. However, if 
you determine that one or more members have made no meaningful effort (e.g., lack of participation in 
meetings, communication, or deliverables), you may formally bring this to my attention. 
In such cases, I will request evidence from all group members. This may include, but is not limited to, 
email or chat exchanges, records of meetings, and documentation of task allocation and completion. 
Therefore, it is your responsibility to maintain clear records that demonstrate your own participation 
and contributions. 
I do not expect perfectly equal contributions from every member; that is rarely realistic. However, if a 
student’s contribution is judged to be objectively minimal or negligible after reviewing evidence, that 
student may receive an individual penalty to their project grade. 
 
Note on AI Usage 
I encourage you to make thoughtful use of modern AI tools in this course. We are living through a period 
of rapid technological change, and learning to work effectively with these tools is part of your professional 
preparation. Open discussion about how AI can help our workflow and quality is welcome. That said, 
please keep two principles in mind: 
1. You are responsible for the final work you submit. 
AI systems can make mistakes, fabricate information, or overlook important nuances. You must 
always review AI-generated content and verify the accuracy of any information before using it. AI 
can enhance your performance, but ultimately, you are the one responsible for the analysis and the 
final product. 
 
2. Do not let AI replace your critical thinking and practice. 
While AI can save time and sometimes produce better results, using it is not always optimal, 
especially when you are still learning. The goal of this class is to develop an intuitive 
understanding of business models, to build and interpret financial models, and to apply them in 
valuation. These skills require critical thinking and repeated practice. If you rely on AI without 
deep thinking, you risk compromising your long-term capabilities as a professional.

Overview
Biochemistry is the study of chemical processes within and 
relating to living organisms. Biochemistry may be used to 
study the properties of biological molecules, for a variety of 
purposes. 
By 
controlling 
information 
flow 
through 
biochemical signaling and the flow of chemical energy trough 
metabolism, biochemical processes give rise to the incredible 
complexity of life. Much of biochemistry deals with the 
structures and functions of cellular components such as 
proteins, 
carbohydrates, 
lipids, 
nucleic 
acids 
and 
other 
biomolecules. Today the main focus of biochemistry is in 
understanding how biological molecules give rise to the 
processes that occur within living cells which in turn relates 
greately to the study and understanding of whole organisms, 
meaning that lots of scientists focus on metabolic pathway. 
This course introduces the foundation of biochemistry and 
provides a variety of medical perspectives.

Overview
"Architecture is the will of an epoch translated into space.“
- Mies van der Rohe, 1923
The primary task of an architect is the design of buildings as material 
entities. However, architecture that inspires across generations stems 
from a profound contemplation of the "space" formed within and 
beyond the physical structure, as well as the "human activities" that 
take place within it. This course explores space multi-dimensionally 
across architectural, urban, and social strata, drawing upon architectural 
theories and practical examples at various scales—from objects and 
rooms to individual buildings and urban fabrics. Through this, the 
course provides a foundation for comprehensively examining and 
understanding the core themes facing contemporary architecture, 
including 
public 
engagement 
, 
history 
and 
memory 
, 
spatial 
atmosphere, consideration for the marginalized, and habitability.

This course aims to explore the relationship between culture and identity through two 
parallel mediums: language and food. In the first part of the semester, we will investigate 
a variety of personal and theoretical engagements with language. Then, we will study the 
ways in which food not only enriches culture, but more importantly, how it reveals 
cultural values embedded in the way we think. 
As a class, we will focus on developing the following skill sets: reading comprehension; 
critical engagement with course material; engaging with and responding to the articulated 
views of fellow students; expressing ideas in both written and verbal form.

Course 
Overview 
 
“Between Public and Private: Between High and Low” 
 
Disconnected cities and architecture 
Especially in Korean cities, architecture has been developed within their 
own property without considerations with its neighborhood and urban 
context. The overall city has been shaped without thoughtful 
considerations of how we shape our public space, while individual 
buildings have huge impact on it. From large-scale apartment complexes 
to the low-rise residential areas and commercial streets, cities have been 
built with the lack of careful plans for building shapes and street borders in 
terms of the public space. 
 
The identity of Korean architecture and Seoul 
The identity of a city is created mostly through the public spaces and public 
landscapes where the exteriors of individual buildings create together with 
the urban fabric such as streets and squares. The reason why many 
Korean architects have difficulty answering the question of Seoul’s identity 
can be seen as that Seoul has not yet successfully created a good public 
area with a good identity.  
 
Between Public and Private  
This studio starts from the boundaries between cities and architecture, 
public and private areas. And it expands the themes of the boundary at 
urban context to the scale of buildings and the principles of architectural 
compositions.  
 
 A building is a word located within the city as a text. By expanding 
architectural understanding into urban context, students are expected to 
develop their own attitudes and approaches to read and design 
architecture as an experiment. Further this design experiments will develop 
with following considerations into student’s own thesis 
- 
How architecture interacts with people, how we use and 
experience architecture as urban and public environment as well 
as individual buildings. 
- 
How architecture should perform and operate for society and its 
sustainable development. As a part of the environment, what is 
architecture’s role in contemporary Korea. 
Identity comes from the commonly shared characters of society but also it 
embraces individual characteristics too. How Korean architecture can 
develop itself considering common virtues as well as individual benefits? 
Considering both common and specific, students can develop the 
alternative directions of architecture in Korea. 
Course 
Objectives 
OUTLINE 
As architecture's role in society becomes increasingly complex and 
constrained, Studio 7 encourages students to thoughtfully define their own 
perspective on architecture. Students are free to choose their focus and 
the architectural problem they aim to solve, within the studio’s thematic 
framework. As this project continues into Design 8, the scope should be 
complex, proposing clear solutions. It requires systematic research and 
analysis to establish the project's purpose, program, site, user, and target 
application. The outcome could range from a physical structure to virtual 
systems encompassing culture, environment, technology, and politics.  
 
Studio 7 initiates the Graduation Project, spanning two semesters. 
Students must apply all their skills in research and urban contextualization. 
This includes a thorough analysis of their chosen site or sites and 
proposing an architectural program that enhances urban life and 
community. Students are developing their thesis topic into architectural 
projects, while the project should be based on comprehensive research 
into materials, technology, and societal trends, with an emphasis on digital 
tool application and data analysis. 
 
The project's scope should strike a balance between urban significance 
and manageable complexity, allowing students to complete the schematic 
design at the building level (in Studio 7) and advance to detailing and 
technical development in Studio 8. Proposals for larger scale urban design 
and master planning are also welcome, provided that some portion of the 
master plan is documented in sufficient detail to develop a detailed 
architectural proposal. 
 
PEDAGOGIC OBJECTIVES 
The student must demonstrate previously acquired skills for research and 
analysis with an open, creative, and critical mind. Then must elaborate a 
comprehensive architectural intervention (including all aspects of design, 
as urban, functional, constructive, symbolic, formal, environmental, etc.) 
based on the findings of the site's analysis, design intent, and prospective 
users. All the processes, from preliminary research to final design, must be 
arranged and presented through texts, diagrams, graphics, drawings, 
models, and digital representation (renders, videos, VR, etc.), as they are 
the basis of the professional architectural work. 
 
1. Detailed and systematic site analysis and urban/human needs. A 
clear understanding of the urban/political reality, its problems, and their 
opportunities mean a personal interpretation, going beyond mere data 
accumulation and quantitative statistics. This analysis is the starting of the 
project intent, the qualitative and quantitative program, the urban, 
technical, and sustainability strategies, and the integration of all of them as 
the start of the design process. 
 
2. Conceptual design must have a clear architectural and urban intention. 
Serious considerations of materiality, structural concept, architectural 
systems, sustainability strategies must be set from the start to be 
integrated into the overall idea. They do not become a hindrance in the 
following steps of the process. (Depending on students’ concept, even 
when the structure and systems may not be considered in a serious 
manner, they should be integrated into the design for at least Studio 8)  
 
3. The design results from a process in which the building is shaped 
step by step. The student must be conscious of this process and must be 
able to express it clearly in its output. A clear process is much more 
meaningful than a good looking at final results without a process behind it. 
 
4. The design should be consistent and inclusive of all previous 
materials and studies, assuming the inherent complexity of the 
architectural facts. 
 
5. The design should integration of all relevant technologies: Envelope, 
structure, environmental, urban, and service systems. that have 
sophisticated architectural definitions, including clear structural ideas, 
passive and active environmental systems, circulation strategies, exterior 
envelopes, life safety systems, universal access, and specific material 
qualities. Deploy architectural components both pragmatically and 
poetically.

KAAB’s PC assigned to this course 
 
10 Architecture and Urban Planning  
Students are expected to understand the importance of urban context 
and its relationships with architecture and individual buildings. They can 
develop architecture with close understanding of urban conditions and 
conceive architectural concepts from urban analysis.  
 
11 Research-Embedded Comprehensive Design  
Students are expected to conduct in-depth research and analysis and 
develop their design based on their understandings and findings from the 
research. The research can play a key role in supporting students’ design 
directions and development. Also, through this studio, student can 
develop their design comprehensively and present through various 
formats 
 
KAAB’s Common Values for this studio 
01 Sustainability of the Environment 
Our studio embraces the core values of sustainable architecture and 
urbanism, rooted in the vital coexistence of humanity and nature. 
Environmental stewardship is not just a goal but the primary driver of all 
our design work. 
 
02 Future Technologies  
We encourage the integration of emerging technologies throughout the 
design process. Students are invited to use these technologies as both 
practical tools for research and as central themes for their thesis 
explorations. 
 
03 Creative Problem-Solving  
Our pedagogy is designed to help students navigate complex conditions 
to identify and define critical architectural problems. Through rigorous 
dialogue with professors, students can develop and guide their own 
visions and methodologies that result in solutions that are both innovative 
and universally meaningful.

[Thesis Booklet Guide] 
Conduct preliminary research on the graduation design thesis you wish to pursue (during 
vacation, before the beginning of the semester). 
The contents of the preliminary survey should be organized according to each student's 
topic, but the content below must be included and an in-depth survey related to it will 
be conducted. 
The topic, research that matches the topic, questions, identification of problems, and the 
resulting conclusions (or assumptions) are supposed to be archived and edited into a 
systematically organized booklet. 
Format: A4 Booklet Any format including width, height, placement, font, etc. (digital file 
submission: PDF, 150dpi) 
Length: Approximately 50 to 80 pages (including images) based on 10pt font size and 
160% character spacing. (the no, of pages can be further consulted with instructors) 
Submission: First day of semester. 
 
Thesis Topic and Research Process for Booklet (only for reference) 
1. Topic Selection (at the beginning The topic direction may be broad)  
What you are intereseted in (Suggesting the direction of research initially) It may be a 
relatively broad topic in the beginning, but as you research, please narrow it down to 
specific topics and use it as an opportunity to clearly organize your directions. (A topic 
that presents a minimum direction for research is required) 
2. Research & Questions 1: from your own experience and research  
Conduct research by setting the direction of research according to the topic (your 
interest) determined in step 1. Questions are created through one's own experience, 
research and analysis, and the problems and solutions discovered through the questions 
are deepened and developed into (more specific) topics. 
3. Research & Questions 2: Articulate the questions through in-depth research 
In-depth research, researching the topic you want to pursue and your awareness of the 
problem in more detail. Through research, the direction you want to take becomes more 
concrete and clear. 
4. Topic & Research Organizing and Editing :  
Finally, select the thesis topic you wish to pursue and conduct in-depth research related 
to it.. Repeat steps 2 and 3 above while concretizing the selected topic. Finally, analyze 
and organize the 2nd, 3rd, and additional investigations conducted according to the topic. 
Presenting suggestions and directions based on the topic. Organized into booklet from 
step 1 through 4) 
[Thesis Booklet Structure] 
Part 1 Thesis Topic 
1. Thesis Topic / Title  
Graduation Thesis design title, suggested through research, etc.) 
2. Thesis Text  
Topic article for graduation design, article matching the topic, Max. 
Approximately 400 to 800 characters 
3. Background-necessity-importance of the topic 
Summarize the background and necessity of why the topic is worth presenting as 
your design thesis (being supported by thr results of your research) 
4. Research and Analysis 
Specifies the need for the background of the topic. 
Organizes the research and analysis that serve and support as the background 
for selecting the topic (finally organizes and organizes research, questions, 
identification of problems, etc., focusing on content that matches the topic) 
If necessary, please include images such as photos, drawings, field visits, and 
case studies. 
5. Conclusions 
At this initial research stage, please made a conclusions(this will be your thesis 
topic or related issues) by comprehensively organizing the topic/background-
necessity/research and analysis contents 
 
PART 2 Project  
1. 
Program Proposal 
Select a program to proceed with the topic, organize the program list, size, and 
other requirements 
2. 
Site Proposal 
Selection of destination for topic progression 
3.  Site Analysis (and other relevant additional analysis for your design) 
Analysis of the site for topic progression 
(Add other necessary content depending on the topic )

2
Course Description
Organic chemistry is a fundamental and pivotal discipline that bridges
diverse fields—including life sciences, materials science, energy,
environment, and medicine—through the design of novel molecules and the
discovery of innovative reactions.
This course delivers the essential principles of organic chemistry to
chemistry majors, establishing a solid conceptual foundation that supports
advanced studies and empowers students to contribute to these
transformative scientific frontiers.
3
Learning Objectives
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
- Comprehend the molecular structures and chemical properties of organic
compounds.
- Elucidate organic reaction mechanisms by visualizing and tracing the flow of
electrons (arrow-pushing).
- Analyze the characteristics of diverse organic reactions and apply them to
solve complex synthetic problems.
- Identify organic compounds using various spectroscopic techniques (e.g., IR,
MS, NMR).

▷ 강의개요 
개요 
이 강의는 전자기학 I에서 학습한 정전기 및 정자기 이론을 바
탕으로, 맥스웰 방정식의 완전한 형태와 그 응용을 심도 있게 
다룬다. 보존 법칙(에너지, 운동량)을 시작으로, 전자기파가 진
공 및 다양한 물질 내에서 어떻게 전파, 반사, 투과, 분산되는
지를 
중점적으로 
학습한다. 
이후 
지연 
퍼텐셜(Retarded 
Potentials) 개념을 도입하여 전하의 가속 운동에 의한 전자기 
복사(Radiation) 원리를 규명한다. 강의 후반부에는 특수 상대
성 이론의 기초 원리를 다루며, 전자기학과 상대론의 물리적 
연계성을 이해하는 것으로 과정을 마무리한다.

수업운영원칙 
강의는 이론 중심의 설명과 예제 풀이를 병행하여 진행한다. 
학생들은 예습과 복습을 통해 능동적으로 학습에 참여해야 하
며, 과제를 통해 학습 내용에 대한 이해를 높인다. 
중간고사 및 기말고사를 통해 이해도를 평가하며, 성실한 과제 
수행과 출석 또한 평가에 반영한다.

▷ 수업목표 
수업목표 일반 
본 강의는 맥스웰 방정식을 기반으로 전자기파의 전파 특성
과 물질과의 상호작용(반사, 흡수, 분산)을 광학적 원리와 연
계하여 심도 있게 다룬다. 또한 지연 퍼텐셜을 도입하여 전하
의 가속에 의한 전자기 복사(Radiation) 원리를 규명하고, 특
수 상대성 이론의 기초를 학습하여 전자기학의 상대론적 완
결성을 이해하는 것을 목표로 한다. 
세부목표 1 
맥스웰 방정식을 기반으로 전자기장의 에너지와 운동량 보존 
법칙을 이해하고, 이를 통해 전자기파의 발생 원리와 다양한 
물질(유전체, 도체) 내에서의 광학적 특성(굴절, 흡수, 분산)을 
심도 있게 해석하는 것을 목표로 한다. 
세부목표 2 
시간 지연 효과를 고려한 지연 퍼텐셜(Retarded Potentials)을 
도입하여 움직이는 전하와 쌍극자로부터 방출되는 전자기 복
사(Radiation) 현상을 물리적으로 설명할 수 있는 역량을 기른
다. 
세부목표 3 
특수 상대성 이론의 기본 가정을 학습하여 전자기학과 상대
론의 물리적 연계성을 파악함으로써 고전 전자기학의 체계를 
완성한다.

의기본개념과성질, 그응용에대해다루고, 다양한문제해결을통해습득한수학적지식에대한이해를돕는다.

What is this class and who is it for?:
• Join us on an fascinating journey as we delve into the most captivating and thought-provoking topics of our 
time. This engaging course takes you on a global adventure, exploring intriguing conspiracy theories, 
controversies, and mysteries that have sparked intense debate and curiosity. Through lively discussions, in-
depth analysis, and later diving into your own research topic, you'll develop your critical thinking skills, 
challenge your perspectives, and gain a deeper understanding of the complexities surrounding these 
fascinating phenomena.
• This course is perfect for those who are curious about the unknown, enjoy exploring the unexplained, and are 
eager to sharpen their analytical minds. Get ready to question, investigate, and discover the truth behind some 
of the world's most captivating enigmas as we investigate these stories, seek the truth, and have a little fun 
along the way!
