COURSE POLICIES 
 
· 
Course Type 
This course will be a full offline mode. 
 
· 
Copyright Law 
Materials and lectures in this course are strongly protected by Copyright Law. Materials are presented 
in an educational context for personal use and study and should not be shared, distributed, or sold in 
print - or digitally - outside the course without permission. Electronic video and/or audio recording 
is not permitted during class unless the student obtains permission from the instructor. If permission 
is granted, any distribution of the recording is prohibited. 
 
· 
Anti-graft Law 
Do not ask the instructor to change the grade unless there is a flaw in grading. Improper solicitation 
and graft for any matters are strictly prohibited by Anti-graft Law. 
 
· 
Attendance Policy 
Do not miss the class more than three times! If you have any justifiable reason to miss a class such 
as emergencies (e.g., job interview, funeral, etc.), please report at least before the class by email or by 
phone, and get the formal allowance from the instructor to minimize the deduction of your points. 
The allowed one will not be counted as absence, but as being late.  
 
· 
Expectations about preparation for class 
You are expected to come prepared to class. Preparation for a class involves downloading, reading, 
and working on the teaching material indicated in the schedule. You are strongly expected to access 
the course website for downloading and reviewing the material, which will be uploaded a few days 
before each session.  
 
· 
Peer Evaluation 
In order to exactly evaluate the degree of contribution made by team members within a team, the 
peer evaluation system will be adopted. At the end of the semester, the peer evaluation form will be 
distributed to all students. Each student should fill in the form and return it to the instructor when it 
is due. 
 
· 
Presentation Guidelines 
All teams will present two times throughout the semester. Each team member has to get involved in 
presentation at least more than one time without exception. In addition, it is not allowed to simply read 
written script for presentation. All presentation should be done in the professional manner. 
 
· 
Participation and Feedback 
This course strongly pursues a two-way communication mode between instructor and students as 
well as between students. Therefore, your strong participation is required not only to get a better 
score but also to share each other’s knowledge and experience in class. 
In terms of feedback, it is hoped that the communication process will indeed be two directional. 
Feedback is to reflect not only how well class objectives are being met, the effectiveness of the 
instructional facilitation, and the extent to which individual needs are being fulfilled, but also the 
quality of student contribution and involvement. Consequently, your oral and written feedback 
relative to questions or concerns you have, more information you need, and any evaluation you have 
of process, content, or the instructor are welcome at any time. In addition, the instructor is willing to 
provide evaluative feedback in the way of comments, advice, and resource suggestions in response to 
any submitted materials. 
 
· 
Academic Dishonesty Policy 
Dishonest academic behaviors are subject to punishment under the Undergraduate Program 
Handbook at Korea University Business School.

COURSE OVERVIEW 
This course offers an in-depth explanation of the Korean Constitution from both normative and 
contextual perspectives. It aims to help students develop a comprehensive understanding of 
Korean constitutional law and politics, which serve as a fundamental basis for the structures 
and functioning of Korean society. By the end of the course, students are expected to under-
stand not only the origins and historical development of the Korean Constitution and constitu-
tionalism, the political structure, and the mechanisms of a democratic constitutional order, and 
human rights protection and relevant constitutional cases, but also how such normative and 
political contexts have shaped and impacted Korean society. 
This course is structured around the lectures, but the students are encouraged to actively par-
ticipate in class discussions. Prior study of law is not a prerequisite. This course is open to 
students of all levels, regardless of whether they are international or domestic students. The 
only requirement is a willingness to better understand Korean society through the lens of the 
Korean Constitution and its political system. 
 
REQUIREMENTS AND EVALUATION 
1. Attendance (10%)  
Students are required to attend all classes, which consist of two sessions each week. According 
to the statutes and rules of Korea University,1 at least 2/3 attendance is required to receive 
credit. If unavoidable circumstances prevent you from attending a class, please email the pro-
fessor in advance. 
2. Participation (20%) 
Students are expected to demonstrate good attitudes and academic integrity in class assign-
ments and actively participate in class discussions. 
3. Midterm paper (30%)  
Instead of taking a midterm exam, students are required to submit a short research paper of up 
to 1,500 words. The topic should be selected from the list that will be provided. 
4. Final exam (40%)  
The final exam will take place in class without notes, computers, or any other aids.

진

 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중
히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정
진

 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기

 ※ This is an 8 week intensive course which will start on April 28th 
  
Overview 
The study of international trade and finance has never been as important as it is now. 
These days, nations are more closely integrated through trade in goods and services, 
investment in each other’s economies. The global economy created by these growing real 
economic and financial linkages has given potential opportunities to participants in the 
world market as well as it has thrown up many challenges such as unprecedented series 
of financial crises and trade wars between countries. Thus, it is essential for future 
business leaders to understand what drives this real linkage across countries. By doing so, 
they cope with global challenges and look for potential opportunities in the global market. 
 
This course first introduces basic principles and theories of international trade and 
investment: Ricardian, Neoclassical trade model, New trade theory (monopolistic 
competition model of trade), other modern theories of international trade, and the theories 
of foreign direct investment. Then, the course applies these theories to understand 
international trade flows and foreign direct investment decisions, particularly from a firm’s 
viewpoint. After the midterm, the course also introduces the world trade environment by 
addressing the issue of trade policy. 
 
Textbook (not required, and lecture notes will be provided) 
Feenstra, Robert C. and Alan M. Taylor, International Economics, Worth Publishers. 
(only the first part of the book, ch.1~ ch.11) 
 
Other references 
Krugman, Paul, M. Obstfeld and M. Melitz, International Economics: Theory & Policy, 
2014, 10th edition, Pearson Addison-Wesley. 
 
Pre-requisite* 
Introductory knowledge of micro-economics is strongly recommended, either 
through principles of economics course or private reading any textbooks about 
intermediate level of micro-economics.

개요
생명체들은 다양한 구조와 형태들을 가지고 있으며, 이들은 공통적
인, 또한 각각의 특이적인 방법으로 에너지 대사와 생명 현상을 하
며 주변 환경에 적응하여 생존하고 있다. 본 과목에서는 생명체를 
이루는 기본 구조와 에너지 대사 활동, 유전적 특성들에 대해 먼저 
공부하고자 한다. 또한 이들 생명체들의 각 기관계 기능과 주변 환
경과의 상호 작용에 대해 학습함으써 학습자의 다양한 생명체들의 
생명 현상들과 특성에 대한 기초적인 지식을 배양하고자 한다.

성적 처리 기준

3) 강의에 참여할 수 없는 경우, 전날 오전 11시까지 담당 교수에게 연락해야 한다. 유고 
등 부득이한 사유는 학교 규정에 따라 처리한다.

교과목 개요
본 교과목은 학생들로 하여금 노인의 케어에 초점을 맞추는 노인간호학 분야를 탐험할 수 있는 기회를 제공한다. 노인의 간호 요구는 젊은 성인의 것과 
다르며, 따라서, 양질의 간호를 제공하기 위해서는 간호사가 노인의 특별한 요구를 제대로 확인하는 것이 중요하다. 본 교과목에서는 노인과 관련된 사
회, 심리, 생리적 변화를 이해하고, 주요 건강 문제 및 노화의 과정과 결과에 영향을 미치는 개인, 가족, 환경적 요소들을 파악한다. 또한, 노인의 건강을 
유지 증진하기 위한 기본적 간호 조정 방법 및 노인간호와 관련된 다양한 윤리적 이슈에 대해서도 학습한다.

할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

▷공통 안내 및 주의사항 
∙ [출석] 
 -1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가능, 단 출
석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함
∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 모든 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정
진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중
히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술
∙ [실험실습 안전]
 -연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분
야 대상 학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습
을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수
 -신규교육(신입생 2시간), 정기교육(고위험학과 학기별 6시간, 저위험학과 학기별 3시간)
 -대상학과(부): KUPID > 지식관리 > 안전관리지식 > 연구실안전
 -이수방법: 포탈시스템 상단 메뉴에서 “정보생활” 클릭, [안전교육(서울), (세종)] 클릭하여 안전교육 페
이지 접속(“크롬”으로 접속, 접속 오류 시 인터넷 설정에서 “팝업 차단 해제” 설정 필요)
 -포탈 아이디가 없는 경우, 국가연구안전관리본부 연구실안전교육시스템(https://edu.labs.go.kr/) 접속하여 수강 가능

Description 
The course is an introductory course of Thermodynamics for sophomores. Students will learn the basic 
concepts of classical thermodynamics including conservation equations, state relations, and first and 
second laws of thermodynamics. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze and 
characterize thermodynamic states and equip the skills necessary for systematic problem-solving.  
 
The topics to be covered include but not limited to 
- 
Thermodynamic properties  
- 
First and Second laws 
- 
Evaluating thermodynamic properties 
- 
Energy conservation using control volume analysis 
- 
Analysis using entropy 
 
Grading 
The students will earn their final grade based on their work throughout the semester, as described 
below. There will be no make-ups for the extra credit. 
 
Assignments (7 – 9 sets) 30 % 
Midterm (TBD, 1:30 pm – 2:45 pm in class) 20% 
Term Project (TBA) 10% 
Final Exam (TBD, 1:30 pm – 4:30 pm, 3 hours) 40 % 
 
Course Policy 
Attendance at lectures is expected as active class participation. If students have any conflicts or 
experience difficulties (e.g., athletic competition, medical issues), students must notify the instructor 
prior to the class. In case of emergency, students can notify the instructor afterwards; however, 
supporting documents by proper authorities (e.g., doctors, police, etc.) should be sent to the instructor. 
If a student is regarded as inactive for class participation, a penalty will be applied to the final 
grade. 
 
Homework assignments will be given to the students. Students will have a week (or more depending 
on the course schedule) to turn in their solution sets. Homework solutions will be collected in class 
on the date due. No late homework solutions will be accepted unless students discuss with the 
instructor in advance. Only valid exceptions, such as participating in competitions (athletics or 
academics), attending conferences, or medical emergencies, will be acknowledged for the late 
homework submission. The homework solution should be original, well-organized, and readable. It 
should include problem description, assumptions, solution procedure, results, and discussion of the 
solution as appropriate. Please refer to the homework grading guideline. 
 
Each exam will cover cumulative materials up to the exam date. However, the emphasis will be given 
to the more recent materials to the exam. Exams will be closed book and note, but students are allowed 
to bring two pages (both sides of one A4 size sheet) of their own summary. During exams, only 
scientific calculators will be permitted if needed, unless specified otherwise. Using any other 
electronics including cell phone is strictly prohibited. Failure to follow these rules during exams 
will result in immediate exam confiscation. 
 
Any grading disputes on homework or exams must be brought to the instructor, not the TAs. 
 
Students are expected to follow the University Honor Code, as appears in the international school 
Website (https://summer.korea.ac.kr/all/src/board/view.php?no=6704). All materials such as 
homework and exam solutions should be original, i.e., each student should work out the solutions on 
his/her own. Discussion for homework problems are encouraging. However, each student should 
submit their own solution. 
 
The course is foundational to students’ mechanical engineering education. It requires a high degree of 
mathematical and scientific rigor to solve even simple problems. Therefore, you should expect to 
complement each hour of lecture with at least 2 hours of personal work. 
 
If you wish to request course accommodations for properly documented disabilities, please speak with 
the instructor at your earliest convenience. 
 
Refer course website for announcements, homework assignments and solutions, exam solutions, and 
grading 
Course Website 
KU's LMS 
Please check the course website regularly as the announcements will be made frequently. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
HOMEWORK SET GUIDELINES 
 
A. Problem solutions should meet a few professional standards. Adherence to these standards 
will facilitate the grader’s interpretation of your work; the solutions, if neatly written, will 
provide you with important reference material that can be easily reviewed before the exams. 
Each problem solution should contain the following basic elements; 
 
Find: State the question briefly to be answered and identify what is to be found. 
Given: Present the given information in a concise form. Include a sketch of the system that 
shows concisely (but clearly and accurately) any control volumes to be used in the 
analysis. Label all forces, velocities, flows, and system states. Graphs should be neatly 
prepared. 
Assume: State all important assumptions. Use a short, numbered list, such as: 
(1) isentropic 
(2) 1D at stations…. 
Basic Laws: Give all basic principles, in general form, and show how the simplifying 
assumptions reduce the problem to a solvable form. 
Solution: Avoid “plug and chug” into formulas unless you really know what you are doing. 
Try to carry all solutions out in symbolic form before substituting in numerical values. 
All physical equations from basic laws are dimensionally homogeneous, so check to 
see that all terms have the same units in a consistent set (e.g. S.I.) 
 
B. Writing up assignments 
 
1. Use a new paper. 
2. Graphs should be neat with appropriate axis labels and lines on constant properties (e.g., s 
= constant). 
3. Staple all sheets together and hand in flat (i.e., don’t fold). 
 
C. Problem grading will be done using a ten-point scale. 
 
10 points for good solution. It may contain one minor numerical error. Errors in units are not 
minor 
8 points for a fair solution which is generally okay, but with some errors which are not judged 
too basic or serious. 
6 points for a solution with one major conceptual error, or a solution which is too flawed to be 
corrected by minor improvements. 
4 points for a solution with two or more major errors. 
2 points for an attempted at solution, but no evidence of progress. 
1 point will be taken off for sloppy work.

Spring 2026 
 
MONDAYS & WEDNESDAYS 4:30 – 5:45  
 
 
ENGL 310: English Major Training Course  
(Writing for English Majors) 
 
Lecturer: Peter McAuley 
Office Hours: After class or by appointment 
 
           
Office: 540 Woodang Hall 
e-mail: petermcauley@korea.ac.kr  
 
THIS SYLLABUS IS SUBJECT TO MINOR REVISIONS BEFORE THE FIRST CLASS OF THE SEMESTER. 
 
I. Course Description 
 
The goal of this course is to develop your reading, writing and critical thinking skills so you 
can better communicate your ideas successfully as an English major. Our focus is on three 
major “skill sets” this semester: 
 
 
Practical 
• Mastering the fundamentals of the writing process and essay writing. 
 
 
• Improving your reading and note-taking skills. 
 
 
• Revising your own written work more effectively. 
 
 
• Defending your viewpoints in English writing and discussion. 
 
 
• Conducting extensive research on an assignment topic. 
 
 
Creative  
• Understanding better how to read and analyze different literary forms. 
 
 
• Expressing your own viewpoints on what you read. 
 
 
• Incorporating literary criticism into your viewpoints. 
 
 
• Writing for a classroom presentation. (If time permits.) 
 
 
• Developing a clear and central idea in your writing (thesis). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Technical 
• Correct use (quote, summary, paraphrase) of research materials. 
 
 
• Identifying and avoiding plagiarism. 
 
 
• Sentence-level grammar issues. 
 
 
• Proper citation of academic sources: MLA format for literature papers. 
 
 
Our course will focus on both reading and writing skills, so you will be reading samples of 
various literary forms throughout the semester, and you will be responding to these works 
through your own writing in English. They will include a play, a novella, some short stories 
and a selection of poems. We will discuss literary texts in class as a group, and you will 
receive feedback on your writing from both me and your fellow students. 
 
Finally, one of my jobs as your teacher is to make our classroom a challenging and enjoyable 
learning environment for you and your classmates; so, please talk with me at any time if you 
have a suggestion on how best to meet your needs in this regard. 
 
 
 
 
II. Path to Your Final Grade 
 
 
 
1. Writing Assignment #1: Close Reading 
 
30 % 
 
 
 
2. Mini-Presentation on Assignment #1 
 
 5 % 
 
 
 
3. Writing Assignment #2: Research Paper  
35 % 
 
 
 
4. Attendance and Participation 
 
 
10 % 
 
 
 
 
5. Discussion Board 
 
 
 
      10% 
 
 
 
6. Two Multi-Choice Conrad Quizzes  
  
10 % 
 
 
 
 
 
Writing Assignment #1 requires writing one short essay in answer to a question on Part I of 
Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness. The focus will be on close reading and interpretation of a 
short passage from the novel. More generally, you will practice the organization and style of 
writing about fiction as an English major. You will have the opportunity to write rough drafts 
and get feedback on your work in a tutorial setting before it is given a grade. The final draft 
of this assignment will be your midterm evaluation.  
 
 
As part of your preparation for Assignment #1, you will give a simple, two-minute  
mini-presentation to your classmates outlining which passage from Heart of Darkness you 
will be writing about, why you chose that particular section from the novel and what will be 
your main opinion or thesis about this episode from the text. 
 
 
Writing Assignment #2 will ask you to do your own library and online research on a topic of 
your choosing connected to Heart of Darkness and will require you to incorporate research 
sources and secondary materials to help you raise the standard of your future academic 
writing. In addition, it will be an opportunity to demonstrate the other English reading and 
composition skills we will be practicing this semester. Most importantly, it’s an opportunity 
to improve your own writing and research skills without the assistance of any AI technology. 
 
 
Participation is not a grade on your personality; rather, it is an assessment of your efforts to 
do your best. It does not require you to ask questions on a weekly basis, but there are 
certain minimum expectations such as not engaging in work for other courses on your laptop 
during our class time. As a general guide, if you fulfill the minimum requirements to do the 
homework and keep up with the assignments, then you will likely get a B/B+ grade for this 
section. Notable efforts beyond this standard expectation will be rewarded with more 
points, just as any effort below will lose them.  
 
 
Attendance is not monitored during the add/drop period. From next week, you begin with a 
“credit” of one unexcused absence for the entire term. After that, your attendance grade will 
drop rapidly with each subsequent absence. In general, supporting documentation is 
required for any excused absences due to illness, university events or professional 
commitments. 
 
 
The Discussion Board will be an ongoing assignment; however, you must make 12 postings 
to our discussion threads on Heart of Darkness no later than week 12. It is important to 
contribute on a regular basis, so after two posts each week, any additional posts will not 
count towards your target of twelve. (There is more information at the end of this 
document.) 
 
 
There will be two short multi-choice reading quizzes on Heart of Darkness to encourage and 
reward the timely completion of the reading homework. The first quiz, covering Part I of the 
novella, takes place in week 3. The second quiz, on Parts II and III, takes place after the 
midterm. 
 
 
 
III. Miscellaneous 
 
Chat GPT & LLM AI assistance  
To maintain an equal and fair environment for all writers in this class, the use of any AI 
technology to complete assignments is not permitted. Likewise, plagiarism, even the copying 
of a single sentence without acknowledging the source, will also result in a lower grade. 
More importantly, I am interested in what you have to say, not what an LLM has generated. 
If you are having any difficulties with developing or communicating your own ideas, then the 
solution is to visit my office for advice. 
 
Translation Software 
It’s perfectly fine to use a dictionary or translation software to find suitable words or phrases 
in English for your writing; however, composing an entire assignment in your native 
language and then using software to translate it all into English is not permitted. Simply put, 
it defeats the purpose of this writing class if the writing in English is not your own. As stated 
already, if you are unsure about your English level being suitable for this course, please feel 
free to consult with me anytime before the add/drop period ends. 
 
Public Holidays  
Any class meeting canceled due to a public holiday or exceptional circumstance will be made 
up from recorded video content rather than requiring an additional in-class meeting that 
might disrupt your regular schedule. 
 
 
IV. Reading Materials  
 
 
 
 
Reader 1:  
Janet E. Gardner & J. Diaz, Reading and Writing About Literature:  
 
   
A Portable Guide, 5th Edition. 
 
Reader 2:  
Joseph Conrad, Heart of Darkness, plus a selection of “secondary” or critical 
 
 
opinions on Conrad’s novel. Using such materials as part of our own  
 
 
discussions and writing about literature is an essential aspect of this course.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
V. First Writing Assignment Instructions 
 
First draft length: 
   1000 - 1100 words [excluding direct quotes and references] 
First draft due date:    Monday, March 30 
Email address: 
   310writing@gmail.com 
Format: 
 
   Please send it as a .doc file for editing: not .pdf or .hwp 
Percentage:   
   This first draft is not graded, but a strong effort is expected. 
 
 
 
   Only the final draft, due on April 16, receives a grade. 
 
Provenance: Your essay must be composed using Google Docs so that the “version history” 
of your answers can be read. The completed file must then be shared with the following 
address, and you need to both email the paper but also make the following address an editor 
for the file and send the Google Doc link to the same address: 310writing@gmail.com. 
 
Writing your draft in this format is a requirement for all students. Please do not begin your 
essay without taking this step first. Also, it is not permissible to cut and paste a pre-written 
paragraph of your essay in the Google Docs file.  
 
Please note that grammar errors will not affect anyone’s grade, but it is not permitted to 
feed paragraphs of your writing through a translation app. Individual sentences or phrases 
are fine, but writing the entire essay in your first language and then using an app to translate 
it into English is not permitted, as it does not help you to improve your own writing in 
English. Keep in mind, our goal is progress, not perfection.  
 
 
Written Assignment Procedure to Deter Unfair AI Usage 
 
To restate, written assignments must be begun, composed, and completed using Google 
Docs with accessible “version histories” so that the evolution of the composition can be 
tracked from start to finish. Cutting and pasting of any written text into Google Docs is not 
acceptable. Any other format, such as Microsoft Word, HWP, or PDF, will not be accepted. 
Failure to follow the correct procedure will result in a loss of 15% of the value of the 
assignment.

ENGL 310: Writing Assignment #1 
 
 
 
Part A 
 
Please choose only ONE of the following four questions 
 
1. Choose one character from Heart of Darkness who is not the protagonist,   
  Charles Marlow, and discuss their role and function in the novel. 
 
2. Discuss the narrative perspective of the story. How important is this element  
  to our understanding of the theme(s) of this text? 
 
3. Discuss how at least one theme of Conrad’s text can be interpreted and  
  understood in relation to any of the settings depicted in Heart of Darkness. 
 
4. Identify and discuss the significance of one motif or symbol in  
Part I of Heart of Darkness. 
 
[Please limit yourself to choosing a passage from PART I of the novel only.] 
 
 
 
Part B 
   Include all of the following in your chosen answer to Part A 
 
i) Above all else, ensure that you have a thoughtful and defensible thesis in your 
essay answer. In other words, make sure you are expressing a clear point of view 
on the question you have chosen from Part A of this assignment. 
 
ii) Perform an explication or “close reading” of one passage from Part I of Heart of 
Darkness. Demonstrate how it is related to the rest of Conrad’s novel, and use 
your reading of your chosen passage to argue for a specific thesis (or viewpoint). 
 
iii) Through your own research, find and include one secondary source to assist 
you in developing your argument and reference it in the assignment.  
 
iv) Incorporate some discussion of different “elements of fiction” (from Chapter 
5), as applicable.  
 
 
* Any use of AI to write this essay is not permitted.* 
* Discovery of the use of AI will result in a lower grade.* 
 
 
 
Discussion Board for Heart of Darkness 
 
12 WEEKS - 12 POSTS - 120 WORDS 
 
 
·  Your contributions can take the form of questions, comments, 
internet links, biographical or historical detail, movie references or any 
other material that you think will add to your classmates’ knowledge or 
understanding of the novel. 
 
·  There are no strict limitations on content. If you feel you are adding 
something helpful or interesting to our discussion, your entries need 
not always be directly about the novel. For example, you could discuss 
wider issues such as other works of literature that relate to this text. 
 
·  Feel free to comment on other students' contributions. I encourage 
you to argue and debate ideas whilst remaining considerate and 
respectful to each other. Constructive criticism is a positive learning 
experience. 
 
·  Finally, this online discussion will also help you test and shape ideas 
for the research assignment at the end of the semester. 
 
 
Posts: A minimum of 12 posts. Each post must be at least 120 words. 
 
Deadline for completion of all entries: You have until the end of week 
12 to complete this assignment. Week 12 ends on May 22. It is 
important to contribute on a regular basis, so after two posts in a single 
week, any additional posts will not count towards your target of twelve.  
 
Evaluation: Postings will not be evaluated for grammar or spelling, but I 
will expect a sincere engagement with the texts and with the opinions 
of your fellow students.  
 
If any posts are AI generated instead of your own thoughts, then they 
will not count towards the twelve required; in addition, the participation 
grade will be lowered.

What is this class all about? 
Welcome to Mr. Wellbaum’s Academic English course!  
The purpose of this course is to help students improve their 
English abilities in all areas, from speaking and listening to 
reading and writing.   The course will utilize a number of 
different activities and assessments to help develop those 
skills.  The students will (hopefully) enjoy lectures, 
interviews, discussions, debates, writing projects, and a 
variety of task-based learning exercises to help develop 
confidence and fluency.   This is a challenging class, so 
participating as much as possible will greatly improve your 
performance and grades! Note: You will not need to buy a 
book for this class.  I will provide students PDF files to use 
in the LMS system prior to the start of our classes.

Korea University
Syllabus Spring Semester 2026 
Academic English 
 
My attendance policy is strict.  All students are required to 
attend all classes on time.  Being late twice will result in 
one absence (whether offline or online).  Attendance will 
be taken at the beginning of every class.  
I do not regularly excuse any absences, so sending me 
documents (such as prescriptions from hospitals or 
pharmacies, or notes from your major’s administration 
about a special activity) will not give you an automatically 
excused absence.  My attendance policy is not aligned with 
any exemptions other departments may use, so simply 
submitting documents into KU Portal does not excuse an 
absence. However, if there is an emergency or unique 
situation, we can discuss it in person for exemptions (I am 
reasonable about this as long as it is done in a timely 
manner - please do not wait several weeks to explain an 
absence to me). This policy is in place to prevent an 
excessive amount of exemptions that would severely affect 
participation.  
The total value for the attendance grade is 20 points, but 
for each class you miss, you will be subtracted 3 points 
from your final grade for the first 2 absences, and then 
4 points for any additional absence. I do give each 
student one free absence, with no point penalty at all 
(see, I’m not a total monster!).  I would save it for an 
emergency situation.  That may seem like a strict policy, but 
because we have only two short classes per week, I believe 
this policy to be fair for all.  Attendance is a huge part of 
learning a foreign language, so I take this grading seriously.  
Lastly, please remember that per Korea University policy, 
students may not miss 7 classes before failing the course.   
This is a general syllabus for all of my Academic English 
courses and is subject to change.  While the classes I teach 
are structurally similar, I often design different midterms or 
quizzes to fit the needs of the students I am working with.  
The midterm in one class, for example, may differ greatly 
from that of another class, but the point system is still the 
same and rarely changes. Often times, class content will be 
tailored to be relevant to the needs of the students’ majors 
or special fields of study. 
It would be a good idea to frequently check the LMS Bulletin 
Board System as well.  During the semester I put all grading 
information and announcements there.

be shy.  You can visit me in my office in room 717 in the IFLS building by appointment (though I

for online classes.).  If you have any questions at all, please email me at

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

Course Objectives 
 
The two semesters sequence will introduce students to the disciplines of 
Architecture through an iterative approach to thinking and making. The first year 
is structured to develop critical thinking through a process of making, reflection 
and invention. Understanding will be developed through and communicated by 
two and three-dimensional exercises. These will respond to object, body, space, 
and address responsibility for individual actions as an ethical and sustainable 
engagement. The first-year sequence will provide a foundation to connections 
between studio, academics and personal experiences accessed through a 
variety of creative disciplines fostered both individually and within group 
activities. 
 
Students will work at times individually and at times in groups of students. As 
each exercise is introduced, developed, and reviewed, instructors and students 
will engage in critical explorations and discussions of the idea of “design.” 
Selected readings, films, and lectures will enrich this exploration. 
 
BASIC STUDIO I object: INQUIRY – FOUNDATION - PROCESS 
The studio will focus on developing the language, knowledge and skills of 
 
KOREA UNIVERSITY ARCHITECTURE DEPARTMENT                              SPRING SEMESTER 2026 
students through a hands-on course of design, thinking and learning. This 
integrated cross-fertilized sequence of structured exercises in composition and 
skill thinking provides pathways for engagement for future application of design, 
which will be focused on a series of media / material explorations and tech-
niques to provide tools for visual analysis and representation in developing a 
process of making. 
In the year-long studio sequence, students will be asked to cultivate:  
 
• an understanding of principles and vocabulary of designs 
• compositional methods and principles 
• an understanding of material language 
• observation and awareness of the built environment 
• engagement in social, ethics and sustainable thought  
• critical analysis and thought 
• a discipline of making 
• individual and group character 
• visual and perceptual facility 
• plan, section and orthographic understanding 
 
A studio-based environment with the focus of the design lab will be the making, 
assembly, analysis of the compositional skills of the object at 1:1 scale and 
scaled-models. Students will explore a variety of representation and 
presentation conventions to visualize the relationship between ideas, material 
and whole. Considering an object’s material properties, mechanical operation 
and logic of assembly to explore and understand the compositional nature of the 
object and space. For the period of the semester, students will employ various 
manipulations to explore part to whole in material and graphic representation of 
systems and patterns.

1년 과정의 기초 스튜디오 시퀀스에서 학생들은 다음을 발전시킬 것입니다: 
 
• 디자인의 원리와 어휘에 대한 이해 
• 구성 방법 및 원리 
• 재료 언어에 대한 이해 
• 건축 환경에 대한 관찰 및 인식 
• 사회적, 윤리적 및 지속 가능한 사고에 대한 참여 
• 비판적 분석 및 사고 
• 제작 훈련 
• 개인 및 그룹 특성 
• 시각적 및 지각적 시설 
• 평면, 단면도 및 정사영적 도면에 대한 이해 
 
디자인 실험에 초점을 맞춘 스튜디오 기반 환경은 1:1 크기와 축소된 모형에서 대상의 구성 
기술을 만들고, 조립하고, 분석하는 것입니다. 학생들은 다양한 표현 및 프레젠테이션 규칙을 
탐구하여 아이디어, 재료 및 전체 간의 관계를 시각화 합니다. 물체의 재료적 속성, 구조적 작
동 및 조립 논리를 고려하여 물체와 공간의 구성적 본질을 탐구하고 이해합니다. 학기 동안 
학생들은 다양한 조작을 사용하여 시스템과 패턴의 재료적 및 그래픽 표현에서 부분과 전체를 
탐구합니다. 
 
Projects 
 1. 100 Composition (2 weeks) 
 2. Space Container (2 weeks) 
 3. Cubes (4 weeks) 
 4. Small Building (7 weeks) 
 
Complementary Activities 
 Lectures (on practical and theoretical topics)  
 Desk critic, pin-ups, and presentations 
 Field trips (visit to buildings or places)  
 Inter-studio mingles 
 
The design studio periods will consist of formal introductions to the exercises, 
pin-up, midterm review, discussions of work in progress, work sessions, and 
final reviews. When there are no group discussions scheduled, students are 
expected to use the full class time to develop their projects. Efficient work habits 
in the studio will reduce the demand for this course outside of scheduled class 
time.

Evaluation of your work and learning behavior is an ongoing process in which

Students are supposed to attend each class, punctually. Each absence must

The final grade will be given only after all the required submission of

A_ EXCELLENT - Work of excellent quality:  
Work reflects outstanding achievement in both content and execution. Work must far 
surpass the given requirements. Work is extremely thorough and cohesive. Student 
contributes to larger studio discourse. 
B_ GOOD - Work of good quality:  
Work reflects high achievement in both content and execution and excels beyond the 
minimum stated requirements. Work demonstrates good consistency and progress. 
C_ AVERAGE - Work of average quality:  
Average, acceptable work that fulfills the given requirements. 
D_ BELOW AVERAGE - Work of below average, but passing quality:  
Work is less than satisfactory and minimally competent. Work demonstrates little 
progress or advancement and does not fulfill stated requirements. 
F_ FAILURE - Work resulting in failure of the course:  
Work fails to meet the minimum standards for passing the course. Work that is 
incomplete and unacceptable by the standards of the department. Work that is not 
turned in, incomplete, or demonstrates little or no progress.

Introduction to English Linguistics (ELED  161-01) 
Spring 2025 
 
Time: Mon & Wed (3:00-4:15pm) 
 
Classroom: 교육관 #406 
Prof: Sang-Geun Lee  
 
 
Email: slee16@korea.ac.kr 
Office: 교육관 #707 
 
 
 
Office hour(s): Mon & Wed (4:30~6:00pm) 
 
1. Course description  
Have you ever thought about how some medical practitioners fail to treat patients properly because they don’t 
understand the root cause of the illness? The same thing could happen in English education! If teachers don’t 
understand how the English language works, they might struggle to help their students and could even make things 
worse. That’s why we start with English linguistics in the first semester of English education. This course, 
Introduction to English Linguistics (for EFL Teachers), is designed to give students the tools and knowledge they 
need to connect linguistics with real-life teaching and learning. In this course, we will explore the key areas of 
linguistics – like pragmatics, semantics, syntax, morphology, and phonology/phonetics, to see how tiny pieces of 
language like sounds and words come together to form sentences that make sense and help people successfully 
communicate. After all, this course will help students to find out an answer for the question why English works the 
way it does. So, if you’re thinking about becoming an authentic English teacher, this class is a must. To make things 
even more relevant, we will use teaching methods like project- and team-based learning and PBL (problem-based 
learning), which reflect real classroom experiences and help students improve their teaching skills while working 
closely with their classmates. 
 
2. Goals: By the end of the course, students should be able to … 
(a) manage raw English data and do fieldwork, 
(b) analyze English phones, morphemes, words, phrases and sentences, 
(c) determine underlying structures hidden below surface forms, 
(d) understand rules and principles working for the generation of English, 
(e) and have fun learning about the English language. 
 
3. Textbook 
An Introduction to Language (by Fromkin, Victoria, Robert Rodman, and Nina Hyams) 
(*Any edition will work.) 
 
4. Requirements 
a. General: Students should actively (1) participate in discussion of problem sets, assignments, and mini-project, 
and (2) take two comprehensive exams covering core linguistic areas. 
- Problem-set discussions: Students will be randomly divided into groups for problem sets, and each group 
should solve the PbLs after discussion with his/her members and present the solutions to the class. 
- Group assignments: Students will be divided into groups for Group Assignment, and each group should 
submit the answers on LMS on the due date. 
- Mini project: “When Humans and AI Judge Language, Do They Think the Same Way?” (*Refer to 
another page for details.)  
- Exams: Students will take two in-class comprehensive exams. 
b. Reading: Students should read the material (textbook & PPTs) assigned before you come to the class; it will 
help you to better understand English lecture and actively participate in class discussion. Read Ch1 and Ch2 
of the textbook before you come to the first class! 
c. Attendance and participation:  
- Your attendance credits (10%) in class will be automatically added up according to your active 
participation in discussion for problem sets.  
- Students may be allowed “exceptional” absence before/after they get the instructor’s approval. (You may 
contact the instructor through email.) 
- Absent students are responsible for all class materials and activities, which will be uploaded on LMS.

⚫ Mini Project Title: “When Humans and AI Judge Language, Do They Think the Same Way?” 
 
1. Project Overview  
⚫ In this project, you will: 
◼ 
Collect human judgments on English sentences or words. 
◼ 
Collect AI judgments on the same data. 
◼ 
Compare similarities and differences: Where do humans and AI agree and disagree? 
◼ 
What might explain the differences? - You are not testing who is “smarter.” You are 
investigating what kind of knowledge is linguistic knowledge. 
 
2. Project Structure  
① Research plan + question  
② Design data + prediction 
③ Collect human (native speaker) judgments 
④ Collect AI judgments 
⑤ Compare & present 
 
3. Research Plan/Question Options (You may choose ONE domain): 
(1) Option A: Syntax Judgment - Do humans and AI agree on word order violations, movement 
violations, or pronoun interpretation, etc.: 
⚫ Example Data Set:  
◼ 
Koreans love memes. 
◼ 
Love Koreans memes. 
◼ 
The dog that chased the cat ran away. 
◼ 
The dog chased the cat that ran away. 
◼ 
What did you eat? 
◼ 
What did you eat an apple? 
⚫ Task: Participants (native speakers & AI) rate each sentence: 
⚫ “Does this sentence sound natural?” 
1 = Completely unnatural, 2 = A bit unnatural, 3 = So so, 4 = Quite natural, 5 = Completely natural 
 
(2) Option B: Morphology Productivity - Do humans accept new verbs differently than AI? 
⚫ Example Data Set: 
◼ 
I googled it. 
◼ 
I Ubered home. 
◼ 
I Zoomed my professor. 
◼ 
I lunch-ed at noon. 
◼ 
I weekend-ed in Busan. 
⚫ Task: Participants (native speakers & AI) rate: 
⚫ “Does this sound like possible English?” 
 
1 = Completely unnatural, 2 = A bit unnatural, 3 = So so, 4 = Quite natural, 5 = Completely 
natural 
 
(3) Option C: Semantics & Pragmatics - Does AI detect presupposition contradictions or implicatures 
(or inferences) like humans? 
⚫ Example Data Set: 
◼ 
I believed she was sick, but she wasn’t. 
◼ 
I knew she was sick, but she wasn’t. 
◼ 
I regret eating it, but I didn’t eat it. 
◼ 
I thought I locked the door, but I didn’t. 
⚫ Task: Participants (native speakers & AI) rate each sentence: 
⚫ “Does this sentence sound logically coherent?” 
1 = Completely unnatural, 2 = A bit unnatural, 3 = So so, 4 = Quite natural, 5 = Completely natural 
 
4. Data Collection  
(1) Human Data Collection 
◼ 
Each group collects minimum 5 native speakers’ judgments. 
◼ 
All participants rate same 10 sentences. 
◼ 
Use 1–5 Likert scale (from 1 to 5) to judge language naturalness.  
◼ 
Students calculate mean score and disagreement patterns. 
 
(2) AI Data Collection 
◼ 
Input the same data into AI (e.g., ChatGPT).  
◼ 
Example prompt: “Please rate the following sentence from 1–5 in terms of grammatical 
naturalness.” 
◼ 
Students record AI scores. 
◼ 
Optional extension: Ask AI to explain its reasoning. 
 
5. Final Delivery: Presentation Structure (10 minutes for each group) 
◼ 
State Research Question 
◼ 
Describe Method: How you collected the judgments 
◼ 
Present Key Results (simple table) 
◼ 
Discussion 
◼ 
What we learned about linguistic knowledge 
 
6. LMS Submission: Upload the materials to LMS by due date.

습과 평가를 위한 유럽연합 공통의 참조기준 Common European Framework of 
Reference for Language]이 정 한 B1 수준에 해당한다. 읽기, 듣기, 말하기, 쓰기 영역 
전반에 걸쳐 기초 독일어를 완성하고 중급 단계 진입을 위한 어휘 및 문법을 학습하는 과목
이다. CEFR의 기준에 따르면 A1는 외국어 학습의 Beginner 단계에 해당하고 A2는 Elementary 
그리고 B1는 Intermediate 단계에 해당한다. 따라서 B1는 이전 단계인 A2, A1의 기초 내용을 
기저에 두고 출발한다. 해당 외국어권에서 일상 생활을 유지하는데 필수적으로 요구되는 최소
한의 구사력인 B1는 독일어의 경우 Goethe-Zertifikat B1 및 TELC B1 시험을 통해 확인 및 증
명될 수 있다. 본 과목은 따라서 기초 독일어의 내용학습을 완결하고자 하는 학습자 뿐만 아
니라 Goethe-Zertifikat B1 시험을 앞두고 있거나 준비하고 있는 학생들에게도 적합하다. 실제로 
본 과목의 교재 – 아래에 자세히 소개됨 - 는 유럽공통 참조기준에 의거하여 그 기준이 요구
하고 평가하는 항목들을 반영해 편찬되었다. CEFR B1는 B1-1 및 B1-2로 나뉘어지고 각 단계를 
각각 한 학기에 걸쳐 다루는데 이번 학기에 우리는 B1-1를 다룬다. 각 과마다 주요 주제가 있
고 그에 따른 읽기, 듣기, 말하기 및 쓰기영역이 훈련되며 매 과(Kapitel)마다 주요 문법 사항
이 집중 연습을 통해 습득된다. B1 단계가 과연 어떤 수준이며 어떠한 수행능력을 요구하는
지에 관해서는 수업 첫 날 다루게 될 것이다. 
본 과목 [독일어III]은 [독어 CEFR B1-1]과 함께 세트강좌를 구성한다. 두 과목의 교재는 
동일하며 두 과목을 한 학기에 동시에 수강할 때 유럽공통참조기준(CEFR)이 정한 독일어

학습 B1.1 단계를 온전하게 이수하게 된다. CEFR B1.1과 독일어III을 동시에 수강하도록 
한 배경에는 외국어 습득수준에서 B1가 차지하는 중요성을 수업시수에 반영하여 집중적인 
어학강좌를 제공하기 위함이며 본교 독어독문학과 학생들의 독일어 구사능력의 향상에 기여
하기 위함이다. 불가피하게 두 과목 가운데 하나만을 수강하려는 학생들도 있을 수 있는데 원
칙적으로 두 과목을 함께 이수하는 것이 유의미하며 학기초 정확한 인원이 파악되는 대로 경
우에 따라서는 합의를 거쳐 운영의 묘가 도출되어야 할 가능성이 있다.

Goethe- Zertifikat B1 수준으로 끌어올리고 더 나아가 동명의 어학 시험에 성공적으로 합
격하는데 본 과목의 목표가 있다. 전통적인 외국어 학습의 주요 영역인 읽기, 말하기, 듣기, 
쓰기 외에도 토론의 기초적인 기술적 표현들 및 주제에 대한 개인의 생각을 피력하는 요령을 
습득하는 데 본 과목의 목표가 있다. 자신의 고유한 생각을 표현하고 타인의 말을 경청함으로
써 건설적인 토론을 통해 생산적인 합의에 이르는 과정은 독일어 학습의 전 단계에 걸쳐 매우 
중요하게 다루어 진다. 기초적인 문법을 완성하는 단계인 만큼 관련 연습문제도 집중적으로 
다루게 될 것이다. 말하기는 듣기를 전제로 하고 쓰기 또한 읽기 능력을 전제로 한다. 사실 
이 네 영역은 서로 따로 존재할 수 없으며 상호 매우 밀접하게 연결되어 있어서 어느 한 영역
만을 따로 향상시키기 어려우며 한 영역이 향상될 때 나머지 다른 영역이 동시에 향상되는 예

[수업운영] 
본 과목은 수강생 모두의 독일어 구사력을 향상시키는데 목적이 있으며 경쟁을 통해 순위를 
정하고 점수를 매기는 데 목적이 있지 않다. 따라서 기본적인 수업방식은 수강생 간의 협력을 
통한 상호 보완과 시너지 창출이다. 기존의 독일어 학습자와 처음 시작하는 수강생들이 함께 
그룹을 이루고 때로는 일대일 파트너가 되어 자유롭게 의견을 교환하고 서로를 돕는 방식이 
바람직하며 수업의 기본적인 운영도 이러한 회화 중심의, 수강생이 주도하는 형태가 될 것이
다. 
Netzwerk neu B1.1는 B1.2와 마찬가지로 총 6 단원으로 이루어져 있다: B1.1는 1과부터 6과까지, 
B1.2는 7과부터 12과까지 다룬다. 본문교재 Kursbuch와 더불어 연습문제용 Übungsbuch가 따로 
있으며 수업시간에 이 연습문제집을 다루기도 하지만 상당 부분은 과제로 주어진다. 주제와 방
식에 따라 교재 이외의 자료들이 연습과제 및 유인물로 전달되며 모든 자료는 일련의 번호를 
매겨 하나의 자료로 보관할 것을 권고한다. E-book 및 Video를 비롯, 다양한 매체들이 수업에 
이용되며 교재 홈페이지 온라인 연습문제(klett.sprachen.de/netzwerk-neu)는 개인별 복습에 주요하
다. 
수업 내용에 질문이 있거나 보충 설명이 필요할 경우 수업을 전후하여 강의자에게 언제든 문
의할 수 있으며 혼자 학습하다가 궁금한 것이 있으면 학교 LMS/Learning Management 
System의 Q&A 코너에 질문을 올려 다음 수업시간에 설명을 들을 수 있다.  
 
구체적인 수업 방식을 나열하면: 
 
1. 강의: 본 강좌는 독일어로 진행되므로 소통상의 오해와 중요한 학습 내용에 대한 이해가 
충분하게 이루어지지 않을 가능성이 실질적으로 존재한다. 그러므로 무엇보다 중요한 것이 강
좌 구성원 전체의 원활한 소통이며 이를 위해서는 그것을 실현하려는 노력이 필요하다. 언제
든 묻고 답하는 태도가 중요한데 이 때 질문자는 반드시 손을 들어서 발언의 의사가 있음을 
표시해야 한다. 설명 중에 갑자기 끼어드는 식으로 질문하는 것은 글로벌 매너에 맞지 않을 
뿐만 아니라 수업 진행의 기본 흐름을 방해할 수 있다. 주요 문법 사항 등은 Power Point를 통
해 소개되고 연습문제의 듣기 자료가 학교 LMS에 업로드 될 것이다.

2. Gruppenarbeit bzw. Partnerarbeit: 조별 협동과제는 어휘 학습이나 토론에 특히 유효하다. 학습
자 사이의 원활한 소통은 학습 능력 향상과 매우 밀접한 관계가 있고 서로 부족한 부분을 보
충하는데 매우 효과적이다. 질문과 대답이 자유롭게 오가는 과정에서 상당히 많은 부분을 배
울 수 있다. 파트너 과제는 대화 연습 및 연습문제 해답 찾기에서 특히 효과를 발휘하며 조 
구성과 파트너를 정하는 방식은 수시로 필요에 따라 달라진다. 
3. 소규모 평가: 통상 중간 고사와 기말 시험으로 이루어지는 2회의 필기시험이 아니라 두 단
원이 끝날 때 마다 읽기, 쓰기 및 듣기 영역을 간단히 테스트하는 총 3회의 시험이 예정되어 
있다. 그 밖의 구체적인 수행과제는 
- 텍스트 요약하기 
- 코멘트 작성하기 
- 듣고 내용을 요약하기 
- 통계자료를 해석하기 
- 대화를 완성하기 
- 문장을 완성하기 
- 적절한 낱말을 넣어 텍스트를 완성하기 등이 있다. 
4. 수시과제: 과제 중에는 제출을 요하는 것들이 있다. 특히 쓰기  
영역 훈련은 대부분 학교 LMS 제출 과제를 통해 이루어진다. 기한을 지켜 성실하게 제출하는 
것이 중요하다. 
5. 보충자료 및 연습문제: 수업 시간에 handout 형식으로 배분되거나 학교 LMS에 업로드 된
다. 
6. 수업시간에 Google-docs, Padlet, Mentimeter 같은 온라인툴을 이용해 작성된 조별활
동 및 개인활동의 결과물도 교정을 거쳐 모두 학교 LMS에 업로드 된다. 이로써 학습자 모두 
이전 결과를 조회하고 복습할 수 있으며 실력향상의 과정도 스스로 체크할 수 있다. 
7. 듣기: 본문교재용 오디오파일(강의자용)은 주로 수업시간에 함께 듣기에 이용되며

[과제물] 
1. 중요한 학습목표는 다양한 과제를 통해 습득 여부가 확인되어야 한다.  
2. 거의 매 시간 Übungsbuch 연습문제 일부가 과제로 주어진다. 성실하게 수행하고 궁금한 
점이 있을 시 반드시 질문하는 것이 중요하다.  
3. 쓰기 제출과제와 같은 개인과제는 반드시 교정되어 되돌려지며  
4. 이 때 공통적으로 문제가 있는 부분에 대해서는 집중적인 설명과 연습이 반복될 것이다.  
5. 과제는 얼마나 잘 했느냐의 여부도 중요하지만 (“잘한다”는 과연 무슨 뜻일까?) 
6. 기한을 지켜 성실하게 제출하는 것이 더 중요하다. 
7. 문서로 만들어 제출하는 과제의 경우 (작문과제 등) 학교 LMS 과제물코너에 제출할 수 
있으며  
 
7
8. 모든 과제는 평가의 대상으로서 제출기한과 내용 모두 중요한 평가요소가 된다. 
 
 
[평가방법] 
1. 수시과제: 수시과제는 평가 총점의 6%를 차지한다. 정답 유무보다 중요한 것은 제출기한
을 지키는 것이며 모든 과제는 교정단계를 거쳐 제출자에게 되돌아간다. 쓰기 과제의 경우 
요구된 분량과 내용을 준수하여 작성하는 것이 중요하다. 
2. 출석: 출석은 매 시간 체크되며 전체 평가 총점의 15%를 차지한다. 수업 시작 15분 이후
의 입실은 지각이며 당연히 감점의 요인이다. 지각 자체는 - 습관적인 것이 아니라면 - 사실 
양해의 여지가 있다. 지각 자체보다 더 심각한 것은 지각생의 태도이다. 수업에 방해가 될 정
도로 소음을 내며 입실하는 경우가 있는데 반드시 지양되어야 할 것으로 본다. 지각 자체는 
타인에게 손해를 입히지 않지만 부주의한 소음으로 타인의 집중력을 흩트리는 것은 글로벌 매
너에 어긋나기 때문이다. 결석은 불가피한 사안이 있을 때 미리 이메일을 통해 양해를 구할 
것을 권고하며 이러할 때에만 소위 entschuldigt/excused가 가능하다. 여학생을 배려하는 
[유고결석] 이용은 한 학기 최대 2회까지만 허용한다. 
3. 참여도: 출석이 성실하다 해도 수업에 집중하지 않거나 참여도가 낮다면 목적한 성과를 
이루기 어렵다. 본 과목의 특성상 파트너와 하는 과제와 그룹별 수행과제가 수시로 
주어지는데 타인과의 소통이 중요하고 공조해야 하는 이러한 형식의 수행과제에 적극적으로 
참여하고 기여하는 것이 매우 중요하다. 따라서 출석과 별도로 참여도를 평가 기준으로 전체 
총점의 4%를 할애한다. 
4. 필기시험(2회): 기존의 중간과 기말시험이라는 두 번의 필기시험 대신 교재의 1과와 
2과를 마친 후 중간고사 기간 이전에 1차 필기시험을 실시한다 (총점의 24%). 2차 필
기시험은 5과와 6과를 마친 후 기말시험 기간에 실시한다 (총점의 26%). 이 두 번의 
필기시험 반영비율은 총점의 44%이다. 답안은 필기시험 직 후 공개하며 수강생 본인의 
점수를 스스로 확인할 수 있다. 필기시험 후 첫 시간은 문제풀이 시간(review 
sessions)에 할애한다. 필기 테스트는 약 40분 내외 소요되며 읽기, 듣기, 쓰기 영역을 
테스트한다. 정규 수업시간에 시험을 실시하고 나머지 시간(약 35분)에는 정상적으로 수
업한다. 학습 성취도를 보다 정확하게 파악하고 적절하게 피드백을 제공하기 위해 테스
트의 범위를 소규모로 하고 두 번의 필기시험 사이에 한 번의 구술시험을 실시하는데 그 
시기와 방법은 다음과 같다: 
5. 구술시험(1 회): 총점의 25%를 차지한다. 교재의 3 과와 4 과를 마친 후 앞선 1 차 
필기시험의 내용을 포함하여 각각 약 15 분에 걸쳐 두 사람이 짝을 이루어 말하기 시험을 
치룬다.

Globalization is a concept frequently discussed yet often misunderstood. To clarify this 
pivotal theme, the course begins by examining the multiple definitions, dimensions, and 
interpretations of globalization. We will explore the complex interconnections it 
generates—linking traditional and modern cultures, fostering both diversity and 
homogenization, and shaping migration, immigration, and ethnic identity. While 
adopting a global perspective, this course places particular emphasis on Korea as a case 
study of globalization’s paradoxes and challenges. We will analyze how Confucian 
traditions and family-centered values interact with global cultural flows, how Korean 
society negotiates issues of gender inequality, aging populations, and shifting family 
structures, and how international migration reshapes ethnic diversity within Korea. 
Special attention will be given to the Korean Wave (Hallyu) as a cultural export, 
illustrating how globalization not only transforms Korea internally but also projects 
Korean culture worldwide. Ultimately, the course highlights how Korea’s rapid 
modernization and global prominence coexist with deeply rooted traditions, creating a 
unique lens through which to understand globalization’s impact on culture, society, and 
everyday life. 
 
 
II. COURSE OBJECTIVES  
The principal objective of this course is to equip students with the knowledge and 
analytical tools necessary to develop balanced perspectives on globalization and its 
impact on Korean society. To achieve this, students are expected to: 
• 
Understand the multidimensional nature of globalization, with particular 
 
2
emphasis on its cultural and social dimensions. 
• 
Examine the effects of globalization at both individual and societal levels. 
• 
Develop nuanced and balanced views of Korean culture—often taken for 
granted by Koreans and frequently misunderstood by foreigners. 
• 
Critically question commonly held beliefs and stereotypes about Korean culture 
and society in light of global transformations. 
• 
Analyze the key dimensions and major trends of Korean society, especially those 
shaped by globalization. 
• 
Develop the ability to compare Korea’s experience of globalization with that of 
other societies, identifying similarities and differences. 
• 
Explore pressing social challenges in Korea, including gender inequality, 
population aging, and urban overcrowding, while considering potential solutions. 
 
 
III. REQUIRED READINGS  
Kim, Andrew Eungi, ed. 2018. Korean Society: An Introduction. Seoul: Korea  
 
University Press 
 
Recommended Readings 
Ritzer, George and Paul Dean. 2019. Globalization: The Essentials, 2nd Edition. Sussex:  
 
Wiley-Blackwell. 
 
Note: The assigned “Required Readings” are not typically covered in lectures, as 
class time is devoted to instructor-prepared materials. Nevertheless, you are 
expected to be familiar with the readings for both the midterm and final exams. 
 
 
IV. REQUIREMENTS AND EVALUATION 
1. Class Attendance (10% of the final grade) 
Attendance will account for 10% of the final grade. For each unexcused absence, points 
will be deducted from the final grade. Missing a class, for example, will lower your 
final course grade by 3%, etc. As required by the Ministry of Education, moreover, you 
will automatically fail the course if you miss more than one-third of the classes. 
 
2. Midterm Exam (45% of the final grade)  
The midterm is intended to assess your understanding of the content covered in the first 
 
3
half of the course. The midterm exam will cover material from Weeks 1-7 and will 
cover lecture materials and assigned readings from those weeks. At least one-fifth of 
the exam questions will be selected from the required readings. The format of the 
exam is essay questions, both short and long. 
 
3. Final Exam (45% of the final grade) 
The final exam is intended to assess your understanding of the content covered in the 
second half of the course. The final exam will cover material from Weeks 9-14 and will 
cover lecture materials and assigned readings from those weeks. At least one-fifth of 
the exam questions will be selected from the required readings. The format of the 
exam is essay questions, both short and long.

Overview
Why do some countries go to war while some states maintain a 
relatively peaceful relationship with other countries? This 
course explores conditions of interstate conflicts and peace 
using interstate conflict literature. This course begins with a 
scientific study of war with a brief history of the scientific 
study of war. After that, students will learn the systemic and 
individual approaches to studying wars. As the class progresses, 
students will learn how to understand interstate disputes and 
wars more objectively based on data analysis. Also, we will 
discuss how international relations will change.

 ‘가깝고도 먼 나라 일본’. 일본의 꼬리표처럼 따라다니는 오래된 문구입니다. 여전히 우리에게 일본은 지
리적 거리는 가까우나 심리적 거리가 먼 나라이지요. 일본은 어떤 나라일까? 일본의 문화는 거만해 
보이기도 하고, 비굴해 보이기도 합니다. 상냥하게 느껴질 때도 있지만, 답답하게 여겨질 때도 있습니
다. 이러한 일본문화가 좋던 싫던 일본은 우리와 지리, 경제, 역사 등 여러 분야에서 얽혀 있기에 일본
문화를 이해한다는 것은 우리에게 이득입니다.
 본 강의는 미묘하게 우리와는 달라 혼란스럽게 느껴지는 일본의 문화를 체계적으로 정리해 나가고, 
역사적으로 왜 이러한 문화가 발달했는지를 고찰해 보겠습니다. 지금까지 일본에 무관심했던 학생에게
는 일본문화와 역사에 대한 새로운 정보를 제공할 것이고, 이전부터 일본에 관심을 가지고 있던 학생
에게는 학문적 즐거움과 더불어 일본인과의 문화적 교류에 적용할 수 있는 스킬을 제공할 것입니다.  
다음 3가지에 초점을 두고 강의를 진행합니다.
첫째, 아스카시대(飛鳥時代, 6세기말)부터 일본을 지탱하고 있는 ‘화(和) 사상’에 대해서 설명할 수 있다.
둘째, 원칙 문화(일관성 문화), 구분문화(개인주의 문화), 고맥락 문화, 결속 문화(반복확인형 문화), 축
척 문화 등, 일본의 문화 패턴에 대해서 이해할 수 있다. 
셋째, 일본문화의 장단점을 이해하고, 타문화에 대한 시야를 넓혀 국제적 감각을 익힐 수 있다.
필수 선수과목은 별도로 없습니다. 
일본어에 대한 어학지식이 없어도 수강할 수 있는 역사문화 강의입니다.

개요
 
이 수업은 AI 시대의 리터러시(Literacy)—읽기·쓰기 중심의 문자 리터러시에 말
하기·듣기를 결합한 체화된 리터러시—를 핵심 역량으로 삼는다. 단순한 정보 해독 
능력을 넘어, 텍스트와 세계를 함께 읽고 쓰며, 토론을 통해 지식과 권력의 작동을 
비판적으로 성찰하는 비판적·관계적 리터러시 형성을 목표로 한다.  
 이를 위해 인문·사회·과학의 관점에서 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰과 실천적 가
치를 종합적으로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하며 미래의 변화에 
대응할 수 있는 토의·토론의 학습 환경을 구성한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 
비판적·융합적·창의적 사고를 촉진하고, 새로운 관점에서 문제를 제기하고 타인과의 
소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 지향점으로 
삼는다.  
 이 수업은 플립트 클래스(Flipped Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방식으
로 운영되며, 질문 중심 학습(QBL: Question Based Learning), 함께 읽기,  
토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다. 학기 말에는 포
럼과 아고라의 형식을 통해 탐구 결과를 공유하고 성찰을 확장한다.

개요 
본 과목의 전반부에는 국제 거시경제학을 공부한다. 국제수지 회계, 환율 결정, 거시경제 
정책이 환율에 미치는 영향, 환율 제도 등을 다룬다. 이러한 주제들을 다루는 
국제거시경제이론들은 “글로벌 비즈니스 환경”으로서의 세계경제가 어떻게 작동하고 
진화하는지 이해하는 데 유용한 사고의 틀을 제공한다. 본 과목의 후반부에는 외환 및 
파생상품 시장에 대한 주제를 다룬다. 외환과 관련된 금융 파생상품에 대한 지식을 
바탕으로 기업이 외환 리스크를 피하기 위해 다양한 헤지 활동을 하는 방법을 공부한다. 본 
과목은 상당히 분석적이며 특정한 사례보다는 개념에 중점을 둔다. 미래의 경영자로서The 
Economist, The Wall Street Journal and The Financial Times 등 세계유수의 경제지를 읽으며 
국제거시경제환경에 대한 최신정보를 흡수하는 능력을 키우는 것 또한 본 수업의 
목적이다. 
교과서 
1. Krugman, P., Obstfeld, M., and Melitz, M. International Economics: Theory and Policy 
(12th edition, Pearson, 2022) 
2. Shapiro, A. C. and Moles, P. International Financial Management (Wiley, 2015)  
 
참고문헌 
1. Bekaert, G., Hodrick, R. J. International Financial Management (3rd edition, Cambridge 
University Press, 2017) 
2. 이환호, 김성은 공저 외환론 (제3 판, 경문사, 2024) 
3. 최생림 외환론 (7 판, 박영사, 2021) 
4. Krugman, P. Return of Depression Economics and the Crisis of 2008 (W.W. Norton, 
2009) (역서: 불황의 경제학, 세종, 2015) 
5. Eichengreen, B. Exorbitant Privilege (Oxford University Press, 2012) (역서: 달러제국의 
몰락, 북하이브, 2012) 
6. Prasad, E. S. The Dollar Trap (Princeton University Press, 2014) (역서: 달러트랩, 
청림출판, 2015) 
7. Rogoff, K. Our Dollar, Your Problem: An Insider’s View of Seven Turbulent Decades of 
Global Fiance, and the Road Ahead (Yale University Press, 2025) (역서: 달러 이후의 
질서, 윌북, 2025)

준비사항 
본 과목을 수강하기 위해서는 거시경제학에 대한 경제원론 수준의 기초지식이 필수적이다. 
기초지식이 취약하다고 생각하는 학생들에게는 경제원론 교과서의 거시경제 부분을 다시 
일독할 것을 권한다.

성적산출 방식  
 
수업참여: 강의 출석은 필수이며, 출석점수는 최종성적의 10%를 차지한다. 출결확인은 
지정좌석제와 seating chart를 활용하여 매 시간 진행된다. 지각 3회는 결석 1회에 해당하며, 
결석이 3회를 ‘초과’할 경우 최종 성적은 자동적으로 F 처리된다 (예: 결석 4회, 또는 결석 
3회 + 지각 1회의 경우 F 처리 대상임). 지각 및 결석 시에는 출석점수에서 감점이 적용되며, 
해당 감점은 최종성적에 반영된다. 취업 관련 인터뷰나 인턴십 등은 출석으로 인정되지 
않으며, 가족 경조사, 질병, 예비군 훈련, 학교 공식행사 등으로 인한 결석은 증빙서류 제출 
 
3
시 출석으로 인정된다. 질병의 경우, 진단서, 통원확인서, 입·퇴원확인서 등 질병 사실을 
확인할 수 있는 공식 서류를 제출해야 한다. 출석인정 관련 서류는 반드시 조교에게 
이메일로 제출해야 하며, 포털 상의 출석인정 신청만으로는 인정되지 않는다. 
 
수업태도: 본 수업에서는 수업시간에 스마트폰을 사용하는 것을 금지한다. 수업시간에 
스마트폰을 사용하는 것이 발견되었을 때마다 최종학점은 한 단계씩 낮아진다.  
 
중간시험: 최종 성적의 40%에 해당하며 중간시험을 결시하는 경우 최종학점은 
자동적으로 F를 받게 된다. 
 
기말시험: 최종 성적의 50%에 해당하며 기말시험을 결시하는 경우 최종학점은 
자동적으로 F를 받게 된다. 
 
최종학점은 협상의 대상이 아님. 최종학점이 공지된 이후에 근거가 없는 학점조정을 
요청하는 이메일은 보내지 말 것.

Objectives 
This course aims to empower students with the technical and 
intellectual abilities to participate in the global academic environment. 
 
In Academic English, we develop critical thinking, academic writing, and 
speaking skills with a focus on writing paragraphs and discussion.  
 
AI Policy 
 
(LLMs, 
ChatGPT, 
Papago, etc) 
This class balances ethical AI use with the development of students’ 
independent research, creative and technical abilities. 
 
          You may use AI tools to:  
• Research information or examples. 
• Find reliable academic sources. 
• Translate individual words. 
 
          You may not use AI to:  
• Generate whole essays, assignments, or presentations. 
• Provide essay or presentation outlines. 
• Translate entire essays or presentations into English. 
 
Submitting AI-generated work as your own will be treated as plagiarism. 
 
Resources 
PDF content will be available online for download and use in class. 
Students can either print the content or access it in class with a laptop 
or tablet (not a smartphone, please). Bring materials to take notes. 
 
Class 
Approaches 
This is an English Only class.  
 
If you are absent, please review what we covered in class. Students 
are expected to complete homework / assignments set in their 
absence. 
 
To maintain a positive and productive study environment, please treat 
your classmates and professor with respect. 
Lateness/ 
Absences 
Late 3 times = 1 unexcused absence 
More than 15 minutes late = absent 
 
If you are late for class, please let me know after class so that I can 
change your attendance record to “present”, otherwise you may be 
marked absent. 
 
Students are permitted 2 unexcused absences without penalty. 
Further unexcused absences will affect your attendance grade. 
Students missing 6 additional classes (8 absences in total) without a 
valid reason will receive an F.  
 
If you are absent but have a valid reason (death in the family, hospital 
stay, serious illness) please send me the relevant document within a 
week of your absence and submit requests for absences through the 
KU portal. Absences for periods/military obligations are permitted 
within reason. 
 
Please tell me at least a week in advance (after class or by email) if 
you have a class trip, military day, or other pre-planned reason to be 
absent from class. 
 
Plagiarism  Students who copy and resubmit another student’s work must rewrite 
their assignment and will have their score for that assignment reduced 
by 50%. 
 
Copy/pasting material from the internet without citation is 
unacceptable and will lead to either grade reduction (depending on 
the severity of the plagiarism) or an instant F. 
 
Do not use Papago to translate your assignments or ChatGPT (or any 
other AI) to write them. 
 
Late 
Assignments 
Late assignments will receive a deduction of -3 points and an additional 
-1 point for every day after the deadline. 
 
Course 
Grading 
Final grades for this class are assigned based on these categories: 
• (40 points) Narrative Paragraph  
• (40 points) Graded Discussion  
• (40 points) Midterm Quiz  
• (40 points) Final Quiz  
• (20 points) Attendance (-1 point per unexcused lateness, -3 points 
per unexcused absence) 
• (20 points) Participation (Students start with 10 points. Points can 
be earned by asking/answering questions in class, actively 
participating in class discussions, completing homework to an 
acceptable standard and being kind. Points can be lost by not 
participating in pair discussions, being unprepared for class, not 
submitting homework, etc.) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Final grades are awarded on an absolute grading scale according to 
the total points achieved in the categories above. 
 
Please let me know at the start of the semester if you require a 
specific minimum grade for a scholarship or military reason.

PROFESSOR: Kihoon Kim 
EMAIL: kihoon@korea.ac.kr 
PHONE: 3290.2621 
OFFICE HOURS: By appointment 
 
TEACHING ASSISTANT: Jaeduk Kim 
TA EMAIL: jaeduk3119@korea.ac.kr 
 
 
 
DESCRIPTION  
 
In today’s increasingly global and competitive economy, businesses are striving to use analytics (i.e., the 
use of data, together with statistical and quantitative models, to make better, data-driven business 
decisions) to gain competitive advantage. Yet, there is still a significant shortage of business analysts and 
project managers who are adept at effectively utilizing analytics to create substantial value to an 
organization by solving impactful business problems. 
 
The use of business analytics has exploded and become pervasive in small and large businesses. 
Business analytics now drives ticket pricing, retail assortments, movie recommendations, digital 
marketing campaigns, healthcare scheduling, crime fighting, social media investments, capacity decisions 
and more. Today, companies generate an immense volume of transactional data, capturing trillions of 
bytes of information about their customers, suppliers, and operations. Millions of networked sensors are 
embedded in the physical world in devices such as computers, mobile phones, smart energy meters, 
automobiles and industrial machines that sense, create, and communicate data. In a digitized world, 
consumers communicate, browse, buy, share, and search, creating extensive trails of valuable data. 
 
In this course, students are introduced to the foundations of business analytics. The course is designed to 
teach business managers how to use data and models to make better decisions in complex business 
settings. Note that a good outcome does not imply a good decision. A good outcome may simply be a 
matter of luck, and, conversely, a bad outcome is not always evidence of a bad decision. students will 
develop sound reasoning skills and learn how to utilize information to arrive at good decisions.  
 
 
OBJECTIVES 
 
To be an intelligent user of analytics, a manager must be able to: 
 
• 
Identify analytical structure in complex decision problems 
• 
Understand the role of uncertainty and risk in the decision-making process 
• 
Analyze available data to understand relationships among variables and create predictions 
• 
Understand the trade-offs involved in any decision 
• 
Use available computing technology (e.g., R, Radiant, and Excel) to arrive at better solutions 
 
To equip you with these skills, several analytical methods will be covered including: 
 
• 
R introduction 
• 
Decision analysis 
• 
Data visualization

Case Studies 
 
There will be 4 ~ 5 case write-ups worth a total of 25 percent of your grade. One report per team should 
be handed in at the beginning of class on the day we cover each case. It is recommended that you keep 
a copy for your own reference during class. The goal of each case study is for you to discuss the case in 
detail with your team and then together agree upon recommendations. These recommendations should 
be backed by solid arguments and analysis.  
 
A case write-up should consist of (i) a memo that is no more than two single-sided pages of text, and (ii) 
up to six pages of supporting documents (charts, figures, calculations, etc.). The memo should not have 
any calculations and be written in a managerial style that clearly articulates your recommendations.  
 
 
 
 
Exams 
 
There will be two exams for this course. The exams will be open book, open notes. However, you may 
not communicate with anyone or seek help from any third party during the exam. You should have 
Radiant and Excel Solver working on your laptop in order to solve some of the exam questions. 
 
Class Participation 
 
Your class participation grade is based upon your contribution to class discussion, case presentations, 
and familiarity with required readings.To prepare for class you should fully complete the required readings 
and assignments. You should strive to be an active participant during class and contribute to the quality of 
the discussion. Please note that the frequency of your interventions in class is not a key criterion for 
effective class contribution. On the other hand, attendance is a factor in your ability to contribute to the 
learning environment. Based on these criteria, a class participation grade between 0 and 10 points will be 
assigned.

1. Course Description 
 
The human body is embedded in communities with particular attributes such as collective lifestyles and 
health practices, population-based health programs, economics, health services, built environments and 
social characteristics. Those communities are embedded within contexts of the natural environment, 
culture and politics, which all exist within a particular place and time in history. These upstream factors 
influence health and physiologic underpinnings of disease. This course is thus intended to provide an in-
depth introduction to the major conceptual frameworks of social determinants of health and empirical 
research examining social factors that influence individuals’ health and illness. This course examines the 
social causes and context of health, illness, death, longevity, and health care. 
 
In this course, we will consider how social scientists, epidemiologists, public health experts, and doctors 
address them—how they use theory to understand them and how they make causal inferences based on 
observational or experimental data. However, students are not expected to have in-depth knowledge of 
social science methods or statistics. The readings span the medical, public health, and social science 
literatures, and they reflect both quantitative and qualitative approaches. 
 
2. Learning Objectives 
 
Upon the successful completion of this course, students will be able to: 
• define and elaborate on major concepts in social determinants of health and health inequality; 
• describe the best ways to measure each social determinant, including strengths and weaknesses of 
existing measures; 
• explain the state of the evidence on causal associations between the social determinants addressed 
in class and health, including gaps in knowledge; 
• describe plausible mechanisms by which social factors may influence health; and 
• understand and synthesize practical policy interventions that could be effective at reducing social 
disparities in health

과목 개요 및 설명 
제조 중심의 산업 시대에는 창업을 위해 막대한 설비·자본이 필수였지만, 지식 경제로 전환된 오늘날에는 
아이디어·팀·디지털 도구만으로도 사업을 시작할 수 있다. 여기에 생성 AI 까지 대중화되면서 진입장벽은 한층 
더 낮아졌다. 덕분에 기하급수적 성장을 노리는 스타트업은 물론, 1 인 기업(솔로프러너)까지 누구나 창업자가 될 
수 있는 시대가 도래했다. 
본 과목은 실제 스타트업 비즈니스를 '0'에서 시작하여 '1'을 만들며 성장할 수 있는 초석 쌓기를 목적으로 한다. 
사업의 기회는 어떻게 발견하는지, 지속 가능한 성장을 만들기 위한 비즈니스 모델과 수익구조는 어떻게 
설계해야 하는지에 관한 기본 이론과 함께 유니콘 스타트업들에 대한 케이스 스터디를 병행한다. 더불어 다양한 
분야의 전문가 강의를 통해 기업 경영을 위해 필요한 지식을 쌓는다.  
스타트업은 한 사람의 출중한 능력으로 완성되는 것이 아니라 훌륭한 팀의 긴밀한 협업과 노력에 의해서만 
성장할 수 있다. 따라서 아이디어 발견부터 성장 가능한 모델을 설계하는 스타트업 비즈니스 디벨롭핑 과정을 
팀 단위로 수행하도록 함으로써 스타트업 비즈니스 실전 경험을 하도록 한다. 이 수업을 통해 지식 강화 뿐만 
아니라 미래를 스스로 창조하는 앙트러프러너로서의 역량, 그리고 팀 빌딩과 팀 워크를 통해 '업'을 키워나가는 
과정에 실질적인 도움을 얻도록 한다. 
 
학습 목표 
ü 일상의 관찰을 통해 문제의식을 가지고 지속적으로 아이디어를 발견하는 능력을 키운다. 
ü 스타트업 비즈니스란 무엇인가를 이해하고 고객 중심 관점을 통한 스타트업과 모든 신사업을 시작하고 
성장시키기 위한 요소와 방법론을 체득한다. 
ü 경영학에서 배우는 다양한 요소들이 실제 스타트업을 시작하고 성장시키는 과정에서 어떻게 
작동하는지 이해하고 적용하는 능력을 키운다. 
ü 팀으로 함께 스타트업을 이루기 위해 필요한 커뮤니케이션 능력을 함양하여 함께 성과를 이루어낸다.

평가 내용 및 방법 
출석 
출석은 매 수업시간 체크. 2 번 지각은 결석 한번으로 처리됨. 15 분 이상 늦을 시 지각으로 간주. 3-4 번 결석시 
성적이 한 단계 내려감 (예, A->B). 5 번 이상 결석 시 자동으로 F 처리됨. 취업관련 활동으로 수업에 참여하지 
못할 때에도 예외 없이 결석으로 처리됨. 중간 고사나 기말 시험을 대체하는 어떠한 종류의 보충 시험이나 
보고서가 없음을 주지할 것. 학교에서 공식적으로 인정하는 사유를 제외하고, 시험에 빠질 시에 시험 점수는 
0 점 처리됨. 
팀 
팀 스킬은 사업을 위해 꼭 필요한 요소임. 팀 성공을 이끌어내고 기여하는 정도에 따라 팀 성적과 개인 성적이 
결정됨. 조직과 마찬가지로 팀은 구성원으로부터 자원과 경쟁력을 끌어오게 됨. 멤버들 간 각각의 역량을 
고려하여 팀 내 활동을 배분할 것이며, 팀 배정은 다양성을 고려하여 이루어질 것임 (예: 경영학과 학생 + 타 
대학 학생). 이를 통해, 팀 구성은 실제 사업을 런칭 시키는데 도움이 되도록, 다양한 경력과 멤버쉽을 기반으로 
이루어 질 것임 (개인의 선택에 의한 구성이 아님). 팀 발표는 oral 과 written presentation 으로 나누어 점수를 
매기게 됨. 
팀 구성원 간 평가  
팀 구성원간 평가에서 좋은 평가를 받기 위해서는 책임감을 가져야 함. 자주 의사소통하고, 모임에 참여하고, 
맡은 임무를 시간 내에 완수하고 또한 팀 활동을 성공적으로 이끌도록 노력할 것. 팀 내 구성원이 가진 자원을 
최대한 활용하도록 할 것. 모든 멤버가 서로 경쟁하는 것이 아니라 서로의 부족한 부분을 보완하는 것이 
중요함. 다면평가의 결과를 바탕으로 팀 구성원들은 개개인이 다른 평가 점수를 받게 됨. 
 
3 
평가  
(성장 마인드셋) 스타트업 비즈니스는 창업자 그리고 팀의 의지와 노력에 따라 엄청난 변화를 이끌 수 있다. 
주도적인 변화의 마음가짐, 즉 성장 마인드셋이 갖추어졌을 때, 팀과 사업 모두가 끊임없이 성장을 이룰 수 
있다. 따라서 이 강의에서는 실제 스타트업 경영자로 성장하겠다는 열정에 기반하여 필요한 스킬을 배우며 
성장하려는 마인드셋이 중요하다. 
(몰입과 주도성) 기본적으로 수업시간 동안 다루고 접하는 자료와 지식에 대한 평가와 팀 단위 프로젝트 
수행과정과 결과에 대한 평가가 종합적으로 이루어짐. 따라서 매 수업에 대한 몰입도와 적극적 참여도가 평가에 
중요한 영향을 미치게 됨. 만약 학생들의 수업 관련 성과가 저조할 경우 개선해야할 부분에 대한 피드백을 받게 
될 수 있음.  
(평가 방법) 강의와 토론을 통한 수업 진행이 일반적이지만, 팀 단위 프로젝트 수행 또는 발표 등도 수반될 수 
있기 때문에 다각적인 평가가 이루어질 수 있음. 구체적인 평가 내용은 다음과 같음.

COURSE OVERVIEW 
 
 
 
◼ 
Course Objectives 
 
Marketing involves the study of institutions and business activities designed to plan, 
price, promote, and distribute products and services to current and prospective 
consumers. By understanding customer needs and analyzing competitors, a 
marketing-oriented firm identifies its target market’s preferences and strives to deliver 
superior satisfaction more efficiently than its competitors. This course aims to equip 
students with a comprehensive understanding of fundamental marketing concepts and 
their practical application across various contexts. It also serves as a foundation for 
students intending to pursue advanced marketing courses. 
 
 
 
◼ Course Format 
 
This is a hybrid course, with approximately half of the sessions conducted via lecture 
recordings and the other half in person. It is your responsibility to check the course 
schedule and attend in-person classes. Course schedules are provided in syllabus, and 
any changes will be notified in advance. 
 
Students must watch the lecture recording and be familiar with the content before 
attending the classroom sessions. I will cold call and ask questions about the materials 
taught in recordings, and your responses will count toward your final grade. To 
benefit fully from the classroom sessions, it is crucial to come prepared by watching 
the recorded lectures in advance. The recording file will be uploaded on LMS before 
the class time.

Both Midterm and Final will be in an in-person format.  Anyone not being able to 
attend the exams physically cannot take this course. The exams are closed book and 
closed notes and they will cover lectures, textbook, and class discussion. Final exam 
will be noncumulative. 
 
2. Attendance & Participation (15%) 
You are expected to attend in-person classes. Class attendance will be checked 
regularly. It is recommended that you prepare thoroughly for each class since the 
quality of your contribution is directly related to your preparation for class. There may 
be some individual- level assignments involving finding real-world examples/cases 
related to the topic discussed in the class. 
 
3. Group Project & Presentation (25%) 
Students are required to complete a group project. You will form a group with peer 
students (Individual works are not permitted) and work on solving marketing 
problems. The objective of this project is to provide you with the opportunity to apply 
the concepts and methods of marketing learned in this course to a real-world 
marketing problem. Your term project should detail the marketing strategy for a new 
product or service that you deem viable in today's market; or an ailing product or 
service, whose performance in the market you think can be improved with the help of 
a new marketing program (Specific Guideline can be found in the “Group Project 
Guideline” posted in the LMS).

the company, the competitive environment, and the consumers (i.e., SWOT 
analyses)

-

- 
Marketing Mix Strategy: Detailing of the recommended marketing strategy, 
including a discussion of the 4Ps

wait until the deadline and I will assign a group for you. Please submit a group 
roster by 3/25 (Wed). Regardless of whether you have a complete group or not, you 
must submit the roster by this date. 
 
Presentation/Report: The work will be presented in the class on the 14th week. All 
teams must submit their PPT file to LMS by 9PM on 5/31 (Sun). The note section in 
the PPT file should contain detailed descriptions/comments for the corresponding 
page of the slide. No separate report (write-up) is required, and your project grade will 
be based on the comments in the PPT note section. 
 
Peer Evaluation: To stimulate equal contribution of all group members, there will be 
a peer evaluation at the end of the semester (i.e., you will evaluate each member of 
your group based on the contribution he/she made throughout the semester). This peer 
evaluation score will be incorporated into the final project grade for the individual 
member. Remember, while you are submitting one work for the group project, scores 
can vary by members based on peer evaluation. Download the “Peer Evaluation” 
sheet from “Group Project” folder and submit it on the last day of the group

audience involved. Audience will evaluate your work and presentation. This audience 
evaluation score will account for 50% of your presentation grade (5% of the group 
project). The audience evaluation criteria are listed on the “Audience Evaluation” file 
in the “Group Project” folder. Please take a look at the evaluation criteria before 
preparing your presentation. The evaluation criteria are listed in the "Audience Evaluation" 
file in the "Group Project" folder. The audience evaluations must be submitted in class on 
each presentation day.
