2026 Spring BUSS313(5) International Business 
 
Jongik Chang 
FYI: Last semester, 14.28% of students in this course received an F,                               
so please enroll only if you can commit to its high workload and continuous engagement. 
 
Korea University Business School 
BUSS313 (5) – International Business (English) 
Spring Semester, 2026 
 
1. General Information 
Lecture time: Monday and Wednesday (3), 12:00-13:15 
Classroom: LG-Posco Business Hall #107 
 
2. Instructor Information 
Lecturer: Jongik Chang, Ph.D Candidate 
Office: KUBS Main Building #417 
E-mail: jongikchang@korea.ac.kr 
Office Hours: 14:30 pm to 16:30 pm on Wednesday & Thursday (by an appointment) 
 
3. Course Description 
The boundary of competition has been expanded globally more and more, not 
only multinational firms, but also even small domestic firms would face global level 
competition nowadays. Moreover, current global-level events such as war situations 
(Russia-Ukraine war, Israel-Hamas & Iran war, US-China trade war, China-Taiwan 
tensions, etc.) recent trade related turmoil such as U.S. reciprocal tariffs, 
heterogeneous central banks’ policy to overcome Covid-19 shock in their economies, 
and de-globalising movements (Post-Brexit and Make America Great Again), 
escalated the uncertainties significantly and called into questions our previous 
understanding of international business. Thus, it is paramount for business experts to 
have international minds, perspective, knowledges, and absorbing capabilities to deal 
with those uncertainties and opportunities in the international business environments. 
The purpose of this course is to introduce the concepts and theories related to 
the international business environments and to construct the strategy [1. To compete 
others and 2. To work with people who comes from different backgrounds]. Some 
renowned analysing tools will be taught, which were developed to help managerial 
decisions for the multinational firms in the business field.  
To improve the understanding of the theories; concepts; and analysing tools, 
there will be many case studies (Mainly Harvard Business Cases) from real world and 
team discussions. Team-based activities would be helpful to practice working with 
other colleagues who have different backgrounds (nationalities, cultures, etc). Some 
activities will be evaluated by both individually and team-based scheme. Peer 
evaluation would be applied either for the last group projects. 
2026 Spring BUSS313(5) International Business 
 
Jongik Chang 
4. Course Objectives 
a. To explain the impact of globalisation for the domestic firms, multinationals, and 
global firms (including platform businesses) 
b. To understand the national differences in various criterions such as political; 
economic; institutional; and cultural environments and to evaluate those 
differences by using appropriate analysing tools. 
c. To understand the international monetary systems and the foreign exchange risk, 
and how to deal with the risk by firm-level decisions. 
d. To formulate the international business strategy based on the firms’ managerial 
situations based on the analysis of external market environments (uncertainties) 
and internal capabilities. 
e. To examine the real successful entering strategies and failure cases to develop the 
capabilities to consult the international firms and to suggest alternatives with the 
professional views. 
f. To practice team-based activities and business reporting 
 
Textbook: Global Business Today – International Student Edition (After 12th edition) 
Written by Charles Hill, Published in 2021 by McGraw Hill   
 
5. Grading (Total: 110 points) 
Criteria 
a. Class participation: 15 points 
b. In-class HBS case study (team-based): 15 points 
c. Mid-term exam (Off-line and closed book): 25 points 
d. Final exam (Off-line and closed book): 25 points 
e. Group projects-Report and presentation (team-based): 30 points 
*Below 50/110 points: F without exceptions (14.28% in last fall semester) 
 
a. Class participation: 15 points 
Class attendance will be checked only for counting the minimum requirements 
of attendance by the rule of KUBS (at least 2/3 for the classes). 2 tardy or early leave 
will be equivalent for 1 absence. For the class participation evaluation, individual 
students would be awarded class participation points in accordance with their active 
engagements during the lecture, such as raising the meaningful questions, suggesting 
other perspectives, answering with students’ own analysis, etc. During the group 
projects sessions, students who conduct good comments and discussion with other 
teams’ presentation would be awarded class participation points too. Feel free to raise 
your voice during the class for your colleagues and yourself!  
2026 Spring BUSS313(5) International Business 
 
Jongik Chang 
b. In-class HBS case study (team-based): 15 points 
We will do one simulation session (Harvard Business Simulation) and one 
discussion session (Harvard Business Case Study) based on team-basis during the 
class. Moreover, each team is responsible to submit 2-pages team report at the end of 
the same week. During the session, it would be recommended to voluntarily share 
their ideas with other classmates. The points would be awarded by both participation 
during the class and the quality of the report. These points would be team-based. 
 
 
 
*Team building (5-7 personnel in each team) 
 
 
The team members would be determined by the instructor’s rule (minimising 
sample selection). All students will be divided into some categories according to their 
(1. seniority of the student ID numbers; 2. Business major or non-business major; and 
3. Korean or foreign students). One or two students from each category will be chosen 
by randomly to compose each team (5-7 personnel in total). Then, these activities 
would be conducted by team based: 1. In-class case study discussion (15 points) and 
2. Group projects-report and presentation (30 points, final sessions of this class). The 
number of team members could be changed depending on the total number of enrolled 
students, but the fundamental rule of team building would not be changed. 
 
 
The purpose of this team building is to practice conducting team-based task in 
real business world for the students. It would be rare to work with your close friends 
or same age peers only in the real field after the graduation. Therefore, it is a good 
opportunity to work with juniors and seniors who do not have personal relationship in 
advance. But I hope that all teams would show fantastic teamwork on their reports and 
presentations at the end of the semester. 
 
c. Mid-term exam (Off-line and closed book): 25 points 
The mid-term exam includes multiple choice questions; True or False 
(penalties to choose the wrong answers); filling the blank (less than three words); and 
short essay questions based on the materials from the lecture. The purpose of mid-
term exam is to evaluate the level of understanding the contents of the lectures. The 
brief feedback of mid-term exam results would be provided at the first class after the 
mid-term period.  
 
d. Final exam (Off-line and closed book): 25 points 
The final exam includes same types of the mid-term exam and several long 
essay questions, which would be practical cases in real world, to evaluate the students’ 
capability to use all the analysing tools and knowledge from the lecture. The important 
evaluating scheme of the final exam would be your analysing capability, logical 
thinking and persuading ways based on your perspectives and ideas.  
 
2026 Spring BUSS313(5) International Business 
 
Jongik Chang 
e. Group projects-report and presentation (team-based): 30 points 
Each group would select one country from the designated continents from the 
class. Analyse the business environments of the country by using various framework 
and tools which they have learned from the lectures. And evaluate the firm’s entry 
strategy with one successful case of global firm and one failure case of another firm. 
(Two firms do not have to compete in the same industry). The contents should include 
additional strategy for the successful case to enhance their competitiveness and 
alternative strategy for the failure case (As similar to the consulting report). 
20 points would be awarded to group presentation. Group presentation would 
take 25 minutes for each team (20 minutes presentations and 5 minutes Q&A 
discussions) and at least two team members should be speakers of the presentation. 
Time limit is important, therefore exceeding 25 minutes presentations would deduct 
points for presentation. Q&A time could be expanded flexibly by the instructor. Active 
participation of Q&A discussions would be recommended; both individual and team-
based points will be awarded depending on your engagements.  
10 points would be awarded to group report. It would include core materials 
of the group presentations and some feedback from the presentations in class. The 
reports would not exceed 10 pages using single spaced (Times New Roman 11 font 
size with one-inch margins all around), and there is no minimum requirement. It must 
include appropriate citations for the sources. Tables, charts, and other visual aids would 
be recommended for readers to understand the report better. References and appendix 
would not be included in 10 pages limit. The deadline of the group report would be 
announced by the instructor. Late submission will seriously deduct the points assigned 
for the group report. Peer evaluations will be applied for individual grades. 
*Important: All group reports would be analysed by the ‘Turn-it-in’, 
plagiarism tool. Over 20% relevance result would be regarded as plagiarism in the 
academia, so please keep in mind that your reports should be less than 20% relevance. 
It would be highly recommended to conduct using ‘Turn-it-in’ before submitting the 
report. You could access this program from Korea University Library. Please refer the

Course Overview 
Hanbok is a comprehensive term for traditional dress that offers a glimpse into Korea’s distinctive 
culture and national heritage. It is one of the tangible heritages that most vividly reflects the history, 
philosophy, and aesthetics developed over 10,000 years. This course provides an opportunity to explore 
the intricacies of traditional Korean attire, fostering a comprehensive understanding across dimensions 
such as history, culture, philosophy, aesthetics, craftsmanship, and design.  
 
This curriculum combines theoretical insight with practical experience, allowing students to not only 
understand the subtle nuances of Korean traditional dress, but also apply them to their own creations. 
By connecting theory and practice, this course enables students to create meaningful cultural content, 
such as fashion products, inspired by Korean culture. 
 
The broader purpose of this course is to enhance students’ empathic communication, interdisciplinary 
thinking, and creative problem-solving skills, and to develop them into global leaders who are prepared 
to navigate the complexities of a constantly evolving world. 
 
Course Objectives 
1. Gain insights into the origins, evolution, cultural significance, and global recognition of Hanbok. 
2. Explore the philosophical and aesthetic foundations inherent in traditional Korean attire. 
3. Comprehend the distinctive features and intricacies involved in crafting traditional Korean dress and 
related craftwork; apply this knowledge to plan and craft cultural products inspired by these traditional 
items.

Ÿ
안과는 안구와 안구 주변에서 일어나는 병적인 현상을 주 대상으로 하며 미세 수술기구와 
레이저 등의 발달로 나날이 치료 영역이 확대 되어 가는 과이다. 안구의 특성상 타과와 구
별 되는 진단기구와 진찰 방법 등이 이용되며, 따라서 고도의 전문성과 기술이 요구되는 
과이다.
Ÿ
구로병원 안과는 의학적인 면에서 수준 높은 진료를 하는 것 외에도 환자들이 진료에 만족
하고 다시 오고 싶은 안과가 되기 위해 부단히 노력하고 있으며, 각 Staff는 안과의 각 분
야를 독립적으로 분담하여 연구하고 있고 국내 안과 발전에 중추적인 역할을 하고 있다.
Ÿ
녹내장, 백내장 (강형주 교수)
1) 녹내장: 개방각 녹내장, 폐쇄각 녹내장, 선천 녹내장, 정상 안압 녹내장, 고안압증 
2) 녹내장 환자의 정밀 검사 (시야, 시신경, 안압, 전방각경 검사 등) 
3) 섬유주 절제술 등 수술적 치료
4) 레이저 홍채 절개술 등 레이저 치료
5) 백내장: 노인성 백내장, 선천성 백내장, 외상성 백내장 
6) 백내장 초음파 유화술
Ÿ
성형안과 (백세현 교수)
1) 눈물길 폐쇄: 내시경과 LASER을 이용하여 외부에 수술 흉터를 남기지 않고 누도를 만
드는 누강비강 문합술 시행
2) 안검하수: 선천성 혹은 외상에 의해 생긴 눈꺼풀 처짐을 교정 
3) 안검 성형: 눈썹 찌름, 안검 내반, 안검 외반, 쌍거풀 교정, 흉터제거

4) 안와내 혹은 안검 종양 절제술
5) 안와골절 정복술
6) Botox 주사, PERLANE 주사 
7) 인공안구 삽입술: 최신 움직이는 의안 수술

Ÿ
임상실습을 모두 마친 학생은 다음 사항을 할 수 있어야 한다.
1) 시력을 결정하는 안구 및 안구 외 구조의 기능을 설명할 수 있다.

2) 급성과 만성 시력이상의 발생 원인을 각각 설명할 수 있다.
3) 시력장애가 있는 사람에게서 원인 감별을 위해 적절한 병력청취를 할 수 있다.
4) 시력장애가 있는 사람에게서 시력확인을 위한 눈 진찰을 할 수 있다.
5) 시력장애가 있는 사람에게서 외안부검사, 검안경검사, 시야검사를 시행하고 그 결과를 
설명할 수 있다.
6) 시력장애가 있는 사람에게서 응급치료가 필요한 경우를 선별하고 적합한 치료계획을 세
울 수 있다.
7) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 외상성과 비외상성 원인을 구분할 수 있다.
8) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 감염질환과 비감염질환을 구분할 수 있다.
9) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 병력청취와 신체진찰을 통해 원인과 중증도를 평가할 수 있
다 (시력저하, 눈손상).
10) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 검안경검사를 통해 망막출혈과 망막박리 여부를 판단할 수 
있다.
11) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 세극등 검사와 안압검사가 필요한 사람을 골라낼 수 있다.
12) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 원인에 따른 적합한 치료계획을 세울 수 있다.
13) 충혈눈이 있는 사람에게서 시력장애 예방을 위한 대책을 세울 수 있다.
14) 시력저하와 눈손상이 있는 사람에게서 적절한 조치를 적시에 취할 수 있다.
6. 학생활동
1) 교수님 외래 특진시간을 참관하고 수술실에서 안과 수술을 직접 관찰한다.
2) 환자의 병력 청취에 참여한다 (History taking)
3) 일과 시간 후 안과 당직 선생님의 수술 예정 환자 진찰에 참여하여 본인이 수술실에 함
께 들어가는 경우 사전에 환자에 대하여 충분히 숙지한다.
4) 응급실 환자의 진료를 참관한다.
5) 안과 진료 및 수술 중 발생할 수 있는 환자 안전사고에 대한 내용을 숙지한다.
예) 감염성 결막염의 외래에서 병원내 감염 예방에 대한 수칙
일회용 검사장비 및 수술장비 사용 원칙 및 과학적 근거
시력 저하 환자 및 시야 감소 환자에게 적용해야할 안전 수칙의 차이
안질환 및 그에 따른 시기능 저하의 단안 혹은 양안 이환에 따른 차이
고령 환자 수술을 위한 환자 수술 전후 병실 및 이송 중 낙상 예방에 대한 수칙

1) 출근은 8시 30분까지 안과 외래로 하며, 퇴근은 다음날 수술 예정 환자의 검사가 끝난

대로 한다. (다음날 해당 part 수술이 없을 경우 5시 귀가)
2) 안과는 관찰이 대부분의 실습을 차지하므로 실습 중간에 질문을 많이 하고, 적극적으로 
실습에 임한다.
3) 단정한 복장과 예의 바르게 환자와 선생님들을 대하며, 예비의사로서의 바른 자세를 유
지한다.
4) 실습 첫 주 월요일에 반드시 발표할 주제를 지정 받도록 한다. 주제는 안과 증상에 따른 
접근 방법, 진단, 치료에 대한 내용으로 각자 모두 다른 주제로 한다. (분야: 시력 저하, 
충혈, 안구 통증)
5) 각 분과 별 교수님의 외래 진료와 수술을 참관하며, 안과적 질환에 대한 전체적인 개념
을 익힌다.
6) 안과 검사 및 안과기구 실습 시간에는 직접 시야검사, 산동검사, 굴절검사, OCT 혹은 
GDx 중에 일부를 검사 받아 본다.

안산병원 안과는 이 화 교수(성형안과), 하석규 교수(사시 및 소아안과), 윤철민 교수(망막), 
박지혜 교수(녹내장), 안소민 교수(망막)가 각 분야의 전문의들이 자신의 분야를 독립적으로

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

1. 강의 개요  
이 강의는 심리철학 입문 교과로, 분석철학의 전통에서 제기되는 심리철학의 주요 쟁점과 
입장들을 공부한다. 수업의 전반부에서는 마음의 본성에 대한, 특히 “심신 문제”에 대한 다양한 
견해들을 살펴볼 것이다. 후반부에서는 “의식의 문제”와 “물리주의”를 중심으로 한 형이상학적 
쟁점들을 집중적으로 살펴볼 것이다.  
 
2. 수업 목표 
1) 수업의 일차적 목표는 심리철학의 기본적 쟁점과 주된 입장들을 이해하는 것이다. 
2) 강의를 통해 학생들은 논의의 중심이 되는 1차 문헌들을 비판적으로 읽고 자신의 생각을 
명료하게 표현, 전달하는 능력을 기른다.  
3) 자신의 입장을 짧은 논문의 형식에 맞게 논증의 형태로 구체화시키는 훈련의 기회를 
갖는다.

  수업에서 읽을 자료는 pdf 파일로 게시판을 통해 제공될 것이다. 
 
4. 강의 진행 
Ÿ 강의의 상당 부분은 교수자가 해당 쟁점과 이론을 설명, 강의하는 방식으로 진행될 
것이지만, 수업의 일정 부분은 토론식으로 진행한다.  
Ÿ 모든 수강생들은 각주 할당된 글을 “미리” 읽고 수업에 참석해야 한다. 분량은 많지 
않을지 모르나 내용이 압축적이고 때로는 난해한 글(그리고 때로는 번역본이 아닌 원문)을 
매주 읽을 것이며, 수강생들은 해당 문헌을 두 번 이상 꼼꼼히 읽은 후 그에 대한 자신의 
생각을 말할 준비를 하고 수업에 참석해야 한다.

수강생들은 수업 내용에 대해 궁금한 점이나 할당된 글을 읽고 이해가 가지 않았던

Office Hours 
10:00am - 11:00am on Monday and Wednesday. If these times are not convenient for you, you 
can send me an email to make an appointment, or just stop by my office anytime. 
 
Content 
This course is designed to provide an introduction to industrial organization in food industry 
with an emphasis on the theoretical and empirical tools used to analyze imperfectly competitive 
market. This course deals with firm behavior, market structure, pricing strategies, entry and 
exit, vertical relationships, etc. Students who complete this course should be comfortable with 
analyzing firm behavior and market structure. 
 
Course Objectives 
The objective of this course is that students learn to understand food market and its structure 
in terms of economic theory and be comfortable with the subjects as an economist. 
 
Textbooks 
There is no required textbook for this course, but the following textbook is useful for your 
better understanding. 
• Dennis W. Carlton and Jeffrey M. Perloff (2015). Modern Industrial Organization(4ed). 
Boston: Pearson/Addison Wesley. 
 
Grading Policy: This grading policy is tentative, so I will provide detailed information on the 
first day of class. 
• Attendance: 10% 
• Assignments: 10% 
• Midterm exam: 35% 
• Final exam: 45% 
- 
According to this University rule, the number of your attendance days must be greater 
than 2/3 of total number of class days. Your final grade will be “F” automatically if 
you miss more than 1/3 of total class days. 
- 
I will be regularly giving you assignments and occasional quizzes throughout the 
semester.  The purpose of these assignments and quizzes is to facilitate and further 
enhance learning of the materials that we will be covering during the semester. 
- 
The exams will be in-class, closed book and notes. 
 
Attendance and Feedback  
Although it is your decision whether to attend class or not, it is highly recommended that 
regularly come to class and arrive on time. You will learn better through active attendance and 
participation. It is also highly recommended that you provide feedback to me about the course 
since this will help me improve class materials and lectures. You can ask questions in class, 
email me with questions/suggestions, and stop by my office at any time.

Introduction 
 
To be successful in an organization, you need to be a good communicator, be able to 
collaborate with other group members, be a critical thinker, and creative person. 
Organizational Behavior is the study of human behavior in organizations. This course 
provides you an introduction to the various aspects of behavior in terms of basic 
human processes, individual behavior, group dynamics, and organizational processes. 
 
The goals of this course are: 1) to introduce basic concepts in organizational 
behavior in an integrated manner, 2) to discuss concepts in terms of actual 
organizational situations, 3) to convey the excitement and importance of analyzing 
organizational problems. These goals will be accomplished through lectures, 
discussion of current events in the corporate world, and a project requiring you to 
analyze an organization of your choice. 
 
My objective is to make this course both theoretical and applied. My success 
in meeting this objective depends critically on your active participation and 
contribution to the learning process. It is therefore important that you prepare for each 
class by completing the assigned reading and attending class prepared to contribute to 
your learning.

Grading 
 
The final grade for the course will be distributed among the various activities as 
follows:

1. Class Participation (20%)  
Students are expected to attend every class session, complete the assigned readings 
before each class, and be ready to discuss the materials covered in the reading 
assignments. To provide students with ample opportunity to participate, class sessions 
will go beyond a purely lecture mode (e.g., individual and small group discussions of 
case studies, exercises).  
 
2. Group Project (Video-Clip Presentation) (25%) 
The video-clip presentations will be based on group work. Students will form small 
groups (consisting of about 8 members per group, depending on class size). Each 
group will make a 20-minute presentation of one model of leadership. The 
presentation will be composed of (1) a short lecture on the specific leadership model 
assigned to the group, (2) showing a short video sequence illustrating the leadership 
style in action, (3) making connections between the theoretical model and the video, 
and (4) leading discussions on the topic. There will be no written assignment of this 
activity, but each group are expected to upload your ppt file on the blackboard. 
 
The video-clip presentation will be evaluated based on the followings:  
(1) accuracy of the theoretical model and concepts presented  
(2) appropriateness of the video-clip in illustrating the specific leadership model 
(3) application of the concepts to the video-clip  
(4) overall quality of the presentation and discussion 
 
3. Team Member Evaluation (5%) 
Students are encouraged to work effectively with others in a group, 10 percent of the 
final grade will consist of an evaluation made by your group members. Each team 
member will evaluate the other members on their contributions to the group, the 
degree of reliability, motivation, and cooperation with others, and the extent to which 
they are open to other members’ ideas and suggestions. 
 
 
4. Exams (50%) 
There will be 2 exams during the course. The exams will cover theoretical concepts 
and their applications from the textbook and class discussions.

structure and ﬁnancial asset valuation especially focusing on equity and ﬁxed income valuation. The main
topics of the course are arbitrage, portfolio management, equilibrium asset pricing (CAPM), ﬁxed income
securities, and (if time allowed) options.
You are expected to understand valuation formulas and be able to apply them to new problems.
The
appropriate tools necessary for solving these problems will be developed at each stage and practiced in
the homework assignments. The models we will cover have immediate applications and implications for
real-world ﬁnancial decisions. Every eﬀort will be made to relate the course material to current ﬁnancial
news.
Blackboard: The course Blackboard will be the site for all course materials. All information relevant to the
course will be put up on here: powerpoint presentations, problem sets, solutions, sample exams, handouts.
Announcements will be posted throughout the semester.
Prerequisites: Students must be comfortable with statistics, linear algebra, calculus, and microeconomics.
Please review Handouts 0, 9, and 10, and ensure you have a good understanding of the
material or are capable of self-studying it before enrolling in the course. I will not cover them
in the class.
Main Class Material: The main class material are all powerpoint slides that I use in class, handouts with
important material covered in class, problem sets, and practice exams.
Required and recommended readings : The main role of the textbooks is to serve as a source where
you can review lectures. At times BKM is very good and tightly linked to the material I cover. However,
for other topics the link to the material I cover in class is a bit weaker. The textbooks for this class are:
1 “Investments” by Zvi Bodie, Alex Kane, Alan J. Marcus, 13th edition.

are only minor changes between editions. Page and chapter numbers may vary slightly, but this is hardly
a reason to buy a new copy. If you use an older edition it is your responsibility to ﬁnd out the diﬀerences
with the latest edition.

reasons of religious observance or civic obligation will only be made available when the assignment

Welcome to Academic English 1 for Informatics 
Students Spring 2026! (IFLS 800) 
 
Class Delivery: Classes are offline (face-to-face) unless otherwise indicated.  
Class Language: English   Credits: 2   Time Per Week:  2 X 50 minutes (All of KU’s Academic English 
classes are 50 minutes) 
Classroom: International Studies Building, 408B 
Midterm Assessment: In-class Written Test (Problem-Solution Essay) 
Final Assessment: How-to Presentation / Discussion 
 
Instructor: Dr. Ksan Rubadeau, Ed.D.  
Classroom: See KUPID 
E-mail: ksanrubadeau@korea.ac.kr 
Office phone: 02-3290-2945   
Office: Institute of Foreign Language Studies, Room 713 
Office hour: by appointment. Please email me in class to arrange an appointment at a mutually suitable time. I 
would be very happy to meet with you! 
 
Kindly let me know who you are and which class you are in when emailing, and remember to allow at least 24 
hours for a response. Emails received on weekends might not be answered until the following Monday. Emails 
asking questions about assignments and tests should be sent in at least three days before deadlines.  
 
General description and aims: 
The overriding goal of this course is to build up your confidence in using English for several types of academic 
tasks. In order to achieve this, you will be given opportunities to try various tasks and will work towards 
becoming a more autonomous learner by practicing academic skills. By the end of the course, you should feel 
more confident doing the following in English: 
1.​
writing a polite, appropriate email to a professor in English  
2.​
describing problems and persuading readers about solutions related to informatics in an academic 
essay using APA 7th edition referencing style 
3.​
writing and delivering a persuasive elevator pitch 
4.​
creating and delivering an engaging live presentation and leading a discussion 
5.​
critically assessing academic listening content, including information related to informatics 
6.​
participating in academic discussions

and appropriate learning opportunities and 
content

Format: 
English proficiency levels will differ among participants. Therefore, we will focus on building general academic 
skills. Sometimes I will lead workshops and discussions, and sometimes you will be leading. Each class, you’ll 
review a little bit of what you’ve seen before and will keep building up a body of language specific to our class.  
 
Required Materials: 
You are required to bring a pencil, eraser, and a printed copy of our coursebook pages to every class and to 
have access to Google Slides (phone, tablet, or computer). For concentration purposes, we are going to 
attempt to do most classes in Spring 2026 via paper and pencil. You may not take notes on your phone.  
 
In the unlikely event that we need to move to remote learning via online classes, you will need a webcam and 
microphone.  
 
Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Regulations 
●​ Academic honesty is expected. All work you produce will be your own. Copying homework (from 
another person or an AI( or cheating on tests is obviously unacceptable.  
●​ As per Korea University regulations, students caught cheating on any assignments or submitting work 
that includes improperly cited sources will be penalized.  
●​ This class includes referenced research projects. ***Any work containing hallucinated references 
(non-existent citations fabricated by an AI or citations that are mash-ups or one or more real 
references) will be heavily penalized in the rubric category for referencing, and the work itself may be 
considered AI-generated. Check all DOIs and URLs very carefully.  
●​ Wholly plagiarized work will be marked “F.” We will have a refresher lesson to make sure you know 
how to avoid plagiarism before written work. Please note that rubrics for our tasks  
●​ Acceptable generative AI use will be clarified for each out-of-class assignment, and rubrics will reflect 
the need for your writing to be in your own voice. As a rule, anything above the sentence level 
written by an AI or a translation app is not allowed in this class. If you use a chatbot for proofreading, 
be sure not to copy/paste whole documents. Instead, ask specific questions to the chatbot and make 
the fixes yourself.  
●​ You are required to include an AI disclaimer on all submissions clarifying whether generative AI was 
used or not and in what capacity. An example will be shown in our Google Drive 
2 
 
 
●​ Please do not input any Academic English course materials, including course instructions, into an AI. 
These are the instructor’s and Korea University’s intellectual property.  
 
 
Accessibility and Accommodations for Learners with Disabilities: Materials and tasks need to be 
accessible to all the learners in this course. If you need some accommodations for lectures, assignments, or 
exams please feel free to contact me to discuss options at least two weeks before assignments are due. For 
alternatives to assessed tasks due to a disability, official documentation from KU’s Center for Students with 
Disabilities may be required. Note that these documents are not automatically forwarded from the Center, so 
you must notify me directly.  Late penalties will apply to all assignments unless specific 
accommodations/extensions have been discussed and arranged with me in advance of the deadline (barring 
medical emergencies). If your condition involves difficulties getting started on tasks (e.g., some cases of 
ADHD), please see me early for support so that we can strategize together on task completion. For more 
information on support at KU for students with disabilities, please see: 
https://gsc.korea.ac.kr/usr/service/support_center.do 
 
Assessments 
      
Midterm: Problem/Solution Essay: 42%  (15% Draft 1; 25%, Referenced Essay;  2%, Typed) You will 
describe a problem and propose a solution in an in-class APA 7th edition essay about a topic related to 
Informatics. Closed book, paper-and-pencil.  
 
Elevator Pitch (10%) You will practice speechwriting and delivery by pitching your solution in a 90-second 
pitch.  
 
Workshop- Presentation + Discussion (30%) You will deliver a how-to presentation and handle Q and A. 
Then, you’ll lead your table of classmates in an engaging discussion on your topic.  
 
APA 7th Edition Quizzes (10%) You will complete a series of very short in-class closed-book quizzes on 
citing sources and the use of APA 7th edition.  
 
Assorted Weekly Tasks and Participation (8%) 
You will demonstrate learning and share your amazing insights through discussion board posts, uploads, 
classroom activities, and other small tasks, as well as through on-time attendance. You will complete work 
by the deadlines, bring your materials to every class, speak in English during class time, and volunteer 
answers without being called on. Participation and the completion of optional tasks (e.g., worksheets, 
learning journal) may make a difference to your final grade. For example, if your final grade is very close to 
the line between an A and an A+, stellar attendance, class participation, and the completion of optional 
worksheets might be able to lift the grade slightly.  
 
For small homework tasks (unless specified otherwise): 3 points = on time, complete, instructions followed, effort 
demonstrated, 2 points = late same day or incomplete, but there’s still effort, 1 point = handed in the next class, 0 
points = not completed within the time frame.  
      
Attendance: Up to four (4) absences are allowed without them affecting your final score (excused or 
unexcused absences.) No note is required for these; however, an email to me is always appreciated if 
you know you will be absent.

Attendance Grade Deductions: Starting from five (5) absences, 1.5% will be deducted from your total 
final grade for each absence. At eight (8) absences, the grade for the class will be an F (fail).  
 
3 minutes to 19 minutes late = late:  3 lates = 1 absence 
20 minutes+ late = 1 absence 
 
Graded Tasks: Please note that if a graded task occurs in class on the day you are absent, you will not 
be able to make up the points for that task. Please notify me in advance if you have a class in a building 
far away before this one and will be late regularly.  
 
Just as professionals are expected to show up for work, students are expected to come to class 
consistently and on time. While ultimately engagement is crucial, there is also a strong positive 
correlation between class attendance and learning achievement (Lam et al., 2025). At the same time, 
however, learners who are physically present in a classroom but mentally elsewhere are not 
maximizing their learning time. It is hoped that if you are in the classroom, it is because you are there 
to learn.  
 
     Submitting Official Absence Documentation 
At KU, students are generally excused from classes only for the following official reasons: military 
service, family bereavement, hospitalization and/or medical emergency,  or required academic events 
related to their major, including education majors’ practica. If you prefer to have recognition for an 
excused absence, you must submit official documentation through the required process in KUPID’s 
출석인정신청 system and also email me. I will then go into the KUPID system to confirm the absence. 
However, in most cases, the grade deductions starting from five (5) absences or more will still apply, 
except in the case of students receiving special dispensation for early-start military service or an 
education practicum.  
 
Mandatory Attendance Days: If you are late or absent on the days of quizzes, Essay Draft 1, Referenced 
Essay, Elevator Pitch, or your own Student-led Discussion, you will be permitted to make up the tasks if 
there was an immediate medical emergency.  You will not be allowed to make up these assignments 
unless you both 1) contact me immediately and 2) provide official documentation signed by a doctor 
(의사소견서 or 의사진단서, not 진료확인서) that there was a genuine medical emergency requiring

백을 제공받을 수 있고, 질문과 토론 또는 과제를 통해 실습학생을 하여금 실무 능력 및 의료인 직업전
문성을 학습하도록 돕는 교육프로그램임.
◎ 개설배경 및 목적
의학과 3학년의 임상실습은 이론으로 터득했던 의학지식이 진료현장에서 어떻게 적용되고 있는지를 배
우는 시간으로, 학생들은 실습조별단위로 나뉘어서 적극적인 환자 진료 참여를 전제로 진행되지만 현실
적으로 주로 참관 위주로 진행되는 경우가 많았음. 
이 과정에서 각 과의 교육프로그램에 따라 여러 명의 교수님들의 회진이나 외래, 수술을 참관하는 것도 
큰 장점이 있으나 특정 환자를 처음 외래부터 입원, 수술을 지속적으로 관찰하고 진료에 참여하는 것은 
한계가 있었음. 
이러한 점을 보완하기 위해 심화임상실습(서브인턴)과정은 학생들이 관심 있는 과를 선택하여 1명의 담
당 교수님 지도하에 외래, 수술, 입원환자 진료에 참여해서 환자에 대한 일련의 진단, 치료과정을 경험함
으로써 졸업후 1차 진료를 수행할 실무 능력을 배양할 수 있도록 배울 뿐 아니라 세부 전공의 실무에 
대한 이해를 높일 수 있도록 설계되었음.
◎ 구체적 목표
1) 연속성 있고 책임감 있는 진료현장 참여를 통한 의료 실무역량강화
2) 교수-학생 사이 멘토쉽 형성을 통한 전공 심화 체험을 통한 의료인 직업전문성 강화
3) 실무바탕 교육을 통한 자기 주도 학습 역량 촉진 
    
◎ 실습 방법 : 멘토 교수-학생 일대일 clinical attachment
2주 기간 동안 교수 1명에 학생 1명이 배정되어 멘토 교수가 지정해주는 환자의 진료에 적극 참여
(active engagement)하게 됨. 학생들이 1-2명의 환자를 연속성 있고 책임감 있게 진료경험을 할 수 있
도록 지도함.
예1) 정형외과 홍길동 교수와 김슬기 학생 
  김슬기 학생은 홍길동 교수가 배정해준 환자의 수술을 참관 또는 assist 한다 → 환자의 입원기간 
동안 홍길동교수의 밀착 감독 하에 주치 의사처럼 진료에 참여한다 → 환자가 퇴원하여 외래 F/U 
시, 김슬기 학생은 외래에서 환자를 다시 만나고 경과를 관찰한다.

Introduction to Political Science 
Korea University, Spring 2026 
 
 
Class Time & Room: Friday 2-3, Room. 423 (International Studies Building) 
 
Instructor: Dr. Seonhee Kim (seonheekim.politics@gmail.com)  
 
Office Hours: email for separate appointments, for offline and/or zoom meetings 
 
 
Course Description:  
Introduction to Political Science serves as a foundational course, offering students a comprehensive introduction 
to political science as a vital social science discipline. Throughout the Spring semester, the curriculum spans 
essential aspects of political philosophy, comparative politics, and international relations. 
This course is designed to guide students to the fundamental concepts of political science, providing a 
panoramic view of topics such as political theory, ideologies, the evolution of modern states, government 
constitution, political economy, electoral systems, political culture, manifestations of political violence, and 
international relations. By incorporating reading materials from classics of politics, the course aims to equip 
students with the necessary tools to become an enlightened civic mind. 
Course Learning Objectives: 
 
After successful completion of this course, students will expand their understanding of politics and political 
science in general drawing on political thoughts in Western tradition, theories on how a social science 
inquiry is questioned and answered, and finally, different cases of current political systems in the world. 
The primary objective is to instill a curiosity that encourages students to delve deeper into political science 
either through further courses or independent exploration. I hope this course serves as a steppingstone, 
paving the way for students to engage with political science on a more sophisticated and nuanced level in 
subsequent classes down the line.  
This course also seeks to improve critical thinking skills and the ability of students to formulate clear and 
logical written and oral arguments that are supported by sound evidence. We use books, articles, primary 
documents, films, and other in-class activities as learning tools. 
 
 
Required Readings:  
 
o Shively, W.P. and Schultz, D., 2022. Power and choice: An introduction to political science. Rowman & 
Littlefield. (Hereafter Power & Choice) <- Purchase this one, other older versions fine.  
 
Other reading materials are listed on KULMS or available through online/library search 
 
2
Grading and Requirements:  
 
For successful completion of the course, students are expected to follow the guidelines for each grading 
determinants:  
 
Sum: 100%  
Attendance and Participation: 20% 
Film Analysis Essay: 10%  
Midterm Exam: 30% 
Final Exam: 35% 
In-Class Activities: 5 ~ 15% 
 
 
▪ 
Attendance and Participation (20%): Attendance and participation grade will be based on (1) 
attendance records, and (2) active and thoughtful participation in class discussion and activities. 
 
Note that attendance records will automatically place (lower down) your participation grades in the 
grading block according to the number of absences. (Appendix I).  
 
All the in-class activities (including lectures, discussion, activities) assume that students come 
to class having read, understood, and critically analyzed the required readings.  
 
Specifically, students should be prepared to discuss the authors’ arguments, the evidence the authors 
provide, how well the authors’ arguments hold up against alternative arguments dfon the topic, and 
how the readings relate to other course readings. I recommend finishing weekly reading materials by 
the start of the class each week. Please see additional information about evaluation of class participation 
on the back page, including participation if health conditions require inevitable absences (Appendix I). 
 
▪

This essay aims to analyze how such concepts as power, politics, nations, social hierarchies, and the 
relationship between the ruler and the ruled are depicted in film and how these themes connect to real-
world cases. You will choose one of the following films and critically examine its portrayal of power, 
governance, or political values, linking it to historical or contemporary political events, cases, or 
personal experiences.

Phase I: Collective Living, Choice, and Power  
Week 1 ~ Week 4 
 
This Phase I introduces the intellectual foundations of politics—the questions every serious student must 
grasp before moving forward. We will consider the meaning and idea of politics, the nature of political 
power, and how the necessity of collective life imposes collective decisions upon human communities. 
We will revisit ancient philosophers’ reflections on politics, not out of antiquarian interest, but because 
they framed the very problems that remain with us today. From there, we will distinguish the concerns of 
political philosophy from the methods of political science, setting clear ground for the discipline you 
are entering. These are the fundamental stones; without them, there is no path forward in the study of 
politics.

Phase II: The Beginning of the Modern Politics - the State and its Formation 
Week 5 ~ Week 7 
 
 
We turn to the birth of the modern state—the decisive break that marks the beginning of our political 
age. We will trace its origins and functions, distinguishing the pre-modern from the modern, and 
examining the particular historicity of the modern state: the precise conditions and constitutive elements 
that brought it into being. Within this framework, we will ask what politics looks like inside the state, how 
power is organized, and what the state does to—and for—its people. Equally important, students will be 
expected to engage the assigned texts with rigor: to read closely, to think critically, and to form opinions 
that respond directly to the arguments presented. This is not a passive exercise in history, but the training 
ground for disciplined thought about the modern political world.

Phase III: Making Sense of Political Economy and State-Society Relations 
Week 9 ~ Week 12 
 
In phase III, we move to the hard ground of political economy and state–society relations, the terrain 
where theory meets historical and material reality. We begin with the political economy of the state, 
interrogating how money, markets, and state power intersect and mutually reinforce one another, before 
turning to the historical weight of slavery and global capitalism as formative engines of modern 
statehood. From there, we examine constitutions—not merely as legal texts but as codifications of political 
power and societal compromise, with Locke and modern constitutional documents as our guides. Finally, 
we confront the variety of political regimes—democratic, authoritarian, and hybrid—and the ways in 
which states sustain, distort, or subvert the rule of law. Throughout these weeks, students will not only read 
canonical and contemporary texts but also learn to engage them rigorously: identifying arguments, 
interrogating assumptions, and forming their own analytical responses.

Phase IV: A Peek at the Global Politics 
Week 13 ~ Week 15 
 
In the closing weeks, our attention turns outward to global politics, the arena in which states, ideas, and 
power contend on the largest stage. We begin by situating ourselves historically, examining the forces that 
have shaped the making of the twenty-first century, before moving into the theoretical frameworks that 
scholars use to interpret this world: realism, liberalism, and constructivism. Here we read Snyder on 
competing paradigms, Wivel on the security dilemma, and Mearsheimer at his most forceful on the tragedy 
of great power politics, alongside contemporary debates over grand strategy and offshore balancing. Finally, 
we take up the pressing current issues of global politics—those dilemmas of conflict, cooperation, and 
order that will define the century you are now living through. At this stage, students are expected not simply 
to absorb theory, but to wield it: to analyze events, challenge assumptions, and form arguments of their 
own. For those who have followed the course with discipline, this is the moment where the study of politics 
becomes not only an academic pursuit but an intellectual habit of mind.

Course Objective 
 
Brands represent the value offering of the firm and as such is one of the firm’s most important 
strategic asset.  Companies are increasingly becoming aware of the importance of their brand 
strategies, realizing that brand equity is one of their most important strategic assets. The 
brand — and its promise — is a source of value to both the company and the customer. The 
effective management of the product and brand presents the manager however with enormous 
challenges in today’s dynamic business environment.  This advanced level marketing course is 
designed to develop new skills and consolidate prior knowledge and skills learned in other marketing 
courses to develop a proactive brand management approach.  
 
AIMS  
The course deals primarily with an in-depth analysis of a variety of concepts, theories, facts, analytical 
procedures, techniques and models with the development, evaluation, and implementation of 
strategic brand management issues in complex environments.  
 
OBJECTIVES 
At the end of this course you should have an understanding of the following topics: 
 
Branding fundamentals: the importance of branding will be introduced. 
 
Developing a brand strategy:   discuss the roles of brands, the concept of brand equity and the 
advantages of creating strong brands. 
  
Designing and implementing brand marketing programs:  examine the ways to build brand equity by 
properly choosing brand elements, designing marketing programs and activities, and leveraging 
secondary associations. 
 
 
2
Measuring and interpreting brand performance: examine different approaches to measuring brand 
equity and how to implement a brand equity measurement system. 
Growing and sustaining brand equity:  examine different alternative branding, brand extension, and 
market extension strategies to grow and enhance brand equity over time. 
 
 
 
TEACHING AND LEARNING APPROACHES 
 
The lectures will enable students to develop generic attributes of knowledge and problem-solving in 
business through exposure to concepts, theories, tools, frameworks, models and contemporary 
issues/debates on product and brand management.

COURSE CONTENT 
This course is the undergraduate introductory course in child development. The course covers the 
following subject area:  
ㆍ Major theories of child development 
ㆍ Research methods in the field of child development  
ㆍ Biological processes, physical and perceptual development 
ㆍ Cognitive and language development  
ㆍ Socioemotional development  
 
LEARNING GOALS 
In this course, students will gain… 
ㆍ An understanding of major theories of child development  
ㆍ An appreciation of child development research strategies  
ㆍ Knowledge of both the sequence of child development and the processes that underlie it  
ㆍ An understanding of the joint contributions of biology and environment to development 
ㆍ An appreciation of the impact of context and culture on child development

media influences child development.

representative episode or content. The analysis should: 1. address the

discuss both positive and negative influences on at least two

evaluate the content.

심화임상실습 과정 소개 
◎ 정의
예비 전공의로서 관심있는 임상과의 전공의 업무를 파악할 수 있고, 진료업무에 실제적으로 참여하여 3
학년 핵심실습에서 배운 환자진료역량을 심화하는 실무역량 강화 프로그램(work-based learning)임. 인
턴과 달리 담당지도교수(이하 멘토교수)의 close observation 과 supervision을 바탕으로 실시간 피드
백을 제공받을 수 있고, 질문과 토론 또는 과제를 통해 실습학생을 하여금 실무 능력 및 의료인 직업전
문성을 학습하도록 돕는 교육프로그램임.
◎ 개설배경 및 목적
의학과 3학년의 임상실습은 이론으로 터득했던 의학지식이 진료현장에서 어떻게 적용되고 있는지를 배
우는 시간으로, 학생들은 실습조별단위로 나뉘어서 적극적인 환자 진료 참여를 전제로 진행되지만 현실
적으로 주로 참관 위주로 진행되는 경우가 많았음. 
이 과정에서 각 과의 교육프로그램에 따라 여러 명의 교수님들의 회진이나 외래, 수술을 참관하는 것도 
큰 장점이 있으나 특정 환자를 처음 외래부터 입원, 수술을 지속적으로 관찰하고 진료에 참여하는 것은 
한계가 있었음. 
이러한 점을 보완하기 위해 심화임상실습(서브인턴)과정은 학생들이 관심 있는 과를 선택하여 1명의 담
당 교수님 지도하에 외래, 수술, 입원환자 진료에 참여해서 환자에 대한 일련의 진단, 치료과정을 경험함
으로써 졸업후 1차 진료를 수행할 실무 능력을 배양할 수 있도록 배울 뿐 아니라 세부 전공의 실무에 
대한 이해를 높일 수 있도록 설계되었음.
◎ 구체적 목표
1) 연속성 있고 책임감 있는 진료현장 참여를 통한 의료 실무역량강화
2) 교수-학생 사이 멘토쉽 형성을 통한 전공 심화 체험을 통한 의료인 직업전문성 강화
3) 실무바탕 교육을 통한 자기 주도 학습 역량 촉진 
    
◎ 실습 방법 : 멘토 교수-학생 일대일 clinical attachment
2주 기간 동안 교수 1명에 학생 1명이 배정되어 멘토 교수가 지정해주는 환자의 진료에 적극 참여
(active engagement)하게 됨. 학생들이 1-2명의 환자를 연속성 있고 책임감 있게 진료경험을 할 수 있
도록 지도함.
예1) 정형외과 홍길동 교수와 김슬기 학생 
  김슬기 학생은 홍길동 교수가 배정해준 환자의 수술을 참관 또는 assist 한다 → 환자의 입원기간 
동안 홍길동교수의 밀착 감독 하에 주치 의사처럼 진료에 참여한다 → 환자가 퇴원하여 외래 F/U 
시, 김슬기 학생은 외래에서 환자를 다시 만나고 경과를 관찰한다.

□강의개요
1980년대이후급격한과학의상업화로인해과학기술을둘러싼상황이크게바뀌고있다.
과학기술과사회의관계가고도화되고GMO와인공지능등신흥기술(emerging technology)

과학
(post-normal science)의양상을띠고있다. 특히COVID19의발발과백신을둘러싼갈등에
서나타나듯이첨단과학기술의발전과전개양상은사회적불평등과정의문제와직결되어
과학기술의시민참여를비롯한과학과민주주의의깊이있는논의를요구하고있다. 이수업
은수강생들이융합적사고를통해사회적문제해결능력을함양하는것을목표로삼는다.
이런점을고려하여수강생은이론적, 실증적, 실험적기반에서과학과민주주의문제에접
근하고참여한다. 특히, 행위자-연결망이론(ANT)이제시하는새로운정치생태학을고찰하
고, 그실험모델인, ‘사물의의회(Parliament of Things)’를학습한다. 이를바탕으로사물의
의회실험을직접기획하고구성하여수행해본다. 이로써비인간으로민주주의를확장하는
문제에대한경험적견해를형성한다.

1주차: 강의안내, 민주주의: 신화와역사사이에서
고대사회에서민주정은소망이었고놀이였다. 그것은전혀현실성이없는것이었다. 어떻게
민주정이현실정치체계가되었나? 과학은민주정의대상인가?
2주차: 근대과학(1) 전쟁과거대과학, 테크노사이언스
전쟁과거대과학그리고테크노사이언스(techno-science)는현대과학의특징을잘표현한다.
과학이이론을기술이응용을담당한다는전통적이분법은오해를부른다. 오히려기술적
프레임워크가과학을배치한다.
3주차: 근대과학(2) 생명과학, 생명기술정치, 생명자본
20세기가장성공한과학분야는생명과학이다. 인간이생명원리를통제한다는기대가높아
졌다. 생명기술은국가통치와공진화했다. 근대국가는생명기술을토대로강력하고효율적인
통치체제를유지할수있었다. 순종하는주체덕분이다.
4주차: 근대과학(3) 약물사회
SF <멋진신세계>는‘소마’를보급하면서사회질서를낙관적으로유지한다. SF 디스토피아
는먼미래가아니라이미와있다. 우울증과같은질병진단이크게증가하고있다. 대머리
도환자로간주된다. 건강보조제는점점특수해지고있다. 약물소비량이급격하게증가했다.
약과병원처치는간단하게우리를정상화시켜줄것인가?
5주차: 퀴즈1, 팀활동(주제토론)
6주차: 기술의윤리(1) 인공지능과윤리
인공지능은아주짧은시간동안에우리일상을바꾸고있다. 인공지능의성능을약속하는
장밋빛비전이유행한다. 거의아무도반론을내지않는다. 학교와생산현장은무너질것인
가? ‘윤리없는지능’은작동하나? 균형을조정하기위해서무엇을할것인가?

과학기술은거대해졌고, 지구차원의재난을불러왔다. 개인의현명함이나역량으로회피할
수없는위험에직면하고있다. 기후위기가현실화되자사람들은기술로생긴이문제를다
시새로운기술로해결할수있다고믿기시작한다. 기술결정론와자동화신화를제거하는
것이민주주의확장에결정적이다.

강의 개요 
본 강의는 언어학 이론이 실제 세계에서 어떻게 적용되고 활용될 수 있는가를 이해하며, 
언어적 현상과 비언어적 현상 사이의 복잡한 관계를 탐구한다. 동물은 어떻게 의사소통을 
하는가에 대한 질문에서 강의를 시작하여 인간이 의사소통하는 방식을 구어, 수어, 문자로 
나누어 상세하게 살펴본다. 다음으로는 개인 차원으로 초점을 옮겨서 시간의 축을 따라서 
인간이 언어를 습득하는 과정과 노화와 함께 언어가 상실되는 과정을 탐색한다. 다시 사회 
차원으로 초점을 이동하여 언어가 나타나고 소멸하는 과정을 알아보면서 언어 사용에 시간과 
다른 요소들이 어떻게 얽혀 있는가를 이해한다. 마지막으로 언어학과 인접한 심리학, 병리학, 
사회학에서는 언어와 관련된 어떤 문제에 관심을 갖고 연구하고 있는지를 톺아본다.  
수업 목표  
 이론 언어학과 응용 언어학을 구분할 수 있다.  
 응용 언어학의 하위 분야의 연구 대상과 연구 주제를 설명할 수 있다.  
 이론과 응용, 이론과 실제 사이의 복잡한 관계를 이해하고, 인간의 언어 사용을 통합적인 
시각으로 바라볼 수 있다.

스포츠사회학 강의계획서
Sociology of Sport
1st Semester, 2026
Department of Physical Education, Korea University
Hours: 12:00-14:45 on Fridays at 운초우선교육관 407
Instructor: Prof. Seung-Man Lee
1. Outline
본 강의는 학생선수들이 매일 경험하는 스포츠 현장을 사회적 맥락 속에서 비판적으로 이해하고 해
석하는 능력을 기르는 데 목적이 있다. 스포츠사회학은 스포츠가 정치, 경제, 미디어, 젠더 등 다양
한 사회 구조와 상호작용하며 형성되는 복합적인 현상이다. 이에 따라 학생들은 구조기능주의, 갈등
이론, 상징적 상호작용론 등 핵심 사회학 이론을 토대로 팀 내 역학 관계, 스포츠 비즈니스의 구조, 
선수로서의 정체성 형성 과정을 깊이 있게 탐구한다. 이는 선수들이 자신이 몸담은 세계를 객관적으
로 바라보고, 경기장 안팎에서 발생하는 다양한 사회적 쟁점들을 통찰력 있게 조망하는 훈련이 될 
것이다.
특히 본 강의는 학생선수들이 은퇴 이후에도 스포츠 행정가, 지도자, 마케터 등 다양한 분야에서 주
도적인 역할을 할 수 있도록 역량을 강화하는 데 집중한다. 학생들은 주어진 스포츠 현상을 사회학
적 시각으로 분석하는 과제를 수행하는 과정에서 자신의 관점을 글쓰기로 확장함으로써 전문가로서 
갖춰야 할 비판적 사고력과 커뮤니케이션 능력을 배양한다. 궁극적으로 본 강의는 학생들이 사회학
적 시각과 거시적 안목을 갖춘 전문가로 성장하여, 미래 스포츠 사회를 긍정적으로 변화시키는 주체
적 인재가 되도록 돕는 것을 목표로 한다.
2. Expectations
본 강의를 통해 학생선수들은 스포츠 현상을 사회적 구조 안에서 다각도로 분석하는 비판적 안목을 
갖추게 된다. 스포츠와 연결된 권력, 자본, 미디어의 관계를 이해함으로써 선수 생활 중 마주하는 
다양한 사회적 이슈를 객관적으로 해석하고 성숙하게 대응할 수 있는 지적 토대를 마련한다. 나아
가, 현장 경험을 이론과 결합하여 글로 정리하고 성찰하는 과정은 향후 지도자나 행정가 등 스포츠 
산업 전반에서 활약할 수 있는 논리적 사고력과 전문적 식견을 함양하게 하며, 궁극적으로 사회적 
감수성을 겸비한 주체적인 스포츠 리더로 성장하는 발판이 될 것으로 기대된다.
3. GRADING
1) Attendance & Class Participation (20%)
출석은 이 강의에서 가장 중요한 부분이다. 정해진 수업 시간과 자리를 성실히 지키는 책임감을 강
조하며, 전체 수업의 1/4 이상 결석할 경우 다른 영역의 점수 획득 여부와 관계없이 학점을 부여하
지 않는다. 다만, 선수의 특수성을 고려하여 공식 대회 참가 및 진료확인서를 첨부한 경우에 한하여 
출석으로 인정한다. 이 외의 개인 사유는 출석으로 인정되지 않으며, 매 수업 시간에 임하는 적극적
인 참여 태도 역시 성적 산출의 중요한 지표가 된다.
2) Term Paper (20%)
학생들은 ‘내가 운동하고 있는 스포츠를 사회학적 상상력으로 조망해보고 한 가지 이슈를 찾아 이를 
개선하기 위한 방안’에 대한 과제를 제출해야 한다. 과제 제출 마감일은 5월 31일 23시 59분이며, 
마감 이후 제출하는 경우에도 접수는 가능하나 감점이 적용된다.
3) Mid-term Exam (30%)
중간시험은 강의의 1주차에서 7주차까지 다룬 내용을 대상으로 실시되며, 8주차에 시행된다. 시험은 
다양한 형태(단답형, 서술형, 선택형 등)로 출제될 예정이다.
4) final-term Exam (30%)
기말시험은 8주차부터 13주차까지의 강의 내용을 대상으로 하며, 15주차에 실시된다. 시험의 방식과 
유형은 중간시험과 동일하게 다양한 형태로 출제될 예정이다.
4. TEXTBOOK & READING
1) Main Book : 남상우 (2021). 스포츠사회학. 궁미디어.
2) Sub Materials
- 한국스포츠사회학회 (2021). 스포츠사회학. 레인보우북스.
- 임번장 (2009). 스포츠사회학. 레인보우북스.
- 각 주차별 강의 주제에 해당하는 논문자료, 정책자료, 뉴스 등 다양한 읽기 자료
- 담당교수가 제공하는 PDF 파일
5. How to Do a Term Paper
본 과제는 학생선수가 자신이 몸담고 있는 종목을 사회학적 상상력(Sociological Imagination)으로 
조망하고, 현장의 실질적인 변화를 이끌어낼 수 있는 비판적 사고력을 기르는 데 목적이 있다. 학생
들은 본인이 참여하고 있는 스포츠 내에서 발생하는 한 가지 사회적 이슈(예: 수직적인 팀 문화, 선
수 인권, 학습권 보장, 공정한 경쟁, 스포츠 조직 변화 등)를 선정하여, 이를 사회학적 이론으로 분
석하고 개선 방안을 제안하는 글을 작성해야 한다. 과제는 서론(이슈 선정 배경 및 문제의식), 본론
(사회학 이론을 통한 현상 분석 및 구체적 개선 방안), 결론(선수로서의 성찰과 미래 비전)의 구조로 
구성한다. 글의 명료성, 논리적 구성과 함께, 동료 선수와 스포츠 현장에 실질적으로 기여할 수 있
는 비판적 통찰력을 핵심 평가 기준으로 삼는다. 모든 참고 자료는 출처를 명확히 밝혀야 하며, 전
문 스포츠인으로서 갖추어야 할 정직하고 엄격한 작성 형식을 준수해야 한다. 특히 생성형 AI를 활
용할 경우 0점 차리됨을 숙지해야 한다. 다소 부족하더라도 자신의 언어로 글쓰기를 수행해야 한다.
6. Weekly Schedule
본 강의는 매주 한 가지 사회학적 주제를 바탕으로 스포츠 현장의 이면을 심도 있게 탐구한다. 학생
들은 스포츠사회학의 기초 이론부터 시작하여 몸, 정치, 경제, 교육, 미디어 등 스포츠를 둘러싼 다
양한 사회 구조적 쟁점들을 학습한다. 특히 학생선수로서 직접 경험하는 학교 운동부의 생태계, 젠
더와 계층의 불평등, 지구화 시대의 스포츠 이주 및 일탈(폭력) 문제 등을 사회학적 시각으로 분석
하며, 이를 통해 경기장 안팎의 현상을 비판적으로 성찰하는 힘을 기른다. 매주 진행되는 이론 학습
과 사례 분석은 학생들이 사회학적 감수성을 갖춘 스포츠 전문가로 거듭나는 발판이 될 것으로 기
대한다.

스포츠 속 몸의 의미를 사회학적으로 깊이 있게 성찰하는 기회를 갖게 된다.

과목 개요
수어(Sign Language)의 언어학적 구조와 특성을 탐구하는 과목이다. 수어를 시각-공간적
양식을 지닌 완전한 자연언어로 이해하고, 그 언어학적 체계를 음운,형태, 통사, 의미, 화용의
측면에서 살펴본다. 수어와 구어의 공통점과 차이점을 폭넓게 다루며, 시각적 양식에서 표현
되는 언어로서 수어의 조음 단위와 비수지적 요소, 문장 구조와 통사적 제약, 의미 구성과 개
념 체계, 수어와 제스처의 관계, 사회언어학적 변이, 언어습득과 발달, 농문화의 언어적 기반
등이 포함된다. 인간 언어의 보편성과 다양성을 수어를 통해 이해하며, 수어의 구조를 기술
하고 분석하기 위한 언어학적 관점을 익히게 된다. 본 교과는 수어 실습보다 이론 및 분석 중
심의 과목으로, 수어에 대한 사전 지식이 없어도 수강 가능하다.

I. Course Description 
This seminar is a paper-writing course in empirical microeconomics focused on program and 
impact evaluation. It is aimed at advanced undergraduates who wish to write an empirical micro 
paper using modern causal inference methods. 
 
Throughout the semester, students will: 
1. Develop their own research question, data, and empirical strategy. 
2. Learn and apply core methods for policy evaluation—especially Difference-in-
Differences (DID) and Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). 
3. Receive feedback through individual meetings and midterm and final presentations. 
The final deliverable is a short empirical microeconomics paper that implements a modern 
causal inference method to estimate the causal effect of a policy or program. 
 
II. Course Objectives 
By the end of this course, students will be able to: 
1. Formulate a policy-relevant economics question. 
2. Acquire data and design a credible empirical strategy aligned with their question. 
3. Present their work in a seminar-style talk. 
4. Draft an empirical microeconomics paper by following a structured template for 
empirical writing. 
 
III. Textbooks 
There is no required textbook. Instead, the instructor will share handouts, academic papers, and 
other necessary materials as needed.

출석관련 규정
총 수업시간의 1/3 이상 결석하는 경우 성적을 부여할 수 없음. 단 
담당교수가 불가피한 결석으로 인정하는 경우에는 예외적용 가능
개요
본 과목은 학교 현장에서 학습자들이 발달 과정상 경험할 수 있는 
다양한 주제를 바탕으로 집단상담 프로그램을 기획 및 운영할 수 있
도록 집단상담 이론과 실제를 학습하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 이를 
위해 집단상담의 유형, 과정, 역동 등을 학습하고, 다양성 존중, 공감, 
의사소통, 촉진 기술 등 집단상담 리더로서 필요한 역량을 습득한다. 
또한 학교 현장에 적용 가능한 집단상담 프로그램을 개발하여 이론
을 실제에 접목시키는 과정을 경험하게 된다.

화와 성장이 어떻게 촉진되는지 이해할 수 있으며 이러한 이해를 
실제에 적용할 수 있다.

∙ [출석] 
 -1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가능, 단 
출석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함
∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 학습에 적극적으
로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서 위치를 작가하며 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 
정진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과 약속한 사항을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생들의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 학문적 지식탐구 및 미래 비전과 연결된 교과목 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 미리 교육자료 탐독하고 확인
 -정해진 수업시간에 결석, 지각, 중도 이탈 유의
1. 본 수업은 학습한 이론을 실제에 적용해 볼 수 있도록 실습과 팀 프로젝트로 구성되어 있습
니다. 수업에 참여하는 여러분들이 서로를 존중하는 마음으로 적극적인 참여를 해주실 것을 
기대합니다. 
2. 본 강의의 주차별 계획 등은 수강 인원 등을 고려하여 변경될 수 있습니다. 수강신청 정정 
기간 이후, 최종적인 변경 사항은 LMS 공지사항을 통해 공지될 예정이니 참고 바랍니다.
3. 교생실습을 나가는 학생들도 수강 가능합니다. 단, 교생실습 기간 동안에도 과제는 제출해
야 합니다. 중간고사 기간 진행되는 중간과제와 집단상담 개발을 개인 프로젝트로 진행하게 
됩니다. 단, 별도의 발표는 진행하지 않습니다.

▷ Course Outline 
Prerequisites  Principles of Accounting 
Course 
Description 
This introductory course provides a foundational overview of the core 
concepts, principles, and techniques of managerial and cost accounting. 
Emphasis is placed on the role of accounting information in facilitating 
internal decision-making, planning, and control within organizations. 
Students will gain an understanding of cost identification, classification, 
and allocation methods, and will develop analytical skills to interpret 
internal reports and apply cost data to basic managerial decisions. 
Course  
Objectives 
By the end of this course, students will be able to: 
• 
Identify and classify different types of costs, apply various 
costing methods, and analyze cost behavior to support 
managerial decisions.  
• 
Students will learn to prepare budgets, conduct cost-volume-
profit analysis, and use relevant-cost frameworks for short-term 
decision-making. The course also develops the ability to 
evaluate performance using standard costing, variance analysis, 
and responsibility accounting.  
• 
Through these competencies, students will learn to integrate cost 
information into strategic and operational planning and to 
communicate managerial insights clearly and effectively for 
internal decision-making.

0. Recommended Prerequisite Courses  
 BUSS164 Business for Society  
 
1. Course Overview 
This course is a required course for the Business Administration students. The primary 
objective of this course is to help students grasp the big picture of how various academic 
knowledge learned in the field of business administration can be integrated and applied in 
practical settings. The course will cover four authentic problem situations, both cooperative 
and conflicting types, that encompass major issues in the field of business administration at an 
introductory level, allowing students to explore various disciplines of business studies. 
This course will be conducted using a competency-based, learner-centered teaching method 
that focuses on fostering team-based collaborative problem-solving skills. To address the 
presented problems, students will engage in a series of learning activities, including self-directed 
learning and preparation, team discussions in a collaborative situation, team discussions and 
negotiations in a conflicting situation, and team presentations. The key criteria of evaluation 
include the collaborative attitude and behavior of individuals and teams throughout the problem-
solving process, as well as their level of participation. Additionally, since student absences and 
tardiness can significantly hinder team activities, consistent attendance and active participation 
take a significant portion of the evaluation. 
This course will be delivered in a hybrid Problem-Based Learning (PBL) class format that 
incorporates three different types of classes: 1) Asynchronous Online (AO) class, 2) 
Synchronous Online (SO) class via Zoom, and 3) Face-to-Face (F2F) class. Students are 
strongly advised to review the class format for each session as shown in the weekly course plan. 
Furthermore, to participate in synchronous online class activities, you will need a personal device, 
e.g., desktop, laptop, or tablet, and a quiet place where you can participate in the Zoom discussion.  
 
2. Learning Objectives 
By successfully completing this course, you will be able to:  
• 
Analyze the focal points of problems 
2 
 
• 
Effectively explain team-level perspectives and arguments to others 
• 
Collaborate with others in planning problem-solving methods and procedures, and 
derive solutions 
• 
Collect and analyze various information required for problem-solving 
• 
Communicate effectively with individuals holding different opinions/perspectives 
 
3. Class Format 
 
 
This course consists of four modules, each of which will be presented in a context of an 
imaginary company and its two departments, e.g., finance team and marketing team. Each module 
consists of a total of six sessions in three weeks, except the Korea Office Module which consists of 
five sessions, and follows the sequence of [Self-Directed Learning] → [Group Discussions] → 
[TFT Meetings] → [TFT Presentation].  
• 
Session 1. Self-Directed Learning (AO): In the first session, you will engage in 
asynchronous online learning. You will start with watching two video clips – one 
presenting the problem scenario in the form of a web drama and another providing 
background knowledge – on LMS by yourself. Then, you are required to complete an 
online quiz on LMS, and submit an individual problem analysis report via LMS (template 
available on LMS).  
• 
Session 2. Group Discussion Part I (F2F): In the second session, you will meet with 
your team in face-to-face at Sudang Creative Learning Center to identify the task, discuss 
and decide your team’s perspectives/opinions on the task,  and create a plan (methods, 
strategies, and procedures) for the upcoming events. After the Part I of Group Discussion, 
each team is required to submit the first problem-solving process report by exporting the 
3 
 
Padlet project into a pdf file and submit it on LMS. 
• 
Session 3. Group Discussion Part II (SO): The Third session, you will continue group 
discussion via Zoom in a real-time setting. Each group is supposed to finalize its group-
level solution which is to be presented in Session 4. 
• 
Session 4. TFT Meeting Part I (SO): The four session takes place in a real-time setting 
via Zoom, where two different groups come together to share and discuss their 
perspectives, reconcile their differences, and derive a final solution.  
• 
Session 5. TFT Meeting Part II (SO): The fifth session also takes place in a real-time 
setting via Zoom. Each TFT needs to create a final solution and TFT-level presentation 
materials.  
• 
Session 6. Final Presentation (F2F): The last session, i.e., the sixth session (cf. the fifth 
for the Korea Office Module), will be conducted in a face-to-face classroom setting. In this 
session, you will present the final solution as TFT and receive feedback from the audience. 
Since this course adopts a combination of three different types of class format, it is essential 
for students to understand and confirm the class format for each session.  
 
 
4. Grading and Evaluation 
The grading for this course will be based on an absolute evaluation.

based on the number of absences or being late.

                          문화의 철학적 이해 수업계획서 
수업 개요; 
본 수업은 ‘인간이란 무엇인가’라는 철학적 질문에 대해 문화적 측면에서 접근한다. 다시 말하
면 문화의 본질과 현상을 정치, 경제, 사회적 맥락과 관련하여 철학적 관점에서 고찰하는 것
을 통해 인간에 대한 보다 본질적인 이해를 시도한다. ‘인간이란 무엇인가’라는 질문은 철학에
서 가장 중요할 뿐만 아니라 오래되었지만, 여전히 우리에게 새롭게 다가오는 질문이며 문화
는 이러한 질문을 던지며 답을 찾는 인간 삶의 배경이 되는 모든 것들이다. 인간의 이해와 문
화의 이해는 분리될 수 없다고 할 수 있다. 특히 ‘문화의 세계화’ 시대를 살아가는 우리에게 
문화의 이해는 인간 이해의 중요한 통로다. 
수업 목표; 
본 수업의 우선적인 목표는 현재 우리 문화의 주요 구성 요소들과 관련되는 서양의 주요 문화
를 철학적 관점에서 이해하는 데 있다. 위에서 언급했듯이 ‘문화의 세계화’ 시대를 살아가고 
있는 우리에게 이에 대한 이해는 필수적이다. 이러한 이해를 통해 우리는 지금 여기서 살아가
는 우리 문화뿐만 아니라 그 속에서 살아가는 ‘개별적 한 인간인 나’를 더 잘 이해할 수 있을 
것이다. 이것이 우리의 이차적인 목표다. 본 수업을 통해 우리 각자는 정치문화, 경제문화, 사
회문화와 관련된 주요 논쟁이 되는 주제들에 대한 철학적 이해를 지식으로 배우는 것만이 아
니라 이들에 대해 고유한 시각을 지닐 수 있을 것이다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

▷ Course Outline
Overview
COURSE DESCRIPTION
Information is everywhere and technology is ubiquitous. As a result, all business school
graduates are expected to be able to understand, use, and participate effectively in the design or
acquisition of information systems as part of their future careers for any discipline. One does not
have to be a technology specialist to have an appreciation for the significant and evolving role of
information in today's organizations and our modern society. Tomorrow's graduate, in any
company, public agency, or
2026-1
Korea University Syllabus
association can serve far more effectively and increase their value with an awareness of the
advantages, risks, and trends in business technology management.
This course is designed to provide that broad perspective for all students. Throughout the course,
we focus on the relationship that MIS has across the enterprise and business environment –
people, process, and technology. Most importantly, it includes our everyday life. As such, this
course provides a brief foundation for those who wish to pursue a career in MIS or utilize
information systems in their own preferred discipline, and highlights the relevant relationships to
senior level MIS courses. Additionally, this course will delve into the intricacies of Generative
AI, technologies that have become indispensable in our daily lives and from which we cannot
extricate ourselves. The class provides you with a concrete foundation in information systems
from which you can shape further through formal or informal education streams.
Who Should Take
This Course
This course is ideal for:
1. Business majors seeking to understand the critical role of information systems in modern
business environments.
2. Students interested in the intersection of technology and business who want to learn how
technology is applied to business operations and decision-making.
3. Aspiring data analysts looking to develop skills in analyzing business problems and finding
data-driven solutions.
4. Future IT leaders aiming to develop skills in technology project management and team
leadership.
5. Entrepreneurship-minded individuals who want to leverage technology in their future
ventures.
6. Non-business majors seeking to complement their primary field of study with business and
technology knowledge.
This course is beneficial for any student who wants to develop the ability to understand and
manage information systems in organizations, integrating both technological and business
concepts.

강의개요 
본 과목은 경영대학 신입생들이 고려대학교 경영대학의 교육 목표인 Business for Society - 
Inspiring Next Leaders에 따라 인격과 실력을 갖춘 세상을 바꿀 사회적 리더로 성장할 수 있도록 
경영학의 기본 이론과 다양한 경영학 각 분야에 대한 소개를 제공한다. 근대 경영학 교육의 
시작점에서 Joseph Wharton은 “경영 교육은 우리 문명에 내재한 사회적 문제들에 대한 
해결책을 찾는 것이어야 하며 비즈니스 리더란 사회적 요구에 책임을 지는 공동체의 
건설자이어야 한다”고 역설하였다. 본 과목의 전반부에서는 이러한 교육 철학에 기반하여 
리더십에 대한 고찰, 경영 윤리에 대한 이해, 그리고 기업의 존재 이유에 대한 논쟁들을 
바탕으로 기업과 사회의 관계를 조망하고 이를 바탕으로 기업경영에서 이윤과 사회적 
가치를 함께 추구하는 것이 왜 중요한지, 그리고 어떻게 가능한지를 탐구한다. 경영의 
기능적 구분에 따른 전공별 소개를 다루는 후반부에서는 KUBS의 8개 세부 전공(경영관리, 
회계, 재무금융, IS, 마케팅, LSOM, 글로벌 비즈니스, 전략)에 대한 전공별 소개와 함께 각각의 
세부 전공 범위 내에서 어떻게 기업가치와 사회적 가치가 함께 추구될 수 있을지에 대해서 
알아본다.

ELED 233 
Cross-Cultural Understanding of English-Speaking Cultures 
 
Instructor: Julie Yang  
Office hours: Please make an appointment by emailing me.  
Email: yykjulie@korea.ac.kr / yang.eunkyu@gmail.com  
*Please note: email is the best way to reach me. During normal business hours (M-F, 9am-6pm) I will 
respond to emails within 24-48 hours (probably sooner). If you email me outside of those times or if I give 
you some notice about limited email, it may take me longer to respond. On weekends, I may not respond 
until Monday. If it has been more than 24 hours and you think I may have missed your email, please send 
another. 
 
Description and Objectives of the Course 
What makes one an American? Underlying at the root of the concept of American is the belief in one’s 
ability to “make” oneself into the image of an ideal American, which is inextricably linked with the 
cultural myth of self-invention that underwrites the American Dream. In this course, we will examine 
how various American texts from the founding of the nation to the early 1930s contribute to, challenge, 
and revise our understanding of the American self, and consider how these texts give voice to particular 
social and historical experiences—both individual and national—and how those voices simultaneously 
direct and question the way we read such experiences as “American.” Students will explore how changing 
social and political conditions are reflected in various texts, and how theses texts participate in or question 
the construction of national identity. In this process, we will ponder the ways in which these cultural texts 
both articulate and participate in broader historical struggles to establish the meaning of “America” itself. 
 
In this course, students will learn to: 
 
read representative texts in relation to their historical period; 
 
explain each text’s relationship to the key concepts of that period; 
 
differentiate historical periods, understand how canons evolve, and recognize how periods and 
canons influence how we read in the present; 
 
engage secondary sources while making arguments about texts and their relationships to history. 
 
Required Course Materials and Technology Specifications 
No books are required for this course. All readings will be posted on Canvas. 
 
Coursework and Class Etiquette 
A significant aspect of our coursework includes engaging with other students in the class in either Canvas 
Discussions, Google Doc group work, or other interactive activities. The purpose is to hear different 
perspectives to get a better sense of audience when writing your papers. It also assists with understanding 
the readings better since everyone takes away something a little different from a reading depending on 
their experience. The point is not to advance a particular point of view but rather to unpack what it is the 
authors are saying and how they are presenting the information. Some of the readings include 
controversial ideas and you may read about topics you are not completely comfortable with. Using critical 
thinking is not always comfortable but we can enter this as a “brave space” where we try to examine 
things we don’t always like to think about. To assist with making our interactive space a place where we 
can be brave, every student has a responsibility to make others feel comfortable learning, participating, 
and asking questions. We are all here to learn and work with others, and any activity that runs contrary to 
the spirit of learning and collaboration will not be tolerated.  
 
Careful reading of all assigned texts.  The quality of our classes and the quality of your own experience 
depends upon your having completed the reading assignment before class.  
 
Grading Policy 
1) 3 Reading Journals before Quiz I and 3 Reading Journals after Quiz I: 30% 
i) First three reading journals (before Quiz I): primary sources  
ii) Last three reading journals (after Quiz II): current events  
2) Two Quizzes: 40% 
3) Microteaching Lesson Plan: 15% 
4) Attendance and Participation: 15% 
 
6 Reading Journals. Throughout the semester, you will post a total of 6 short (200-250 words) reading 
journals on Canvas. Your reading journals will be a place to try out and explore ideas concerning our 
readings, lectures, and discussions without worrying too much about being evaluated. The point of the 
journal is to develop a regular, habitual practice of figuring out what you think of our course materials. 
Please feel free to write in the first person. It is a form of free-writing, and it will neither be edited nor 
graded for style and grammar. Possible approaches include: looking at a passage or episode that puzzles, 
moves, or confuses you; connecting this week’s reading with other readings; being self-aware about 
what you are studying and why you are studying it. I also encourage you to connect the course to your 
other classes, books, movies, TV, current events, and your own life experience. Just remember to anchor 
the entry in the week’s reading. 
 
2 Quizzes: The quizzes consist of identification, short answer, and long answer questions.  
 
One Microteaching Lesson Plan. The purpose of this assignment is to gain practice and experience 
developing lesson plans and practice teaching. You will develop a complete lesson plan integrating at 
least one primary source on an assigned topic in American culture.  
*Extra Credit: Up to four students can sign up to “teach” his/her lesson plan to the class. The 
teaching activity should take about 10 – 15 minutes. We will then take time to debrief and discuss. 
Additional prompts for this lesson plan will be distributed during class. 
 
Policy of Academic Honesty  
Plagiarism is the unacknowledged use of another person's labor and presenting it as your own: another 
person's ideas, words, or assistance. In general, all sources must be identified as clearly, accurately, and 
thoroughly as possible. Academic cheating is, in general terms, the thwarting or breaking of the general 
rules of academic work and/or the specific rules of individual courses. It includes submitting, without the 
instructor's approval, work in one course that was done for another; helping others to plagiarize or cheat 
from one's own or someone else's work; or actually doing another person’s work. Of course we do not 
want to discourage you from using other people’s ideas or data. Our aim is exactly the opposite. But you 
must always make clear your sources and you must always be sure that the work you submit is your own.

English for Contemporary Issues, Spring Semester 2026 
Course Number: ENGL 122-02 
Instructor: Jiyeon Hwang 
Class Time: TR (Tuesday and Thursday) (Period 5: 3: 00 p.m. - 4: 15 p.m.) 
Location: 305 Uncho Useon Education Hall   
Office Hour: By Appointment 
Email: mepilope@korea.ac.kr 
 
 
Course Description:  
English for Contemporary Issues is designed to both enhance students’ understanding of the current world 
and improve their English skills by reading English news articles dealing with issues facing the world today. 
Students are expected to read given articles before class to grasp the main events and the main messages 
described in them. In-class activities will focus on discussions based on the given texts and student-posed 
questions. Considering our fast-changing and complex world, this course will cover various issues ranging 
from international politics, economic issues, and social problems to science, technology, and pop culture. 
All students are welcome if you want to expand your knowledge of the current world and improve your 
English fluency through active discussions about various global issues.  
 
 
Course Objectives: 
By the end of the semester, it is expected that  
 
1) Students will increase their knowledge and insight about the current world. 
2) Students will improve their English-speaking ability by participating in class discussions (small group 
discussion and whole-class discussion included) and presentation. 
3) Students will improve their vocabulary and further English reading fluency. 
4) Students will improve their critical reading and thinking skills by formulating critical questions and 
connecting different areas of knowledge. 
 
 
Required Texts: The news articles for each class will be accessible via the course LMS. 
 
 
Grading Rubric: 
1) Attendance: 10%. 
2) Presentation: 10% 
 
3) Class Participation: 20% 
- (Students are expected to actively participate in class discussions and group activities.) 
 
4) Exams (Midterm & Final): 40% (20 % each)  
-(Tentative midterm exam date: April 21) 
-(Tentative final exam date: June 18) 
 
5) Assignments: 20% 
- (Students will primarily formulate critical questions regarding the assigned news topics.) 
 
 
 
 
Note: A detailed class schedule will be announced on the first day of class.

6. 학생활동 또는 실습내용
l 직접 경험
1) 외래 환자 중 신환은 담당진료의가 보기 전 초진을 시행하여 병력, 진찰을 통해 환자의 
문제목록을 작성하고 담당교수와 리뷰한다.
2) 감기 등 담당교수가 판단하기에 일차 진료라고 생각되는 초진환자를 먼저 진료하여 처방
해보고 담당교수나 전공의의 확인을 받는다.
3) 입원환자를 배정받아 주치의 역할을 한다(입원환자를 주치의에게 배정받아 실습이 종료될 
때까지 아침에 직접 환자브리핑을 할 수 있다).
4) 외래환자나 입원환자 의무기록을 POMR에 의거하여 작성한다.
5) 배정받은 입원환자나 외래환자 중 1인을 지정하여 실습기간 이후에도 지속적인 주치의의 
역할을 한다(환자교육자료를 직접 작성하여 제공하고 환자가 가장 먼저 접할 수 있게 한다.)
6) 실습 마지막 날 담당했던 입원환자의 브리핑 또는 조사한 자료를 발표한다.
7) 모의 환자를 진료하는 모습을 촬영하여 환자 진찰과 면담 기술에 대한 자가평가 하고 담당
교원과 동영상을 함께 시청하며 피드백을 받고 내용을 공부한다.
8) Simulator를 통하여 직접 환자에게 수행하기 어려운 진찰을 시행한다 (정맥주사(line  잡
기), 정맥채혈, 내진, 유방촉진, 직장진찰, 피부 봉합 등).
9) 최신 논문 검색을 익히고 1개의 논문을 직접 찾아 점심 집담회에서 발표한다.
발표내용은 배정받은 환자 질환에 관한 것을 권장한다.
10) 아침공부에 참석하고 실습기간 내 2회 교과서 사독을 직접한다.
11) 매일 낮 12시 45분 의국에서 열리는 점심 집담회에 참석한다.

1) 외래참관과 입원환자의 회진에 참여하여 관찰하고 학습한다.
2) 외래에서 시행하는 초음파 등의 시술을 관찰한다.

About the Course
Course description
This course is designed to bridge the gap between physics and mathematics, linking the conceptual understand-
ing of natural phenomena with their rigorous mathematical formulations. The focus is on analytical techniques
involving vector calculus, curvilinear coordinates, linear algebra, and complex analysis, with applications to
classical and quantum systems.
Texbook(s)
• Lecture notes notes written by the instructor will be distributed before each class.
• G. B. Arfken, H. J. Weber, and F. E. Harris, Mathematical Methods for Physicists, 7th Edition, Academic
Press (2012).
• M. L. Boas, Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences, 3rd Edition, Wiley (2005).
Prerequisites
• Power and Taylor series, complex numbers, vectors and matrices, single- and multi-variable calculus.
• Calculus I and II (MATH161, MATH162).
• General Physics I and II (PHYS161, PHYS162).

Helpful tips
While mathematical reasoning and proofs are essential components of this course, it is strongly recommended
to devote sufﬁcient time to solving exercises that model a variety of physical situations. Studying this course
alongside other physics-major subjects is likely to create strong synergies and deepen overall understanding.
Classroom Conduct and Expectations
• Respect for learning environment: Students are expected to maintain a professional and respectful
atmosphere. Please refrain from any behavior that may disrupt the class or interfere with other students’
right to learn.
• Academic integrity: Cheating, plagiarism, or any form of academic dishonesty will result in disciplinary
action according to university policies. Students are expected to complete their own work and properly
cite sources when applicable.
• Use of AI Tools: Students are encouraged to use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) as a supplementary resource
for learning. For homework assignments, AI assistance is permitted provided that the student fully un-
derstands each step of the reasoning and derivation. Submissions that are found to be direct, unmodiﬁed
copies of AI-generated output will incur a substantial penalty, receiving a zero score for that assignment.
Students should also be aware that AI-generated content can contain errors, and verifying the correctness
of all solutions is the student’s responsibility.

료 의사로서의 정신과적 진단, 치료, 재활에 대한 기본적인 수기와 지식을 함양하며, 자신의 임무를 수
행할 때 올바르고 자신 있게 임할 수 있는 소양과 자질을 개발한다. 또한 임상에서 정신과적인 문제에 
봉착할 때 이를 정확히 접근하여 정신건강의학과 전문의에게 의뢰할 수 있는 능력을 배양한다.

4. 과 소개
정신건강의학과는 한국의 정신의학계의 발전에서 있어 중심적인 역할을 해온 역사와 전통을 
자랑하는 과이다. 본과에 실습을 나온 학생들은 정신건강의학과 교수의 지도감독 하에 외래 
환자와 입원 환자에 대해 공부하게 된다. 입원 환자에 대한 학습은 교수, 전공의 등과 함께 
진행되며, 실습 1주차부터 외래신환 예진을 담당한다. 본과의 실습에서 주로 다루게 될 내용
은 정신과 환자의 이해에 대한 것이다.
1) 안암병원
Ÿ
본과의 구조는 고려대 안암병원 본관 81병동의 정신건강의학과 전용 보호 및 개방병동, 본
관 2층의 정신건강의학과 외래와 임상 심리 검사실, 신관 6층의 수면 검사실로 구성되어 
있고, 타과 병동에서 환자를 진료하는 경우도 있다. 현재 함병주 교수, 이헌정 교수, 조철
현 교수, 한규만 부교수, 염지원 조교수, 김수진 임상조교수, 정재권 임상강사, 박지훈 임
상진료조교수가 환자 진료와 전공의 및 학생교육을 담당하고 있다. 병동 치료진은 수간호
사 이하 15명의 간호사와 2명의 병동 업무원으로 구성되어 있으며, 외래 간호사, 사회복지
사 및 사회복지사 수련생, 임상심리 전문가 및 임상 심리 수련생, 수면다원검사 기사가 본
과에 소속되어 진료 업무를 보조하고 있다.
2) 구로병원
Ÿ
본과의 구조는 고대구로병원 9층의 정신건강의학과 전용 보호 및 개방병동 (90병동), 미래
관 5층의 정신건강의학과 외래와 임상 심리 검사실로 구성되어 있고, 타과 병동에서 환자
를 진료하는 경우도 있다. 현재 한창수 교수, 이문수 교수, 정현강 교수, 이승훈 조교수가 
진료와 전공의 및 학생교육을 담당하고 있다. 병동 치료진은 수간호사를 포함한 간호사들
과 병동 업무원들로 구성되어 있으며, 외래 간호사, 임상심리 전문가 및 임상 심리 수련생
이 본과에 소속되어 진료 업무를 보조하고 있다.

6. 실습 시 주의사항
2주간의 정신건강의학과 임상실습은, 이론교육을 통해 습득한 지식을 다시 확인하고 정리하는 
장이며, 환자들을 치료하는 과정을 관찰할 뿐만 아니라 치료에 직접 참여하는 기회를 갖게 된
다. 이 과정에서 실습학생들은 환자들의 마음을 깊이 이해하고 공감하는 능력을 키워야 한다. 
그러나 정신건강의학과 병동은 보호 병동으로 타과의 병동과 동일한 점도 있는 반면에 다른 
점도 많다. 따라서 다음과 같은 사항들을 주의하고 규칙을 준수하여야 한다.
(1) 실습기간동안에 간단한 사물이나 책 등을 놓아두거나 잠깐의 휴식 등이 필요한 경우에 병
동 내에 있는 전공의 의국을 이용한다. 그러나 이곳은 학생들뿐만 아니라, 전공의들도 사
용하는 곳이므로 항상 깨끗하게 사용해야 한다.
(2) 매주 화(안암) / 화, 목(구로) / 화, 금(안산)은 보호자 면회시간이므로, 반드시 면담실을 
비워주어야 한다(이 시간 동안은 자신이 담당하고 있는 환자가 가족을 만나는 상황을 관
