end of each class if they have participated in discussions. A record showing 15 times or more of participating in discussions will earn 
20 points, 14 times 19 points, 13 times 18 points, 12 times 17 points, and so on. 1 time will earn 6 points, none leads to 0 points.  
In-class activities (10%): Students will be expected to engage actively with brief in-class writing and reading exercises throughout 
the semester, as well as small group activities and film screening sessions.  
Attendance (0%): Absences and tardiness will NOT affect your grade. Students do not need to provide documentation for their 
absences, lateness, etc. I will not accept them and will not read emails regarding attendance/absence. The university policy, however, 
mandates students to attend at least 2/3 of the semester in order to get a passing letter grade. This means that students who miss 
more than 10 sessions will get an automatic F. For this I will go over the roster every session.  
 
Plagiarism and Academic Dishonesty: Plagiarism is a serious academic breach. Students must always acknowledge the sources

ENGL 421: The Irish Literary Revival 
 
THIS SYLLABUS IS SUBJECT TO MINOR REVISIONS BEFORE THE FIRST CLASS OF THE SEMESTER. 
Lecturer: Peter McAuley            
Office Time: After every class or  
          by appointment 
Personal e-mail: petermcauley@korea.ac.kr 
Office: 540 Woodang Hall               
 
 
I. Course Description 
 
For an island on the western edge of Europe, Ireland is notable for having produced four Nobel laureates 
during the twentieth century: W.B. Yeats, George Bernard Shaw, Samuel Beckett and Seamus Heaney. 
Several courses in your major already offer opportunities to study these well-known figures within the 
paradigm of “English” literature, but this “special topics” course gives you the opportunity to better 
understand the distinct cultural, historical and political context of Irish literature. 
 
Our course will focus primarily on literary works produced from the end of the C19th to the beginning of 
the C20th. This brief time span was one of the most turbulent and transformative eras in Irish history, as 
the national independence movement eventually led to the end of British rule in most, but not all, of the 
island of Ireland. (As with Korea later in the C20th, Ireland was partitioned into two separate states.) 
During this period, there was also a remarkable flourishing of literary production across a range of forms 
including plays, folklore and poetry that came to be known as the “Irish Literary Revival,” and it is the 
focus of our study this semester. 
 
Poems, plays and stories by writers such as Yeats, J.M. Synge, James Joyce and others will introduce us to 
the main political and aesthetic concerns of this “Revival.” Our readings are divided into three topics that 
will allow us to situate these texts in proper historical and social contexts and better grasp the individual 
writers’ themes, style and concerns. The “Revival” was a powerful combination of literature, culture and 
politics that not only impacted Irish history but also influenced writers and intellectuals from the USA to 
Africa to Korea. Consequently, this course might be of interest to any student wishing to learn more about 
the relationship between nationalism, literature and literary movements.

Reading quizzes will be given on several of our authors/texts prior to our discussion in class.

Participation is not a grade on your personality; rather it is an assessment of your efforts to

4. 과 소개
Ÿ
마취통증의학과: 마취통증의학과는 수술 후 통증, 근골격계의 퇴행성 또는 사고나 스포츠 
손상에 의한 통증 등 급성 통증과 근골격계에서 지속되는 만성 염증성 통증, 신경계 이상
에서 기인한 다양한 신경병증성 통증, 암성 통증 등 만성 통증을 다룬다.
Ÿ
신경외과: 신경외과는 뇌, 척수, 말초신경과 이를 보호하는 두개골 및 척추에 발생하는 다
양한 신경근골격계 질환과 외상에 대하여 수술적 치료를 하는 분야이다. 
Ÿ
정형외과: 척추 및 팔, 다리 관절 및 근 골격계통에 발생되는 병변과 손상을 진료하고 연
구하는 분야로 '완벽한 진단 및 최고의 수술기량을 통한 환자 절대 만족'을 모토로 각 교
수별 전문영역으로 특화된 진료를 제공하고 있습니다. 
Ÿ
재활의학과: 신경근골격계 영역에 대한 재활의학은 크게 뇌졸중과 척수손상을 포함한 중추
신경계 재활, 척추질환과 말초신경, 근육 및 관절 질환을 다루는 근골격계 재활, 신경-근
육계 질환의 진단과 재활에 대하여 전기진단검사·초음파검사 등이 있다.

수 있다.

3) 신경근골격계 문제의 원인에 따른 적합한 치료계획을 수립할 수 있다.

실습 중 학생에게 제공하는 피드백
1) 마취통증의학과: 상하지 통증을 유발할 수 있는 질환에 대한 포트폴리오를 작성 후 담당 
교수와 토의하며 피드백을 제공한다. 외래 참관시 수행한 내용(초진, 이학적 검사, 감별
진단 및 치료 계획)을 담당 교수와 확인하며 토의한 후 피드백을 제공한다.
2) 신경외과: 학생이 예진한 환자의 담당교수 진료를 참관하고, 예진기록 및 진찰소견에 대
해 담당교수와 같이 토의하며 대면 피드백을 제공한다. 실습 중 실시간으로 환자에 대한 
질의응답 과정을 통해 피드백을 제공한다. 실습 종료 시점에 책임교수와 면담하며 피드
백을 제공한다. 회진 참여 후 회진 중 진찰한 환자에 대해 피드백을 한다. 
3) 정형외과: 외래 진료할 때 예진하고 진찰한 환자에 대해 담당교수와 같이 토의하며 대면 
피드백을 제공한다. 학생들이 수행한 CPX 체크리스를 교수와 함께 확인하며 토의한 후 
피드백을 제공한다.
4) 재활의학과: 학생들이 제출한 기본신체진찰(심부건반사, 근력검사, 감각검사) 동영상을 
보고 피드백을 제공하고, 외래에서 문진 및 신체진찰을 했던 환자에 대해 진료 후 담당
교수와 토의하며 피드백을 제공한다. 근력약화에 대한 포트폴리오를 작성하게 하여 실습 
종료시점에 책임교수와 면담하며 피드백을 제공한다.

Basic course information 
 
Students 
❖ College of Politics and Economics, College of Media,  
     College of International Studies

❖ two academic credits

❖ two 50-minute classes per week 
Classroom 
❖ See schedule below

❖ absolute grading

❖ mandatory (according to Korea University’s regulations) 
Language of instruction 
❖ English 
 
 
Purpose of Academic English 
 
1 - To prepare students for taking English mediated courses (EMC) in their major. 
2 - To prepare students to be part of the global community of academia. 
3 - To prepare students for studying abroad in an international-language  
       environment. 
4 - To prepare students to thrive (survive) in a foreign language environment 
5 - To prepare students to be independent learners and thinkers. 
 
 
 
 
 
Academic English focuses on developing students’ academic skills in 
critical thinking, argumentation, academic writing, academic 
discussion and presentation (all in English).  
 
These crucial skills are transferable to any course, any major,  
any language or taught in any country. 
 
 
 
 
2 
 
Evaluation 
 
 
Attendance 
10 % 
Class participation 
10 % 
Assignments* 
80 % 
Total 
100 % 
 
 
 
 
* Includes an academic essay, graded academic discussion and presentation assignment. 
 
Typically, a maximum of about 40-50% of you will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”. Evaluation in 
this class is based strictly on performance, and not on English language proficiency. All parts of 
the evaluation system must be completed in an exceptional manner if you want to get an “A+”.   
 
 
Need Help? 
Getting adjusted to university life can sometimes be tough, dramatic even traumatic, especially 
during a pandemic.  Help is available, however.  The KU Student Counseling Center offers 
help to students having trouble at university or with their feelings. They are very good at 
listening. They have one to one counseling, group counseling, and even some tests people can 
take about their lives, feelings, personality, relationships, and more. During the semester, they 
are open from Monday-Friday from 9 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. (closed for lunch). They are located in 
the 과학도서관 307 호. Tel: 3290-4581~4582. Website: http://kuscc.korea.ac.kr (in Korean). 
 
 
 
 
3 
 
Class Expectations (Please READ CAREFULLY!) 
 
This class is not like your other classes.  It is NOT a lecture class, so you must be 
active instead of passive in this class.  The following are some guidelines for 
conduct that I expect in this class.  Following these expectations will assist in 
enhancing your academic skills as well as improving chances of a good grade.  
 
 
1. 
 
Ask me questions:  This course is about communication, and it is extremely 
important for us to understand each other.  Feel free to ask me at any time to 
repeat or explain something if you do not understand. I am also available in my 
office, Rm 711, by appointment or during my office hours. Please remember that  
it is your responsibility to tell me if there is something you do not 
understand or need help with. 
 
 
2. 
 
You must use English in class: You must try as best as you can to 
communicate all of your thoughts in English.  If you cannot find the correct words 
in English, try to find some other way to express yourself (body language, face 
expressions, drawing pictures, etc.).  Be creative! It is a requirement of this 
course that you use English in this class. 
 
 
3. 
 
Participate actively in the class!  Do not be afraid to speak in class, and do not 
worry about making mistakes.  Incorrect speaking is better than no speaking.  
Perfect English is not necessary, but class participation is necessary.  It is a 
part of your grade! 
 
 
4. 
 
Assignments and projects!  Any assignment or project not ready by the 
assigned deadline will receive a grade of “0”.  If you are absent, make sure to ask 
your classmates or contact me about what you missed.  Copying homework 
(plagiarism) will automatically get you an "0". Any assignments fully created 
with generative A.I. (like ChatGPT) will receive a grade of “0”. 
 
 
5. 
 
Grades!  Although important to you and your GPA, improving your skills in a 
foreign language is not only about grades.  It is a skill that can be life changing for 
your future.  Developing good English language skills can open opportunities for 
employment and future study abroad, it can help you connect to the world beyond 
the borders of your country, and it can enhance your understanding of other 
cultures.  Please view this course as an opportunity to build your future, and 
not simply as an influence on your GPA.  Furthermore, in Korea, English is 
often used as a measure of a person’s value in society, but NOT in this class!   
The grades I assign to you are not an evaluation of you personally nor 
reflective of my likes or dislikes.  It is simply an evaluation of your performance in 
class tasks and activities. 
 
 
6. 
 
Absences!  If you are going to be absent from class for any reason, I will mark 
you as absent for that class, but I allow you 3 absences in the semester 
without any academic penalty.  You can notify me about an absence through the 
Korea University portal, but it will still count as an absence, so use your free 
absences wisely.   
 
- Students missing more than 6 classes will receive a grade of “F”. 
 
 
 
4 
 
 
7. 
 
Be in class on time!  Students who are late are disturbing for the class and for 
me. If you are more than 10 minutes late, I will mark you absent for that class.  If 
you are late 3 times, I will mark you absent for one class.   
- This will NOT count as one of the allowed absences in #6. 
 
 
8. 
 
No distracted sessions!  The use of mobile telephones for communication 
purposes is not allowed in this class.  It is disruptive and rude to other participants.  
Use of cell phones for communicative purposes (including Kakao Talk) will 
result in being marked absent for that class! Use of other devices (laptops, 
tablets, etc.) for communication purposes during class will also result in being 
marked absent. If you are using your phone as a dictionary or for fact checking, 
make it clear to me that you are doing so.  No exceptions. 
 
9. 
 
Textbook materials!  On most days we will be using our textbook materials. All of 
these materials are made available through KU-LMS.  Please make sure you have 
them available for every class.  Repeated failure to do so will affect your class 
participation grade.  Textbook materials can be used in either paper (strongly 
recommended) or digital form. 
 
10. 
 
Bathroom Breaks!  Please use the break time BETWEEN CLASSES for things 
like getting drinks, making phone calls and going to the toilet.  If it is an 
emergency, you do not have to ask me for permission to go to the toilet.  If it is 
not an emergency, you do not have to go! 
 
11. Pay attention to the details!  Students who get A+ in this course tend to be those 
who read instructions carefully, ask me questions, and focus on accomplishing the 
tasks in detail. If you miss something important, refer to #1! 
 
12. 
 
Show respect and courtesy to your classmates!  Please be respectful of your 
classmates and help me to provide a positive and encouraging learning 
environment.  Your enjoyment of this class and the development of your 
academic English skills depend on the attitude you bring to this class every day.   
Please be positive, be polite and be kind.

Purpose of the Course 
 
The purpose of the course is to develop the students’ ability to talk, think, and act on 
marketing management issues with the Business school students’ level competence and 
sophistication. 
 
⚫ 
“Talk” refers to sufficient familiarity with standard concepts and principles of 
contemporary marketing.  Students must achieve the Business school students’ level 
proficiency of marketing terms and principles in discussions of marketing issues. 
⚫ “Think” refers to the ability to analyze marketing problems by applying appropriate 
concepts, principles, and techniques.  This requires that students develop the ability to 
“dissect” a real-world marketing problem using relevant marketing concepts and 
theories and to identify the critical factors driving the solution to the problem. 
⚫ 
“Act” refers to the ability to synthesize various marketing analyses for strategic 
decision making in marketing.  The focus is on the ability to assess the full impact of 
a proposed marketing action as a strategic alternative. 
 
Objectives of the Course: 
 
⚫ 
To introduce you to marketing strategy and the elements of marketing analysis 
(customer analysis, competitor analysis, and company analysis) so that you can 
understand the marketing and business environment in which the firm is operating and 
determine it's major opportunities and problems; 
⚫ 
To familiarize you with elements of the marketing mix (product strategy, pricing, 
advertising, promotion, distribution), and to enhance your problem solving and decision 
making abilities in these operational areas of marketing.  You should be able to develop 
a creative set of alternative marketing strategies and convert a chosen strategic 
alternative into an implementable course of action; 
⚫ 
To present examples of the ways in which firms organize their marketing efforts and 
integrate the various elements of their marketing programs.

과목개요
효율적인학습을위한인간의기본적인인지적, 정서적, 동기적, 발달적, 사회적특
성에관한각종심리학적이론들과원리들을이해하고, 이를토대로AI기반의새
로운패러다임의미래교육현장에서의문제해결방안, 적용가능성및기타문제
점등에대해심도있게논의하고자한다.
수업방식
수업은강의/토론의형식으로진행되므로해당주제에관한교재나기타관련참
고문헌을읽고질문이나토론주제를가지고수업에임하도록하며, 토론에적극
참여할것을권한다. 매주몇가지의주제나질문을웹을통해토론하므로웹을
통한상호작용에도적극참여할것을권한다.
성적
본강좌의성적은총점100점만점으로, 기말고사(30%), On-line 토론(15%), 수업
참여도(15%), 및팀프로젝트(40%)의합으로결정된다.

팀프로젝트
한학기동안배운교육심리학적이론및원리를토대로미래교육현장설계를
제안하는팀프로젝트를완성한다. 우리의교육현장과관련된중요한주제를선정
하여독창적인방식으로문제점을해결하되, 미래교육장면에응용이가능한형태
로제안하도록한다.
이프로젝트의목적은이강좌를수강한학생들만이수행할수있는새롭고창의
적인팀프로젝트를완수하는데있으므로, 기존연구결과를요약하여정리하지말
고, 교육심리학적이론과원리에근거하되직관과상상력을동원하여창의적인문
제해결방안을제시하도록한다.
각학생은5 인으로구성된연구팀을조직하여공동으로보고서를작성하고발표
하여야한다. 3 주차이내로연구팀을구성하여팀의명단을웹에올리고, 10 주차
이내로프로젝트의주제를결정하여웹에올린다. 프로젝트주제를승인받으면프
로젝트를시작할수있다.
무한한상상력을가지고자신만의언어로독창적이고설득력이넘치면서논리적
인데다가감동적인보고서를작성하라.
발표는연구진모두가참여하여야하며, 흥미롭고창의적인방식으로전달하기를
권장한다. 최종보고서의분량은20-30 쪽정도로하고제출기한은학기말시험
전까지로한다.

The overriding goal of this course is to build up your confidence in using English for several types of academic 
tasks. In order to achieve this, you will be given opportunities to try various tasks and will work towards 
becoming a more autonomous learner by practicing academic skills. By the end of the course, you should feel 
more confident doing the following in English: 
1.​
writing a polite, appropriate email to a professor in English  
2.​
describing problems and persuading readers about solutions related to informatics in an academic 
essay using APA 7th edition referencing style 
3.​
writing and delivering a persuasive elevator pitch 
4.​
creating and delivering an engaging live presentation and leading a discussion 
5.​
critically assessing academic listening content, including information related to informatics 
6.​
participating in academic discussions

Format: 
English proficiency levels will differ among participants. Therefore, we will focus on building general academic 
skills. Sometimes I will lead workshops and discussions, and sometimes you will be leading. Each class, you’ll 
review a little bit of what you’ve seen before and will keep building up a body of language specific to our class.  
 
Required Materials: 
You are required to bring a pencil, eraser, and a printed copy of our coursebook pages to every class and to 
have access to Google Slides (phone, tablet, or computer). For concentration purposes, we are going to 
attempt to do most classes in Spring 2026 via paper and pencil. You may not take notes on your phone.  
 
In the unlikely event that we need to move to remote learning via online classes, you will need a webcam and 
microphone.  
 
Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Regulations 
●​ Academic honesty is expected. All work you produce will be your own. Copying homework (from 
another person or an AI( or cheating on tests is obviously unacceptable.  
●​ As per Korea University regulations, students caught cheating on any assignments or submitting work 
that includes improperly cited sources will be penalized.  
●​ This class includes referenced research projects. ***Any work containing hallucinated references 
(non-existent citations fabricated by an AI or citations that are mash-ups or one or more real 
references) will be heavily penalized in the rubric category for referencing, and the work itself may be 
considered AI-generated. Check all DOIs and URLs very carefully.  
●​ Wholly plagiarized work will be marked “F.” We will have a refresher lesson to make sure you know 
how to avoid plagiarism before written work. Please note that rubrics for our tasks  
●​ Acceptable generative AI use will be clarified for each out-of-class assignment, and rubrics will reflect 
the need for your writing to be in your own voice. As a rule, anything above the sentence level 
written by an AI or a translation app is not allowed in this class. If you use a chatbot for proofreading, 
be sure not to copy/paste whole documents. Instead, ask specific questions to the chatbot and make 
the fixes yourself.  
●​ You are required to include an AI disclaimer on all submissions clarifying whether generative AI was 
used or not and in what capacity. An example will be shown in our Google Drive

●​ Please do not input any Academic English course materials, including course instructions, into an AI. 
These are the instructor’s and Korea University’s intellectual property.  
 
 
Accessibility and Accommodations for Learners with Disabilities: Materials and tasks need to be 
accessible to all the learners in this course. If you need some accommodations for lectures, assignments, or 
exams please feel free to contact me to discuss options at least two weeks before assignments are due. For 
alternatives to assessed tasks due to a disability, official documentation from KU’s Center for Students with 
Disabilities may be required. Note that these documents are not automatically forwarded from the Center, so 
you must notify me directly.  Late penalties will apply to all assignments unless specific 
accommodations/extensions have been discussed and arranged with me in advance of the deadline (barring 
medical emergencies). If your condition involves difficulties getting started on tasks (e.g., some cases of 
ADHD), please see me early for support so that we can strategize together on task completion. For more

Assessments 
      
Midterm: Problem/Solution Essay: 42%  (15% Draft 1; 25%, Referenced Essay;  2%, Typed) You will 
describe a problem and propose a solution in an in-class APA 7th edition essay about a topic related to 
Informatics. Closed book, paper-and-pencil.  
 
Elevator Pitch (10%) You will practice speechwriting and delivery by pitching your solution in a 90-second 
pitch.  
 
Workshop- Presentation + Discussion (30%) You will deliver a how-to presentation and handle Q and A. 
Then, you’ll lead your table of classmates in an engaging discussion on your topic.  
 
APA 7th Edition Quizzes (10%) You will complete a series of very short in-class closed-book quizzes on 
citing sources and the use of APA 7th edition.  
 
Assorted Weekly Tasks and Participation (8%) 
You will demonstrate learning and share your amazing insights through discussion board posts, uploads, 
classroom activities, and other small tasks, as well as through on-time attendance. You will complete work 
by the deadlines, bring your materials to every class, speak in English during class time, and volunteer 
answers without being called on. Participation and the completion of optional tasks (e.g., worksheets, 
learning journal) may make a difference to your final grade. For example, if your final grade is very close to 
the line between an A and an A+, stellar attendance, class participation, and the completion of optional 
worksheets might be able to lift the grade slightly.  
 
For small homework tasks (unless specified otherwise): 3 points = on time, complete, instructions followed, effort 
demonstrated, 2 points = late same day or incomplete, but there’s still effort, 1 point = handed in the next class, 0 
points = not completed within the time frame.  
      
Attendance: Up to four (4) absences are allowed without them affecting your final score (excused or 
unexcused absences.) No note is required for these; however, an email to me is always appreciated if 
you know you will be absent.

be able to make up the points for that task. Please notify me in advance if you have a class in a building

Just as professionals are expected to show up for work, students are expected to come to class 
consistently and on time. While ultimately engagement is crucial, there is also a strong positive 
correlation between class attendance and learning achievement (Lam et al., 2025). At the same time, 
however, learners who are physically present in a classroom but mentally elsewhere are not 
maximizing their learning time. It is hoped that if you are in the classroom, it is because you are there 
to learn.

service, family bereavement, hospitalization and/or medical emergency,  or required academic events

excused absence, you must submit official documentation through the required process in KUPID’s

Course Objectives: 
 
Welcome to Business English. The overriding goal of this course is to develop your business 
communication skills in the form of spoken and written tasks; both academically and professionally. What 
will be covered? Business related topics or themes which may be highlighted orally: discussions through 
case studies, meetings, networking, socializing, presentations; and writing business correspondence such 
as emails, letters, briefs, and/or reports. Whether you are taking this course to improve your general 
English skills or for business purposes, hopefully after 16 weeks, you will be prepared to participate in the 
professional/business world using English.

Textbook? TBA. Course materials will be posted on the new KULMS, emailed or given in class.

● A file folder or binder to organize your handouts

● Cue cards

Office Hours & Communication: 
 
My aim is to help you improve as much as possible. Therefore, I welcome your queries about anything, 
small or big. Communication is fundamental in so many aspects of life, so it is better to ask than to remain 
in the dark. There will be times when I am unable to answer your questions right away due to my 
schedule and other students’ inquiries; please understand this and make an appointment if you 
want to meet me via online. I will make time for you if you let me know in advance.

announcements and course work uploads, so it is essential that you always check new KULMS and 
your email.

Responsibility of Students: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The Business English class is not your typical class. It’s not just a passive lecture 
class. Active participation is required. Following the class guidelines can help your 
confidence and communication skills. 
 
 
Class Guidelines:  
 
 
 
● Come to class every day and be prepared for class. At a minimum, bring your notebook for 
note taking and file folder for your handouts to every class. 
● Participate in class. It is required. 
● Complete assignments on time. 
● If you are absent, it is your job to find out what was taught in class.  
● Stay in class. Leaving freely in-and-out of the classroom is distracting. Students are to be in 
the class at all class times and not go in and out for their convenience. These behaviors 
distract other students and disturb the class environment. Tardiness will also be reflected in 
your final grade. 
● Listen carefully and ask me questions if you don't understand something or make an 
appointment to speak to me. 
● Do not submit work (old or new) from another course/class.

disruptive. These will affect negatively on your class participation grade.

participation grades.  
● Do not use Korean or another language. 
● Use of offensive language will not be tolerated (English, Korean, etc.).  
● Be positive and encourage other members of the class.  
● Acknowledge and respect other members of the class.

Course Description 
This course is an introduction to the study of language from a social and cultural perspective. In the course, 
the relationship among language, society, and culture will be explored. Focus is placed on variation in 
English use and the influence of social variables such as gender, social class, and age. 
 
 
Course Objectives 
 To understand the relationship among language, society, and culture. 
 To become aware of social variation in general language and English use. 
 
 
Textbook 
Van Herk, G. (2018). What is sociolinguistics (2nd ed.). Hoboken, NJ: John Wiley & Sons. [VH] 
 
 
Requirements 
 
Attendance & Participation (30%) 
Regular attendance to class is essential. Attendance will be recorded after the add/drop period is over. 
Being late for more than 30 minutes or leaving class early will be considered an absence. Being late for 
class two times will be counted as one absence. 유고결석 (excused absences) are not granted for this 
course. TWO absences (including sickness and other reasons) will not affect the grade. Each absence after 
the second absence will take off 3% of the total grade. According to university regulations, students 
missing more than 1/3 of the course (excluding classes held before the add/drop period) will automatically 
receive an F. Students missing more than four classes will NOT receive a grade higher than a B+ 
regardless of the nature of absence. In case of absence, it is the students’ responsibility to catch up with 
what they missed by asking classmates and/or instructor. 
Students are to proactively participate in class discussions and activities for this course. Throughout the 
semester, students will engage in discussions on various issues and questions related to sociolinguistics and 
complete in-class activities. 
 
Quizzes (10%) 
Students are expected to complete multiple quizzes over the course of the semester. Specific information 
regarding the quizzes will be announced in class. 
 
Assignments (10%) 
Students are required to complete various assignments throughout the semester. Further details about them 
will be provided in class. 
2 
Revised on March 16, 2026 
 
 
Group Presentation (20%) 
Students will form groups of approximately four members and present their sociolinguistic research to the 
class. Each group is required to select a topic of interest from the course textbook, design their own original 
research project related to the chosen topic, conduct experiments or data collection, analyze the findings, 
and present the results to the class. At least 2 discussion questions must be included at the end of the 
presentation. Students are required to use and submit PowerPoint slides for the presentation. Further details 
about group formation, research design guidelines, and presentation requirements will be provided in class. 
 
 
Final exam (30%) 
Students will take a final exam based on the textbook and course materials. The exam will be closed-book 
and make-up exam will NOT be provided except in cases of extreme emergencies.

I. Course Description 
COURSE AIMS 
  This course serves as an introduction to the academic field of marketing 
management. For those students who will not specialize in marketing, the course will 
provide introductory background. For those students planning to specialize in 
marketing, the course will help guide them to further in-depth study. 
 
LEARNING OBJECTIVES 
This course deals with six fundamental dimensions of marketing:  
  1) Marketing’s contribution to the short and long term success of the firm,  
2) How firms can be more market-oriented, specifically how they can better analyze 
    customers and competitors,  
  3) How to evaluate alternative marketing strategies,  
  4) How to plan marketing strategies over the product life cycle,  
  5) New product development and introduction strategies, and  
  6) Price, promotion and distribution strategies.   
 
By the end of this course students should: 
  Have an appreciation of contemporary market orientation perspectives 
  Understand how consumers and customers behave and how markets function and 
  evolve 
Evaluate the place of competitor and stakeholder analysis within the process of 
  strategic marketing 
Critically evaluate how firms use the marketing ‘mix’ framework to relate to these 
  markets 
Be  able  to  reflect  on  the  contribution  marketing  might make  to  organizational 
  performance 
 
II. Assessment 
MID-TERM EXAM

will be given out to students 1 week before the examination. Mid-term exam will be 
consisted of multiple choices and short essays. The examination represents 30% of the

FINAL-TERM EXAM 
The final term exam will take the form of one 75-minute examination. Information 
will be given out to students 1 week before the examination and one review session 
will be arranged. Final-term exam will be consisted of short essays and long essays. 
The examination represents 30% of the assessment. 
 
MARKETING PROJECT 
This  will  be  one  group  project  designed  to  give  you  opportunities  to  obtain  
hands-on experience of the concepts and methods covered in the course.  
Your group project is to generate a new product concept and develop a marketing 
program for the new product that you will introduce to the market. 
 
Groups will be self-selected. The optimal size for the group is 5 people. Your group 
should be formed by week 4. If you have difficulty forming a group, please see the 
instructor as soon as possible. Please approach the instructor at the earliest time if 
there appears to a problem arising in the project. Each group member is expected to 
contribute equally to the project. Collaboration across groups is not allowed. Peer 
evaluation form will be given at the end of semester-this may result in loss of grade if 
contribution is not deemed to be sufficient. The written report should be no longer 
than 12 pages (excluding appendices). Standard business reporting style should be 
used, which includes an executive summary, background, analysis and key 
recommendations on the marketing tools that should be used for the new product 
concept. 
 
I will schedule several meetings throughout the semester to assist and monitor the 
progress of your team project. The deadline for submission of the assignments will be 
announced as the course progresses. The team project (report: 15% and presentation: 
15%) represents 30% of the assessment. 
 
CLASS PARTICIPATION 
The result of class participation represents 10% of the assessment.  
 
BONUS POINTS (Research Participation)

research project that is conducted by KU marketing faculty. Research participation 
opportunities will be announced on the Blackboard or in class. The study that you are

개요
 이 수업은 AI 시대의 리터러시(Literacy)—읽기·쓰기 중심의 문자 리터러시에 말
하기·듣기를 결합한 체화된 리터러시—를 핵심 역량으로 삼는다. 단순한 정보 해독 
능력을 넘어, 텍스트와 세계를 함께 읽고 쓰며, 토론을 통해 지식과 권력의 작동을 
비판적으로 성찰하는 비판적·관계적 리터러시 형성을 목표로 한다.  
 이를 위해 인문·사회·과학의 관점에서 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰과 실천적 가
치를 종합적으로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하며 미래의 변화에 
대응할 수 있는 토의·토론의 학습 환경을 구성한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 
비판적·융합적·창의적 사고를 촉진하고, 새로운 관점에서 문제를 제기하고 타인과의 
소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 지향점으로 
삼는다.  
 이 수업은 플립트 클래스(Flipped Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방식으
로 운영되며, 질문 중심 학습(QBL: Question Based Learning), 함께 읽기,  
토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다. 학기 말에는 포
럼과 아고라의 형식을 통해 탐구 결과를 공유하고 성찰을 확장한다.

진

초점을둔다. 강의는주어진시간동안서양철학의수많은주제를두루살펴보기보다는
두가지주제에선정해서그에초점을두고함께탐구한다. 우선‘도덕’(윤리)의문제와
관련해서근대이후서양철학논의에서중심이되는학설들을살펴보고서로비교해본
다. 다음주제는‘자아’ 문제를둘러싼근현대철학의논의, 특히실체적관점, 관계적관
점, 해체적관점등을살펴본다. 주제탐구는시대적으로주로근대이후의서양철학논
의에맞추어져있지만필요에따라훨씬과거고대의논의도살펴볼것이다. 선정된두
주제에대한탐구를통해수강생은각주제에대해접근하는관점의다양성을경험하게
될것이다. 더불어관점의다양성에는동일사태나문제를어떤식으로개념화하고이를
논리적으로전개하는가가주요함을알아차리게될것이다. 한편으로모든학문에서와마
찬가지로서양철학에서도어떤문제나주제에접근하고논의할때핵심개념을어떻게
설정하는지가중요하다. 또다른한편으로어떤주제에대한주요개념의시대나관점에
따른변주곡을포괄적으로이해하는작업은그주제에대한편향되지않은이해와결부
된다. 이강의는수강생에게서양철학에대한이런식의접근을제시하고자한다.
강의는몇가지주제탐구를통해철학하는행위가각사태와관련해서어떤차원과지
평에서혹은어떤방식으로접근하는지살펴볼것이다. 이과정에서철학뿐만아니라학
문에서개념규정과이해가얼마나중요한지그리고주요개념을이용해서자기생각을
논증해나가는과정이얼마나치밀해야하는지를차근히살펴볼것이다. 이를통해철학
하는행위를좀더이해해나가는개념적바탕을마련해보고자한다.

Course Description 
 
This course serves as an undergraduate-level seminar on international marketing (IM) 
for Korean firms.  The primary objective of the course is to provide a framework for 
managing marketing operations across borders.  Emphases will be given to the 
analysis of international markets, their respective consumers and environments, and 
various marketing management issues required to meet the demands of true global 
markets. 
 
In particular, this course will focus on: 
 
(1) international marketing challenges from the perspective of Korean firms, 
(2) developing marketing strategy based on analysis of customers and markets in 
foreign countries, and 
(3) various marketing examples in the context of Asian markets as well as emerging 
markets, such as Japan, India, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Philippines, and 
Thailand. 
 
 
Course Material 
 
Primary 
- lectures 
- cases & journal articles: a list will be provided in class & on LMS 
- presentations, discussions and Q&As 
- tutorials 
 
Secondary (required, but subject to change) 
- Green & Keegan (2020), Global Marketing (10th edition), Pearson 
 
If you have not taken any marketing courses yet, pick an introductory marketing 
textbook, then begin reading chapter 1 and other chapters dealing with STP, consumer 
behavior, product and brand, among others. 
 
 
Course Format & Grade 
 
International Marketing (U) 
2
This course is conducted along a seminar format, using a combination of lectures, 
class discussions, case analysis, in-class exercises, and student presentations. Given 
the format, it is essential for students to read assigned book chapters, cases, articles 
and/or other reading materials for each class.  Refer to the Class Schedule to be 
available on Blackboard. 
 
The lectures will often focus on advanced international marketing issues that are 
neglected in contemporary IM textbooks. In addition, IM challenges and strategies 
adopted by Korean and Asian firms are not necessarily covered in most textbooks 
(based on marketing practices of North American and European firms). 
 
 
Participation & discussion  
 
20+ 
 
Assignment & quiz (5 points each)  
30

25

25 
 
Total  
 
 
 
 
100+ points 
 
Optional: case presentation, extra credit (maximum 10 points) 
 
 
Quiz 
 
Quizzes will be given regarding reading assignments such as cases, articles, and 
textbook chapters. Further information will be provided in class.  
 
 
Tutorial 
 
A total of six tutorial sessions are offered to enhance student learning and participation. 
For each session, a practical international marketing topic is pre-announced with 
reading assignments, based on which students will be able to join group discussions 
exploring the topic in the classroom. From each tutorial, students can get a maximum 
of five points toward his/her final grade. Zero point in the case of absences or no 
participation. 
 
 
Case Analysis 
 
To give a pragmatic focus to the course, a series of cases and managerial issues will be 
discussed. Case analysis will be a core component of learning in this course. For each 
case, a list of issues will be announced for discussion (see LMS).  
 
For extra credits, some students may make a presentation to address the questions 
concerning each case analysis. Typically, two students will be responsible for 
presenting a case for about twenty minutes, followed by Q&As.  Your presentation will 
have to address the afore-mentioned issues assigned for each case. 
- Look at the list of issues for each case presentation. 
- Upload the ppt slides in advance so that other students will have a chance to review 
your material.

3
- Before presentation, turn in a printed copy of your slides (black & white, six slides in 
each page). The first slide should include your name & the title of your presentation.

Assignments 
 
1. All the assignments submitted or presented should be an original work 
independently prepared by each student or group. Copying and/or exchanging 
assignments between students or from other external sources are strictly prohibited. 
2. Whenever applicable, the reference section should reveal all relevant information 
on each referenced article, book, URL, interview, etc. 
3. Chat GPT issues will be announced in class. 
 
 
Group Project 
 
To be announced in class. 
 
 
Additional Notice 
 
1. A teaching assistant will be available to facilitate lectures and student evaluation. 
The TA will be responsible for course administrative issues and grading. 
 
2. Announcements regarding assignments and other coursework will be frequently 
made during class sessions. It will be the individual student’s responsibility to take 
note of these announcements for him/herself. TA is not responsible for a student’s 
negligence concerning assignments and due dates. 
 
3. Students are expected not to interfere with lectures, discussions and presentations 
with inappropriate behavior. Do not use notebook or smartphone for other matters. 
 
4. Absences count. Multiple absences can have a significant influence on a student’s 
final grade, as the student is not able to participate in class discussions at all. 
 
5. In the case of absences (e.g., hospital visits), each student will have to follow the 
procedures set by the university. No need to submit any document to the TA or the 
professor.

격히 금지된다. 부정행위가 적발될 경우, 해당 시험은 즉시 0점 처리되며 재시험

▷ 강의개요
개요
이 강의는 외국인 재학생(수준: 고급)을 위한 교양필수 강의로서, 학문 세
계의 핵심 주제들에 대해 한국어로 사고하고 표현하는 능력을 향상시켜 
‘자유, 정의, 진리’를 달성하는 데에 목적이 있다. 이를 위해 토론과 발표를 
통해 자신의 생각을 한국어로 자유롭게 표현하며, 다양한 언어적 표현과 
기초 교양 지식을 익혀 대학생으로서의 정의로운 인성을 기르고, 인문, 사
회, 과학 분야의 다양한 융복합적 주제에 대한 진지한 탐구를 한다. 학문
세계의탐구Ⅰ에서는 심리, 경제, 과학, 문화, 예술, 기술에 대한 탐구를 통
해 글로벌 인재로 성장하기 위한 기초 교양 지식을 기른다.

Imporant Note: This course is conducted as an 8-week intensive program under the 
Flexible Semester system. 
 
Course Objective 
 
Marketing is the business process of creating, delivering, and communicating “value” to 
customers and managing good customer relationships for the benefit of the organization 
and its stakeholders. In the process, companies can build intangible assets such as brand 
equity and customer equity through successful marketing investments. This course is an 
introduction to the field of marketing, focusing on marketing issues faced by a typical 
organization. The course is designed to give students a thorough understanding of the 
basic concepts of marketing and to enable them to apply these concepts in a variety of 
situations. It also provides the necessary foundation for students who wish to take higher-
level marketing courses. This course also bridges the gap between traditional marketing 
and the Artificial Intelligence (AI) revolution. Students will explore how AI is reshaping 
the industry while engaging in analog activities to develop the human creativity and 
critical thinking that machines cannot replicate. 
  
Textbook & References 
 
There is no single required textbook for this course. However, the following book serves 
as a primary reference for the fundamental concepts: 
 
Kotler, Philip, Gary Armstrong, and Sridhar Balasubramanian (2023), Principles of 
Marketing, 19th edition, Prentice Hall. (ISBN 978-1-292-44936-4)  
 
Students are strictly required to study all assigned reading materials and watch the 
designated video clips before attending each session. Some readings are available through 
Korea University Online Library at library.korea.ac.kr

Course Description 
This course explores major critical theories that are widely discussed in literary and cultural 
studies. Critical theories are perceived as notoriously challenging and often accused of being 
overly abstract rather than providing practical solutions to problems they are addressing. 
Then, why should we learn critical theories? Critical theories unravel how social structures 
and norms benefit specific groups of people, grappling with how to challenge such 
inequalities. Rejecting linear notions of progress and social norms widely deemed “good” or 
“proper,” critical theories instead highlight the transformative potential of marginalized 
groups and concepts that have long been deemed unpleasant and undesirable (e.g. failure, 
loss, abject, uncertainty, and so on). To gain deeper understanding of how critical theories 
offer powerful tools for imagining a more ethical, inclusive, and liberating society, students 
will learn how theoretical concepts and ideas are revised and developed across diverse 
historical, cultural, and social contexts.

Course Description 
In this course, we will draw on narrative theory to explore how the forms of storytelling and 
literature that are created, shared, and experienced both traditionally and through digital 
platforms such as social media, podcasts, and AI-generated content. In addition, we will 
examine narratives about digital media by paying attention to discourses that celebrate or 
critique the influence of digital technologies on culture, identity, and communication. 
Course Objectives 
1) Through hands-on experience of AI tools and systems, students gain comprehensive 
knowledge of how  Large Language Models and AI systems process human language and 
identify the strengths, weaknesses, capabilities, and blind spots of AI technologies and tools.  
2) Use literary criticism methods and close reading to analyze AI-generated texts, including 
AI-generated stories and AI-generated literary interpretations. 
3) Understand how AI can enhance one’s critical and creative engagement with literary texts 
and diverse people and cultures of this world.

1) 류마티스내과 입원 환자를 담당하여 병력청취를 실시하고 류마티스 질환이 의심되는 경우 
병력 청취 시 알아야 하는 항목들을 숙지하여야 한다.
2) 근골격계 진찰을 숙지하여야 한다. 특히 관절의 운동 범위 및 압통, 종창, 삼출 유무, 관절 
변형(ulnar deviation, swan-neck deformity, Boutonnier deformity, Herbeden’s 
node, Bouchard node), 각종 결절(tophi, rheumatoid nodule), 모발 및 피부의 변화, 근
력 평가 등에 대해 알고 환자에게 적용할 수 있어야 한다.
3) 흔한 류마티스 질환(류마티스 관절염, 골관절염, 강직성 척추염, 통풍, 전신성 홍반성 루푸
스, 베체트씨병 등) 환자에서 병력 청취 및 신체검사를 적절히 시행하고 기술할 수 있어야 
한다.
4) Rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen test, 
anticardiolipin antibody, lupus anticoagulant, uric acid, acute phase reactant 등의 
검사 의의를 설명할 수 있어야 한다.
5) 근골격계 증상이 있을 때 X-ray 검사가 필요한 경우와 왜 필요한지를 설명할 수 있어야 
하며, 단순 골절 X-ray를 판독할 수 있는 능력을 갖도록 한다.
6) 임상수기로서 관절 천자법 및 주사법의 적응증과 시술 방법을 숙지하고 견학하며 편광현미
경 작동법을 숙지하고 요산 결정을 찾을 수 있어야 한다.
7) 실습기간 동안 류마티스내과 외래 진료에 참여하여 입원 환자에서 볼 수 없는 다양한 질환 
군을 접하고 환자 진료과정을 모니터링 및 피드백한다.
8) 만성질환을 가진 환자들의 특성 및 이를 대하는 바람직한 의사의 자세, 또한 만성질환 환자
의 안전한 관리에 대하여 논할 수 있어야 한다.

4. 과 소개
l 류마티스내과에서는 류마티스관절염, 강직성 척추염, 전신홍반루푸스, 전신경화증, 염증성근
염, 쇼그렌증후군, 혈관염 등 다양한 전신 류마티스 질환을 다루는 내과의 한 분과이다. 우리 
과는 전임교원 2인, 임상교원 1인, 전공의 1인으로 구성되어 있으며, 신관 83병동을 주병동으
로 사용하고 있다.
5. 학습목표
1) 류마티스내과 입원 환자를 담당하여 병력청취를 실시하고 류마티스 질환이 의심되는 경우 
병력 청취 시 알아야 하는 항목들을 숙지하여야 한다.
2) 근골격계 진찰을 숙지하여야 한다. 특히 관절의 운동 범위 및 압통, 종창, 삼출 유무, 관절 
변형(ulnar deviation, swan-neck deformity, Boutonnier deformity, Herbeden’s 
node, Bouchard node), 각종 결절(tophi, rheumatoid nodule), 모발 및 피부의 변화, 근
력 평가 등에 대해 알고 환자에게 적용할 수 있어야 한다.
3) 흔한 류마티스 질환(류마티스 관절염, 전신홍반루푸스, 강직성 척추염, 전신혈관염, 통풍 관
절염 등) 환자에서 병력 청취 및 신체검사를 적절히 시행하고 기술할 수 있어야 한다.
4) Rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen test, 
anticardiolipin antibody, lupus anticoagulant, uric acid, acute phase reactant 등의 
검사 의의를 설명할 수 있어야 한다.
5) 근골격계 증상이 있을 때 X-ray 검사가 필요한 경우와 왜 필요한지를 설명할 수 있어야 
하며, 단순 골절 X-ray를 판독할 수 있는 능력을 갖도록 한다.
6) 관절 천자법 및 주사법의 적응증과 시술 방법을 숙지하고 견학하며 편광현미경 작동법을 
숙지하고 요산 결정을 찾을 수 있어야 한다.
7) 실습기간 동안 류마티스내과 외래 진료에 참여하여 입원 환자에서 볼 수 없는 다양한 질환 
군을 접하고 환자 진료과정을 모니터링 및 피드백한다.
8) 만성질환을 가진 환자들의 특성 및 이를 대하는 바람직한 의사의 자세, 또한 만성질환 환자
의 안전한 관리에 대하여 논할 수 있어야 한다.

7. 학생활동 또는 실습내용
1) 지식 습득
l 교과서는 ‘Harrison’ 최신판을 기준으로 함.
l 저널은 3개 병원이 공통된 저널로 통일함.
l 주제 발표는 교과서와 저널에서 다루지 못한 주제를 선정하여 발표함.
- 류마티스 관절염: 류마티스 관절염 진단기준에 포함된 관절에 대한 이학적 검사와 평가 
및 항류마티스약제(DMARDs)에 대한 이해
- 골관절염: 골관절염에 가장 흔한 X-ray 소견에 대한 이해 및 이학적 검사방법 치료 습
득
- 강직성 척추염: 강직성 척추염 환자의 이학적 검사 방법 및 X-ray 소견 습득
- 통풍: 급성 통풍 관절염 환자의 임상적 특징과 관절 천자술기 관찰 및 유지 치료에 대한 
이해
- 전신홍반루푸스: 전신홍반루푸스 진단에 필수적인 검사 항목 및 임상 소견에 대한 지식 
습득
- 베체트병 및 전신혈관염: 베체트병을 포함한 전신혈관염의 임상 양상 및 검사 결과에

3. 과 소개
l 류마티스 내과에서 주로 다루는 내용은 류마티스 관절염을 비롯한 염증성 관절염, 루푸스, 
전신성 경화증을 포함한 결체조직질환, 강직 척추염 등의 척추를 침범하는 질환, 통풍 등의 
결절성 관절염, 점액낭염, 건초염, 혈관염, 골관절염 등이며 우리 과의 구성은 전임교원 1
인, 임상교원 1인으로 구성되어 있으며, 주 병동은 83병동이다.
4. 학습목표
1) 류마티스내과 입원 환자를 담당하여 병력 청취를 실시하고 류마티스 질환이 의심되는 경
우 병력 청취 시 알아야 하는 항목들을 숙지하여야 한다.
2) 근골격계 진찰을 숙지하여야 한다. 특히 관절의 운동 범위 및 압통, 종창, 삼출 유무, 관절 
변형(ulnar deviation, swan-neck deformity, Boutonnier deformity, Herbeden’s 
node, Bouchard node), 각종 결절(tophi, rheumatoid nodule), 모발 및 피부의 변화, 
근력 평가 등에 대해 알고 환자에게 적용할 수 있어야 한다.
3) 흔한 류마티스 질환(류마티스 관절염, 골관절염, 강직성 척추염, 통풍, 전신성 홍반성 루
푸스, 베체트병 등) 환자에서 병력 청취 및 신체검사를 적절히 시행하고 기술할 수 있어야 
한다.
4) Rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen test, 
anticardiolipin antibody, lupus anticoagulant, uric acid, acute phase reactant 등
의 검사 의의를 설명할 수 있어야 한다.
5) 근골격계 증상이 있을 때 X-ray 검사가 필요한 경우와 왜 필요한지를 설명할 수 있어야 
하며, 단순 골절 X-ray를 판독할 수 있는 능력을 갖추도록 한다.
6) 임상수기로서 관절 천자법 및 주사법의 적응증과 시술 방법을 숙지하고 견학하며 편광현
미경 작동법을 숙지하고 요산 결정을 찾을 수 있어야 한다.
7) 실습기간 동안 류마티스내과 외래를 참관하여 입원 환자에서 볼 수 없는 다양한 질환 군
을 접하고 이후 만성질환을 가진 환자들의 특성과 이를 대하는 바람직한 의사의 자세에 
대하여 논할 수 있어야 한다.

EDU 271 Career Counseling  
Spring 2026 
Tuesdays and (Fridays) 9:00 – 10:15am 
Uncho-Useon Education Bldg. #507 
 
Instructor:    
         Bora Lee, Ph.D. 
Office:                   Uncho-Useon Education Bldg. Rm #715 
Contact:                    boralee117@korea.ac.kr (email), 2296 (campus direct) 
Office hours:            Tuesday 10:30-11:00 or by appointment 
 
*The current syllabus is a work in progress. The final version will be distributed on the 
first day of class.  
 
Course Overview 
The course Career Counseling is an undergraduate course that focuses on learning career counseling theories 
and basic skills that can be applied to various settings, such as in schools, community centers, and counseling 
centers, by school teachers and counselors working with adolescents and adults.  
  
Course Objectives  
After taking this course, students should be able to: 
ú describe and critically discuss major career counseling theories. 
ú apply skills and techniques based on a specific career counseling theory. 
ú use basic counseling skills and techniques in an individual counseling setting.  
 
Course Operation  
This course is operated in a combination of online and offline classes (a.k.a. flipped learning).  Students will 
participate in online lectures that cover the course contents for a given week’s topic. The contents covered in the 
lectures will function as your basic knowledge for advanced learning during an offline face-to-face class. In 
general, Fridays will be reserved for online lectures. Students come to class on Tuesdays to participate in in-
class discussion, role-plays, activities, and case analyses.  
A new policy starting in 2026: No use of digital devices is allowed in the classroom (e.g., laptops, pads, mobile 
phones, etc.) except for on designated dates. In this course, we will learn how to think critically WITHOUT the 
help of internet or AI. We will also learn how to interact with other human beings WITHOUT any other media. 
In the classroom, whenever there is an assignment, students will be given a paper worksheet to fill in. So, please 
bring your writing tools.   
 
Course Materials  
There is one required textbook for this course: 
 
Brown, S. D., & Lent, R. W. (Eds.). (2020). Career development and counseling: Putting theory and research 
to work (3rd edition). John Wiley & Sons. 
 
 
2 
• 
The textbook can be purchased through amazon.com. Students can also buy or rent an e-textbook 
through amazon.com. But remember that you CANNOT browse your e-textbook in class.  
• 
The textbook will also be on reserve at the Korea University Main Library.  
Supplemental readings and other course materials will be handed out during class time OR will be posted on 
Blackboard (http://kulms.korea.ac.kr).  
 
Course Requirements  
1. Take-home assignments (20%): There will be occasions when students are asked to do an assignment 
that is to prepare for the consecutive class. These assignments are graded on a “all or none” grading 
system. If you complete the assignment, you get full points. If you do not complete the assignment by 
due date, you get no points. Each assignment is 5 points worth. NO LATE ASSIGNMENTS are 
allowed. 
 
§ 
Complete Interest Inventory via https://www.work24.go.kr/ or https://www.career.go.kr  (due Mar. 
23)  
§ 
Fill out your career rainbow (due March 30) 
§ 
Ryan’s case analysis (due May 11) 
§ 
Completing your career genogram (due May 25)  
 
2. In-class assignments (20%): There will be four types of in-class activities. At the end of each activity, 
students will be asked to submit a tangible outcome (e.g., reflection paper, case analysis report, pros-
cons analysis sheet, etc.). Each outcome will be graded based on its performance level. Six (6) in-class 
activities will be counted towards your final grade, out of random occasions of in-class activities. If you 
complete more than six assignments, only the highest scored assignments will be counted towards your 
final grade.  For those who missed a class, you can regard the missed assignment as one of the lowest 
grade assignments. There will be NO MAKE-UPS for missed classes (*exceptions only apply for 
students who go out for teaching training).  
 
A. Activity (AC): Activities are designed to help you better understand concepts or theories covered in 
class. These will be games or drawings or other types of activities that can be fun ways to learn. 
These activities can also be used and applied in settings working with youth or adults in school, 
community centers, or other appropriate contexts.  
B. Role-play (RP): Because this course is a counseling course, we will also have opportunities to do 
role-plays in class. Typically, one student would play the counselor role and another student would 
play the client role. At times, a third person can be an observer to provide feedback to the students 
who play roles of the counselor and client. These role-plays should help students gain a sense of 
how counseling works in real-world setting, practice their counseling-related skills and techniques, 
and exercise how theory can be applied in practice.  
C. Group discussion (GD): Students will be given questions that are related to subject knowledge 
and/or those that are challenging to answer (for example, questions that are challenging to answer 
because there are multiple sides that do not agree upon each other, or because we do not know 
much about the problem). Most of the times, students will discuss in small groups (2-5 persons) and 
then discuss as a whole class. The primary goal of group discussions is to critically think about a 
given problem/issue, share ideas with peers, and develop skills to come to a conclusion as a group. 
D. Case study (CS): Sometimes, we will read or watch about a client who is going through a specific 
career issue. Students are asked to analyze the case from a particular theoretical perspective and 
think about how they would actually conduct counseling with the client. The purpose of doing case 
 
 
3 
studies is to learn how theory is applied in practice. 
 
3. Mid-semester reflection paper (15%): Students will write a short reflection paper on their experiences as 
a client/student in a career counseling session. Students will be matched with a graduate student taking a 
course on career assessment and will be asked to join either an individual or group session before week 
8 of the semester. After joining the session, write a brief reflection on how it felt as a client.  
§ 
Format: Times New Roman 12pt font size, Double-spaced, 1-inch indent, no more than three pages 
§ 
Content:  
- 
Write the name of the person who led the session you participated.  
- 
Choose three primary emotions you experienced during and after the session 
- 
Write briefly on why you think those emotions arose.  
- 
Think about what those emotions are telling you.  
- 
Briefly reflect on what you have learned about career counseling from a client perspective and 
how you would do as a career counselor/teacher in the future.  
 
4. Semester-long project (45%): Students will practice semi-realistic counseling sessions with a high 
school or college student (at least) three times.  
§ 
Format: Times New Roman 12pt font size, Double-spaced, 1-inch indent, no more than 10 pages. 
§ 
Task:  
- 
The pseudo client should be the age of 11~21 years old.  
- 
Each session should take about 30-60 mins.  
- 
In the first session, meet with the student to get a sense of what their career concerns are.  
- 
Design the second session, talk with your pseudo client based on your analysis of the first 
session.  
- 
Make sure you receive consultation from the instructor either after the 1st or 2nd session. 
- 
In the last session, discuss any unresolved issues and wrap-up.  
§ 
Content of your paper: 
- 
Write a counseling report after each session. Also, take a selfie of the two of you and attach it 
to the report.  
- 
After the first session, include your case analysis and counseling plans for the subsequent 
sessions. In your planning, you need to include an analysis of the case, background theory (or 
theories) that you think is suitable to deal with the case, and any kind of assessments or tools 
you plan to use with the client. 
- 
After the second session, describe what went well and what did not go well, especially from 
the client’s perspective.  
- 
After the final session, describe how the client thinks about the issue since the first session. 
- 
As a wrap-up, include your own reflection as a counselor.  
§ 
A 15-minute instructor consultation  
- 
Must be received by May 22.  
- 
The consultation session is not graded, but those who do not receive consultation will lose 5 
points.  
- 
By the time of consultation, the student must have met with the pseudo client at least one time.  
 
* Students who are going out for teacher training should inform the instructor by 3/27 regarding their 
requirements during their absence.  
 
 
4 
** By university policy, students have to attend at least two-thirds (2/3) of the class to receive a valid grade. 
Attendance for online classes will be verified based on the completion of video viewings by the scheduled class 
date. For offline classes, attendance will be recorded in person through roll call during the class 
 
Classroom Policies  
ú 
Tardiness: The instructor will take attendance at the beginning of each class. Students who arrive late 
will receive a deduction on the day’s in-class assignment. Specifically, students who enter while the 
instructor is explaining the assignment will receive a 2-point deduction, and those who arrive after 
students have begun working will receive a 5-point deduction, regardless of performance. This policy is 
intended to ensure full participation and maintain a fair learning environment for all students.  
ú 
Electronic devices: Students are not permitted to use digital devices during class. One of the primary 
goals of this course is to develop effective client-interaction and communication skills, and I have 
observed that digital devices often disrupt interpersonal engagement. To maximize learning, devices 
must remain unused during activities focused on communication and counseling practice. However, 
there will be designated times when laptops, smartphones, tablets, or other devices may be used for 
instructional purposes. In such cases, the instructor will provide explicit guidance. Please note that all 
electronic devices are strictly prohibited during in-class examinations, if there are any. 
ú 
Online classes: Please turn on your camera when we meet online. In case you do not have a camera on 
your device or have technical issues that prevents you from turning on your camera, please put up a 
photo of yourself so that we know who you are when you are present. Remember that learning occurs 
through human interaction, and we would like to know that we are interacting with a HUMAN BEING. 
Learning occurs through relationship building, and interacting with verbal AND non-verbal language is 
important in building a supportive relationship with each other. Let us all contribute to a safe, 
supportive, and encouraging learning environment!

 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정
진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중
히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술
∙ [실험실습 안전]
 -연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분
야 대상 학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습
을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수
 -신규교육(신입생 2시간), 정기교육(고위험학과 학기별 6시간, 저위험학과 학기별 3시간)

이지 접속(“크롬”으로 접속, 접속 오류 시 인터넷 설정에서 “팝업 차단 해제” 설정 필요)

JMCO382: Entertainment Industries 
엔터테인먼트 산업 (영강) 
 Spring 2026 
College of Media & 
Communication Korea University 
 
Schedule: Class meets Tu/Th 10:30AM-11:45AM in 교양관 108 
 
Instructor: Dr. Dam Hee Kim 
Office: Media Hall 608 
Office hours: Thursday 1PM-2PM or by appointment 
Tel.: 02-3290-2260 
E-mail: damheekim@korea.ac.kr 
 
E-mail policy: Please include [JMCO382] in the subject line. During the workweek, I 
will typically reply to student emails within 24-hours of receiving the email. On weekends, there 
may be a slight delay in responding but this will never be longer than 48-hours. Please check the 
syllabus or LMS before emailing. For example, if you are emailing to ask about what the late 
work policy is or what reading is due for the next class, this information is already provided. 
 
Course Description 
This course will help students gain an understanding of how the entertainment industries 
work. Students will be reading both classic and current research in this area while paying 
particular attention to critical issues such as digitization, fragmentation, globalization, changing 
business models, AI, transparency and control. Through intense reading, discussion and research, 
by the end of the semester, students will gain a comprehensive theoretical and practical 
understanding of entertainment media practices as well as entertainment media-related research 
skills. 
 
Learning Outcomes 
By the end of the semester students will be able to: 
- 
Compare and contrast the theories and concepts related to entertainment media research 
- 
Apply important concepts and research skills related to entertainment media to draw 
conclusions about today’s practices in the entertainment industries 
- 
Demonstrate their knowledge about the significance of current research in the field by 
delivering a research report 
 
Required Texts 
There is no required textbook for this class. Required readings for the course will be 
available on LMS. Students will read journal articles, book chapters and reports in English. 
 
Topics 
- 
Conceptualizing entertainment and the audience  
- 
Live streaming and video services such as Netflix, YouTube and TikTok  
- 
Platformization, the K-pop industry, and Webtoon & Webnovel communities 
- 
Financial performance and critical acclaim in the film industry 
- 
Issues of algorithms, transparency & control, and artificial intelligence (AI) 
 
 
** Draft – Subject to Change ** 
2 
 
Course Format and Teaching Methods 
The class will employ the following formats and teaching methods: lecture, in-class 
discussion, and small group activities. 
During class, my overarching goal is for you to have a good conceptual as well as applied 
understanding of class subjects. To accomplish this, discussion facilitators and I will bring 
relevant, up-to-date examples from the real world (e.g., news articles, videos, and case studies). 
That said, readings should be completed before class for your active participation in class. You 
are responsible for reading, understanding, and coming to class with more than a passing 
familiarity with the readings so that you can apply concepts from the readings to contemporary 
examples in class. 
 
Course Grade 
- 
Participation 10% 
- 
Group Discussion facilitation 15% 
- 
Group Compare & Contrast Project Presentation 25%  
- 
Exams 50% (25% x 2) 
 
Participation (10%) 
Students are expected to come to class prepared to discuss the readings in thoughtful 
ways, and fully participate in class activities. Students are encouraged to provide insights, ask 
questions, build on others’ ideas, and respectfully disagree. In addition, your participation grade 
will be based on several in-class activities. 
 
Here are some questions you may consider when you do the readings (especially 
academic articles): 
- 
Would you agree with or challenge some of the findings? 
- 
What alternative explanations could the authors have considered for their findings? 
- 
What were the weaknesses/strengths of the methods employed? 
- 
What future research can be conducted related to these studies? 
- 
How do the findings relate to your life and the real world? 
 
Group Discussion Facilitation (15%) 
Students will serve as discussion facilitators in a group for 15 minutes once a semester. 
In the beginning of the semester, students will look at the topics and readings, and sign up for the 
day in which they wish to be a discussion facilitator. Discussion facilitators will be responsible 
for a) recapping the assigned reading, b) showing a related video or two (or sharing one news 
article related to the weekly reading) to the class to apply theories and findings to the real world, 
and c) providing multiple discussion questions linking the reading, the video/news article, and 
the topic/reading, and then share their answer briefly. 
One student from the group will email their slides/plan (including a news 
article/video and discussion questions) to both the instructor and the graduate assistant for 
approval/feedback by 12PM the day before class. Once approved, they will submit their 
slides (or the link to their slides) on LMS before class. 
 
Group Compare & Contrast Project Presentation (25%) 
Students will work in a group and analyze two companies/businesses in one 
entertainment industry (e.g., Netflix vs. TVing, Melon vs. YouTube Music, Naver Webtoon vs. 
Kakao Webtoon). Groups will compare and contrast what their key services and business models

3 
 
are, and how they have responded to technological change.  
Questions to answer: 
1. Key services & business models: What does each of the businesses do? How do 
they each generate revenues? 
2. Response to technological change: How have the companies responded to 
technological change? Were their services and business models challenged and/or 
changed at all? 
3. Key differences: How do they differ? What are their respective strengths and 
weaknesses?  
4. Prospects: Which one do you think is going to prosper vs. fail? Why?  
Students must use concepts/theories/research findings covered in class, and cite at least 
TWO academic background articles that are relevant to their topic, yet are not included in the 
course reader. The articles MUST be empirical and taken from a peer-reviewed scholarly 
research journal. Websites, popular press articles, and conference presentations are generally not 
acceptable. More information on the group presentation: 
- 
Do a 12-minute-long presentation as a group; every member needs to speak. 
- 
Peer evaluation – in case members did not contribute equally to the project 
            On 4/15 and 5/29, we will have project workshop sessions so that students can ask 
questions and/or discuss concerns with the teaching team. The final presentation on 6/5 and 6/10 
will be 10 minutes.  
 
Exams (25% x 2) 
You will have two exams over the course of the semester (each worth 25% of your 
grade). These exams may include multiple choice and true/false questions and short answers. 
They will cover all material that has been assigned even if that material was not discussed in 
class. They will also cover material that was discussed in class but was not present in the 
readings. The first exam will cover everything up to that point in class, the second exam will 
cover everything after the first exam to that point in class (i.e., the second exam is not 
cumulative). 
Lecture slides are your study guides. Make sure you are familiar with slides with 
underlined content for exams! 
 
Course Policies 
 
Late Work Policy 
Students are entirely responsible for the timely submission of assignments. If they do not 
arrive by the due date, they will be marked down 10% per day. 
 
Make up Exam Policy 
If you miss an exam, you must notify me within 24 hours as to the reason for your absence. 
Make ups will be given at a time to be determined later and may not necessarily followthe same 
format as the scheduled exam. However, in order to qualify for a make-up exam, you must have 
unimpeachable documentation from a qualified third-party source explaining why you were not 
able to take your exam at the scheduled time. 
 
Grade Disputes 
If you wish to dispute a grading decision, you have three business days from the time you 
receive your grade to formally dispute your grade. We will not entertain any discussion of a

grade, you will need to meet with us face-to-face. 
Moreover, if you wish to dispute a grading decision, we will consider the assignment in 
its entirety. In other words, if you wish to dispute a grading decision on an exam, Dr. Kim will 
re-grade your entire exam, which might mean that you actually end up with a lower grade. 
Final grades are not debatable. We will not entertain any requests to round a grade up 
(e.g., your grade is an 89.2 and you ask for it to be a 90). There is typically a curve already 
applied to your grade and it is unfair to other students who have not asked for their grade to be 
changed without a legitimate reason. Furthermore, we will not engage in any discussions with 
students who come to us at the very end of the semester to ask how they might obtain a better 
grade. If your goal is to receive a certain grade in this class, we will be more than happy to work 
with you to help you earn that grade provided you talk with us early on in the semester. 
 
Student Code of Academic Integrity 
Students are encouraged to share intellectual views and discuss freely the principles and 
applications of course materials. However, graded work/exercises must be the product of 
independent effort unless otherwise instructed. Selling class notes and/or other course materials 
to other students or to a third party for resale is not permitted without the instructor’s written 
consent. 
 
Subject to Change Statement 
Information contained in the course syllabus, other than the grade and absence policy, 
may be subject to change with advance notice, as deemed appropriate by the instructor. Any 
changes will be announced in class and posted on LMS.

OVERVIEW OF ASSIGNMENTS 
 
1. One Daily Small Talk: At the beginning of each class, one student will be chosen at random to 
give a short talk for about 45 seconds to a minute. You can talk about anything that you want to 
share with our class: a thought, a story, an insight, a question, or a feeling you are carrying into 
class, a tv show, a movie, something you witnessed or thought about on your way to class, 
something you’re excited or worried about. 
 
2. Individual Weekly Assignment: once a week, you need to use each week’s assigned media outlet 
and find a specific topic that interests you. Make a vocabulary list and write a summary as well as 
one discussion question of each content and post it on Blackboard by noon on Tuesdays. Please 
cite sources and be prepared to share the materials with your partner/small group.  
 
- 
Article: The article should be from a reputable and well-written English-language medium 
source (min. 500 words)  
- 
Podcast: min.7 minutes  
- 
Video: min. 7 minutes

- 
You will be expected to select an article and/or a video clip to use as the basis for 
discussion on your day.  
- 
You are welcome to use the material(s) you submitted for the individual weekly 
assignment.  
- 
You are expected to monitor and guide your peers during their discussion. 
- 
You must post all the materials on the day before your presentation (by 10 PM).

- 
Your demonstration of preparedness for class.

Your ability to communicate your ideas and opinions clearly.

사회와 일상생활의 구성요소로 자리잡았다. 정보사회로의 변동 및 4차 산업혁명은 현대사회

Politics of International Economy 
봄학기  2026 
 
Professor: 김동훈 교수  
Office: 정경관 411 호  
Email: dhkim71@korea.ac.kr 
 
I. 수업개요 Course Description: 
 
This course surveys and critically discusses the contemporary issues in international political 
economy.  Substantively, it addresses key domains in IPE such as politics of international trade, 
international finance, exchange rates and currency, foreign investments, development, and 
international organizations and global governance.  The course is intended to lay the 
groundwork for future studt in the fields of international political economy and international 
relations by examine theoretical answers to questions such as Why do countries open their 
markets? Why some remove restriction on capital flows? What explains foreign investments? 
How globalizations affect economic growth? and etc.  In doing so, we will gain insights into 
how domestic/international politics shape domestic/international economics and vice versa.  
For analytical insights, we look to political science, economics, business, sociology, and history.    
 
읽을거리: The following textbook should be available at LMS 
 
(1) Oatley, Thomas, International Political Economy. 6th edition  - LMS 
(2) 논문집 – LMS

Future of International Monetary System, Oxford University Press  
 Jeffrey A. Frieden, Global Capitalism: Its Fall and Rise in the 20th century (W.W. Norton & 
Company, 2006). 
 Findlay, Ronald, and Kevin, H. O'Rourke, Power and Plenty: Trade, War, and the World 
Economy in the Second Millennium (Princeton University Press, 2007) 
 Irwin, Douglas A., Against the Tide: An Intellectual History of Free Trade (Princeton 
University Press, 1996)

Overview 
This course serves as an introduction to fundamental physics concepts, 
focusing on classical mechanics, rotational motion, waves, and 
thermodynamics. Students will explore the principles governing the 
physical world and develop a strong theoretical foundation through 
lectures and problem-solving exercises. Emphasis will be placed on 
enhancing analytical thinking and applying physics principles to real-
world scenarios. By the end of the course, students will be equipped 
with the skills and knowledge necessary for further studies in physics 
and related disciplines.

environmental challenges in 
modern society while emphasizing 
resilience as one of the key factors in prevention and recovery.

navigate life’s challenges. Through discussions and activities, students 
will develop inner strengths, build healthier relationships, and promote 
mental health for themselves and others.

This Course
There are no restrictions.

공정성을 확보하기 위해 ChatGPT 등 생성형 AI를 활용한 과제 수행을 제한하고 있습니
다. 교수자가 허용하지 않는 범위에서 생성형 AI를 활용할 경우, 해당 과제는 표절로 간주
되어 Fail로 처리될 수 있으니 유의 바랍니다.

1. Course Description 
The DISS314 International Economic Cooperation course aims to provide undergraduate students 
with a comprehensive framework for understanding the mechanisms of global economic governance. 
This course is designed to equip students with the analytical capacity necessary to evaluate critical 
issues and emerging trends in the contemporary global economy. 
While the preceding decades were characterized by unprecedented levels of globalization, we are 
currently navigating a transformative period marked by rising geopolitical tensions and shifting 
paradigms of economic integration. The extensive liberalization of trade, once the hallmark of the 
GATT/WTO framework, now presents complex systemic challenges alongside strategic opportunities. 
In response to this shifting landscape, nations have moved beyond traditional integration to pursue 
resilient global supply and value chains. This evolution necessitates navigating the intricate balance 
between traditional multilateralism and the rise of plurilateralism, while addressing the imperatives 
of economic security and strategic autonomy through diverse forms of bilateral and regional 
cooperation. 
The scope of international economic cooperation has expanded from traditional trade 
liberalization to a broader spectrum of strategic priorities. While facilitating the cross-border 
movement of goods, services, labor and capital remains essential, modern cooperation is increasingly 
defined by deep integration. This includes the governance of digital trade, environmental 
sustainability, and supply chain resilience, which have become central to global economic policy. 
Today, these initiatives represent a shift toward resilient diplomacy, moving beyond mere market 
efficiency to address the complexities of a changing global order. 
This course integrates theoretical foundations with contemporary case studies to navigate the 
complexities of the global economy. By examining established frameworks and new developments, 
students will build analytical skills and gain insights to understand changing economic landscapes 
and address key global issues in international economic cooperation. 
 
2. Course Objectives 
This course is designed for undergraduate students to achieve the following objectives: 
• 
To develop a comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and analytical foundations 
governing international trade, economic integration and global economic cooperation. 
- 2 - 
• 
To critically assess regional and multilateral frameworks through case studies of key 
agreements, examining their historical evolution and roles in navigating contemporary 
geopolitical tensions. 
• 
To analyze the shift toward deep integration by exploring frontier issues, including supply 
chain resilience, digital trade, sustainability and the evolving dynamics of the global order. 
 
3. Lecture Notes and Readings 
• 
Lecture slides will be made available to students prior to each session to facilitate student 
preparation. 
• 
Supplementary materials and academic resources will be accessible via LMS (or provided 
as hard copies when necessary). 
• 
Students are encouraged to engage with the recommended readings outlined in the syllabus 
to gain a deeper understanding of the core topics. 
 
4. Course Evaluation 
Assessment for students will be based on the following criteria: 
 
Class Attendance and Participation (15%) 
 
Group Policy Project & Presentation (20%) *A written policy brief and in-class presentation 
 
Midterm Examination (30%) 
 
Final Examination (35%) 
※ “Academic Integrity and Honesty” - Students are expected to uphold the highest standards of academic 
integrity and honesty. 
※ “Engage in thoughtful discussion with peers!” - As part of the course, students will be encouraged to actively 
participate in insightful group discussions, sharing their perspectives on the economic impacts of the various 
topics we will be exploring.

목적: 
본『토질공학』강의에서는 토질역학에서 배운 지식을 바탕으로 
하여 대한민국 미래를 책임질 건축사회환경 공학도로서 반듯이 
숙지해야 할 압밀, 전단강도, 사면안정, 기초설계 등 흙의 
역학적 특성을 고찰하고, 이러한 이론적인 지식들이 실제 
문제에서 어떻게 적용되는가를 익히는 과정을 배우게 됩니다. 
특히, 『토질공학』은 향후 지반관련 전공과목 (토질역학실험, 
기초공학, 토질 및 기초설계, 첨단도로인프라공학, 암반역학, 
지반조사입문, 등)의 기초가 됩니다. 물론, 학생들이 지금까지 
일반적인 공업역학이나 재료역학 등 연속체 역학에 익숙해져 
있어, 흙 알갱이, 물, 공기로 구성된 삼상구조인 토질을 
다루는데 처음에는 다소 생소할 수 있으나 토질역학에서 배운

Dr. Hangseok Choi

있습니다.

Course Format 
 
강의 
모든 학생들은 정기적으로 수업에 참석해야 하고 제시간에 
강의실에 도착해야 합니다. 정규 강의시간은 반드시 엄수해야 
합니다. 만일 피치 못할 사정(본인 병환, 가족과 관련된 
긴급사항, 또는 공적 업무 등) 과 이에 대한 합당한 사유가 있을 
시 학생 본인이 KUPID 에 유고출석을 신청해주세요. 
 
조교연습 
중간시험이나 
기말시험을 
대비해서 
조교들이 
연습문제를 
풀어주거나, 학생들의 질의에 대한 응답시간을 갖습니다(예정). 
시간과 장소는 추후 조교와 협의하여 결정할 예정입니다. 수업 
진도에 따라, 정규 수업시간에 조교연습을 실시할 수도 
있습니다(특히 시험 전).   
 
 
과제 
과제는 기본적으로 매주 또는 2 주일에 한번 배부될 예정이며 
과제는 과제 배부 후 1 주일(시간엄수)과 지정된 수업시간의 
시작할 때 제출하기 바랍니다. 특별한 사유가 없는 과제 
제출기한을 지키지 않는 과제는 허용되지 않습니다. 과제 다른 
학생들과 함께 작업할 수 있지만 과제제출은 학생 개인이 각각 
제출해야 합니다. 
 
 
 
시험  
이번 학기에는 두 번의 평가시험이 있습니다. 중간시험은 대학 
중간고사 기간 수업시간에 치루고, 기말시험는 계획된 예정 
수업시간표의 기말고사 기간에 치룰 예정입니다. [토질공학]은 
지반의 역학적이고 공학적인 문제를 다루므로 모든 시험은 
Closed-book 문제로 구성됩니다. 시험은 토질공학과 관련된 
기본적 지식을 묻는 문제와 과제문제 또는 이와 관련된 문제, 
그리고 수업시간에 배웠던 내용의 응용을 다루게 될 것입니다. 
 
 
 
토질공학,  2026 년 1 학기  
 
Dr. Hangseok Choi 
3 
 
퀴즈 
퀴즈는 이전 시간에 미리 공지하거나, 혹은 별도의 공지 없이 
하지 않고 수업시간에 퀴즈를 볼 수 있습니다. 퀴즈는 이전 
수업내용 또는 과제문제와 관련된 내용으로 구성될 예정입니다. 
특히, 본격적인 토질공학 강의에 들어가기 앞서 [토질역학]에서 
배운 내용을 정리하고 복습하는 퀴즈를 학기 초에 갖도록 
하겠습니다. 
 
 
 
 
담당조교: 
조교는 여러분의 학업을 도와줄 것입니다. 조교학생의 목적은 
여러분이 수업내용을 배우고 이 수업에서 최선을 다할 수 
있도록 도와주는 것입니다. 조교를 잘 활용하는 것이 과제문제 
해결이나 강의내용 이해 및 시험 대비에 유리할 것입니다. 
 
Counseling Hours 모든 수강생들은Office hour 나 기타 사전에 면담시간을 별도로 
예약해서 Counseling hour 를 갖도록 해야 합니다. 이 개별면담 
시간에는 주로 강의내용에 대한 질문, 학교생활, 그리고 향후 
진로문제 등 다양한 주제로 담당교수와 면담을 하게 됩니다.

면담시간 
2026 년 1 학기 [토질공학] 담당교수 면담시간은 강의일정을 
고려하여 화요일 오후 1:30-3:00 입니다. Counseling hour 를 
주로 면담시간에 신청하되 혹시 시간이 안될 경우에는 별로 
면담을 담당교수에게 이메일로 신청해주세요.  
 
기타 
기타 문의사항이나 의견이 있으면 터널지반시스템 연구실 
홈페이지(http://geosys.campushomepage.com/)를 
방문해 
주세요.  
 
성적 평가 
 
수강생들이 [토질공학] 강의에 만족하고, 공학도로서 역량을 키우며 전문가로서의 
삶을 풍요롭게 하기 위해서 모든 학생들의 개별적 학업 성취를 기대 하고 있습니다. 
여러분이 배운 지식과 습득한 기술, 그리고 학업에 대한 자세에 대한 평가를 위하여   
학생들의 학업성취도는 다음 평가항목과 비율에 따라 측정됩니다. 성적평가는 
수강생들의 상대적인 성적을 기초로 이루어집니다(KUPID 절대평가 표기).
