Budgeting and Financial Management 
 
 
Instructor: Young Joo Park (youngpark@korea.ac.kr)  
Course Meetings: Tuesdays and Thursdays 9:00 – 10:15 AM 
Class Location: Korea University College of Political Science and Economics 113 
Office Hours: By appointment 
 
 
Preface 
The purpose of this course is to develop your knowledge and skills in the management of public financial 
resources. The readings, video content, weekly topics of study, and course assignments were selected to 
broaden your understanding of public budgeting and financial management and to make you a better 
public administrator. You may not “connect” with each topic, but if you engage yourself in this course, 
you will increase your ability to achieve policy objectives, overcome administrative challenges, and 
manage public organizations. 
 
Course Objectives 
By the end of this course, students should be able to: 
1. Identify what purpose public budgets serve and what types of budgets there are. 
2. Describe major government revenue sources and spending categories; 
3. Describe and demonstrate an ability to use basic financial management tools; 
4. Analyze government financial reports. 
 
Required Materials 
There is no single required textbook for this course. Instead, students will be assigned weekly 
readings and lecture slides, which may include selected book chapters, journal articles, case 
studies, and other materials. All assigned readings and/or multimedia materials must be completed 
before the class session for which they are listed. 
 
Suggested Materials (Optional) 
• 
Kioko, S., & Marlowe, J. (2023). Financial Strategy for Public Managers. Rebus Community. (Open-
source textbook) https://press.rebus.community/financialstrategy/ 
• 
Menifield, C. E. (2020). The Basics of Public Budgeting and Financial Management: A Handbook for 
Academics and Practitioners. Hamilton Books. 
• 
Wang, X. S. (2014). Financial Management in the Public Sector: Tools, Applications and Cases. 
Routledge.

Assignments: Each class will have some sort of assignment to assess your understanding of the course

과목개요 (DESCRIPTION) 
 
오퍼레이션스 관리(OM)는 기업의 제품이나 서비스를 만들어 전달하는 시스템의 
설계, 운영, 개선이라 정의된다. 즉, 제조업이든 서비스업이든 모든 조직은 
투입-전환-산출이라는 오퍼레이션스 기능을 갖는다. 이러한 오퍼레이션스 
기능에 대한 전략적 이해를 바탕으로 가치창출과 경제적 생산을 통해 기업의 
목표를 달성할 수 있도록, 오퍼레이션스 경영자 관점에서 운영 시스템을 설계, 
운영, 개선하는데 필요한 다양한 의사결정 문제들을 살펴본다. 
또한 제4 차 산업혁명과 포스트 팬데믹 시대의 공급망 관리의 중요성을 
추가적으로 인지하고, Smart Service 개념하의 OM 에서의 AI 의 역할을 집중 
조명한다. 
 
강의 목표 (OBJECTIVES) 
 
효율적이고도 유연한 오퍼레이션스 경영을 위해, 관리자는 다음 사항들을 수행할 
수 있어야 한다. 
- 제품 및 서비스 설계 및 운영 프로세스에 대한 전반적인 이해 
- 제품과 수요의 특성을 반영하는 재고 및 공급사슬 전략 
- 주요 오퍼레이션스 성과지표간 상관관계 이해 
- 품질경영의 중요성에 대한 이해 
- 정보의 가치에 대한 이해와 데이터 분석을 통한 수요예측 능력 보유 
- 입지계획 및 공급망 네트워크 설계 능력 보유  
- 리소스계획 (MRP & JIT) 
- 재고의 역할 재 조명 및 적정재고 수준 계산 
- 서비스관리에 대한 이해  
- 제반 컴퓨팅 기술(예: Excel)을 효과적으로 활용한 실질적인 문제해결 능력

Gum-Ryeong Park, PhD, Division of Health Policy & Management  
Email: gumryeong_park@korea.ac.kr  
Office Location: Hana Science Hall 370 
Office Hours: By Appointment  
 
2. COURSE OVERVIEW & OBJECTIVES 
Policy change encompasses incremental adjustments to existing structures or policies as well as the 
development of entirely new and innovative approaches. But why do policies change, for whom, and 
how? Numerous factors or events—such as political shifts or economic crises—can drive policy 
change. These changes are particularly pronounced in healthcare settings due to several reasons: (a) 
health policy involves multiple stakeholders, including governments, insurers, healthcare providers, 
and patients; (b) it must address a broad set of objectives, such as improving the quality of care and 
health outcomes; and (c) its priorities are constantly shaped by emerging challenges, such as 
demographic aging and the COVID-19 pandemic. This course provides a comprehensive 
understanding of the theories and current trends in health policy change. By the end of the course, 
students will be able to:  
• How and under what circumstances policy change is initiated in policy making process  
• Different theories of (health) policy change  
• A case study for application of policy change theories to health policy

By the end of this course, students will be able to: 
• Understand health policy as a dynamic and political process, explaining when, why, and how 
policy change occurs in different institutional and social contexts. 
• Apply major theories of health policy change—including the Multiple Streams Framework, 
Advocacy Coalition Framework, Policy Feedback Theory, and Punctuated Equilibrium Theory—to 
analyze real-world health policy cases. 
• Critically assess the implications of health policy change, identifying key actors, power 
dynamics, and distributional consequences for different populations.

진

ENGL 171 
Cross-cultural Communication in English 
 
Instructor: Minhwan Chang (장민환)  
 
 
Term: Spring, 2026 
Class: 09:00-11:45, College of Liberal Arts 222B & 223 
 
Office Hours: by appointment 
E-mail: hwantastic@korea.ac.kr 
 
 
 
TA: kuccdl@korea.ac.kr, (02) 3290-1316 
* It is required for the students to bring their own laptop and headset for the joint sessions. 
 
1. Course Description 
This course is a part of the Korea University-Waseda University Cross-Cultural Distance 
Learning Program (KWCCDLP). As a major-related elective course, the course welcomes 
undergraduate students (regardless of major and year of study) who are interested in 
cultivating the knowledge, attitudes, and skills necessary for intercultural communication 
through project-based learning. The aim of this course is to foster students' intercultural 
communicative competence through class discussions and authentic interaction with speakers 
from different linguacultural backgrounds. This course will focus on local issues. 
 
NOTE 
 The class is a 5-way joint class with Waseda University, Ritsumeikan University, 
Japan; Tamkang University, Taiwan; and Hannam University, Korea 
 There are no prerequisites for this course. Note ENGL 172 is part of the KWCCDLP. 
 This course is composed of three modules 
Module 1: KU-only class; Module 2: KU-TK joint sessions; Module 3: 5-way joint sessions. 
 Attendance will be taken.  
 The class will be conducted in-person while the joint class modules will be conducted 
online.  
* This syllabus is subject to change throughout the semester. Any changes will be posted on KULMS 
and announced in class. 
 
2. Course Objectives  
(1) Engage in problem-based learning using English as a lingua franca (ELF). 
(2) Explore current issues related to language and intercultural communication. 
(3) Develop, express, and share personal opinions, experiences, and perspectives  
(4) Learn and challenge preconceived notions about what it means to be intercultural. 
*Note: This syllabus is tentative and subject to change 
2 
3. Course Materials 
Course materials will be uploaded and available on KULMS. Students will be asked to read 
selected book chapters and news articles and will be encouraged to bring in the assigned 
readings to each class. 
 
Learning Management Systems (LMS) 
- KULMS (https://lms.korea.ac.kr/)  
Students are required to periodically access KULMS for course-related announcements and 
course materials specific to the Korea University side. Any assignments specific to the KU 
side are to be posted on this site. 
-Waseda Moodle (https://moodle.org/)  
Students are required to access Waseda Moodle (an LMS maintained by Waseda University). 
Reports, replies, responses, PowerPoint files, etc. are to be posted on this site. Some 
assignments must also be submitted to KULMS.

5. Requirements 
(1) Attendance (10%) 
Students are expected to attend all classes, as attendance is paramount in this course.  
 
Tardies:  
-1 point up until 15 minutes; -3 points afterwards 
 
Absences: 
KU-only class (Module 1), KU-TK session (Module 2): -5 points 
 
 
 
5-way joint session (Module 3): -10 points 
Attendance will be recorded after the add/drop period is over. Being late for more than 30 
minutes or leaving class early will be considered an absence. Being late for class two times 
will be counted as one absence. 유고결석 (excused absence) is not accepted for this course. 
However, ONE absence (including sickness and other reasons) will not affect the grade. Each 
absence after the one absence will take off 5-10% of the grade. In addition, according to 
university regulations, students missing more than 1/3 of the course (excluding classes held 
before the add/drop period) will automatically receive an F. Students missing more than three 
classes (including the ONE absence) will NOT receive a grade higher than a B+ regardless of 
the nature of absence. In case of absence, it is the students’ responsibility to catch up with 
what they missed by asking classmates and/or instructor. 
 
(2) Participation (10%) 
As a significant amount of time will be spent on critical thinking and discussion on thought-
provoking reading selections, students will be required to actively participate in pair work, 
small group, and whole class discussions. Participation will be graded based on their 
attentiveness and contribution in leading lively discussions. Any disruptive or disrespectful 
behavior will affect the students’ participation grade. 
 
(3) KU-TK Joint Sessions (30%) 
Individual Pre-activity (10%) 
To ensure that students are well-prepared (having read the related reading materials and being 
able to express their personal opinions on the topic) for KU-TK joint sessions, they will be 
asked to conduct an individual research on the topic and post on KULMS (by 10 AM on 
Friday). 
 
Group Pre-activity (10%) 
Students will engage in group and whole class discussions within KU. During the discussions, 
they are expected to share individual research findings written as individual pre-activity and 
then choose discussion questions and have a brief discussion. They are also required to post 
their discussion questions that they wish to discuss in KU-TK joint-session and discussion

summary on KULMS before the KU-TK joint sessions begins.  
 
Joint Session Participation (10%) 
Students will engage in KU-TK joint sessions with the participating university students 
through a video conferencing system. Students are expected to actively engage in the sessions. 
Evaluation will be based on a relative scale according to quantity and quality of contribution. 
 
(4) 5-way Joint Sessions (30%) 
Joint session reports (5%)  
Students are to write reports describing how the projects are progressing. In addition to 
summarizing, students are to expand what was discussed and include more personal opinion. 
The reports are to be uploaded to Waseda Moodle. Minimum word count is 200 words. Points 
will be deducted for late postings and those which do not meet the guidelines. Quality of 
content will also be relatively graded. 
Report: Minimum 200 words + 1 interactive question (not counted in word count) 
Posting deadline: following by Monday, 10 pm 
 
Replies and Responses (5%) 
Students must discuss their projects and post interactive questions and replies on Waseda 
Moodle. Students are to comment or reply to other students’ postings and are to respond to 
replies they have received. All posts must be made by the designated date. Points will be 
deducted for late postings. 
Posting deadlines: 
2 Replies (to other students’ interactive questions): by Wednesday 10pm 
 
2 Responses (to replies on your original question): by Thursday 10pm 
 
Individual Pre-activity (10%) 
To make sure that students are well-prepared for 5-way joint sessions, KU students are 
required to conduct individual research on their discussion topic and upload the findings to 
KULMS (by 10 AM on Friday).  
 
Joint Session Participation (10%) 
Students will engage in joint sessions with the participating university students through a 
video conferencing system. Students are expected to actively engage in the sessions.

(5) Presentation (10%) 
Students will present on their project in joint groups. PowerPoint slides must be uploaded on 
Waseda Moodle and on KULMS-Assignments by the first day of the presentation. 5 points 
will be allotted to peer evaluation (KU side only) and 5 points will be given at the instructor’s 
discretion. 
 
(6) Final report (10%)  
Students are to individually write a summary of their project/presentation by incorporating 
feedback given by their peers. The paper should have an organizational structure that 
effectively and clearly presents their research. The project/presentation should be their 
original work, including an individual perspective. Submit the final report on KULMS. In 
case of late submission, points will be deducted. 
-Format: length 2~3 pages excluding references (if any); Microsoft word, double-spaced, 12-
point font, 1inch margins 
- All reports will be run through a plagiarism detection program.

의 도움을 받기 바람)
▶ 과목개요와 목표
(1) 본 강의는 서양 정의론 일반에 대한 이해를 목표로 한다. 이를 위해 고대 그리스 철학
자들과 근대, 그리고 현대 철학자들의 정의론을 살펴본다. 특히 고전적인 정의론을 제시하는  
비극작가들, 투퀴디데스, 플라톤과 아리스토텔레스를 포함하여 근대의 흄, 벤담, 밀, 칸트, 마
르크스, 그리고 현대의 하이에크, 노직, 롤즈, 드워킨의 정의론이 중요하게 소개될 것이다. 본 
강의는 이 들 철학-사상가들의 정의론 관련 작품들에 대한 비판적 검토와 이해를 통해 ‘정의
의 기원과 탄생 조건은 무엇인가’ , ‘우리가 어떻게 타인과 함께 조화롭게 살 수 있는가’, ‘불
평등은 과연 어떻게 정당화될 수 있는가’, ‘국가는 어떤 분배적 정의를 추구해야 하는가’, ‘ 누
가 정의로운 인간인가’와 같은 물음들에 대한 합리적이며 지혜로운 답을 모색한다. 
(2) 무엇보다 본 강의의 주된 목표는 정의론 관련 텍스트의 논쟁 형식과 내용을 분석하는 
것이다. 본 강의의 전반부는 서양 정의론의 고전적인 작품으로 평가되는 아이스퀼로스와 소포
클레스의 비극작품들, 튀퀴디데스의 <펠로폰네스스 전쟁사>, 그리고 소크라테스의 <변론>편과 
<크리톤>편, 정의론의 전범으로 평가되는 플라톤의 <국가>편 그리고 아리스토텔레스의 정의
론을 <니코마코스 윤리학>과 <정치학>을 통해 살펴본다. 강의의 후반부에선 근,현대의 중요한 
문제로 등장하는 ‘분배적 정의’(distributive justice)의 문제를 5가지 유형의 정의론를 갖고 비
판적 관점에서 비교,평가한다. 공리주의 정의론(J.Bentham, J.S.Mill), 마르크스 정의론, 자유 
소유권적 정의론(Hayek, Nozick)과 자유 평등주의적 정의론(J.Rawls, R. Dworkin, 운평등주의
luck-egalitarianism 포함), 그리고 공적주의(meritocracy) 정의론이 여기에 해당된다. 고대부
터 현대까지의 정의론사에 관한 이러한 통시적 접근은, 또한, 정의에 관한 다양한 실천적 사고 
또는 추론을 필요로 하는 역사적 사례나 사고실험에 관한 예들을 통해 구체적 상황에서 올바
른 행위란 무엇인가에 관한 철학적 사고를 훈련하는 방법을 익히는 과정이 될 것이다.

Academic English (Public Health) 
 
Spring 2026 
 
 
Welcome to Academic English class. In this class, we will be studying English at the intermediate 
level, involving speaking, listening, reading and writing, with the goal of improving your ability 
in all of these skills. Many topics will be used to practise your English, including those topics 
related to your major. 
 
This class is very important for your studies at Korea University. Many of your textbooks and 
lectures will be in English, as will a number of written resources required for research you must 
conduct. You may also take whole classes in English, in which you will need to write essays, 
have discussions and make spoken presentations in English. Additionally, some of you may study 
in an English-speaking country after graduation. For these reasons, having an efficient level of 
English is extremely important to you. 
 
By the end of the semester, it is expected that students can: 
 
• have a discussion on a range of health-related topics in which you give an opinion, and 
express agreement or disagreement with the opinions of others; 
• write an essay using clear sentences and correct paragraphs, and in correct essay format; 
• make a formal speech on a topic related to health with clarity and confidence. 
 
Text  Teacher produced text – Academic English. David Michael Duke. Korea University. 
 
Evaluation  A final grade will be given to each student based on the following: 
 
• 20% attendance and participation; 
• 30% midterm exam (having a discussion); 
• 20% writing task (writing a research essay); 
• 30% final exam (making a speech). 
 
Students are expected to attend all classes and must successfully complete all exams and 
assignments. Under Korea University policy, students are permitted to have a small number of 
absences each semester without penalty. This includes absence due to illness and any other 
officially recognized reason. Any number of absences beyond this will result in points deducted. 
In addition, missing more than a third of all classes, or 11 or more absences, will, as stated by 
Korea University guidelines, automatically result in an F grade. 
Grades will be displayed at the end of the semester. If you think your teacher may have made a 
mistake with calculating your final grade, ask your teacher to check your score. These final grades 
are non-negotiable and cannot be changed for any other reason. 
 
Most importantly, remember that the grade you receive at the end of the semester should be 
regarded as just a general description of your performance in the class over the course of the 
semester. The emphasis of your studies should be on learning the content and skills studied in 
class.   
 
Rules  The following rules must be remembered. Not following any of these rules may result in 
points lost. 
 
1) Always attend class. Students more than a few minutes late will be marked as late, and 
students more than 30 minutes late will be marked as absent. Also, don’t leave your class 
until the end of the lesson. If you must go to the toilet or bathroom, ask your teacher and 
be as quick as possible. 
2) Always bring your textbook, paper, pens and pencils, and a dictionary to class. 
3) Listen to your teacher and don’t talk socially to your friends. Remain active and awake 
throughout the lesson. Also, turn off your mobile phones and keep them in your bags. 
4) Do all exercises and homework your teacher gives you. 
5) Enjoy the class and study hard to improve your English. 
 
Class Plan  For this semester, classes will proceed according to the following schedule.  
 
Week 1  Class and Student Introduction 
Weeks 2 – 6  Having a Discussion and Giving an Opinion 
Week 7  Writing in Paragraphs 
Week 8  Midterm Exam 
Weeks 9 – 11  Writing an Essay 
Weeks 12 – 15  Making a Speech 
Week 16  Final Examss 
 
This is a general plan and can possibly change. In addition, remember to talk to your teacher if 
you have a problem with the class. Good luck!

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습

Course Description 
 
The objective of this course is to introduce students to marketing analytics, i.e., the world of 
quantitative approaches to analysis for marketing decision making. Examples include how to 
quantitatively make positioning decisions, how to configure new products, what price to charge, how 
to understand the effect of advertising over time, and how to forecast the diffusion of newly 
developed products. 
 
The challenges driven by uncertainty in today’s marketing environment require managers to make 
high-quality decisions. Good decisions call for good information, and such information is ultimately 
produced through accurate model building and data analytics. We live in a data-rich environment and 
in the era of AI, where algorithmic approaches enable a high level of automation in marketing 
decision making. 
 
Marketing analytics and AI are introduced as decision-support tools that help marketers better 
understand market phenomena, develop informed forecasts, and choose appropriate marketing 
actions in a timely manner. 
 
The course format will be a mixture of lectures, discussions, and lab sessions. Students are 
encouraged to read related materials ahead of class. We will work through many real-world 
marketing examples and cases that require data-driven thinking, often supported by analytics tools. 
For data-related work and problem solving, we will mainly use RStudio, along with Excel for 
selected topics. The focus is on how to use analytical outputs for marketing decisions, rather than on 
advanced programming techniques.

Course Material 
 
There is no designated textbook for this course. Students may use any materials that are relevant to 
the weekly topics at their own convenience. The use of AI environments is encouraged for preparing 
class discussion and for supporting individual learning.  
 
Common introductory frameworks will be provided in the form of lecture notes in PDF format. 
These materials will be uploaded sequentially to the LMS as the course progresses. The common 
materials we share will be posted on the course website including datasets, exercise problem sets, 
etc.

All exams are not cumulative and will cover class lecture and class discussion only. Exams are 
closed-book by default. However, specific materials may be announced in advance and permitted for 
use during the exam when appropriate. Exam questions focus on interpretation, intuition, and 
decision making rather than technical derivations.  
 
Assignments include both take-home work and in-class exercises, completed individually or in 
groups. Class participation is evaluated based on attendance as well as the frequency and quality of 
in-class contributions, including discussions and presentations.

n There will be two real-time online lecture sessions each

students are responsible for checking their attendance 
during every session.
Course Management
n This course introduces the emerging field of neuroscience 
known as social neuroscience. 
n Lectures will cover key topics in the field, including self-
perception, face processing, facial impressions, 
stereotypes, empathy, social emotions, self-esteem, 
morality, fairness, and altruism. 
n Additionally, this course will explore how advancements in 
neuroscience may influence and reshape various aspects 
of future society through group discussions and critical 
analysis.

review them thoroughly!

approval).

elementary statistics.

Course 
Objectives 
COURSE OUTLINE 
Introduction 
Architectural Design Studio 3 builds over the previous 2nd year studios, advancing one step further in building scale, urban 
significancy (including the historical and social issues any city) and program complexity. At the same time the students have to 
be more conscious on the integration of the technical side of architecture, especially safety and accessibility. 
Topic 
The students will work on the subject of A COMMUNITY CENTER, to accommodate a public program to provide a service to the 
local community.  (실버타운 복합문화센터) 
도심 역세권 실버타운 COMMUNITY CENTER 
현재 강남의 화려하고 호화로운 모습 뒤에는 여전히 1980 년대의 낙후된 흔적이 남아 있는 곳들이 적지 않다. 천정부지로 
치솟았던 강남의 땅값은 최근 부동산 시장 침체와 건설 경기 위축으로 인해 하락세를 보이며, 과거처럼 투자가치가 보장되지 않는 
상황이다. 그럼에도 불구하고, 일부 투자자들은 여전히 강남 곳곳을 탐색하며 숨겨진 기회를 모색하고 있다. 
이와 함께, 서울시는 ‘역세권 활성화’ 사업을 통해 사업성이 부족한 토지의 용도를 상향 조정하고, 일부를 기부채납받아 낙후된 
역세권 지역의 개발을 유도하고 있다. 그러나 경기 침체로 인해 개발 사업의 추진 속도가 더뎌지고, 기존의 부동산 공급 과잉 
문제와 맞물려 시장의 불확실성이 커지고 있다. 
이러한 가운데, 베이비부머(1955~1963 년생) 세대의 대거 은퇴와 기대수명의 증가로 인해 노인 주거 문제는 더욱 심화되고 있다. 
특히 기존의 노인복지시설은 수요를 충족하지 못하고 있으며, 고소득·고학력층을 중심으로 전통적인 요양시설보다 자율성과 
품격을 유지할 수 있는 주거형 실버타운에 대한 선호도가 높아지고 있다. 그러나 도심 내 노인 주거시설을 조성하려면 높은 토지 
비용과 사회적 합의라는 난관을 넘어야 하는 상황이다. 
고급 실버타운은 일반적인 교외형 실버타운과 달리 도심 역세권에 위치해야 한다. 하지만 현재의 부동산 시장 침체 속에서 신규 
공급을 늘리는 것은 쉽지 않으며, 개발 사업이 경제적 논리만으로 추진되기 어려운 만큼, 공급자와 사용자의 이해관계를 조정하는 
정치적·사회적 합의와 계층 간 상생이 필수적이다. 
이번 학기에 다룰 잠원동 지역은 이러한 문제 해결과 더불어 창의적이고 혁신적인 건축적 대안을 요구한다. 단순한 디자인 차원의 
접근이 아니라, 정치·사회·경제적 요소를 종합적으로 고려한 통합적 해결책을 모색하는 것이 이번 학기의 핵심 목표다. 
Site 
Specific site and bundling to be announced in the course introduction lecture on day 1. (강남 신사역세권) 
 
Course Objectives 
This task enables students to confront all aspects concerning a building for public use. Beyond the necessary functionality of the 
 
ARCH333. Syllabus 2026. page 2 
project, students must fully comprehend the characteristics of the community they serve, striving to interpret its practical and 
cultural needs. Essentially, the building should represent the community, and the community should see itself reflected in it.
"Community" may refer to all residents in a neighborhood or a specific group within it.   
The process begins with analyzing the physical and social characteristics of the context and its inhabitants, conducted as a group 
(class activity). The aim is to identify the community's traits and needs, shaping an appropriate program for the building. Any
program offering services to the local community is suitable (e.g., cultural center, community center, new-generation market, 
ateliers, etc.). The specific program will be determined post-analysis. The class may either adopt a common program or explore 
different, yet comparable, programs. An analysis of relevant case studies will conclude the preparatory phase, providing design 
process references. 
 
In the design phase, students are free to adopt the design philosophy they believe in, provided they logically justify their choices. 
Creativity and experimentation are encouraged. However, designs must also address certain practical and functional issues, such 
as accessibility and safety (PC 7), which will be elaborated on in specific lectures and instructions. Designs may be developed
either individually or in small groups (2-3 people). 
The course will coordinate activities with other studios. Particularly, the midterm review will be shared, and some lectures will
feature guest speakers or instructors from these studios. 
Course activities  
—  Commons critique sessions (pin-up, PPT projection) and discussions on analysis and design process and results  
—  Individual tutorial (desk review) on design process and personal development feedback 
—  Workshops to practise some relevant aspects of the topic 
—  Lectures and seminars to provide more solid theoretical background  
—  Field Trips to experience first hand relevant case studies. 
—  Common Public Presentation with invited critics, graded (at least two, Midterm and Final)

Performance 
Criteria 
06. Site and  External Space Planning 
Ability to analyze and evaluate the natural and human environment of a site, understand the characteristics of the region, and plan external 
spaces, site, and site planning based on an understanding of Urban Landscape Planning. 
10. Architecture and Urban Planning 
Ability to understand the basic principles of urban planning, community planning, and District Unit Plan, and to perform town planning. 
C02. Sustainability 
The program must be able to encompass values of sustainability in architecture and urbanism, grounded in a broad understanding of 
coexistence between humans and the natural environment and the responsibility of environmental conservation. 
C04. Fostering Creative Problem Solving Skills 
The program must be able to demonstrate nurturing students' ability to creatively and innovatively solve a wide array of potential problems 
in the field of architecture, encompassing areas such as design, technology, and theory.

Assignment 1  Case Studies/Site Research 
Assignment 2  Site Proposal, An Outline of the Program, Design Intent

ATTENDANCE 
Attendance and punctuality are expected. According to KU regulations, 30% unjustified absences per semester can result in a 
final F score. Whenever you have a cause that prevents you from attending the course, please provide us with a certificate 
(sickness, job interview, etc.). Each unjustified absence makes you lose 1/5th of the attendance score and that day's share of 
participation score. Studio time is to concentrate on studio work and participate in critics or attend lectures. Regularity in 
everyday work and development and the constant process will be evaluated better than sudden final last-minute results. 
PRESENTATIONS SUBMISSIONS 
Students must attend all presentations, and submit all assignments complete and on time. Incomplete assignments, incomplete 
presentations, late submissions or late attendance in presentation sessions, will have a negative impact on the final grade. 
LANGUAGE (only for English mediated groups) 
The official language of the course in this studio is English. Please plan all presentations and texts (included those in drawings) 
in English language. Note also that although we understand how tough is it to follow basic courses in a foreign language, if you 
get used to communicate and express yourself in English, your skill will improve very fast over the following semesters.

∙ [출석] 
 -1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가능, 단 출
석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함
∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 모든 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정
진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중
히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

-모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
-과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
-협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
-시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
-한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

야 대상 학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습
을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수

Course Objectives: 
 
Academic English is not a conversation class. It is a formal class to prepare you for university and life 
beyond.  
 
This course is designed to improve your speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills for academic 
applications. Speaking and writing will be the primary focus of class activities. Listening and reading skills 
will be taught during the sixteen weeks, although they will be focused on more during assignments and self-
study activities. The primary focus will be on writing, discussion and presentation. By the end of the 
sixteen weeks, I hope that you will have:  
 
● first and foremost, improved your English ability  
● the ability to discuss and present topics appropriately and professionally in English 
● learned the importance of communication and teamwork  
● become more adept in verbal, non-verbal and written communication  
● built your academic vocabulary  
● become a critical thinker and an effective independent learner  
● gained confidence in your English ability and not rely solely on AI. 
 
 
Office Hours & Communication: 
 
My aim is to help you improve as much as possible. Therefore, I welcome your queries about anything, 
small or big. Communication is fundamental in so many aspects of life, so it is better to ask than to remain 
in the dark. I am also available by appointment or via Zoom or after class time. There will be times when I 
am unable to answer your questions right away due to my schedule and other students’ inquiries; 
please understand this and make an appointment if you want to meet me via online. I will make time 
for you if you let me know in advance. 
 
My Gmail account, hawkplynn@gmail.com and KULMS will be utilized for basic communication, 
announcements and course work uploads, so it is essential that you always check KULMS and your 
email.

This class is not like your other classes.  It is not a lecture class, so you must be active 
instead of passive in this class.  The following are some guidelines for conduct which I 
expect in this class.  Adherence to these expectations will assist in enhancing your English 
proficiency as well as improving chances of a good grade.

appointment to speak to me. 
 
This course is about communication, and it is extremely important for us to understand each 
other.  Feel free to ask me at any time to repeat or explain something if you do not 
understand.  
 
 
Please remember that it is your responsibility to tell me if there is something you don’t 
understand or need assistance.

2. ENGLISH 
 
You must use English in class: Do not use Korean or another language. 
You must try as best as you can to communicate all of your thoughts in English.  If you 
cannot find the correct words in English, try to find some other way to express yourself 
(description, body language, face expressions, drawing pictures, etc.).  Be creative.  
 
It is a requirement of this course that you use English in this class. 
 
 
 
3. PREPAREDNESS 
 
Be prepared for class. At a minimum, bring your notebook for note taking and file folder to 
every class. You are expected to read ahead any information, course material, pages, 
etc. your professor assigns to you. Being prepared includes by evidence of study outside 
of class; accessing and reviewing KULMS’s Announcements/Course Materials; being aware 
of due dates. 
 
One thing to get you through university is being organized and prepared for each class; 
hence the GF and file folder requirement. 
 
 
4. PARTICIPATION  
 
 Participate actively in the class.  Don’t be afraid to speak in class, and don’t worry 
about making mistakes.  
 
      It is important to remember mistakes do not matter to me at all, so please do your     
      best. 
 
 Incorrect speaking is better than no speaking. Perfect English is not necessary,  
but class participation is necessary.  It is a part of your grade.  
 
 Use your level of interest and motivation to create, expand and express your ideas, 
thoughts, feelings and questions. Even if you are not confident, you will have the chance 
to do well. Overtime, your confidence in speaking up in class will improve. 
 
 Use class time wisely and be prepared for each class.  
 
 Complete assignments thoroughly in a timely manner. 
 
Do not sleep in class. This will affect negatively on your participation grade. 
 
Involve yourself in every class activity; be positive and ready to learn and participate 
including asking questions. 
 
5. ASSIGNMENTS 
 
 Complete all assignments in a timely matter. Late assignments or projects will result in 
points deducted: 1 point for each day late including the weekends and holidays.  
 
 Copying assignments, homework or cheating on tests will automatically get you an “F/0". 
See also page 6. 
 
 Do not rehash and/or submit work (old or new) from another course/class. 
 
 
 If you are absent, make sure to contact me or ask your classmates about what you 
missed.   
 
 
 
 Submitted work must include a cover page, be paginated and include subtitles when 
necessary. Do not include the course material or lecture notes with your 
assignments. 
 
 As #4, use class time wisely and be prepared for each class and complete assignments 
thoroughly in a timely manner.

 Create a GF for this class to keep your assignments, etc. safe and organized.

6. ABSENCES   
 
Come to class every day and on time and stay in class.  
 
 
If you are going to be absent from class for any reason, I will mark you as absent for that 
class, but I allow you 4 absences in the semester without any academic penalty.  
 
 If you will be absent for a special reason, and you wish to be excused from attending class, 
you must tell me before the class.  In addition, you can apply for an excused absence 
through the Korea University portal. It will still count as an absence, so use your free 
absences wisely.  
 
 
Just because you are absent for any reason does not absolve you of your responsibility. You 
are still responsible for content missed. 
 
 
Proper documentation must be provided for all special school-related absences: illness, 
death in the family or military. NOTE: a prescription is not valid documentation. 
 
Sleeping in class. This will affect negatively on your class attendance as well as your 
participation grade.  
 
Students missing 9 classes total will automatically receive a grade of “F”. 
 
See page 6 for more information. 
 
7. GRADES   
 
Although important to you and your GPA, learning a foreign language is not only about 
grades.  It is a skill that can be life changing for your future.  Developing good English 
language skills can open opportunities for employment and future study abroad, it can help 
you connect to the world beyond the borders of your country; and it can enhance your 
understanding of other cultures.  Please view this course as an opportunity to build your 
future, and not simply as an influence on your GPA.   
 
Furthermore, in Korea, English is often used as a measure of a person’s value in society, but 
NOT in this class.  It is a useful tool just as mathematics, critical thinking or creativity.   
The grades I assign to you are not an evaluation of you personally nor reflective of my likes 
or dislikes.  It is simply an evaluation of your performance in class tasks and activities.  
 
See page 7-8 for detailed assessments. 
 
8. TIME 
 
Be in class on time.  Students who are late are disturbing for the class and for me. Enter the 
class quietly. If you are more than 15 minutes late, I will mark you absent for that class.   
 
If you are late 3 times, I will mark you absent for one class. This will NOT count as one of 
the allowed absences in #6.

Classrooms are sometimes arranged in rows. It is advisable to avoid sitting in the back since 
you might miss important information; it can be a sign you are shy but also a sign you’re

Therefore, sit in the front or close to the front of the class. Choose a seat for a few 
weeks, so I can remember who you are including your name.  
 
Depending on the assignment, new seating arrangements maybe created.

Please use the break time BETWEEN CLASSES for getting drinks, making phone calls and 
going to the washroom.  If it is an emergency, you don’t have to ask me for permission to go 
to the washroom.  If it is not an emergency, you do not have to go. 
 
 
13. MANNERS MAKETH THE PERSON 
 
Show respect and courtesy to EVERYONE in the class.  Acknowledge people with a 
simple hi or hello, or good morning/afternoon or a nod. (Basic Communication)  
 
Please be respectful of your classmates and help me to provide a positive and encouraging 
learning environment.   
 
Use of offensive language will not be tolerated (English, Korean, etc.).  
 
Your enjoyment of this class and the development of your academic English skills depend on 
the attitude you bring to this class every day.  Please be positive, be polite and be kind. 
 
 
 
Speaking English isn’t only about fluency. It’s about being in class, doing the work, understanding, 
and following instructions and making an effort. 
 
 
 
 
KU’S AI POLICY 
 
 
The use of generative AI in class without basic guidelines. Itt may negatively impact the quality of teaching and 
learning. Common negative impacts include: 
 
(1) Violations of academic integrity, such as plagiarism and cheating. 
(2) Decline in critical thinking, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills due  
     to over-reliance on generative AI. 
(3) Acquisition of inaccurate or biased information. 
(4) Reinforcement of entrenched stereotypes.

Evaluation Method 
 
Typically, a maximum of about 40-45% of you will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”. Evaluation in this class is 
based strictly on performance, and not on English language proficiency. All parts of the evaluation system 
must be completed in an exceptional manner (above and beyond) if you want to get an “A+”.   
 
I employ rubrics where students are evaluated on organization (see below), content (see below) and 
language (see below). More criteria will be given when the projects are assigned. Many students ask for a 
word count for written assignments. My philosophy is that students should be focusing on answering the 
question and providing enough support for their answer. So concentrate on fully exploring your answer.  
This is done through research (what have others said on the topic); planning (brainstorming and outline and 
deciding on your answer), and editing (checking your work for mistakes in organization, content and 
language).

Course Description & Goals  
English for Contemporary Issues is designed as a thoroughly STUDENT-CENTERED CLASS that fosters critical perspectives for understanding and 
analyzing problems across various fields in today’s world. Using a wide range of materials from texts to visual media sources, the course provides 
opportunities for students to independently unpack complex discourses related to politics, economics, technologies, media, human relationships, and 
so on allowing them to collaborate, coordinate, and engage meaningfully with their own and others’ ideas. By exploring the diverse interests and 
dynamics of contemporary society with English, the course goes beyond language development and helps students use English as a practical tool to 
understand social complexity. The ultimate goal of this course is to help students cultivate a critical lens through which you can better understand their 
place in the world and recognize the roles you should play within it. 
 
Attendance Policy  
As for the attendance policy, 2 unexcused absences are allowed without deduction. Additional absence requests (such as sickness, family affairs, 
traveling, internship, job interview, double-major interview, conference, contest, festival, club activities, awards, and so on) will NOT be approved for 
any reason other than reservist training (예비군). Participation in reservist training, which involves fulfilling duties required by law, is considered an 
exception if documentation is submitted; however, a document issued by any department office at KU or other institutions out of KU does not 
guarantee anything regarding absence at all, thus use 2 free chances provided by this course cleverly to cover your own excuse. 4 points are deducted 
from the 3rd absence and a failing grade is given for more than 8 absences including 2 unexcused ones. Except for 2 free absences, absence itself gives 
you not just 4 points deduction but also another 2 points deduction on your participation due to your lack of an in-class activity on that absent day. 
Late arriving twice are counted as absence.   
 
Class Participation with 3 Required Activities [50] 
This course is designed as THE SUPER STUDENT-ORIENTED CLASS in which you should play the role of facilitators and active participation serves as the 
primary basis for assessment. Participation consists of three major components: 
1. 
Writing in-class notes and archiving online materials on KU LMS: You are expected to critically analyze the social issues addressed in each session 
based on your own interpretations. This involves taking handwritten notes during class and saving relevant online materials to a personal archive 
on KU LMS. Handwritten notes must be submitted at the end of each class. In addition, AI prompts, online articles, images, videos, and any other 
collected resources should be continuously uploaded and organized in the personal archive throughout the semester. 
2. 
Group discussions: Drawing on these notes and archived materials, you participate in group discussions with randomly assigned classmates.  
3. 
Whole class discussion: Each group is expected to synthesize its ideas into a coherent position and present to the entire class. 
Together, these three components constitute the full participation requirements for each class session. 
 
Team Project for Contemporary Issues [20]  
Team project is done with 3 to 4 students in one team delivering an in-depth presentation on an assigned topic. All the members of one team manage 
75-minute class period by themselves. All team members are required to participate as speakers on the stage. The presentation is allocated 30 to 35 
minutes, followed by Q&A session for 20 to 25 minutes. Then, during the remaining time after the presentation, the students in the audience have the 
opportunity to share their own analyses, which they have previously saved in their personal archives. The presentation can be primarily formal in style, 
presenters are encouraged to incorporate a variety of formats such as role-play, interviews, talk shows, or performance elements.  
 
Archiving Contemporary Issues with Your Analysis [15]  
This assignment is designed for students, as audience members, to collect and analyze necessary materials before team project presentations in order 
to better understand other teams’ subjects. When each team presents on a different topic, you are expected to 1) gather at least three different types 
of materials (such as text articles, images, videos, AI-generated conversations, etc.) and 2) triangulate these materials to produce a comprehensive 
analysis of 300 words or more in your own words. This process must be completed as a pre-class assignment, submitted prior to the presentations, 
and all collected materials must be uploaded to the KU LMS in order for the submission to be considered valid. 
 
Panel Discussion [10] 
A panel discussion is a student-leading activity where 3-4 students are serving as individual panelists who are assigned a hypothetical role as an expert 
in a particular field. Student panelists are required to prepare a one-page report of their content to facilitate the panel discussion and upload it to KU 
LMS prior to the session. Based on these materials, the remaining students engage as audience members in this activity through a free Q&A session 
with a critical question.  
 
Wrap-up Report [5] 
A wrap-up report includes what you achieve from all class activities including reading, discussion, analysis, and presentation. At the end of the semester, 
you gather the whole data you learn in a class and compose a reflection paper as a wrap-up report. It needs to be uploaded onto KU LMS at the end of 
the semester.

This course highly requires you to engage in class actively. Your enthusiastic attitude for communicating with others and respectful mindset for them

and 2) leaving a classroom without a notice especially during the students’ presentation. If this rule is violated, you are considered absent in that you 
are not fully concentrating on a required activity which should be done in a collaborative way with other peers.  
 
Guidelines for Using AI in Class Activities 
This course does not prohibit the use of AI; however, AI-generated materials are only permitted when the following requirements are met: 1) Prompts 
must be conversational rather than seeking a single, definitive answer (e.g., Questions such as “My position is X based on evidence A, B, C; what are 
three pieces of evidence that support the opposing position?” are allowed, whereas questions that simply ask for a definitive answer, such as “Explain 
the pros and cons of this issue,” are not permitted.), 2) For assignments that must be written in your own words, you must compose your text with 
your language not with AI-polished one, 3) if you use AI-generated responses, you must properly cite the source and attach the exact prompt used as 
a separate appendix.

 이 강의는 외국인 재학생(수준: 중급)을 위한 교양필수 강의로서, 학문 세계의 핵심 주제들
에 대해 한국어로 사고하고 표현하는 능력을 향상시켜 ‘자유, 정의, 진리’를 달성하는 데에 
목적이 있다. 이를 위해 토론과 발표를 통해 자신의 생각을 한국어로 자유롭게 표현하며, 다
양한 언어적 표현과 기초 교양 지식을 익혀 대학생으로서의 정의로운 인성을 기르고, 인문, 
사회, 과학 분야의 다양한 융복합적 주제에 대한 진지한 탐구를 한다. 학문세계의 탐구Ⅰ에
서는 윤리, 문화, 경제, 과학에 대한 탐구를 통해 글로벌 인재로 성장하기 위한 학문적 소양
을 기른다.
■ 학습목표
(1) 기본적인 교양 지식을 이해함으로써 대학생으로서 갖춰야 할 학문적 교양을 갖출 수 있다.
(2) 인문학, 사회과학, 자연과학 분야의 다양한 텍스트를 읽고 비판적, 융·복합적으로 사고할 수 있다.
(3) 학문적 토론 및 발표에 필요한 다양한 언어 기능을 익혀 실제로 토론과 발표를 수행할 수 있다.
(4) 상황이나 목적에 맞게 청중을 설득하는 발표 기술을 기르고, 학술적 쟁점이나 사회 문
제에 대해 자신의 의견을 주장하고 상대방의 의견을 청취, 비판할 수 있다.

Course Overview 
Digital data has become a fundamental component of modern Earth and environmental science 
research. The volume of environmental data collected from observations, monitoring networks, 
and simulations continues to grow rapidly. Effectively utilizing these large datasets requires 
computational approaches for data processing, analysis, and visualization. This course introduces 
the fundamental concepts and practical techniques required to analyze Earth and environmental 
datasets. Students will learn how to process, analyze, and visualize geological and environmental 
data using Python. Through hands-on exercises, the course emphasizes extracting scientific 
insights from real datasets. Beyond basic data processing, the course also introduces numerical 
analysis concepts that support modeling and predictive analysis in environmental sciences. By 
integrating data analysis with numerical methods, students will develop analytical skills needed to 
investigate real environmental problems using data-driven approaches. 
 
Course Objectives 
• Understand the role of digital data in Earth and environmental sciences. 
• Apply data-driven approaches to scientific problems in geoscience. 
• Use Python libraries such as Pandas and NumPy to explore datasets. 
• Visualize environmental data using time-series, spatial plots, and interactive graphics. 
• Interpret and communicate scientific results obtained from environmental data analysis. 
• Apply basic numerical analysis techniques used in environmental modeling. 
• Evaluate uncertainty and error in environmental datasets.

to Machine Learning. Springer. 
2. Additional materials provided by instructors.

POLI391 Nationalism and World Politics  
 
Course Description 
 
How does nationalism shape interactions between states? Understanding this question has 
increasingly become important with the resurgence of nationalism across the globe. In this course, 
students will explore the diverse and complex nature of nationalism and evaluate its role in world 
politics. Students will first examine the different meanings of nationalism in international relations, 
such as national identity, patriotism, and nationalistic sentiments. With these conceptual building 
blocks, students will examine how nationalism affects states’ foreign policy behavior as well as 
their perception of Self and Other, discussing issues such as war, ethnic conflict, territorial disputes, 
military occupation, and international trade.  
Through this course, students will:  
• 
Develop a deep understanding of various meanings of nationalism in international 
relations  
• 
Understand and be able to use key theoretical concepts related to nationalism to explain 
major international security and economic issues 
• 
Critically interpret and assess others’ arguments in political science research  
• 
Develop active discussion skills  
 
Course Materials  
All course materials are either available on the course website or through the KU library. 
 
 
Assignment and Grading  
• Class Participation and attendance (20%) 
• Mid-term Exam (20%)  
• Group Project (40%): Presentation (10%)+ Individual Prep (10%)+Group work (20%)  
• Final Exam (20%) 
 
 
2 
 
 
• Class Participation and attendance (20%): Students are expected to come to every class 
session. Six or more absences will result in course failure (F). Any excused absence due to 
illness or personal emergency will require documentation and is limited to three times in 
maximum per semester. Being late will be considered as ¼ absence. Students are also 
expected to come to class after completing assigned readings and actively participate in 
class discussions. Students are strongly encouraged to share their thoughts and respond to 
each other’s comments in a respectful way. 
• 
Mid-term Exam (20%) and Final Exam (20%)  
• 
Final Group Project (40%): Students will be divided into groups of five to seven, depending 
on class size, and will draft a speech that reflects the nationalism of an assigned country. 
Each student will first write an individual memo characterizing the assigned country’s 
nationalism (due June 1 at 1:30 p.m.). Based on these memos, group members will discuss 
the content of the speech and collaboratively produce a draft and a reasoning memo. A 
separate assignment sheet will provide additional details. The group speech draft and 
reasoning memo are due June 10 at 1:30 p.m., and teams will deliver their speeches 
during the final weeks of the course. 
 
Late Policy 
Assignments will receive a 1/3 grade deduction for each day that they are past due unless 
permission for an extension has been granted by the instructor. Therefore, an “A” paper that is 1-
day late, will receive a grade of “A-,” 2-days late will receive a grade of “B+,” and so on. 
 
Academic Honesty 
Violations of academic integrity are among the most serious offenses that students can commit; 
any violation may result in consequences at both the course and institutional levels.

적ㆍ조직적 차원에서 마주하게 되는 상황에 대하여 논의하고, 그

민하는 자리가 될 수 있게 운영하려 함. 이를 위해 학습자의 적극
적인 참여가 필요함

spectives.

knowledge, the course will help students cultivate the ability to generate innovative ideas.

교과목 개요
의료기기란 사람이나 동물에게 단독 또는 조합하여 사용되는 기구·기계·장치·재료 또
는 이와 유사한 제품으로 정의한다. 현대 의료의 발전은 약물뿐만 아니라 이런 의료
기기의 발전을 통해 이루어졌다고 해도 과언이 아니다. 학생들은 장비를 통해 얻은 
임상결과에 대해서는 많은 학습 기회가 있지만 이들 기기의 발전과정과 미래에 대해
서는 전문적인 학습 기회가 많지 않았다. 앞으로의 의료기기의 주요한 아이디어를 생
각하고 새로운 기기를 창출하는 일은 우리 의료인들의 몫이라 볼 때 조기에 의료기
기에 대한 소양을 갖추는 일은 중요하리라 생각한다. 이를 위해 다양한 의료분야에서
의 의료기기에 대해 소개하고 토의 하고자 한다. 각 분야의 전문 교수님들이 암치료 
장비, 영상진단장비, 수술 장비, 재활관련 장비, 심혈관계 장비에 대해 알려주고 토의
한다.

ㅇ 출석
  - 무단결석 1회 시 2점을 감점, 지각의 경우 1회 시 1점을 감점
  - 무단결석 4회 이상이면 최고 학점이 A0, 무단결석 5회 이상이면 최고
    학점이 B+임
  - 사유가 있는 결석의 경우 출석으로 인정 : 사전에 먼저 알릴 필요 없고
    추후 1주 안에 포털의 출석인정시스템을 통해 출석 인정을 신청하면 됨
  - 수업일수의 1/3을 초과하여 결석하는 경우 F학점을 부여(학교 규정)
ㅇ 학점 부여
  - 학점 부여 시 중간고사의 경우 각자 취득한 점수에 ‘40/중간고사의 
    만점’을 곱한 환삼점수를, 기말고사의 경우는 각자 취득한 점수에 ‘50/
    기말고사의 만점’을 곱한 환산점수를 사용 
  - 위 환산점수에 출석점수를 더하여 총점을 계산하고 이를 기반으로 하여
    학점을 부여
개요
‘비주류의 경제학’은 현대의 주류경제학, 즉 ‘신고전파 경제학(Neoclassical 
Economics)’과는 다른 이론적 기반을 가지고 있는 비주류 경제학, 그중에서
도 특히 ‘포스트 케인지언(Post-Keynesian)’ 경제학의 전반적인 연구주제 및 
내용을 소개하는 과목이다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

Ⅰ. Objectives &
     Overview
•
The purpose is to acquire the ability to systematically and scientifically study and 
research physical education by learning the types, values, and analytical methods 
of the diverse information existing within physical education, along with 
mastering the application and utilization methods of computers, which are 
essential elements in sports science research. Furthermore, through the learning 
process, university students majoring in physical education will acquire the basic 
computer usage and data analysis methods that they need to learn.
•
This course is composed of a process to understand the increasingly diversified 
and expanded sports information resulting from the development of the data 
science field, to examine its value, and to acquire practical skills to analyze and 
utilize this information.
Ⅱ. Summary
4
1. Elements and structure of sports information
• Explores the development of sports information.
• Explores the elements and structure of sports information.
• Explores the types and attributes of various types of information in sports and the 
value of their use
2. A look at the future of data science and how it's changing.
3. Understand the structure and composition of computer systems
• Learn about the types of hardware that make up a computer and their roles, as well 
as the characteristics and connections of each part.
4. Operating System(OS) and main applications
• Learn the basic usage of the OS (Windows) and how to utilize key software

Office Hours: Every Thursday 1:30pm - 2:45pm in Asan Science Hall 619.
Course Overview: This undergraduate course is a 1st part of a two-semester sequence in topology. This
is a proof-based introduction course for math majors. Topology is an abstract subject that generalizes the
notion of open (and closed) intervals in R to general sets (including Rn and beyond), so that the notion
of continuous maps can be defined without using Euclidean distance on Rn. While the subject may feel
abstract, it is
1. a foundation of modern geometry (differential, algebraic, arithmetic, etc), and
2. an essential tool for “advanced” analysis in upper years (e.g. measure theory, complex analysis, etc).
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to
1. (Abstract) Topological Spaces, Open/Closed Sets, and Continuous Maps: what do they mean?
2. Metric Spaces (and various examples): what makes them so special?
3. Compact Sets: what do they mean and how they act under continuous maps?
4. Connected Sets: what do they mean and how they act under continuous maps?
5. 1st/2nd Countability: what do they mean and why are they important?
6. Separation Axioms (Tn for 0 ≤n ≤4): how are two distinct points “separated”?
Prerequisites:
• Calculus I (MATH161): open/closed intervals, limit, continuity, intermediate value theorem
• (Optional but strongly recommended) A proof-based course for math majors (MATH201, or math
major sections of MATH211/212 or MAT221/222, etc)
• (Optional) Analysis I (MATH211) for motivations
Textbook: Topology (2nd edition) by James Munkres.
Grade Distribution: Attendance (10%), Assignments (10%), Midterm (40%), Final Exam (40%).
F, D, D+ < 60 ≤C, C+ < 70 ≤B, B+ < 85, A,A+ ≤100 (in %)

• There will be 2 Assignments in Wednesdays of Weeks 5 and 13.

진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중
히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

 -연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분
야 대상 학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습
을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수

▷ 강의개요
개요
조선전기의 국왕을 중심으로 각 왕대의 정치·경제·문화·사회의 제 양상을 
종합적으로 파악함으로써 해당 시기를 이해하도록 한다. 『조선왕조실록』
을 바탕으로 한 기본 텍스트를 중심으로 해당 왕대에 밸생한 주요 사건
의 배경 과정 결과 등을 설명한 동영상을 제작하여 사전에 학습하게 하
고 , 본수업에서는 그를 토대로 다양한 형태의 대중 영상물을 보조적으
로 활용하여 해당 시기의 역사적 대세를 파악할 수 있도록 강의한다. 이
를 통해 역사적 객관성을 담보할 수 있는 실재 역사상을 구현하고, 그를 
통해 현재를 이해하고 미래를 전망할 수 있도록 한다.

조선 창업 군주 태조 대부터 7대 국왕 세조 대에 이르는 『조선왕조실록』
의 내용을 파악하게 함으로써 조선전기 역사 지식의 정보를 전달하여 이
해를 심화시키고, 이를 통해 조선의 역사와 문화가 주는 의의를 알아 역사
학의 대중화를 꾀하도록 한다. 
1) 본 과목의 대상 시기는 조선 태조 대 이후 세조 대까지로 한다. 
2) 본 과목은 해당 시기의 정치사를 각 주차별 주제에 따른 강의와 사전 
동영상 학습 방식을 통해 파악하도록 한다. 
3) 해당 시기의 정치사를 이해하기 위해 각 시기별로 특정한 주제를 중심
으로 한 영화, 드라마(이하 사극으로 칭함), 음악을 교육보조재료로 이용 
한다.

▷ 기타사항
1. 실시간 줌 회의를 통해 원격 강의합니다. 
2. 자체 제작한 강의자료를 교재로 합니다.
3. 출석은 회의에 참여한 시간으로 확인합니다. 
4. 유고 결석 사유는 불문합니다. 다만, 결석일 기준 6일전 혹은 6일후까지 기한 한에 신청한 경우에 인
정합니다./메일로 개별적으로 신청한 것은 인정하지 않습니다.  
5. 유고 사유로 인해 출석 인정을 신청할 경우에는 반드시 포털 출석인정 신청을 통해 아래 규정된 증

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

Course Overview  
This course provides the incoming freshmen with fundamental theories of business, along with 
introduction to various areas of business. The purpose of this course is to help students become 
business leaders that are true to the mission of KUBS, “Business for Society – Inspiring Next 
Leaders.” At the dawn of modern business education, Joseph Wharton emphasized, “Business 
education should find solutions to the social problems inherent in our civilization, and business 
leaders should be community builders who are responsible to society’s shared needs.” Based on 
this educational philosophy, the first half of this course seeks to engage students in the discussion 
of business philosophy, leadership, business ethics, and the theory of the firm, so that students 
realize the importance of pursuing social value while seeking business profit. The emphasis will 
be placed on learning how to create social value in doing business. In the second half of the 
course, seven functional areas of business, namely, management, accounting, finance, IS, 
marketing, LSOM, global business and strategy will be introduced, again emphasizing how social 
value can be created visà-vis firm value in each area of business.  
Course Objective  
- To understand why a firm exists in the society  
- To understand the importance of pursuing social value along with profits  
- To understand the educational philosophy of modern business  
- To understand leadership of community builders in a society  
- To understand the importance of business ethics  
- To introduce the main themes of specific areas in business administration  
- To understand how social value can be created vis-à-vis firm value in each area of business

Magretta, J. (2012) What Management Is: How It Works and Why It’s Everyone’s Business, Free 
Press

Course Overview 
 
This course is an introduction to the basic concepts and topics in organizational behavior 
(OB) and management. We will survey several topics that are related to managing people in 
organizations, including leadership, decision-making, motivation, conflict resolution, and 
organizational structure and culture. 
 
Course Objectives 
 
This course focuses on improving your ability to diagnose and solve problems related to the 
major challenges employees and managers face in contemporary organizations, such as 
building and sustaining organizational commitment and performance. The course introduces 
insights and tools from the behavioral and social science research that will help you develop 
and hone your ability to analyze organizational dynamics and to take effective action. 
 
Specifically, this course will provide tools, skills, and strategies for: 
 
• Thinking about yourself and your development as a member and/or leader 
• Increasing your understanding of how organizations and the people within them work 
• Diagnosing problems and using evidence to develop sound solutions 
• Controlling and designing organizational units and their activities 
 
Course Materials 
 
The course’s textbook is Organizational Behavior (19th Edition) by Stephen P. Robbins and 
Tim Judge (Pearson). You can use the 17th edition of this book, which is available from the 
university library as an e-book. Additional materials will be posted via KU LMS.  
 
Assignments and Grading 
 
Your final grade will be composed of: 
• Course participation and attendance

Course Participation and Attendance (20%) 
Every session of the course involves interaction in the form of class discussion and exercises, 
which are an important part of the learning process. You are expected to actively involve in 
this process.   
 
Attendance. If you miss a class, you can’t contribute much to class discussion. Thus, any 
absence will have a negative impact on your grade. If you need to miss class for a foreseeable 
reason (e.g., job interview), it is essential that you notify me at least 48 hours in advance.  
 
Participation. Your course participation grade will be based not only on the frequency of 
participation (neither too much nor too little) but also on the quality of your contributions to 
the ongoing discussion and your success in leading the discussion in productive, analytical 
directions. Quality of your participation will be assessed using the following criteria:   
 
• Relevance: How is the comment related to the current discussion? Is it related to ideas 
in the course readings or prior discussions? 
• Logic: Do you explain the reasoning behind your comment using clear evidence and 
coherent arguments? 
• Integration: Does your comment move the discussion forward by building on previous 
contributions with new insights? 
• Individuality: Does your comment contribute a new perspective to the discussion, or 
does it simply repeat what others have already said? 
 
You will get the most out of this course if you share your perspectives with others. I expect 
each of you to participate fully in all class exercises and to voice your views in class 
discussions. I also expect you to ask questions about things that you don’t understand, which 
can be an intimidating thing to do. However, asking questions in class not only helps you, but 
it also helps your classmates by moving the discussion forward in a new direction.   
 
*** Simply being present in class does not help your class contribution grades. Do not 
confuse physical attendance with active participation.  
 
Team Project (Team Contract: 5%, Presentation: 10%, Paper: 10%, Peer Evaluation: 
10%, 35% total) 
Within two weeks after the drop/add deadline, I will assign you to a team (5 or 6 members), 
and you will work with your team for a team project assignment. Each team will be required 
to interview at least one working manager. Your team can choose to interview more 
managers, but at least one manager must be interviewed for this project. This will give you an 
opportunity to explore a person, an organization, or an industry.   
 
Your task is to identify problems and/or difficulties the manager may be experiencing 
(primarily through your interview), and to use your knowledge of course concepts to create 
potential solutions to the problems/difficulties.  
 
Team contract (5%). Before you start working on the team assignment, your team should 
develop a team contract—a written agreement between members on the team’s objective(s), 
roles and responsibilities, ground rules, timelines, etc. It is ESSENTIAL that every member 
agrees on “inclusion” of terms in the contract: as long as everyone is fine, your team contract 
can have anything, and these terms can be both very specific and highly abstract and vague. 
As in most other contracts, your team contract should include signatures of every party—
 
3 
team members—involved and the date on which the contract is signed. I will provide you 
with a team contract template. You are free (not) to use the template, but you should make 
sure that the date and every party’s full name and signature are included.  
 
Team Presentation (10%). Your team will make a short presentation (max. 20 minutes 
including Q&A) about your interview, analysis, and recommendations. Your team’s 
presentation will be evaluated on the basis of (a) proper use of course concepts, (b) logic and 
appropriateness of your recommendation, and (c) how engaging the overall delivery is. After 
your team’s presentation, I will provide each team with brief feedback about the presentation 
and its content. This feedback should be used to strengthen the written analysis of the 
interview (i.e., team paper). 
 
Team Paper (10%). Your team will also have to submit a written report of your analysis and 
recommendations. This paper should be no longer than 10 double-spaced pages with 12-
point font size. The paper should include (and be evaluated on): (a) description of the 
situation/context/problem(s), (b) analysis of the situation/context/problem(s), and (c) your 
team’s solution(s) and explanations for why the solution(s) will work. Papers submitted after 
this time will be penalized 10 percent of the possible grade. Each additional day the paper is 
late will be penalized an additional 10 percent of the possible grade. 
 
*** I recommend starting the interview as early as possible in the semester, as interviewees 
may have extremely constrained schedules.  
 
*** There is considerable flexibility about how you carry out this team assignment. Feel free 
to ask me about topics or approaches you are considering taking. 
 
Peer Evaluation (10%). Within a week after the submission of your team’s final report 
paper, each member is expected to evaluate his or her teammates’ overall contribution to the 
team project on a 10-point scale, with 0 being no contribution at all and 10 being maximum 
contribution. Contribution scores each student receives from teammates will be averaged to 
calculate his or her peer evaluation score. These evaluations are expected to be made in 
ABSOLUTE, not in relative terms. Thus, every team member can receive 100% of peer 
evaluation score.   
 
Exams (45%) 
The exams will include multiple choice questions, True/False questions, and essay questions 
about the material we have learned in class. Each exam will cover materials from textbook, 
readings, lectures, and class discussion. Exams will not be cumulative. 
Make-up exams will not be offered. Students with prior commitments on scheduled exam 
dates should adjust their plans accordingly or consider enrolling in a different section of the 
course.

Honor Code 
 
Honesty and trust are the cornerstones of learning process and anyone’s professional career. I 
expect you to maintain the highest standards of personal conduct; by voicing their

All written work should be the original product of the individual or team members. If you

Office hours: by appointment. Please email or talk to me in class to arrange an appointment at a mutually suitable time. Kindly let me

FAQs: 
 
Why should you take this course? 
Seoul is a special place. Whether you’re a long-term Seoulite or a newcomer, if you’re interested in 
reflecting on the city we all call home now while honing your academic communication skills, this is the 
right course for you.  
 
What English-language proficiency is required?  Our tasks are devised for anyone with 
upper-intermediate to advanced proficiency in English. Individual projects will allow students of all levels 
to engage with the materials and with one another and to produce their work in English. 
 
How heavy is the workload? It’s reasonable for a three-credit university class. Expect to spend an 
average of about seven hours per week on the course. You’ll also need to be prepared to get out of your 
home and get around parts of Seoul. The final project requires a significant amount of time. Check out 
the list of tasks in “Assessments” below for the approximate workload.  
 
General description and aims: 
In this exciting look at South Korea’s capital, you will explore aspects of the city’s history, architecture, 
environment, transportation, social dynamics, arts, and culture. Each week, you will engage with diverse

English-language multimedia and the city itself. You will ponder, research, discuss, and write critically about 
city life. In doing so, you will gain insights into this ever-changing metropolis and your own position within it 
while upgrading your academic communication skills, critical thinking abilities, and creativity.  
 
You will present and lead a discussion about a Seoul-related topic, write short response papers on city life, and 
produce a creative, engaging final project in which you conduct field research to analyze two aspects of Seoul. 
 
By the end of the course, you’ll have better questions about Seoul and about your place in the world than you 
did at the start. You’ll have transformed your knowledge and yourself.  
 
Specific aims: By the end of the course, you will have: 
1.​ Expanded your knowledge of and ability to discuss the city of Seoul Produced personal reflective and 
academic writing that demonstrates an understanding of aspects of Seoul discussed in our course. 
2.​ Presented on and led your peers in a discussion about one Seoul-related topic 
3.​ Discussed and debated connections between Seoul and other cities 
4.​ Critiqued texts and considered artifacts related to Seoul with clarity, coherence, and academic rigor 
5.​ Demonstrated proficiency in finding, analyzing, and incorporating sources from different fields 
utilizing APA 7th edition 
6.​ Developed analytical skills through the interpretation of texts, videos, and artifacts related to Seoul

Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Regulations 
●​ Academic honesty is expected. All work you produce will be your own. Copying homework (from 
another person or an AI( or cheating on tests is obviously unacceptable.  
●​ As per Korea University regulations, students caught cheating on any assignments or submitting work 
that includes improperly cited sources will be penalized.  
●​ This class includes referenced research projects. ***Any work containing hallucinated references 
(non-existent citations fabricated by an AI or citations that are mash-ups or one or more real 
references) will be heavily penalized in the rubric category for referencing, and the work itself may be 
considered AI-generated. Check all DOIs and URLs very carefully.  
●​ Wholly plagiarized work will be marked “F.” We will have a refresher lesson to make sure you know 
how to avoid plagiarism before written work. Please note that rubrics for our tasks  
●​ Acceptable generative AI use will be clarified for each out-of-class assignment, and rubrics will reflect 
the need for your writing to be in your own voice. As a rule, anything above the sentence level 
written by an AI or a translation app is not allowed in this class. If you use a chatbot for proofreading, 
be sure not to copy/paste whole documents. Instead, ask specific questions to the chatbot and make 
the fixes yourself.  
●​ You are required to include an AI disclaimer on all submissions clarifying whether generative AI was 
used or not and in what capacity. An example will be shown in our Google Drive 
●​ Please do not input any City of Seoul course materials, including course instructions, into an AI. 
These are the instructor’s and Korea University’s intellectual property.  
 
Etiquette 
●​ If you have an urgent situation and know that you need your phone to be on during a class, please let 
me know before the class starts. It takes discipline to resist checking your messages in class, so if 
need be, try switching to airplane mode. 
●​ If you are very tired,  sick, or occupied with something that involves communicating via the phone, 
please take the day off. If you come to class unable to participate properly,  you will likely be marked 
absent and asked to leave the room.

과목개요 
본 강의는 기업이 경쟁 우위를 확보하고 지속 가능한 성장을 이루기 위한 전략을 
탐구하는 데 중점을 둡니다. 수강생은 전략적 관리 프로세스를 통해 주요 전략적 이슈를 
파악하고, 효과적인 전략을 수립 및 실행하는 방법을 학습합니다. 또한, 실제 비즈니스 
사례를 분석하며 최고 경영자의 관점에서 문제를 해결하는 통합적 사고 방식을 익히는 
것을 목표로 합니다. 
 
이 과정에서는 전략적 사고 능력을 배양하고, 복잡하고 비정형적인 문제를 체계적으로 
분석하며 해결하는 역량을 개발합니다. 현대 비즈니스 환경에서 발생하는 다양한 
전략적 이슈를 논리적이고 창의적인 방식으로 해결하는 방법을 학습하며, 경영 전략의 
이론을 실제 사례에 적용해 실질적인 문제 해결 능력을 강화합니다. 이를 통해 다양한 
비즈니스 상황에서 이론을 효과적으로 활용하고 응용하는 데 필요한 능력을 기를 수 
있습니다. 
 
이와 함께 데이터를 활용해 설득력 있는 주장을 개발하고, 이를 바탕으로 논리적인 
근거를 제시하는 데이터 기반 의사결정 능력을 갖추는 것을 주요 목표로 합니다.

시험 
중간고사는 없으며, 기말고사는 종합적으로 출제되며 객관식 문제 혹은 서술형 문제로 
구성됩니다. 
 
수업 참여 
 
 
본 강의의 중요한 학습 목표 중 하나는 전략적으로 사고하는 능력을 기르는 것입니다. 
이 능력은 이론과 사례 분석에 대한 수업 토론에 참여함으로써 증진될 수 있습니다. 
수업 참여 점수는 수업 중 질문에 대한 답변과 토론의 내용을 기준으로 평가되며, 수업 
참여 평가의 객관성을 높이기 위해 BIO 시트를 제출해 주시기 바랍니다. 
 
동료 평가 
 
 
조별 사례 분석 및 프로젝트를 성공적으로 수행하기 위해서는 팀 멤버 모두의 적극적인 
참여가 필수적입니다. 조별 멤버 각자의 공헌도에 대한 동료평가는 기말 시험과 함께 
실시됩니다. 
 
출결 사항  
 
결석 횟수가 3 회를 초과할 경우, 성적과 상관없이 F 학점을 받게 됩니다. 두 번의 지각은 
한 번의 결석으로 간주되며, 출석 및 지각 확인과 관련된 구체적인 사항은 블랙보드 
공지사항을 참조해 주시기 바랍니다. 
 
사례 분석  
본 강의에서는 전체 수강학생의 숫자를 감안하여 분석할 사례 및 조별 숫자가 결정될 
예정입니다. 20 분 발표 및 15 분 질의응답 시간이 진행됩니다. 발표 자료는 페이지 
번호가 삽입된 PPT 로 작성해야 하며, 발표 예정 시점 최소 24 시간 전에 담당교수에게 
이메일로 제출해 주기 바랍니다. 이때 모든 팀원들이 참조되도록(cc) 포함해 주기 
바랍니다. 미리 제시된 질문에 대한 답변을 도출하는 과정에서 다음의 요소들을 
분석/포함하는 것을 고려할 수 있습니다.  
1. 산업 분석: 5 Forces 모델을 활용한 산업 구조 분석, 주요 경쟁사 분석, 고객 인구 
통계, 기술 동향, 제품 수명 주기 등 
2. 내부 분석: SWOT 분석, VRIO 분석, 제품 믹스 분석, 재무 성과(자본 구조, 수익성 
비율, 유동성 비율, 레버리지 비율, 활동성 비율), 조직 구조, 기업 문화 등 
3. 기타 환경 분석: 거시경제 조건, 법적 및 정치적 환경, 문화적 요인 등 
4. 제안 사항: 단기 및 중장기적 전략 
 
 
3
발표가 예정되지 않은 그룹은 사례와 관련하여 미리 제시된 질문에 대한 답변을 Word 
로 작성하여 수업 시작 최소 2 시간 전에 조교(TA)에게 이메일로 제출해 주기 바랍니다. 
이 과제의 목적은 학생들이 수업 중 사례 토론에 충분히 준비할 수 있도록 하는 데 
있습니다. 답변에는 페이지 제한이 없으나, 일반적으로 3~5 페이지 정도의 분량이 
적정할 것으로 판단됩니다.  
 
 
프로젝트  
경영전략은 비즈니스 환경 분석, 전략 수립 및 실행, 평가를 포함하는 체계적인 
의사결정과 행동의 집합입니다. 이는 기업이 경쟁 우위를 확보하고 유지하는 데 
필수적이라고 여겨지지만, 전략적 경영만으로 성공이 보장되지는 않습니다. 실패하거나 
성과가 저조한 기업 사례에서 이를 확인할 수 있습니다. 한때 업계를 선도했던 
기업들조차 시장에서 퇴출되거나, 동종 업계 또는 다른 산업의 기업에 인수되는 경우가 
많습니다. 기존 기업들은 신생 기업과의 치열한 경쟁에 직면하며, 많은 기업들이 실패에 
이를 가능성이 높습니다.   
 
본 프로젝트에서 각 조는 기업이 직면한 주요 문제의 원인과 결과를 분석하고, 이를 
해결할 수 있는 제안을 통해 “기업 지속 가능성”을 강화할 방안을 제시해야 합니다. 이를 
위해 최근 평판, 시장 점유율, 수익, 업계 리더십 등에서 ‘저조한 성과’를 보이거나 
실패한 기업을 선택한 후 다음과 같은 분석 절차를 제안합니다.  
 
 1. 기업의 문제점 식별 
• 
왜 해당 기업이 그 문제를 겪고 있다고 판단하는가? 
• 
비재무적 성과: 평판, 고객 만족도, 브랜드 이미지 등 
• 
재무적 성과: 재무 건전성, 수익성, 경쟁력, 시장에서의 평가 변화 양상 등 
 
2. 분석  
• 
외부 환경:  업계 동향 및 경쟁 압력, 현재/미래의 경쟁자, 기회와 위협 등 
• 
내부 환경: 자원 및 역량, 강점과 약점, 수준 별 주요 전략  
• 
기업이 직면한 가장 중요한 전략적 이슈 
 
3. 평가 및 제안 
• 
기업이 이해관계자와 가치사슬 전반에서 저지른 문제와 실수는 무엇이었는가? 
• 
이러한 문제와 실수가 기업의 지속 가능성에 어떤 영향을 미쳤는가? 
• 
'실패' 또는 '불만족스러운 성과’를 피하기 위해 무엇을 했어야 했는가? 
• 
기업의 지속 가능성을 강화하기 위한 단기적 또는 장기적 제안은 무엇인가? 
 
4
4. 일정  
프로젝트 제안서는 3 월 18 일에 제출합니다. 제안서에는 팀 이름, 팀원 이름 및 연락처, 
선택한 기업과 그 기업이 직면한 문제에 대한 간략한 설명이 포함되어야 합니다. 
제안서는 PPT 로 작성하여 수업 최소 2 시간 전에 조교에게 이메일로 제출해야 합니다. 
제안서는 3 월 30 일 및 4 월 1 일에 발표될 예정입니다. 
 
4 월 22 일~29 일에 프로젝트의 중간 발표를 진행합니다. 이 발표는 기업 분석과 문제 
식별 내용을 포함해야 하며, 산업 통계 및 재무/비재무 성과와 같은 관련 데이터를 통해 
뒷받침되어야 합니다. 발표 자료는 PPT
로 작성하여 수업 최소 2
시간 전에 
Blackboard 에 업로드해야 합니다. 
 
6 월 8 일~15 일에 최종 발표를 진행합니다. 최종 프로젝트 결과물은 PPT 로 작성하여 
수업 최소 2 시간 전에 Blackboard 에 업로드해야 합니다. 최종 프로젝트 결과물은 
내용과 스타일 면에서 모두 전문성을 갖추어야 하며, 그래프, 통계, 표, 참고문헌, 
데이터/정보 출처 등 관련 첨부 자료를 포함해야 합니다. 
 
5. 기타  
다른 사람들에게 자신이 알고 있는 것을 발표할 준비를 하는 과정은 학습 과정에서 매우 
중요합니다. 각 발표의 날짜는 수업 중에 결정됩니다. 모든 팀원은 발표에서 각자 
역할을 맡아야 하며, 다른 팀원들과 담당 교수가 해당 기업의 CEO 라고 가정하고 발표를 
준비해야 합니다. 발표 후에는 질의응답(Q&A) 시간이 이어질 예정입니다. 
 
발표 방식은 팀의 재량에 따라 자유롭게 결정할 수 있으며, 관련 내용을 충실히 담고 
논리적이고 일관된 방식으로 팀의 분석 결과를 전달하면 됩니다. 팀은 발표의 명확성과 
정보 전달력을 높이기 위해 시각 자료나 기타 도구를 창의적으로 활용하는 것을 
권장합니다. 
 
다른 수업에서 작성한 사례 분석을 이 과제에 사용하는 것은 허용되지 않습니다. 표절은 
심각한 위반 행위입니다.  직접 인용하거나 내용을 바탕으로 재구성(paraphrase)한 모든 
자료는 반드시 출처를 명시해야 합니다.

동인에 대한 심층적 이해를 도모한다. 
본 강의는 과거를 단순한 사실의 집적이 아닌, 현재까지 지속적으로 영향을 
미치는 복합적이고 역동적인 과정으로 파악하는 성찰적 역사 접근법을 장려한

구축하고자 한다.

By examining how historical events and processes have shaped our understanding 
of time and space, particularly in the context of East Asia, we can gain a deeper 
understanding of the forces that have shaped our current reality. It encourages a 
reflective approach to history, recognizing that the past is not simply a collection 
of facts, but a complex and dynamic process that continues to influence our lives 
today. By exploring the historical context of the present, we can gain insights into 
contemporary issues and challenges, and develop a more nuanced understanding 
of our place in the world.
