2. Class Preparation and Participation (10%)
- Preparation
To ensure that students are adequately prepared for in-class activities, such as being able to 
articulate their personal opinions, they are required to read the assigned readings and complete pre-
class exercises in the textbook prior to attending class.
- Participation
A significant amount of time will be spent on critical thinking and discussions on thought-
provoking reading selections. Students are expected to actively engage in small group and whole 
class discussions. Participation will be assessed based on their attentiveness, contributions to 
discussions, facilitation efforts, and completion of in-class activities. This course adopts a learner-
centered approach where students are encouraged to actively engage in co-constructing knowledge 
in order to create rich learning opportunities.
Classroom Etiquette
Unnecessary use of laptops or smartphones, passing notes, sleeping, leaving class without the 
instructor’s permission, or displaying any disrespectful or disruptive behavior during class hours 
will not be tolerated. 
3. Vocabulary Quizzes (10%)
Two short quizzes will be administered to assess students’ understanding and use of the vocabulary 
covered in the course. Students must be present on the day of each quiz, as there will be no make-up 
quizzes. Details will be announced later.
4. Writing Assignments (30%)
Students are expected to complete several writing assignments: an interactive response journal, a 
textbook exercise, and a paragraph writing task. Further details will be announced in class and 
posted on the LMS. All assignments must be completed and submitted by the assigned due dates. 
Late submissions will result in point deductions.
(1) Interactive Response Journal (10%)
Students are expected to write a response journal incorporatingcritical thoughts and ideas by 
making connections and reflecting on personal experiences and perspectives, and to engage in an 
asynchronous online discussion.
(2) Textbook Exercise (10%)
Students are expected to analyze several texts from the textbook and submit their responses.
(3) Paragraph Writing (10%)
Students will be asked to incorporate outside sources into their writing by using in-text citations and 
including a reference list.
4
5. Final Project (40%)
(1) Group Presentation (20%)
The final project offers students the opportunity to consolidate their learning by applying their 
knowledge and critical skills to topics related to their interests in recent local and global issues.
Students will work in groups of four to five and select an engaging topic. They are expected to 
collect, investigate, and analyze texts from diverse sources such as TV, radio, films, magazines, 
periodicals, books, and/or online resources. Each group will present their critical stance on the topic, 
highlighting insights that are worth sharing with the class. 
Presentations should not exceed 30 minutes (20 minutes of presentation + 10 minutes of discussion 
and Q&A). All group members must contribute, either by presenting or by facilitating class 
discussion. 
- 10 points will be allotted based on class evaluation and 5 points will be given at the 
instructor’s discretion.
- 5 points will be allotted to peer evaluation of group members’ contributions. Students will 
therefore receive relative grades according to their group’s evaluation.
(2) Final Mini Paper (20%)
Students will individually write a mini paper synthesizing information from the sources that were 
used in their final presentation and incorporate their own perspectives on their presentation topic. 
The paper should follow a clear organizational structure (introduction, body, and conclusion) that 
effectively presents their stance and analysis. It must be the student’s original work with appropriate 
in-text citations. The paper should be 4 pages long (excluding references) and formatted in 
Microsoft Word using Times New Roman, 12‐point font, double‐spacing, and 1-inch margins. A 
peer-review checklist will be later provided, and further details will be announced in class.

Course 
Description 
This course provides a deeper exploration of financial accounting 
concepts under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). 
Significant emphasis is placed on the IFRS conceptual framework and 
its role in guiding recognition, measurement, and disclosure decisions. 
The course also covers more complex and judgment-intensive issues in 
the reporting of cash, receivables, inventories, property, plant and 
equipment, and current liabilities. It strengthens students’ technical 
understanding of IFRS and prepares them for advanced accounting study 
and professional practice. 
Course  
Objectives 
By the end of this course, students will be able to: 
• 
Apply the IFRS conceptual framework to analyze accounting 
issues and support recognition, measurement, and disclosure 
decisions. 
• 
Prepare and present financial information related to cash, 
receivables, inventories, property, plant and equipment, 
depreciation, impairment, and current liabilities in accordance 
with IFRS. 
• 
Evaluate alternative accounting treatments and exercise 
professional judgment in resolving more complex or estimation-
based financial reporting matters. 
• 
Interpret and analyze financial statement effects of various 
accounting policies for assets and current liabilities. 
• 
Communicate accounting conclusions using appropriate IFRS 
terminology and reasoning.

Course Description 
 
Hello Future Leaders! Are you ready to dive into the exciting world of Information Systems (IS)?  
In an era dominated by digital transformation, understanding Information Systems (IS) is crucial for any 
aspiring business leader. This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive grasp of how information 
technology (IT) catalyses change and presents both opportunities and challenges across various industries. Far 
from being mere tools for back-office automation, IS are now at the forefront of business strategy and 
competitive positioning. 
 
Our curriculum covers key technology concepts and trends essential to current and future IT developments, 
with a special emphasis on the digital economy, e-commerce, and business analytics. Topics include big data 
analytics, hardware/software fundamentals, networking, the social networks, database management, 
cybersecurity, and enterprise applications. Through practical case studies and discussions on the latest 
technological trends, students will gain both theoretical knowledge and hands-on experience. 
 
This course is designed not just to educate but to empower students, equipping them with the skills and insight 
needed to lead and innovate in the rapidly evolving digital business world.

Imporant Note: This course is conducted as an 8-week intensive program under the 
Flexible Semester system. 
 
Course Objective 
 
This course focuses on understanding the process and results of marketing research (MR) 
and its applications. After taking this course, students will be able to experience the entire 
process of MR, including problem definition, research design, data collection, data 
analysis, interpretation, and reporting of results. This course also emphasizes an applied 
approach to the practical application of MR to marketing management. In particular, the 
course highlights how to effectively utilize Generative AI throughout the research process 
and demonstrates how MR contributes to the various strategic decisions marketers must 
make.   
 
 
Textbook & References 
 
There is no single required textbook for this course. However, the following book serves 
as a primary reference for the fundamental concepts: 
 
Burns, Alvin C. and Ann Veeck (2020), Marketing Research, 9th edition, Pearson 
Education, Upper Saddle River, NJ.  
 
Students are strictly required to study all assigned reading materials and watch the 
designated video clips before attending each session. Some readings are available through 
Korea University Online Library at library.korea.ac.kr

수업 소개 
 
환경정책은 과학, 정치, 경제가 복잡하게 얽혀 있는 분야입니다. 이는 곧 정부, 시민사회, 
시장 모두가 정책의 수립과 실행에 나름의 역할이 있음을 의미합니다. 본 수업에서 
우리는 환경문제의 정의, 목표의 설정, 해결책 제시를 위한 다양한 이해당사자들의 상호 
작용 방식을 살펴볼 것입니다. 이를 통해 환경문제가 지속되는 이유를 밝히고 문제에 
대응하기 위하여 진화한 정책수단에 대한 이해를 높이기를 희망합니다. 
구체적으로 본 수업은: 
 
환경문제의 근본 원인에 대한 경쟁적인 관점을 소개합니다. 
 
환경문제에 대처하기 위한 다양한 정책도구를 비교하며, 각각의 전제와 작동 기제를 
설명합니다.

*** IMPORTANT REMINDER ***

◼ Division of International Studies (DIS) 
◼ Global Korean Studies and Open Majors

ACADEMIC ENGLISH - Spring Semester 2026 
 
Course Syllabus  
Instructor:  Mr. Mumford (Michael) 
Email:  acadenglishku@gmail.com** 
                    **The main way to contact me outside of class 
Classroom:  Room 414 [국제관] 
Office hours: Student consultations available throughout the semester 
 
1. Overview: Intermediate Academic English is a 2-credit course aimed at introducing the language 
and practices of the global English-speaking academic community. 
2.  Course Objectives:  
- Improve your confidence and fluency in English through active discussion 
- Practice effective communication and public speaking 
- Use English for research, writing, and analysis 
- Develop your academic integrity and skills 
- ‘Unlearn’ inaccurate language, habits, and strategies 
- Emphasize independent learning 
3. Materials Needed for the Course: 
- Reading Materials and Google Form Assignments will be uploaded to KULMS over the course of 
the semester (https://lms.korea.ac.kr/) 
- Laptop or Smartphone for in-class tasks  
 
4. Course Grading:

discussions

      Total Semester Points: 80   
(=100%) 
 
 
 
 
4.1 Participation:  
Listening actively, asking questions, volunteering answers, and engaging with your partners in group 
activities. 
Additionally:  
Accessing KULMS regularly for notices, assignments, and other materials 
Being Prepared: looking over the Course Materials and being aware of work that is due 
Completing your assignments thoroughly and on time 
** Each lecture is worth at least 0.5 points towards your overall semester grade.  
4.2 Attendance/Being on Time:  
If you miss class more than 6 times [for any reason] you will fail the course. Being absent more than 3 
times (either ‘excused’ or ‘unexcused’) means you cannot earn more than a B+. Two lates (under 10 
minutes) equal one absence.  Each absence after your 3rd time equals 1 point off your final grade.   
Additionally:  
If you are not present after 10 minutes, you will be marked absent. If you join class after a group 
activity has begun, you may be asked to come back later. 
If you think you will be absent, let me know before class via e-mail ⬧⬧ See below 
 
⬧⬧ Reporting an absence through KUPID is not required. Instead, to maintain your overall 
participation score you want to send me a direct email with YOUR NAME, STUDENT 
NUMBER, and CLASS NUMBER with a brief explanation of your reason for being absent 
(acadenglishku@gmail.com). You could lose valuable semester points if you fail to notify 
me of your absence. 
⬧⬧ Absences might require make-up work if you expect to receive top marks in the course. 
Only students who email me directly (acadenglishku@gmail.com) can expect to receive 
updates on what they missed, or work that is due. Students who apply for absences 
through KUPID are responsible for everything discussed in class and for any work that is 
due.  
  
COURSEWORK:  
4.3 At-home Assignments/In-Class Discussions (25 semester points): 
Short writing tasks, preparation for upcoming lessons, research, reading comprehension tasks through 
Google Forms. The texts you will read and discuss can be considered high intermediate or advanced-
level. In-class work will involve reading, group discussion assignments, and group ‘note taking’ (= Google 
Form).  
If you miss an assignment because you were absent or late, it is your responsibility to contact me to 
obtain the lesson materials. 
 
4.4 Group Discussion Exam (20 semester points):  
The Group Discussion Exam [3 to 4 participants] will require active interaction by all participants aiming 
to: “unpack” a topic question, cooperate, interject with healthy skepticism, while advancing the 
discussion through a clear, systematic, and analytical approach. Participants will be assessed 
individually. The graded Group Discussion will take place between Weeks 6 and 7 of the semester. 
 
 
 
 
4.5 Academic Writing (25 semester points): 
The Academic Writing is an in-class assignment. It will involve data analysis, organization, 
interpretation, critique, and reporting sources (Referencing). We will begin to discuss Academic Writing 
in the second half of the course, while the final writing will be completed in the final week of the 
semester. 
 
5. Group Work (In-Class Discussions) 
Working in groups (usually 3-4 classmates) will be the norm in this class. In each lecture, be prepared to 
engage in active discussion aiming to “unpack” topic questions, cooperate, interject with healthy 
skepticism/criticism, while advancing discussion through a clear, systematic, and analytical approach.  
In sum, you will be expected to interact actively with your classmates in each lesson. 
6. KULMS (KU Course Management Website: https://lms.korea.ac.kr/) 
You are expected to check the KU Course Management Website (KULMS) regularly.  
 
7. Misuse of Mobile Devices will not be tolerated. 
 
8. English is the sole language of Instruction and Interaction during the course. 
 
9. All forms of Plagiarism and passing off ‘AI-generated’ work as your own will result in a failing grade on 
the assignment 
 
 
 
APPENDIX 
 
1. Repeated Absences:  
Because class attendance offers you a rare chance to develop your English skills, students who miss 
class regularly (for example, several classes in one month) are at risk of failing the course. If you think 
you might need to miss several classes for any reason (for example: participation in university 
activities, applying for jobs, etc...) it is your responsibility to contact me in advance in person or by e-
mail. Please note, however, that you may have to complete considerable “make-up work.”  
 
2. Completing the Major Projects: 
In order to pass the course, you need to complete the 2 major assignments (the Group Discussion and 
Academic Essay)  in addition to making sure you miss no more than 6 days over the entire Semester. In 
other words, you will receive an F grade if you fail to complete these major tasks, regardless of your 
attendance. 
 
3. Plagiarism and submitting Original Material [e.g. use of Large Language Models (LLMs)]:  
Plagiarism is “passing off someone else’s work as your own.” It is dishonest and illegal. Furthermore, it 
will not help you improve and establishes a bad pattern in your university education. You will 
automatically receive an F grade on any assignment that is plagiarized. This will considerably and 
irrevocably lower your semester grade. Additionally, make sure to submit “original content” for your 
assignments—meaning that you personally wrote the content and have not submitted the work in 
another course. 
 
4. Late work: 
Late assignments will be penalized 10% of the assignment grade per day until the work is submitted. 
Your work will also be considered late if you are late on the day an assignment is due.  
 
5. Important information about Grades: 
Your overall course grade is earned based on specific assignment criteria.  Earning an A or 
A+ mark requires exceptional work throughout the entire semester.

지원 교수, 비과에 김태훈 교수, 신재민 교수, 두경부 외과에 백승국 교수, 김연수 부교

는 4년차 이승혁이 담당한다. 외래는 병원 3층에 위치하고 주 병동은 88병동이다.

1) 이과학 분야
(1) 정상 고막의 구조를 알고 이경의 사용법을 익힌다.
(2) 외이도염의 치료 원칙을 숙지한다.
(3) 급성중이염 및 삼출성중이염의 진단 및 치료를 숙지한다. 
(4) 만성중이염의 진단 및 수술적 치료에 대하여 숙지한다. 
(5) 외상성 고막천공의 진단 및 치료를 설명할 수 있어야 한다.
(6) 어지럼 환자의 문진 및 진단방법에 대해 숙지한다. 
(7) 안면신경마비의 진단 및 중추성과 말초성을 구분을 할 수 있어야 한다.
(8) 전음성 난청과 감각신경성 난청을 구분하여야 한다.
2) 비과학 분야
(1) 전비경으로 비중격 만곡증, 비후성 비염, 알레르기성 비염, 비용을 비교, 관찰할 수 
있어야 한다.
(2) 콧물의 원인을 알레르기비염, 비알레르기비염, 감염성비염으로 구분하여 각각의 질환
을 감별진단할 수 있도록 한다. 
(3) 알레르기비염의 기전과 치료원칙을 알아야 한다.
(4) 급성과 만성 부비동염의 감별 및 치료원칙을 알아야 한다.
(5) 비강 내 양성 및 악성종양의 진단방법에 대하여 설명할 수 있어야 한다.

(1) 갑상선 종물을 감별진단할 수 있어야 하고 치료에 대해 설명할 수 있어야 한다.

Academic English 2026-1 Syllabus
  Korea University
Prof. Blackwood	
	
	
	
course code: IFLS800-81 (Public Health umbrella majors)
email@mikeblackwood.net	 	
	
office # 722 International Studies Hall
office phone 3290-2451	
	
	
office hours: (to be announced)	
	

Course Structure:
The course has been structured for individual and group work through readings, lectures, and writing, with 
opportunities for speaking and, if practical and meaningful, some peer review activities.
Texts:
The Last Hours of Ancient Sunlight (AS)	
	
	
Hartmann; one text per class
The Way of Academic Essays (school year 2024) 	
	
Blackwood; one per student
Please do not purchase the above books yet; they will both likely be uploaded as pdf versions to KULMS.  We 
will cover 2/3 of the Hartmann text, perhaps more if time permits.
Participation: 
• Active participation in class, in English, is required. All discussions, exercises, and assignments must be conducted in 
English. Participation includes attendance; arrive on time and prepared. Late arrivals and absences disrupt the class and 
will result in penalties. You are allowed up to four excused absences; ten or more absences (including excused) will result 
in a failing grade, as per Ministry of Education policy.
• Excused absences and tardies do not excuse missed work; you are responsible for catching up. Excused absences must be 
documented with official paperwork, not phone photos, and communicated promptly. Email all correspondence to the 
address provided, not through EKU email. Missed assignments receive a zero; missing a midterm or final may result in 
failing the course. It is your responsibility to ask about missed work and adhere to deadlines.
FYI (for your information):
• I expect English to be spoken during class.  People who speak another language will be considered absent.
• Please be aware that deadlines are final. If late work is accepted (due to an excused absence, for example), it will be 
penalized by daily increments.  Deadline extension must be granted by the professor prior to the due date.  Failure to 
complete the midterm or final exam, and/or failure to complete assignments or tasks could result in failure of the course. 
To ensure academic integrity and facilitate plagiarism checking, students are required to upload their final paper to the 
university website by the deadline. Failure to upload final paper will result in a deduction of 2 points.
• Scholarly behavior is expected: arrive on time, prepared with necessary materials, and refrain from using cell phones or 
chatting during class. Points will be deducted for lack of preparation or disruptive behavior.
• All submitted work must include your name, student number, and class name/code (AE-81). Incomplete information or late 
homework will result in lost points. Homework must be submitted in class when collected; do not send assignments by 
email unless specifically instructed.
• Assignments of two or more pages must be stapled in the upper left corner (one staple per assignment), but do not staple 
multiple assignments together.
• Emails must be written professionally, not like text messages. Include your name, student number, and the course name, 
and use proper spelling, grammar, and salutations. Questions about the syllabus or grading should be asked early in the 
semester, not at the end of the semester.
• Failure to follow these guidelines will result in point deductions.
AI Usage:
• Students can use generative AI tools like ChatGPT to enhance their learning outcomes (for example, asking ChatGPT to 
check work for mistakes) and have positive educational experiences (for example, asking to explain terms or concepts 
from class that the student cannot understand themselves; however, if students use generative AI without basic guidelines 
(for example, creating answers to an assignment), it may negatively impact the quality of teaching and learning.
• Common negative impacts include: (1) violations of academic integrity, such as plagiarism and cheating; (2) decline in 
critical thinking, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills due to exercising the “other brain” and not your own; (3) 
acquisition of inaccurate or biased information; and (4) reinforcement of entrenched stereotypes.
• In short, “There is no royal road to learning” (Euclid).  If you use generative AI to do your work for you, you have not 
learned the skills you took the course to learn and so have wasted your money.
Course Outline and Goals:
• Outline:  This course is designed to stimulate students' thinking of the world around them, as well as to provide the chance 
to employ communication skills through reading, writing, listening, and speaking.  All activities are provided as a means to 
further stimulate students' thinking and to facilitate writing. Special effort has been taken to establish process rather than 
product goals.  Also, see attached week-by-week syllabus for further details.
• Goals:  The goals for this course include, but are not limited to, critical thinking, a willingness to explore ideas contrary to 
one's own beliefs, as well as knowing when information or data are relevant to an issue and how to find that information.  
In addition to these general concepts, the instructor also wishes to address student concerns for self discovery.
Overview of tentative grading criteria
Grade Codes
Overview of letter grade criteria:
95-100: A+, 90-94: A, 85-89: B+, 80-84: B, 75-79: C+, 70-74: C, 65-69: D+, 60-64: D, 59 and below: F
For Grade calculation, there are 5 units, as follows:
Unit I (Participation/Attendance) general participation, scholarly conduct/attitude/initiative/motivation
Weighted score (10%)
Unit II (Speaking) presentation (except ppt score), discussions, consultations
Weighted score (20%)
Unit III (Writing) video reaction papers, ppt slides (for group presentation)
Weighted score (10%)
Unit IV (Midterm) written exam (objective: multiple choice, true/false, matching, fill in the blanks, complete table)
Weighted score (25%)
Unit V (Final) referenced essay with in-text citations, outline draft(s), LMS digital upload
Weighted score (35%)
These five units are then added together, yielding a subtotal for points earned for the course, plus/minus attendance, relative 
evaluation standards, as well as other sundries.
Attendance Policy
Tardies, absences:
You are permitted up to three excused absences. For each unexcused absence beyond the third, your final course grade will 
be reduced by 1 percentage point through Participation (E.g., if you earn 87%, but have eight absences (three excused and 
five unexcused absences), then your final grade will be 82%.). Being late three times constitutes one absence.

The above system of penalties follows the spirit of university policy passed down from the Ministry of Education of 1/3 
absences (>10 absences) being an automatic “F”.
What is excused or unexcused?
Excused: Illness (with documentation), family emergencies, university-sponsored events, military test, etc.
Unexcused: Absences beyond the allowed number, or those without valid documentation.
Counseling Services
The KU Student Counseling Center offers help to students having trouble at university or with their feelings. They are very 
good at listening. They have one to one counseling, group counseling, and even some tests people can take about their lives, 
feelings, personality, relationships, and more. During the semester, they are open from Monday-Friday from 9 a.m. - 5:30 
p.m (closed for lunch). They are located in the Central Plaza Room 114. Tel: 3290-1540~1. Website: http://kuscc.korea.ac.kr 
(in Korean).

Info on Thom Hartmann, our key author this semester, in Korean:
톰 하트만(지은이)
진보주의자로, 세계적인 라디오 TV 토크쇼 진행자다. 그의 쇼는 매주 전 세계 104개국 약 5억 가구에 방영되
고 있다. 그는 언론 감시 단체인 ‘프로젝트 센서드’가 선정하는 올해의 뉴스상을 네 차례 수상했고, 그의 책 스
물네 권은 5개 대륙에서 17개 언어로 출간되었다. 
톰 하트만은 문화, 환경학, 심리학, 정치학, 경제학 등 여러 방면의 글을 써왔다. 환경학과 인류학을 접목시킨 
<마지막 시간들The Last Hours of Ancient Sunlight;은 그의 책들 중 가장 유명한데, 레오나르도 디카프
리오Leonardo DiCaprio가 이 책을 원작으로 한 영화 [열한 번째 시간The 11th Hour](톰 하트만도 출연했
다)을 제작했다. 그의 책 <주의력 결핍 장애Attention Dificit Disorder: A Different Perception;는 미국 
전역에서 ADD·ADHD와 영재성부터 자폐성까지 이들의 신경학적 차이를 둘러싸고 심리학·정신의학 커뮤니
티와 일반 대중 사이에서 논쟁을 불러일으켰다. 
아메리칸 드림을 재부팅하라Rebooting the American Dream; 또한 크게 주목받았다. 미국 상원의원 버니 
샌더스Bernie Sanders는 상원의원 99명에게 톰 하트만의 책을 나눠 주기 위해 편지를 썼고, 그의 유명한 의
사진행방해(필리버스터filibuster) 기간 동안 상원의원석 여기저기에서 이 책을 읽었다. 
탁월한 작가인 그는 아내 루이스와 함께 버림받은 아이들을 위해 많은 사업과 커뮤니티, 그리고 학교 관련 일
을 시작했다. 이들 부부는 4개 대륙에서 기근 구제, 의료센터, 학교에 이르는 다양한 분야의 프로그램이 시작
되도록 도왔다. 그와 아내는 워싱턴 DC의 한 보트 위에서 고양이 히긴스Higgins와 함께 살고 있다.

2) 격주 화요일, 목요일 오전에 신장내과 의국에서 분과 저널 (8:00~8:30)과 가이드라인 리뷰가

시에  발표합니다. 이때, 의학용어를 정확하고 간결하게 사용하여 의미가 잘 전달되도록 하며 
진단 및 치료 등의 관계에 대하여 이해합니다. 
5) 맡은 환자는 매일 진찰하고 경과기록을 남기며 중요시술에 참관합니다. 
6) 외래 참관 시 신래 환자를 맡아 병력 청취 및 이학적 검사를 시행하여 기록합니다. 이후 교수님
과 같이 환자를 보며 질의 문답 시간을 가지고 환자의 진단에 따라 그에 대한 병인 및 치료 
등에 대하여 공부할 수 있도록 합니다.

에 대해 담당 교수님과 강의 및 토론하는 시간을 가질 예정이며 강의 전 해당 주제를 예습합니
다.
8) 따로 배부된 신장내과 임상 실습 노트를 직접 작성하여 학습 성과에 도달할 수 있도록 합니다.
9) 정해진 실습 이외 시간에는 문진,병력 청취, 의무기록 작성 및 영상, 검사 해석을 시행합니다.
10) 실습 중 정해진 날짜에 CPX와 OSCE 실습 평가에 참여합니다.

l 실습시작 첫째 주 월요일 오전 8시 30분 신관 3층 인공신장실 내 신장내과 의국으로 모인다.
4. 과소개
l 실습을 나온 학생들은 신장내과 교수 및 임상교수, 전공의 지도 감독 하에 입원 및 외래 환자
를 보면서 의사와 환자의 관계에 대해 이해하며 신장질환에 대해 접근, 감별진단, 치료에 대
해 학습한다. 입원 환자에 대해 회진, bed side teaching, 아침 증례발표, order 연습 등을 
중점적으로 하고, 외래 환자는 1회 외래를 참관하여 짧은 시간내 진단으로 이어가는 과정을 
견습한다. 과의 구성은 4명의 교원, 5명 (3명은 3월 근무 예정)의 임상교원이 있으며 신장실 
수간호사외 간호사 16명과 복막투석 간호사 1명, 장기이식코디네이터 1명, 외래간호사 3명이 
있다. 주병동은 52병동 (신관)과 응급 및 내과 중환자실(본관, 신관 2층)이고, 인공신장실 (혈
액투석실, 신관3층)과 복막투석실 (본관1층 신장내과 외래 내), 장기이식센터 (본관 1층 감마
나이프실 옆)가 있다.

5. 신장학 학습목표 
l 임상 실습을 마친 학생은 다음 사항을 할 수 있어야 한다.
1) 신기능 검사, 일반 뇨검사와 24시간뇨 검사의 결과를 해석할 수 있다.
2) 전해질 이상을 평가하고 원인을 감별하고, 치료 계획을 수립할 수 있다.
3) 산염기 이상을 평가하고 동맥혈 분석결과를 해석할 수 있다.
4) 혈뇨와 단백뇨의 원인을 감별하고, 사구체 질환의 증상과 조직진단을 설명할 수 있다.
5) 핍뇨/무뇨의 원인을 감별하고, 급성/만성 신부전을 분류하며 보전적 치료와 신대체 요법 적
용에 대해 설명할 수 있다.
6) 부종, 빈뇨, 배뇨통과 배뇨장애의 병력청취와 진찰을 통해 감별진단과 치료계획을 수립할 수 있다.

9. 환자안전교육
* 환자안전교육 (3개 병원 공통)
1) 조영제를 사용하는 영상 검사 시 발생 가능한 합병증에 대한 환자 안전 교육을 시행하고 
이에 대해 모니터링한다. 
2) 신장 조직 검사 시 발생 가능한 합병증에 대한 환자 안전 교육을 시행하고 이에 대해 모니터
링한다.
3) 혈액 투석 도관 삽입시 시 발생 가능한 합병증에 대한 환자 안전 교육을 시행하고 이에 대해 
모니터링한다. 
4) 복막 투석 도관 삽입시 시 발생 가능한 합병증에 대한 환자 안전 교육을 시행하고 이에 대해 
모니터링한다. 
5) 동정맥루 수술 시 발생 가능한 합병증에 대한 환자 안전 교육을 시행하고 이에 대해 모니터
링한다. 
6) 도뇨관 삽입 시 발생 발생 가능한 합병증에 대한 환자 안전 교육을 시행하고 이에 대해 모니
터링한다.
7) 의료정보 유출의 위험성을 알고 숙지한다. 환자 정보는 익명화함을 원칙으로 하며, 민감한 
개인정보 (환자번호)는 사용하지 않는다. 또한, 임상실습기간동안 부여받은 실습용 ID와 비밀
번호가 외부에 유출되지 않도록 주의한다. 원내 전자의무기록 프로그램에 접속할 때는 사용 후 
반드시 로그아웃을 한다.
8) 원내 감염 발생의 위험성을 알고 실습기간 동안 손위생을 철저하게 실시한다. 특히, 손위생
이 필요한 다섯가지 시점 (환자 접촉전, 청결/무균술 전, 혈액 및 채액 접촉 후, 환자 접촉 후, 
주변환경 접촉 후)을 숙지한다.

환자의 올바른 병력청취, 신체진찰, 검사해석 등을 통하여 스키마를 이용한 실세계의 임상 상황 또는

Ÿ

Ÿ
본인이 알고 있는 지식과 정보를 다른 사람에게 정확히 발표 전달하고 토론하는 능력을 키운다.

실, 외래 환자를 공부한다. 환자에 대한 실습은 전임교수, 진료교수, 임상강사, 전문간호사와 
함께 진행되며 모두 평가에 참여한다. 오전 8시반(혹은 9시)부터 2층 인공신장실 안의 신장
내과 의국에서 환자브리핑(혹은 병동회진)을 한다. 매주 화요일, 수요일, 금요일 오후 12시
30분부터 별관 지하1층 소강당 또는 화상회의를 통한 내과콘퍼런스 참석한다. 
2) 월요일 첫 날 오전 책임교수로부터 오리엔테이션(인공신장실, 신장내과 외래, 복막투석실 
소개, 2주간 실습일정, 입원환자 배정, 외래참관 날짜배정, 협진환자 배정)을 받는다. 매일 
오전 입원 환자 회진 후 맡은 환자를 진찰하고 의무기록지를 작성하고 오후 협진환자 회진

과 실습미팅을 주제별로 미리 준비한다. 참관해야 하거나 익혀야 할 술기나 검사 등을 일정
을 확인하여 종료시간 전까지 챙겨서 익힌다. 아침 신환 발표는 현황표에 적인 순서대로 한 
명씩 매일 발표하며 요일별로 교수님께 상의하여 총 3명을 유지한다. 의무기록지는 매일 진
찰하고 경과기록을 남기며, 주 2회 담당교수에게 확인받는다. Grand Rounding (화요일과 
수요일)에 오전 회진 시 맡은 환자를 직접 진찰하고 이에 대해 토론한다. 
3) 2주간의 실습기간동안 학생들의 참고서적은 신장내과 의국에 비치해 있으므로 가능한 한 
신장내과 의국 내에서 실습준비와 숙제와 공부를 한다. 의국 내 서적은 외부로 반출이 안 
된다.
4) 직접 시행하여야 하는 임상술기는 전공의, 수련의와 미리 약속을 잡고 시행하고 확인받으
며, 신장조직검사, 투석도관 삽입술, 이식등 참관해야 하는 시술은 병동에서 환자의 일정을 
미리 확인하여 약속하여 참석하도록 한다. 기본적인 술기시행은 수련의나 전공의 선생님과 
일정을 잡아서 시행한다. 
5) 외래환자 참관실습은 매주 목, 금요일 오전 09:30-12:30에 차대룡, 차진주 교수 외래에서 
이뤄지며 부종(Edema), 혈뇨(Hematuria), 단백뇨(proteinuria), 핍뇨(Oliguria), 다뇨
(Polyuria)에 대하여 기본문진과 진찰을 할 수 있어야 한다. 
6) 매일 오후 실습미팅은 의국 내 일정표를 참고하여 신장내과 의국에서 주제에 따라서 진행되
며 증례 중심으로 하며 학생들은 충분히 예습을 해 와서 담당교수와 충분한 토론을 할 수 
있도록 한다.
7) 필수적으로 습득해야 할 흔한(또는 중요) 문제 및 질환을 과제로 실습 마지막 날까지 작성하
여 실습평가서, 임상술기 체크리스트와 함께 제출한다.
8) 환자 한 명의 증례에 대하여 질환 리뷰와 함께 마지막 주에 파워포인트 발표하고 담당교수
와 증례발표에 대하여 피드백을 받는다.

Course Description: This class reads recent novels firstly in order to explore issues pertinent to the twenty-first century, and secondly to try to 
determine novelistic aesthetics unique to the contemporary times. This class is conducted in English and will mainly consist of lectures, 
discussions, and in-class activities.

2. 
Normal People by Sally Rooney

*** Students are responsible for purchasing their own books. They may choose e-books instead of print editions, and the print editions do not 
need to match the editions used by the instructor. ***  
Course Objectives:  
-learn to read novels written in English as non-native speakers of English  
-learn to think about the “contemporaneity” through reading fictions 
-understand the aesthetics and politics of some of the recent novels 
 
Course Requirements/Grading Guidelines:  
Midterm and Final Exam (5% each): This is a low-risk, low-stress exam in which students will be required to write a short, handwritten essay 
for 30 minutes. Some clues about the topic will be provided prior to the exam. Students may bring short handwritten or typed memos of no more 
than a page to the exam. More details will be provided in advance. 
Quizzes (60%): This class will have quizzes almost every session throughout the semester. Each quiz will have 5 questions, mostly in the form of 
multiple-choice questions, short response questions, True or False/ Yes or No questions. Students who read the class materials on time will have 
no problem doing well on the quizzes. The quizzes will take no longer than 3 minutes. The lowest 5 quiz scores will be dropped when grading. No 
makeup quizzes will be given for any reason. 
In-class discussions (20%): Regular participation in class discussion is required. Students must sign their names on a sheet at the end of each 
class if they have participated in discussions. A record showing 15 times or more of participating in discussions will earn 20 points, 14 times 19 
points, 13 times 18 points, 12 times 17 points, and so on. 1 time will earn 6 points, none leads to 0 points.  
In-class activities (10%): Students will be expected to engage actively with brief in-class writing and reading exercises throughout the semester, 
as well as small group activities. What constitutes in-class activities?: group discussions, if applicable, in-class writing exercises, film screening, etc.  
Attendance (0%): Absences and tardiness will NOT affect your grade. Students do not need to provide documentation for their absences, 
lateness, etc. I will not accept them and will not read emails regarding attendance/absence. The university policy, however, mandates students to 
attend at least 2/3 of the semester in order to get a passing letter grade. This means that students who miss more than 10 sessions will get an 
automatic F. For this I will go over the roster every session.  
 
Plagiarism and Academic Dishonesty: Plagiarism is a serious academic breach. Students must always acknowledge the sources they consult. 
Acts of cheating and any other forms of academic dishonesty are violations of the university policy. The class imposes zero-tolerance policy on 
plagiarism and other forms of cheating. The misconduct will result in F. 
 
Other class policies:  
-I might occasionally make class announcements via email. Make sure that you have working email addresses. Make sure the email addresses saved 
in the Blackboard accounts are functioning. 
-I respond to student email queries within 48 hours during weekdays.  
-Grades are non-negotiable and can neither be lowered nor raised.  
-Uses of electronic devices are allowed in class for typing, searching, and reading. Recordings, however, are strongly discouraged. Should the need 
arise, please come talk.  
-I do not provide lecture notes, organized and visualized, in the form of ppt files or else. Students must take notes as needed.  
-No tolerance for disrespectful behavior and speech in the classroom.

Korean 003: Korean Language Variation 
 
Class time: Monday & Wednesday, 12:00 PM—1:15 PM 
Location: 국제관(International Studies Hall) 110 
Instructor: Dr. Drew Crosby 
E-mail: dmcrosby@korea.ac.kr 
Office Hours: Monday & Wednesday after class. 
 
 
Course Description 
The purpose of this class is to explore the ways in which the usage and perception of Korean varies 
both within and across individuals. Our exploration of this variation will include factors such as 
regional origin, age, gender, race, and native status. We will also look at many examples of real 
linguistic studies 
 
If you are a native speaker of Korean: Please be aware that this class includes a group project, and 
that many students in the class will be non-native speakers of Korean. If you do not want to work 
together with non-native speakers, please do not enroll in this class. 
 
If you are a non-native speaker of Korean: I recommend that you only enroll in this class if you have 
had the equivalent of at least 2 years of college-level Korean. Some assignments in this class will 
require you to interact with native Korean speakers (e.g. collecting survey data), and our discussion 
of various linguistic phenomena will assume that you already have a basic understanding of how the 
language works. If your Korean proficiency level prevents you from completing the required 
assignments or understanding the lecture, your grade will suffer. 
 
Course Objectives 
The overarching goal of this course is to acquire a basic knowledge of how language varies in the 
Korean language. More specifically students who complete the course should be able to do the 
following: 
1. Identify how languages (esp., Korean) vary linguistically and provide examples 
2. Outline the history of sociolinguistics and relate it to research on variation in Korean 
3. Discuss ideologies of authenticity in language 
4. Classify linguistic variants into stereotypes, markers, and indicators 
5. Define dialect/accent; 
6. Discuss what differentiates a langage from a dialect and relate this to 제주말 
7. Discuss the notions of enregisterment and standard language ideology and relate them to 
(standard) Korean 
8. Outline the different ways that people perceive languages and their users 
a. Identify several ways that researchers collect data on language perception 
9. Identify how languages (esp., Korean) vary socially and provide examples 
10. Discuss how gender and language interact with each other and outline the theories explaining 
this 
11. Discuss how language variation relates to language change 
12. Identify and provide examples of different types of politeness 
a. Discuss how these notions of politeness are (not) applicable to Korean 
b. Discuss the influence of politeness of language variation 
13. Discuss how languages influences one another and identify several areas that this can be seen 
in Korea(n) 
Textbook 
You do not need to purchase any textbooks for this course. All assigned readings will be made freely 
available to students.

Course Policies 
 
Class participation 
Class participation constitutes 10% of your course grade. For each class period, you can earn up to 
10 points. 2.5 points from being on time, 2.5 points from attendance, and 5 points from active 
participation. 
 
To receive active participation points you must contribute during class to the class as a whole. You 
will receive active participation points for the day when you ask or answer questions, share an idea 
or opinion with the class, or doing anything else that enriches the class in some way. I realize that 
some students will find this easier than others and that some students would have a hard time with 
this requirement even if the class were conducted in Korean. Please understand that the quality of 
this course depends on your collective participation. You will learn much more if you test your ideas 
by sharing them with the class and seek clarification when you don’t understand something. 
 
Attendance 
For your own learning and participation points, it is important to attend class when possible. 
However, I understand that life happens, and so it is natural to need to miss class sometimes and is 
important to prioritize your own health and the health of others by staying home when you feel ill, 
for example. The flip side of the coin is that you should come to class when you feel well and are 
able! Missing class occasionally should not cause problems if you make a sincere effort throughout 
the semester. Nevertheless, please let me know in advance if you know you’ll need to miss class. 
 
Electronic devices 
The use of laptop computers or tablets in class is OK, but I strongly encourage you to leave your 
mobile phone in your bag or pocket during class. You may use your phone for course-related 
activities (e.g., looking up a word in the dictionary), but they can also be very distracting, so please 
consider whether it is a good idea to keep it on your desk in front of you. 
 
Late work 
Assignments are due at 11:59 PM on the day indicated. Every day that it is late your assignment 
grade will receive a 20% penalty. The penalty will not be applied for weekends or holidays. 
 
Email 
I will send notices regarding class through Blackboard. Please make sure to check your KU email 
regularly.

Course Description
This course provides a systematic introduction to the core theories of mobile communication
engineering. Topics include large-scale and small-scale wireless channel modeling, modulation
and demodulation techniques, link budget analysis, performance evaluation over fading chan-
nels, and multi-antenna communication systems. The course emphasizes analytical approaches
based on probability and random processes and builds a solid foundation for understanding
modern mobile communication systems.

Korean companies and the Korean market. The course contents consist of three parts. First, an 
overview of the structure and specific features of the Korean economy will be given. Second, 
the management and international business of Korean firms will be discussed. Third, entry 
strategies for foreign firms on the Korean market will be studied. The participants of this course 
will work on these topics through class discussions, case studies, market entry proposals and 
team presentations.

In this project, you analyze one case study in a pre-assigned team and discuss it with your 
classmates during a course session. The team size will be determined depending on overall 
class size. A list of case studies will be provided at the beginning of the semester. You can 
choose any case study from the list provided. However, each case study will be assigned to 
only one student team on a first-come, first-served basis. The case studies need to be purchased 
online by students. The case study facilitations will be subject to a peer evaluation by all 
members of each respective team. 
(b) Case quizzes (Korea University students only): 
Short pop-up quizzes related to case studies that are discussed in the same session will be 
randomly given to students without pre-announcement over the duration of the semester. 
Except from the students who are facilitating the related case study, all participants have to take 
these quizzes.

(c) Market entry proposal (Korea University students only): 
In this project, you develop a proposal for a foreign company which currently does no business 
in Korea on how to enter the Korean market. Specifically, based on an analysis of the 
company’s profile and the market situation in Korea, you develop recommendations with 
which products or services the company should enter the Korean market, what is the best entry 
mode, and how the market entry should be implemented. You will work with the same team 
members as for the case study facilitations. You can select a company of your own choice for 
this project. However, each company will be assigned only to one team on a first-come, first-
served basis.  
Brief proposals (length: max. 2 pages) for each project need to be submitted by a to-be-
specified date in May. Thereafter, all proposals will be presented during the final weeks of the 
course. The market entry proposal projects will be subject to a peer evaluation by team 
members. 
(d) Midterm exam (Nanjing University students only) 
The midterm exam will consist of a series of questions related to the contents of the first half 
of the course, to be responded to by text answers. 
(e) Final exam: 
In the final exam you will write an in-depth essay. Within this essay, you apply your knowledge 
acquired in this course to a short business case. 
(f) Class participation: 
Class participation will be evaluated based on the quality and contents of your contributions. 
The level of your English language capabilities will not influence your grade as long as you 
can make yourself understandable in English.

students will be participating online. This course is a Korea University e-school course 
designed to enable students from overseas partner universities to participate online. Due to this 
particular format, course sessions are opened only once a week.

강의개요
 우리나라의 주거는 전통적으로 가족 중심의 단독 주거에서 출발하여, 산업화 이후 급격한 도시화 과정을 
거치며 대량 공급 중심의 집합주거로 변화해 왔다. 이 과정에서 주거는 삶의 방식과 사회적 관계를 담는 
공간이기보다는, 효율과 수량 중심의 유형으로 고착되었으며, 사적 영역과 공적 영역은 명확히 분리되어 왔다. 
그 결과 현대의 공동주택은 개인의 생활을 보호하는 데에는 성공했지만, 도시와 이웃, 공동체와의 관계를 
형성하는 데에는 한계를 드러내고 있다.
본 스튜디오는 이러한 한국 주거의 역사적 맥락을 바탕으로, 공동주택을 개인의 삶과 사회적 관계를 매개하는 
공간적 장치로 재해석하는 것을 목표로 한다. 특히 사적 공간과 공적 공간 사이에 존재하는 중간영역과 공유 
공간의 가능성에 주목하여, 거주자의 생활이 완전히 분리되거나 과도하게 노출되지 않는 새로운 주거 구조를 
탐구한다.
 설계 대상지는 용산구 한남동 705번지 일대 공터로, 이곳은 과거 도시계획시설(근린공원)로 지정된 토지를 
민간이 매입한 이후, 개발을 원하는 주체와 공공의 보존 논리가 충돌하며 장기간 갈등과 법적 분쟁을 겪은 
장소이다. 그 결과 개발도, 공원 조성도 이루어지지 못한 채 도시 속 공백 상태로 남아 있으며, 공공성과 
사유재산, 도시계획과 민간 개발의 긴장이 물리적으로 드러난 대표적인 장소라 할 수 있다.
 본 스튜디오는 이와 같은 도시적 갈등과 역사성이 축적된 공터를 설계 대상으로 삼아, 공동주택을 통해 새로운 
건축적 해석과 공간적 제안을 시도한다. 학생들은 도시 맥락 속에서 주거의 공공성, 공유 공간의 성격, 시선과 
동선의 관계, 공공성의 밀도를 종합적으로 고려하여, 이 장소에 대한 건축적 아이디어와 실천적 대안을 
제시하게 된다. 이를 통해 주거 건축이 동시대 도시와 사회 속에서 수행할 수 있는 역할을 비판적으로 탐구하는 
것을 본 스튜디오의 궁극적인 목표로 한다.
 
학습목표
 본 스튜디오는 공동주택을 단순한 주거 유닛의 집합이 아닌, 개인의 삶과 사회적 관계를 매개하는 공간적 
장치로 재해석하는 것을 목표로 한다. 학생들은 사적 공간과 공적 공간 사이에 존재하는 중간영역에 주목하여, 
거주자의 생활이 완전히 분리되거나 과도하게 노출되지 않는 새로운 주거 구조를 제안한다.
도시 맥락 속 공동주택을 설계 대상으로 삼아, 공유 공간과 반공적 영역의 역할, 공공성의 밀도, 시선과 동선의 
관계를 종합적으로 고려한다. 이를 통해 공동체가 자연스럽게 형성되는 공간 조직을 탐구하고, 건축이 사회적

수업개요 
생성형 AI의 급속한 확산은 미디어 산업과 연구 환경 전반에 구조적인 변화를 가져오고 있다. 데
이터 수집, 전처리, 분석, 해석의 많은 과정이 AI 도구를 통해 자동화되고 있지만, 이러한 변화는 
오히려 기초적인 코딩 원리에 대한 이해의 중요성을 더욱 부각시키고 있다. AI를 효과적으로 활용
하고 그 결과를 비판적으로 해석하기 위해서는, 알고리즘이 어떤 논리로 작동하는지, 데이터가 어
떤 과정을 거쳐 처리되는지를 이해하는 기초 역량이 필수적이기 때문이다.  
본 수업은 이러한 변화된 환경 속에서 미디어 전공자가 갖추어야 할 데이터 사이언스의 기초 역
량을 강화하는 것을 목표로 하며, 특히 프로그래밍 언어를 데이터 분석의 도구이자 사고 방식으로 
이해하는 데 초점을 둔다. 프로그래밍 언어는 컴퓨터와 소통하기 위한 가장 기본적인 언어이자, 
오늘날 다양한 학문 및 산업 분야에서 필수적인 범용 역량으로 자리 잡고 있다. 여러 프로그래밍 
언어 가운데 파이썬(Python)은 비교적 직관적인 문법 구조를 가지고 있어 사회과학 전공자도 접근
하기 용이하며, 데이터 수집·전처리·분석을 위한 풍부한 라이브러리를 제공한다. 
본 수업에서는 데이터 사이언스 분야에서 널리 활용되는 파이썬의 기본 문법과 논리 구조를 체계
적으로 학습한 후, 이를 바탕으로 웹 데이터 수집, 데이터 전처리, 텍스트 분석 등 미디어 데이터 
분석 실습을 진행한다. 나아가 수업 후반부에는 실제 미디어 데이터를 활용한 팀 프로젝트를 통해, 
분석 결과를 해석하고 의미 있는 시사점을 도출하는 경험을 제공한다. 아울러 본 수업은 데이터 
분석의 전체 흐름을 이해하고, AI 기반 도구를 블랙박스가 아닌 분석 파트너로 비판적으로 활용할 
수 있는 기초 역량을 함양하는 것을 핵심 목표로 한다.

2. Course Description 
This course examines the relationship between health and nutrition, focusing on how 
dietary patterns influence physical, mental, and social well-being. Students will learn 
fundamental concepts of nutrition, including macronutrients, micronutrients, and energy 
metabolism, and explore their application to weight management, nutritional assessment, 
and patient care.

categories rather than precise nutrient calculations.

Course Description 
This required course at KUBS offers a broader and more integrative perspective than your 
previous courses, encompassing key concepts from accounting, finance, marketing, and 
operations management. Strategic management focuses on the systematic study of how 
organizations can achieve sustainable competitive advantages. We aim to bridge theory with 
real-world business examples through a variety of learning methods, including exercises and 
case studies.  
In each class, we will discuss actual business situations, adopting the perspectives of general 
managers, CEOs, presidents, or management consultants. The challenges faced by general 
managers are often complex and unstructured, necessitating decisions made with incomplete 
information. This course aims to replicate these ambiguous scenarios, encouraging students to 
recommend strategies that enhance their analytical and decision-making skills. Through this 
approach, we aspire to equip students with the tools necessary for effective strategic 
management in dynamic business environments. 
 
Course Objectives 
1. To learn the jargon of the business world in preparation for your career.  
2. To see the ‘big picture’ facing general managers. Even though it is unlikely that you 
will start your career as the CEO, the sooner you begin thinking strategically about the 
overall goals of the organization, the faster your career will progress.  
3. To distinguish between basic causes, and symptoms of business problems.  
4. To apply the conventional wisdom of strategic management to practical settings.  
5. To integrate the knowledge accumulated in previous core courses, and experience.  
6. To learn from each other by sharing perspectives and experiences.  
7. To develop critical thinking skills – a capacity for analyzing problems on a broad 
business and company-wide basis.  
 
Subject Design and Requirements 
This course will thrive on active student participation, which greatly enhances the learning 
experience for everyone involved. Your insights and contributions are invaluable to our 
collective understanding of the material. The course will employ a combination of lectures, 
discussions, case analyses, and in-class exercises. We will conclude the course with both 
individual and group case reports, providing you with the opportunity to apply the conceptual 
materials in a competitive environment. 
In a typical class session, we will begin with a lecture that introduces key concepts and 
provides guidance for your studies. It is essential that you read the assigned texts before each 
lecture, as the materials covered will be integral to your team and individual analysis reports. 
PowerPoint slides will be available for download from Blackboard (or other tools) to aid your 
preparation. 
After several lectures, we will engage in exercises designed to reinforce the material learned. 
These may include mini-cases, situational analyses, and other interactive activities. While no 
formal grades will be assigned to these assignments, your active, positive, and enthusiastic 
involvement will be reflected in your class participation grade. 
Attendance is expected at all classes, and punctuality is crucial, especially for Zoom sessions 
(if applicable) and presentations. Your commitment to being present and contributing to 
discussions will significantly enrich the learning experience for both you and your peers. 
 
KUBS Attendance Policy: If you are absent for more than one-third of the 30 scheduled 
classes (more than 10 sessions), you will automatically receive a failing grade (F) for the 
course. Some students may consider 9 absences acceptable. BUT,  
**Missing nine classes will not automatically result in an F. However, accumulating nine 
absences is inconsistent with the goals of class participation and the instructional purpose of 
the course, and it will therefore have a substantially negative impact on your final grade. 
Absences due to documented illness or emergencies will not have a negative impact. At the 
same time, students who attend all sessions without any absences (including excused absences) 
can expect a positive impact on their final grade through attendance and participation credit. 
*** From Third Week, students can choose their own seats, which will be their permanent 
seats for the semester. 
 
Assessment 
A) Class participation = 20% 
B) Midterm Test = 20% 
C) Team Case Analyses = 30% (25% + Debating Group Score = 5%) 
D) Final Exam = 30% 
Total Points Possible = 100% 
 
A. Class participation  
Since this course employs an action-oriented learning approach through case 
discussions and exercises, it is essential for students to attend class and actively 
participate. This aspect of your grade is based on your proactive involvement in class 
activities.  
B. Midterm Test 
The midterm test will include multiple-choice questions, short answer questions to 
assess your understanding of key concepts, and analytical questions based on the 
material covered in class. 
C. Team Case Analysis Presentation 
Students will be assigned a case as part of a team project, in which you will identify 
relevant problems and analyze the situations facing the organization. Each team will 
select one firm from the list provided (to be announced) and will be responsible for 
identifying relevant issues, analyzing the organization's situation, and developing 
strategic recommendations to address these challenges. 
Your team will present your assigned firm. Each group will be responsible for 
identifying relevant problem(s), analyzing the situation facing the organization, and 
developing strategy recommendations to address these issues. Additionally, there will 
be a debating group assigned to challenge your presentation. 
Your presentation should include the following elements:  
◼ Situational analysis with recent data 
◼ Identification of problem(s) and/or issue(s) 
◼ Tools and methods employed for analysis 
◼ Strategy formulation and recommendations 
◼ The recommendations should encompass corporate-level strategies, business-
level strategies, international strategies, etc. There are no specific formatting 
requirements for the presentation—this is your opportunity to showcase your 
creativity (e.g., PowerPoint presentation, audio and video, drama, games, etc.). 
Presentation Formatting Requirements: 
  
Length: 20 minutes + 5 minutes for Q&A 
 
File name and format: PT_Team_TOPIC.pptx (e.g., PT_TeamA_Google. Pptx) 
Submission due: the day before your designated presentation, 6pm via email (to me, 
and to your counterparts) 
 
*For the debating group: You are expected to challenge the presenting group by posing 2 
questions that oppose their arguments. Your performance will be evaluated based on the quality 
of your questions and the effectiveness of your debate.  
** Other Class Manner: To encourage audience engagement, laptops are not permitted during 
presentation days. I also recommend that students refrain from using laptops during my lectures.  
Additionally, earbuds and recording devices are not allowed. Please do not sell class 
recordings or course materials online, such as on Klue or everytime.kr. 
*** If you miss any section and receive a score of zero, your final grade will be an “F”. 
For example, if the final exam score is 0 due to absence or an uncorrected zero, the final 
grade will be an F. This policy is non-negotiable. 
 
**** If you expect to be inattentive during class due to job hunting or other 
personal reasons, please consider switching to a different section. This is to ensure 
fairness for all students. Hardworking students will be appropriately rewarded, 
but there will be no leniency for those who are inattentive1.

OFFICE HOURS: By appointment 
 
 
 
COURSE DESCRIPTION  
Combining theories and practices, this course supports the graduation level of design study for product 
development. It is a combined studio-based work and students will be provided with different topics and 
process every year. The class will introduce strategic design thinking associated with major contemporary 
issues on human society and complex systems in exploring and creating a new type of product and 
service. 
* NOTE) Since this course is one of the graduation exhibition courses in design, non-design majored students 
will NOT be allowed to take this course. Students must complete all the prerequisite courses in design major 
and should be qualified with a graduation level of design knowledge (e.g., design research methods) and 
practical skillsets (e.g., Rendering & 3D modeling, Service UX Design) before enrolling in the class. 
 
COURSE OBJECTIVES 
The goal of this course is to learn and practice the comprehensive aspects in product design development 
in the modern interdisciplinary context. 
- To learn about the convergent design process in developing a new category of products and services  
- To understand the critical principles of design thinking in identifying and solving contemporary issues  
- To practice various design methods and skills for the competitive design setting 
 
EVALUATION & GRADING  
While a term project itself is a major object of evaluation, in-class participation and attitude are also 
critical in individual grading. Final grading will be made based upon participation of class activities, 
research quality, and project outcomes and in order to maximize class learning process, peer evolution in 
each phase of presentations can be included. 
- Weekly Assignments: 20% 
- Mid-term report: 30% 
- Term project: 40% (Research & Rationale 30%, Creativity & Aesthetics 30%, Degree of Completion 40%)     
- Attendance & Collaboration: 10%

이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으

할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비

Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습

▶ 과목개요 
 본 수업에서는 일본 헤이안(平安)시대(8-12세기)에 쓰여진 일본고전문학작품과 문
화의 양상을 <문자텍스트>가 아닌 <그림>을 통해 접근해보고자 한다. 
-우선,  헤이안(平安)시대 문학과 문화, 역사에 대한 전반적 설명을 통해 개괄적 이
해를 꾀한다.
-당시 회화 작품들의 작법과 구도, 구성,  미술사적 흐름과 위상을 파악한다.
-일본 대표적 고전작품인 『다케토리모노가타리(竹取物語)』 『겐지모노가타리(源氏
物語)』의 중요 장면을 그린 그림을 해독, 감상한다. 특히, 당시 그림에 담긴 내용을 
일본고전문학작품과 관련시켜 해독함으로써 문학과 생활, 역사, 건축, 예술 등 당시
의 전반적인 문화의 양상을 살펴본다.  또한 국보 『겐지모노가타리에마키(源氏物語
絵巻)』와 거의 동시대에 그려진『시기산엔기에마키(信貴山縁起絵巻)』『반다이나곤
에마키(伴大納言絵巻)』『조수인물회화(鳥獣人物戯画)』와 같은 설화에마키와 풍속
화를 대상으로 하여 당시 문화, 예술, 사회와 연관시켜 고찰한다.
▶ 학습목표 
-회화와 문학이라는 장르를 연관시켜 살펴봄으로써 일본 고전문학과 문화에 대한 
개괄적인 특징을 학습하고 이해를 높이고자 한다.
-일본고전문학작품과 그림 속에 반영된 시대상과 일본인의 정신세계를 파악한다.

개요 
Radiation Biology provides a comprehensive exploration of the fundamental 
principles that govern the interactions between radiation and living organisms. 
This dynamic field sits at the intersection of physics, biology, and medicine and 
focuses on the effects of various forms of radiation on biological systems. The 
course is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in radiation 
biology, covering essential concepts, mechanisms, and applications.

medical physics, radiation therapy, radiology and related fields where an 
understanding of the biological effects of radiation is essential.

수업목표 일반 
Overall Goals of the Radiation Biology Course 
 
1) Comprehensive Understanding: 
To provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental 
principles and concepts of radiation biology. 
 
2) Healthcare Application: 
Enable students to apply their knowledge of radiation biology in the context of 
health care, particularly in radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, and related 
medical fields. 
 
3) Interdisciplinary Knowledge: 
Develop an interdisciplinary perspective by integrating principles from physics, 
biology, and medicine in the study of radiation biology. 
세부목표 1 
Cellular and Molecular Understanding: 
Explore the cellular and molecular mechanisms of radiation interaction with living 
organisms, with emphasis on DNA damage, repair processes, and cell cycle 
responses. 
세부목표 2 
Radiation Effects on Tissues and Organs: 
Examine the differential sensitivity of various tissues to radiation, understanding 
both acute and chronic effects on organs and their functional consequences. 
세부목표 3 
Clinical Applications: 
Discuss the clinical applications of radiation biology in radiation therapy, including 
treatment planning, dose optimization, and the use of advanced technologies.

Sustainable Development Goals: Quality Education
Course objective:
• SPGE400: From Galileo to Einstein (Undergraduate/Credits: 3)
We investigate the history of science since its birth by Galileo through the discovery of the
special theory of relativity by Albert Einstein.
We focus on the fact that revolutionary
transitions in human history always stem from scientific observations of natural phenomena,
followed by the leading escape from scientific absurdity by physicists like Galileo, Newton,
and Einstein.
– Goal 1: enhance the ability of quantitative reasoning
– Goal 2: enhance the ability of qualitative reasoning
– Goal 3: investigate the history of science starting from Galileo to Einstein.
• SPGE401: Escape from Scientific Absurdity (Undergraduate/Credits: 3)
We mainly focus on escaping from the ignorance of the physics background of various math-
ematical formulas. Calculus and differential equations originate not from pure mathematics
branches but from physicists’ pioneering efforts to solve problems such as classical mechanics
and electrodynamics. We first deal with Euclidean Geometry with vector algebra, which is
also developed by physicists. We experience the analytic properties of power-series expansions
to approximate useful functions appearing in physics problems. The analytic nature of physi-
cal functions leads us to explore the nature of the Newtonian equation of motion. Finally, we
investigate the equivalence of the Euler-Lagrange equation to Newtonian mechanics and the
development of the calculus of variations, resulting in the discovery of Hamilton’s least-action
principle.
– Goal 1: enhance the ability of quantitative reasoning
– Goal 2: enhance the ability of qualitative reasoning
– Goal 3: investigate first principles of the physical universe
• SPGE412: Intellectual Beauty Hiding in Physics (Undergraduate/Credits: 3)
We appreciate and enjoy the intellectual beauty hiding in physics by investigating the his-
torical and philosophical aspects of the fundamental theoretical structure that has led to the
scientific revolution.
– Goal 1: enhance the ability of quantitative reasoning
– Goal 2: enhance the ability of qualitative reasoning
– Goal 3: appreciate and enjoy the intellectual beauty hiding in physics
1
• UNIV534: KPOPE Physics Series X (Undergraduate/Credits: 3)
We study fundamental concepts of classical mechanics of particles and waves, thermal and
statistical mechanics.
– Goal 1: understand elementary concepts of classical mechanics of a particle and a system
of particles
– Goal 2: understand elementary concepts of wave
– Goal 3: understand elementary concepts of thermal and statistical physics
• UNIV535: KPOPE Physics Series Y (Undergraduate/Credits: 3)
We study fundamental concepts of electromagnetism, interference of light waves, relativity,
and quantum mechanics.
– Goal 1: understand elementary concepts of electromagnetism
– Goal 2: understand elementary concepts of the light wave
– Goal 3: understand elementary concepts of relativity and quantum mechanics
• PHY505: Quantum Mechanics I (Graduate/Credits: 3)
We study the fundamental theoretical framework of quantum mechanics. The first part covers
the review of classical mechanics, including relativity and classical electrodynamics. After
constructing the Lorentz covariant form of Maxwell’s equations, we construct Schr¨odinger
equation. The second part covers the time evolution of state kets. We focus on the state kets
for a free particle state and a harmonic oscillator to evaluate the propagators. Feynman’s
path integral approach is also employed to reproduce them. The third part is devoted to the
unitary transformations of translation and rotation.
• PHY506: Quantum Mechanics II (Graduate/Credits: 3)
We study fundamental concepts for quantum mechanical descriptions of hydrogen atom, per-
turbation theory, and scattering theory

ORGANIZATIONAL DESIGN AND COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE 
 
Spring 2026 
Tuesday and Thursday 1:30-2:45 pm @ LP217 
 
Instructor: Juyoung Lee 
Email: jlee29@korea.ac.kr 
Office Hour: by appointment 
 
 
 
COURSE DESCRIPTION                                                  
This course examines what organizations are and how they are designed and managed to 
achieve goals, sustain competitive advantage, and survive in dynamic and uncertain 
environments. Adopting a macro-level perspective, the course focuses on the organization as 
the primary unit of analysis while also considering internal groups and the external 
environment. By integrating theoretical frameworks with real-world examples and case 
analyses, students explore how organizational design influences effectiveness and adaptation, 
along with contingency factors such as the external environment. 
 
COURSE MATERIAL 
Daft. 2021. Organizational Theory and Design (13th Asia Edition). Cengage.

For students who elect to take this course under the Pass/Fail grading option, successful 
completion of the course requires fulfilling all course requirements. Failure to complete any 
assignment, or submitting work that does not meet the minimum acceptable level of quality, 
will result in a grade of “Fail.” 
 
Individual Attendance, Participation, and Quizzes (60%) 
⚫ 
Class Attendance (10%): Regular attendance is required. Up to four absences per 
semester will not be penalized, provided prior written notice is given to the instructor via 
email. Students absent for more than one-third of total class hours cannot receive a grade.   
2 
⚫ 
Class Participation (10%): Active participation in discussions and in-class activities is 
expected and assessed throughout the course. 
⚫ 
Quiz 1 (20%) and Quiz 2 (20%): Two quizzes are scheduled for April 23 and May 28. 
These quizzes are designed to assess both your understanding of the course material and 
your ability to apply concepts and theories to real-world cases. Each quiz will include a 
variety of question formats, such as multiple-choice, short-answer, and essay questions, 
as well as case or article analyses. The quizzes will be closed-book; however, you may 
bring one one-page summary note to support your recall during the quiz. 
 
Group Project (40%) 
At the beginning of the semester, students will form groups of three to four members. To 
facilitate this process, each student is required to post a brief self-introduction on the LMS by 
March 9. Based on these introductions, groups will be formed during the class session on 
March 10. Once established, groups will remain unchanged throughout the semester and will 
serve as the primary working units for all group projects and in-class breakout activities. 
For the group project, each team will select a real organization that is currently facing an 
organizational challenge. Groups are expected to conduct in-depth research on the selected 
organization, analyze the nature of the challenge, and develop well-reasoned 
recommendations using concepts and theories from the course. 
 
⚫ 
Mini Presentation (10%). This mini presentation is intended to set the foundation for 
your final project. Each group will select one organization of any type (e.g., company, 
nonprofit organization, government agency, student organization, or community 
organization). The presentation should:  
 
Introduce the organization, including its mission, goals, and basic structure  
 
Clearly identify and explain one or more key organizational challenges it is 
currently facing.  
 
⚫ 
Final Presentation (20%). In the final presentation, groups will present well-supported 
recommendations for addressing the identified organizational challenges, drawing 
explicitly on relevant course concepts and theories. Participation should be balanced, 
with all members actively contributing to both the analysis and delivery (Each group 
member must speak at least once). 
 
⚫ 
Final Paper (10%). A final written report on the case organization is due by 11:59 p.m. 
on June 18. The final paper should provide a thorough analysis of the organization’s 
challenge and present theoretically grounded recommendations supported by clear 
reasoning and evidence. The paper should not exceed 2,000 words, excluding tables, 
figures, references, and supplementary materials, and should be formatted in single-
spaced, 12-point Times New Roman. 
 
⚫ 
Peer Evaluation: At the end of the semester, each student will complete a brief peer 
evaluation assessing the contributions of their group members. These evaluations are 
intended to ensure fairness and accountability within each team. If the evaluations 
indicate that a member did not contribute an appropriate and equitable share of the work, 
their individual project grade may be adjusted downward, regardless of the overall team 
performance.

(전략과 정보의 경제학) 
Spring 2026 
 
 
1. Basic Course Information 
• 
Course number: ECON 324 
• 
The class meets at 1:30-2:45 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays.  
• 
Classroom: SK Mirae Hall #4119 
 
2. Instructor Information 
• 
Instructor: Professor Wonki Cho (Department of Economics; chowonki@korea.ac.kr)  
• 
Homepage: https://sites.google.com/site/wonkijocho/ 
• 
Office: Political Science and Economics Building #316 
• 
Office hours: 10:15-11:45 a.m. on Mondays or by appointment 
• 
Teaching Assistant: Young Hyun Yu (melody9503@gmail.com) 
 
3. Course Overview 
• 
Description: This course aims to provide basic tools in game theory and information 
economics at a rigorous level. It also covers some applications.  
• 
Prerequisites  
◦ ECON173 (Mathematics for Economists, 경제수학) 
◦ Calculus (differentiation and integration): Students with a weak mathematical 
background should review basic concepts in calculus.  
• 
Course format 
◦ About 90% of each class will be devoted to lecture and the remaining 10% to Q&A 
sessions and discussions.  
◦ Lectures focus on understanding basic concepts and solving problems. Asking 
questions is a critical part of learning and students are strongly encouraged to do so in 
class. 
◦ The course is delivered in English. 
 
4. Evaluation  
• 
Evaluation scheme:  
Mid-term exam (35%), final exam (40%), assignments (20%), participation (5%) 
• 
Exam dates are fixed as follows. 
◦ Mid-term exam: 6:30-9:00 p.m. on April 24, 2026 
◦ Final exam: 6:30-9:00 p.m. on June 19, 2026 
• 
Requirements  
◦ Check the course webpage on Blackboard on a regular basis and ensure that your 
email address is up to date in the system. All announcements and course material are 
posted there.  
◦ Take two exams.  
◦ Problem sets will be assigned roughly every three weeks, with two problem sets 
assigned before the mid-term exam and another two after the exam. The lecture notes 
uploaded to Blackboard after each class may contain further assignments. Late 
submissions of assignments will not be accepted.  
◦ “Participation” is not the same as just attending classes. It means participating in 
discussions and asking questions in class and office hours.  
• 
Grades 
◦ Except in the case of wrongly entered grades, final letter grades will not be changed 
for any reason. In particular, a C will not be downgraded to an F.  
◦ Failure to take the mid-term or final exam automatically results in an F.  
 
5. Materials and References 
• 
Main textbooks  
◦ P. K. Dutta, 1999, Strategies and Games, MIT Press.  
◦ I. Macho-Stadler and J. D. Perez-Castrillo, 1997, An Introduction to the Economics of 
Information (2nd edition), Oxford University Press.  
• 
Other references 
◦ 
왕규호∙조인구, 2004, 게임이론, 박영사 
◦ 
김영세, 2002, 게임이론 (3판), 박영사 
 
6. Topics To Be Covered 
• 
Introduction: Modeling strategic interactions  
• 
Strategic-form games 
◦ Basic concepts: strategy (pure and mixed), payoff, rationality and common 
knowledge of rationality 
◦ Dominance, best response, Nash equilibrium 
◦ Application: Cournot duopoly, tragedy of commons 
• 
Extensive-form games 
◦ Basic concepts: game tree, subgame, strategy (pure and mixed) 
◦ Nash equilibrium, subgame perfect Nash equilibrium 
◦ Repeated game 
◦ Application: bargaining, entry game 
• 
Games of incomplete information  
◦ Basic concepts: type, prior distribution, Bayes’ rule 
◦ Bayesian Nash equilibrium 
◦ Application: Signaling value of education 
• 
Information economics 
◦ Moral hazard 
◦ Adverse selection 
◦ Mechanism design 
 
7. Classroom Decorum 
• 
Use of mobile devices such as cell phones and laptops is restricted, except for the purpose of 
note-taking. 
• 
Do not eat or sleep in class.

본 교과목은 주요 다변량 통계 기법을 체계적으로 학습하고, 이를 실제 데이터 분석 문제에 적용하는 능력을

다변량 분석기법의 개요를 제시하고, 벡터와 행렬의 기하학적 해석 등 기본적인 배경지식 및 다중회귀분석에

사용되는 여러 방법을 소개하며, 여기에는 잠재변수를 포함한 구조방정식모형(SEM), 로짓 선택모형(logit

▷공통 안내 및 주의사항 
∙ [출석] 
 -1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가
능, 단 출석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함
∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 학습에 적
극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서 위치를 작가하며 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐
구에 정진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과 약속한 사항을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생들의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 학문적 지식탐구 및 미래 비전과 연결된 교과목 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 미리 교육자료 탐독하고 확인
 -정해진 수업시간에 결석, 지각, 중도 이탈 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -적극적으로 토론, 질의응답 등 수업활동에 참여
 -스스로 성실하게 작성한 과제를 제출하고 인용한 모든 자료는 변조, 왜곡 없이 표시
 -협동학습의 경우 자신이 맡은 부분을 책임있게 완수하고 최선의 노력을 다함
 -교과목에서 요구하는 시험의 목적과 의미를 인식하고 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한학기 수강한 교과목의 강의 품질 개선을 위한 강의평가를 정직하게 수행
∙ [실험실습 안전]
 -연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과
학기술분야 대상학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 
하므로 실험·실습을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수

认真履行与教师及同学在教育活动中约定的事项。

尊重教师和同学的人格，遵守基本礼仪。

充分了解课程计划，选择与学术知识探索及未来愿景相关的课程。

提前阅读和确认教育资料，积极参与每堂课。

注意避免在规定的上课时间内缺席、迟到或中途离场。

禁止与出席相关的欺诈行为（如代替出席等）。

积极参与讨论、问答等课堂活动。

-

한다.

망을 파악하고, 관련 분야 간의 연계성과 전체적인 산업 흐름을 학습한다.
영문요목
- This course aims to provide comprehensive knowledge of energy conversion 
systems based on thermal, chemical, and mechanical energy.
- Students will acquire specialized understanding of electrochemical energy 
systems beyond traditional energy generations, such as batteries and fuel cells, 
alongside an in-depth analysis of global industry trends.
- Through a comprehensive study of the energy-related industry, the course 
explores future technological and industrial prospects, emphasizing integration and 
connectivity among related fields.

19th century English Novel (기말시험 6월15일)
Overview
The module aims to read Tess of the d’Urbervilles (1891) that catapulted its author Thomas 
Hardy into the midst of a violent storm of controversy. Tess of the d’Urbervilles, published in 
the fin de siécle, is the place where the vital energy of conventional values and the strength of 
the forces that demolish them are mixed in great tension. Encompassing as it does both the 
closing and onset of an era, the novel represents the Victorian period of degeneration, yet at 
the same time a period of hope for a new beginning at various points of conflict. In order to 
appreciate all the implications registered in this conflict, students are asked to read the novel 
closely, paying full attention to pictorial forms and furthermore contrasting it with Wuthering 
Heights (1847) by Emily Bronte and Middlemarch (1874) by George Eliot, for Hardy’s 
authorial intention is most vocal in his original use of word painting and he stands apart from 
other eminent Victorian writers in the way word painting is used as a narrative ruse. This 
module is designed to enhance students’ own critical thinking and develop aesthetic 
imagination through in-depth analysis of the texts. Discussion will revolve around pictorial 
forms in view of theme, structure, voice, and stylization.
Course Objective
The module focuses on the nature of Hardy’s pictorial writing which contrasts with that of 
Emily Bronte’s and George Eliot’s pictorial writing. Hardy’s philosophical and aesthetic 
thinking gains its momentum from a subterranean contest between centuries old binaries, 
such as feeling/form and nature/art; traditionally, these binary terms include the opposition of 
woman/man and present themselves in the inferior/superior hierarchy while the latter is 
always placed higher than the former. Hardy questions this hierarchy on the ground that one 
of the binaries can be central in human existence but cannot succeed in preventing the other 
from being present, though in background; in other words, it is impossible to isolate these 
binaries in pure form, because they are indissolubly intertwined and incessantly cross- 
fertilized. Students examine this dynamic mixture that goes to the creating of Hardy’s self- 
reflexive pictorial writing, thereby demonstrating that the main feature of this pictorial 
writing is that it is a battlefield in which an intense war between the afore-said binaries—for 
instance, feeling in constant flux and reason as a form-shaping force—takes place.
Primary Text
Tess of the d’Urbervilles (신아사 edition annotated by 정병조) 
Wuthering Heights (신아사 edition annotated by 김병익) 
Middlemarch (Oxford World’s Classics edited by David Carroll)
Reference Books
Ingham, Patricia. The Brontes (Oxford: OUP, 2008)
Hardy, Barbara. George Eliot: a Critic’s Biography (London: Continuum, 2006)
Cross, J. W. George Eliot’s Life, as Related in her Letters and Journals, 3 vols (NY: CUP, 
2010)
Millgate, Michael, ed., The Life and Work of Thomas Hardy (London: Macmillan, 1984) 
Bijork, Lennart A., ED., The Literary Notes of Thomas Hardy, 2 vols (Sweden: Acta 
Universitatics Gothoburgensis, 1974)
Orel, Harold, ed., Thomas Hardy’s Personal Writings (London: Macmillan, 1969)

심화임상실습 과정 소개 
◎ 정의
예비 전공의로서 관심있는 임상과의 전공의 업무를 파악할 수 있고, 진료업무에 실제적으로 참여하여 3
학년 핵심실습에서 배운 환자진료역량을 심화하는 실무역량 강화 프로그램(work-based learning)임. 인
턴과 달리 담당지도교수(이하 멘토교수)의 close observation 과 supervision을 바탕으로 실시간 피드
백을 제공받을 수 있고, 질문과 토론 또는 과제를 통해 실습학생을 하여금 실무 능력 및 의료인 직업전
문성을 학습하도록 돕는 교육프로그램임.
◎ 개설배경 및 목적
의학과 3학년의 임상실습은 이론으로 터득했던 의학지식이 진료현장에서 어떻게 적용되고 있는지를 배
우는 시간으로, 학생들은 실습조별단위로 나뉘어서 적극적인 환자 진료 참여를 전제로 진행되지만 현실
적으로 주로 참관 위주로 진행되는 경우가 많았음. 
이 과정에서 각 과의 교육프로그램에 따라 여러 명의 교수님들의 회진이나 외래, 수술을 참관하는 것도 
큰 장점이 있으나 특정 환자를 처음 외래부터 입원, 수술을 지속적으로 관찰하고 진료에 참여하는 것은 
한계가 있었음. 
이러한 점을 보완하기 위해 심화임상실습(서브인턴)과정은 학생들이 관심 있는 과를 선택하여 1명의 담
당 교수님 지도하에 외래, 수술, 입원환자 진료에 참여해서 환자에 대한 일련의 진단, 치료과정을 경험함
으로써 졸업후 1차 진료를 수행할 실무 능력을 배양할 수 있도록 배울 뿐 아니라 세부 전공의 실무에 
대한 이해를 높일 수 있도록 설계되었음.
◎ 구체적 목표
1) 연속성 있고 책임감 있는 진료현장 참여를 통한 의료 실무역량강화
2) 교수-학생 사이 멘토쉽 형성을 통한 전공 심화 체험을 통한 의료인 직업전문성 강화
3) 실무바탕 교육을 통한 자기 주도 학습 역량 촉진 
    
◎ 실습 방법 : 멘토 교수-학생 일대일 clinical attachment
2주 기간 동안 교수 1명에 학생 1명이 배정되어 멘토 교수가 지정해주는 환자의 진료에 적극 참여
(active engagement)하게 됨. 학생들이 1-2명의 환자를 연속성 있고 책임감 있게 진료경험을 할 수 있
도록 지도함.
예1) 정형외과 홍길동 교수와 김슬기 학생 
  김슬기 학생은 홍길동 교수가 배정해준 환자의 수술을 참관 또는 assist 한다 → 환자의 입원기간 
동안 홍길동교수의 밀착 감독 하에 주치 의사처럼 진료에 참여한다 → 환자가 퇴원하여 외래 F/U 
시, 김슬기 학생은 외래에서 환자를 다시 만나고 경과를 관찰한다.

Course Objective: Carry out fundamental laboratory experiments involving classical mechanics, rotational
motion and waves.
Major Competency based Course Objective:
 This course aims to enhance integrative thinking by connecting the theoretical classical mechanics
learned in General Physics and Exercise I with real-world applications. Through measurement and anal-
ysis in experiments, students will deepen their understanding of physical phenomena from multiple per-
spectives.
 This course aims to enhance students’ understanding of physical phenomena encountered in everyday
life, including noise cancellation, through such experiments as superposition of wave. Building on this
knowledge, the course will help students cultivate the ability to generate innovative ideas.
 This course aims to develop problem-solving skills by identifying and defining challenges that extend
beyond the manuals, analyzing these issues, and deriving solutions to successfully carry out experiments.

개요
미시경제이론은 미시경제학의 다양한 주제들을 포괄적으로 소개하는 과목으로 
수요-공급 분석, 개별 경제주체(가계와 기업)의 경제적 선택, 시장구조와 각 
시장 구조에서의 조정 및 경제적 성과, 일반균형이론과 후생경제학 등의 내용
을 다룰 것이다

제학의 가장 기본적인 연구 주제를 경제원론1보다 더 심화하여 습득하기를 원

  - 강의안에 내용이 비교적 자세하게 정리되어 있고 강의안을 숙지하면 풀수
    있는 수준으로 시험문제를 출제할 것이므로 수강을 위해 별도의 교과서를

  - 필요한 경우 시중에 있는 다양한 교과서들 가운데 본인이 마음에 드는

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

w

1. 한국어의 문장 구조를 이해하고 초급 수준의 어휘와 문법 표현을 사용하여 문장을 정확하게 쓸 수 있다.

3. 계획하는 글, 소개하는 글, 설명하는 글, 묘사하는 글의 기본 구조를 배워 목적에 맞는 글을 완성할 수 있다.

■ 강의 개요
읽고 쓰기, 듣고 말하기를 통합하여 배우는 통합 강의입니다. 초급 단계의 학습을 마친 학습자가 일
상적인 상황 및 친숙한 사회적 상황에서 자주 접하는 의사소통 과제를 수행하는 데에 필요한 언어 
항목을 학습합니다. 어휘, 문법 및 담화 표현을 학습한 후, 연습과 기능 통합 활동을 통해 정확하고 
유창한 한국어 사용에 도달하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 
■ 학습목표
 듣기, 말하기, 읽기, 쓰기에 대한 한국어 의사소통 능력을 키워 다음과 같이 수행할 수 있습니다.
  - 개인적, 사회적 주제에 대해 이해하고 단락 단위로 표현할 수 있다.
  - 사회적 관계를 맺거나 사회적 맥락에서의 의사소통 기능을 수행할 수 있다. 
  - 구어와 문어의 차이를 알고 맥락에 따라 표현할 수 있다.

3. 과 소개
l 감염질환을 포함하여 열 증상을 동반하는 질환들에 대하여 체계적인 접근방법과 적절한 검사
를 이용하여 원인을 규명하고 치료하는 임상 진료를 담당하고 있다. 또한, 다른 임상부서 환
자의 협의 진료와 원내 항생제 관리, 병원 감염관리 등의 업무를 수행한다. 환자 진료뿐만 
아니라 신종전염병 연구소를 운영하며 기초 및 임상 중개 연구, 신약 및 신의료 기술 개발과 
관련된 임상 시험을 진행하고 있다.
4. 학습목표
감염내과 임상실습을 모두 마친 학생은 다음 사항을 이해 및 이행할 수 있어야 한다.
1) 발열(불명열) 환자의 접근 방법 
2) 패혈증의 진단 및 치료
3) 감염 질환에서의 항생제 사용법 및 흔한 부작용
4) 균 동정법에 대한 이해와 임상 적용
5) 혈액배양 검사의 올바른 시행
5. 학생활동 또는 실습내용
# 실습 기간 중 포트폴리오를 작성하여 학습 자료를 증빙 서류화
1) 입원 환자 중에서 주당 최소한 2명 이상의 환자를 배정받아 보조 주치의 역할 수행
: 담당 환자의 의무 기록지 작성(둘째 주 금요일 제출)
2) 입원 및 협진 환자 회진에 참여하여, 환자 병력 청취 및 이학적 검진 방법 학습
3) 감염내과관련 임상 술기 참관 및 실습
- 실제 환자를 대상으로 시행되는 각종 술기 교육을 참관하고, 수기 참관 경험 기록지 작성
(둘째 주 금요일 제출)
- 실제 환자를 대상으로 시행되는 혈액배양 검체 채혈 과정을 참관한 후, 모형을 활용하여 
혈액배양 채혈을 실습
4) 병원 내 감염 관리의 중요성과 기본 개념 이해 및 이행
5) 저널 발표를 통한 최신 지식 및 저널 요약 및 발표 요령 습득

7. 환자 안전교육
○ 개인정보 보호
▸ 의료기관 개인정보
 - 식별정보: 성명, 주민등록번호, 연락처, 환자등록번호, 진료카드번호, 건강보험증번
   호 등 환자를 식별할 수 있는 정보
 - 의료정보: 환자의 건강상태, 신체적 특징, 병력(가족력 포함), 체력, 유전정보와 
   진료과정에서 생성되는 정보 및 기타 환자와 관련된 정보
 - 개인정보보호법상의 개인정보는 성명, 주민번호, 영상 등을 통하여 개인을 알아볼 
   수 있는 정보를 말하며, 다만 해당 정보만으로는 특정 개인을 알아볼 수 없더라도 
   다른 정보와 쉽게 결합하여 알아볼 수 있는 것도 개인정보에 포함  
- 개인정보보호 규정 위반시 원내 개인정보보호지침에 따라 징계 등 조치가 취해짐
  
▸ 부적절 열람이란?
 - 진료, 업무용 이외에 열람한 경우
 - EMR 권한을 오남용한 경우
 - 지인의 부탁으로 환자 상태를 확인해주는 경우 (외부 유출에 해당될 수 있음)
 - 동료 교직원이 입원한 경우 상태 확인을 위해 검색하는 경우
 - 가족의 진료기록을 검색하는 경우
 - 본인 진료기록을 본인이 확인하기 위해 검색하는 경우
  : 부적절 열람 모니터링 후 원내 규정에 의한 징계 절차에 따라 조치가 취해지며 
   외부 유출의 경우에는 법적인 조치가 취해질 수 있음 
▸ 개인정보보호 준수
 - 계정 공유 금지
 - 환자 정보를 타인에게 누설 금지
 - 진료기록, 환자 정보 등 불법 공유 금지
 - 자리를 비울 때 반드시 컴퓨터 로그아웃
 - 개인정보가 담긴 문서는 파쇄하여 처리 
○ 환자 확인
▸ 환자참여
 - 환자가 의사소통이 가능한 경우 개방형 질문으로 확인

1) 과학지식 이해와 임상적용
2) 진료 능력
3) 자기주도학습 및 비판 능력

7) 리더십

1) 건강상태를 유지하는 정상 구조와 기전을 설명：정상 상재균과 체온 조절 기전
2) 건강문제의 병태생리학적 원리 설명：전신염증성반응증후군과 패혈증의 기전
3) 주요 질환에 대한 임상 추론 수립
l 폐렴, 요로감염, 피부 및 연조직 감염, 위장관 감염, 카테터 관련 혈류감염
l 각 기관별 증상 파악, 문진 및 이학적 검사 수행, 필요한 검사 시행 및 결과해석, 치료 계
획 수립
l 임상 상황에 맞는 적절한 항생제 처방
4) 임상 술기 시행
l 손씻기, 말초 혈액 배양 검사(모형 활용), 척추 천자, 창상드레싱, 흉수 천자, 도뇨관 삽입, 
동의서 받기, 산소 공급(기관 삽관 등), 경비위관 삽입, 중심 정맥관 삽입, 동맥관 삽입, 
환자 상태 보고, 환자 및 보호자 면담
5) 의학적 견해를 동료에게 설명 및 논의
l 아침 브리핑
l 증례 및 저널 발표
l 동료 및 선후배 의사들과 효과적으로 의사 소통
l 정보 검색 및 적절한 활용

3. 과 소개
l 감염내과는 미생물에 의한 감염성 질환과 원인이 불분명한 발열 질환을 다루며, 병원 내에서
는 외래환자와 입원환자의 진료, 타과 환자의 협진, 원내 감염관리 등을 담당한다. 실습학생
은 감염내과 교수의 지도감독 하에 입원환자와 협진 의뢰된 환자를 공부한다. 입원환자에 대
한 학습은 직접 환자 2명 이상을 담당하여 발표하며, 협진 의뢰된 환자를 preview한 후에 
컨설트 회진 중 진단 접근 방법과 치료 방식에 대해 토의한다.

1) 발열(불명열) 환자의 접근 방법

3) 감염 질환에서의 항생제 사용법 및 흔한 부작용
4) 균 동정법에 대한 이해 및 실제 수행
