POLI395 African Politics 
Spring 2026 
Korea University 
Instructor: Kangwook Han 
Class: Tuesdays and Thursdays 12:00-13:15 
Office: Sangnam PoliSci & Econ 517 
Email: kangwook@korea.ac.kr 
Office hours: by email appointment 
Course Description 
We often justify our ignorance of the African continent by regarding it as the unexplored or 
unknown continent. This lack of understanding leads us to perceive African citizens solely as 
victims of underdevelopment and political violence or as passive recipients of aid from developed 
countries. In this course, we will explore the history of African citizens' struggles for democracy 
and their efforts toward development. Through this, we aim to deepen our understanding of Africa 
and actively consider our role in supporting its development. 
Course Objectives 
By the end of this course, students will be able to: 
•
Gain a foundational understanding of key historical and contemporary political 
developments in Africa. 
•
Explore how colonial legacies have shaped states and societies in Africa. 
•
Examine the role of ethnic politics, land conflicts, and economic factors in governance. 
•
Understand how democracy, elections, and political parties influence governance in 
Africa. 
•
Engage with major discussions in African politics and apply basic theoretical concepts to 
real-world cases. 
Reading and Materials 
Students are not required to purchase or read specific textbooks or academic papers before class. All 
learning materials, including core readings and supplementary documents used during the session, 
will be uploaded to the LMS after each class.  
•
Full lecture slides will be shared with students a day before each class.  
•
For each week’s topic, NotebookLM links will be provided. These AI-powered study guides 
will include synthesized summaries and interactive query capabilities to assist in your self-
paced review and deep learning. 
/1 11
Course Requirements 
1. Class Attendance and Participation (10%) 
All students are required to attend class regularly and actively engage in discussions. Students are 
allowed up to two unexcused absences without prior notice. 
2. Map Quiz (10%) 
To develop a foundational geographic understanding of the continent, a map quiz will be 
administered. This quiz ensures that students can accurately identify key political boundaries. 
Establishing this foundational geographic knowledge is essential for the subsequent examination of 
regional developments and colonial legacies within the course. 
• The map quiz will be held during the first session of Week 3. To ensure a smooth transition from 
the lecture, the assessment will begin exactly 10 minutes before the end of the class. 
• The quiz is designed to be mobile-friendly and will be administered through Google Forms for 
immediate automated grading. 
• Students must correctly identify the locations of ten (10) designated countries on a numbered 
blank map of Africa. 
• A Dropdown (Multiple Choice) menu will be used for each question to allow for easy navigation 
on small screens. 
• A direct URL link and a QR code will be displayed on the classroom screen at the start of the 
quiz. 
• Students are required to bring a laptop or smartphone to the classroom. 
3. African Culture Log (15%) 
Every student is required to submit a total of two (2) entries to the LMS Discussion board. To 
ensure a multi-dimensional understanding of the continent, the requirements are as follows:
• Requirement
• Music: One (1) YouTube link of an African artist with a rationale and imagery description.
• Cultural Item: One (1) photo/media of an African-related item, food, architecture, or 
anythings found in Korea with a brief description
• Group Structure & Sub-Group Division
• The class is divided into five (5) Relay Groups (Groups A–E), consisting of 15-20 students 
each. Within each group, students are further divided into two sub-groups:
• Sub-Group 1 (9 students): Assigned to post Music during the first rotation. 
• Sub-Group 2 (9 students): Assigned to post Cultural Items during the first rotation.
• Once the first rotation is complete (after Group E finishes), the sub-groups will swap their 
assigned topics for the second rotation.
• Extra Credit: While the schedule dictates mandatory posts, students are welcome to share 
additional discoveries or music at any time for extra credit.
• Engagement & Grading
• All entries must be posted on the designated LMS Discussion board during your group's 
assigned week.
/2 11
• Grading is based on the completion of both requirements according to the relay schedule.
• Class Choice: Outstanding music entries will be selected via bi-weekly voting and played 
during lectures.
4. Policy Brief for the Future (25%)  
The objective of this brief is to analyze a critical challenge facing the African continent and propose 
strategic policy solutions. Students are required to act as policy analysts, using AI as a sophisticated 
research partner.
• Due Date: May 1, 2026. 
• You must select one (1) specific African country as the focus of your analysis. 
• Topics (Select One): 
• AI and Digital Transformation  
• Industrialization  
• Climate Change  
• Food Security and Agricultural Productivity  
• Urbanization  
• Rapid Population Growth and the Youth Bulge 
• Requirements:  
• You must cite at least two (2) peer-reviewed academic articles relevant to your chosen topic. 
• Any use of "Fake Articles" (hallucinated citations generated by AI) will result in an 
immediate score of zero (0/F) for the entire assignment. Verification of sources is 
solely the student’s responsibility. 
• The main body of the brief must be a minimum of 5 pages (A4, 12pt, single-spaced). There 
is no upper limit. 
• The final policy brief must be submitted entirely in English. 
• AI Usage and Language Policy 
• This assignment assumes that all students will use AI tools. You must specify the exact 
tool and version used (e.g., ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet).  
• You may interact with AI in English or Korean. If you use any other languages (e.g., French, 
Portuguese, Spanish), you must provide an English translation alongside the original logs. 
• However, the final submission files should be written in English. 
• Submission Files: You must submit two (2) separate PDF files:  
1. Final Policy Brief: Includes the main text and the mandatory Appendix about AI usage 
and critic.  
2. AI Interaction Log (Shared URL Link + Full-Text Transcript): A complete PDF of 
your prompt history and AI responses. 
A. Shared URL Link:  
•
Generate a "Share Link" from your AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, 
etc.).  
•
Ensure the link is set to 'Public' or 'Anyone with the link can view.'  
•
Student Responsibility: The link must remain active until the final grades 
are officially posted and the appeal period has ended. If the instructor 
cannot access the link, the "AI Interaction" portion of your grade may be 
forfeited (0 points). 
/3 11
B. Full-Text Transcript (Backup & Quick Review): Immediately below the URL, 
copy and paste the entire text of your conversation with the AI. This serves as a 
critical backup in case of link failure and allows the instructor to review your 
logic within the LMS viewer without opening external tabs. 
• Mandatory Appendix: AI Critique Section 
• This section is separate from the 5-page main body and is a crucial part of your evaluation. 
It must include: 
• Specify exactly where and how the AI was helpful (e.g., structuring, brainstorming, or 
refining prose). 
• Identify where the AI failed or provided generic, insufficient, or inaccurate suggestions 
regarding the specific political and social context of your chosen country. 
• Describe the specific actions you took to overcome these limitations (e.g., additional 
manual research, analyzing academic papers, or refined prompt engineering). 
5. Final Exam (40%)  
The final exam for this course is designed as an 8-hour Take-home Assessment. Beyond testing your 
knowledge of African politics, this exam evaluates your ability to navigate the complexities of AI-
human collaboration. In an era where AI can generate plausible but often superficial or inaccurate 
information, the core competency of a modern researcher lies in the ability to critically steer, verify, 
and refine AI-generated content. You are expected to demonstrate high-level analytical skills by 
treating AI not as an answering machine, but as a research partner that must be constantly 
challenged and contextualized through academic rigor.
• Logistics 
• 8-hour Take-home Exam. 
• Date & Time: June [TBD], 2026, 09:00 – 17:00. 
• The exam consists of 2 comprehensive questions covering theoretical and empirical themes 
from the semester. 
• Each question will require students to apply, compare, and critically evaluate academic 
frameworks discussed in class in relation to a specific African country or political scenario. 
(Answers based primarily on summary or definition will not receive high marks.) 
• Evaluation Principle: AI Use and Analytical Thinking 
• This exam does not evaluate whether you used AI. Rather, it evaluates your ability to 
critically assess, revise, contextualize, and improve AI-generated responses.  
• High marks will be determined not by prompt-writing technique itself, but by the quality of 
your theoretical understanding, analytical reasoning, judgment, and critical intervention. 
• The Interactive Refinement Methodology 
• Step 1. Obtain an AI Baseline Response (Before Entering Your Draft)  
• For each question, first ask AI to generate an initial response (baseline response) 
without inputting your own draft.  
• The purpose of this step is to secure an AI baseline that is not influenced by your own 
framing.  
• In your AI log, clearly label the baseline prompt so it can be identified easily (e.g., [Q1 
BASELINE], [Q2 BASELINE], [Q3 BASELINE]). 
• Step 2. Write Your Draft Offline (Required Submission) 
• For each question, you must write a draft outside the AI chat window (e.g., Word, 
HWP, notes app, handwritten notes). 
/4 11
• Your draft must include at least:  
• a tentative thesis (1–2 sentences),  
• 2–3 theories/readings you plan to use,  
• uncertainty, limitation, or expected counterargument 
• Important: 
• This draft is a provisional analytical plan and may be revised later.  
• The draft must be submitted at the end of the exam. 
• Step 3. Human Critique First (Critical Review Before AI Refinement) 
• Before entering your draft into AI (or using AI for refinement), you must first 
independently and critically evaluate the limitations of the AI baseline response. 
• Examples of critique points include: 
• overgeneralization, missing regional/historical context, weak empirical fit, 
theoretical misunderstanding or superficial comparison across theories, omission 
of counterexamples or scope conditions. 
• The purpose of this step is not simply to “improve” the AI response, but to ensure that 
you first identify what is wrong and why. 
• Step 4. Begin AI Refinement (with Time Marker) 
• Only after completing Step 3 may you begin AI refinement using your draft and 
critique points. 
• At the beginning of your first refinement prompt, ask the AI to print the current 
date and time first.  
• In your AI log, clearly label the refinement-start prompt (e.g., [Q1 REFINEMENT 
START], [Q2 REFINEMENT START], [Q3 REFINEMENT START]).  
• Note: This time output is not a strict time-authentication device. It is a time marker to 
document the point at which you began AI refinement after completing your 
independent critical review. 
• During refinement, you are expected to provide substantive inputs such as:  
• course theories and concepts, specific empirical context, counterarguments and 
alternative theses, corrective logic, scope conditions and/or possible 
counterexamples. 
• Step 5. Write the Final Answer in English 
• Your final answer must reflect your own analytical judgment and must not consist of a 
simple copy-and-paste of AI-generated text. 
• Note on Draft Writing and the Risk of “Contamination” 
• If you use AI while writing your draft, or directly input your draft into AI too early, your 
subsequent analysis may become contaminated by AI framing. 
• For example: 
• your draft itself may already be shaped by AI framing,  
• later AI responses may become anchored to that framing,  
• your “critical review” may become a minor revision of AI logic rather than an 
independent judgment. 
• For this reason, students are strongly encouraged to write their draft outside the AI chat 
window and independently. In high-scoring answers, students’ own problem framing and 
judgment are usually visible at this stage. 
• Nature of the Draft (Your Outline Written in Step 2) 
• The draft is not a contract; it is a provisional analytical plan.  
• Changing your thesis during the exam is not a reason for penalty.  
/5 11
• In fact, it may be desirable to revise your argument after evaluating the AI baseline, 
counterarguments, and additional evidence.  
• The key criterion is not whether your final answer matches your draft, but the quality of 
your revisions and the justification for them.  
• The instructor may review your draft, AI log, and final answer together to assess your 
independent judgment and critical intervention. 
• Academic Standards and Integrity 
• You must cite at least two (2) peer-reviewed academic articles per question, which are 
covered in our class. 
• The use of "Fake Articles" (citations invented by AI) is strictly prohibited. If any 
fabricated sources are detected, you will receive an automatic score of zero (0/F) for the 
entire exam. Always verify every source. 
• You may interact with AI in English, Korean, or even your native language. However, the 
final submission files should be written in English. 
• Submission Requirements  
• Submit three (3) separate PDF files via LMS by 17:00:  
1. Draft (Your Outline): Your pre-analysis plan (Output from Step 2) 
2. Final English Answers: Your synthesized responses to the questions.  
3. AI Interaction Log (Shared URL Link + Full-Text Transcript): The complete history 
of your prompts and AI responses, documenting the evolution of your final answer. 
• Required AI Reflection (for Each Question) 
• In your final answer, include a short reflection (approximately 5–8 sentences per question) 
addressing the following:  
1. What was the most superficial or misleading part of the AI baseline response?  
2. Why was it inadequate for this question?  
3. What did you replace it with, and on what basis (theory/case evidence)?  
4. Did your tentative thesis change? If yes, why? If no, what was strengthened? 
Grading Policy 
All grading in this course will be conducted under the assumption that students used AI. However, 
the purpose of evaluation is not to reward AI tool usage itself, but to assess students’ understanding 
and analytical reasoning through their ability to critically evaluate, revise, and contextualize AI-

개설학기

금요일 1,2 교시 (오전 9:00-11:45) 
*연강이므로 중간에 20분의 휴식 시간을 가질 
예정임. 
강의실 
문과대학 서관 307호 
1. 강의 개요 
The study of law must be informed by an examination of the socio-cultural narratives that shape legal meaning and 
empower legal norms; conversely, the study of culture requires an understanding of the law as a normative edifice and 
coercive system. 
-Guido Calabresi (Sterling Professor Emeritus and former Dean of Yale Law School) 
본 강의는 법과 문학의 접점을 탐구하며, 두 분야가 서로를 어떻게 비추고 형성하는지 살펴본다. 법은 단순한 규범과 제 
도의 집합체가 아니라, 사회와 문화를 형성하고 재구성하는 강력한 서사적 도구이다. 한편, 문학은 법의 작용을 재현하 
고 비판하며, 법이 정의를 실현하려는 방식과 그 한계를 조명한다. 
학생들은 영미 고전 문학부터 현대 대중 문학, 법학 이론과 판례까지 폭넓은 텍스트를 통해 법과 문학이 교차하는 지점 
을 탐색하게 된다. 이 과정에서 법률 문서(판결문, 변론서, 계약서 등)의 서사적, 언어적 구조와 해석의 틀을 분석하는 
한편, 문학 작품 속에서 법과 법률가가 어떻게 그려져 왔는지 살펴본다. 강의는 법학적 분석력과 문학적 감수성을 함께 
키울 수 있도록 구성될 것이며, 강사의 학문적·실무적 경험을 바탕으로 영미법 체계 일반, 미국 법원과 대형 로펌, 로스 
쿨 교육, 법조 실무 등 현실적인 주제도 함께 다룬다. 
이 강의의 궁극적인 목적은 학생들이 다양한 법과 문학 텍스트를 병렬적으로 읽음으로써 비판적 사고력과 해석력을 기 
르며, 법과 문학을 넘나드는 융합적 사고를 훈련하도록 돕는 것이다. 법적 규율의 냉철함과 구속력 및 문학이 제공하는 
위로와 상상력 사이 여러 지점을 찾아가며 끊임없이 질문하고, 재해석하고, 대안을 모색하는 태도를 배우고 그 과정에서 
재미와 즐거움도 느낄 수 있도록 이끌고자 한다. 이 강의로 말미암아 학생들이 법과 문학이라는 두 가지 렌즈를 통해 
우리 삶과 사회를 보다 깊이있고 균형있게 바라보며 이해할 수 있는 한 걸음을 내딛을 수 있길 바란다. 
2. 강의 진행 방식 
1. 강사 주도식 렉처 수업 
• 
파워포인트 슬라이드를 이용하여 강의하며, 해당 자료는 추후 학생들에게 제공됨. 더하여 강의 취지에 맞는 
영상물을 간간이 감상한다. 
• 
질문은 강의 직후, 총 20분의 휴식 시간 중, 또는 언제든 이메일을 통해 가능함. 
2. 정규 수업시간 중 Guest Lecture 1회 (Tentative) 
• 
법과 인문학, 법과 예술의 교차점 또는 실무에서의 ‘스토리텔링’의 중요성에 대하여 생생하고 현실적인 이야기를 
들려줄 수 있는 강연자를 초청. 
3. 강독 자료 
정해진 교과서는 없으며, 자료는 강사가 선정하여 복사물로 직접 배포하거나 블랙보드를 통해 제공한다. 다양한 관점에 
서 법과 문학의 관계를 탐구한다는 취지 아래 법 텍스트와 문학 텍스트를 고르게 병행하여 읽는다. 
문학 텍스트는 영국·미국 문학 작품을 중심으로 다루며, ‘법과 문학’ 연구에서 필수적으로 언급되는 정전(canon)부터 법 
정 스릴러, 추리소설 등 대중문학까지 폭넓게 포함한다. 법 텍스트는 역사적으로 중요한 ‘landmark case’로 꼽히거나 시 
사성이 있는 미국 연방대법원 판례, 로리뷰·로저널에 게재된 학술 논문, 미국 로스쿨 교과서(casebook)에서 발췌한 내 
용, 중요 재판 기록, 그리고 비교법적 차원에서 선정한 국내법 자료 등을 포함하여 다각도로 살펴본다. 
본 강의는 깊이만큼 폭도 중요하게 여긴다. 따라서 대부분의 텍스트는 강사가 학생들에게 가장 필요하다고 판단한 부분 
을 선별하여 발췌독함으로써 풍부한 읽을거리를 수월하게 접할 수 있도록 한다. 추가적으로 통독이 바람직한 텍스트에 
대해서는 제목과 저자명을 제공하고 개별적인 읽기를 권장할 것이지만, 시험 범위에는 포함되지 않는다. 
4. 강의 내용 
강의는 다음과 같은 주제를 중심으로 진행된다. 각 주제의 내용과 순서는 수업의 흐름에 따라 변경될 수 있다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

DISS 310: East Asian Economies 
Spring 2026 
 
Innwon Park 
Professor Emeritus 
College of International Studies 
Korea University 
Homepage: https://faculty.korea.ac.kr/kufaculty/iwpark/index.do 
 
 
This course offers a comprehensive analysis of East Asia's economic development, focusing 
on 10 Southeast Asian nations (10 ASEAN member countries: Brunei Darussalam, 
Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, 
and Vietnam excluding recently joined Timor-Leste) and 6 Northeast Asian nations (China, 
Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, and Taiwan). Students will examine these countries' 
economic features, pressing issues, and regional and global economic connections. By 
integrating theoretical frameworks with practical case studies, the course aims to provide a 
thorough understanding of the factors driving East Asia's economic transformation. 
 
This course covers the following topics: 
 
• 
Conceptualizing the measures and dimensions of economic well-being and development. 
• 
Analyzing the economic development models and evolutionary processes of East Asian 
economies. 
• 
Comparing the contemporary economic status and performance of nations within the 
region. 
• 
Classifying regional economies by identifying structural similarities and divergent 
characteristics. 
• 
Investigating the multifaceted contemporary economic challenges facing East Asia. 
• 
Evaluating intra-regional and extra-regional economic linkages and their broader 
strategic implications. 
 
CLASSROOM ACTIVITIES 
 
1. Lectures 
2. A Mid-term Quiz 
3. Group Presentations 
4. A closed-book in-class Final Examination 
 
A required textbook is not assigned. Instead, all necessary lecture PDFs will be accessible 
on the LMS (https://lms.korea.ac.kr/) in advance. Students are encouraged to engage 
thoroughly with these digital resources as their primary study material. 
 
LECTURE HOURS AND VENUE 
 
 
Date and Time: 3:00~4:15 pm on Mondays and Wednesdays 
 
Venue: Room 114, International Studies Hall 
 
For inquiries, iwpark@korea.ac.kr 
 
No class on Monday, May 25 (Buddha’s Birthday) and Wednesday, June 3 (National 
Simultaneous Local Election Day). 
 
Regular class during the Mid-term and Final examination period 
 
2 
 
GRADING 
 
1. Participation (10%): Attendance and Discussion 
2. Mid-term Quiz (25%): 3:00~4:15 pm on Monday, April 27 
3. Group Presentation (25%): A Country Profile (May 27 ~ June 17) 
4. Final Examination (40%): 3:00~4:15 pm on Monday, June 22 
 
Country Profile Presentation Guidelines 
1. A group of 4 students will deliver a 25-minute presentation, including a Q&A session 
lasting up to 5 minutes. 
2. Group formation and country selection for presentations will be conducted via the 
provided Google Sheets link (TBA). 
3. Grouping, country assignments, and the presentation order will be finalized during class 
on Wednesday, March 25.  
4. The group representative must submit their presentation file (PPT or PDF) via email by 
midnight on Friday, May 22. The file should include Student names, Title (clearly 
identify the country), Table of contents, Main text (with tables and figures), and 
References. Once submitted, the presentation file cannot be revised, ensuring fairness 
regardless of the presentation order.  
5. The presentation should address the following: (1) Socio-Economic Systems and 
Policies (40%): Provide an overview of the country's socio-economic systems and 
policies during its economic development process, including its current economic status. 
(2) Key Economic Issues (60%): Discuss 2 or 3 major economic challenges the country 
is currently facing and propose relevant policies to address these challenges, with a focus 
on sustainable economic development. Support your analysis with a literature review and 
accurate statistical data. 
6. Evaluation Criteria: Group performance will be assessed based on (1) Content: Depth of 
research and quality of information; (2) Delivery: Presentation clarity and editorial effort; 
and (3)Time Management: Adherence to the allotted time. 
7. Participation Requirement: All group members are strongly encouraged to contribute 
equally as speakers during the presentation.

이건희 
 
강의 개요 
- 본 강의는 일반화학에서 학습한 이론적 개념을 실험을 통해 직접 검증하고, 화학적 현상을 
정량적으로 측정하는 능력을 배양하는 과정이다. 물질의 양적 관계(몰, 화학식)에서부터 
열역학, 화학 평형, 전자기 복사, 물질의 상태와 분자 간 인력에 이르기까지 화학의 핵심 
영역을 실험적으로 탐구한다. 실험 기구의 올바른 사용법과 데이터 분석 능력을 함양하여 
과학적 사고와 문제 해결 능력을 갖춘 기초 과학 인력을 양성하고자 한다. 
 
기존 개설대비 변경 사항 
- 특별한 변경 사항은 없음. 
 
수강 대상 
- 생명과학대학의 1학년 재학생 
 
수업 목표 
- 정량적 분석 능력 배양: 몰수, 아보가드로 수, 화학식 결정 실험을 통해 물질의 양적 관계
를 이해하고 정확하게 계산한다. 
- 화학 평형 및 반응 원리 습득: 약산의 이온화 상수 측정과 산화-환원 적정을 통해 평형 상
수와 당량점의 개념을 실험적으로 규명한다. 
<잠정 최종> 2026.01.15 
2 
 
- 물질의 물리적 성질 이해: 기체의 특성, 증발과 분자 간 인력 실험을 통해 거시적 성질과 
미시적 상호작용의 상관관계를 파악한다. 
- 측정 및 분석 기술 숙달: pH 측정기, 스펙트럼 측정 장치, 전도도 측정기 등 다양한 분석 
기기의 원리를 익히고 정밀한 데이터를 도출한다. 
- 열역학 및 구조 분석: 반응열 측정을 통해 에너지 변화를 관찰하고, 원자 방출 스펙트럼을 
통해 원자 구조의 양자화된 특성을 이해한다.

과제 
▪ 실험리포트를 제출해야 함. 
▪ 타인의 것을 베끼거나, AI의 작성한 것을 그대로 베끼는 것은, 불이익이 있습니다.  
 
장애 학생 
▪ 장애가 있는 학생은 담당 교원에게 필요한 사항을 꼭 사전 통지 바랍니다. 기술적 문제
가 없는 한 최대한 반영하도록 하겠습니다. 
▪ 본 강의를 수강하는 개개인의 특성과 요구에 따라, 지도교수 및 장애학생지원센터와의 
상담을 통하여 적절한 수준의 지원 서비스를 제공합니다. 장애학생에 대한 지원서비스
와 관련하여 문의사항이 있는 학생들은 장애학생지원센터(02-3290-1534)로 문의바랍
니다. 
 
수업운영 원칙 
▪  별도로 기술되어 있지 않더라도, 모든 것은 학칙에 의거합니다. 
▪  교원과 학생은 상호 존중하고 온라인/오프라인에서 모두 예의를 갖춥니다(이메일 포함) 
▪  [보강] 교원 및 조교의 불가피한 사유로 인해, 수업이 불가능할 경우 LMS를 통해 공지

하고 별도의 보강을 진행함. 보강일에 수업 참여하지 않아도 결석으로 처리함.  
▪  [출석] 총 수업일(시험 포함) 가운데, ‘3분의 1’ 이상을 결석한 학생에 대해서는 성적을 
부여하지 아니함. 예외 없음.  
- ‘결석하였지만, 출석으로 인정’(=출석 인정)하는 사유: 출석 인정 지침을 참고. 
- ‘출석 인정’ 신청은 사전 신청을 원칙으로 하나, 부득이한 사유로 사전 신청을 하지 못
한 학생은 해당 사유가 종료된 후 10일 이내에 증빙서류를 첨부하여 신청하여야 함. 
다만, 신청 가능 시기는 종강일 이전으로 한정함. 이메일로 문의한 것은 인정하지 않
음. 반드시 교내 포털시스템의 ‘출석인정신청(유고결석인정)’을 통해 신청할 것. 원칙
은 이러하나, 증빙서류가 있으면 늦게 올려도 인정 가능. 
- 수강신청 정정기간에 수강신청을 하지 못해서 결석한 경우도, 결석으로 처리함.  
- 질병결석의 ‘출석 인정’: 단순 질병의 경우, 결석한 당일에 병원 방문한 것만 인정함. 
병원 방문 없이 ‘출석 인정’을 받기 위해서는, 의사의 진단서를 제출할 것.  
- ‘출석 인정’을 하는 경우에도 실제 출석일수(실제로 강의를 수강한 횟수 또는 일수)가 
총 수업일수의 ‘2분의 1’ 이상인 학생에게만 성적을 부여함. 
- 출석 여부를 결정하는 기준은 ‘출석부’이며, 학생 본인이 본인의 출석을 철저하게 관리 
바람.  
- “졸업 직전학기”에, 취업을 이유로 ‘출석 인정’을 받는 학생은, 건강보험자격득실확인서
를 반드시 제출할 것. 정식 근로계약에 의거하여 취업한 것에 한정하고, 해당 수업 시
간에 반드시 근무를 하는 직장에 한해서 인정 가능함. 아르바이트나, 프리랜서 등과 
같이 시간이 조정한 것은 ‘출석 인정’이 불가함.

진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중
히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술
∙ [실험실습 안전]
 -연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분
야 대상 학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습
을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수

 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

4단계 교수학습 과정에 따라 전개되며, 총 6개의 공통 동영상 주제에 대

평가방법설명
중간고사와 기말고사는 대면 필기시험을 실시한다.
출석관련 규정
수업일수 1/3을 초과하여 결석하는 경우 성적을 부여할 수 없음, 단 
담당교수가 불가피한 결석으로 인정하는 경우에는 예외적용 가능
개요
 본 강의는 동아시아세계 ‘고대문명’의 역사를 살펴보면서, ‘중국고대
사’라는 영역을 넘어서 동아시아사의 이른바 ‘고대’를 이해하고자 한
다. 우선 선사시대부터 초기문명에 해당하는 상․주 왕조와 다른 초기
문명들, 춘추전국시대의 여러 변화, 고대제국질서가 형성되고 전개되
는 진․한 제국의 ‘황제제도’까지 시간 순으로 그 역사적 전개과정을 
정리한다.
 이를 통해 동아시아의 다원적 초기문명의 탄생과 발전, ‘철학적 돌
파’로서 제자백가, 초기문명에서 제국질서로의 변화, 고대제국의 황제
제도, 고대 동아시아세계의 원형적 국제질서 형성 등 주요한 내용을 
이해한다. 아울러 간독자료 등 신 출토자료를 중심으로 근래 고대사
의 새로운 연구경향과 성과에 대해서도 살펴본다.
수강(권장)대상 
학생
중국 고대사의 전개 과정에 대해 관심이 있거나 이해하고 싶은 학생
들에게 수강을 권장한다.
선이수과목(권장)
선이수과목은 특별히 없다. 배우고자 하는 열의만 있으면 된다.
수업운영원칙
본 강의는 중간․기말 고사를 제외한 전체 28개 강의이며, 매 강의는 
75분간의 대면 이론 수업으로 구성된다. 수강생들은 수업을 전후하
여 자유로운 질의응답을 할 수 있다.
기존개설대비
변경,개선사항
일부 강의안의 분량을 강의 시간에 맞게 조절했으며, 수강생들의 이
해를 돕기 위해 강의안 내에 지도․사진 등의 참고 자료를 보강하였
다.
수업목표 일반
동아시아 고대 문명을 조망하고 동아시아(중국) 고대의 사회상을 파
악하여, 이를 기반으로 동아시아(중국) 고대사의 역사상에 대해 이
해하고 해석하는 역량을 기른다.
세부목표 1
동아시아 고대 문명의 탄생과 발전, 변화의 전반적인 과정을 이해한
다.
세부목표 2
중국의 황제 지배 체제의 탄생과 확립, 그리고 유학이 통치 이념으
로 발전하는 과정을 이해한다.
세부목표 3
간독 등 출토자료와 중국 고대 제국의 법률과 문서행정에 대한 초
보적인 이해를 도모한다.

TA: TBA 
 
Course Objectives  
In a complex and rapidly-changing environment, social networks – an actor's relationships 
with other people or organizations – become more important in creating and delivering 
value under various kinds of uncertainties. Moreover, the rise of digital transformation and 
social networking tools has fundamentally changed how we build and maintain 
relationships. While many actors – firms as well as individuals – are eager to build "more 
networks" with other actors, many still do not clearly understand how networks affect their 
performance and outcomes. The effect of social networks on individual and organizational 
achievement is the key issue of this course. 
This course consists of three objectives. First, the course introduces the theory of social 
networks and social capital and provides students with insights into how social networks 
may affect individual outcomes. Understanding the role of social capital in the development 
of human capital has been a major field of study. Thus, by taking this course, students are 
expected to become more competent as creative and productive managers who can 
effectively build and utilize their networks. 
Second, the course introduces cutting-edge strategic management theories related to inter-
organizational relations. At the organizational level, it is becoming increasingly important for 
firms to build social relationships with various actors in society (e.g., governments, non-
profit organizations, platform ecosystems). By studying organizational theories and strategic 
management theories related to social networks and relationships, this course helps 
students explore various strategic alternatives beyond conventional approaches (such as 
building internal capabilities or competing through market mechanisms) to create 
sustainable competitive advantage. 
Finally, the course introduces social network analysis tools and methodologies for students 
to apply course learning to analyze both individual and inter-organizational networks. 
Through hands-on experience with Netminer, students will learn to collect, visualize, and 
analyze network data. This practical component enables students to bridge theory and 
practice, preparing them to leverage network analysis in their future careers. The course 
particularly emphasizes contemporary issues such as digital transformation, AI/big data 
applications in network analysis, platform/ecosystem strategies, and the role of networks in 
driving social change.

There are 4 essentials: Class participation, assignments, exam, and peer review.

Class participation - Individual (30%) 
For the success of our class, students are expected to actively participate in class discussion. 
I will ask you to fill out a seating chart at the beginning of each class and I will grade your 
class participation score based on the seating chart. Please note that you can take a seat 
wherever you want, but it is your responsibility to correctly specify your position in each 
session. In every session, please place your name tag in front of you so that I may easily 
recognize your contribution. If you do not place your name tag, your participation may not 
be correctly recorded.  
 
Class participation score will account for the quality of your comments/questions. Simple 
questions regarding the course logistics will not be counted as class participation. The best 
score will be given if your comments are constructive and creative. Note that the purpose of 
in-class discussion is to help one another's understanding rather than to criticize your 
friend's work. Sharing your valuable experience is also a big plus for your participation score. 
 
For each session, I will use a 30-point scale to grade your class participation score. If you 
attend the focal session, you will automatically get 10 points (0 otherwise). Based on your 
contribution, I will add some points up to 30, while based on your attitude, I may deduct 
some points down to 0. For your final grade, I will compute the average class participation 
score, excluding the case(s) of "legitimate absence." Your absence is legitimate only if you 
can ask for permission in advance through the KU Portal. Job-related matters may not be 
the cause of "legitimate absence," so please make sure to consult with me in advance. 
 
Your attendance in the first two sessions will be able to make up your absence later in the 
semester. 
 
Here is the detail on class participation score for each session: 
⚫ No point is to be assigned (blank) if your absence had a legitimate reason (e.g. 
reserved army training) – thus, this will not be included when I compute the average 
class participation score for the final grade 
⚫ 0 if you do not attend the focal session 
⚫ 18 if you attend the focal session 
⚫ +2 if you participated in class discussion 
⚫ +7 if the level of your participation was "good" 
⚫ +12 if the level of your participation was "great/excellent" 
⚫ -3 to -15 if you arrived late or left early in a focal class, or bother other students 
 
COLD CALL: To facilitate better engagement, I will sometimes call on anybody in class no 
matter whether she or he raises her/his hand. 
 
From time to time, students will be asked to form a small-sized group and have a breakout 
session in a relatively short period of time (e.g., 5-10 minutes). After the breakouts, students 
sometimes will be asked to submit a breakout note, which will be graded as a part of class 
participation. 
 
Assignments (30%) 
Students will receive two assignments. Each assignment is designed to build a student's 
capability to apply social network analysis. The hourly lateness penalty of one-point 
deduction will be applied. 
 
First Assignment (Individual, 10%): Ego-network analysis 
 
Second Assignment (20%): Social Network Analysis on Intra-organizational Network 
◼ Can be done individually or in groups of up to 3 people 
◼ Selected assignments will be presented in class (6/4) 
 
Mid-term Exam (20%) 
The mid-term exam will cover all the materials up to that point, including all the assigned 
readings. 
 
Peer Review of Second Assignments (20%) 
After the presentation and sharing of Second Assignments, students will conduct peer 
reviews of other teams' work. This can be done either individually or collaboratively: 
 
Individual review: Each student reviews 2-3 assigned projects 
 
Collaborative review: A group of 2-3 students works together to review 2-3 assigned 
projects 
 
The review should include: 
 
Critical analysis of the methodology used 
 
Evaluation of the findings and implications 
 
Constructive suggestions for improvement 
 
Potential applications and extensions of the work 
 
Specific peer review guidelines and evaluation criteria will be provided. The peer review 
exercise aims not only to assess other teams' work but also to develop critical thinking and 
analytical skills in network analysis.

Line and Drawing, 2026 Spring Semester 
Instructor: Dr. Zune Lee 
 
 
 
ARDE286: Line and Drawing (선묘와 드로잉) 
Tues(4-6)  Media Hall 701 
Instructor: Dr. Zune Lee, School of Art and Design 
zune@korea.ac.kr | courseemail@gmail.com 
 
※ Note: This syllabus is subject to change at the beginning of the semester to accommodate 
student levels.  
 
1. Introduction 
In this course, the student will understand the fundamentals of line drawing and sketching, 
which form the basis and foundation of artwork creation, and practice using various materials 
and techniques. This course focuses on personal creation and practice, highly valuing 
initiative, experimentation, and a challenging spirit in both artwork creation and class 
participation. 
※ Note: This course will be taught using three teaching types: lecture+lab, lab, and individual 
or group meetings. 
※ Note: This class uses laptops; therefore, students should bring their laptops to class. 
 
2. Purposes 
By experiencing various drawing materials and techniques, including dry and wet media, 
Students aim to select materials that suit their sensibilities and create a complete, 
drawing-based artwork. 
◦ To understand the concept and application of drawing. 
◦ Master diverse drawing techniques using dry and wet media. 
◦ Produce free artwork using your own unique sensibility and emotional expression. 
◦ To cultivate creative minds and abilities to create various drawings from the contemporary 
arts’ perspectives.

Zero Energy Community System 
 
 
Course Information 
Lecture Time: 1:30 – 2:45 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays 
Lecture Location: Classroom B106, New Engineering Building 
 
Instructor: Prof. Yeonsook Heo  
Office: Room 316, Engineering Building 
Email: yeonsookheo@korea.ac.kr 
Phone: 02-3290-4867 
 
Teaching Assistant: TBD 
 
 
Required Textbook 
Mitchell, J. W., & Braun, J. E. (2012). Principles of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning 
in buildings. John Wiley & Sons. 
N. Lechner (2014). Heating, Cooling, Lighting: Sustainable Design Methods for Architects, 
4th Ed., John Wiley & Sons 
 
 
 
Overview and Objectives 
This course provides a fundamental engineering foundation for the design and operation of 
mechanical and renewable energy systems in zero-energy communities. It introduces the 
operating principles and key performance characteristics of major HVAC and renewable 
technologies, enabling students to develop integrated system solutions for achieving zero-
energy buildings. The major objectives of this course are for students to: 
o 
Build core HVAC engineering fundamentals needed for zero-energy building 
design 
o 
Analyze and design major cooling/heating cycles and technologies, with an 
emphasis on efficiency and operating principles. 
o 
Develop energy-supply solutions using renewable energy systems, applying solar, 
wind, hydrogen, and distributed energy concepts for zero-energy communities. 
 
 
 
Course Requirements and Grading Policy 
Students will be evaluated on the basis of homework assignments and exams: 
i. 
Project: 30% (report & presentation) 
ii. 
Mid-term Exam: 35% 
iii. 
Final Exam: 35% 
Submissions: There will be one individual assignment and one group project (3-5 students 
per group). They should be turned in at the beginning of class on the due day. If turned in 
between the beginning and the end of class, they will be docked 10%. If turned in later that 
same due day, they will be docked 50%. No submissions will be accepted after the due day 
unless you have prior approval from me (strict rule without any exception).

HOKA 002: THE KOREAN WAR 
SPRING 2026 
Mon/Weds, 10:30-11:45 
Education Hall (교육관) Room 308 
 
Instructor: Thomas Ryan 
Assistant Professor 
Department of Korean History 
122 West Hall 
thomasryan@korea.ac.kr 
OfSice hours: MW, 1:30-3:00 
 
1. Course Description 
 
This course provides a selective historical overview of the Korean War, known popularly in 
South Korea as the 6.25 War and in North Korea as the Fatherland Liberation War. While 
the war between North and South Korea remains technically ongoing today, these labels all 
designate the period of outright hostilities from 1950-1953, during which upwards of four 
million people, most of them civilians, lost their lives.  
 
The Sirst three weeks of this course offer a conventional account of the most critical period 
of the war, from June 1950 to the summer of 1951, when peace negotiations started and the 
conSlict effectively became a stalemate (despite staggeringly high casualties from 1951-53). 
From week 4 onwards, the course shifts to thematic modules that will both introduce new 
concepts and reconsolidate our knowledge of the historical events covered in the Sirst three 
weeks. In these thematic weeks we will typically read one secondary source (a scholarly 
article or book chapter) and one primary source, often Korean-language short Siction 
translated into English. There will also be four in-class Silm screenings over the course of 
the semester.  
 
ReSlecting the legal continuation of civil war in Korea even after 1953, in the form of 
militarized national division, thematic modules will such on such wartime and postwar 
subjects as: Cold War humanitarianism and Orientalism, communism and anticommunism, 
refugees and exiles, repatriation and migration, military bases and sex work, dead bodies 
and unexploded mines, family separation and reunion, movements for truth and 
reconciliation, and the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) itself. 
 
2. Course Materials 
 
All course readings will be uploaded as PDF documents to LMS. The list of readings and 
Silms is as follows:  
 
Readings: 
 
* Wada Haruki, The Korean War: An International History (Rowman & LittleSield, 2018). 
 
2 
* Daniel Kim, The Intimacies of Con8lict: Cultural Memory and the Korean War (NYU Press, 
2020), 31-52. 
* Bruce Cumings, The Korean War (Modern Library, 2010), 103-146. 
* Hwang Sunwŏn, “Pibari” (비바리, 1956) 
* Pak Wansŏ, “Epiphany,” in Who Ate Up All the Shinga? An Autobiographical Novel (그 많던 
싱아는 누가 다 먹었을, 1993): 210-248. 
* Sandra H. Park, “SalviSic Violence: The Hungnam Evacuation and Anticommunist Rescue in 
US-Occupied North Korea,” Korea Journal 65, no. 2 (2025): 11–47. 
* Sahr Conway-Lanz, “Beyond No Gun Ri: Refugees and the United States Military in the 
Korean War,” Diplomatic History 29.1 (January 2005): 49-81. 
* Sŏnu Hwi, “Thoughts of Home” (망향, 1965) 
* Monica Kim, “On the 38th Parallel: The Third Choice,” in The Interrogation Rooms of the 
Korean War: The Untold History (Princeton University Press, 2019): 259-302. 
* Tessa Morris-Suzuki, “A Dream Betrayed: Cold War Politics and the Repatriation of 
Koreans from Japan to North Korea,” Asian Studies Review 29.4 (2005): 357-381. 
* Katharine Moon, Sex Among Allies: Military Prostitution in US-Korea Relations (New York: 
Columbia University Press, 1997), 17-37. 
* Ch’oe Inhun, “The End of the State Highway” (국도의 끝, 1959) 
* Kang Sŏkkyŏng, “Days and Dreams” (낮과 꿈, 1983) 
* Heonik Kwon, “Empty Old Graves of the Korean War Hill Fight,” Human Remains and 
Violence 10.1 (2024): 55-67 
* Sungman Koh (trans. Brendan Wright), “Trans-Border Rituals for the Dead: Experiential 
Knowledge of Paternal Relatives after the Jeju 4.3 Incident,” Journal of Korean Religions 9.1 
(2018): 71-103. 
* Ha Kŭnch’an, “Red Hill” (붉은 언덕, 1964) 
* Thomas Ryan, “Vagrant Optics: The Seosan Pioneer Corps and Cold War Visual Culture in 
South Korea,” Korea Journal 65.2 (2025): 74-108. 
* Bruce Cumings, “Introduction,” in Lee Jae-eui, Gwangju Diary: Beyond Death, Beyond the 
Darkness of the Age (May 18 Memorial Foundation, 2017), 17-35. 
* Yi Munyŏl (trans. Heinz Insu Fenkl with Yoosup Chang), Meeting with My Brother 
(아우와의 만남, Columbia University Press, 2017; originally published 2002). 
* Hwang Sok-yong (trans. Anton Hur and Sora Kim-Russell), “Visit to the North,” in The 
Prisoner: A Memoir (수인, Verso, 2021), 89-163. 
 
Films: 
 
* The Steel Helmet (dir. Samuel Fuller, 1951). 
* Dear Pyongyang (디어 평양, dir. Yang Yonghi, 2006). 
* Peppermint Candy (박하사탕, dir. Lee Chang Dong, 1999). 
* Joint Security Area (공동 경비 구역 JSA, dir. Park Chan-wook, 2000). 
 
3 
 
3. Course Requirements and Assessment 
 
A. This course culminates in a Einal research project (due June 17) on any aspect of the 
war, past or present. As the course progresses, you should use the readings and lectures as 
a way to carve out an original research question connected to your own interests and 
curiosities (topics related to the war but not covered in weekly modules are especially 
encouraged, e.g. food, visual art, music, photography, architecture, economics, and so on). 
You should meet with me at least once prior to Week 11 to discuss your ideas. The project 
can take the form of a conventional research paper (~8-10 pages, using a mix of primary 
and secondary sources), but you may also choose to submit a travelogue, a photo-essay, a 
YouTube video, an interview, or some other format congenial to your own thinking. You will 
also be required to give a short presentation (5-7 minutes) on your project; the Sinal 
two weeks (14 and 15) will be reserved for student presentations. Please send me your 
slides at least a day before your presentation. 
 
B. Each week, from Week 2 to Week 13, students will be responsible for reading the 
assigned texts and posting at least three critical discussion questions to the 
corresponding LMS forum. Due by Sundays at 6 p.m., these questions should reSlect on the 
assigned readings for the upcoming week: For example, your questions for Week 2 are due 
on Sunday, March 8, and should be related to some part of Wada, The Korean War, pp. 44-
122; for Week 7, to give another example, they will be due April 12, and should be related to 
Kim, “On the 38th Parallel” and Morris-Suzuki, “A Dream Betrayed.”  
 
C. Rather than a conventional midterm and Einal exam, you will have two major 
review quizzes: The Sirst (March 23) will cover the foundational military history 
covered in Wada, The Korean War, xv-xxvii, 1-167; 293-303; it is critical that you read 
and reSlect on these sections, as they will constitute a critical baseline for our shared 
understanding of the basics as we move into thematic modules; the second (May 13) will 
cover the module themes for Weeks 4-11. These quizzes will test your knowledge of the 
readings with short answer, Sill in the blank, and multiple choice questions; lectures will 
help direct your attention to key points, frameworks, and details, but you should keep 
reading notes, as you may use your own notes during the quizzes. 
 
D. Group work: 1) In the Sirst two weeks, students will be assigned to teams of 3 or 4, 
depending on enrollment. Each team will sign up for one week in which to lead the 
discussion of assigned texts (selected from Weeks 4-13) for a given day (usually the 
Wednesday session, except when we have a Silm screening, in which case Monday). As a 
team you should read your classmates’ discussion questions and draw on the most 
interesting ones to produce a list of 5-7 questions of your own, along with a short 
introduction and analysis of the readings (no more than 10 minutes). 
 
2) Group report on Sites of War Memory in Seoul: Teams will also be required to select 
and introduce one interesting war-related “site of memory” in Seoul in the form of a short 
photo-essay or montage (~5-6 pages). Your “site of memory” (named after French historian 
Pierre Nora’s concept lieu de mémoire) should be more original and surprising than, for 
 
4 
example, the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan. In what ways has the Korean War left 
traces or memories in the city? How has the war left its mark on neighborhoods, 
architecture, infrastructure, urban life, leisure, public space, and so on? Your report is due 
on Sunday, April 26, and you will be assigned a date (Weeks 9 or 10: April 27, April 29, 
May 4, May 6) to present your site of war memory to the class. 
 
E. Attendance, participation, and professionalism: You will be graded holistically on 
your level of engagement in the class. While I recognize that some students are more 
comfortable speaking in class discussion than others, you will at least be expected to 
engage in active listening. You will accordingly be assessed on your “professionalism,” 
meaning your ability to pay attention and treat the instructor and your classmates with 
respect; this means no scrolling on your phones, no irrelevant distractions on your laptops, 
no wearing AirPods, no sleeping, no snacking (except during Silm screenings), etc. 
 
4. Assessment Breakdown: 
 
* Attendance, participation, professionalism: 20% 
* Review quizzes (March 23, May 13): 20% 
* Weekly discussion questions (due Sundays, 6 p.m.): 10% 
* Group discussion leading: 10% 
* Seoul sites of memory group report (due April 26): 10% 
* Final project presentation (Week 14 or 15): 10% 
* Final project submission (due June 17): 20% 
 
Grading Scale: A+ (95-100), A (90-94), B+ (85-89), B (80-84), C+ (75-79), C (70-74), D+ 
(65-69), D (60-64), F (0-59).

여 기본적인 병력청취 및 이학적 검사를 원활하게 하며, 2) 수술 환자를 중심으로 수술 전 후 환자 
관리 및 임상 경과를 이해하고 숙지하며, 3) 분과별 대표 질환의 수술에 참관하여 해부학적 지식 및 
수술의 과정을 체험함으로써 교과서적 지식과 임상 실습을 통해 배운 지식을 최대한 접목하는 기회
를 갖고자 한다.

Course Description 
 
The purpose of this course is to develop an understanding of modern corporate finance so that students will have the 
conceptual foundations for making intelligent corporate financial decisions.  In this course, you will be exposed to 
some of the most fundamental concepts in finance and to their practical applications in the financial management of 
firms.  The course begins with the well-known issues of corporate finance such as capital budgeting analysis, capital 
structure decision, general issues in equity and bonds, and how corporations raise capital.  Then attention of the course 
is put on option pricing theory which is applied to corporate finance problems such as valuation of warrants and 
convertible bonds etc.  Throughout the course, theoretical analysis will be integrated with evaluation of the empirical 
evidence and analysis of specific examples. 
 
It is assumed that students have taken at least one basic finance course such as Financial Management (BUSS207) 
before taking this course.  Only English will be used in the classroom. 
 
 
Required Materials 
 
1. Fundamentals of Corporate Finance, by Ross, Westerfield, and Jordon (or Corporate Finance, by Ross, 
Westerfield and Jaffee) (any reasonably recent edition) 
 
2. Lecture notes (available from the course website) 
 
You are expected to finish all assigned readings before each class.  I strongly recommend you to read a Korean 
financial newspaper and one of the followings: the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, or Financial Times to follow up 
on the current developments in financial market.

Course 
Description 
This course provides a deeper exploration of financial accounting 
concepts under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). 
Significant emphasis is placed on the IFRS conceptual framework and 
its role in guiding recognition, measurement, and disclosure decisions. 
The course also covers more complex and judgment-intensive issues in 
the reporting of cash, receivables, inventories, property, plant and 
equipment, and current liabilities. It strengthens students’ technical 
understanding of IFRS and prepares them for advanced accounting study 
and professional practice. 
Course  
Objectives 
By the end of this course, students will be able to: 
• 
Apply the IFRS conceptual framework to analyze accounting 
issues and support recognition, measurement, and disclosure 
decisions. 
• 
Prepare and present financial information related to cash, 
receivables, inventories, property, plant and equipment, 
depreciation, impairment, and current liabilities in accordance 
with IFRS. 
• 
Evaluate alternative accounting treatments and exercise 
professional judgment in resolving more complex or estimation-
based financial reporting matters. 
• 
Interpret and analyze financial statement effects of various 
accounting policies for assets and current liabilities. 
• 
Communicate accounting conclusions using appropriate IFRS 
terminology and reasoning. 
Textbook 
Kieso, D., J. Weygandt, and T. Warfield, Intermediate Accounting: 
IFRS, Wiley&Sons (5th edition)

1 
수업개요 
본 수업에서는 한국을 포함한 세계 전통 복식과 
고대에서부터 20세기말까지 서양 패션의 변화과정을 
역사적 맥락 안에서 살펴보고, 과거의 패션이 현대 
패션에 어떻게 활용되는지 컬렉션에 나타난 다양한 
예를 통해 이해한다.  
 
전공역량 관련 수업 목표 
1. 
전문가적 사고(40%) & 공감소통(10%): 
패션의 변화 과정에 대한 지식을 당시의 사회·문화적 
맥락 안에서 이해하고 이를 활용해 영화에 재현된 
과거 서양 패션을  협동학습을 통해 비평함으로써 
전문가적 사고력과 공감소통 능력을  배양한다. 
2. 
창의융합적 사고(20%):  과거 패션이 현대 
패션디자이너들의 컬렉션에 어떻게 영감을 주는지 
사례를 통해 이해함으로써 창의융합적인 사고력과 
심미적 감성을 기른다. 
3. 
글로벌(25%) & 도전적 리더(5%): 세계 
각국의 민속 복식의 다양성에 대한 이해를 통해 
글로벌 역량을 확장하고, 이를 바탕으로 다양한 복식 
문화의 올바른 패션디자인적 활용 방안을 모색해 
도전적 리더십을 함양한다. 특히, 패션산업에서의 
문화 전유(도용)의 문제점을 살펴보며 DEI(diversity, 
equity, inclusion)을 고려한 지속가능한 
미래지향적인 패션디자인 방안에 대해 논의한다.  
 
수업 운영 원칙 
1. 
출석: 모든 학생들은 수업에 반드시 
참석해야 한다. 특별한 사유로 결석을 할 경우에는 
담당 교수에게 이메일로 미리 연락한다. 출석은 
증빙서류를 제출할 때에만 인정한다. 무단 결석 
시에는 회당 출석 점수의 10%씩 감점한다. 
수업시간에 30분 이상 늦거나 수업을 마치지 않고 
담당 교수의 허락없이 강의실을 나갈 경우 결석으로 
처리한다. 세 번의 지각은 한 번의 결석과 같다. 
2. 
과제: 늦은 과제물은 하루에 해당 과제물 
점수의 10%씩 감점한다. 단, 보너스 점수를 
부여하는 논문 비평문은 늦는 과제물을 받지 않는다. 
3. 
온라인 학습관리시스템: 본 수업에서는 본교 
학습관리시스템(lms.korea.ac.kr)를 통해 모든 
수업자료와 공지사항을 게시할 예정이므로 학생들은 
매 수업 전 사이트를 방문해 필요한 자료를 프린트 
또는 다운로드해서 필기를 준비해야 한다. 모든 
과제물은 해당 사이트를 통해 제출해야 하며, 팀별 
과제 또한 해당 사이트를 이용해 진행할 수 있다.

과제 & 시험 
1. 
퀴즈: 학생들은 본 수업계획서에 제시된 
수업진행 일정에 맞추어 수업내용을 복습하면서 
복식 용어를 정리해야 한다. 퀴즈는 수업 시작할 때 
사진을 제시하고 해당 복식의 용어를 적는 형식으로 
진행한다.  
2. 
중간고사 & 기말고사: 단답형과 서술형의 
조합으로 출제한다. 정확한 용어의 사용 여부, 
사회·문화적 맥락 안에서의 패션 변화과정에 대한 
이해, 과거 복식의 현대적 활용에 대한 이해 등을 
위주로 평가한다.  
3. 
컬렉션 사진 스크랩: 2025년 S/S 이후 
발표된 국내외 패션디자이너 컬렉션 사진 중 서양의 
고대, 중세, 르네상스, 바로크, 로코코, 신고전주의, 
낭만주의, 아르누보 스타일 유행기, 
1920년대~2차세계대전, 1946년 이후 시대의 복식, 
하위문화 스타일, 한국의 상대복식, 통일신라복식, 
고려복식, 조선복식, 개화기복식, 세계 각국의 
전통복식 중 10개의 주제를 선택(중간고사 범위에서 
5개, 기말 범위에서 5개 선택)해 각 주제에서 영감을 
받은 패션디자인 컬렉션 작품을 찾아 스크랩한다. 각 
주제 별로 2-3개의 패션디자인 작품 사진을 
스크랩하고, 사진의 출처(디자이너명, 발표 년도와 
시즌)와 함께 해당 사진을 선택한 이유를 간단하게 
기술한다. 각종 잡지, 온라인 패션 
사이트(vogue.com, nymag.com 등) 등을 참고할 수 
있다. 제출은 pdf의 형태로 학습관리시스템에 기한 
내에 업로드해야 한다. 4월 15일과 6월 15일에 각각 
중간고사와 기말고사 범위에 해당하는 시대에서 
영감을 얻은 컬렉션 사진을 스크랩해 제출한다.  
4. 
영화의상 비평: 수강생을 4-5명으로 구성된 
팀으로 나누어 과거 서양을 배경으로 제작된 영화를 
시대가 중복되지 않도록 하나씩 선택해 협동학습을 
통해 의상비평을 한다. 과제물은 ppt형태로 제작하되, 
시대적 배경, 줄거리, 등장인물, 의상분석의 내용이 
들어가도록 구성한다. 발표 시 다른 수강생들이 
참고할 수 있도록 한 장의 자유형식의 요약본을 
별도로 준비한다. 발표일인 6월 22일 전에 발표 
PPT와 요약본을 pdf 형식으로 학습관리시스템에 
업로드하고, 해당 수업일에 각 팀별로 약 7분의 
발표를 진행한다. 발표 내용은 물론 발표 태도, 시간 
엄수 여부, 팀별 동료평가 결과 등도 평가에 
반영한다.  
5. 
논문 저널: 수업진행 일정에 제시된 논문 
토론일에 보너스 점수를 받고자 하는 학생들은 
논문을 미리 읽고 논문당 A4용지 한 장 내외의 
소감문을 작성해 pdf 형식으로 제출한다. 소감문은 
수업시간 전까지 학습관리시트엠에 업로드 된 것에 
한해서만 논문당 보너스 점수 1점을 부여한다. 
논문은 토론일 1주일 이전에 공지할 예정이다.

Course 
Overview 
“Between Public and Private: Between High and Low” 
Disconnected cities and architecture 
Especially in Korean cities, architecture has been developed within their 
own property without considerations with its neighborhood and urban 
context. The overall 
city has been shaped without thoughtful 
considerations of how we shape our public space, while individual 
buildings have huge impact on it. From large-scale apartment complexes 
to the low-rise residential areas and commercial streets, cities have been 
built with the lack of careful plans for building shapes and street borders in 
terms of the shape of the public space. 
The identity of Korean architecture and Seoul 
The identity of a city is created mostly through the public spaces and public 
landscapes where the exteriors of individual buildings create together with 
the urban fabric such as streets and squares. The reason why many 
Korean architects have difficulty answering the question of Seoul’s identity 
can be seen as that Seoul has not yet successfully created a good public 
area with a good identity. 
This studio starts from the boundaries between cities and architecture, 
public and private areas. And it expands the themes of the boundary at 
urban context to the scale of buildings and the principles of architectural 
compositions. 
A building is a word located within the city as a text. By expanding 
architectural understanding into urban context, students are expected to 
develop their own attitudes and approach to read and design architecture 
as an experiment. Further this design experiments will develop with 
following considerations into student’s own thesis 
- 
How  architecture  interacts  with  people,  how  we  use  and 
experience architecture as urban and public environment as well 
as individula buildings. 
- 
How architecture should perform and operate for society and its 
sustainable development. As a part of the environment, what is 
architecture’s role in contemporary Korea. 
Identity comes from the commonly shared characters of society but also it 
embraces individual characteristics too. How Korean architecture can 
develop itself considering common virtues as well as individual benefits? 
Considering both common and specific, students can develop the 
alternative directions of architecture in Korea. 
Course 
OUTLINE 
 
Objectives 
 
 
As architecture's role in society becomes increasingly complex and 
constrained, Studio 7 encourages students to thoughtfully define their own 
perspective on architecture. Students are free to choose their focus and 
the architectural problem they aim to solve, within the studio’s thematic 
framework. As this project continues into Design 8, the scope should be 
complex, proposing clear solutions. It requires systematic research and 
analysis to establish the project's purpose, program, site, user, and target 
application. The outcome could range from a physical structure to virtual 
systems encompassing culture, environment, technology, and politics. 
 
Studio 7 initiates the Graduation Project, spanning two semesters. 
Students must apply all their skills in research and urban contextualization. 
This includes a thorough analysis of their chosen site or sites and 
proposing an architectural program that enhances urban life and 
community. Students are developing their thesis topic into architectural 
projects, while the project should be based on comprehensive research 
into materials, technology, and societal trends, with an emphasis on digital 
tool application and data analysis. 
 
The project's scope should strike a balance between urban significance 
and manageable complexity, allowing students to complete the schematic 
design at the building level (in Studio 7) and advance to detailing and 
technical development in Studio 8. Proposals for larger scale urban design 
and master planning are also welcome, provided that some portion of the 
master plan is documented in sufficient detail to develop a detailed 
architectural proposal. 
 
PEDAGOGIC OBJECTIVES 
The student must demonstrate previously acquired skills for research and 
analysis with an open, creative, and critical mind. Then must elaborate a 
comprehensive architectural intervention (including all aspects of design, 
as urban, functional, constructive, symbolic, formal, environmental, etc.) 
based on the findings of the site's analysis, design intent, and prospective 
users. All the processes, from preliminary research to final design, must be 
arranged and presented through texts, diagrams, graphics, drawings, 
models, and digital representation (renders, videos, VR, etc.), as they are 
the basis of the professional architectural work. 
 
1. Detailed and systematic site analysis and urban/human needs. A 
clear understanding of the urban/political reality, its problems, and their 
opportunities mean a personal interpretation, going beyond mere data 
accumulation and quantitative statistics. This analysis is the starting of the 
project intent, the qualitative and quantitative program, the urban, 
technical, and sustainability strategies, and the integration of all of them as 
the start of the design process. 
 
2. Conceptual design must have a clear architectural and urban intention. 
Serious considerations of materiality, structural concept, architectural 
systems, sustainability strategies must be set from the start to be 
integrated into the overall idea. They do not become a hindrance in the 
following steps of the process. (Depending on studnets’ concept, even 
when the structure and systems may not be considered in a serious 
manner, they should be integrated into the design for at least Studio 8) 
 
3. The design results from a process in which the building is shaped 
step by step. The student must be conscious of this process and must be 
able to express it clearly in its output. A clear process is much more 
meaningful than a good looking at final results without a process behind it. 
4. The design should be consistent and inclusive of all previous 
materials and studies, assuming the inherent complexity of the 
architectural facts. 
5. The design should integration of all relevant technologies: Envelope, 
structure, environmental, urban, and service systems. that have 
sophisticated architectural definitions, including clear structural ideas, 
passive and active environmental systems, circulation strategies, exterior 
envelopes, life safety systems, universal access, and specific material 
qualities. Deploy architectural components both pragmatically and 
poetically. 
(Depending on studnets’ concept, even when the structure and systems 
may not be considered in a serious manner, they should be integrated 
into the design for at least Studio 8)

Course Objectives: 
 
This skills class is designed to provide guidance and experience in delivering effective oral presentations to 
a range of audiences. Various types of presentations will be introduced, and students will practice the 
structure and delivery of at minimum four types from either (Impromptu, Conference, PPT/Poster, Data, Mock 
Job Interview, Ted Talk, etc.,). Particular attention will be placed on improving audience-connecting oral 
skills—appropriate posture, gestures, volume, intonation, etc.—to appropriately target an audience and 
convey confidence, authority, and/or trust. Active participation is required. Objectives for a successful learner 
are: 
 
first and foremost, produce and conduct effective presentations with confidence 
 
 
enhance oral communication skills necessary for functioning beyond the classroom 
 
 
analyze and practice the structure, content and delivery of different presentation types 
 
 
develop strategies and techniques for designing audience-targeted presentations 
 
 
experience planning, organizing, and delivering speeches & PowerPoint (other) style of 
presentations 
 
 
gain confidence in handling audience/group generated question-and-answer sessions  
 
 
enhance awareness of your verbal and non-verbal communication skills 
 
 
built your academic vocabulary and vocabulary related to presentations 
 
 
Materials & Textbook: 
 
Textbook? None. Course materials will be posted on the new KULMS, emailed or given in class.  
You will though be required to have the following with you during lessons: 
 
● A file folder or binder to organize your handouts 
● A notebook for class notes and/or assignments tasks 
● Cue cards  
● USB/ Flash drive 
● Pen, pencil, highlighters, eraser, white-out, etc.

Office Hours & Communication: 
 
My aim is to help you improve as much as possible. Therefore, I welcome your queries about anything, 
small or big. Communication is fundamental in so many aspects of life, so it is better to ask than to remain 
in the dark. There will be times when I am unable to answer your questions right away due to my 
schedule and other students’ inquiries; please understand this and make an appointment if you 
want to meet me via online. I will make time for you if you let me know in advance.  
 
My Gmail account, hawkplynn@gmail.com and the new KULMS will be utilized for basic communication, 
announcements and course work uploads, so it is essential that you always check the new KULMS and 
your email. 
 
 
 
Responsibility of Students: 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The public speaking class is not your typical class. It’s not just a passive lecture 
class. Active participation is required. Following the class guidelines can help your 
confidence, communication and presentation skills. 
 
Class Guidelines:  
 
 
 
● Come to class every day and be prepared for class. At a minimum, bring your notebook for note 
taking and file folder for your handouts to every class. 
● Participate in class. It is required. 
● Complete assignments on time. 
● If you are absent, it is your job to find out what was taught in class.  
● Stay in class. Leaving freely in-and-out of the classroom is distracting. Students are to be in the class 
at all class times and not go in and out for their convenience. These behaviors distract other students 
and disturb the class environment. Tardiness will also be reflected in your final grade. 
● Listen carefully and ask me questions if you don't understand something or make an appointment to 
speak to me. 
● Do not submit work (old or new) from another course/class. 
● Cell phones, laptops, tablets: inappropriate use  of SMS, Kakao, Instagram, gossiping, etc. and 
working on other class work is not permitted in class for any reason. It’s rude and disruptive. These 
will affect negatively on your class participation grade. 
● Sleeping in class. This will affect negatively on the class attendance and participation 
grades.  
● Do not use Korean or another language. 
● Use of offensive language will not be tolerated (English, Korean, etc.).  
● Be positive and encourage other members of the class.  
● Acknowledge and respect other members of the class. 
 
I am here to help you, but I will not spoon-feed you. Try to research and find answers before you ask me. If 
you cannot find the answer or if you are uncertain, I welcome your questions. Some of the rules below may seem 
obvious but failure to follow them may result in omission from the classroom, lower grades and ultimately an F 
grade.  
 
Attending KU festivals, club events, retreats, military duties, and/or job interviews do not absolve you of 
your responsibility as a student. It is up to you to be responsible and inquire about missed assignments and to 
get missed notes, handouts, etc. I will not track you down. Be responsible for your work.  
 
Complete classwork/assignments conscientiously and on time. You are expected to preview each lesson 
and prepare for class and complete all assignments on time.  Late work will result in points deducted**. Late 
assignment(s) will be penalized point for each day late (including on the due date and the weekend/holidays).  
 
**If you are absent, assume you missed assignments, handouts and notes, so contact one of your classmates 
and talk to me.**

The use of generative AI in class without basic guidelines. It may negatively impact the quality of teaching

(3) Acquisition of inaccurate or biased information. 
(4) Reinforcement of entrenched stereotypes.

Speaking English isn’t only about fluency. It’s about being in class, doing the work,

하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함
∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서 위치를 작가하며 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐고에 정진

 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 학문적 지식탐구 및 미래 비전과 연결된 교과목 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 미리 교육자료 탐독하고 확인
 -정해진 수업시간에 결석, 지각, 중도 이탈 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -적극적으로 토론, 질의응답 등 수업활동에 참여

4. 과 소개
산부인과는 다음의 분과로 구성되어 있습니다. 산모와 태아의 건강을 담당하는 모체태아의학
(산과), 난소암이나 자궁암 같이 여성생식기관에 발생하는 암을 치료하는 부인종양학, 그리고 
성호르몬 연관 질환 치료와 난임치료 및 가임력보존치료를 하는 생식내분비학 분과가 있고, 
이외에도 자궁근종 같은 여성질환을 치료하는 일반부인과로 구성되어 있습니다.
1) 안암병원
Ÿ
안암병원 산부인과의 산과학 담당 교수는 홍순철 교수, 안기훈 교수, 생식내분비학 담당 
교수는 박현태 교수, 류기진 교수, 정혜경 임상교수, 그리고 부인종양학 담당 교수는 송재
윤 교수, 이상훈 교수, 김성민 교수, 이선미 임상교수, 서현경 임상교수가 각각 담당하고 
있습니다. 주병동은 52병동, 54병동 및 분만실이고, 외래 환자는 2층 산부인과 외래에서 
진료하고 있습니다. 본과의 실습에서 주로 다루는 내용은 분만, 수술 참관, 외래 환자 병력 
청취 및 진료 참관, 입원 환자를 대상으로 한 임상 실습입니다.  
2) 구로병원
Ÿ
구로병원 산부인과의 산과학 담당 교수는 오민정 교수, 조금준 교수, 설현주 임상교수, 
송정민 임상조교수, 생식내분비학 담당 교수는 신정호 교수, 김용진 교수, 오수민 
임상조교수, 부인종양학 담당 교수는 이재관 교수, 홍진화 교수, 정소현 임상조교수가 각각 
담당하고 있습니다. 주병동은 51병동 및 분만실입니다. 외래 환자는 미래관 3층 산부인과 
외래에서 진료하고 있습니다. 본과의 실습에서 주로 다루는 내용은 분만, 수술 참관, 외래 
환자 병력 청취 및 진료 참관, 입원 환자를 대상으로 한 임상 실습입니다.
3) 안산병원
Ÿ
안산병원 산부인과는 이낙우 교수(부인종양), 이경욱 교수(생식내분비/난임), 민경진 교수
(부인종양), 김호연 교수(산과), 오영택 교수(부인종양), 송관흡 임상교수(모체태아), 김남경 
임상교수(부인종양), 백승훈(모체태아)로 구성되어 있습니다. 본과의 입원 환자는 51병동 
및 분만실에 주로 분포하며, 외래 환자의 처치(소파술, 소수술)는 입원 후 분만실에서, 난
임시술(난자채취, 배아이식 등)은 외래 난임센터에서 시행됩니다.

공통 실습 지침
1) 실습 개요
Ÿ
학생들은 산과, 생식내분비, 부인종양 파트로 나누고, 매주 파트별로 교대하여 참여합니다.
Ÿ
출근은 오전 8시이며, 사전 공지된 저널미팅, 태아심초음파 컨퍼런스, 산과/소아과 미팅, 
증례 및 토픽 발표, 텍스트북리딩, 등의 일정이 있는 경우에는 시간에 맞게 참석합니다.
Ÿ
일정 정리 시간은 강의, 발표 등이 없는 경우 오후 회진이 끝나는 시간인 5시입니다.
Ÿ
파트별로 학생 개개인의 실습은 외래 참관, 분만실 참관, 수술실 참관으로 구분하여 각자
의 정해진 스케쥴에 따라 순환하여 실습합니다.
2) 실습지침 교육
Ÿ
오리엔테이션: 실습 첫째 주 월요일 오전 산부인과 의국
Ÿ
내용
- 분과별 학생배정 및 실습 스케쥴 확인
- 산부인과 환자의 문진 시 유의사항과 개인정보의 보호에 관한 법률, 의료법의 이해
- 외래 및 수술 참관, 분만실 내 시술 및 분만 참관 시의 유의사항 전달
- 산부인과 병력 청취의 기본 사항과 임상적 의미 / 산부인과적 의학용어의 이해
- 분과별 강의 스케쥴 안내 및 OCSE/CPX 교육 일정 계획 안내
- 시험, 임상증례 발표의 일정과 준비방법, 임상실습 평가 기준의 고지
Ÿ
지침
- 실습 개시 당일까지 분과별 학생 배정 및 실습 스케쥴 작성을 완성하여 교육 시 제출
- 각 분과 당 1주 실습 후 순환하도록 배치
- 산부인과 병력 청취 내용에 대한 교육자료(강의록 ppt, 임상실습지침서)를 지참
- 오전 교육 이후 각 분과별 실습을 개시
Ÿ
포트폴리오 작성 관련
- 포트폴리오를 통해 실습 성적을 최종 평가하게 됩니다. 따라서, 실습 시작 전에 산부인과  
  실습 규정을 다시 한 번 확인하고 실습에 임하기 바랍니다. 실습 종료까지 필요한 과제나  
  시행한 임상 술기 및 시술에 대해 승인 또는 제출하지 않은 경우 실습 종료 후 수정할   
  기회는 없습니다.
2026학년도 전반기 임상실습 지침서
3) 병동 회진
Ÿ
병동에서 회진 시, 교수 가까이 회진을 따라 돌면서 적극적으로 질문하고 교수님의 질문에 
답변합니다. 자신이 맡은 환자의 정보를 명확히 파악하고 있어야 합니다.
Ÿ
회진 시간/장소: 오전 환자 발표 후 또는 각 교수 별 회진 시간 확인 필요
4) 외래 참관 및 예진
Ÿ
분과별 담당교수들의 외래시간표를 파악하여 해당 시간마다 실습 학생 1명씩 참관합니다.
Ÿ
외래 참관 시 환자의 진단에 따라 그에 대한 physiopathology 및 치료 등에 대하여 공부
하며 외래 종료 후 교수님과의 질문답 시간을 통하여 관련 내용에 대하여 review 합니다.
Ÿ
자신이 예진한 환자의 경우 각 진료실로 같이 들어가 환자의 진료 과정을 함께 보고 토론
하면서, 산부인과 외래의 실제적인 진료 과정을 이해합니다.
Ÿ
교육 지침 시 전달받은 환자 문진 및 외래 참관 시 유의사항을 지켜야 합니다.
5) 수술 참관 및 참여
Ÿ
수술실 참관 시 참관 혹은 어시스트 참여(스크럽)를 합니다. 첫 수술일 경우 오전 8시 20
분까지 수술실 내 대기실 또는 각 담당 파트 배정 수술실에서 대기합니다.
Ÿ
참관하는 학생은 수술 받는 환자의 진단, 병력, 치료 방향 등에 대해 미리 숙지합니다.
Ÿ
해당 분과 수술을 모두 참관한 경우 분과 교수님과 상의 후 수술 참관 대신 병동 환자 파
악 등을 진행합니다.
6) 분만실 내 분만/소수술 참관
Ÿ
분만실에서 시행하는 분만이나 수술 등의 처치에 해당 분과 실습학생 1명씩 참관합니다.
Ÿ
분만실 참관 시 산모의 진단에 따라 그에 대한 physiopathology 및 치료와 초음파 및 
NST 등을 통한 환자 상태에 대한 평가 및 환자 상태의 변화에 대하여 공부합니다.
Ÿ
분만실 내에서 교수의 회진을 함께 돌면서 환자에 대해 적극적으로 질문하고 교수의 질문
에 답변합니다. 
Ÿ
처치 및 소수술 일정은 매일 오전 담당 교수에게 확인받습니다. 생식내분비 분과는 아침 
일찍 난임시술이 시작되는 경우가 많으므로 오후 5시경 다음 날 스케쥴 유무 및 참석 여
부를 확인합니다.
Ÿ
응급실 환자가 있을 경우 참관을 통하여 환자의 증상 및 병력을 바탕으로 초음파와 신체검
사 등을 통하여 진단을 내리는 과정에 대하여 이해합니다.
Ÿ
해당 처치 시 필요한 위생수칙을 반드시 엄수하고, 교육받은 실습 지침을 따르도록 합니
다. (예시: 분만장 출입 시 위생모와 마스크 착용, 외부 신발 반입 금지)
7) 환자 배정과 발표 및 평가
Ÿ
담당교수 및 수석 전공의에게서 신환을 배정 받은 후 배정받은 환자를 파악하여, 회진 시
2026학년도 전반기 임상실습 지침서
나 질문이 있을 시, 환자에 대해 발표합니다. 
Ÿ
발표 시에는 의학용어를 정확하고 간결하게 사용하여 의미가 잘 전달되도록 합니다.
Ÿ
맡은 환자는 매일 진찰하고 포트폴리오에 간단한 경과기록을 남기며 중요 시술에 참관 및 
동참합니다. 특히 국가시험에 필수 항목에 대해서는 기회가 될 때마다 반드시 참관하여 익
숙해 지도록 합니다.
Ÿ
평가는 가능한 즉시 포트폴리오를 이용하여 받거나 실습 종료 전까지 확인 받도록 합니다.
Ÿ
실습 3주차엔 환자에 대한 증례발표를 하는데, 증례는 담당 교수님과 상의하여 미리 받도록 
합니다. 발표시 맡은 환자에 대한 disease review에 대하여 담당 교수님과 상의 후 주제
를 결정하며 case 및 disease review의 경우 power point로 준비하여 발표합니다.
Ÿ
산부인과에서 중요한 진단과정 중, 1. 주 증상과 병력, 골반 진찰이 포함된 검진 2. 이러한 
증상을 보일 수 있는 질환들에 대한 감별 진단을 나열하고 그에 맞는 계획을 요약할 수 있
어야합니다.
Ÿ
의료인이 작성한 의무기록을 복사해서 발표하지 않습니다. 교수나 전공의와 함께 직접 환
자를 대면하도록 하고 해당 환자의 수술을 참관하고 작성하기 바랍니다.
Ÿ
정해진 산부인과 실습 이외의 개인 시간에는 환자 문진 및 병력 청취, 의무기록이나 영상, 
검사 소견 및 실습을 시행합니다.
8) 임상 강의
Ÿ
분과별 배치 후 담당교수들에게 강의 시간을 배정받아 진행합니다.
Ÿ
강의 시 분과별이 아닌 전체 학생들이 참석을 원칙으로 하며, 해당 일정 확정 후 실습담당
교수 또는 당일 실습을 지도해주고 있는 분과 교수들에게 반드시 고지해야 합니다.
Ÿ
강의 방식은 분과별로 다를 수 있으며, 담당 교수의 지도에 따라 준비합니다.
9) OSCE/CPX 실습
Ÿ
실습 중 정해진 날짜에 CPX와 OSCE 실습 및 강의에 참여합니다.
Ÿ
OCSE – 도뇨관 삽입과 분만진행단계 진찰을 모형을 통하여 실습
Ÿ
수술 참관 시 도뇨관 삽입을 시행하여 수술 종료 후 전공의 선생님을 통해 포트폴리오에 
평가를 받습니다.
Ÿ
CPX – 산부인과 증례에 대해 학생들이 Role play 형식으로 준비하여, 서로 질문하고 대
답 후 instructor가 첨언하게 됩니다.
10) 시험
Ÿ
마지막 주 월요일에는 3개(안암, 구로, 안산)병원 통합 실습 시험을 시행합니다. 총 30문항
이며, 시험 시간은 1시간입니다.
2026학년도 전반기 임상실습 지침서
6. 학생활동 또는 실습내용
Ÿ
학생들은 임상실습 시작 전 e포트폴리오에 본인의 사진과 자기소개서를 작성합니다. 
Ÿ
학생들은 임상실습 책임교수 및 전공의, 교수진의 지도감독 하에 자발적으로 실습에 참여
하며 컨퍼런스 및 세미나에 참여합니다.
Ÿ
학생들이 알아야 할 CPX 예시
아래 항목은 산부인과 영역 중 의사국가시험에서 출제되는 임상표현문제입니다. 각 문제에 
대한 지식, 관련 술기를 완전 학습하여 행동으로 정확히 숙련되게 표현할 수 있도록 학습합
니다. 해당 문제들에 대하여 KU Simuation Center에서 모의실습 및 평가, 실습중 Role 
play 형식으로 병력과 신체진찰 및 수기수행(모형실습)을 하고 튜터의 피드백을 받게 됩니다.

기본지식과 역량을 습득한다. 둘째, 제조 및 서비스 기업의 운영관리 개

관리, 프로젝트관리 등)을 이해하고, 실제 사례와 데이터를 통해 효율적 
운영전략 수립 능력을 함양한다. 셋째, 조직 내의 정보시스템의 역할과 
더불어 정보 시스템의 기술적 토대, 성공적인 비즈니스를 위한 전략적 활
용, 디지털 기술의 메가트랜드 등에 대한 지식을 배운다. 넷째, 재무회계
와 관리회계를 통합적으로 다루어, 학생들은 재무제표 작성과 분석을 통
해 회계정보의 생산과정과 유용성을 배우는 한편, 원가분석·예산관리·
성과평가 등 내부 의사결정에 활용되는 관리회계 기법을 익힌다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

INTRODUCTION 
 
This course introduces cost and management accounting topics to enable students to understand 
how accounting information is used to manage an organization.  
 
The course focuses on the factors that differentiate one company from another. For example, 
“What makes one company more profitable and/or better managed than another?” The course will 
look at various functional areas within the firm, ranging from manufacturing to marketing, and from 
accounting to human relations. In addition, the concept of management, how senior managers plan, 
implement and control those plans through people will be briefly discussed. 
  
The course will enhance students’ personal skills in preparation for more advanced courses at the 
university in the following ways: working in groups, analyzing cases, writing reports, and making 
presentations. 
  
 
LEARNING OBJECTIVES: 
 
On completion of this course, students are expected to: 
 
• Understand cost concepts and their uses  
• Prepare costing statements using absorption and variable costing systems 
• Able to use ABC (Activity Based Costing) in product costing and decision making 
• Ascertain and account for the costs of labor, materials, and overheads 
• Prepare product costs data using job and process costing techniques 
 
2
• Prepare budgets and set standard costs, calculate and interpret material, labor, and 
overhead variances 
• Understand the use of budgetary control and standard costing 
• Understand the behavioral impact of accounting 
• Perform simple short-term and long-term decision-making exercises 
• Use performance measures in evaluating managers and the firm

Class Preparation & Participation 
 
Students are strongly encouraged to actively participate in class discussions/group presentations. 
Students will be graded on an individual basis according to their contribution to the class through 
homework submissions and class discussions. Instructor may check students’ class attendances and 
preparations from time to time. Homework assignments are to be submitted only through 
Blackboard class website. If you cannot submit your homework via Blackboard due to reasons 
beyond your control, email it to my TA before the due date.    
 
Quizzes 
 
There will be 2 quizzes covering all the topics that are covered up to the class in the previous week. 
The tests will be conducted in class on the 4th and 12th weeks at the start of the class. Further details 
of the quizzes will be announced during the course. If you miss a quiz due to reasons beyond your 
control, bring necessary documents to prove it to your instructor. Then your grade for that test will 
be adjusted by increasing the weight to your next quiz or exam.  
 
Mid-term and Final Examination 
 
There will be the mid-term and final examination in class on 8th and 16th weeks. The mid-term and 
the final examination will be 75 minutes and 120 minutes, respectively, and they may consist of 
multiple-choice questions, fill-blank questions, and problem questions. If you miss the final 
examination, you cannot complete the course and take the whole course all over again in the future. 
Be sure to bring a calculator to the examinations. 
 
In accounting quizzes and exams, students often compete not only in how well you understand the 
materials but also in how quickly you can recall and use the materials in solving problems. After 
reading chapter readings, students are strongly encouraged to gauge their level of understanding 
by solving assigned homework or exercise questions available on LMS.  
 
 
3
ACADEMIC INTEGRITY 
 
Ethics and values are very important in the world of business, government and not-for-profit 
organizations. You will be examining ethical issues throughout this course. Ethics are vital to the 
process of education as well. Your instructors will assume, unless there is evidence to the contrary, 
that you are fulfilling your ethical responsibilities. These are listed below:  
 
Homework assignments 
 
All work is to be performed exclusively by yourself. If outside research is used, sources are to be 
cited and information discovered via outside research is to be clearly labeled as such. The product 
of your research is not to be shared with any students.  
 
Examinations and tests 
 
All examinations and tests must be the exclusive works of the individual student that are completed 
during the exam or test period. Allowing another student to obtain course credit by deceit 
contributes to a general lowering of the ethical standards of the University and to the deception of 
potential employers and other academic institutions. Thus, you have an obligation to inform the 
course instructor if you know another student is violating the University's standards of academic 
conduct.  
 
Penalty for academic integrity violations: 
 
University recommended sanctions for academic integrity violations will be imposed. The penalty 
for cheating in an assignment is a grade of “F” for the course and in the case of cheating in an 
examination; the penalty may be expulsion from the university. All academic integrity violations 
will be reported to the appropriate University officials.  
 
CLASSES 
 
Class Session: 1 hour and 15 minutes per session 
 
The course will be conducted in SEMINAR/LECTURE sessions that will last for one hour and 15 
minutes. You are expected to attend these sessions well-prepared, be ready to respond to questions 
as required. This means doing the required readings and homework assignments before each 
session.  
 
Given time limits, individual seminars/lectures may not necessarily cover all of your readings and 
assignments. However, the materials from the seminars, readings, and assignments may be 
included in the tests and examinations.  
 
REQUIRED TEXT 
 
Garrison, Noreen, and Brewer, Managerial Accounting, 18th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2024.
