1 
 
Academic English  
Spring 2026 
 
 
 
Instructor: 
Glenn Sundeen M.A. 
Office: 
Rm 711, International Studies Hall 
Mobile phone #: 
010-9247-4306 
E-mail: 
gsundeen@gmail.com 
 
 
 
Basic course information 
 
Students 
❖ College of Politics and Economics, College of Media,  
     College of International Studies 
Course credits 
❖ two academic credits 
Course time 
❖ two 50-minute classes per week 
Classroom 
❖ See schedule below 
Grading policy 
❖ absolute grading 
Attendance policy 
❖ mandatory (according to Korea University’s regulations) 
Language of instruction 
❖ English 
 
 
Purpose of Academic English 
 
1 - To prepare students for taking English mediated courses (EMC) in their major. 
2 - To prepare students to be part of the global community of academia. 
3 - To prepare students for studying abroad in an international-language  
       environment. 
4 - To prepare students to thrive (survive) in a foreign language environment 
5 - To prepare students to be independent learners and thinkers. 
 
 
 
 
 
Academic English focuses on developing students’ academic skills in 
critical thinking, argumentation, academic writing, academic 
discussion and presentation (all in English).  
 
These crucial skills are transferable to any course, any major,  
any language or taught in any country. 
 
 
 
 
2 
 
Evaluation 
 
 
Attendance 
10 % 
Class participation 
10 % 
Assignments* 
80 % 
Total 
100 % 
 
 
 
 
* Includes an academic essay, graded academic discussion and presentation assignment. 
 
Typically, a maximum of about 40-50% of you will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”. Evaluation in 
this class is based strictly on performance, and not on English language proficiency. All parts of 
the evaluation system must be completed in an exceptional manner if you want to get an “A+”.   
 
 
Need Help? 
Getting adjusted to university life can sometimes be tough, dramatic even traumatic, especially 
during a pandemic.  Help is available, however.  The KU Student Counseling Center offers 
help to students having trouble at university or with their feelings. They are very good at 
listening. They have one to one counseling, group counseling, and even some tests people can 
take about their lives, feelings, personality, relationships, and more. During the semester, they 
are open from Monday-Friday from 9 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. (closed for lunch). They are located in 
the 과학도서관 307 호. Tel: 3290-4581~4582. Website: http://kuscc.korea.ac.kr (in Korean). 
 
 
 
 
3 
 
Class Expectations (Please READ CAREFULLY!) 
 
This class is not like your other classes.  It is NOT a lecture class, so you must be 
active instead of passive in this class.  The following are some guidelines for 
conduct that I expect in this class.  Following these expectations will assist in 
enhancing your academic skills as well as improving chances of a good grade.  
 
 
1. 
 
Ask me questions:  This course is about communication, and it is extremely 
important for us to understand each other.  Feel free to ask me at any time to 
repeat or explain something if you do not understand. I am also available in my 
office, Rm 711, by appointment or during my office hours. Please remember that  
it is your responsibility to tell me if there is something you do not 
understand or need help with. 
 
 
2. 
 
You must use English in class: You must try as best as you can to 
communicate all of your thoughts in English.  If you cannot find the correct words 
in English, try to find some other way to express yourself (body language, face 
expressions, drawing pictures, etc.).  Be creative! It is a requirement of this 
course that you use English in this class. 
 
 
3. 
 
Participate actively in the class!  Do not be afraid to speak in class, and do not 
worry about making mistakes.  Incorrect speaking is better than no speaking.  
Perfect English is not necessary, but class participation is necessary.  It is a 
part of your grade! 
 
 
4. 
 
Assignments and projects!  Any assignment or project not ready by the 
assigned deadline will receive a grade of “0”.  If you are absent, make sure to ask 
your classmates or contact me about what you missed.  Copying homework 
(plagiarism) will automatically get you an "0". Any assignments fully created 
with generative A.I. (like ChatGPT) will receive a grade of “0”. 
 
 
5. 
 
Grades!  Although important to you and your GPA, improving your skills in a 
foreign language is not only about grades.  It is a skill that can be life changing for 
your future.  Developing good English language skills can open opportunities for 
employment and future study abroad, it can help you connect to the world beyond 
the borders of your country, and it can enhance your understanding of other 
cultures.  Please view this course as an opportunity to build your future, and 
not simply as an influence on your GPA.  Furthermore, in Korea, English is 
often used as a measure of a person’s value in society, but NOT in this class!   
The grades I assign to you are not an evaluation of you personally nor 
reflective of my likes or dislikes.  It is simply an evaluation of your performance in 
class tasks and activities. 
 
 
6. 
 
Absences!  If you are going to be absent from class for any reason, I will mark 
you as absent for that class, but I allow you 3 absences in the semester 
without any academic penalty.  You can notify me about an absence through the 
Korea University portal, but it will still count as an absence, so use your free 
absences wisely.   
 
- Students missing more than 6 classes will receive a grade of “F”. 
 
 
 
4 
 
 
7. 
 
Be in class on time!  Students who are late are disturbing for the class and for 
me. If you are more than 10 minutes late, I will mark you absent for that class.  If 
you are late 3 times, I will mark you absent for one class.   
- This will NOT count as one of the allowed absences in #6. 
 
 
8. 
 
No distracted sessions!  The use of mobile telephones for communication 
purposes is not allowed in this class.  It is disruptive and rude to other participants.  
Use of cell phones for communicative purposes (including Kakao Talk) will 
result in being marked absent for that class! Use of other devices (laptops, 
tablets, etc.) for communication purposes during class will also result in being 
marked absent. If you are using your phone as a dictionary or for fact checking, 
make it clear to me that you are doing so.  No exceptions. 
 
9. 
 
Textbook materials!  On most days we will be using our textbook materials. All of 
these materials are made available through KU-LMS.  Please make sure you have 
them available for every class.  Repeated failure to do so will affect your class 
participation grade.  Textbook materials can be used in either paper (strongly 
recommended) or digital form. 
 
10. 
 
Bathroom Breaks!  Please use the break time BETWEEN CLASSES for things 
like getting drinks, making phone calls and going to the toilet.  If it is an 
emergency, you do not have to ask me for permission to go to the toilet.  If it is 
not an emergency, you do not have to go! 
 
11. Pay attention to the details!  Students who get A+ in this course tend to be those 
who read instructions carefully, ask me questions, and focus on accomplishing the 
tasks in detail. If you miss something important, refer to #1! 
 
12. 
 
Show respect and courtesy to your classmates!  Please be respectful of your 
classmates and help me to provide a positive and encouraging learning 
environment.  Your enjoyment of this class and the development of your 
academic English skills depend on the attitude you bring to this class every day.   
Please be positive, be polite and be kind.

DESCRIPTION 
This course is aimed at providing the students with the basic finance concepts and their 
applications. They include time value of money, risk and return tradeoff, security valuation, and 
capital budgeting, to name a few. After this course, the students are expected to know how to 
think about corporate projects and securities in terms of their cash flows occurring at future 
dates, how to manage the risks associated with the projects, how capital markets function, and 
how companies and capital markets interact with each other.

Corporate Finance by Ivo Welch  
 
This textbook is available at the following web-site free of charge. 
 
https://corpfin.ivo-welch.info/home/ 
 
While we use it as textbook, if there is any discrepancy between the book and our class 
discussions, the class discussions will be given priority. All exam answers will also be based on 
the class discussions, if there is any difference between the book and the class discussions.

ATTENDANCE 
We take attendance of each session (i.e., twice a class day). Attendance is defined as coming to 
class up to 10 minutes into class and staying in class up to 5 minutes before class dismissal. It is 
either attended or absent. There is no “late” – this is to encourage full attendance. Each 
attendance earns 10 points and the total attendance score is capped at 150. We take attendance 
on Exam 1 and Exam 2 dates as well.  
 
The so-called “excused absences” do not earn the attendance scores. As the university requires, 
you must physically attend half of the entire 30 classes, in which case you can earn the full 
attendance score. 
 
The “excused absences” counts towards the university’s another requirement—namely, the 2/3 
attendance. In order to earn any credit from the course, your attendances (physical 
attendances + excused absences) need to be at least 2/3 of the entire 30 classes.  
 
An excuse will be granted for the occasions for which the University allows absence (e.g., job 
interview, medical operation, reserve military drills) and proof is provided at least one full 
day before. If the absence is due to some unexpected event and a proof document is not 
available beforehand (e.g., sudden illness), a request for excused absence needs to be submitted 
on the day at the latest. Also, the proof needs to be submitted as soon as it becomes available. 
For this late submission, I need to see a clear indication that the student was unable to attend 
the class on the day for the reason that the document is attesting. This judgement is at my 
discretion.  
 
Further, there is a minimum physical attendance policy in order to receive a certain letter 
grade: 
 
▪ 
A (+, 0, -): at least 24 physical attendances (appx. 80% of the entire 30 classes) 
▪ 
B (+, 0, -): at least 21 physical attendances (appx.70% of the entire 30 classes) 
▪ 
C (+, 0, -): at least 18 physical attendances (appx.60% of the entire 30 classes) 
 
For pre-scheduled and unavoidable events (judged at my discretion), the denominator (i.e., 30) 
may change. For example, if there is a mandatory military drill and the resulting two absences, 
the denominator will be reduced to 28 (from 30).  
 
 
EXAMS 
There will be 3 exams. All exams are given during the regular class time and the detailed 
schedule is at the end of this syllabus.  
 
For Exams 1 and 2, if a student misses an exam for the occasions for which the University 
allows absence (e.g., job interview, medical operation, reserve military drills) and proof is 
 
3 
provided at least one full day before the missing exam, its weight will be transferred to the 
next exam.  
 
For Exam 3, the arrangement is similar but the *bar* will be much higher, meaning that the 
excuse is granted if and only if it is completely unavoidable. In addition, there will be a 
discount. The missing Exam 3 will be backfilled by 70% of the average of the physically taken 
prior two exam scores. Also, without a physically taken Exam 3 score, the highest letter grade 
for the course will be B+. Finally, the backfill option can be used only once. 
 
 
IN-CLASS WORK & PARTICIPATION 
Throughout the semester in *almost* every session, there will be in-class work in various

with my observations, as a basis for the participation credit for one possible grade level change.

Welcome to the Advanced English Discussion for the Spring 2026 semester.  In this class we are 
going to study advanced-level English through the medium of student-led oral presentations and 
small-group discussions on a wide selection of topics chosen mostly by you and your classmates.  
Through participation in these presentations/discussions, students will achieve the following: 
 
a) become familiar with and develop opinions on a wide variety of current issues 
b) develop critical-thinking and academic argumentation skills 
c) build academic discourse and debating skills 
d) enhance knowledge of academic English vocabulary 
e) gain confidence in using English in both formal and informal settings 
 
The course work and evaluation for this course will be based on four primary components:  
     1. student-led topic modules (presentation + discussion)  
     2. class participation 
     3. vocabulary test(s) 
     4. class attendance 
 
This course is designed for the advanced non-native speaker proficiency 
level.  Native speakers of English are allowed to take this course, but 
please keep in mind the primary target demographic for this course. 
 
Student-led Presentations/Discussions: 
After a few weeks of introductory material led by myself, students will present a topic to the class 
and lead group discussions on that topic.  In most cases, these topics will be introduced through 
the use of media articles.   
 
Student presenters will be expected to complete all of the following: 
1. Choose a topic that will be introduced by a media article.  This article must be provided to your 
instructor at least one week before your presentation date.   
2. Provide the article, together with target vocabulary indicated by underlining or highlighting, as 
well as any useful supplementary materials, at least one class before your presentation date. 
Students are expected to have read these articles before coming to class, and will be required 
to answer comprehension questions based on these articles before coming to class.  
3. Instruct the class on advanced academic vocabulary related to their article and/or related to 
their topic. In addition, at least 3 or 4 idioms, colloquialisms or other informal expressions 
must be included in this exercise. 
4. Conduct a short topic presentation (maximum 10-12 minutes) on your topic, outlining 
background information and the various issues/points of view it concerns.  This presentation 
must be conducted as a team.  
5. Provide intellectually stimulating discussion questions for student groups.  Your discussion 
time is the most important of the class and should be able to fill at least 25 minutes of your 
module. 
6. Manage the class carefully so that all parts of their module can be completed in the 60–65-
minute class time (it is essential that they provide the professor 5 to 10 minutes as well, at the 
end).  This is very important and will be included in your evaluation. 
 
The number of students enrolled in this course will determine the nature of the 
presentations, the number of presentations and whether students present 
alone or with a partner.   
 
 
2 
Presentations will be evaluated in terms of  
a) topic values (topical, controversial, challenging, but sensitive and appropriate for 
classmates) 
b) materials and preparation  
c) presentation delivery  
d) classroom and time management 
e) English usage  
 
Important! Since this presentation/discussion module is so important in this class, students 
failing to complete this requirement will automatically receive an F in this course.  No 
exceptions. 
 
I allow a lot of freedom in the choice of topics, but please choose topics and articles that are 
appropriate for your classmates in terms of length, difficulty, issue sensitivity, and utility.  There 
must be some kind of controversy in order to generate interesting and useful discussion or 
debate.  All topics and articles must be submitted to the instructor at least 1 week before 
your presentation, and are subject to the professor’s prior approval.  The instructor reserves 
the right to disallow any topic or article considered to be inappropriate with regards to length, level 
of English, content, etc.  If you are in any doubt regarding your topic or article, make sure to 
consult with the instructor as early as possible. Failure to submit your materials in advance will 
result in a significant reduction in grade. 
 
Obviously, there is no textbook for this class. All materials will be accessed through the KU-LMS 
platform.   
 
Class Discussion Participation: 
Students will also be evaluated in terms of daily participation in the group discussions.  
 
Participation evaluation includes: 
a) preparation (including reading comprehension questions) 
b) attentiveness (including during presentations, i.e. NO DISTRACTED SESSIONS!) 
c) substantive contribution to the group discussions 
d) response and facilitation of group discussions 
 
Clearly being active and well-prepared will be a significant part of your grade.  Being prepared 
includes having read the article before coming to class and being able to express opinions on 
the topic, competently and succinctly, with sufficient justification for these opinions. Daily reading 
comprehension quizzes will, in part, demonstrate this level of preparation.

Technically we are using absolute grading for Advanced English Discussion. However, 
standards for A+ are quite high, and will be limited to only those students demonstrating 
outstanding performance in all of the above components.  Typically, this means that only 
about 50-60% of students in this class will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”.  Evaluation in this 
class is based strictly on performance, not on English-language proficiency. If you wish to 
receive a grade of “A+,” you will have to earn it through extra-ordinary performance in all 
graded components, and competition in this class will be very strong.  All parts of the 
evaluation system, including attendance must be completed in an exceptional manner if you 
wish to get an “A+”.

Regular Rules of Class Conduct: 
 
1. Ask me questions.  If you are uncertain about something, ask me.  It is your 
responsibility to communicate any difficulties, problems or anxiety you have about the 
course work. 
 
2. Use English.  All class discussions and materials (including graphics and media) 
must be in English.  Please consider this course as if it were being conducted in an 
English-speaking country.  Do not assume that all of your classmates are proficient in 
Korean. 
 
3. Be careful of attendance.  Remember that attendance is part of your grade, and if you 
are not in class, it is also difficult to get a good class-participation grade.  If you are 
absent for any reason, I will mark you as absent.  However, I allow three absences 
without academic penalty.  Attendance is worth 10% of your total grade, regardless 
of whether you register your absence on the KU Portal or not. More than 6 
absences will result in a grade of “F”. 
 
4. Absences for the purpose of job-hunting/interviews will not be excused.   Similarly, if 
you get hired by a company early, you will not be excused of the course work and 
attendance.  Failure to complete the course work will result in an incomplete grade.   
 
5. Be punctual.  I am strict on tardiness as it can be quite disruptive of class work.  Please 
be in class on time.  Students more than 10 minutes late will be marked absent, and 3 
times being late will equal one absence, and this is not one of your free absences 
mentioned in #3. 
 
6. Be prepared on time.  All assignments must be completed at the correct time.  If not, 
the result will be a grade of 0. 
 
7. Do your own work.  Plagiarism will also result in a grade of 0. 
 
8. No distracted sessions.  Use of your cell phone for communication purposes in 
class will result in being marked absent for that class.  This includes text 
messaging and Kakao Talk. Use of other devices (laptops, tablets, etc.) for 
communication purposes during class will also result in being marked absent. 
 
9. Pay attention to the details. Paying attention to instructions and the details of  
    assignments and tasks is very important for getting a good grade in any course.   
    Typically, all of the A+ students read instructions or listen to the professor carefully  
    when completing their tasks. And of you miss something, refer to #1 above! 
 
10. Please be respectful of your classmates and help me provide a positive and  
    encouraging learning environment.  Your enjoyment of this course and the  
    improvement of your academic skills depend on the attitude you bring to this class every  
    day.  Be positive, be polite and be kind.   
 
 
Need Help? 
Getting adjusted to university life can sometimes be tough, dramatic even traumatic, especially during a 
pandemic.  Help is available, however.  The KU Student Counseling Center offers help to students 
having trouble at university or with their feelings. They are very good at listening. They have one to one 
counseling, group counseling, and even some tests people can take about their lives, feelings, 
personality, relationships, and more. During the semester, they are open from Monday-Friday from 9 
a.m. – 5:30 p.m. (closed for lunch). They are located in the 과학도서관 307 호. Tel: 3290-4581~4582.

COURSE OVERVIEW 
 
◼ 
Course Description 
 
Understanding consumer behavior is essential in marketing. This course offers an overview of 
fundamental concepts and the dynamics between consumer behavior and marketing strategies. 
We will examine the factors influencing individuals' purchasing decisions, which are crucial for 
successful management. 
 
Key areas of focus will include consumer research, information processing, and decision-making. 
We will dedicate substantial time to exploring the psychological forces driving consumer 
behaviors, as these insights are particularly useful for developing effective marketing strategies. 
By understanding fundamental consumer behavior psychology, we can create strategies that 
influence consumer behaviors. 
 
Additionally, the course will emphasize research methodology, equipping you with the tools to 
conduct and interpret consumer research. Remember, as a consumer, you engage with market 
research daily. The ability to accurately interpret and conduct market research will make it much 
more actionable in managerial contexts. 
 
 
◼ 
Course Objectives 
 
• Understand Conceptual and Theoretical Foundations: Familiarize yourself with the 
conceptual and theoretical bases of consumer behavior studies. Relevant concepts from the 
social sciences will be introduced within a marketing framework. 
• Develop Critical Thinking: Cultivate the ability to think critically, like a psychologist, 
about how consumers perceive and respond to marketers. 
• Enhance Marketing Strategies: Apply the knowledge gained in this class to improve 
marketing strategies aimed at influencing consumer behavior. 
 
2
• 
Master Consumer Research Methods: Develop a comprehensive understanding of 
consumer research methods and gain hands-on experience in gathering and analyzing 
consumer data to create your own marketing strategies. 
 
 
◼ Course Format 
 
This is a hybrid course, with approximately half of the sessions conducted via lecture recordings 
and the other half in person. It is your responsibility to check the schedule for in-person classes. 
Course schedules are provided in syllabus, and any changes will be notified in advance. 
 
Students must watch the lecture recording and be familiar with the content before attending the 
classroom sessions. I will cold call and ask questions about the materials taught in recordings, 
and your responses will count toward your final grade. To benefit fully from the classroom 
sessions, it is crucial to come prepared by watching the online lectures in advance. 
 
 
◼ Course Materials

Class syllabus, videos, notes, additional materials, and class announcements will be posted 
on LMS. It is your responsibility to check LMS regularly for the most up-to-date information 
and materials.  
• Required Text 
There is no required text for this class; however, I recommend purchasing the textbook by 
Hoyer and MacInnis, "Consumer Behavior," published by Cengage, for your reference.

Attendance at every in-person session is mandatory. Active and constructive participation in

raising your own questions about the topics discussed, and offering suggestions or 
corrections that enhance the discussion. Your class attendance and participation will be 
continuously assessed throughout the term. 
 
3. Final Group Project (25%) 
Students are required to complete a group project. You will form a group with your peers 
(individual work is not permitted) and work on solving problems faced by for-profit 
businesses or non-profit organizations. The objective of this project is to provide you with 
the opportunity to apply the concepts and methods learned in this course to a real-world 
marketing problem. 
 
Project Topic: A group can choose one of two topics: an Observation Study or an 
Experiment Study. Detailed guidelines for the project can be found in the Group Project 
Guideline sheet (“Group Project” folder). 
 
Group Formation: Each group should consist of ____ people (the group size will be 
announced at the beginning of the 2nd week after class enrollment is finalized). Please 
submit a group roster by 3/23 (Mon). Regardless of the completeness of the group 
formation, you must upload the roster by this date. The instructor will assign members to 
groups that do not have the required number of members.  
 
Presentation/Report: The work will be presented in class during the 14th week. Two 
members from the team should present the work and other members should stand next to 
presenters to answer the questions. All teams must submit their PPT file to LMS by 9 PM on 
May 31st (Sunday). The note section in the PPT file should contain detailed descriptions and 
comments for each corresponding slide page. No separate report (write-up) is required, and 
your project grade will be based on the comments in the PPT notes section. 
 
Peer Evaluation: To ensure equal contribution from all group members, there will be a peer 
evaluation at the end of the semester. You will evaluate each member of your group based on 
their contribution throughout the semester. This peer evaluation score will be incorporated 
into the final project grade for individual members. Remember, while you are submitting one 
work for the group project, scores can vary among individual members based on peer 
evaluations. Download the "Peer Evaluation" sheet from the "Group Project" folder and 
submit it on the last day of the presentation. 
 
Audience Evaluation: Effective communication is another goal of this course. It is important 
that you engage the audience and generate enthusiasm. Keep the audience involved 
throughout your presentation. The audience will evaluate your work and presentation, and 
this evaluation will account for 50% of your presentation grade (5% of the group project

Project" folder. The audience evaluations must be submitted in class on each presentation day.

Course Description 
 
This is an introductory course on the economics of international trade and investment. We will 
emphasize both the intuition behind key ideas as well as some simple ways of demonstrating them 
with the help of models. Equipped with those, we will analyze current policy questions throughout 
the course. 
 
Key issues in the course will be:  
 
 The Gains from Trade 
 What Explains the Pattern of Trade and Factor Movements  
 Trade Policy and Protectionism 
 Foreign Direct Investment 
 Globalization: Winners and Losers 
 
 
Prerequisites 
 
 Intermediate Micro economics is a prerequisite for this course.  
 
Required Reading 
 
 Chong-Hyun Nam and Hongshik Lee (abbreviated as N&L), International Economics, 
Theory and Policy, 2nd ed.(in Korean), Kyoung-Mun Sa: 2018.  
 Robert Feenstra and Alan Taylor (abbreviated as FT), International Economics, 3rd ed., 
Worth Publishers: 2015.  
 Paul Krugman and Maurice Obstfeld (abbreviated as K&O), International Economics. Theory 
and Policy, 9th ed., Harper Collins: 2012. 
 Regular reading of The Economist weekly magazine, so that you are on top of major current 
international economic issues. Some of these issues will be discussed in class. All of these 
issues are relevant material for possible test questions.  
2 
 
 
Note: What is taught in lecture is the material for the exams. The textbook is taken as a 
reference, yet I do not follow the book literally. In order to make certain problems more 
accessible, I sometimes discuss the chapters in a different order. The syllabus describes the 
outline of the course. Any changes in the reading will be announced in class. 
 
Further, also a number of journal articles are required reading; you should also read regularly the 
economics pages of the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal, or the Economist magazine so 
that you are on top of current international economic issues. Two other recommended textbooks 
with slightly different emphasis are Richard Caves, Jeffrey Frankel, and Ronald Jones (CFJ), 
World Trade and Payments. An Introduction, Harper Collins and Modern International Economics, 
by Wilfried J. Ethier, Norton.

In case the midterm is missed, the final counts for 60 percent of your grade. 
You should notify me before the exam, should you not be able to attend. In general it is 
smart policy to inform myself in case you are unable to attend classes for a longer period 
of time. 
 
There will be two tests that each account for 70% of the grade. These tests are in-class, closed-
notes, closed-books. The dates are April 22(Wed) and June 17(Wed), 2026. Attendance is required; 
you can not receive a passing grade with less than 90% class attendance. The remainder of 30% 
of the grade is determined by homework and paper presentation.  
 
 
Organization 
 
This primary means of communication outside the classroom will be by Blackboard. All

1.
Course Description
Among various definition of economics, we can find one common theme if we boil down them: “Economics
is the study of how societies use scarce resources to produce valuable goods and services and distribute them
among different individuals.” Upon this definition, economics is divided into two major sub-fields, microe-
conomics and macroeconomics. This course provides an introduction to microeconomics, which attempts to
understand the behavior of individual entities such as households, firms, and government in the market econ-
omy. Consistent with the idea of a “principles” class, we will focus on a core set of fundamental concepts
that help understand various microeconomic topics such as scarcity and choice, opportunity cost, marginal
thinking (analysis), supply and demand, market equilibrium (efficiency and welfare), market failure (exter-
nalities and public goods), production and costs (firm’s behavior), market structure (forms of competition
and strategic behavior), and applying these concepts to real-world issues likes taxes and trade.

4.
Course Objective
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to have new insights on the economic phenomena you
see in the media. In other words, it will give you insights into the world of business and help you understand
the world of economics in which you participate every day. In addition, since this course is a prerequisite of
some upper level courses in business and economics, it will help students succeed in those courses.
5.
Teaching and Learning Methods
This class will be operated by a combination of lectures, online practice questions, in-class quizzes, assign-
ments, and exams. For successful completion of this course, class attendance will be an integral part of this
course and reviewing class materials, solving practice questions and completing assignments will be helpful
for your understanding.
6.
Grading Assessment
• Attendance (5%): During this semester, we will likely have 29 classes, excluding exam days. Atten-
dance will be expected and taken in each class via the Learning Management System (LMS), Learn-
ingX.
– If you attend more than 90%, you will receive full credits, i.e., 5 points. Otherwise, you will
lose some points according to your attendance rate. For instance, if your attendance rate is 93%,
it is worth 5 points, but is worth 4.25 points in case of 85%. Two tardiness are equivalent to one
absence.
– No grade will be given for 1/3 or more absences, except for excused absences, which require
at least 1/2 actual attendance.
– In case of fraudulent attendance check such as proxy or false attendance, you will lose 2 points
for each academic misconduct. To protect fairness, I will randomly check your “physical”
presence during the semester.
– Reasonable grounds must be presented when requesting an official absence due to illness. Simple
medical records, such as medical certificates without explanatory notes from a doctor, will not
be accepted as supporting documentation.
• Online Practice questions (10%): You are supposed to take the online practice questions con-
cerning selected chapters on your own. This process will help you understand the contents of class
and prepare the exams. Specifically, multiple attempts will be allowed for the selected chapters before
their deadline - midterm or final exams. Among your attempts, maximum score will be recorded.
Then, your average performance — the number of questions you answered correctly out of the total
questions provided across all chapters — will be converted into points. If your average percentage is

This course is designed for undergraduate students and provides a comprehensive 
introduction to econometric analysis for applied economic research. Students will learn 
fundamental econometric techniques used to analyze economic data and to assess 
economic model and relationships. The course covers topics including data description 
and exploratory data analysis; linear regression models and statistical inference; 
structural change and analysis of variance; model specification and issues related to 
high-dimensional and big data; selected machine learning methods, such as random 
forests and related learning algorithms; discrete choice models; panel data analysis; 
dynamic models and forecasting; and econometric methods for policy evaluation. 
 
This course emphasizes practical applications of econometric methods using real-world 
data. Accordingly, students are expected to develop proficiency in econometric software 
and to engage in computational experiments. For empirical analysis, students will 
receive instruction in econometric computing using one or more statistical software 
packages, such as Stata, EViews, or R. The teaching assistant (TA) will provide 
guidance and support in the use of these software tools. 
 
Class assignments and quizzes will be distributed approximately every two weeks. 
These assignments will include both analytical problem-solving exercises and empirical 
projects. All assignments will be graded by the teaching assistant and subsequently 
reviewed in class. Empirical projects are designed to develop students’ ability to 
conduct applied econometric analysis. Selected projects will be presented in class, and 
presentations will be eligible for extra credit. Class attendance and active participation 
will be taken into account in the final course grade.

평가방법설명
(일부)강의는 세 명의 교수가 팀티칭으로 한 강의를 담당하며 각 교
수의 강의 부분이 완료되면 해당부분에 대한 평가를 강의 교수의 
주관 하에 실시 (시험 일시 및 장소의 지정, 시험 문제의 출제, 출제 
유형의 결정, 시험 답안의 채점, 최종 학점의 전산 입력 등 평가에 
관한 모든 사항을 강의 교수 책임 하에 진행함) (3차례 시험/한 학
기) 
출석관련 규정
총 수업시간의 1/3 이상 결석하는 경우 성적을 부여할 수 없음, 단 
담당교수가 불가피한 결석으로 인정하는 경우에는 예외적용 가능
개요
 일반생물학 및 연습1은 1, 2학기에 걸친 일년 과정과 한 학기 과정
이 있다. 일반생물학은 21세기 과학의 매우 중요한 분야인 생명과학
의 기본적인 개념을 이해하고 전공과목 수강에 필요한 기초적 지식
들을 광범위하게 공부하는 과목이다.
 1학기 강의는 생물의 기본적인 구성단위인 분자수준에서 세포의 형
성, 기능, 세포분열, 세포와 세포사이의 신호전달 등 세포 수준의 고
찰 및 멘델의 유전법칙으로부터 유전과 관련된 분자적 기작에 이르
기까지 다양한 내용을 공부한다. 또한 생물의 진화에 관한 이론 및 
증거 그리고 그들이 살아가는 지구에서의 다양한 환경에 적응해 나
가는 생태적 특성들을 공부하게 된다. 
 2학기 강의는 1학기 강의의 연장선으로 다음의 세 부분으로 구성되
어 있다. 제 1부에서는 생물계의 다양성 중 동물계의 다양성과 생태
학의 분야를 강의한다. 강의 내용은 동물계의 다양성, 군집 및 집단
생태학, 생태계의 에너지흐름의 영역을 포함한다. 제 2부는 식물의 
구조와 기능을 위주로 강의하며, 강의 내용은 식물의 영양, 식물의 
생식, 식물의 구조적 특성, 식물호르몬, 동물의 영양 및 행동부분을 
포함한다. 제 3부는 사람을 중심으로 동물의 구조와 기능부분을 주
로 강의한다. 강의 내용은 면역계, 삼투조절과 배설, 호르몬과 내분비
계, 생식과 발생, 신경계의 기작을 포함한다.

* 강의 및 실험관련 공지사항 공지: 다음 카페 “고려대학교 일반생물학”
* 강의는 교수의 판단 하에 중간고사, 기말고사 기간에도 진행될 수 있음. 
** 시험은 한 학기 3번 실시되면 강의 마지막 해당 강의시간에 실시하는 것을 원칙으로 
함(학교에서 공식으로 인정한 유고 사유를 제외한 개인적 이유의 결시는 인정하지 않음).
*** 시험 부정행위 적발되는 경우 F 처리함. 무단결시 F 처리함.
*** 한학기 수업태도 점수합계(1~3차)가 -10보다 작은 경우 무조건 F 처리함.  
*** 평가에 따라 A+ ~ F 학점 기준점수를 매 학기말 결정함. 
*** 학점은 수강반 기준으로 산정함
* 지정좌석제 실시: 강의 교수의 선호도에 따라서 실시하며 첫 수업시간에 본인이 원하
는 자리에 앉고 한학기 동안 고정됨.
<일반생물학 및 일반생물학실험 수강안내>
1. 일반생물학 및 실험 성적은 수강반 기준으로 강의 교수의 책임하에 결정함 
2. 한 학기 시험은 3차례 실시한다. 
3. 팀티칭 강의 교수 각각이 채점한 수업태도점수 (출석 및 수업참여도)와 시험점수를 합
산하여 상대평가 한다. 
4. 결시하는 경우(공식 유고 사유를 제외한 개인적 사유 불인정), 유고증빙서 제출 시 한 
차례에 한해서 출석 인정할 수 있다. 일반생물학 실험은 결석하는 경우 반드시 유고 증
빙서를 제출해야만 출석으로 인정한다. 
* 강의 및 실험관련 공지사항은 일반생물학카페 참고: 다음 카페 “고려대학교 일반생물학”

Course overview 
Strategic planning is getting more important as a tool of mission/vision development and organization 
management not only in private firms but also in public organizations. Due to the recent technological 
development and increasing participation of the general public, public policy environment has substantially 
changed, which demands public organizations think more strategically and plan systematically. In this vein, 
it is necessary for students to learn basic tools of strategic planning, such as mission state development, 
environment analysis, and understanding management and organizational issues in implementing strategic 
planning. 
 
Course coverage and learning objectives 
The overall objective of this class to increase students’ abilities as individuals and in groups to think, act, and 
learn strategically, where these latter terms are defined as follows. 
l 
Strategic thinking is thinking in context about how to pursue purposes or achieve goals. This also 
includes thinking about what the context is and how it might or should be changed; what the 
purposes are or should be; and what capabilities or competencies will or might be needed, and how 
they might be used, to achieve the purposes. · 
l 
Strategic acting is acting in context in light of future consequences to achieve purposes and/or to 
facilitate learning.  
l 
Strategic learning is any change in a system (which could be an individual) that by adapting it better 
to its environment produces a more or less permanent change in its capacity to pursue its purposes. 
More in detail, this class expects that students would be able to learn: 
 • Critically analyze a strategic plan 
 • Understand the appropriate use of group facilitation processes for strategic planning 
 • Conduct an organizational and environmental assessment 
 • Develop mission, vision, and values statements  
• Develop strategies to achieve the vision. 
 
Prerequisites 
This class requires no prior knowledge.  
 
Required Text 
Bryson, JM. (2011) Strategic Planning for Public and Nonprofit Organizations, 5th Ed. Wiley 
 
Grades  
Your grade will be determined by class attendance and participation (10%), assignment (20%), midterm 
exam(or paper) (40%), final (group) presentation (30%). Your attendance and participation will be evaluated 
based on attendance records and the overall contribution to the class, including answering questions in class 
when called upon and being able to discuss assigned readings. Midterm and final will mainly focus on the 
evaluation of your overall grasp of strategic planning, case analysis ability and policy development case.  
 
Course Requirements and Grading Policy  
In this course, it is expected that students will spend a minimum of forty-five hours for each unit of credit 
(normally three hours per week), including preparing for class, participating in course activities, completing 
assignments, and so on.

COURSE GOALS 
 
This course uses (1) case analysis and (2) marketing analytics to provide students with practical 
experience in making marketing strategy decisions. Students perform a series of case analyses, 
learning analytical frameworks that guide effective marketing strategy decisions. 
• 
Topics include market segmentation, targeting, and positioning, as well as decisions 
related to pricing, distribution, and communications. 
Students will also engage in marketing analytics, applying data analysis techniques to derive 
insights and support strategic decision-making. The focus is on interpreting and leveraging data to 
address real-world marketing challenges, emphasizing the role of analytics in shaping marketing 
strategies. 
• 
This approach allows students to appreciate the connections between data-driven 
decision-making and marketing performance and to develop strategies that are 
responsive to changing market conditions. 
• 
The topics include pricing strategy, customer segmentation, demand forecasting, and 
measuring customer lifetime value. 
In summary, the course is focused on developing your analytical skills and enhancing your ability 
as a strategic decision-maker 
 
 
LEARNING OBJECTIVES 
After completing the course, students will be equipped with the knowledge and skills to: 
• 
Integrate concepts from marketing and data analytics to perform a comprehensive 
analysis of an organization’s performance in the marketplace. 
BUSS369 MARKETING CASE ANALYSIS 
• 
Apply a variety of data-driven analytical approaches to inform and guide marketing 
strategy decisions across diverse market conditions. 
• 
Strengthen teamwork and communication skills through case discussions, collaborative 
projects, and team-based decision-making exercises. 
• 
Gain a deep understanding of the complexities and challenges faced by the marketing 
function in real-world scenarios

BUSS369 MARKETING CASE ANALYSIS 
 
TEACHING & LEARNING ACTIVITIES 
 
 
1. Case Analysis: 
• 
Case classes focus on class discussion of your analysis and decision-making process. These 
sessions are designed to help you develop the skills needed to analyze real-world business 
information and make strategic decisions as a manager. In each case, you will assume the 
role of a decision-maker, applying the course concepts to evaluate the information provided. 
You will identify key issues, analyze the data, and propose what you believe is the best course 
of action. During class discussions, you will have the opportunity to present and debate your 
decisions with your peers. While I may occasionally present alternative approaches to solving 
the problem, you are responsible for analysis and decision-making. To maximize your 
learning, you must come to class prepared, with a thorough analysis and a clear decision in 
mind. 
2. Marketing Analytics: 
• 
The marketing analytics component of the course emphasizes hands-on learning through data 
analysis and programming. This segment is designed to provide you with practical skills in 
using data to support marketing decisions. You will learn how to use programming tools to 
process, analyze, and interpret data relevant to marketing problems. Activities will include 
exploring datasets, identifying trends and patterns, and applying statistical and predictive 
models to make informed decisions. The focus is on using analytics to address real-world 
challenges such as market segmentation, customer targeting, pricing strategies, and 
performance evaluation. By working on analytics tasks, you will develop the technical skills 
necessary to derive actionable insights from data and build data-driven marketing strategies. 
This experience will prepare you to use analytics in a professional setting confidently and 
understand the critical role of data in today’s marketing landscape. 
 
 
▪ 
Online Pre-Assessments (5%): 
 
- 
With the goal of providing a more active learning experience and ensuring that 
students have read the assigned articles and cases before class, each student will 
complete an online pre-assessment before each class to guide their class preparation. 
Each pre-assessment consists of 4-5 questions and is posted on Canvas. Pre-
assessments must be completed by 12pm the day of class or receive a grade of zero. 
 
▪ 
Class Participation (20%): 
 
- 
Each student will receive an attendance (5%) and participation (15%) score for each 
class, and I will average the score at the end of the course. Respecting your 
classmates is paramount, and I value quality over quantity. 
 
Grading Scale for Class Participation (example): 
0 – Absent or late to class. 
5 – Present but does not participate. 
7 – Participates with basic information such as case 
facts. 9 – Offers an opinion or asks/answers a basic 
question. 
11 – Engages in a meaningful discussion with other members of the class. 
13 – Share an insightful analysis using data or evidence from the case or reading. 
15 – Provides insight or asks a question that is instrumental in advancing understanding. 
 
BUSS369 MARKETING CASE ANALYSIS 
▪ 
Midterm Case Submission – Take-home (30%) 
- 
The midterm case submission is a comprehensive case dealing with issues up to that 
point in the course. You will be asked to answer a number of specific questions that 
require you to analyze the case and make a decision. The case submission is an 
individual assignment. You may not consult with your classmates or any other 
individuals. 
- 
The case and questions will be posted on the portal website at 12pm on Monday, 
April 20. Submissions must be uploaded to the portal website no later than 12pm on 
Wednesday, April 29. We will discuss the case in class on April 29. Consequently, late 
submissions cannot be accepted and will receive a grade of zero. 
 
▪ 
Final Case Exam – In-class (30%) 
 
- 
The final exam will focus on applying marketing analytics techniques covered in the 
second half of the course to address real-world marketing challenges. You will 
demonstrate your understanding of key marketing concepts, identify appropriate analytical 
tools to address marketing problems, interpret results effectively, and apply those results 
to make informed business decisions. The final exam is an in-class, closed-book exam 
designed to assess your ability to synthesize and apply the knowledge and skills acquired 
during the course. It will take place during a session in the June exam period. 
 
 
▪ 
Analytics Homework (15%) 
 
- 
The marketing analytics homework assignments are designed to help you apply data 
analysis techniques to real-world marketing decision-making scenarios. Using R, you will 
analyze datasets to uncover meaningful insights and develop data-driven strategies. 
These assignments will challenge you to interpret the results of your analysis and make 
informed recommendations to address key marketing problems. Through hands-on 
practice, you will gain a deeper understanding of how data analysis supports better 
marketing decisions and enhances strategic thinking. The homework and data set will be 
posted on the portal website at 9 am on Wednesday, June 3. Students need to submit 
answers to the portal website by 11:49 pm on Wednesday, June 10.

4. 과 소개
신경과학은 인체 전반에 분포하고 인간의 모든 활동을 지배하는 신경계(중추 및 말초 신경계, 
신경 – 근 접합부 및 근육)의 구조와 기능을 이해하고 이를 바탕으로 신경계에 발생하는 각 
종 질환의 병인과 병태 생리를 이해하며 궁극적으로 진단과 치료를 목표로 하는 환자 중심의 
임상 의학입니다. 진료 활동은 신경과 외래와 응급실, 신경생리검사실(신경근전도검사실), 뇌
혈류검사실, 뇌파검사실, 신경심리 검사실, 및 신경이안과 검사실 및 병동에서 이루어집니다. 
임상실습학생은 입원 환자의 회진과 당직보고 참여를 통해서 실제 환자에 대한 접근법을 배우
며, 병동에서 행해지는 각종 술기에 대해서 견학합니다. 응급실에서는 환자의 내원 초기부터 
주치의와 함께 적극적으로 참가하여 응급 환자에 대한 접근법을 습득합니다. 과내에서 진행하
는 뇌졸중, 뇌전증, 수면, 치매, 말초신경, 운동장애 및 신경이안과 컨퍼런스에 참여합니다.

박진우, 백경원, 정다다, 박영빈

5. 학습목표
1) 신경계질환과 관련된 필수적으로 습득해야할 흔한 증상 및 질병에 대해서 이해하고 이
를 환자 진료에 응용할 수 있어야 한다.
2) 다양한 신경과적 검사법을 수행하고 이에 대한 결과를 해석할 수 있어야 한다 (신경학적
검사, 간이정신상태 평가, 의식상태평가, 뇌신경 기능평가, 뇌막자극증상검사, 운동감각
검사, 심부건반사 및 병적반사, 소뇌기능검사, 척추천자).
3) 신경과적 응급상태를 파악해야 한다.
4) 신경과 영역에서의 시행되는 신경생리검사, 신경인지검사, 수면검사, 신경영상 등의 원
리, 검사방법, 적응증을 이해한다.

직접경험
1) 입원 환자 중에서 매주 최소 2명 이상의 환자를 배정받아 환자를 진료하고, 진단 및 치
료 과정에 참여한다.
2) 입원 환자 경과기록지 작성을 통해 미래의 주치의로서 간접 경험을 한다.
3) 입원 환자에서 시행할 수 있는 다양한 신경학적검사를 시행하고, 지도전문의에게 피드백
을 받는다.
4) 외래 초진 환자 문진(예진) 및 응급실 내원 환자 진찰에 참여함으로써 신경학적문제의 
초기 접근법에 대해서 배운다.
5) 컨퍼런스, 세미나, 강의 등 신경과 교육프로그램에 참여한다.  
6) 실습 마지막 날 실습기간 동안 담당한 입원 환자 중 선택하여 증례발표 한다. 
7) 의사국가시험 출제되는 신경과 영역의 흔한 임상표현 중 선택하여 환자-의사 역할극을 
하거나 임의로 선택된 한 문항에 대해 모의환자를 대상으로 실습 및 평가를 받고 튜터 
(지도전문의) 및 모의환자에게 피드백을 받는다.

Textbook 
Prof. Bowman’s lecture notes on Fundamentals of Combustion and Combustion Applications 
The textbook will be uploaded to the course website. 
 
Recommended Reading 
S. Turns, An Introduction to Combustion, Concepts and Applications, McGraw-Hill 
 
 
Description 
The course will introduce students to the fundamentals of combustion. This requires the coupling of 
thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, and basic laws of fluid mechanics. Students will learn modeling 
of reacting fluid mechanical systems, subsonic and supersonic combustion, as well as their applications 
to the design and analysis of engineering combustion systems. 
 
The topics to be covered include but not limited to 
- 
Review of thermodynamics, thermochemistry 
- 
Governing conservation equations  
- 
Chemical kinetics 
- 
One-dimensional combustion waves 
- 
Mass and energy transport 
- 
Premixed laminar flames 
- 
Premixed turbulent flames 
- 
Ignition, flammability, and extinction 
- 
Non-premixed gas flames 
 
Grading 
The students will earn their final grade based on their work throughout the semester, as described 
below. There will be no make-ups for the extra credit. 
 
Assignments (6 – 7 sets) 30 % 
Midterm Exam (TBD, in class) 30 % 
Final Exam (TBD) 40 % 
 
Course Policy 
Attendance at lectures is expected as active class participation. If students have any conflicts or 
experience difficulties (e.g., athletic competition, medical issues), students must notify the instructor 
prior to the class. In case of an emergency, students can notify the instructor afterwards; however, 
supporting documents by proper authorities (e.g., doctors, police, etc.) should be sent to the instructor. 
If a student is regarded as inactive for class participation, a penalty will be applied to the final 
grade. 
 
Homework assignments will be given to the students. Students will have a week (or more depending 
on the course schedule) to turn in their solution sets. Homework solutions will be collected in class 
on the date due, otherwise noted in the assignment. No late homework solutions will be accepted 
unless students discuss with the instructor in advance. Only valid exceptions, such as participating in 
competitions (athletics or academics), attending conferences, or medical emergencies, will be 
acknowledged for late homework submission. The homework solution should be original, well-
organized, and readable. It should include problem description, assumptions, solution procedure, 
results, and discussion of the solution as appropriate. For this semester, your homework will not be 
graded extensively. It will be close to the bin-checking method. Thus, as long as you complete the 
homework, you will receive a high score for the assignment. More details will be provided in the first 
lecture. 
 
Each exam will cover cumulative materials up to the exam date. However, the emphasis will be given 
to the more recent materials for the exam. Exams will be closed book and note, but students are 
allowed to bring one A4 size cheat sheet (use both sides) of their own summary. During exams, only 
scientific calculators will be permitted if needed, unless specified otherwise. Using any other 
electronics, including cell phones, is strictly prohibited. Failure to follow these rules during 
exams will result in immediate exam confiscation.  
 
Any grading disputes on homework or exams must be brought to the instructor, not the TAs. 
 
Students are expected to follow the University Honor Code, as appears in the international school 
website (https://summer.korea.ac.kr/all/src/board/view.php?no=6704). All materials, such as 
homework and exam solutions, should be original, i.e.; each student should work out the solutions on 
his/her own. Discussion for homework problems are encouraging. However, each student should 
submit their own solution. 
 
The course is foundational to students’ mechanical engineering education. It requires a high degree of 
mathematical and scientific rigor to solve even simple problems. Therefore, you should expect to 
complement each hour of lecture with at least 2 hours of personal work. 
 
If you wish to request course accommodations for properly documented disabilities, please speak with 
the instructor at your earliest convenience. 
 
Refer to the course website for announcements, homework assignments and solutions, exam solutions, 
and

HOMEWORK SET GUIDELINES 
 
A. Problem solutions should meet a few professional standards. Adherence to these standards 
will facilitate the grader’s interpretation of your work; the solutions, if neatly written, will 
provide you with important reference material which can be easily reviewed before the 
exams. Each problem solution should contain the following basic elements; 
Find:         State briefly the question to be answered and identify what will be found. 
Given:     Present the given information in a concise form. Include a sketch of the system 
that shows concisely (but clearly and accurately) any control volumes to be 
used in the analysis. Label all forces, velocities, flows, and system states. 
Graphs should be neatly prepared. 
Assume:    State all important assumptions. Use a short, numbered list, such as: 
             (1) isentropic 
             (2) 1D at stations…. 
Basic Laws: Give all basic principles, in general form, and show how the simplifying 
assumptions reduce the problem to a solvable form. 
Solution:    Avoid “plug and chug” into formulas unless you really know what you are doing. 
Try to carry all solutions out in symbolic form before substituting in numerical 
values. All physical equations from basic laws are dimensionally homogeneous, 
so check to see that all terms have the same units in a consistent set (e.g. S.I.) 
 
B. Writing up assignments 
   1. Use new paper. 
   2. Graphs should be neat with appropriate axis labels and lines on constant properties 
     (e.g., s = constant) 
   3. Staple all sheets together and hand in flat (i.e., don’t fold) 
 
C. Problem grading will be done using a ten-point scale. 
 
  10 points for a good solution. It may contain one minor numerical error. Errors in units are 
not minor 
  8 points for a fair solution which is generally okay, but with some errors which are not 
judged too basic or serious. 
  6 points for a solution with one major conceptual error, or a solution that is too flawed to be 
corrected by minor improvements. 
  4 points for a solution with two or more major errors. 
  2 points for an attempted solution, but no evidence of progress. 
  1 point will be taken off for sloppy work.

Occupation and Society
 고려대학교 사회학과 2026년도 1학기(봄 학기)

일  시: 월·수요일 5교시(15:00-16:15)                            전 화: 02-3290-1634
장  소: 서 관 202호                                       e-mail: leesun@korea.ac.kr
■ 강의 개요 
사회와 과학기술의 진보에 따라 인간의 노동방식과 직업은 끊임없이 변화하
고 있다. 한 사회에서 중요한 비중을 차지했던 직업도 역사의 뒤안길로 사라
지고 새로운 직업들이 끊임없이 생겨나고 있다. 따라서 직업 세계에 대한 이
해는 곧 역사 시기와 국면에서의 한 사회에 대한 폭넓은 이해와 맞물려 있
다. 『직업과 사회』과목은 어떻게 자본주의 사회에서 다양한 직업들이 생겨
나고 소멸 또는 변화해 나갔는가를 노동·직업 사회학적 관점에서 살펴본다. 
특히 코로나바이러스 19사태 이후 디지털 전환의 가속화와 비대면 사회로의 
전환에 따른 직업 세계의 변화에 대해서도 주목하여 미래 직업 세계의 변화
에 대해 전망해 본다. 이 강의를 통해 학생들은 자본주의 사회의 직업 구조 
변화에 대한 이해와 함께 인공지능(AI), 빅데이터 등 4차 산업혁명 시대에 새
롭게 성장하는 미래 직업들을 탐색하게 될 것이다. 전체 수업 진행은 전반부
에서는 직업에 관한 이론적 접근을 중심으로 한 강의를 위주로 하되 후반부
에서는 그룹별 주제 발표 및 토론 형식으로 이루어진다.

또한, 강의에서는 전문직 종사자(예, 변호사, 회계사, 변리사, AI·빅데이터 
전문가 등)를 초빙해 전문직이 갖는 장점과 어려움을 들어보고 자신의 직업  
탐색을 위해 질의 및 토론의 시간을 할 예정이다. 특히 최근 청년 실업 문제
의 심각성을 감안하여 청년 일자리 현황에 대한 프로젝트 서베이 작업에 대
한 참여 또는 향후 청년 일자리 문제 해결을 위한 정책적 제안에 대한 논의
와 토론의 시간을 갖게 된다. 
■ 권리와 책임 
수업 참여 학생은 자신의 배울 권리를 위해 신체적 또는 정신적 불편한 사
항이 있으면 언제든지 강의자에게 의견을 개진할 수 있다. 또한, 수업 중에
는 자발적 참여는 물론 다른 사람들의 교육받을 권리를 침해하지 않기 위해 
함께 노력해야 한다. 개인별 에세이 및 그룹 과제 수행 시 다른 사람의 아이
디어나 지적 재산을 침해하지 않도록 표절 행위 등에 특히 조심할 필요가 
있으며 이를 위반할 시 학점에 대한 취소가 가능하다는 점에 유의해야 한다.

핵의학과는 방사성동위원소를 이용하여 질병을 진단, 치료하고 방사성동위원소를 이용한

핵의학과에서 담당하고 있는 업무는 감마카메라를 이용한 각종 스캔검사, PET-CT 검사, 
갑상선 섭취율 검사, 방사면역 측정법을 이용한 검체검사(종양마커, 간염항원항체 검사, 그

1) 핵의학 기본원리에 대한 설명을 핵의학과 담당교수로부터 듣는다.
2) 핵의학과 검사 관찰:핵의학검사가 이루어지는 전과정을 환자 접수, 주사, 촬영의 과정을 
직접 관찰하면서 이해한다. 방사성 의약품의 조제, 환자에게의 투여, 검사의 전과정이 
의사의 감독하에 의료기사에 의하여 행해지므로 학생들은 의료기사의 검사 과정을 주의 
깊게 관찰하여 검사의 개념을 이해하여야 한다.
3) 관찰한 환자에 대한 병력, 소견, 검사이유, 기대되는 영상소견을 준비된 양식에 맞추어 
기입하고 간단히 briefing 할 수 있게 준비한다. 이과정은 매일 한 환자를 정하여 반복
한다. 이렇게 함으로써 핵의학과에 검사 중인 실제 환자를 대하여 환자의 상황을 파악하
고 검사의 적응증과 검사방법에 대한 검토 및 예상되는 검사 결과, 실제의 검사 결과에 
따른 임상적 의견을 발표함으로써 치료 과정에 참여하는 기회를 가진다.
4) 방사성동위원소의 인체 이용의 원리 방사선의 단위, 인체에 미치는 영향을 이해하기 위
하여 동위원소 발생 장치와 분배 시설 및 감마카메라를 견학한다.
5) 사용되는 방사성 동위원소의 종류 방사성 의약품의 종류, 섭취 원리 및 각각의 사용되는 
검사 방법을 숙지해야 한다.
6) 각종 스캔 검사에서 정상 비정상 소견을 학습하고 장차 임상에 이용할 수 있도록 한다.
7) PET/CT의 기본 원리에 대하여 이해한다.

개요
이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

이 수업에서는 인류 역사의 다양한 지적 성찰 및 실천적 가치를 종합적으
로 탐구하고, 이를 바탕으로 현재의 사회를 이해하고 미래의 변화에 대응
할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비
판적·융합적·창의적 사고 능력을 함양하고, 나아가 새롭고 다양한 관점에서 
문제의식을 생성하며 타인과의 소통 및 협력을 통해 문제를 해결할 수 있
도록 하는 것이 이 교과의 목표이다. 이를 위해 플립트 클래스(Flipped 
Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습
(QBL: Question Based Learning)과 토론 및 발표를 통해 학습자가 배
움의 주체가 될 수 있도록 한다.

Course 
 
PAPP364(00) Analysis of Policy Case (정책사례분석)

Classroom: SK Future Hall 521 
Instructor 
 
Felicia Istad, Ph.D. 
Assistant Professor, Department of Public Administration, Korea University 
Office 516 College of Political Science & Economics (by appointment) 
Email: istadfelicia@korea.ac.kr | Phone: 02-3290-2281 
Course Outline 
Overview 
Policy analysis is undertaken by various organizations, including 
government agencies, NGOs, consulting firms, and research institutes. In 
this course, students will develop practical skills in identifying, analyzing, 
and addressing policy problems through a structured approach that bridges 
theory and practice. The course examines both traditional and emerging 
approaches to policy analysis, introducing students to a wide range of tools. 
By analyzing diverse cases of policy through complementary perspectives, 
students will enhance their capacity to address complex policy issues and 
propose actionable solutions, preparing them for careers in a variety of 
sectors. 
Activities 
This course adopts a lecture-seminar format that combines theoretical 
foundations with practical applications, allowing students to connect 
abstract concepts to contemporary challenges. Students will participate in 
guided workshops, working collaboratively to apply tools in policy 
analysis. The interactive classroom exercises are designed to contextualize 
key concepts, enhance understanding, and foster critical thinking. Students 
will have the chance to review knowledge acquired in class and develop 
professional analytical skills. 
Prerequisites 
This course does not require prior knowledge. 
 
 
Korea University Spring 2026 
PAPP364 Syllabus 
Course Objectives 
Objectives 
General 
The course aims to equip students with the ability to critically analyze and 
address policy issues. Through the integration of theory and practice, 
students will develop the analytical and problem-solving skills needed to 
engage with policy challenges across diverse contexts. 
Detailed 
Objective 1 
Students will understand and apply both traditional and new approaches to 
policy analysis, including traditional and contemporary frameworks, 
enabling them to critically evaluate and address policy issues from multiple 
theoretical perspectives. 
Detailed 
Objective 2 
Students will enhance their ability to synthesize theoretical concepts and 
practical applications, fostering critical thinking and the ability to propose 
actionable solutions to policy problems. 
Detailed 
Objective 3 
Students will develop collaborative skills critical to the conduct of policy 
analysis, building their capacity to work effectively in multidisciplinary 
and professional settings. 
 
Assignments & Evaluation Methods 
Assignments 
Midterm Exam (40%): Administered in Week 8, covering lecture and 
reading materials from Weeks 1 to 7. The exam will consist of 
multiple-choice and short open-ended questions designed to assess 
comprehension and application of the core concepts and analytical 
frameworks introduced in the first half of the course. 
Final Exam (40%): Administered in Week 16, covering lecture and 
reading materials from Weeks 9 to 15. The exam will consist of 
multiple-choice and short open-ended questions evaluating students’ 
ability to synthesize and critically engage with course content from the 
second half of the semester. 
Workshop Projects (20%): Group-based projects will be prepared and 
conducted during class hours. These projects are designed to apply course 
concepts through collaborative, practical, and analytical exercises. 
Evaluation 
Method 
Students are expected to demonstrate an understanding of the course topics 
in examinations and to apply this knowledge critically in class projects. 
Attendance 
Policy 
No grade may be assigned for absences of 1/3 or more of the class days, 
except in cases of unavoidable absences deemed necessary by the 
instructor. 
Class Rules 
Make-up exams will not be accommodated. Students are advised to contact 
the instructor in the event of any course interruptions.

할 수 있는 토의·토론의 장을 마련한다. 개별 전공들 간의 장벽을 넘어 비

Class) 기반의 학습자 중심 교수학습 방법을 도입하여, 질문 중심 학습

Objectives 
This course aims to empower students with the technical and 
intellectual abilities to participate in the global academic environment. 
 
In Academic English, we will promote critical thinking, creativity, 
confidence and fluency with a focus on academic writing, discussion 
and presentations.  
 
AI Policy 
 
(LLMs, 
ChatGPT, 
Papago, etc) 
This class balances ethical AI use with the development of students’ 
independent research, creative and technical abilities. 
 
          You may use AI tools to:  
• Research information or examples. 
• Find reliable academic sources. 
• Translate individual words. 
 
          You may not use AI to:  
• Generate whole essays, assignments, or presentations. 
• Provide essay or presentation outlines. 
• Translate entire essays or presentations into English. 
 
Submitting AI-generated work as your own will be treated as plagiarism. 
 
Resources 
Materials for this class will be available online in PDF form. Students 
can either print the content or access it in class with a laptop or tablet 
(not a smartphone, please). Bring materials to take notes. 
 
Class 
Approaches 
This is an English Only class.  
 
If you are absent, please review what we covered in class. Students 
should complete homework / assignments set in their absence. 
 
To maintain a positive and productive study environment, please treat 
your classmates and professor with respect. 
Lateness/ 
Absences 
Late 3 times = 1 unexcused absence 
More than 15 minutes late = absent 
 
If you are late for class, please let me know after class so that I can 
change your attendance record to “present”, otherwise you may be 
marked absent. 
 
Students are permitted 2 unexcused absences without penalty. 
Further unexcused absences will affect your attendance grade. 
Students missing 6 additional classes (8 absences in total) without a 
valid reason will receive an F.  
 
If you are absent but have a valid reason (death in the family, hospital 
stay, serious illness) please send me the relevant document within a 
week of your absence and submit requests for absences through the 
KU portal. Absences for periods/military obligations are permitted 
within reason. 
 
Please tell me at least a week in advance (after class or by email) if 
you have a class trip, military day, or other pre-planned reason to be 
absent from class. 
 
Plagiarism  Students who copy and resubmit another student’s work must rewrite 
their assignment and will have their score for that assignment reduced

Course Objective 
BUSS438 is an introductory course on financial institutions (FIs).  The course will revolve 
around the risks facing financial institutions, with a primary focus on commercial banks:  
 
How we measure the various risks.  
 
How FIs manage the risks. 
 
What justifies the regulator’s interventions. 
 
How the regulator responds to protect the financial system’s stability.  
 
This introductory course emphasizes the application of economic and finance theory to the 
management of financial institutions.  In this course, students will come across concepts and 
terms they may not have encountered in other courses, but I expect students to go beyond 
memorization and regurgitation.  Instead, students are urged to engage in critical and 
quantitative analysis of key banking issues.  More broadly, this course will help students 
acquire intellectual skills to tackle financial problems, no matter what paths students follow 
in the future. 
 
 
Prerequisites 
This course presumes basic knowledge of financial management, economics, and statistics.

Email: kwonminsung@korea.ac.kr 
 
CLASS SCHEDULE / LOCATION: Wed (4~6), 141-1001 
 
COURSE DESCRIPTION: 
Design Studio III is an advanced junior-level studio course designed to simulate a professional industrial design 
environment. This course bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, focusing on 
the rigorous development of physical products and systems. 
Students will engage in a comprehensive "Near-Future Concept Development" project, navigating the entire 
double-diamond design process—from initial problem discovery and definition to development and delivery. 
Emphasis is placed on Strategic Design Thinking, User-Centered Research methodologies, and Technical 
Resolvability. Students are expected to produce design outcomes that are not only aesthetically refined but also 
manufacturable, ergonomically sound, and market-viable. 
 
Key Learning Outcomes: 
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: 
• 
Execute Advanced Research: Conduct qualitative and quantitative user research and market analysis 
to identify latent user needs. 
• 
Synthesize Insights: Translate complex research data into actionable design insights and defining 
problem statements. 
• 
Apply Iterative Ideation: Utilize divergent thinking techniques to generate innovative solutions. 
• 
Develop Technical Competence: Demonstrate proficiency in form development, CMF (Color, Material, 
Finish) selection, and design for manufacturing considerations. 
• 
Communicate Effectively: Professionalize visual and verbal presentation skills through design 
storytelling, high-fidelity rendering, and technical documentation. 
 
COURSE METHODOLOGY: 
The semester is structured around three critical phases of the product development lifecycle. The Creative Design 
phase runs concurrently with research and development, ensuring a holistic approach. 
1. Strategic Research (Weeks 1-4): Understanding the macro-environment, identifying opportunities, and 
defining the target user. 
2. Concept Development & Ideation (Weeks 5-10): Translating insights into tangible concepts through 
sketching, prototyping, and validation. 
3. Product Refinement & Realization (Weeks 11-16): Finalizing form, detailing technical specifications 
(CMF, assembly), and preparing professional deliverables. 
 
ASSIGNMENT & GRADING CRITERIA: 
Evaluation is based on the rigor of the design process as much as the final outcome. Students must demonstrate a 
logical progression from research to result.

4. 과 소개
응급의학이란 질병이나 손상의 궁극적 치료에 앞서 응급상황 발생 순간부터 환자의 상태를 최
대로 안정시키는 지식 및 기술을 연구하는 학문이며 삶과 죽음의 경계를 넘나드는 의학의 가
장 본질적 부분에 접근해 있으며, 그 특성상 환자와의 거리가 가장 가까운 분야이다. 그러므
로 적시에 양질의 응급치료를 시행하기 위하여 의학에 관한 폭넓은 지식과 응급치료에 대한 
고도의 기술이 요구되는 전문 과목이다. 또한 기존의 의학체계는 특정 질환 또는 특정 성별 
및 연령에 의한 학문적 전문성을 가지는데 반해 응급의학은 직접적인 일반인 즉 대중의 필요
성에 의하여 발달된 학문이므로 전 연령층을 대상으로 내과계, 외과계를 포함한 전 의학적 문
제점을 가진 모든 응급환자를 취급하는 학문이다. 최근에는 수많은 대량재해의 경험과 수분 
내에 예후가 결정되는 관상동맥질환, 뇌졸중을 비롯하여 약물중독, 외상환자에 대한 사회적 
관심이 증가하면서 응급의학 분야의 빠른 발전을 보이고 있다. 응급환자의 치료 효과를 높이
기 위한 가장 중요한 관건은 신속한 후송과 적절한 응급처치라 할 수 있고 응급 환자 발생 시 
즉각적이고 효율적인 처치를 위해 응급의학의 발달은 필수적이라 할 수 있으며 이에 대한 중
요성은 점차 강조되어지고있는 실정이다.

4. 과 소개
응급의학이란 질병이나 손상의 궁극적 치료에 앞서 응급상황 발생 순간부터 환자의 상태를 최
대로 안정시키는 지식 및 기술을 연구하는 학문이며 삶과 죽음의 경계를 넘나드는 의학의 가
장 본질적 부분에 접근해 있으며, 그 특성상 환자와의 거리가 가장 가까운 분야이다. 그러므
로 적시에 양질의 응급치료를 시행하기 위하여 의학에 관한 폭넓은 지식과 응급치료에 대한 
고도의 기술이 요구되는 전문 과목이다. 또한 기존의 의학체계는 특정 질환 또는 특정 성별 
및 연령에 의한 학문적 전문성을 가지는데 반해 응급의학은 직접적인 일반인 즉 대중의 필요
성에 의하여 발달된 학문이므로 전 연령층을 대상으로 내과계, 외과계를 포함한 전 의학적 문
제점을 가진 모든 응급환자를 취급하는 학문이다. 최근에는 수많은 대량재해의 경험과 수분 
내에 예후가 결정되는 관상동맥질환, 뇌졸중을 비롯하여 약물중독, 외상환자에 대한 사회적 
관심이 증가하면서 응급의학 분야의 빠른 발전을 보이고 있다. 응급환자의 치료 효과를 높이
기 위한 가장 중요한 관건은 신속한 후송과 적절한 응급처치라 할 수 있고 응급 환자 발생 시 
즉각적이고 효율적인 처치를 위해 응급의학의 발달은 필수적이라 할 수 있으며 이에 대한 중
요성은 점차 강조되어지고 있는 실정이다.

• 중증도 분류가 완료된 환자들에게 적합한 진단계획과 치료계획을 세울 수 있다.
2) 필수 진료 수행 항목을 정의하고 감별진단 할 수 있다.

• 흉통
• 호흡곤란
• 의식소실/의식변화
• 급성 복통
3) 응급의학의 특수영역에 대해 습득한다.

• 응급의료체계
• 재난
4) 필수 응급 술기 항목을 습득하고 관찰 또는 수행할수 있다.

 ① 응급진료와 일반진료의 차이를 이해한다.
 ② 중증도 분류의 개념을 이해한다.
 ③ 응급실에서 수행되는 필수 응급술기항목을 관찰 또는 경험한다.
 ④ 병력청취/신체검사/감별진단 등을 통하여 환자평가 및 치료계획을 수립할 수 있다.
 ⑤ 응급의학과의 특수 영역 (소생술, 독성학, 외상, 응급의료체계 등)에 관해 이해한다.

졸업역량(번호)
1) 심정지
심정지 환자에게 기본 소생술을 제공할 수 있다. 
1-1, 1-2, 1-3, 
2-2, 2-3, 2-4, 
2-5, 5-3, 7-1

전문심장소생술시 사용하는 약물 치료에 대해 이해할 수 있다.
소생 후 통합치료과정의 치료 계획을 세울 수 있다.
2) 외상
외상 환자의 일차평가를 통해 즉각적 소생술의 필요성을 판단하고 기도확보, 호
흡보조, 순환유지를 수행할 수 있다.

2-1, 2-2, 2-3,

치료계획을 세울 수 있다.

응급의학이란 질병이나 손상 환자의 최종 치료에 앞서 응급상황 발생 순간부터 최종 치료 제
공 전까지 환자의 상태를 안정시키는 지식 및 의술을 연구하는 학문이다. 응급의학은 삶과 죽
음의 경계를 넘나드는 의학의 본질적 부분에 접근해 있으며, 그 특성 상 의학의 최전선에서 
활동한다.
 
또한, 적시에 최적의 응급진료를 시행하기 위하여 의학에 관한 전반적 이해 뿐 만 아니라 응

Introduction 
This course delves into historical and thematic aspects of the ‘media technologies and culture’, by raising some 
significant questions along with three modules : (l) media ontology ; (ll) media epistemology ; and (lll) media axiology. 
▪Module 1 : Media ontology (Lecture 1-3)
The first three lectures on the existential forms of the media technologies in history will cover : (1) the days of printing 
technology and mass media inaugurated by Johannes Gutenberg since the 15th century ; (2) those of the second media 
age suggested by Mark Poster in the late 20th century ; and (3) the recent interpretations of World Wide Web and 
A4AI(Alliance for Affordable Internet) initiated by Tim Berners-Lee. 
▪Module 2 : Media epistemology (Lecture 4-6) 
The following lectures are about how the media technologies could be comprehended and interpreted in conjunction 
with the societal and cultural transformations : how the new media technologies (1) enact the human digital networks ; 
(2) enable the digital technology-based knowledge system to solidate the social rules and cultural norms ; and (3) 
empower the diverse, digitally-networked institutions and groups of the society.
▪Module 3 : Media axiology (Lecture 7-12)
The focus of next six lectures will be upon what should and could be done with the present and future media 
technologies for sustainable human society and culture.  Discussions on the traditions of dominant political 
philosophies in the age of media and social communication technologies, which are (1) liberalism and 
communitarianism, are followed by specific case studies on the (2) location of human agency besieged by social and 
institutional structure, (3) geopolitics of transnational media and communication industries, (4) intersectional 
convergence of news and data industries, and (5) by the society’s post-truth and (6) post-human transformations.

either offline at Aju Hall or online. Please check the very last digit of your KU registration 
number (Group 1, 2) and remember the days when you must attend the class offline.
▪SMART CLASS : For all the classes, smart attendance policy is adopted. It fully is class 
attendants’ responsibility to check your own attendance (2 points each class) : 90% 
participation rate means a full attendance. (Inquiries to class TA)
▪FLIPPED CLASS : This is a flipped class : essential reading resources and discussion 
subjects for each lecture will be delivered through LMS before the class.  All the students 
should take part in the LMS-based classroom discussion of around 150 words as to the 
given subject one day before the class day every week. Delayed submission will not be 
counted, and both offline and online classroom activities will be counted as bonus points. 
Learning by thinking, expressing and sharing before, during and after the class hours is 
the ultimate goal of this course. (one point each submission and one point each activity)

강의개요: 발생공학은 인체 안에서 난자와 정자의 형성과정 (gametogenesis), 수정 (fertilization), 그리고
수정 후 인체의 각종 장기를 형성하는 과정 (organogenesis)을 세포수준 및 분자수준에서 이해하는 것을
목표로 함. 본 코스에서는 1) Oogenesis & Spermatogenesis, 2) Fertilization and activation of the
oocyte. 3) Morphogenesis: the creation of embryonic structure. 4) Pattern formation: the creation
of embryonic pattern and early neurogenesis. 5) Differential regulation of gene expression를
중점적으로 강의하며, 특히 ”인간 수정란의 초기발생“에 초점을 맞추어 강의를 진행함. 더불어 발생학에 기초를
둔 최신 생명공학 분야 중 1) 동물복제, 2) 체외수정/시험관아기, 3) 형질전환동물, 4) 줄기세포를 이용한
조직재생 및 신약개발, 4가지 관련분야에 대하여 수업진도 및 상황이 허락할 경우, 각 분야별 권위자의
초청강연을 통하여 실질적인 생명공학분야에 발생학의 활용을 체험하도록 함.

: Human Embryology and Developmental Biology by Bruce M. Carlson, Mosby,  : Chapter 1 ~ 6
(early embryonic development). 매주 강의자료는 강의자료실에 업로드 함
참고문헌:
1) Developmental Biology by Scott F, Gilbert, Sinauer Associates. 
2) A Practical Guide to Developmental Biology by Gibbs, Melissa A., Oxford Univ Press.
3) Manipulating Mouse Embryo by Nagy, Andras et al., 3rd edt, Cold Spring Harbor Labratory
Press.
4) Principles of Developmental Biology by Fred H. Wilt & Sarah Hake, W W Norton & Co Inc.

: 최종성적은 출석 (10%) + 중간고사 (30%) + 기말고사 (50%) + 팀별 과제 (10%)으로 산출함.
: 시험성적은 일정 수준의 좋은 점수를 취득하였음에도 불구하고, 상대평가에 의한 불이익을 받는 일이 없도록
절대평가 함. 
: 팀별과제는 상기 4가지 응용분야에 대한 조사 및 PPT 요약 (발표는 없음)

권위자분들을 초청함으로서, 각 분야의 개요 및 최신 동향에 대한 강연을 통해 발생공학의 생명공학적 활용을

강의 소개
본 강의는 현대자동차와 고려대학교 경영대학이 산학 협동 철학에 기초하여 개설한 과정입니다. 마케팅 전략에 대한 이론의 리뷰와 케이스 사전 조사를 비롯, 자동차산업과 경영현장에서의 마케팅 이슈에 대한 심층 토론, 현대자동차 그룹실무진들의 현장경험을 바탕으로 한 강의 및 자체 프로젝트 수행이 주가 되는 수업입니다. 실제 마케팅 의사결정이 어떻게 이루어지는지 학습하고, 현장 전문가들의 이야기를 바탕으로 미래를 고민하고 글로벌 시장 전략수립을 준비하는 기업 의사결정자로서의 역할을 경험함으로써 전문경영인의 자질을 함양하는데 목적을 두고 있습니다.
실무자 특강을 듣고 차후에 이해를 도모하는 방식의 수업이 아니고 사전에 자동차산업 그리고 산업을 둘러싸고 있는 환경의 변화에 대한 철저한 사전 조사와 탐구를 위한 과제를 수행하고, 자체 발표와 토론을 통해 의문점과 자체 가설을 도출한 다음, 현장 의사결정자의 실무적 지식을 반영하여 실증하는 방식의 학습을 하는 수업입니다. 
특전: 인턴십 부여 - 전체 학기를 마치고 나면, 담당교수가 추천한 학생 O 명에 대해 현대자동차에서 4주간 인턴으로 근무하는 기회가 주어집니다. (이 인턴은 학점이 부여되거나, 채용과 연계되지는 않습니다.)

1. 강의 목표 및 개요
이 수업은 사회학과 신입생을 위해 개설된 사회학과 교과목이다. 각 주의 주제와 관련된 읽을거리를 제공하며 수업에서의 강의와 토론을 통해 사회학의 전반적인 분과영역에 대한 학습기회를 갖는 것을 목표로 한다.
이 수업은 두 가지 목적을 갖는다. 첫째, 사회학적 이슈에 대한 문제제기 방식에 대한 이해를 높인다. 둘째, 사회학과 교수진의 연구관심을 조망함으로써 고려대학교 사회학과의 학문적 내용과 지향을 익히는 안내 역할을 한다. 신입생들의 학과 적응과 전공에 대한 관심을 높이는 데 기여한다.
