COURSE DESCRIPTION AND OBJECTIVES:
This course aims to develop students’ academic English proficiency and communicative competence required for university-level study. The course is conducted using academic content to strengthen students’ overall English ability applicable across a range of academic disciplines. Emphasis is placed on practical communication skills through a variety of task-based and interactive activities designed to help students use English effectively in academic and real-life contexts.
Students will also engage with a variety of academic texts to improve reading comprehension skills and to develop an understanding of English expressions related to their fields of study.
We will achieve these goals through a combination of practical activities, in-class assignments, and mini-lectures. This is a list of the core activities and skills we will focus on:
Discussion skills for academic purposes.
Research skills necessary for academic writing and discussion. 
Developing ideas for writing and discussion through conversation, discussion, brainstorming and freewriting.
Learning how to write a basic academic essay with citations, and how to avoid plagiarism.
Expanding upon your current level of academic vocabulary. 
Developing your public speaking skills/presentation skills.
ASSESSMENT: 
Your final grade will be based upon your results from a combination of the following: 
The standard scale for grading is as follows:
ACTIVE PARTICIPATION is:
Willingly taking part in all class activities
Showing interest and motivation to share your ideas, thoughts, feelings, and questions
Completing classwork on time
Examples of active participation include:
Volunteering to answer questions
Asking questions by raising your hand
Speaking actively in group work
Staying awake and attentive during class
Following classroom rules
REGULAR ATTENDANCE is required.
Please note that while you may miss up to 3 classes without penalty, missing 10 or more classes will result in an automatic failing grade, regardless of performance in other areas.
The semester consists of 16 weeks, and we must meet for a minimum of 15 weeks—this means we will meet 30 times in total.
Midterm and final exams (or exam-related assignments/quizzes) each count as one class session.
We are required to make up any missed classes to ensure we reach the 30 required meetings. This includes cancellations due to public holidays, teacher illness, or other disruptions.
My absence/lateness policy (5% of your overall grade): 
You are allowed 3 absences for any reason without penalty. Starting with the 4th absence, you will begin to lose attendance points. If you have a valid reason (see examples below), you must contact me and make arrangements to recover your lost points. 
Regardless of the reason, you are responsible for finding out what homework, quizzes, tests, announcements, or in-class work you missed—and you must complete the missed work. I understand that special situations may arise, but even in those cases, you are still responsible for making up missed work. Please talk to me or a classmate to find out what you missed. Important information—like deadline changes, handouts, or quiz details—is often given in class.
Being absent is not an excuse for turning in homework late or being unprepared for future classes. If you experience an emergency, I will be understanding—but you must speak with me personally to discuss the situation.
Officially excused absences (e.g., military check-ups, a family member’s funeral, etc.) must be supported by official documentation or must be registered online if required. Please make every effort to notify me in advance. If that's not possible, let me know as soon as you can afterward.
ELECTRONIC EMAIL 
Always include the following information in the subject line of your email: 
Your full name, Your student ID number, Our class name (number)
When sending assignments or documents, always use Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx) — do not use HWP (Hangul Word Processor). Most foreign professors (including me) prefer and appreciate Microsoft Word files because they are more accessible and compatible.
My email address is: laramanuel@hotmail.com (do not write lala by accident)
CLASSROOM MATERIALS
You will need access to Microsoft Word for the writing portion of our class. I do not accept HWP documents. There is no single book which can meet the needs of students whose English language levels and learning styles vary considerably. For this reason, we will use a combination of materials and handouts which I will upload to the LMS as needed.
CLASSROOM RULES AND FINAL COMMENTS
Important: a major goal of this class is to help you become a competent, independent learner. After completing this course, you should be able to continue developing your English through self-study and independent learning.
Participation: Often you will be expected to work in pairs or in small groups. Participation includes arriving on time, being prepared (bringing your book, notebook, handouts, and other required materials), listening attentively, interacting with your classmates and teacher, actively engaging in class activities, completing assignments thoroughly and on time, and asking questions when you don’t understand.
Speaking Korean: In most cases, speaking Korean in class is unnecessary. You will lose participation points if you speak Korean without permission. That said, I do allow Korean when helping classmates understand rules, grammar points, or my instructions—but you must ask for permission first.
Plagiarism: Plagiarism means presenting someone else’s ideas or work as your own. It is dishonest, unethical, and—even when unintentional—can negatively affect your grade. Accidental plagiarism is more understandable than intentional plagiarism, but both are serious. Most importantly, plagiarism prevents you from learning and growing as a student. We will discuss how to recognize and avoid plagiarism in this class.
AI (Artificial Intelligence): AI is a powerful tool and has many benefits, and we will occasionally use it as a learning tool in class. I allow the use of AI for some classroom activities, for research and preparation at home, and for any way that you feel it can be helpful in your English learning. However, you are not allowed to use AI programs during exams or quizzes—doing so is considered a form of academic dishonesty. 
Important Note: 
Sometimes the pressures of university life and/or personal matters can cause students to become distressed, which can have a negative impact upon their health. Your health, both mentally and physically, is extremely important. There are counseling services offered at Korea University free of charge, but few students take advantage of these services due to unnecessary fears. There’s a common misconception that people who seek counseling are “crazy.” In reality, most people who seek help are regular individuals dealing with common challenges, such as:
Stress
Self-esteem issues
Relationship problems (with partners, friends, or family)
Anger management
Bullying
Anxiety
Grief
Addictions (to TV, smartphones, gaming, eating, exercise, etc.)
Alcohol-related issues
Loneliness
Depression
Fears
ADHD
Emotional instability
The Counseling Center is a safe and confidential space where you can work through your problems. Unlike talking to a friend, a counselor is professionally trained to support your personal growth and help you deal with life's challenges. They can help you understand your situation more clearly and guide you toward solutions—so you can eventually manage things more confidently on your own. You are free to say whatever you want in counseling, without fear of judgment. You will never be pressured to talk about anything you're not ready to discuss. Reliable research shows that 70–90% of people who attend counseling feel better afterward. Don’t hesitate to seek support—you’re not alone, and help is available.

Overview | This course explores the structure of fashion and related industries from fiber to consumer in relation to sustainability in order to understand the current status of Korean fashion industries. The related industries such as retail, advertising, media, accessories, and home fashions industries will also be explored.
Who Should Take This Course | This course is intended for undergraduate students interested in understanding the structure of the fashion industry and its sustainability challenges. It is especially suitable for students majoring or minoring in fashion, textiles, consumer science, business, marketing, retailing, or related fields.
Objectives 
General | The aim of this course is to equip students with foundational knowledge of fashion production and distribution systems, emerging technologies and developments in the textile and apparel industries, and the strategic issues facing Korean fashion and related sectors today.
Detailed Objective 1 | Understand the processes of fashion product production and distribution, and explore the roles and relationships of related industries
Detailed Objective 2 | Understand the current status of technology, research, and development within the textile and apparel industries
Detailed Objective 3 | Evaluate the challenges and opportunities for Korean fashion, accessories, and home fashions industries.
Burns, L. D., Bryant, N. O., & Mullet, K. K. (2020). The business of fashion: Designing, manufacturing, and marketing, 6th Edition. NY: Fairchild Publications.
Component | Description
In-Class Activities | There will be in-class activities from time to time. The activities aim to help students understand course content by applying theoretical concepts to real-world situations. Varying formats.
Individual Assignment (Current Topic Presentation): | Students are required to select articles from reliable news trade publications or consumer publications such as Business of Fashion, Forbes, NYT, California Apparel News, etc., and deliver a 10-minute presentation. The presentation should include a summary of the article and discussion questions.  The presenters should lead a discussion after the presentation.
Quizzes | Students are expected to study the class preparation materials (chapter summary) before every class. At the beginning of each class, a short quiz will be taken to test students’ class preparation. Each quiz will be composed of 5 true or false questions and 5 vocabulary questions. Only 10 out of the 12 quizzes will count toward the final grade. There will be point deductions for missed quizzes.
Final Exam | Final exam will be a combination of multiple-choice questions, matching questions, short answers, and essay questions. Exams must be taken on the exam date unless you notify the instructor in writing at least two weeks prior to the scheduled final. Makeup may be different from the original exam.
Group Project | Your final assignment is to prepare a business plan for a new socially responsible fashion retailer. Students are required to intertwine the triple bottom line framework (people, planet, profit) into the business plan to create value for all stakeholders. As entrepreneurs, students will develop a practical understanding of the challenges faced when running a “truly” socially responsible fashion business through this project.

과목 개요
오늘날의 세계는 이전과 비교할 수 없을 만큼 빠른 속도로 변화하고 있으며, 다양한 유형/무형의 기반시설을 통해 개인/집단/국가 사이의 연결(connectivity)이 극도로 심화되고 있다. 이러한 변화 속에서 일본에 대한 이해 역시 일본이라는 한 나라에 대한 정보 습득과 학습만으로는 부족하며, 일본이 다른 나라/지역과 관계를 어떻게 형성해 왔는지, 그리고 그것이 어떻게 변화해 왔고 변화해 갈 것인지에 대해 학습하는 것이 중요한 과제가 되고 있다. 
이러한 문제의식에 기반하여 본 강의에서는 일본이 1945년 패전 이후부터 오늘날까지 아시아 지역에 대해 형성해 온 관계를 되짚어보고, 그것이 우리에게 주는 시사점이 무엇인지 살펴보고자 한다. 강의 후반부에는 일본을 중심으로 하는 ‘동아시아’라는 지역 개념이 어떻게 형성, 소멸, 변화해 왔는가를 파악함으로써 동아시아 전체를 조망하는 시야를 가지는 것에 주안점을 둔다.
특히 우리가 살아가는 2020년대 들어 뚜렷해지고 있는 국제질서의 전환, 특히 트럼프의 미국이 주도하는 강대국 정치의 시대에 동남아시아를 포괄한 동아시아 지역의 개념을 사고하는 것이 어떠한 의미가 있는지를 탐구하는 것이 본 강의의 주요한 과제가 될 것이다.
학습목표
본 강의는 다음 3가지에 초점을 두고 강의를 진행한다.
첫째, 패전 후 일본이 냉전이라는 시대적 조건 하에서 아시아 국가들과의 관계를 어떻게 재정립해 나갔는지를 살펴본다. 특히 50년대부터 80년대에 이르는 시기에 동남아시아, 한국, 중국과의 관계 개선을 어떻게 진행했는지에 초점을 맞춘다.
둘째, 냉전 이후 일본이 미국과의 관계를 급속히 재정의하면서 아시아와의 관계를 어떤 방식으로 바꾸게 되었는지에 대해 검토한다. 특히90년대 이후 역사문제에 치우쳐 있는 기존의 시각에서 벗어나, 정치경제적인 측면에서 일본이 동북아 및 동남아시아 국가들과 어떠한 방식으로 관계를 형성했는지를 객관적으로 살펴본다.
셋째, ‘동아시아’라는 지역개념이 어떻게 자유롭게 신축하면서 형성, 소멸, 변화해 왔는지를 이해한다. 그 배경 속에서 동남아시아를 포괄한 동아시아 지역의 과거와 현재를 파악하고, 트럼프의 미국이 주도하는 세계질서의 변화 속에서 한국과 동아시아가 어떻게 대응해야 하는지를 생각한다.
수업자료(교재) 
교재 1: 손열 『개념전쟁: 아시아에서 인도-태평양까지, 강대국의 공간 지배 전략과 한국의 선택』EAI 2023
교재2: 일본과 동남아시아를 포함한 동아시아 지역질서 및 국제질서와 관련된 논문, 연구서 일부(발췌) 및 자료들
・수업에서 사용하는 교재의 언어는 다양할 수 있음. 독해가 어려운 경우에는 인공지능 번역 도구를 사용할 것을 권장함.

2) 5주차~15주차(10개주)는 발표 1명, 지정토론 1~2명을 통한 발표 수업으로 진행함.

- 토론자는 해당 주차의 발표자의 발표자료를 보고 의문사항이나 본인이 읽은 내용에 기반한 독자적인 질문을 준비하여 발표 전날까지 업로드할 것.

평가방법
・성적을 전체 공개하지는 않으나, 원하는 학생에 대해서는 평가 기준에 따른 점수와 전체 수강생 중의 위치를 공개한다. 성적 공개 요구에 따른 불이익은 없다.
- 성적평가 방식: 출석 20점 / 수업참여 30점 / 발표 및 지정토론 50점
- 출석 점수에서 지각 1회당 0.5점, 결석 1회당 2점 감점함. 
- 수강신청을 했으나 정정 기간(1주차)에 출석하지 않은 경우에는 지각 1회로 처리함.
- 결석 6회(수업의 1/5) 이상은 수강 의지가 없는 것으로 보고 F학점을 부여함.
- 발표 및 지정토론을 하지 않을 경우에도 F 학점을 부여함.
- 부득이한 사유에 의한 결석은 학내 규정에 따라 처리함.
・부득이하게 온라인 강의가 될 경우의 출석에 관하여
- 온라인 실시간 강의 로그인 기록을 기준으로 수업 시작 시각의 1분 후부터 지각으로 간주한다. 15분 이상 지각하거나 로그인 상태가 아닐 경우에는 결석 처리한다.
- 온라인 실시간 강의에 참여할 수 없는 경우에는 전날 오전 11시까지 강사에게 연락해야 한다. 유고 등 부득이한 사유는 규정에 따라 처리한다.

About the Course: Overview 
This survey is intended for undergraduate students to improve knowledge in international development cooperation and to understand causes of successful cases in foreign aid regarding political history, political institutions, and political economy. The course proceeds thematically. Each week participants discuss a subset of the pertinent scholarly literature, usually focusing on a major theoretical controversy. This seminar will examine the basic literature and recent findings encompassing contemporary debates on international development cooperation. We will seek to answer questions on international development cooperation. 
	Next, we explore puzzles on the role of foreign aid in economic development—such as economic growth, redistribution, and equality—and political development—in particular state building, political institutionalization, democratization, and consolidation of democracy. 
	The topics of this seminar cover postwar state-building, economic growth, redistribution, democratization, welfare state development, and party system formation. “What are the essential characteristics of democracy regarding international development cooperation?” “What conditions are conducive to the emergence and survival of democracy in East Asian developmental states (henceforth “developmental states”), such as Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan?” “Why don’t these work in East Asian Socialist States, like China and North Korea?” 
	Finally, this seminar focus on not only comparison between each East Asian state but also contrast between East Asian and non-East Asian states. “Why did states in East Asia exert high state capacities under severe international pressures, whereas other war-prone societies failed to do so?” “Why are political institutions in developing countries characterized as weak institutions, while the previous developing countries in East Asia have created strong states with consolidated democracies and stable institutions?” “Why may capitalist development in East Asia bring about redistribution, while it does not in other regions?”

How This Seminar Is Organized 
	Various materials and references (books and articles) will be posted ahead of the relevant weeks and will be provided through i-campus or online. The contents and progress of the materials can be adjusted depending on students’ capacities and research interests as well as class situations. During three-hour lecture in every week, we will read and discuss around one or two papers or book chapters (around 20 pages). 	The main parts of this course are based on the instructor’s lecture with course materials. There will be students’ short presentation, which are relevant to their paper. 	Second, each student will prepare two discussion papers of about 3-5 pages each, explained in detail following the reading list. 4-1. 	The Developmental State Model: Export-oriented Industrialization (EOI)
In the crossroad between development prosperity and disaster, why have East Asian developmental states achieved compressed development (or catch-up growth) which switched their positions from developing to developed countries, while many potential candidates for advanced countries have remained as developing countries, which have failed to avoid the ‘middle income trap’?
If there were not President Park Chung-hee’s leadership and rational plans such as bold investment in key industry sectors, could South Korea achieve rapid industrialization? 
	Does authoritarianism have an eclectic affinity with economic development in South Korea?

Overview
	This course provides an overview of some of the core concepts and works on Introduction to International Development, Political Science, East Asian Studies, and Korean Politics. The syllabus is the product of a close review of related courses at comparable universities, along with the instructors’ and our colleagues’ thinking about what basic training in Comparative Politics entails. The main objective is to introduce key questions, classics, and modern approaches. 
Reading
	The books listed near the start of the syllabus are available at campus bookstores. Those and all other materials are also (if legal) on electronic and/or physical reserve at the library.
The requirements include excerpts from many works to provide an introduction to the range of approaches offered to important topics, and to permit interesting comparisons and contrasts. Even so, the reading may prove overwhelming at times. Remember that skimming is an important professional skill. You need to read purposively or strategically, to identify:
The main question the author wants to answer;
The definition of the dependent variable, or what the author wants to explain;
The main independent variables (causes, explanatory factors) the author thinks are important;
The theory, or logical argument, that knits independent to dependent variables in causal explanations;
The author’s research design: the main types of evidence the author uses to test his or her ideas and the way the evidence was obtained.
If you are unable to keep pace even when reading strategically, we strongly encourage your forming peer discussion groups to assist each other. 
How to Write Papers for This Course
	Two papers of about 3-5 pages (between 1,500 and 2,500 words) each are required. A paper may focus on a general question or cluster of questions from the handout or on a question of your own devising. 
	The papers should be focused literature reviews with a “spin.” That is, they present a sketch of some of the major theories (explanations) and the results of your own assessment, focused on a particular part of that week’s readings. In some weeks, they may focus on research design. The “spin” component is crucial; it gives your own input to the literature, suggesting new direction, new syntheses, new questions from or for the reviewed work.

COURSE OVERVIEW:
Operations is a fundamental function in both profit and non-profit organizations. It has become more important in today’s global customer and digital networked economy with the 4th industrial revolution. This course covers not only basic concepts and techniques but also crucial contemporary issues of operations and supply chain management (OSCM) for manufacturing and service firms from global, strategic, process, technological, managerial, and sustainability perspectives. It consists of the following four modules:
First, it lays out foundations for manufacturing and service operations management, along with the nature of changing competition. 
Second, it examines the development of operations and supply chain strategies and capabilities for performance excellence.
Third, it delves further into the details of critical issues and challenges in managing integrated operations and supply chain solution systems and processes.
And fourth, it envisions the future of smart connected operations and supply chain management involving IoT (Internet of Things), AI (Artificial Intelligence), digital transformation, industry 4.0, smart factory, XaaS (everything as a service), etc., along with macro and micro risk responses. Moreover, it explores the sustainable OSCM strategies and practices of creating social and environmental value based on the triple bottom line (i.e., profit, people, and the planet).
LEARNING OBJECTIVE:
The course aims to accomplish the following three learning objectives: 
First, it intends to help you to develop a holistic and critical understanding (knowledge) of concepts and techniques in OSCM of manufacturing and service firms. 
Second, it aims to guide you to develop analytic and integrative skills and competences for solving macro and micro OSCM issues and problems. 
And third, it plans to direct you to build a creative perspective of framing the mind for the future of OSCM through deep practical learning.

Course Description
This course introduces students to modern and contemporary East Asia through multi-disciplinary approach based in history that is infrastructural. While investigating the formations and transformations of empires and nations as sites of contests and tensions between different ethnicities, polities, and cultures, we will also explore major cities in China, Japan, and Korea as the infrastructure of modernity rooted in the mobility of ideas, goods, capitals, and peoples. In doing so, we aim to gain an inner understanding of the dynamics of changes and continuities that shaped and are shaping the East Asian empires, nation-states, and societies. The major foci of attention are the inter-relations between East Asian civilizations and Western civilization since the late 19th century, and the intra-relations among the three East Asian nations in current days.

This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of negotiation principles and strategies in the context of English communication. Through theoretical discussions, case studies, interactive exercises, and simulations, students will develop the knowledge, skills, and confidence necessary to navigate various negotiation scenarios effectively. The course emphasizes the importance of clear communication, critical thinking, and creative problem-solving in achieving mutually beneficial outcomes.  

By the end of the course, students should be able to:

1.  Develop effective communication skills in English for negotiation purposes, including active listening, persuasion, and assertiveness. 

2. Recognize and manage cultural differences and diversity in negotiation contexts.

3. Apply negotiation techniques to real-world situations through case studies, role-plays, and simulations.

4. Collaborate and negotiate effectively in both individual and group settings. 

5. Develop strategies for resolving conflicts and reaching consensus in negotiation processes. 

6.  Apply negotiation skills across various contexts, including business, legal, interpersonal, and cross-cultural scenarios.

과목명 / Course Title: 한독문화비교 / Korea–Germany Cultural Comparison
담당교수 / Instructor: 신명훈
수업형태 / Course Type: 교수의 강의 및 학생들의 발표와 토론
1. 강의개요 / Course Description
이 교과목은 한국과 독일의 사회·문화·역사적 특성을 비교문화적 관점에서 탐구하는 세미나형 수업이다. 한국 학생과 독일 학생이 2인 1조로 팀을 구성하여 특정 주제를 공동 연구하고 발표한다. 학생들은 양국의 문화적 차이와 유사성을 분석하고, 비교문화 연구 방법론을 실제 사례에 적용하며, 상호문화적 소통 역량을 강화한다.
This seminar course explores the social, cultural, and historical characteristics of Korea and Germany from a comparative cultural perspective. Korean and German students form mixed teams (2 students per team) to conduct joint research and present their findings. Through collaborative inquiry, students analyze similarities and differences between the two cultures, apply comparative methodologies, and develop intercultural communication competence.
2. 강의목표 / Learning Objectives
- 한국과 독일의 주요 문화 요소를 비교·분석한다.
- 비교문화 연구 방법론을 실제 사례에 적용한다.
- 한국 및 독일 학생 간 협업을 통해 상호문화적 소통 능력을 강화한다.
- 발표·토론 중심의 학습을 통해 비판적 사고와 표현 능력을 향상한다.
- Analyze key cultural elements of Korea and Germany.
- Apply comparative cultural methodologies to real-world cases.
- Strengthen intercultural communication skills through Korean–German teamwork.
- Enhance critical thinking and presentation skills through discussion-based learning.
3. 수업방식 / Teaching Methods
- 세미나 및 토론 중심 수업
- 한국–독일 학생 혼합 팀 프로젝트
- 사례 분석, 인터뷰, 현장 조사
- 팀별 두번의 발표
- Seminar and discussion-based sessions
- Mixed Korea–Germany team projects
- Case studies, interviews, field research
- Midterm and final presentations
4. 평가방법 / Evaluation
5. 주교재 및 참고문헌 / Textbook & References
주교재 없음 / No required textbook

- 김혜영(2019), 『한국 가족의 변화와 세대 관계』

개요 | 오늘날 중국은 세계에서 가장 많은 인구를 가진 국가로 세계 양대 열강의 하나로 자리매김하고 있다. 이런 거대한 중국이라는 나라가 형성된 것은 수천년간 단속적으로 이어져온 전란의 결과라는 것은 주지의 사실이다. 강력한 전제왕권과 이에 억눌렸다가 폭발하는 민중봉기는 중국을 수백 년에 한 번씩 뒤흔들었고 북방초원에서 중국의 부를 노리던 북방민족도 중국의 번영을 지속하지 못하게 만드는 중요한 원인이었다. 이에 비추어보면 중국은 세계의 그 어떤 나라보다도 전란이 그 역사의 진행과정에 영향을 많이 끼친 국가 중 하나라고 할 수 있겠다. 본 수업은 이런 중국사의 전란을 이해하는 것을 통해 중국을 이해하고 더 나아가 중국을 중심으로 돌아갔던 동아시아 세계에 대한 이해를 넓히는 것을 목표로 할 것이다.
수강(권장)대상 학생 | 고등학교 세계사 혹은 동아시아사 수업을 듣고서 동아시아사에 대해 보다 심화된 지식을 필요로 하는 학생, 대학교양 한국사 수업을 듣고 한국사와 관련된 주변국의 역사에 관심이 가는 학생. 
기본적으로 한국어 교양 강의를 듣고 이해하는데 무리가 없는 한국인 학생 및 외국인 유학생.

You will need access to Microsoft Word for the writing portion of our class. I do not accept HWP documents. CLASSROOM RULES AND FINAL COMMENTS
Important: a major goal of this class is to help you become a competent, independent learner. After completing this course, you should be able to continue developing your English through self-study and independent learning.
Participation: Often you will be expected to work in pairs or in small groups. Participation includes arriving on time, being prepared (bringing your book, notebook, handouts, and other required materials), listening attentively, interacting with your classmates and teacher, actively engaging in class activities, completing assignments thoroughly and on time, and asking questions when you don’t understand.
Speaking Korean: In most cases, speaking Korean in class is unnecessary. You will lose participation points if you speak Korean without permission. That said, I do allow Korean when helping classmates understand rules, grammar points, or my instructions—but you must ask for permission first.
Plagiarism: Plagiarism means presenting someone else’s ideas or work as your own. It is dishonest, unethical, and—even when unintentional—can negatively affect your grade. Accidental plagiarism is more understandable than intentional plagiarism, but both are serious. Most importantly, plagiarism prevents you from learning and growing as a student. We will discuss how to recognize and avoid plagiarism in this class.
AI (Artificial Intelligence): AI is a powerful tool and has many benefits, and we will occasionally use it as a learning tool in class. I allow the use of AI for some classroom activities, for research and preparation at home, and in any way that you feel it can be helpful in your English learning. However, you are not allowed to use AI programs during exams or quizzes.

There is a common misconception that people who seek counseling are “crazy.” In reality, most people who seek help are regular individuals dealing with common challenges, such as:
Stress
Self-esteem issues
Relationship problems (with partners, friends, or family)
Anger management
Bullying
Anxiety
Grief
Addictions (to TV, smartphones, gaming, eating, exercise, etc.)
Alcohol-related issues
Loneliness
Depression
Fears
ADHD
Emotional instability
The Counseling Center is a safe and confidential space where you can work through your problems. Unlike talking to a friend, a counselor is professionally trained to support your personal growth and help you deal with life's challenges. They can help you understand your situation more clearly and guide you toward solutions—so you can eventually manage things more confidently on your own. You are free to say whatever you want in counseling, without fear of judgment. You will never be pressured to talk about anything you're not ready to discuss. Research shows that 70–90% of people who attend counseling report feeling better afterward. Don’t hesitate to seek support—you’re not alone, and help is available.

Class Description: In this course, basic concepts on electric compartments and circuit will be introduced, and then, students will conduct circuit analysis with instruments such as oscilloscope, function generator, and multimeter. In addition, bio-signal measurement will be introduced.

1. Introduction to measuring devices
2. Measurement of voltage, current, and resistance
3. Kirchhoff’s law
4. DC/AC
5. Bandpass filters
6. Diodes and applications
7. Opamp
8. Biosignal amplifier
Prerequisites: N/A. However, physiology, engineering mathematics, circuit theory, electric circuit would help you to take this course.

Experiment is planned for 4 weeks.

ACADEMIC ENGLISH Spring 2026 
Professor: Darius Goodwin, MA Applied Linguistics
Email: dariusgoodwin@gmail.com 		Office: Room 709 – IFLS building
Course Delivery Method: This course will be taught on campus.
Required Equipment: A notebook computer or tablet with Wi-Fi for on campus in class writing. Please bring it to every class.
Introduction to the Course
	Welcome to Academic English.  In this semester, you will learn valuable language and academic skills that will help you succeed at university, and in your professional careers. Academic English can be challenging, so please ask me if you need help at any time. I enjoy teaching and I want to help you do well. It is important that you feel comfortable in the class, and that you learn useful skills for your future. If you have questions at any time, please let me know. Asking me questions can be an effective way of gaining confidence and practicing your English too.
This syllabus has information about your course. The important information will also be explained clearly in the first week of class. (You can find a schedule for the course on page 5 below.)
STUDY METHOD
This course will use short lectures, individual tasks, pairwork, group discussion, writing in class using Google Docs, and presentations.
A key feature of this course is that your learning is supported at every stage.
You are given time to work on some assessed tasks during class, when you can ask for clarification to ensure you are on track. You can also ask questions conveniently at other times using Google Docs comment feature, or by coming to office hours.
You are given clear checklists for assessed tasks, so you understand exactly how you are graded. You are encouraged to ask questions about these checklists to ensure you can do your best.
A positive class atmosphere with support from your classmates ensures you enjoy learning, feel comfortable and can fulfill your academic potential. 
I will help you make a shared Google folder with me, so I can give you feedback and answer your questions quickly.
II. COURSE OBJECTIVES: 
In Academic English, you will focus on developing academic writing, presentation and discussion skills.
At the end of the course, you will be able to:
write a 4-paragraph research essay in APA style
identify credible academic sources
use AI ethically to help you produce assignments
lead discussions about academic topics related to your interests
give an engaging short academic presentation 
use Google Docs, Google Forms, & Folders to collaborate  
III.COURSE REQUIREMENTS & GRADING CONSIDERATIONS:
Grade equivalents:
A+        	95-100                 A           90-94                   B+        85-89 		B   80-84
C+        	75-79                   C           70-74                   D+        65-69    		D   60-64   	
F           	0-59
Note: Nobody needs to fail Academic English. With your hard and focused work, successful learning is guaranteed.  
Attendance Policy
Students are permitted a maximum of 3 absences in total each semester without grade penalty (or a maximum of 4 if they are all officially excused absences. Documentation for officially excused absences only must be submitted via the K.U. portal.)
Officially Excused Absences 
death in the family (government issued death certificate)
hospitalization (hospital document giving dates of hospitalization)
military service (send photo of document from military)
school trips with a letter from the faculty dean, or by tradition a document from the student council
menstrual pain (notification via portal)
covid diagnosis (notification via portal)
Please note that for academic English courses if a student has more than 3 non-officially excused absences, during the course there is a -1% penalty for each extra day they are absent. 
If you miss more than 8 classes, you automatically fail the course. Please ask me at any time if you are unsure about the rules. I am here to help explain the policies. Attending as many classes as possible makes it easier for you to follow the course and do well.
Lateness: If you arrive more than 3 minutes late, you receive a late mark. Every 3 late marks equals one class absence. You are responsible for telling the teacher at the end of the class if you arrived late. I may not have noticed you joined late. If you do not tell the teacher, you could be marked absent. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the official start of the class, you are marked absent.
Test Days: If you miss an official test day (e.g. Writing 2 - Midterm in-class Writing, Your Presentation, Final Quiz), you receive a significant grade penalty unless you can prove officially with documentation signed by a doctor (의사소견서 or 의사진단서, not 진료확인서) that there was a genuine medical emergency requiring urgent hospital treatment. The documentation must show that the medical emergency prevented you from taking the test. If you miss your presentation for any other reason, the highest score you can achieve is 20/30 for the rescheduled assessment. If you miss the final exam, the highest score you can receive is 7/13. If you miss Writing 2 - midterm in class writing, there is an automatic 5-point penalty. It is extremely important for your grade that you attend these test days. Please set multiple alarms, so that it is impossible to miss a test day. These rules need to be strict to ensure fairness. There can be 150 students, and it is logistically very difficult to reschedule tests.
Other Late or Missing Assignments: If you fail to complete an assignment by the specified deadline, the penalty to your total grade for the course is 0.5%. if submitted within the next 24 hours, 1% within 48 hours, 1.5% within 72 hours, 2% within 96 hours etc. until the points for that task reach 0. However, if you completed the task before the deadline, but forgot to move the file to your folder, move the file, and email me and there is no late penalty. 
Missing Presentation Slide Deadline: Students must submit their presentation slides (Google Slides only) by 9pm the night before their presentation or receive a 4-point penalty. This is necessary so slides can be graded before your presentation day.
Asking for Help: If you have any difficulty understanding a task, it is very important to ask me for help as soon as possible. You can ask during class, or use Google Doc comment feature, or by email. I can also arrange to help you on Zoom. However, you should ask me early, and no later than 4 days before the assignment deadline, or you may not receive help in time. Please feel you can talk to me about any problems you have related to the course. 
Preparing & Submitting Assignments: On this course, all assignments must  be written in Google Docs only so I can see the document history. I need to see how you developed your work at every stage. This helps to prove that it is your work and not AI. Failure to write assignments in Google docs will result in grade penalties. Students must submit assignments by moving the Google Doc to the shared folder. If you can see the file in the shared folder, you have successfully submitted your work. Google Docs keeps a record of when the file was completed or changed. This helps you show it is your work.
Grade Questions: Questions about scores received for assignments must be asked within 7 days of receiving the score. Please do not ask professors to give you a higher grade as there are strict university rules against this. However, if you think there may have been a miscalculation or you need further explanation to understand the score, please contact me immediately. I am very happy to meet you during my office hours if you need further explanation, or have questions about your score.
Professionalism: Bringing a notebook computer/tablet, always producing outstanding work, speaking in English as much as possible, encouraging others to speak in English, being enthusiastic and focused on learning, asking questions and frequently contributing ideas, no inappropriate use of cell phone, trying to use the language and skills we have studied, etc. 
Webcams: If we need to move online temporarily (very unlikely), all students will need a webcam with a working microphone. 
Participation: If a student is not participating in activities or is disruptive, it can reduce their grade. As this is a language class, participation and collaboration with students and the professor is especially important to achieve the course's learning goals successfully. If there is a problem, the student will receive an email warning first. If the problem reoccurs, a penalty of 2% will be applied for each incident. However, this is extremely rare in my experience, and has never happened at K.U. on any of my courses.
Cell phones: Generally, phones should be turned off. However, phones may be used for dictionary work and research. Naturally, Kakao and other social media should not be used during class as they can interfere with concentration and learning.
IV. OFFICE HOURS:
I have office hours every week. These will be announced in the first few days. These are great opportunities to ask me for help. I am also available at some other times if the office hours are not suitable. Please make an appointment by email. When you email me, can you always include your name, student number and class code. I look forward to seeing you either in my office (Room 709), or we can easily meet on Zoom.
V. PLAGIARISM: 
Copying some words/phrases or sentences from another person and claiming it as your own writing is not allowed.  Please do not copy. You should summarize and paraphrase others’ ideas and include a citation. I will teach you these important skills on the course. If three or more words are together in your writing or are copied directly from another source this can be plagiarism. Any assignment that has significant (more than 25 words) plagiarism will receive a zero. If you need help with an assignment, please ask me before the deadline. Please do not copy. I will know.

Note: This is an advanced course mainly targeting year 4 students. Selected, qualified year 3 students may be allowed into the class. First and second-year students are not eligible.
COURSE OVERVIEW
Education and health are two of the key factors in achieving global development goals. This course explores how education, health, and development are connected in different contexts. We will investigate how schooling influences health, how health shapes learning, and how both matter for the achievement of broader development outcomes.
What makes this course different: you will get an introduction into data analysis and the work with large-scale education and health survey data. Data skills can be extremely useful for many career paths. 
It is recommended to have taken at least one course in international development and an introductory statistics course prior to this course.
COURSE HOURS
Tuesdays and Thursdays 3:00 to 4:15pm in Room tbd. Lecture notes will be made available on KULMS prior to the lectures.
OFFICE AND CONTACT NUMBERS
Office Hours: Right after class (or by appointment), Room #528, International Studies Hall. Email: rrudolf@korea.ac.kr
PROCEEDING
Students are expected to have completed the readings prior to class and to actively contribute to class discussions. In-class participation is a core ingredient in this course to create an interactive and effective learning atmosphere.
STUDENT TASKS AND GRADING*
In-class participation (30%)
Group Project (Presentations & Final paper) (70%)
*Note: Alternative evaluation options are available for students with disabilities.
AI POLICY
AI is a super-intelligent colleague at our side who we all need to learn to work with effectively. However, this colleague makes mistakes and sometimes generates false facts, while taking no liability. You are free to use AI, but always with caution because you alone bear full responsibility for the outcome. Your main task is therefore to always critically double-check AI-generated content. Moreover, any time you use AI, be transparent about it, e.g. by adding a note like this: “Portions of this assignment (idea brainstorming and copy-editing) were assisted by ChatGPT (OpenAI; accessed 12 Sep 2025). I reviewed, fact-checked, and edited all AI-generated text.”

Introduction to Korean History Syllabus
○ 과목 개요와 목표: 외국인 학생을 위한 한국사 입문 수업이다. 간략히 고대부터 조선시대까지 한국사의 흐름을 학습한 뒤, 현재와 관련이 깊은 근현대사를 집중적으로 살펴볼 것이다. 특히 중국, 일본 등 동아시아 지역 여러 나라와 관계 속에서 한국사를 이해하고 그 의미를 세계사적 맥락에서 검토하려 한다. 학습목표는 외국인 학생이 세계사적, 동아시아적 맥락에서 한국의 역사와 한국인의 경험을 이해하는 데 있다.   
Course overview and objectives: This is an introductory course in Korean history for foreign students. After briefly learning about the flow of Korean history from ancient times to the Joseon Dynasty, we will focus on modern and contemporary history, which is closely related to the present. In particular, we will try to understand Korean history in the context of world history and examine its significance in the context of world history by understanding Korean history in relation to other countries in East Asia, such as China and Japan. The learning objective is for foreign students to understand the history of Korea and the experiences of Koreans in the context of world history and East Asia.

수강요건(필독)
▶ 학교 교양과목 교과개편으로 인하여 디지털인문학 입문 Ⅰ,Ⅱ 통합하여 디지털인문학 응용(COLA 173)으로 개편
▶ 24학번부터는 디지털인문학 응용 교과목이 문과대학 졸업 필수요건으로 설정되어 있으며 학교 코딩수업(GECT002, GECT003) 3학점, 디지털인문학 응용 3학점 이수하여야 졸업요건을 채울 수 있음
▶ 졸업 필수요건인 22, 23학번 미수강자들을 고려하였으며 기존의 2학점이 3학점으로 변경됨
▶ 21학번 이상 학생들도 수강할 수 있으나 졸업 필수 요건이 아니며 교양학점(3학점)으로 인정 됨 
▶ 실습수업으로 노트북 지참 필 (필요 없는 주차는 별도 통지)
과제물
▶ 공통 온라인 교육 수강소감문 작성 1회 (A4 1 page 내외)
▶ 중간고사 (학습 내용 온라인 시험)
▶ 기말고사 (팀별 과제물 + 팀별 역할 및 수업 소감 포함)
수업의 구성
강의소개: 1주
분반별 학습: 12주
공통온라인 교육 1주 (예정)
중간/기말: 2주
수업목표
▶ 이 과목은 디지털 시대에 문과대학 학생들이 필수적으로 알아야 할 다양한 기술이 인문학 분야에서 어떻게 활용되는지를 직접 배우고 연습해보는 기회를 제공한다.
▶ 4차 산업 혁명 시대에 새로운 기술 활용이 갖는 철학적 함의와 인간 본연의 정체성에 대해 성찰하고 토론하며 디지털 기술 활용 능력을 연계하여 다양한 사회문제를 포착하고 해결할 수 있는 능력을 키우는 것을 목표로 한다. 
▶ 분반별로 디지털 툴을 학습하고 활용하여 독자적인 인문학적 성찰을 제시하는 것을 목표로 하며 토론의 시간을 통해 서로의 생각을 공유하는 기회를 갖는다.
분반 소개
1. [공통 개요]
▶ 인문학 분야에서 자주 사용되는 기초적인 디지털 도구를 이용하여 실제 데이터를 수집, 분석, 해석하는 과정을 실습함으로써 디지털 인문학 연구 방법론에 대한 실질적 이해를 도모하고자 한다.
▶ 인문학과 디지털 기술의 융합이 지닌 철학적 함의를 비판적으로 고찰하고, 인공지능이 등장하는 4차 산업혁명 시대에 인간의 정체성을 함께 고민해본다. 이를 통해 디지털 지식을 갖춘 인문학도로서 향후 진로를 탐색해볼 기회를 갖는다.
2. [주요 설명]
▶ 이 수업은 인문학 전공 학생들이 생성형 인공지능(generative AI)의 개념을 이해하고, 이를 활용하여 텍스트 기반 데이터를 수집, 전처리, 분석, 시각화하는 전 과정을 경험할 수 있도록 구성되었습니다.
(1) 파이썬 기초 문법을 복습하고, 생성형 AI API 및 플랫폼 사용법을 익힌 뒤, “소규모 텍스트 데이터셋(예: 시, 뉴스 기사, 인터뷰 대본 등)”을 활용하여 인문학적 의미를 도출하는 실습을 진행합니다.
(2) 이를 통해 학생들은 기술 도구를 단순히 사용하는 수준을 넘어, 생성형 AI의 한계와 가능성을 인문학적 비판의식과 함께 성찰할 수 있는 능력을 기르게 됩니다.
▶ 강의 후반부에는 수업 시간에 학습한 분석 기법과 생성형 AI 활용 역량을 바탕으로, 팀 혹은 각자가 선정한 주제에 따라 텍스트 데이터를 분석하는 독립 프로젝트를 기획하고 수행합니다.
(1) 학생들은 직접 데이터를 수집하거나 제공된 데이터를 활용하여 분석 전략을 수립하고, ChatGPT 등을 통한 요약, 감성 분석, 키워드 추출, 토픽 모델링, 네트워크 시각화 등을 선택적으로 적용합니다.
(2) 최종 프로젝트는 발표 형식으로 공유되며, 동료 학생 간 상호 평가(peer review) 를 통해 다양한 관점에서 피드백을 주고받는 기회를 갖습니다.
▶ 본 수업은 실습 과목입니다. 매시간 반드시 노트북을 가져오기 바랍니다.

출석인정
모든 경우, 포털 시스템 상에서 출석인정신청을 제출해야 함
학교 내규에 따라 10일 이내 제출

(부득이한 사정 예: 가족상 등 불가항적 사항, 일반 사정 예: 생리공결) 
질병으로 인한 출석인정의 경우
의료기관에서 발행한 “진단서” 원본을 담당 교수 혹은 조교에게 제출하여 확인 받아야 인정 가능함(진료확인서, 처방전, 병원기록 촬영물 등 인정 안됨).
생리공결의 경우
제출해야 할 증빙서류는 없으나, 한 학기에 1회만 인정 가능하지만 부득이할 경우에 신청하기를 권장함
또한 부득이하게 2회 이상 인정을 받고자 하는 경우, 담당강사와 면담을 거쳐야 함
학교 공식 행사 참석의 경우
학생처, 학과 세미나실, 학생회 등의 공식 기관에서 발행한 공문을 담당강사에게 제출하여야 함
직계 가족의 사망으로 인한 경우
해당 사실에 대한 증빙 문서를 담당강사에게 제출하여야 함
5. 평가방법
모든 제출물은 지각 제출시 1일당 10% 감점
중간 고사: 30% (30점)
중간고사(30점): 총 3회의 퀴즈로 대체합니다. 
퀴즈는 강의 내용 이해 확인을 위한 질문에 대한 응답, 코드를 입력하는 방식으로 구성됩니다. 
기말 고사: 30% (30점 – 중간 계획안 3점 / 중간 발표 6점/ 최종 발표 9점 / 최종 보고서 9점 / 동료평가 3점)
기말고사(30점): 조별 또는 개별 프로젝트 결과물로 대체합니다.  
 프로젝트는 조별 진행을 원칙으로 하나 희망하는 경우 개인 프로젝트로 진행할 수 있습니다. (단, 프로젝트의 성취도는 팀원의 숫자를 고려하여 평가되지 않습니다.)
 프로젝트 주제는 자유롭게 정합니다. 
 9주차 이후에는 프로젝트의 개요(주제, 계획)를 제출하며 이에 대한 피드백을 받게 됩니다.  
 13주차에는 프로젝트 개요에 대한 조별 발표를 진행합니다. 
 16주차에는 프로젝트 결과물을 워드 파일, 코드 압축 파일로 제출합니다.

College of International Studies 
Tuesdays & Thursdays - 1:30~2:45pm (4교시)
Prof. Sung H. Lee (이성희)
Email: Slee7647@gmail.com
Course Overview 
This course is designed to introduce students to the study of human rights. The primary focus will be to analyze human rights from a political science perspective, but this will be supplemented by perspectives from other fields, including international law, history, and philosophy. The course will take students through an understanding of how the ideas of human rights and discourses about human rights have been structured and discussed in the context of domestic and international politics. Students will also explore how actual human rights norms are acknowledged or rejected, observed or ignored, and promoted or withdrawn at the domestic as well as international level. 
The course will cover diverse topics within the field of human rights. The first half of the course will start an overview of some basic concepts and issues in human rights studies. This will include discussions on competing human rights interests, understanding who the main actors in international politics are, international organizations, international law, and practical and theoretical methods for analyzing these issues. We will also look at the past, present, and future of population control by nation-states and issues of eugenics, discrimination, women’s rights, and reproductive rights. Lastly, we will study the impacts of digital technologies on human rights, such as how the Internet, social media, and AI technologies affect the right to privacy and freedom of expression.

Plagiarism will not be tolerated and excessive usage of generative AI technology (E.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, etc.) is highly discouraged. Currently, generative AI is an incredibly useful tool to aid with research, brainstorming, finding references, etc. However, it is my strong belief that the over usage of such tools, particularly for brainstorming and for writing, has an incredibly inhibitive effect on the learning process. Among others, the purpose of university studies is to gain skills, practice, and to hone one’s analytical skills. Excessive usage of generative AI tools is antithetical to these goals. While I do not ban their use, I do expect that your work is original and authored by you.

Objectives 
General | To understand key concepts, issues, and debates within the study of human rights and how these are being challenged by globalization, the advancement of technology, etc. In particular, the role of the State, how the State promotes or restricts certain human rights concepts, and how they balance these with other concerns will be examined.
Detailed Objective 1 | How was the modern conception of human rights developed? What are its strengths and weaknesses? In the modern world, does it need better application and reinforcement, or does the existing human rights framework need to be reformed to handle new challenges?
Detailed Objective 2 | What role does the State play in protecting and promoting human rights? What role does the UN and other international organizations play? What are the implications of these roles and how do they impact individuals?
Detailed Objective 3 | How have current advances in technology impacted human rights and what are some trends? How will the advancement of technology impact human rights at the domestic and international level?

The purpose of this course is to introduce the historical, and the theoretical origins of Russian foreign policy, with emphasis on the major internal and external drivers of its national security policy from the antiquities to the present. Having been accepted as a major pillar of the European international system since the Congress of Vienna in 1815, the proclivities of post-Soviet foreign, and it more innate, national security policy (1991-), depends to a large extent on the unfinished nation-state building process since its 1989-1991 implosion of the USSR on the one hand, and the extent to which the West accepts what are considered as legitimate Russian national security interests, and its great power role in the international system on the other.

Course description
이 과목은 학과 연구실 체험의 기회를 제공하고 현장의 다양한 난이도의 이슈 해결을 위한 공학적 해결책 발굴을 목표로 하는 최신 연구 동향을 소개함으로써, 교과서 중심의 학부 전공 지식의 실제 적용성에 대한 학부생들의 이해도를 높이고자 한다. 학부생들에게 매주 한 실험실의 탐방, 진행 연구 과제에 대한 정보 습득, 교수 및 대학원생으로 구성된 연구진과의 대담 기회를 제공한다. 이는 수강생들이 건축사회환경공학 전공의 미래 발전상을 파악하고 향후 전공 관련 진로를 탐색하는데 중요한 경험이 될 것이다. 
Course objectives
건축사회환경공학의 다양한 관련 세부 분야의 최신 연구 동향을 이해한다.
다양한 전공의 연구실 방문과 수행 연구 주제의 소개를 통해 각 분야의 해결 난제와 공학적 접근법에 대한 개괄적 정보를 얻는다.
연구실 체험을 통해 학부 전공 지식과 현장 연구 주제와의 연계성을 탐구한다.

Maintaining high level of academic integrity standard is very important. During the coursework, a particular attention should be given to plagiarism. Overview | The United States has exerted a special influence on the modern world. It has served as the architect of modern democratic systems, the manager of the global capitalist system, a fervent debater on issues of race and gender, and a villain responsible for military and environmental problems. Furthermore, this history is not merely the process of American power being projected onto the world, but also the process by which the U.S. has reacted to the forces of the world.  

This course aims to encourage students to contemplate what U.S. history means to people living outside the U.S. To achieve this goal, we will not confine U.S. history to the internal development of a specific nation. Instead, we will trace the complex historical processes through which the U.S. has become connected to the world. 

By tracking the intricate relationships between the U.S. and the world—spanning politics, economy, and culture—students will move beyond being mere knowledge consumers interested in a history of one country. They will be encouraged to understand the links between their own lives and the United States.
Who Should Take This Course | This course is designed for students seeking to understand the U.S. not just as a nation, but as a complex global actor responsible for both the systems of modern democracy/capitalism and major military/environmental problems. It is ideal for individuals living outside the U.S. who want to go beyond being knowledge consumers and actively trace how their own lives, culture, and economy are intertwined with the history of the United States. If you are eager to analyze this intricate relationship, this is the course for you.
Prerequisites (Recommended) | n.a.
Class Rules | To ensure a successful and respectful learning environment, students must adhere to the rule of respectful dialogue, meaning all discussions must be conducted with mutual respect, avoiding personal attacks or hostility toward differing viewpoints. Preparation and participation are mandatory, requiring the completion of all assigned readings before class and active, informed engagement, which contributes significantly to the final grade. Finally, upholding academic integrity and critical engagement is essential: all work must be original, and critiques should focus on historical evidence and ideas rather than on individuals.
Changes and improvements | This syllabus is a guide and is subject to change to ensure the most effective and relevant learning experience for the current cohort.
Objectives 
General | Students will learn how to critically examine the dynamic interactions between their own lives and U.S. history as stakeholders, thereby reflecting on the historical significance of the United States in the modern world.
Detailed Objective 1 | Students will learn how to deeply understand the United States as an empire and the complex ways in which it engages with the world.
Detailed Objective 2 | Students will learn how to critically understand the historical context in which U.S. political, economic, and cultural actors were situated in historical contexts, and to analyze the historical consequences of their actions on the world.

Spring 2026
Basic course information
Purpose of Stage and Script 
This course aims to:
 Develop students’ comprehensive understanding of script analysis and performance critique: including character development, plot structure, themes, dialogue, and subtext Through this understanding, students will gain the ability to interpret scripts effectively, uncover deeper meanings, and identify the motivations behind characters' actions and words.
 Enhance students’ English language proficiency through script interpretation
 Cultivate critical thinking and communication skills such as logical
reasoning, problem-solving, and perspective-taking, as well as effective
communication skills including verbal expression, articulation of ideas, and active listening.
 Facilitate the creation and communication of ideas, thoughts and feelings through dramatic presentations and performance reviews that are meaningful to themselves and the intended audience
 Develop students’ appreciation of the value of, and enjoyment of the dramatic arms
 Enable personal engagement with theatrical presentations, drawing
connections between the self and society; enable collaboration with one another, valuing individual and group contributions towards shared goals that are part of the drama practice
 Facilitate the investigation, analysis and evaluation of their own work and that of others in order to develop their critical and inventive thinking.
Evaluation
Evaluation Method
Typically, a maximum of about 40-45% of you will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”. Evaluation in this class is based strictly on performance, and not on English language proficiency. All parts of the evaluation system must be completed in an exceptional manner if you want to get an “A+”.  
I employ rubrics where students are evaluated on organization(see below), content(see below) and language (see below). More criteria will be given when the projects are assigned. Many students ask for a word count. My philosophy is that students should be focusing on answering the question  and providing enough support for your answer. So concentrate on fully exploring your answer.  This is done through research (what have others said on the topic),planning (outline and deciding on your answer), and editing (checking your work for mistakes in organization, content and language).
Class Expectations (Please READ CAREFULLY!)
This class is not like your other classes.  It is not a lecture class, so you must be active instead of passive in this class.  The following are some guidelines for conduct that I expect in this class.  Adherence to these expectations will assist in enhancing your English proficiency as well as improving chances of a good grade.

It’s a pleasure to have you in this class. Please read the following information: This course is for freshmen students. Although the general focus of this class will be on all four skills (reading, writing, listening and speaking), it is predominantly an English class for academic purposes to help you study in English at Korea University.
Objectives:
This course will help you attain the following goals:
-  The ability to listen to and comprehend lectures in English and the skill to take comprehensible notes.
-  To be able to study from English course materials, such as books and journals.
-  Developing the confidence to converse in English in real life situations.

Attendance is important. Students are expected to come to class on time. If you are regularly late and disrupt the class by coming late you will lose points from your final mark. 개요 | 고전은 단순히 '오래된 것'이 아니라 시간의 흐름을 이겨내고 우리 곁에 남아서 그 가치를 인정받는 어떤 것을 말한다. 고전에 부여되는 가치는 끊임없는 재해석을 통해 얻어지는데, 바꾸어 말하면 재해석될 만한 가치가 있는 것이 고전으로 인정받는다는 뜻이다. 이 수업에서는 동양고전, 특히 유가, 도가, 불가 사상의 원형을 담고 있는 고전 작품들을 살펴봄으로써, 그 안에 담긴 철학적 의미를 음미해보고자 한다. 특히 『논어』, 『맹자』, 『순자』, 『노자』, 『장자』 및 본생담, 『숫타니파타』, 『화엄경』 등에 나타나는 '문제 설정과 대응'의 방식을 들여다봄으로써, 그들의 사유 방식이 현재를 살고 있는 우리에게 어떤 유의미한 메시지를 던져주고 있는지를 살펴보고자 한다.
수강(권장)대상 학생 | 동양의 철학적 전통 혹은 삶의 태도, 그리고 동양 사상의 현대적 재조명에 관심이 있는 모든 학생
선이수과목(권장) | 없음

기존개설대비
변경,개선사항 | 동양 철학을 ‘삶을 대하는 태도’라는 관점에서 조망하여 고전 읽기를 시도해본다. 더불어, 고전 작품 자체를 비롯하여 그 배경을 묘사한 당대의 문학 작품, 철학 사상을 원용하여 만들어진 현대의 영상물과 그에 대한 철학적 해석 등 동양 고전을 이해하는 다양한 방식을 제시한다.
수업목표 일반 | 동양 고전, 특히 유, 불, 도 삼교 사상의 원류를 살펴봄으로써, 동양사상의 근간을 이해하고, 그것이 현재 우리의 삶과 어떻게 연결될 수 있는지 생각해 본다.
세부목표 1 | 동양의 주요한 사상적 흐름과 관련된 고전 읽기를 통해 그것이 보여주는 철학적 문제의식이 각각의 시대에 따라 어떤 모습으로 나타나는지 살펴본다. 예컨대, 유가와 도가로 대표되는 제자백가 철학의 큰 축이 태동된 춘추전국 시대의 시대적 상황을 살펴보고, 각각의 지적 전통과 개별 사상가들이 어떠한 방식으로 문제를 진단하고 대응하고자 했는지 이해한다. 이와 함께, 불교 사상의 원류에서 출발하여 대승불교에 이르기까지의 불교의 역동적인 변화가 시대의 흐름과 어떤 방식으로 호흡해왔는지를 살펴본다.
세부목표 2 | 동양 고전에서 발견되는 질문들이 궁극적으로는 오늘날의 우리의 삶에도 투영되어 있음을 이해한다. 그리고 그것이 우리의 개인사적, 시대사적 문제를 진단하고 해결하는 데 어떤 방식으로 원용될 수 있는지 생각해 본다.

1. 중간 리포트 (중간고사 대체: 8주차)
중간 리포트는 기말 프로젝트를 위한 '아이디어 맵' 및 '텍스트 독해 초안'의 성격을 띤다. 1~7주차에 수업 시간 중 작성한 '에세이 조각'들을 포함하여, 자신이 선택한 고전(유/불/도 중 택 1)에 대한 주체적 해석 제출할 것. 이 과제는 학생들이 미리 기말 리포트 주제를 정하고 사유를 축적하게 하는 데에 있다.
2. 기말 프로젝트 발표 (14~15주차)
중간 리포트의 논지를 발전시켜 학우들과 공유하고 피드백받는 시간으로 활용한다. 1인당 5분 정도의 발표 후 후 질의응답 시간을 갖는다. 학생들이 자신의 글에 대한 장악력을 확인하는 '구술 평가'의 성격을 지닌다. 
3. 기말 리포트 (기말고사 대체 최종 통합 리포트: 16주차)
중간 리포트의 에세이 조각을 포함하여 발표 시 받았던 피드백과 13주차 AI 비교 활동의 통찰을 반영한 '최종 완성본'을 제출한다.
본 강의는 AI(ChatGPT, Gemini 등)를 학습의 보조 도구(개념 이해, 브레인스토밍 등)로 활용하는 것은 허용하나, '사유의 주체성'을 포기하는 모든 행위를 엄격히 금한다. 특히 리포트 작성 시 '본인의 사유와 본인의 언어'가 없는 대필이나 생각의 외주화는 학생 본인의 학문적 성취로 인정하지 않는다. AI가 생성한 문장을 그대로 제출하거나 약간의 윤색만 거치는 등의 과도한 의존 정황이 발견될 경우, 이는 '표절'과 동일한 학업 부정행위로 간주하여 성적 부여 시 엄중한 불이익을 부과한다. AI를 통한 대필은 본 강좌의 학습 목표인 '주체적 사유 역량 강화'에 위배되므로, 적발 시 미제출(F학점 처리 등)에 준하는 조치를 취할 것임을 명시한다. 아울러, 제출된 글과 필자(학생 본인)의 사유가 일치하는지 확인하기 위해 '인클래스 쓰기(In-class Writing)' 및 '스팟 인터뷰'를 병행할 예정임을 고지한다.

개요 | 본 교과목은 유니콘 스타트업의 성공 사례를 학습을 넘어, 각 기업이 어떤 문제를 정의하고, 어떤 고객과 시장을 전제로 비즈니스모델을 설계했는지를 구조적으로 분석하는 데 목적이 있다.
학생들은 사례 분석을 통해 비즈니스모델의 구성요소를 이해하고, 이를 자신의 관심 분야와 문제의식에 적용하여 스스로 ‘비즈니스모델’을 설계할 수 있는 사고 프레임을 학습하게 된다.
특히 기술창업융합 전공의 특성을 반영하여, 기술·제품 중심의 사고에서 나아가 시장·고객·수익구조를 고려한 ‘회사 설계’의 관점으로 사고를 확장하는 것을 목표로 한다.

-1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가능, 단 출석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함

∙ [학습윤리]
-대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 학습에 적극적으로 참여
-고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서 위치를 작가하며 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐고에 정진
-교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과 약속한 사항을 성실히 이행
-교원과 동료학생들의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
-강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 학문적 지식탐구 및 미래 비전과 연결된 교과목 선택
-매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 미리 교육자료 탐독하고 확인
-정해진 수업시간에 결석, 지각, 중도 이탈 유의
-출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
-적극적으로 토론, 질의응답 등 수업활동에 참여
-스스로 성실하게 작성한 과제를 제출하고 인용한 모든 자료는 변조, 왜곡 없이 표시
-협동학습의 경우 자신이 맡은 부분을 책임있게 완수하고 최선의 노력을 다함
-교과목에서 요구하는 시험의 목적과 의미를 인식하고 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
-한학기 수강한 교과목의 강의 품질 개선을 위한 강의평가를 정직하게 수행

∙ [실험실습 안전]
-연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분야 대상학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수
-신규교육(신입생 2시간), 정기교육(고위험학과 학기별 6시간, 저위험학과 학기별 3시간)
-대상학과: KUPID > 지식관리 > 안전관리지식 > 연구실안전
-포털시스템 상단 메뉴에서 “정보생활” 클린, [안전교육(서울)] 클릭하여 안전교육 페이지 접속(“크롬”으로 접속, 접속 오류 시 인터넷 설정에서 “팝업 차단 해제” 설정 필요)
-포털 아이디가 없는 경우, 국가연구안전관리본부 연구실안전교육시스템(https://edu.labs.go.kr/) 접속하여 수강 가능함. 
-외부기관에서 안전교육을 이수한 경우 별도의 등록절차를 통한 이수 가능
-미이수 시 불이익: 학부생(성적열람 제한), 대학원생(출입제한)
-문의사항: 교육문의(안전관리팀 02-3290-2763), 시스템문의(아키시스템즈 02-2664-5354)

∙ [인권성평등 교육 필수이수] 
-본교는 인권,성평등 교육 의무수강 제도를 운영(「양성평등기본법」 제31조 근거 법정의무)
하고 있으며 매학년도 1회 이상(학부생의 경우 총 4회 이상 이수필수)
 -수강방법 : LMS(https://lms.korea.ac.kr)에 로그인하여 수강(LMS 로그인 → 상단 '[비정규 과정] > [강좌 검색]' → 좌측 [구분] 메뉴에서 “법정의무 및 교내권장 교육”을 체크하거나, 강좌 이름 검색 → 신청 버튼 클릭 → ‘학습하러 가기’ 클릭 → [공지] 메뉴 클릭 → [주차학습] 메뉴 클릭 → 안내사항 확인 후 영상 클릭하여 시청
-문의: 서울캠퍼스 humanrights@korea.ac.kr  /  세종캠퍼스 sjequality@korea.ac.kr

∙ [2025학년도 서울캠퍼스 정규학기 시간표]
 1교시(9:00~10:15), 2교시(10:30~11:45), 3교시(12:00~13:15), 4교시(13:30~14:45), 5교시(15:00~16:15), 6교시(16:30~17:45), 7교시(18:00~18:50) 이후 50분 수업, 10분 휴식 
∙ [2025학년도 서울캠퍼스 계절학기 시간표] 
 1교시~8교시 50분 수업 및 10분 휴식

∙ [전공이수 등 교육과정정보]
  검색사이트에서 ‘고려대학교 교육정보 홈페이지(http://registrar.korea.ac.kr)’를 검색해 본인 교육과정, 다전공 등 주요 정보를 확인하시기 바랍니다. 

∙ [학사관련 안내] 
  고려대학교 포털(http://portal.korea.ac.kr) 학사일정 안내 게시판을 참고하시기 바랍니다.

Atmospheric Science, EAES209, Spring 2026
Course Overview:
This lecture will explore the major atmospheric phenomena, and their related basic concepts of atmospheric dynamics, optics, chemistry, thermodynamics, and meteorology. By the end of the semester, students are expected to…
Understand theoretical background beneath the meteorological/atmospheric phenomena that can be observed in the real world.
Analyze the real-world weather/meteorological/air pollution data
Propose unrevealed issues in climate change & air quality
Instructor:
Prof. Taekyu Joo
Office: Mediheal EES Hall 708
Email: taekyujoo@korea.ac.kr
Office hour: Tuesday, by appointment 
Teaching Assistant:
Hee Yeon Lim
Office: Mediheal EES Hall 709
Email: 1206lhy@korea.ac.kr
Class hour: Mon/Wed 1200 - 1315
Classroom: Asan Science Hall Rm113
Textbook: 
Main: 알기쉬운 대기과학, 한국기상학회 저, 시그마프레스
Sub: 
Essentials of Meteorology, C. Donald Ahrens
An Introduction to Dynamic Meteorology, James R. Holton
Introduction to Atmospheric Chemistry, Daniel J. Jacob

Attendance: 10%
Assignments: 30%
Midterm: 30%
Final: 30%
Assignments: 
Team project (15%): Weather prediction 
Practice (5%): HYSPLIT backtrajectory analysis (https://www.ready.noaa.gov/HYSPLIT.php) 
Homework (10%): 4-5 homework will be given that covers what you learned from the lecture
Exams: 
True/False questions
Describing and explaining meteorological phenomena 
Problem solving (calculator required)
Prerequisites: 
(Essential) Earth Environmental Science (1,2), Calculus (1,2)
(Recommend) General Physics (1,2), General Chemistry (1,2)

Course Syllabus
EDUC 265: The Future of Higher Education (Spring 2026)
Instructor: Dr. Hyun Kyoung Ro
Class Time: Mondays and Wednesdays, Period 3 (12:00 PM – 1:15 PM)
Classroom: Room 308, College of Education
Office: Room 602, College of Education
Office Hours: By appointment only
Phone: +82-2-3290-2300
Email: hro25@korea.ac.kr
Course Goals
1. Higher Education, Society, and the Future
Students will:
Understand how rapid social, economic, technological, and political changes — in Korea and globally — shape the future of higher education.
Develop perspectives on how colleges and universities can contribute to, respond to, and sometimes lead broader societal change.
Reflect on the purposes and responsibilities of higher education in uncertain and rapidly evolving contexts.
2. Higher Education as Organizations and Their Roles
Students will:
Analyze colleges and universities as complex organizations.
Examine how institutional leaders, staff, professionals, and faculty work within unpredictable environments.
Consider how organizational decisions influence students, communities, and society.
3. Student Identities, Learning, and Opportunity 
Students will:
Understand how student identities, privilege, and institutional policies shape equitable access and college experiences.
Explore inclusive teaching and learning practices that support belonging and success.
Examine how higher education supports (or constrains) student development and career pathways.
Course Expectations
Attendance and communication
If you are unable to attend class due to unavoidable circumstances, please inform the instructor in advance whenever possible.
Preparation for class
You will complete 4 small team projects throughout the course.
I will not assign heavy weekly reading loads; however, you will search for and select readings for some assignments.
Much of our discussion will build directly on your preparation for your team project, and the quality of conversation depends on your engagement and understanding.
Participation and engagement
Active participation is essential. Engaging respectfully with classmates, contributing thoughtfully, and listening carefully all support a strong learning environment. I will be flexible when accommodations are needed; however, completing team assignments on time affects not only your own learning but also your classmates’ experience.
Collaborative responsibility
Students are expected to develop and uphold collective expectations and group guidelines, and to hold one another accountable in constructive and respectful ways.
Respect for diverse perspectives
All class members share responsibility for ensuring that a variety of ideas and viewpoints are welcomed, explored, and discussed with respect.
Assignments and due dates
Deadlines are set to support steady progress and meaningful learning. If circumstances prevent you from meeting a deadline, email the instructor as soon as possible to make alternative arrangements. I will accommodate reasonable requests to the best of my ability. Please communicate early, avoid falling far behind, and be mindful of how delays affect group work and class progress.
Language expectations
This course is taught in English. Students are expected to have sufficient English proficiency to follow instructions, participate in discussions, and complete assignments.
Assessment
This course emphasizes active engagement, collaboration, and reflection. Your grade reflects not only what you produce, but how you participate in learning with others.
Participation and Engagement (20%) Participation is assessed throughout the semester and includes:
Attendance – 5%
Regular attendance and punctuality are expected. Please inform the instructor in advance if you must miss class.
Peer Evaluation – 5%
After each team project, you will evaluate your teammates’ contributions. This ensures fairness and accountability and helps prevent free riding.
Active Participation – 10%
Active participation includes:
Active listening: listening without interrupting, respecting different viewpoints, and not dominating discussion
Active discussion: contributing thoughtful comments, questions, and connections to course topics
Participation is evaluated on quality, consistency, and respectfulness, not how often you speak.
Team Projects – 60% Total
You will complete four small team projects during the semester.
Project 1 – 15%
Project 2 – 15%
Project 3 – 15%
Project 4 – 15%
Projects are evaluated based on understanding of course concepts, analysis, clarity, and collaboration. While most team project preparation will occur in class, teams would need to complete additional work outside of class to finalize their projects. Individual project grades may be adjusted based on peer evaluations.
Reflections and Online-discussion – 20%

Project Details
Project 1: Rethinking the Campus and the Future of Higher Education
Project 2: Learning Beyond the Classroom: Programs and Professionals
Project 3: Student Identity, Belonging, and Unequal Opportunity
Project 4: Teaching and Learning for Student Success in Higher Education
Project 1: Rethinking the Campus — Futures of Higher Education (Weeks 2–4)
Students examine the campus as a higher education environment shaped by history, policy, and imagined futures. Through observation, discussion, and reflection, we will consider what the university offers students today, what goals guide these offerings, and what institutions intend students to learn and achieve. Building on what college education looks like in 2026, students will explore how higher education may evolve over the next 20 years and how the campus experience might look different from today. Each team will present what Korea University looks like today and how it might change over the next 20–30 years in response to shifting societal needs.	Assignment: Team presentation in class
Project 2: Learning Beyond the Classroom (Weeks 5–7, Week 14)
Learning happens beyond the classroom, and this project focuses on who supports and takes responsibility for student learning outside of formal coursework. Students will meet and learn from at least one individual who can speak to learning outside the classroom, such as higher education professionals (administrators, staff, or researchers), family or community members who were actively involved in college organizations 10–30 years ago, or current college students with varying levels of co-curricular involvement. Students will analyze how co-curricular programs and higher education professionals support student learning, development, and opportunity, and will consider how learning beyond the classroom may look 20 years in the future. Students will present co-curricular programs they would like to offer now and in 20–30 years, informed by the materials they collected and the interviews they conducted. Assignment: Team presentation in class
Project 3: Student Identity, Belonging, and Unequal Opportunity (Weeks 7–10)
Although students attend the same university, they do not begin from the same starting point. Resources, social and cultural capital, academic preparation, and access to opportunity vary based on background and identity. In this project, students explore social identities, privilege and marginalization, patterns of inclusion and exclusion, and how universities address—or fail to address—equity and equal opportunity. The instructor will share reflection questions, and students will have time in class to begin writing and continue developing their reflections at home. You may use AI to help with your writing, but your reflection should be personal and based on your own honest and genuine stories. Students will reflect deeply on how identity and institutional structures shape college students’ experiences, sense of belonging, and access to opportunity in higher education. Assignment: Individual reflections and sharing in class
Project 4: Teaching and Learning for Student Success in Higher Education (Weeks 11–15)
This final project examines the purpose of higher education, why students attend college, and what meaningful learning should look like in both current and future contexts. Students will focus on teaching and learning for student success by interviewing at least one individual—such as a faculty member, parent or family member, community member, or higher education professional—who can speak to college student experiences and success. Drawing on interview findings and course readings, students will design a learning activity they would want to teach college students 20 years in the future, articulating goals, learning experiences, and approaches to supporting student success. Assignment: Team presentation in class
Interview Ethics & Consent
For interview-based projects, students must obtain verbal consent, explain the purpose of the project, and respect interviewees’ privacy. Names and identifying details should not be shared without permission.

기업 현장에서 활동하는 분들로부터 소중한 경험과 경영원칙, 미래에 대한 제안과 인사이트 등을 직접 들음으로써, 수강생이 자신과 기업 경영의 미래에 대한 생각을 하는 기회를 제공합니다. 특강을 통해 다양한 산업과 기업의 현실, 관련 커리어 및 미래 방향에 대해 깊이 있는 이해를 도모하고, 경영자들의 경험을 공유함으로써 성공적인 경영(자)의 조건을 파악하며, 사회적 리더가 되기 위한 품성과 역량을 함양하는 것을 목표로 합니다.

이 수업은 외부연사들을 초청해서 강연을 듣는 형식이므로 정해진 시간에 정확하게 수업이 시작될 수 있도록, 가능한 미리 교실에 와서 자리에 앉아서 기다리기 바랍니다. 또한, 모든 동료학생들이 차분한 분위기에서 수업에 집중할 수 있도록 출석을 엄격하게 운영합니다. 매시간 출석 체크합니다. 두번째 수업(3/12)부터 지정좌석으로 운영합니다. 수업 시작 후 10분 지난 시점(3:10PM)부터 지각 처리됩니다. 사전 양해 없이 수업 시간 종료 전 자리를 떠나는 경우도 지각으로 처리합니다. 지각 2번은 결석 1번으로 계산합니다. 결석은 총 3번까지 허용되고 4번째 결석부터 전체 성적은 F가 됩니다. 따라서, 수업시간에 늦지 않게 오시고, 수업에 빠지지 마시기 바랍니다. 직계가족의 경조사, 천재지변, 남학생의 경우 예비군 동원 외 취업 등 다른 이유로는 결석 예외를 인정하지 않습니다. 따라서, 질병으로 인한 결석은 3번 결석기회를 이용하면 되고 별도도 출석인정은 하지 않습니다. 예외적으로, 수업에 참여하지 못할 정도의 사유는 진단서 제출 후 판단합니다.

Office Hrs: Wednesday. 2:00-3:00pm or by appointment
