ACADEMIC ENGLISH Spring 2026 
Professor: Darius Goodwin, MA Applied Linguistics
Email: dariusgoodwin@gmail.com 		Office: Room 709 – IFLS building
Course Delivery Method: This course will be taught on campus.
Required Equipment: A notebook computer or tablet with Wi-Fi for on campus, in class writing. Please bring it to every class.
Introduction to the Course
	Welcome to Academic English.  In this semester, you will learn valuable language and academic skills that will help you succeed at university, and in your professional careers. Academic English can be challenging, so please ask me if you need help at any time. I enjoy teaching and I want to help you do well. It is important that you feel comfortable in the class, and that you learn useful skills for your future. If you have questions at any time, please let me know. Asking me questions can be an effective way of gaining confidence and practicing your English too.
This syllabus has information about your course. The important information will also be explained clearly in the first week of class. (You can find a schedule for the course on page 5 below.)
STUDY METHOD
This course will use short lectures, individual tasks, pairwork, group discussion, writing in class using Google Docs, and presentations.
A key feature of this course is that your learning is supported at every stage.
You are given time to work on some assessed tasks during class, when you can ask for clarification to ensure you are on track. You can also ask questions conveniently at other times using Google Docs comment feature, or by coming to office hours.
You are given clear checklists for assessed tasks, so you understand exactly how you are graded. You are encouraged to ask questions about these checklists to ensure you can do your best.
A positive class atmosphere with support from your classmates ensures you enjoy learning, feel comfortable and can fulfill your academic potential. 
I will help you make a shared Google folder with me, so I can give you feedback and answer your questions quickly.
II. COURSE OBJECTIVES: 
In Academic English, you will focus on developing academic writing, presentation and discussion skills.
At the end of the course, you will be able to:
write a 4-paragraph research essay in APA style
identify credible academic sources
use AI ethically to help you produce assignments
lead discussions about academic topics related to your interests
give an engaging short academic presentation 
use Google Docs, Google Forms, & Folders to collaborate  
III.COURSE REQUIREMENTS & GRADING CONSIDERATIONS:
Grade equivalents:
A+        	95-100                 A           90-94                   B+        85-89 		B   80-84
C+        	75-79                   C           70-74                   D+        65-69    		D   60-64   	
F           	0-59
Note: Nobody needs to fail Academic English. With your hard and focused work, successful learning is guaranteed.  
Attendance Policy
Students are permitted a maximum of 3 absences in total each semester without grade penalty (or a maximum of 4 if they are all officially excused absences. Documentation for officially excused absences only must be submitted via the K.U. portal.)
Officially Excused Absences 
death in the family (government issued death certificate)
hospitalization (hospital document giving dates of hospitalization)
military service (send photo of document from military)
school trips with a letter from the faculty dean, or by tradition a document from the student council
menstrual pain (notification via portal)
covid diagnosis (notification via portal)
Please note that for academic English courses if a student has more than 3 non-officially excused absences, during the course there is a -1% penalty for each extra day they are absent. 
If you miss more than 8 classes, you automatically fail the course. Please ask me at any time if you are unsure about the rules. I am here to help explain the policies. Attending as many classes as possible makes it easier for you to follow the course and do well.
Lateness: If you arrive more than 3 minutes late, you receive a late mark. Every 3 late marks equals one class absence. You are responsible for telling the teacher at the end of the class if you arrived late. I may not have noticed you joined late. If you do not tell the teacher, you could be marked absent. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the official start of the class, you are marked absent.
Test Days: If you miss an official test day (e.g. Writing 2 - Midterm in-class Writing, Your Presentation, Final Quiz), you receive a significant grade penalty unless you can prove officially with documentation signed by a doctor (의사소견서 or 의사진단서, not 진료확인서) that there was a genuine medical emergency requiring urgent hospital treatment. The documentation must show that the medical emergency prevented you from taking the test. If you miss your presentation for any other reason, the highest score you can achieve is 20/30 for the rescheduled assessment. If you miss the final exam, the highest score you can receive is 7/13. If you miss Writing 2 - midterm in class writing, there is an automatic 5-point penalty. It is extremely important for your grade that you attend these test days. Please set multiple alarms, so that it is impossible to miss a test day. These rules need to be strict to ensure fairness. There can be 150 students, and it is logistically very difficult to reschedule tests.
Other Late or Missing Assignments: If you fail to complete an assignment by the specified deadline, the penalty to your total grade for the course is 0.5%. if submitted within the next 24 hours, 1% within 48 hours, 1.5% within 72 hours, 2% within 96 hours etc. until the points for that task reach 0. However, if you completed the task before the deadline, but forgot to move the file to your folder, move the file, and email me and there is no late penalty. 
Missing Presentation Slide Deadline: Students must submit their presentation slides (Google Slides only) by 9pm the night before their presentation or receive a 4-point penalty. This is necessary so slides can be graded before your presentation day.
Asking for Help: If you have any difficulty understanding a task, it is very important to ask me for help as soon as possible. You can ask during class, or use Google Doc comment feature, or by email. I can also arrange to help you on Zoom. However, you should ask me early, and no later than 4 days before the assignment deadline, or you may not receive help in time. Please feel you can talk to me about any problems you have related to the course. 
Preparing & Submitting Assignments: On this course, all assignments must be written in Google Docs only so I can see the document history. I need to see how you developed your work at every stage. This helps to prove that it is your work and not AI Failure to write assignments in Google docs will result in grade penalties. Students must submit assignments by moving the Google Doc to the shared folder. If you can see the file in the shared folder, you have successfully submitted your work. Google Docs keeps a record of when the file was completed or changed. This helps you show it is your work.
Grade Questions: Questions about scores received for assignments must be asked within 7 days of receiving the score. Please do not ask professors to give you a higher grade as there are strict university rules against this. However, if you think there may have been a miscalculation or need further explanation to understand the score, please contact me immediately. I am very happy to meet you during my office hours if you need further explanation or have questions about your score.
Professionalism: Bringing a notebook computer/tablet, always producing outstanding work, speaking in English as much as possible, encouraging others to speak in English, being enthusiastic and focused on learning, asking questions and frequently contributing ideas, no inappropriate use of cell phone, trying to use the language and skills we have studied, etc. 
Webcams: If we need to move online temporarily (very unlikely), all students will need a webcam with a working microphone. 
Participation: If a student is not participating in activities or is disruptive, it can reduce their grade. As this is a language class, participation and collaboration with students and the professor is especially important to achieve the course's learning goals successfully. If there is a problem, the student will receive an email warning first. If the problem reoccurs, a penalty of 2% will be applied for each incident. However, this is extremely rare in my experience and has never happened at K.U. on any of my courses.
Cell phones: Generally, phones should be turned off. However, phones may be used for dictionary work and research. Naturally, Kakao and other social media should not be used during class as they can interfere with concentration and learning.
IV. OFFICE HOURS:
I have office hours every week. These will be announced in the first few days. These are great opportunities to ask me for help. I am also available at some other times if the office hours are not suitable. Please make an appointment by email. When you email me, can you always include your name, student number and class code. I look forward to seeing you either in my office (Room 709), or we can easily meet on Zoom.
V. PLAGIARISM: 
Copying some words/phrases or sentences from another person and claiming it as your own writing is not allowed.  Please do not copy. You should summarize and paraphrase others’ ideas and include a citation. I will teach you these important skills on the course. If three or more words are together in your writing or are copied directly from another source this can be plagiarism. Any assignment that has significant (more than 25 words) plagiarism will receive a zero. If you need help with an assignment, please ask me before the deadline. Please do not copy. I will know.
The use of AI and other writing tools should be limited to grammar and style corrections, and not to generate full sentences or paragraphs. Submitting work that is partially or completely generated by AI writing tools will result in a grade of zero for the assignment.
(It is important to note that AI writing tools cannot substitute for originality and critical analysis required for academic work.) As students write in Google Doc, I can review the file history to check that the assignment has been developed by you over time, and has not been copied and pasted from another source or A.I. This is why students must write their assignments in Google Docs. 
If AI is permitted to be used by the teacher for a specific class activity, they will inform you explicitly. Students should be careful to follow the instructions for AI use carefully. Please ask the teacher if you are unsure and feel free to discuss any concerns regarding the use of AI during office hours or by email. 
VI. ANNOUNCEMENTS & ADDITIONAL COURSE INFORMATION
Please make sure you have your correct email address on the university system. During the semester and before the grades are finalized, there will be announcements. It is also important to keep checking your email, especially after the final assessments in case I need to contact you about your work. Also, after the final grades are announced, please contact me immediately if you think there may be an error with your score. There is a short period when this is possible, but after this period has finished it is not possible to make changes to scores.

Office Hours: before and after the class, or by appointment
Email: mafaldakim@gmail.com 
[Course Description] 
This course explores what are the social, economic, and political forces behind the configuration of global spaces and what are the institutional structures and processes that govern those forces. 
First, we will explore the concepts of global actors, global community, and global order, with special attention to the analytical usefulness of shifting the unit of analysis from the local and the national to the global and the transnational. 
Second, we will deal with global justice system (or the lack of it). The global legal system is representative of the common notion that global governance is “governance without government.” We explore the mismatch between the state-centered law-enforcement system and the wrongdoings committed by transnational actors. We will also explore the changing nature of “sovereignty” under global forces. 
Third, we will look at spatial manifestations of global forces, i.e. how global forces manifest themselves when they touch specific locality. We will deal with both cultural and economic aspects of peace-time and conflictual aspects of war/disaster-time. 
[Class format and grading structure]
This course is mainly composed of lectures. Yet, during the semester we will have two discussion sessions. Before each discussion session, students are required to prepare discussion questions related to the designated topic. 
The grading structure consists of 1) attendance 10%, 2) discussion participation 20%, 2) mid-term exam (in class) 30%, and 4) final paper (1500~2500 words or 5~10 pages) 40%. For all assignments, you may write either in Korean or in English. If you don’t submit the final paper, the grade will be an automatic F, regardless of other assignments.

개요 | 기호학과 미디어철학의 세계적인 석학 이시다 히데타카(石田英敬)에 따르면 21세기의 정보혁명은 단순한 기술의 발달이 아니라 인간 정신의 근간을 흔드는 문제이다. 특히나 2023년부터 본격화된 A.I. 기술은 디지털 미디어를 매개로 인류문명의 근간에 대격변을 일으키고 있기에, 격변기의 세상을 이해하기 위한 새롭고 보다 깊은 사유와 질문이 절실히 요구되는 바이다. 본 강의는 이시다 히데타카의 기호론과 미디어론을 바탕으로 인류문명의 변천사를 학습하고, 마셜 맥루언, 프리드리히 키틀러의 고전 미디어 이론과 존 더럼 피터스의 최신 미디어 이론(원소 미디어론 혹은 생태 미디어론) 등 또한 학습할 것이다. 물론 소쉬르와 퍼스의 기호학 이론과 바르트의 미디어 비평문(사진, 영화 등)을 다룰 것이며, 필요에 따라 이론과 텍스트가 다루는 예시들(사진, 영화, 비디오 게임 등)을 감상할 것이다.

∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 모든 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

∙ [출석] 
-1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가능, 단 출석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함

∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 모든 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

∙ [실험실습 안전]
-연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분야 대상학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수
-신규교육(신입생 2시간), 정기교육(고위험학과 학기별 6시간, 저위험학과 학기별 3시간)
-대상학과: KUPID > 지식관리 > 안전관리지식 > 연구실안전
-포털시스템 상단 메뉴에서 “정보생활” 클린, [안전교육(서울)] 클릭하여 안전교육 페이지 접속(“크롬”으로 접속, 접속 오류 시 인터넷 설정에서 “팝업 차단 해제” 설정 필요)
-포털 아이디가 없는 경우, 국가연구안전관리본부 연구실안전교육시스템(https://edu.labs.go.kr/) 접속하여 수강 가능함. 
-외부기관에서 안전교육을 이수한 경우 별도의 등록절차를 통한 이수 가능
-미이수 시 불이익: 학부생(성적열람 제한), 대학원생(출입제한)

막연하고도 어려운 질문이 될 수 있다. 이 교과목은 시대별 장르별 대표적인 오페라 작품을 접하며 오페라의 구성요소와 올바른 감상태도를 습득하여 위에 제시되어 있는 명제에 대한 답을 찾을 수 있도록 한다. 더불어 전공자는 아니지만 각자의 역량 아래서 부분적으로나마 오페라 곡을 직접 불러볼 수 있도록 한다.

Course Overview
Designed to provide students with an in-depth exploration of the scientific principles and technological advancements that underpin the production, analysis, and innovation of textiles, this course bridges the gap between science and practical application, equipping students with a robust foundation to navigate the complex world of textiles in various industries. 
This course offers a comprehensive perspective on the development, manufacturing, and application of textiles, exploring their profound influence on design and construction of clothing. The characteristics of different fibers, yarns, fabrics, and finishes are investigated.
Course Objectives
Explore Textile Fundamentals and Cultivate Fabric Evaluation Skills: Develop a comprehensive understanding of textile materials, fibers, yarns, and fabric structures, examining their properties and potential applications in the context of fashion design. Learn to assess and analyze various textiles for their aesthetic qualities, durability, comfort, and suitability for different fashion applications, enhancing the ability to make informed design and production decisions.
Study Textile Technologies and Understand Sustainable Practices: Investigate modern and traditional textile production techniques, including weaving, knitting, printing, and dyeing processes, to gain practical knowledge of industry-standard methods and technologies. Explore the ecological impact of textile production and investigate sustainable alternatives, fostering an awareness of environmentally conscious practices within the fashion industry.
Integrate Technology in Textile Design and Develop a Design Portfolio: Explore the intersection of technology and textiles, incorporating digital tools and software into the design process, and understand the role of smart textiles in contemporary fashion. Build a professional portfolio showcasing a diverse range of textile samples, designs, and projects, demonstrating proficiency in textile design and its application in the broader field of fashion.

Course Description and Objectives  
This course is designed to provide undergraduate students with basic knowledge and skills needed to cope with various marketing problems. Marketing management involves all activities related to creating and delivering satisfactory value for customers and marketers as well.  These activities include market and environment analysis, the development of marketing strategies and plans, and the implementation and control of marketing programs. This course is designed to stress the application of unique marketing concepts such as customer value; customer satisfaction management; customer relationship management; consumer and organizational buying behavior; market segmentation, targeting and positioning; and the formulation of product, price, promotion, and distribution strategies on practical situations and problems.
	To facilitate interactive learning experience, students are encouraged to prepare a short essay for each subject and share their own thoughts and ideas with other classmates. I want you to become a willing participant in the process of creating, sharing, and utilizing knowledge. 
Recommended (not required) Book	
Principles of Marketing by Kotler and Armstrong, Pearson Education International (available at Korea University Book Store)
You may buy any Korean or international books on the topic.
Required Case: Allbirds: Can the Sustainable Shoe Company Reinvigorate the Brand? (Harvard Business School, CU380-PDF-ENG)
Course Structure:  This course will incorporate both lecture, case analysis, and discussion. Extensive class participation through discussion and preparation of assigned materials is expected. Lectures will reinforce and expand upon materials in the text. Lecture, discussion, and other in-class activities are designed both to bring new perspectives to the material and to foster the active application of text and lecture content to business problems and situations. For the type of discussion and application that I envision to be worthwhile, you will have to do a lot of work to be properly prepared.  Preparation for class will require reading the text and extra readings before coming to class.
Grades will be determined in the following way:
	Case Analysis	(G)					25%
	Short Essays on Marketing Issues (I)			30%
	Group Project Report and presentation (G)		25%
	Participation (I)					20%
Case analysis report
This exercise is to help you to enhance your business writing skills. You should be able to organize your thoughts logically when analyzing problems in your hands and present alternative solutions and recommendations in logical pattern. The guideline for how to write case analysis proposal is 
Executive summary
One page summary of problems and recommendations.
Problem/Issue Statement
There are usually one or more core problems that a firm in the case is facing. If your diagnosis of the core problem(s) were wrong, the following analysis would be a complete waste. It is critical for you to identify the right problems to be a successful manager. This section should be in maximum of two paragraphs. Do not waste limited space giving background information or case facts.
Listing of Alternatives that may be used to resolve focal problem(s)
You have to list a set of alternatives logically. Some cases included suggested alternatives to be considered which might be a decoy to cloud your analysis. You have to develop your own alternatives and show how each alternative would help in solving the focal problem(s). 
Recommendations
This section should describe the recommendation offered and they should be keyed to the issues identified previously. When making your recommendation, make sure that you have considered the feasibility and ramifications of enacting your action plan (identify why it is a good plan and how it overcomes the problems). You need not provide the rationale for your recommendation in this section. The rationale should be provided in the following section.
Rationale and Analysis
In this section you justify your recommendations. This section would usually be the longest part of your report. The logic can be established using any quantitative analyses, evaluations, projections, and qualitative analyses that you feel relevant. Also address the impact of potentially negative outcomes of you plan and address counter-arguments like “but what if” questions.
Attachments
These attachments are exhibits, tables, graphs, or whatever, and consist of support materials. Make sure that they specifically address the questions in the proceeding sections. Also make clear references to the particular attachments in the main body of the report. A reasonable number of appendices are allowed and will not be counted toward this limit. Appendices should not be used to provide a written explanation of your argument points. The violation of this limit will result in deduction of points.
Please refer all attachments and appendices properly in the main text. All attachments and appendices should have a clear heading.
The physical formats for written case reports are;
The maximum length of the content should not exceed 10 pages, double-spaced, triple spaced between each paragraph. Exhibits and cover page are not included in the maximum length for the report.
The cover page should include the name of the case, names and students ID numbers of your group members, date of submittal, and course number.
It should be page-numbered either on the middle of each page bottom or on the upper right corner.
The font of characters should be 11.
The overall appearance should be very professional. Remind yourself that you are writing the report for either your clients as a consultant or a member of a task force for a company. If your report has more than five misspelling, you will be penalized by one letter grade.
The deadline for the report is before the beginning of the class for which a case is assigned. Any late report will not be accepted!
Short Essays on Marketing Issues: Before a topic is covered in the class, students should read assigned materials and prepare a two-page long essay that contains each student’s thought on how the specific marketing topic is related to his or her everyday life. This exercise is to demonstrate that marketing is a part of everyone’s life. Each student is required to hand in the short essay a week before the specific topic is covered in class. I will select a couple of excellent essays to share one’s thoughts with other classmates. The writers of the chosen essay will be asked to present his/her essay for class.
An excellent essay is not a simple summary of a marketing concept. For example, I am not asking you to write what market segmentation is. I do not need a definition of it. What I want to read is your effort to understand a specific concept and to imply the knowledge to see what kind of marketing activities are happening around us. With keen observation, I want you to evaluate the effectiveness of various marketing practices that you can observe around your life.
Group Project and Presentation:  Developing a marketing strategy of a brand, a product, or a service that is facing a marketing problem is the nature of group project. The contents that must be included are;
A brief history of the industry in which the selected firm or organization operates
A brief history of the selected firm
Detailed description of product(s) or service(s) which the selected firm or organization has
Description of the current marketing strategies (Marketing 4 P’s) of the selected subject
Identification and description of the current problem(s) that the chosen subject faces at the current time
4 C analysis
general Circumstance analysis
Competition analysis
Company analysis
Customer analysis
SWOT analysis (include description of sustainable competitive advantages, relative weaknesses compared to competitors, and all relevant environmental conditions)
Development of several alternative actions that the chosen subject should consider to solve the current problem(s)
Recommendation of a marketing strategy that you think is the best alternative at the given time. Your recommendation should include a complete set of strategic marketing process contents.
Among the contents that you need to include, you should pay extra attention on the problem(s) that you identify by justifying why they are important, the alternatives that you suggest as possible solutions to those problems, and your recommendation with clear and creative logic of your thought process.
You can choose any product or service from an existing company or one in inception. It can come from a manufacturing or service firm; a commercial or non-profit organization; an online company or off-line company, etc. As a matter of fact, it can be anything. However, make sure that you consult with me before finalizing the subject of your group project.
You are asked to submit a MS Power Point report. The physical formats of the presentation report, which each group should follow, are:
Maximum length is 20 pages in MS Power Point format, including all exhibits, figures, or tables;
A cover page should include at least project title, name and ID number of group members, and submission date;
The report should be page-numbered either on the upper right corner or on the middle of each page bottom, starting after the cover page;
It should be stapled on the upper left corner. Do not use fancy report covers;
Any late report will not be accepted!!!
Even though your report format is MS PowerPoint, your report should do your best in describing your marketing strategy as detailed as possible.
Class Participation and Attendance:  Each of you is expected to contribute to class discussion. This includes preparation for class by reading the text and other reading assignments and presenting your analyses, opinions or summaries of materials covered in class if called upon to do so. The level of individual class discussion participation will be closely monitored and will be reflected on your final grade as suggested. To facilitate such monitoring and intimate atmosphere, I will create a seating chart and you will be assigned to a seat for the remainder of the semester.  Seat will be assigned to you on first-come first-choice base. Attendance is required for this course and will be checked every class using the seating chart.  If you miss more than three week class time, you will be automatically given a F.  Use your options carefully to avoid getting the penalty!!!
Course Policies

Materials are presented in an educational context for personal use and study and should not be shared, distributed, or sold in print - or digitally - outside the course without permission. Electronic video and/or audio recording is not permitted during both online and offline classes unless the student obtains permission from the instructor. Even if permission is granted, any distribution of the recording is prohibited.

강의 개요 및 목표
라틴아메리카의 데이터과학의 이해는 현재 중요성이 강조되고 있는 데이터 분석에 관심 있는 모든 사람들을 대상으로 한다. 이 강의는 엑셀, SQL, 파이썬에 대한 기초 지식이 전혀 없어도 수강할 수 있도록 기초부터 차근차근 진행될 것이다. 따라서 최종적으로 수강생들이 사회에 나가 실무에서 바로 활용할 수 있는 다양한 기술을 배우는 것을 목표로 한다.
본 강의는 데이터 과학의 기초를 학습하고, 특히 스페인어 데이터 및 라틴아메리카 데이터를 다루는 능력을 배양하는 데 중점을 둔다. 또한 수강생들은 디지털 도구를 통해 라틴아메리카의 다양한 데이터를 분석하고, 이를 통해 지역적 특성을 반영한 데이터 분석 능력을 배양할 것이다. 또한, 데이터 예측의 기본 원리와 이를 실무에 적용하는 방법을 학습하여, 미래의 트렌드와 변화를 예측하고 이에 대한 전략을 수립할 수 있는 능력을 갖추는 것을 목표로 한다.
이 강의는 수강생들이 데이터 분석의 기초부터 차근차근 학습하며, 실질적인 데이터 분석 및 예측 능력을 기르는 것을 목표로 한다. 매 시간 학생 한 명 한 명의 코드를 검토하고 피드백을 제공하여, 생소한 데이터 분석 코딩이 학생들에게 부담스럽지 않게 느껴지도록 하며, 그 재미를 느끼게 하는 것을 목표로 한다. 
  또한, 강의를 통해 최종적으로 수강생들이 향후 전공 수업뿐만 아니라 사회에서 다양한 데이터를 효과적으로 분석하고 활용하는 능력을 기르기를 목표로 한다.

데이터 처리 및 분석: 5주

강의 소개
인공지능 및 언어모델, chatGPT, 빅데이터 분석의 발전은 데이터 수집 및 분석의 필요성과 중요성을 높이고 있다. 데이터는 현 시대의 새로운 자원으로 평가되며, 이를 효과적으로 수집하고 분석하는 능력은 개인과 기업 모두에게 중요한 경쟁력이 된다. 본 강의는 이러한 시대적 흐름에 맞추어 데이터 과학의 기초와 실제 활용 방법을 학습한다.
특히, 본 강의는 스페인어 데이터 및 라틴아메리카 데이터를 다루는 것을 중점으로 한다. 라틴아메리카는 다양한 문화와 경제적 특성을 가지고 있으며, 이를 데이터 분석에 반영하는 것은 매우 중요하다. 우리는 라틴아메리카의 경제, 사회, 문화적 데이터를 분석하여 이 지역의 특성을 이해하고, 이를 통해 더욱 정확하고 유의미한 분석 결과를 도출하는 방법을 학습할 것이다.
데이터 분석을 수행하기 위해서는 엑셀, SQL, 파이썬과 같은 도구들의 활용이 필수적이다. 엑셀은 데이터 관리와 기본적인 분석 작업에 유용하며, SQL은 데이터베이스에서 데이터를 추출하고 조작하는 데 필수적인 언어이다. 파이썬은 데이터 분석 및 머신러닝에 있어 강력한 도구로, 본 강의에서는 이들 도구들을 활용하여 실질적인 데이터 분석을 수행하는 방법을 학습한다. 특히, 스페인어 데이터를 다루는 실습을 통해 실제 현장에서의 활용 능력을 키우는 것을 목표로 한다.
올바른 데이터 분석을 위해서는 데이터베이스 관리, 데이터 구조, 기초 통계 지식이 필요하다. 이러한 기초 지식은 데이터의 올바른 수집, 저장, 분석을 가능하게 하며, 분석 결과의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 기여한다. 본 강의는 이러한 기초 지식을 이해하고 적용하는 방법을 제공한다. 또한, 라틴아메리카 데이터의 특성을 고려한 분석 방법론을 소개하고, 이를 통해 지역적 특성을 반영한 데이터 분석 능력을 배양한다.
마지막으로, 데이터 예측의 필요성에 대해 다룬다. 데이터 예측은 미래의 트렌드와 변화를 예측하고 이에 대한 전략을 수립하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다. 본 강의에서는 데이터 예측의 기본 원리와 이를 적용하는 방법을 학습한다. 라틴아메리카의 데이터를 활용한 예측 사례를 통해 실제 응용 능력을 키우는 것을 목표로 한다.
본 수업에서는 데이터 과학의 기초를 학습하고 라틴아메리카의 다양한 데이터를 활용하여 실제 분석을 수행하는 첫걸음을 내딛는 것을 최종 목표로 한다. 수강생들은 엑셀, SQL, 파이썬을 통해 데이터 분석을 수행하고, 이를 통해 실제 문제를 해결하는 능력을 갖추게 될 것이다. 이 강의를 통해 수강생들이 향후 전공 수업뿐만 아니라 사회에서 다양한 데이터를 효과적으로 분석하고 활용하는 능력을 기르기를 목표로 한다.

Course Description and Objectives

This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and strategies essential for successful debating. Building upon foundational skills in critical thinking and communication, this course aims to cultivate advanced proficiency in argument construction, analysis, and delivery.
Throughout the semester, students will become more familiar with both Lincoln-Douglas and Parliamentary style debating.

Mid-Term Exam 25%
Scheduled for April 23rd 
The Mid-Term Exam will be written and cover the material taught on fallacies, definitions, and basic debate skills covered in the first part of the course. 


Final Exam  15%
Scheduled for June 16th -22nd 
 The Final Exam will be a final 1-1 interview based on the argumentative essay and final debate activity. Evaluation criteria for this will be provided closer to the date. 



 Essay Assignment 15%

You will be required to submit an argumentative essay on a debate topic. We will cover the writing strategies required for this in class. 

Participation (Debate Activity)  20%

There will be debate activities in class. Evaluation criteria for this will be given. 

Quiz 15%  

There will be a quiz after the mid term exam and prior to the final debate. 

Attendance  10%  

The policy for attendance is as follows: you can be absent for acceptable reasons from a maximum of 3 classes without penalty. You cannot be absent from more than 66% of classes or an ‘F’ grade will result. In order to be eligible for an A+, you cannot be absent from more than two classes.

개요 | 이 강의는 러시아어를 전공 학생들이 러시아의 정치, 경제, 사회, 문화를 지역학적 시각으로 이해하는데 도움을 주고자 한다. 특히, 우크라이나 전쟁 이후 급변하고 있는 유라시아의 지정학적 구조는 어문학 전공자들에게 단순한 언어능력을 넘어서 심층적인 지역 문해력을 갖도록 요구하고 있다. 따라서 본 강의는 노어노문학과 학생들이 러시아 사회의 맥락과 현재의 국제 질서를 종합적으로 분석할 수 있는 능력을 함양하는 데 중점을 두며, 학생들이 실제 국제 정세와 러시아 관련 이슈를 비판적으로 해석하고 활용할 수 있는 지역전문성을 기르는 것을 목표로 한다.

세부목표 2 | 냉전 이후 러시아의 체제 전환 과정과 대내외 정책 변화를 분석하고, 우크라이나 전쟁 이후 변화하는 유라시아 국제질서를 맥락적으로 해석할 수 있다.
세부목표 3 | 러시아 및 유라시아 지역 관련 주요 현안을 자료 분석과 발표·토론을 통해 비판적으로 검토하고, 전공 언어능력과 결합된 지역 분석 역량을 실질적으로 강화한다.

개요 | 이 강좌는 인간의 창조적 이성의 한 측면인 비판적 사고를 연마하는 강좌이다. 비판적 사고의 핵심은 논리적 사고라는 전제 하에 여러 가지 논리적 추론 방식을 익힌다. 연역법, 귀납법, 가설상정논법(귀추법 abduction), 정언논리, 비형식적 오류 등이 다루어질 예가 되는 주제들이다. 다른 한편, 이 강좌는 논리적 사고가 비판적 사고의 핵심이지만 전부는 아니라는 점을 잊지 않는다. 논리 이외에도, 비판적 사고를 위해 필요한 것에는 자유와 정의와 진리를 추구하는 열린, 공정한, 그리고 용감한 마음씨도 필요하다.

아울러, 비판적, 논리적 사고의 한가지 응용으로서, 이번 학기가 세번째 학기가 되는데, 공직적격성평가(PSAT)와 법학적성시험(LEET) 기출문제 일부를 맛보기 정도로 다룰 계획이다.
수강(권장)대상 학생 | 지적 호기심이 있는 학생들에게 권장한다. ‘또는’ 현명한(judicious) 판단과 비판적(critical) 사유를 사랑하는 마음씨를 가진 학생들에게 권장한다. 앞 문장의 ‘또는’은 ‘포괄적 또는(inclusive or)’이다. ‘포괄적 또는’이 무슨 말인지 아직 모르는 학생들에게도 권장한다.
선이수과목(권장) | 선수과목이나 예비지식은 필요치 않다.
수업운영원칙 | 인간의 비판적 사유의 지평선까지 두려움 없이 나아간다.
기존개설대비
변경,개선사항 | 공직적격성평가(PSAT)와 법학적성시험(LEET) 기출문제를, 여전히 맛보기이긴 하지만 시대의 요구를 좀더 예민하게 감지하여, 지난 학기보다는 조금 더 긴 시간 다룰 예정이다.
수업목표 일반 | 비판적 사고가 무엇인지 알고, 그 기법을 익혀, 실제 삶에 적용할 수 있는 능력을 기르는 것을 목표로 한다. 이 과목을 성공적으로 수강한 학생들은 아래 세부목표들을 성취한다.

Typically, a maximum of about 40-45% of you will receive a grade of “A” or “A+”. Evaluation in this class is based strictly on performance, and not on English language proficiency. All parts of the evaluation system must be completed in an exceptional manner if you want to get an “A+”.

과목 개요
디자인 대상(액세서리:신발, 가방)에 대한 기본 정보 및 패션 디자인 프로세스를 학습하고 상품성/창의성을 고려한 디자인 개발을 실체화하는 실습을 한다. 디자인 아이디어를 실제 제작 가능한 방식으로 구현하고 커뮤니케이션 할 수 있는 기초를 다진다.
학습 목표
액세서리에 대한 이해: 액세서리의 종류를 살펴보고, 액세서리 시장의 대표적인 아이템인 신발과 가방의 구조 및 제작 과정에 대해 이해한다.
파우치 제작 및 가방 가봉: 기초 봉재, 가방의 구조, 패턴, 제작 실습을 통해 실제 디자인 구현에서 고려해야 할 사항에 대한 이해도를 높인다.
업사이클링을 통한 소프트 굿즈 제작: 디자인 개발과정에 대한 이해를 바탕으로 창의적, 실용적인 소프트 굿즈(가방, 파우치를 포함한 패션 액세서리 및 리빙 제품) 디자인 개발을 실습하고 나아가 새로운 가치 창출에 대한 마인드를 함양한다.
수업 방침
모든 학생은 수업 전 LMS(kulms.korea.ac.kr)의 강의자료실에서 자료를 다운로드 받아 수업을 준비한다. 
1강, 강의 소개도 출결에 반영. 단 수강정정으로 추후 들어온 수강생에 한하여 출석 인정. 1강에도강의 진행 예정이므로 추후 수강을 희망하는 학생은 청강 가능
결석 시 출석 점수 10점 만점에서 1점씩 감점하고, 세 번 지각, 혹은 조퇴 시 결석 1회와 동일하게 처리한다. 30분 이상 지각한 경우 해당 수업은 결석 처리한다(특별 사유가 있을 경우 강사와 사전에 논의 요망)
수업 중 다른 과제를 수행하거나 장시간 이탈 시 태도 점수(5점)에 반영한다.
과제는 제출기한보다 늦게 제출할 경우 마감 시간 이후 1점/24h씩 감점한다.
수강 요건ㄴ
별도의 수강요건 없음
과제물
수시과제: 수업 및 과제 수행 전 준비 사항으로 수업의 이해를 돕고 과제의 방향성을 지도하기 위한 과제로 수업 중 자유로운 형식으로 공유. 완결된 과제가 아닌 중간 과정이므로 각 과제의 수행 여부만 평가한다.
과제 1_파우치 제작: 가방 제작을 위해 봉제의 기초 기술을 실습하는 과정으로 지퍼가 달린 파우치를 제작한다.
과제 2_가봉 및 포트폴리오: 본인의 디자인을 가봉 제작함으로써 평면의 스케치를 입체화하는 과정을 실습한다. 이를 통해 가방의 패턴을 직접 제도해 보고 필요한 부자재를 접목해 봄으로써 디자인과 기획에서 고려해야 할 사항을 습득한다. 가봉(시뮬레이션) 및 디자인 포트폴리오를 제출한다.
과제 3 창작 디자인 및 영상 (팀프로젝트): 업사이클링 소재를 활용하여 각 팀의 주제에 따라 창의적인 발상으로 문제를 해결하고 디자인을 구현해보는 과정. 실제 완성품과 디자인 컨셉 및 스토리 영상을 제작한다. 우수한 기말 성과물에 한하여 학기 종료 후 한국의류산업학회에서 개최하는 2026년 SFTI Re:Lab 소프트굿즈 디자인콘테스트 참가를 위한 피드백 및 사후 가이드를 제공한다.

 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

Overview | This course provides a comprehensive overview of international economics, examining the theoretical underpinnings of global trade. We will delve into the economic theories that explain why nations trade, the macroeconomic factors that shape trade patterns, and the policies that governments employ to regulate and promote trade.
Who Should Take This Course | This course is designed for students interested in pursuing careers as economists or international professionals. We will focus on providing insights and analytical tools relevant to roles such as international analysts working for multinational corporations/organizations.
Prerequisites (Recommended) | Introduction to Economics (Mandatory)
Class Rules | Students are expected to have completed the reading prior to lecture.
Changes and improvements
Objectives 
General | Understand comprehensive overview of international economics.
Detailed Objective 1 | Explain the economics of producers. We will learn productions and costs of firms and the aggregate economy.
Detailed Objective 2 | Explain the economic theories underpinning international trade and analyze the factors influencing trade flows. Evaluate the impact of government policies on international trade and assess the effectiveness of different policy instruments.
Detailed Objective 3 | Identify the opportunities and risks associated with international business transactions and develop strategies to mitigate these risks.

COURSE OBJECTIVES
The objective of this course is to improve students’ academic and professional skills in Business English. By the end of this course students will be more prepared to participate successfully in English-related academic and professional settings.  The course uses current topics and situations related to successfully navigating in society using English. 
REQUIRED MATERIALS
Each student is responsible for bringing the following materials to class: notebook, writing utensil, and a file folder.  Students will be expected to save all handouts, organize them in the folder, and bring it to class every day. If you are absent for class, please ask your classmates for any handouts. PPT's from class will be downloaded to blackboard.

This course explores issues of economic development in a globalizing world. Today, trade policy is at the forefront of the development agenda, and it is a critical element of any strategy to fight against poverty. This renewed interest in trade liberalization does not come from dogma, but instead is based on a careful assessment of development experience over the last 50 years. In the first half of the semester, we study how multilateral trade cooperation in the World Trade Organization (WTO) helps developing countries create and strengthen institutions and regulatory regimes that will enhance the gains from trade and integration into the global economy. In the second half, we also survey how the growth of regional trading blocs affects developing countries that are turning to regionalism as a tool for economic development.

If you fall behind, it will be very difficult to catch up.

COURSE OVERVIEW
Academic research aided by artificial data analytics and intelligence (AI) applications is a fast-growing research area in business studies. Researchers have actively developed and/or adopted computational and statistical analytics to generate practical insights for managers, policy makers, and other researchers. The main objective of this course is to introduce students to up-to-date data analytics and AI applications along with the latest research topics. The course will cover general concepts in the domain of AI, along with widely accepted machine learning (ML) algorithms. Students will also acquire experience using software tools. This course will focus on the use of Python, which is the most popular data analytics tool in modern research. 
Learning Objectives 
 Gain a general understanding of data analytics and AI
 Gain a practical understanding of various AI methods 
 Acquire an understanding of when/how to use AI in business contexts
 Become aware of up-to-date trends in AI
Pre-requisites and Requirements 
- Basic Skills in Python
- Undergraduate-level Mathematical and Statistical Knowledge (e.g., Algebra, Probability, etc.)
- STUDENTS ARE ADVISED TO ENSURE THAT THEY MEET THE STATED PREREQUISITES, AS LACKING THIS FOUNDATIONAL KNOWLEDGE WILL MAKE IT DIFFICULT TO FOLLOW THE COURSE MATERIAL AND KEEP PACE WITH THE LEARNING PROCESS.

Required textbooks: No textbook is required.
Software: Python and its relevant libraries and APIs including Pandas, Numpy, TFKeras, etc.

- In addition, the instructor provides supplemental readings throughout the semester to introduce background, fill gaps in the lectures, and broaden the students’ general knowledge about AI
COURSE MODULES
The course comprises the following modules:
1. Basic Understanding of AI
2. Basic ML
3. Advanced ML (Recent Developments in Neural Networks)
4. AI Agents with Language Models (In-Context Learning; Instruction Tuning, Retrieval Augmented Generation [RAG], Agentic AI, etc.)

Course Description: This course is designed to provide students with basic knowledge of functional genomics. It is suitable for beginners to obtain fundamental concepts in this field.

3. Other genome-related technologies
Course PDF files are available on LMS (학습관리시스템).
Summary of Functional Genomics Class
(1) Introduction to the World of Omics
Overview of various “omics” fields (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, etc.) and their roles in understanding biological systems.
(2) DNA sequencing & the History of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)
- First-generation sequencing: traditional Sanger sequencing methods and its automation
- Second generation sequencing (NGS): high-throughput sequencing technologies that revolutionized genomics
- Third generation sequencing (next NGS): advanced sequencing technologies offering longer reads and real-time data
(3) Other genome-wide technologies associated with deep sequencing
Studies of genome-wide DNA features
- DNA methylation and other epigenetic marks
- Chromatin structure & remodeling
- Interaction between DNA and proteins/RNAs
- Chromosome conformation capture techniques (e.g., Hi-C...)
- Genome editing techniques
(4) Single species genome projects
- Insights gained from sequencing individuals species’ genomes
- Importance of reference genomes in biological research including comparative genomics
(5) Recent genome projects
Overview of the latest large-scale genome sequencing initiatives
(6) Genomes & biology
How genomics data contributes to understanding biological functions, disease mechanisms, and evolution

NGOs: Language of Social Change
Peter Sylvestre, M.Sc., M.Phil., MIEM
Email: pssylveku@gmail.com / Phone: 010-9009-1733 / Office: IFLS #719
All students regardless of year or national status are welcome!
I. General Description & Course Content
This course explores the role of Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) in driving social change and their impact on global issues. Through analyzing real-world case studies and engaging in peer discussions, students will examine the language and communication strategies used by NGOs to advocate for social justice, human rights, environmental sustainability, and community development. By developing their linguistic and critical thinking skills, students will gain a deeper understanding of the power of language in promoting positive social change. This course is designed for university students with an upper-intermediate level or above in English. This course is designed to give students practical, proficient spoken and written communication skills necessary to both decode and employ the discourse of NGOs and have knowledge of their operations.
However, this course is not merely a language course as it also designed to ensure socio-pragmatic competence in NGOs through discourse analysis of various NGO literature such as websites, public outreach, appeals for public support, advocacy campaigns and academic research. 
This course is not intended as primarily a theoretical, lecture based course. Rather, it seeks to be student-focused where students will participate in group discussions and pair-work, project design, problem analysis and solution, presentations, and interviews. 
Spoken (Verbal): Students will participate in group discussions/meetings, participating in interviews, role-play simulation involving crisis management, expressing quantitative data, etc. As many students perform at the C1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Language, students should be reasonably proficient in English, i.e., high intermediate/advanced.
Written: As written organizational documents (a) reflect the individual’s and organization’s professionalism, (b) are permanent and therefore form a lasting impression and (c) are legal business documents, employees of organizations must be able to communicate coherently and effectively in writing. Hence, this course emphasizes texts such as vision statements, memos, presentation visual aids (e.g., PowerPoint) etc.

수업개요
우리가 행복한 삶을 사는 데 필요한 것은 여러 가지가 있습니다. 친구, 가족 등도 필요하지만 무시할 수 없는 것은 소득입니다. 우리는 소득을 얻기 위해 일을 하는데, 그 일을 통해 물질적인 보상 뿐만 아니라 성취감이나 자긍심과 같은 정신적인 보상을 얻기도 합니다. 이 수업에서는 일자리가 어떻게 만들어지고 소득은 어떻게 결정이 되는지에 대해 알아보고자 합니다. 그러기 위해서는 노동시장이 어떻게 작동하는지를 아는 것이 중요합니다.
노동시장이 어떻게 작동하는지를 탐구하는 학문이 바로 노동경제학입니다. 노동경제학에서 연구하는 노동시장에는 고용주(employer)와 고용인(employee)이라는 두 참여자가 존재합니다. 우리는 이 수업에서 이 둘의 행위와 의사결정을 분석하고, 그 둘 간의 상호 관계를 연구합니다. 즉, 노동시장의 수요와 공급을 공부하는 것입니다. 
이런 의미에서 노동경제학은 광의로 미시경제학(microeconomics)의 일부라고 할 수 있고, 이 수업의 원활한 이해를 위해서는 미시경제학의 수요-공급이론에 관한 기본 지식이 필요합니다. 노동경제학의 분석에는 실증적 측면과 이론적 측면이 있는데, 수업에서는 우선 이론을 소개하고, 이론이 제시하는 가설을 실증분석한 결과를 살펴볼 것입니다.
* 본 수업은 최대한 수학을 덜 사용하고, 도형을 많이 이용하려 합니다.

K-Contents and K-Wave
Course Instructor: Tian Li
Instructor Email: estherli@Korea.ac.kr  
Office: Media Hall 1203

Course Description
The Korean Wave, or Hallyu, has evolved from a regional media trend into a global cultural phenomenon. This course offers a comprehensive exploration of K-Contents, examining its historical roots, industrial structures, and cultural impact. We will move beyond a simple celebration of its popularity to critically analyze the economic, political, and social forces that shape its production and global circulation. The course covers a wide range of media, including film, television dramas (K-dramas), popular music (K-pop), and variety shows.
Key questions we will engage with include: How did South Korea become a major exporter of popular culture? What are the roles of the state and digital platforms in facilitating the K-Wave? How do these cultural products negotiate issues of national identity, gender, class, and modernity? And how are they received, adapted, and sometimes resisted in different local contexts? Through a combination of theoretical readings and close analysis of primary texts, students will develop a nuanced understanding of one of the most significant cultural developments of the 21st century.
Course Goals and Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will:
✓ Understand the historical development and industrial structure of the Korean Wave.
✓ Critically analyze key K-content texts (film, TV, music) using frameworks from media, cultural, and gender studies.
✓ Evaluate the complex dynamics between local production and global reception in transnational media flows.
✓ Articulate well-reasoned arguments about K-contents in both written and oral forms.
Course Expectations
Course Structure
These will be a combination of lectures, small group discussion, and in-class activity sessions where you will discuss, solve problems, and complete activities with a few of your classmates. 
What you can expect from me
I will do my best to give you the tools, learning resources, feedback, and support to succeed. Learning is a never-ending process, so I hope to motivate students to seek out more information on topics we don’t have time to cover. I will try my best to respond to your email within 24 hours during weekdays. In return, I expect you also to respond to my email within 24 hours. Never hesitate to email me, join me in my office hours, or set up a Zoom meeting. I want to get to know you and support you in this learning experience!
What I expect from you
I ask that you try as best as you can to remain focused and engaged during class. I expect you to take an active role in your learning by coming to our class meetings prepared and ready to collaborate with your classmates. Moreover, keep in mind that each member of this class has different ideas and perspectives that will enrich the experience for us all.
Course Policies
Academic Integrity
Students are responsible for turning in their own work, citing material properly, and conducting themselves in a civil and ethical manner. All work should be entirely your own and must use appropriate citation practices to acknowledge the use of books, articles, websites, lectures, discussions, etc., that you have consulted to complete your assignments. Students are also responsible for abiding by Korea University guidelines for academic integrity and plagiarism. Those found guilty of plagiarism will automatically fail the assignment and will potentially face academic sanctions.
Academic Accommodation
If you need accommodation of any sort to participate in this course, please contact the Center for Students with Disabilities as soon as possible since timely notice is needed to coordinate accommodations.
Email etiquette
Please feel free to send me emails at any point during the semester with questions or concerns. In order to receive a response, however, your email must use capital letters when appropriate and include salutations.
Late Penalty 
You are allowed 5 “late days” for your assignments (not for midterm or final). In other words, there would be no penalty if you submitted one of the four assignments five days late, or one assignment 2 days late and another 3 days late, etc. After those 5 “late days” are used, your assignments will be penalized one-third of a grade.
Course Privacy Statement
As noted in the University’s recording and broadcasting course policy, unless otherwise notified by the instructor, under no circumstances may students record lectures, discussions, or classroom activities.
Class Climate:
Students will take collective responsibility for the success of every class discussion. You are expected not only to complete the required reading, viewings, and assignments, but also to think about them before class and to arrive in class with thoughts and questions. In class, all students will listen actively to and engage productively with their classmates, and all will express thoughts in a respectful manner that advances the conversation. Practices that disrespect one’s colleagues and hinder conversation are unacceptable (for example, texting, interrupting, hogging the floor, launching personal attacks, or surfing the web). Some of our required readings and viewings include nudity and/or explicit sexual content. Some of our readings and viewings represent violence and racist imagery. If you do not wish to engage with such materials, you should not enroll in this course. If you have questions about the content of this course, you are of course welcome to speak with the instructor.

Grading Policies 
Participation/Quizzes/Discussions: 25%

Weekly Schedule (14 Weeks)
Week 1  3/5: Introduction: Conceptualizing the Korean Wave
Themes: Defining Hallyu, historical context, and theoretical frameworks for studying transnational pop culture.
Readings:
Chua Beng Huat, “Conceptualizing an East Asian Popular Culture,” Inter-Asia Cultural Studies (2004).
Doobo Shim, “Hybridity and the Rise of Korean Popular Culture in Asia,” Media, Culture & Society (2006).
Audiovisual: Clips from Winter Sonata (2002) and Gangnam Style (2012).
Week 2  3/12: Historical Foundations: Cinema from Colonial Era to Golden Age
Themes: The roots of Korean screen culture, colonialism, post-war society, and the "Golden Age" of film.
Readings:
Nayoung Aimee Kwon, “Collaboration, Coproduction, and Code-Switching...” Cross-Currents (2012).
Steven Chung, “Regimes within Regimes: Film and Fashion in the Korean 1950s,” from Split Screen Korea (2014).
Audiovisual: Madame Freedom (1956) - Full Film.
Week 3  3/19: The Blockbuster Era and Transnational Genre-Bending
Themes: The Korean Film Renaissance, genre hybridity, and achieving global visibility.
Readings:
Christina Klein, “Why American Studies Needs to Think About Korean Cinema...” American Quarterly (2008).
Jinhee Choi, “Blockbusters, Korean Style,” from The South Korean Film Renaissance (2010).
Audiovisual: The Host (2006) - Full Film.
Week 4  3/26: Soft Power and the Cultural Industries， 
or Guest lecture TBD
Themes: The role of the state, cultural policy, and the deliberate construction of "soft power."
Readings:
Koichi Iwabuchi, “Pop-culture diplomacy in Japan: soft power, nation branding...” International Journal of Culture Policy (2015).
Chua Beng Huat, “Pop Culture as Soft Power,” from Structure, Audience and Soft Power in East Asian Pop Culture (2012).
Audiovisual: Episode 1 of Dae Jang Geum (Jewel in the Palace) (2003).
Week 5 4/2: The Politics of Gender and Body
Themes: Manufactured masculinity/femininity, the female gaze, the idol industry, and gender inequality.
Readings:
Sun Jung, “K-Pop Idol Boy Bands and Manufactured Versatile Masculinity...” from Korean Masculinities and Transcultural Consumption (2011).
Yeran Kim, “Idol republic: the global emergence of girl industries and the commercialization of girl bodies,” Journal of Gender Studies (2011).
Audiovisual: Music video compilations of BTS and BLACKPINK; clips from Descendants of the Sun.
Week 6  4/9: Media, Memory, and Democratization
Themes: How screen culture engages with national trauma, historical memory, and social movements.
Readings:
Manas Ghosh, “History, nation, and memory in south Korean cinema: Lee Chang-dong’s Peppermint Candy,” Asian Cinema (2012).
Audiovisual: Peppermint Candy (1999) - Full Film.
Week 7  4/16: Transnational Flows: Remakes, Adaptations, and Fandoms
Themes: Cultural translation, untranslatability, and the active role of fans in the K-Wave.
Readings:
Henry Jenkins, “Thinking Transnationally,” from Spreadable Media (2013).
Tian Li, "Rhizome in the shadows: transplantation of Korean Running Man..." Continuum (2019).
Audiovisual: Clips from Korean Running Man vs. its Chinese remake; fan-made content.
Week 8  4/23: Midterm Exam
Week 9  4/30: Global Phenomena: Parasite and the Politics of Class
Themes: Neoliberalism, social inequality, and the global reception of a landmark film.
Readings:
Dal Yong Jin, “Cultural politics in Korea’s contemporary films under neoliberal globalization,” Media, Culture, and Society (2006).
Seow Ting Lee, “Film as cultural diplomacy: South Korea’s national branding through Parasite (2019),” Place Branding and Public Diplomacy (2021).
Audiovisual: Parasite (2019) - Full Film.
Week 10  5/7: Digital Frontiers: Webtoons, K-Dramas, and Transmedia Storytelling
Guest Lecture by Professor Dal Yong Jin, Simon Fraser University
Themes: The infrastructure of the K-Wave: digital platforms, transmedia ecosystems, and the webtoon-to-screen pipeline.
Readings:
TBD by the guest speaker 
Week 11  5/14: Zombies and Techno-Futures: Posthumanism in K-Content
Themes: Technophobia, posthumanism, and social allegory in Korean (post)apocalyptic stories.
Readings:
Sarah Juliet Lauro and Karen Embry, “A Zombie Manifesto: The Nonhuman Condition in the Era of Advanced Capitalism” Boundary 2 (2008).

Themes: Ethics, affect, and the portrayal of North Korea in South Korean media; concepts of cosmopolitanism.
Readings:
Shine Choi, “I love you, do you love me?: Conflict, melodrama, and reconciliation...” from Reimagining North Korea in International Politics (2015).
Audiovisual: Joint Security Area 
Screening flips in class from: Crash Landing on You (2019), Episode 1.
Week 13  5/28:  Law, Justice, and Media: The "Dogani Effect" and Virtual Publics
Themes: This week explores how K-content engages with the legal system, social justice, and trauma. We analyze how films and TV shows can catalyze real-world legal and social change, creating a "virtual space" for public deliberation. We'll examine the adaptation of real events, the representation of justice, and the role of digital media in feminist and activist movements.
Readings:
Tian Li, “Opening a Virtual Space Before the Door of the Law: The Dogani Effect from Silenced to Angels Wear White,” positions: asia critique (2024). (This is your own work, perfectly connecting Korean and Chinese media through this theme).

Course Syllabus
Korea University 
BUSS 394-02, Spring 2026
Instructor:	Class meetings:
	Tai Gyu Kim		LG-POSCO 432
	E-mail: kimt@korea.ac.kr	    Mondays and Wednesdays
	Office: LG-POSCO 422		1:30-2:45
	Phone: 3290-2828
	TA: 
	Office Hours: By appointment		
Course Overview:
The course is designed to help develop negotiation skills experientially (through participation in negotiation role-play exercises) and to understand negotiation in useful analytical frameworks.  The following is a partial list of course objectives: 
Improve your ability to negotiate effectively
Be able to analyze negotiation situation
Develop a strategic plan for effective negotiation
Gain an intellectual understanding of negotiator behavior
Gain confidence as a negotiator 
Course Material: 
We will use the total of ten role-play exercises published by Dispute Resolution Research Center (DRRC) of Northwestern University. These are copy-righted materials and there is a charge of $3.50 for the usage of each copy. For the purpose of convenience, I will distribute e-copies of those materials for each exercise. You are responsible to directly pay DRRC for the cases that you use at the end of the semester. There is no textbook required. But if you need some guiding textbook on negotiations, I encourage you to use “Negotiation: Readings, exercises, and cases” by Lewicki, Saunders, Minton and Barry, and/or “The Mind and Heart of the Negotiator” by Leigh Thompson. Other reading materials will be handed out in class.
Important First Week Attendance Policy:
The course format is different from other regular lecture-type classes since it is based on experiential learning that includes interactions with other students. DURING THE FIRST WEEK OF THE SEMESTER, we will discuss basic rules and theories with which you will use for role-play exercises for the rest of the semester. Therefore, your absence during the first week sessions will critically influence other students’ learning experiences in a very negative way. For such reasons, I strongly discourage students missing any of the first week sessions (for any reasons) from taking the course in order to protect other students’ learning opportunities. 
Assignments and grading: 
Your final grade will be based on:
Participation	 				             30%
Midterm                                                                       20%
Real World Negotiation				  30%
Reflection Paper					  20%	
Participation (30%)
Your participation grade consists of three things:
Attendance
The structure and content of the negotiations class makes it extremely important that you participate in all negotiation exercises and discussions. The course attendance policy requires that if you must miss a negotiation exercise, it is your responsibility to contact me before the class materials are sent (usually a week before). Failure to contact me and make arrangements for your negotiating partner (either by providing a substitute or rescheduling to negotiate outside of class) will result in a drop of 1/2 of a grade (for example, A+ to A or B+ to B) for the course.
Preparation (20%)
Preparation is probably the single most important thing you can do to improve your performance in any negotiation. In class, it is essential that you read and prepare for every negotiation exercise. Lack of preparation destroys the value of in-class negotiations, not only for you, but also for your negotiating partners. Participation in the weekly negotiation exercises necessitates full preparation, and lack of preparation will be treated as an absence.
You will be required to turn in planning documents for each negotiation over the course of the semester. You may use the planning document attached to the back of syllabus, or you may create your own. I encourage you to create your own. It should include the things you find to be most useful. Your customized planning documents can and should be different for each different negotiation, and may be as long or short as you need it to be.
Planning documents must be handed in on the day you complete negotiation for which you prepared them. (Please use blackboard for negotiation plan submission)
In-class participation (10%)
In-class participation reflects your overall dedication and conscientiousness to the class discussions. During the debrief of each negotiation, I will solicit your inputs and thoughts about your own experiences with the negotiation exercise. The more you contribute and participate in this discussion, the more you will learn. Therefore, participation and interaction count. 
Midterm (20%)
There will be a mid-term that covers basic concepts and learning during the term. The exam will be based on an online submission in the format of open book, open note and open access to the web.  No make-up exam will be available without emergency situation with supporting evidence.
Real World Negotiation (30%)
Sometime during the semester, you will plan and execute a negotiation outside of class for something and report your strategy and negotiation results in a paper. You can negotiate for anything you like – a good or service, salary, whatever. The paper is not due until the end of semester, so you should have plenty of time to find an interesting negotiating opportunity. The paper should be no more than 2000 words of text (about 6 pages of double-spaced text in 12-point font, with one-inch margins all around). It is due at midnight on the day of the final class meeting (6/12). No late submission will be accepted.
Reflection papers (20%: two papers and 10% each)
Reflection assignment will give you an opportunity to think and reflect on your negotiations, your actions, your opponents, and yourself as well as receive more information and feedback about your negotiations from me. In addition, your opponents’ reflection papers allow you an insight into the minds of those with whom you negotiate. 
You must turn in TWO reflection papers during the semester. You may choose which negotiations you write reflection paper about. Each reflection paper should be less than three pages in length, and should be completed as soon as possible after the debriefing of that week’s negotiation exercise. When it is complete, e-mail copies of it to all the people involved in your negotiation, and submit another copy to me through blackboard. At the very latest, they are due 1 week after the negotiation debriefing. Late reflection papers will not be accepted.
The reflection papers should not be a blow-by-blow account of what happened in the negotiation, but should focus more on what you were thinking. The reflection papers should be useful to both you and your opponent(s). They should help you clarify what you learned and give feedback to your negotiating opponent(s). Your reflection papers might address some of the following:
What might you have done differently that would have improved your outcome?
What might your opponent have done differently that would have his/her outcome? What did your opponent overlook?
What did you learn about negotiation, bargaining, or conflict from this exercise?
What did you learn about yourself from this exercise?
What did you learn about the behavior of others?
How do the concepts presented in lectures or readings enrich your understanding of the process of this negotiation, its outcome, or your own style?

수업목표
▶ 이 과목은 디지털 시대에 문과대학 학생들이 필수적으로 알아야 할 다양한 기술이 인문학 분야에서 어떻게 활용되는지를 직접 배우고 연습해보는 기회를 제공한다.
▶ 4차 산업 혁명 시대에 새로운 기술 활용이 갖는 철학적 함의와 인간 본연의 정체성에 대해 성찰하고 토론하며 디지털 기술 활용 능력을 연계하여 다양한 사회문제를 포착하고 해결할 수 있는 능력을 키우는 것을 목표로 한다. 
▶ 분반별로 디지털 툴을 학습하고 활용하여 독자적인 인문학적 성찰을 제시하는 것을 목표로 하며 토론의 시간을 통해 서로의 생각을 공유하는 기회를 갖는다.
분반 소개
▶ 본 분반에서는 코딩을 처음 접하는 학생들을 대상으로 기초적인 코딩 능력을 습득하기 위한 강의가 진행된다. 프로그래밍 언어로는 2026년 현재 웹 개발, 데이터 분석, 인공지능 등 다양한 분야에서 전 세계적으로 널리 쓰이는 Python을 활용한다.
▶ 본 분반의 강의는 ‘디지털’, 그중에서도 코딩에 초점이 맞추어져 이루어진다. 따라서 강의 중 인문학적 내용을 직접 다루기보다는 인문학 데이터를 다루기 위한 기초 능력을 함양하는 데에 주력하게 될 것이다. 데이터로는 한국어 위주의 언어 데이터를 주로 활용한다.
▶ 강의와 함께 조 단위 실습이 이루어지며, 실습 결과를 발표하고 상호 평가하는 시간을 갖는다.
▶ 실습의 내용은 이미 갖추어져 있는 Python의 여러 기능들을 직접 구현해 보는 것이다. 이를 통해, 단순히 Python의 사용법을 익히는 데에 그치지 않고, 컴퓨터 프로그램이 작동하는 원리를 이해할 수 있도록 한다.
▶ 학생의 요청이 있을 시 수업과 관련한 면담을 진행할 수 있으며, 일시 및 장소는 별도로 협의한다.

Purposes
The purpose of this class is to introduce and explain agricultural policies in the sectors of agricultural production, distribution, consumption, and trade. In particular, this process investigates the impact of agricultural policy in Korea changes on agricultural markets and industries. Through this class, students can learn the importance of agricultural policy, which is the basis of the agricultural sector, and discuss interesting topics in the agricultural policy sector. I aim to introduce agricultural policies in each field in Korea, US, EU and help students understand why the policies were necessary in each situation. Regarding recent agricultural policies, I aim to enhance the content and understanding of the policies by utilizing audio-visual materials.

El objetivo de este curso de Español como Lengua Extranjera (ELE) de nivel inicial plus es desarrollar habilidades conversacionales sólidas. Se busca que los estudiantes adquieran confianza para participar en diálogos cotidianos, expresar ideas y comprender respuestas simples. A través de enfoques interactivos y prácticos, se fomentará la fluidez oral, el vocabulario útil y la comprensión auditiva, sentando una base efectiva para futuras interacciones en entornos de habla española.
이 초급 플러스 수준의 스페인어 강좌의 목표는 견고한 대화 능력을 개발하는 것입니다. 학생들이 일상 대화에 참여하고 아이디어를 표현하며 간단한 답변을 이해하는 능력을 키우는 것을 목표로 합니다. 상호작용적이고 실용적인 접근을 통해 구어 능력, 유용한 어휘, 청취 이해를 촉진하며, 이를 통해 효과적인 기반을 마련하여 향후 스페인어 환경에서의 상호작용에 대비할 수 있도록 합니다.
Materiales:
Materiales proporcionados por la lectora. Entre algunos de los materiales: presentaciones, materiales elaborados por la misma profesora, materiales extraídos de libros de texto, etc. 
강사가 제공하는 자료. 일부 자료로는 프레젠테이션, 강사가 직접 제작한 자료, 교과서에서 추출한 자료 등이 포함됩니다.
Notas:
La evaluación tendrá las siguientes partes enfocadas en la participación activa y la asistencia en clase: examen parcial 10%, examen final gramática 10%, examen final oral 20%, presentación 50% y participación y asistencia (incluye deberes) 10%. 
평가는 수업 내 활발한 참여와 출석에 중점을 둘 것입니다. 구성 요소는 다음과 같습니다: 중간 시험 10%, 문법 기말 시험 10%, 구어 기말 시험 20%, 발표 50% 그리고 참여 및 출석 (숙제 포함) 10%.

ACADEMIC ENGLISH Spring 2026 
Professor: Darius Goodwin, MA Applied Linguistics
Email: dariusgoodwin@gmail.com 		Office: Room 709 – IFLS building
Course Delivery Method: This course will be taught on campus.
Required Equipment: A notebook computer or tablet with Wi-Fi for on campus, in class writing. Please bring it to every class.
Introduction to the Course
	Welcome to Academic English.  In this semester, you will learn valuable language and academic skills that will help you succeed at university, and in your professional careers. Academic English can be challenging, so please ask me if you need help at any time. I enjoy teaching and I want to help you do well. It is important that you feel comfortable in the class, and that you learn useful skills for your future. If you have questions at any time, please let me know. Asking me questions can be an effective way of gaining confidence and practicing your English too.
This syllabus has information about your course. The important information will also be explained clearly in the first week of class. (You can find a schedule for the course on page 5 below.)
STUDY METHOD
This course will use short lectures, individual tasks, pairwork, group discussion, writing in class using Google Docs, and presentations.
A key feature of this course is that your learning is supported at every stage.
You are given time to work on some assessed tasks during class, when you can ask for clarification to ensure you are on track. You can also ask questions conveniently at other times using Google Docs comment feature, or by coming to office hours.
You are given clear checklists for assessed tasks, so you understand exactly how you are graded. You are encouraged to ask questions about these checklists to ensure you can do your best.
A positive class atmosphere with support from your classmates ensures you enjoy learning, feel comfortable and can fulfill your academic potential. 
I will help you make a shared Google folder with me, so I can give you feedback and answer your questions quickly.
II. COURSE OBJECTIVES: 
In Academic English, you will focus on developing academic writing, presentation and discussion skills.
At the end of the course, you will be able to:
write a 4-paragraph research essay in APA style
identify credible academic sources
use AI ethically to help you produce assignments
lead discussions about academic topics related to your interests
give an engaging short academic presentation 
use Google Docs, Google Forms, & Folders to collaborate  
III.COURSE REQUIREMENTS & GRADING CONSIDERATIONS:
Grade equivalents:
A+        	95-100                 A           90-94                   B+        85-89 		B   80-84
C+        	75-79                   C           70-74                   D+        65-69    		D   60-64   	
F           	0-59
Note: Nobody needs to fail Academic English. With your hard and focused work, successful learning is guaranteed.  
Attendance Policy
Students are permitted a maximum of 3 absences in total each semester without grade penalty (or a maximum of 4 if they are all officially excused absences. Documentation for officially excused absences only must be submitted via the K.U. portal.)
Officially Excused Absences 
death in the family (government issued death certificate)
hospitalization (hospital document giving dates of hospitalization)
military service (send photo of document from military)
school trips with a letter from the faculty dean, or by tradition a document from the student council
menstrual pain (notification via portal)
covid diagnosis (notification via portal)
Please note that for academic English courses if a student has more than 3 non-officially excused absences, during the course there is a -1% penalty for each extra day they are absent. 
If you miss more than 8 classes, you automatically fail the course. Please ask me at any time if you are unsure about the rules. I am here to help explain the policies. Attending as many classes as possible makes it easier for you to follow the course and do well.
Lateness: If you arrive more than 3 minutes late, you receive a late mark. Every 3 late marks equals one class absence. You are responsible for telling the teacher at the end of the class if you arrived late. I may not have noticed you joined late. If you do not tell the teacher, you could be marked absent. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the official start of the class, you are marked absent.
Test Days: If you miss an official test day (e.g. Writing 2 - Midterm in-class Writing, Your Presentation, Final Quiz), you receive a significant grade penalty unless you can prove officially with documentation signed by a doctor (의사소견서 or 의사진단서, not 진료확인서) that there was a genuine medical emergency requiring urgent hospital treatment. The documentation must show that the medical emergency prevented you from taking the test. If you miss your presentation for any other reason, the highest score you can achieve is 20/30 for the rescheduled assessment. If you miss the final exam, the highest score you can receive is 7/13. If you miss Writing 2 - midterm in class writing, there is an automatic 5-point penalty. It is extremely important for your grade that you attend these test days. Please set multiple alarms, so that it is impossible to miss a test day. These rules need to be strict to ensure fairness. There can be 150 students, and it is logistically very difficult to reschedule tests.
Other Late or Missing Assignments: If you fail to complete an assignment by the specified deadline, the penalty to your total grade for the course is 0.5%. if submitted within the next 24 hours, 1% within 48 hours, 1.5% within 72 hours, 2% within 96 hours etc. until the points for that task reach 0. However, if you completed the task before the deadline, but forgot to move the file to your folder, move the file, and email me and there is no late penalty. 
Missing Presentation Slide Deadline: Students must submit their presentation slides (Google Slides only) by 9pm the night before their presentation or receive a 4-point penalty. This is necessary so slides can be graded before your presentation day.
Asking for Help: If you have any difficulty understanding a task, it is very important to ask me for help as soon as possible. You can ask during class, or use Google Doc comment feature, or by email. I can also arrange to help you on Zoom. However, you should ask me early, and no later than 4 days before the assignment deadline, or you may not receive help in time. Please feel you can talk to me about any problems you have related to the course. 
Preparing & Submitting Assignments: On this course, all assignments must be written in Google Docs only so I can see the document history. I need to see how you developed your work at every stage. This helps to prove that it is your work and not AI Failure to write assignments in Google docs will result in grade penalties. Students must submit assignments by moving the Google Doc to the shared folder. If you can see the file in the shared folder, you have successfully submitted your work. Google Docs keeps a record of when the file was completed or changed. This helps you show it is your work.
Grade Questions: Questions about scores received for assignments must be asked within 7 days of receiving the score. Please do not ask professors to give you a higher grade as there are strict university rules against this. However, if you think there may have been a miscalculation or need further explanation to understand the score, please contact me immediately. I am very happy to meet you during my office hours if you need further explanation or have questions about your score.
Professionalism: Bringing a notebook computer/tablet, always producing outstanding work, speaking in English as much as possible, encouraging others to speak in English, being enthusiastic and focused on learning, asking questions and frequently contributing ideas, no inappropriate use of cell phone, trying to use the language and skills we have studied, etc. 
Webcams: If we need to move online temporarily (very unlikely), all students will need a webcam with a working microphone. 
Participation: If a student is not participating in activities or is disruptive, it can reduce their grade. As this is a language class, participation and collaboration with students and the professor is especially important to achieve the course's learning goals successfully. If there is a problem, the student will receive an email warning first. If the problem reoccurs, a penalty of 2% will be applied for each incident. However, this is extremely rare in my experience and has never happened at K.U. on any of my courses.
Cell phones: Generally, phones should be turned off. However, phones may be used for dictionary work and research. Naturally, Kakao and other social media should not be used during class as they can interfere with concentration and learning.
IV. OFFICE HOURS:
I have office hours every week. These will be announced in the first few days. These are great opportunities to ask me for help. I am also available at some other times if the office hours are not suitable. Please make an appointment by email. When you email me, can you always include your name, student number and class code. I look forward to seeing you either in my office (Room 709), or we can easily meet on Zoom.
V. PLAGIARISM: 
Copying some words/phrases or sentences from another person and claiming it as your own writing is not allowed.  Please do not copy. You should summarize and paraphrase others’ ideas and include a citation. I will teach you these important skills on the course. If three or more words are together in your writing or are copied directly from another source this can be plagiarism. Any assignment that has significant (more than 25 words) plagiarism will receive a zero. If you need help with an assignment, please ask me before the deadline. Please do not copy. I will know.
The use of AI and other writing tools should be limited to grammar and style corrections, and not to generate full sentences or paragraphs. Submitting work that is partially or completely generated by AI writing tools will result in a grade of zero for the assignment.
(It is important to note that AI writing tools cannot substitute for originality and critical analysis required for academic work.) As students write in Google Doc, I can review the file history to check that the assignment has been developed by you over time, and has not been copied and pasted from another source or A.I. This is why students must write their assignments in Google Docs. 
If AI is permitted to be used by the teacher for a specific class activity, they will inform you explicitly. Students should be careful to follow the instructions for AI use carefully. Please ask the teacher if you are unsure and feel free to discuss any concerns regarding the use of AI during office hours or by email. 
VI. ANNOUNCEMENTS & ADDITIONAL COURSE INFORMATION
Please make sure you have your correct email address on the university system. During the semester and before the grades are finalized, there will be announcements. It is also important to keep checking your email, especially after the final assessments in case I need to contact you about your work. Also, after the final grades are announced, please contact me immediately if you think there may be an error with your score. There is a short period when this is possible, but after this period has finished it is not possible to make changes to scores.

강의개요

중간시험 (30%)
기말시험 (40%)
출석 (20%)

A. 중간시험 (30%)
중간시험은 강의한 내용을 기초로 주어진다. 따라서 시험에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해서는 수업에 적극적으로 참여하여야 한다. 
B. 기말시험 (40%)
기말시험도 강의한 내용을 기초로 주어진다. 따라서 시험에서 좋은 성적을 받기 위해서는 수업에 적극적으로 참여하여야 한다. 
C. 출석 (20%) 
출석은 매 수업마다 확인하며 결석에 대해 1회당 2점(지각 또는 조퇴는 1회당 1점 )을 감점한다. 이것보다 중요한 것은 총 수업일수의 3분의 1이상 결석한 경우(28번의 수업중 10번 이상 결석한 경우)는 성적을 부여하지 않는다. 
참고: 정정기간 이후에 들어온 학생의 경우 정정기간 동안 배운 내용에 대한 과제로 출석을 대체한다
D. 수업참여도 (10%) 
수업시 제시된 주제에 대한 수업시 토론실 참여를 기준으로 다음과 같이 0점에서 10점으로 평가한다.
