영미문학특수과제 II (ENGL 422)
SPRING 2026
강의시간: 화목 10:30 am-11:45am
강의실: 교육관 403호 
담당: 오한솔 (ohhansol@korea.ac.kr)
I. 강의 개요
이번 학기 특수과제 수업에서는 지난 사반세기 동안 발표된 동시대 미국 희곡 작품들을 선독합니다. 
세대, 계층, 정체성, 몸, 기술, 예술, 이주, 다양성, 권력, 노동, 돌봄, 장애와 같은 우리 시대의 화두들은 미국 연극에서 어떻게 다루어지고 있을까요? 이번 학기 수업에서는 다양한 주제와 형식의 희곡들을 함께 읽으며, 이러한 작품들이 한국의 독자 또는 관객들과 어떻게 공명할 수 있는지 고민해 봅니다. 또한 원하는 콘텐츠를 원하는 때에 원하는 만큼 원하는 방식으로 소비할 수 있는 초개인화된 미디어 환경 속에서, 연극이라는 매체는 어떤 울림과 의미를 가질 수 있는지 생각해봅니다. 연극을 통해 다른 삶을 감각하고 상상하는 일은 오늘날 우리에게 어떤 의미를 지닐까요? 
희곡이라는 장르를 더 깊이 알고 싶은 학생들, 미국 희곡 개관 수업에서 접하기 어려운 동시대 작품들이 궁금한 학생들에게 추천합니다.
II. 강의 교재
수업에서 사용되는 모든 읽기 자료는 LMS를 통해 pdf 로 제공됩니다. 
수업 중 다루는 작품들의 영어 난이도는 높지 않은 편이지만, 대부분 우리말 번역본이 없는 작품들입니다. 
매주 해당 차시의 읽기 자료를 수업 전에 미리 읽어오는 것을 전제로 수업을 진행하며, 수업에는 반드시 텍스트를 지참하기 바랍니다. 
강의와 토론, 과제 및 퀴즈는 모두 지정된 텍스트의 영어 원문을 기반으로 합니다. 
III. 성적 평가   
출석.......................................................................................................................................... 15 % 
*공결을 포함해 전체 수업일수의 1/3(10회)을 결석하는 경우 자동으로 F 처리됩니다. 결석은 사전에 고지하고 증빙자료를 제출하기 바랍니다 (공결처리). 
* 무단결석 1회당 최종 성적에서 0.5%씩 감점하며, 4회 이상 무단결석 하는 경우 1 full letter grade 감점 (ex. Final calculated grade A+  Final grade B+; B  C)
* 수업 시작 10 분 후 도착 = 지각 1회, 지각 3 회 = 결석1 회. 
* 20 분 이상 지각 및 수업 도중 10분 이상 강의실 무단 이탈= 결석 1 회. 
* 메신저 및 소셜미디어를 사용하거나 또는 다른 수업 과제를 하다가 지적을 받는 경우, 해당 수업에서 결석 처리합니다.
*조기취업자의 경우 전체 수업일수의 1/2 이상 결석하는 경우 학칙에 따라 학점을 부여할 수 없습니다. (포털을 통해 유고결석 신청 필수)
참여 ………………………………………………………………………………………………….… 15%
중간, 기말고사 .……..………………….…………………………………………..………………..... 50%
각 25%, 100점 만점, 대면 지필고사. 시험 형식에 대해서는 수업 중 안내. 
조별 발표 (Staged Reading) ……..…………..………………….…..….…………..…………………. 20% 
IV. 수업 커뮤니케이션 관련 
수업과 관련한 공지사항은 LMS 공지 또는 개인 이메일로 이루어집니다. 공지 내용을 제때 확인, 숙지하는 것은 전적으로 본인의 책임이며, 커뮤니케이션 문제가 생기지 않도록 학기 초에 반드시 다음 사항을 체크하세요.
본인이 가장 자주 확인하는 이메일 계정이 LMS와 연동되어 있는가? 중요한 공지사항과 수업 알림을 제때 받을 수 있도록 해당 이메일을 자주 확인해 주세요.
수업 첫날 이메일 수신이 됐는가? 이메일이 수신함에 없는 경우, 스팸 메일함을 확인하고 수업 관련 알림이 스팸으로 분류되지 않도록 조치하세요.
V. 강의실 에티켓
건전한 학습 분위기를 조성할 수 있도록 모든 구성원의 적극적인 협조를 요청합니다. 수업 중 메신저, 소셜미디어, 수업과 무관한 웹서핑 등 멀티태스킹은 하지 않습니다. 즐겁고 유익한 강의 진행을 위해 교수자와 학우들에 대한 예의와 존중을 갖추기 바랍니다. 
전자기기 사용: 학습과 무관한 용도로 전자기기 사용을 금지합니다. 필기 목적의 전자기기로는 태블릿과 랩탑을 권장하며, 휴대폰은 필기 용도로 사용할 수 없습니다.
수업 내용은 녹음 및 녹화가 불가능합니다. 
VI. Schedule Breakdown
*상세 일정은 상황에 따라 변동될 수 있으며, 읽기 및 영상 자료가 추가될 수 있습니다. 
이 경우 별도의 공지를 통해 안내할 예정입니다. 
한 학기 동안 수업의 구성원들은 하나의 학문적 공동체를 이루며, 각자는 이 공동체에 어떤 방식으로 기여할 수 있는지를 고민하고, 실천하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 이 수업에서는 다양한 형태의 기여를 장려하지만, 참여 평가의 중심은 수업 중 이루어지는 토론 참여입니다. 질문을 던지거나 자신의 해석을 나누는 것, 다른 사람의 발언에 응답하고 연결하는 행위는 어떤 것이라도 환영입니다.
구성:
작품에서 1-2 장면을 낭독 (20분) 
발표 장면 및 연출적 선택에 대한 간단한 설명 및 Q & A 진행 (10분)

한국어로 번역/각색도 가능. 15분 내외.
미니멀한 소품/분장 사용 가능. 
연기용 대본은 하드 카피로 지참. 휴대폰/아이패드는 소품인 경우를 제외하고 사용 불가.
*수강 인원에 따라 횟수 및 분량 변동 가능. 기타 세부사항은 수업 중 안내.

수업목표 일반 | 의생명 연구를 위한 인공지능 분야의 기초가 되는 확률, 통계, 및 관련 수학을 이해한다. This course aims to provide a foundational understanding of probability, statistics, and related mathematical concepts for machine learning methods in biomedical research.
세부목표 1 | 생명현상의 불확실성을 확률적 사고를 통해 정량적으로 해석할 수 있다. Students will be able to quantitatively interpret uncertainty in biological phenomena using probabilistic thinking.
세부목표 2 | 가설 검증 및 통계적 기법을 통해 의생명데이터를 해석하고 생물학적 통찰을 이끌어 낼 수 있다. Students will be able to analyze biomedical data using hypothesis testing and statistical methods to derive biologically meaningful insights.
세부목표 3 | 다변량 생명데이터의 구조를 파악하고 다룰 수 있다. Students will be able to understand and handle the structure of multivariate biological data.

학점(시간) : 3(3)
담당교수 및 연락처 : 
김성진 / 02-3290-4695 (우정간호학관 521호) 
ssjj910523@korea.ac.kr
교과목 개요 :
모성간호(Maternity & Women’s Health Nursing)는 임신, 출산, 산욕과정에 있는 모성, 고위험 모성 및 생식기 건강문제를 가진 여성의 생식건강 증진에 초점을 둔다. 학생들은 모성간호에 대해 배움으로써 여성의  생리· 심리사회적 특성, 기본 간호요구, 건강 영향요인과 건강관련 과학적 지식 및 원리의 학습을 통해 간호인으로서의 비판적 사고 능력 및 통합적용 능력을 함양하게 된다. 
모성간호학Ⅰ 교과목에서는 생식주기에 있는 여성의 정상 생식관련 해부, 생리 및 성 (Sexuality), 정상 임신과정에 있는 여성과 가족이 경험하게 되는 건강 및 간호요구, 그리고 생식기 건강문제가 있는 여성과 가족이 경험하게 되는 건강 및 간호요구를 사정(assessment)하고 이를 중재(intervention)하는 방법을 학습한다.

Course Description
This course introduces the basic mathematical foundation of probability theory and random processes. The basic concepts of Probability, random variables, multiple random variables, the sum of random variables, long-term averages, and random processes will be covered. The probability theory serves as a foundational model for many engineering applications, including communications, control theory, and robotics. In particular, the gap between the simplified model based on classical physics and real experiments can be reduced to estimate expected outcomes in real applications.

Main textbook (not required): Leon-Garcia, A., 2017. Probability, statistics, and random processes for electrical engineering.

Learning Outcomes
A student who successfully fulfills the course requirements will have demonstrated: 
A basic concept of probability as a measure of the events in the sample space.  
Understand the mapping from the event to measurable space using real numbers (random variable)
An ability to analyze higher-dimensional uncertainty using the multiple random variables (Multiple random variable)
An ability to analyze a change in uncertainty with respect to the observation time (Random process)
These outcomes will be measured via assessments including homework assignments, exams, and 
projects.

Course Description & Objectives 
This course will provide students with an overview of the key psychological concepts and theories and how those apply to branding and marketing. The ultimate goal of this course is to provide students with a sound understanding of the dynamics of the psychological mechanism underlying the processes of branding including planning, execution, and effects and how branding impacts consumers.
Course Format
Class presentations and the reading assignments are designed to motivate students to engage in an active learning procedure. Offered in the formats of lecture, discussion, and in-class assignments, the material presented in class will supplement and complement the reading assignments by providing focus and additional insight on the major topics. Students are expected to come to class prepared to actively participate in the class activities.
Course Website
You are encouraged to keep up with your performance in the class, pick up both lecture materials and reading assignments and other useful information about course content, and check grades and announcements by visiting Blackboard regularly. Be sure to receive emails from the professor and the TA by registering the email address you regularly check in the system.
Course Requirements & Evaluation
Midterm					100 
Individual/Team assignments 			100
Group project*					200
Total						400 points
* Group project grades will be adjusted based on peer evaluations.
A standard scale will be used to determine overall letter grades. Your course grade is based on your total points score. I will add together all the points you earned and divide by 4 to yield a percentage score. 
Borderline Grades Stay Borderline: Every semester, some students score just below the borderline of the next highest grade. Often students believe that a grade just below a cutoff guarantees them the higher score. This is NOT correct. Borderline grades, even 1/10 of a point below the cutoff, do NOT guarantee a higher grade. It is possible that I will raise grades above a borderline, but this will be my decision – a decision that I will not negotiate or even discuss. I have great sympathy for people who find themselves in that position, but I have also found that raising those grades simply uncovers a new group of students whose grades are near the new borderline. This situation makes everybody edgy. Therefore, my policy must be that borderline grades stay as they are. 
Exam 
Midterm will be on date indicated in the class schedule. Midterm is designed to test the students’ knowledge and application of the main ideas covered in the text chapters, class discussions and exercises covered within the exam units specified by the course schedule. No early or make-up exam will be given. Any student who misses an exam will receive a zero for the exam. Extremely exceptional cases that the university officially recommends might be considered for a make-up. Exam will cover materials presented in class and from assigned readings. In general, they will consist of T/F, multiple choice, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer questions. A study guide and a review session will be provided prior to the exam. After the exam is graded and the grades are posted, students will be given ONE WEEK to look over the exam during the professor’s office hours. Any disagreements concerning the grading of each test must be resolved during this one-week period. 
Individual/Team Assignments
Students will work to complete in-class exercises and homework assignments throughout the term that are intended to help them to gain experiential learning as to the course topics. There will be an undetermined number of in-class exercises. These exercises are designed to help students keep up with the pace of the class and to improve their understanding of the course material. These exercises will be distributed and completed during the class time (“in class”) and therefore they cannot be made up unless the professor excuses the absence in advance. If you are absent and have a valid excuse (i.e., serious illness or family emergency), you must bring the appropriate documentation on your first day back. 
Attendance & Participation
Class attendance is the student’s responsibility. Students are expected to arrive at class on time and to stay for the entire class period (or until dismissed). Random arrivals and exits are unprofessional and distracting. I will keep track of the frequency and quality of your contributions throughout the semester. I will not be taking attendance every class, but most of them. Any undocumented absence will not be excused. If you are absent and have valid excuse (e.g., serious illness or family emergency), you must bring the appropriate documentation on your first day back. It is not enough just to come up and tell me where you were. Make every effort to schedule doctors’ appointments, job interviews and other events so that they do not conflict with any of your classes.  
Students are responsible for any information missed during an absence.  Handouts or lecture notes from previous days are NOT available from the professor.  Significant absence from class, team, and other meetings can reduce your final grade in the course by up to two letter grades. Attendance of 70%, excluding tests, will be used as an operational definition of “minimum reasonable attendance.” Attitude will also be considered in determining final class participation grades. 
Group Project
This group project includes defining the consumer behavior and branding problems, designing a study, planning the data analysis, collecting and analyzing the data, interpreting the results and presenting the results/conclusions. The written analysis will be presented in a professional manner including a title page and in a binder or folder. Each group will give a presentation explaining their consumer analysis and branding campaign. The time limit allowed each group will be determined once the number of groups is established. All members of the group must contribute to the preparation of the project and participate in the presentation. The details of this project will be explained to you early in the semester. 
This is a group grade so all students will have a chance, at the end of the semester, to evaluate the level of participation of the members in their group. Note that peer evaluations constitute a substantial portion of your group project grade. Since it is impossible for me to be present at all of your team meetings to see who actually is doing most of the work, and who is trying to get a grade based on the work of their teammates, I rely on each of you to be my eyes and ears.
Other Issues

If you bring a computer to class, multitask modestly and discreetly. Excessive searching, messaging, or typing is distracting to other students and rude to the instructor. 
Rude behavior such as talking, chatting, Internet surfing, or other disruptive or distracting behavior will not be tolerated in class.
You may contact me by my office telephone or email. In general, I prefer email.

Policy on Scholastic Dishonesty
The University defines academic dishonesty as cheating, plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, falsifying academic records, and any act designed to avoid participating honestly in the learning process. By accepting this syllabus, you have agreed to these guidelines and must adhere to them. Scholastic dishonesty damages both the student's learning experience and readiness for the future demands of a work-career. Students who violate University rules on scholastic dishonesty are subject to disciplinary penalties, including the possibility of failure in the course and/or dismissal from the University.

Purpose of Advanced Reading 
This course is for high-intermediate to advanced students, and is designed to reinforce the

select texts independently to supplement those used in the classroom.
select challenging texts to support their learning needs and special interests.
select texts to increase their range of interest.
refine and extend their own processes and strategies in exploring, interpreting, and reflecting on sophisticated texts and tasks

12. | Learners can use generative AI tools like ChatGPT to enhance their learning outcomes(For example: ask ChatGPT to check their work for mistakes) and have positive educational experiences.(For example: ask to explain terms or concepts from class that the student cannot understand themselves.)
However, if students use generative AI in class without basic guidelines (For example: to create the answers to an assignment), it may negatively impact the quality of teaching and learning.
Common negative impacts include:
(1) Violations of academic integrity, such as plagiarism and cheating.
(2) Decline in critical thinking, creative thinking, and problem-solving skills
due to over-reliance on generative AI.
(3) Acquisition of inaccurate or biased information.
(4) Reinforcement of entrenched stereotypes.
 “There is no royal road to learning.” (Euclid)  If you use generative Ai to do your work for you, you have not learned the skills you took the course to learn and so have wasted your money.

개요 | 유기화학 과목은 유기화합물의 구조, 명명법, 성질 및 주요 반응 메커니즘을 학습하여, 유기반응을 이해하고 예측하는 능력을 키우는 데 목적이 있다.
유기화학은 생명체를 이루는 분자 구조와 반응을 이해하는 데 필수적이며, 신약 개발과 대사 과정 연구 등 생명과학 전반에서 중요하다.
수강(권장)대상 학생 | 기초 화학 지식을 갖춘 생명공학(과학), 화학, 약학, 의학 등 관련 전공자
Undergraduate students with a basic background in chemistry, including majors in biotechnology, life sciences, chemistry, pharmacy, medicine, or related fields
선이수과목(권장) | 일반화학
수업목표 일반 | 유기화합물의 구조, 명명법, 반응 메커니즘 및 물리적화〮학적 성질을 학습하여 유기화학 반응을 예측하고 분석할 수 있는 능력을 기른다.
By studying the structures, nomenclature, reaction mechanisms, and physical and chemical properties of organic compounds, students develop the ability to predict and analyze organic reactions.
세부목표 1 | 공유결합, 극성, 입체화학 등 기본 개념 습득:
유기화학에서 중요한 결합의 특성과 분자의 입체구조(입체화학)를 이해하여, 분자의 물리적화〮학적 성질과 반응성을 설명할 수 있다.
Grasp fundamental concepts such as covalent bonding, polarity, and stereochemistry:
Understand key chemical principles including bonding characteristics and stereochemical properties to explain the physical and chemical behavior of organic molecules.
세부목표 2 | 주요 유기반응 메커니즘의 이해 및 적용:
친전자성친〮핵성 치환반응, 첨가반응, 제거반응 등 유기반응의 기본 메커니즘을 이해하고, 이를 통해 유기반응의 반응 경로를 예측할 수 있다.
Comprehend and apply basic organic reaction mechanisms:
Study fundamental mechanisms such as nucleophilic and electrophilic substitution, addition, and elimination reactions, and apply this knowledge to predict reaction outcomes, particularly in biological contexts.
세부목표 3 | 생명과학 및 생명공학과의 연계성 인식:
유기화학이 단백질, 핵산, 효소 반응 등 생명과학의 다양한 분야에 어떻게 응용되는지를 이해함으로써, 생명공학적 문제 해결에 유기화학 지식을 통합할 수 있는 능력을 기른다.
Recognize the relevance of organic chemistry in biotechnology and life sciences:
Understand how organic chemistry underpins key biological processes and apply this knowledge to solve problems in molecular biology, biochemistry, and biotechnology.

과목 개요/ 설명:
기업은 혁신하거나 그렇지 않으면 살아남을 수 없다고들 한다.  이 수업에서는 이처럼 기업의 생존과 관련한 중요한 이슈인 Entrepreneurship을 다루고자 한다. Entrepreneurship 에 대해서는 광범위한 개념으로 정의하며, 이는 기업이 인력과 자원들을 동원하여 가치를 창출하는 것과 관련된 모든 아이디어들이 정당화되는 일련의 과정이다. 이 수업을 통해서 중점을 두는 부분은 기업이 어떻게 사업을 시작하고 발전해 나가는지에 대하여 살펴보는 것이다. 
이 과목은 신규사업을 시작하고 운영하는 데에 필요한 프로세스와 기술들을 살펴보는 개괄적인 과목이다. 학생들은, 비즈니스 아이디어 포착, 비즈니스 아이디어 평가, 그리고 적합한 비즈니스 모델을 정립하는 것에 대하여 학습하게 될 것이다. 수업에서는 신규사업 기회와 시장에서 존재하는 불확실성 그리고 기업의 행동양식에 대해 공부하게 된다. 
특히, 이 수업은 팀 단위로 진행이 되며, 학생들의 다양성에 기반하여 팀이 정해진다. 예를 들어, 경영학과 학생들은 타 대학 학생들과 한 팀이 되어 창의적인 사업계획서를 작성해야 한다.  
수업 참여 학생들은 학기말 창업 경진대회에 출전하면 우수팀에 대해 시제품 제작비 및 창업활동 공간지원 등의 혜택이 부여 된다. 
특히, 이 수업에서는 문제해결을 통한 신사업 창출을 강조한다. 문제 해결이 소비자의 문제이면 일반적인 기업이 되지만, 사회적인 문제를 해결하는 것을 본업으로 하는 기업이면 사회적 가치 기반의 스타트업이 된다. 창의적인 문제 해결 영역이 사회적 가치 기반의 스타트업의 근본임을 염두에 두고, 비즈니스 모델, 워크샵, 주제 발표 등과 같은 활동을 통해 초기 기업을 육성하게 된다. 
수업에서는 벤처 창업을 위한 경영과정의 전반에 대해 이해하고자 한다. 이를 통해, 학생들은 벤처 기업 내부 혁신의 성공과 실패를 좌우하는 요소들에 대해 규명하는 법을 배울 것이다. 또한, 수업 전반에 사용되는 분석의 단위는 기업 단위에 기반을 두고 있음을 명심해야 한다 (개인수준의 창의성 개발은 본 수업의 주요 강조사항이 아님).
이 수업은 또한 벤처 기업의 장기적인 전략적 비전을 어떻게 창출하고, 유지하며, 더 나아가 이러한 비전에 상응하는 경쟁 전략을 어떻게 수행할 것인지에 대한 내용을 담고 있다. 이를 위해, 이 수업은 마케팅, 회계, 재무, 그리고 경영관리와 같은 경영학의 모든 기능적 영역을 포괄하고 있다. 기업이 전략적 포지션을 어떻게 수정하고 발전시켜 나갈지를 더욱 깊이 이해하기 위하여 케이스, 외부전문가 강좌, 사업 계획서 작성 등의 과제를 병행한다. 
마지막으로, 이 수업에서는 학생들이 자신의 아이디어를 효과적으로 소통하는 것이 매우 중요하다. 훌륭한 의사소통 기술을 타고난 사람은 드물기 때문에 이 수업은 더 나은 의사소통을 배울 수 있도록 설계되었다. 
수업 목적:
사업 기회의 탐색: 사업 기회를 어떻게 발견하고 추구할 것인지, (개인 혹은 기업 단위)
위험 요소들 분석: 1) 사업 시작과 관련한 근본적 이슈들을 어떻게 정의할 것인 지와 2) 위험요소, 문제상황 등을 어떻게 평가할 것인지,
이론과 실제의 연결: 1) 아이디어를 어떻게 아이템으로 변환시킬 것인지 2) 벤처 기업의 전략을 어떻게 디자인하고 실행할 것인지, 
재무, 회계, 관리, 마케팅 및 경제 분야 등을 포함한 다양한 영역들의 지식을 통합하고 분석적 기술을 적용. 이를 통해 전략적 이슈를 규명 및 분석하고, 기업의 경쟁 우위를 창출 및 유지시키는 계획 실행을 발전시켜 나가고자 함.

출석
출석은 매 수업시간 체크한다. 2번 지각은 결석 한번으로 처리됨. 15분 이상 늦을 시 지각으로 간주. 3-4번 결석시 성적이 한 단계 내려감 (예, A B). 5번 이상 결석 시 자동으로 F처리됨. 취업관련 활동으로 수업에 참여하지 못할 때에도 예외 없이 결석으로 처리됨. 중간 고사나 기말 시험을 대체하는 어떠한 종류의 보충 시험이나 보고서가 없음을 주지할 것. 학교에서 공식적으로 인정하는 사유를 제외하고, 시험에 빠질 시에 시험 점수는 0점 처리됨.
팀
팀 스킬은 사업을 위해 꼭 필요한 요소임. 팀 성공을 이끌어내고 기여하는 정도에 따라 팀 성적과 개인 성적이 결정됨. 조직과 마찬가지로 팀은 구성원으로부터 자원과 경쟁력을 끌어오게 됨. 멤버들 간 각각의 역량을 고려하여 팀 내 활동을 배분할 것이며, 팀 배정은 다양성을 고려하여 이루어질 것임 (예: 경영학과 학생 + 타 대학 학생). 이를 통해, 팀 구성은 실제 사업을 런칭 시키는데 도움이 되도록, 다양한 경력과 멤버쉽을 기반으로 이루어 질 것임 (개인의 선택에 의한 구성이 아님). 팀 사례 발표는 oral과 written presentation으로 나누어 점수를 매기게 됨. 
팀 구성원 간 평가. 팀 구성원간 평가에서 좋은 평가를 받기 위해서는 책임감을 가져야 함.
자주 의사소통하고, 모임에 참여하고, 맡은 임무를 시간 내에 완수하고 또한 팀 활동을 성공적으로 이끌도록 노력할 것. 팀 내 구성원이 가진 자원을 최대한 활용하도록 할 것. 모든 멤버가 서로 경쟁하는 것이 아니라 서로의 부족한 부분을 보완하는 것이 중요함. 다면평가의 결과를 바탕으로 팀 구성원들은 개개인이 다른 평가 점수를 받게 됨. 
평가
실제 사업을 하게 되면 거래 파트너, 부하직원들, 동료들, 그리고 고객들을 매일매일 접하게 되고 이에 대한 준비 또한 매일매일 해야 함. 학생들 역시, 한 학기라는 시간 속에서 바쁜 스케쥴을 벼락치기하는 것이 아니라, 매 시간 수업에 대한 준비를 철저히 해야 함. 따라서, 학생들의 성과는 해당 수업 시간 동안 다룰 교재와 지식에 기반하여, 퀴즈와 참여를 통해 거의 매 수업시간 평가됨. 학생들은 수업에 대한 준비 없이 단지 “나타나기”만 해서는 안됨. 반드시 철저한 준비를 하고 올 것! 만약 학생들의 수업 관련 성과가 심각하게 좋지 않을 경우 피드백을 받게 됨. 피드백은 학생들이 원하는 최종 성적을 보장할 수 있도록 결점을 수정하고 적절한 수업참여를 할 수 있는 기회를 제공할 것임. 더불어 한 학기 동안 다양한 방식으로 수업이 진행됨. 대부분의 수업은 강의와 토론으로 이루어짐. 또한 실제 창업 아이템 선정과 경제성 평가 등으로 수업이 진행되기도 함. 성적은 다음과 같이 평가됨.

∙ [출석] 
-1/3 이상 결석시 성적부여 불가, 특정 사유에 한해 출석인정신청 및 시험 불응시 신청 가능, 단 출석인정 제외하고 1/2 이상 실제 출석 필요함

∙ [학습윤리]
 -대학의 목적과 본교 교육이념에 따라 성실하고 정직한 마음과 열정적인 태도로 모든 학습에 적극적으로 참여
 -고등교육을 받는 교양인으로서의 품위를 유지하며, 도덕적 민감성을 바탕으로 창의적 학문탐구에 정진
 -교육활동과 관련하여 교원 및 동료학생과의 약속을 성실히 이행
 -교원과 동료학생의 인격을 존중하고 기본적인 예의를 준수
 -학문 공동체의 일원으로서 학문의 진실성을 지키며, 본교 「AI 활용 가이드」를 성실히 준수
 -강의계획서 등을 충분히 탐색하여 자신의 학문적 탐구 방향과 미래 비전에 부합하는 교과목을 신중히 선택
 -매 수업에 적극적으로 임할 수 있도록 수업자료를 사전에 탐독하고 준비
 -정해진 수업시간을 준수하며, 결석·지각·중도 이탈 등으로 타인의 학습을 방해하지 않도록 유의
 -출석 관련 위계행위(대리출석 등) 금지
 -모든 수업활동에 주도적으로 참여하고, 토론·질의응답 등을 통해 교과목 이해와 통찰력 향상에 노력
 -과제는 스스로 성실하게 작성하며, 인용한 모든 자료(책·논문·인터넷·AI 등)는 변조나 왜곡 없이 출처를 명확히 표기
 -협동학습의 경우 자신의 역할을 책임감 있게 수행하여 공동의 학습성과 달성에 기여
 -시험의 목적과 의미를 이해하고, 부정행위 없이 정직하게 응시
 -한 학기 수강한 교과목의 교육 품질 향상을 위해 강의평가에 성실히 참여하고, 개선이 필요한 사항을 충실히 서술

∙ [실험실습 안전]
-연구실 안전환경 조성에 관한 법률 제20조(교육·훈련)에 의거, 연구실안전법이 적용되는 과학기술분야 대상학과에 소속된 연구활동종사자는 매학기 일정시간의 안전교육을 이수하여야 하므로 실험·실습을 수강하는 모든 대상학과 학부생 및 대학원생은 교육참여 필수
-신규교육(신입생 2시간), 정기교육(고위험학과 학기별 6시간, 저위험학과 학기별 3시간)
-대상학과: KUPID > 지식관리 > 안전관리지식 > 연구실안전
-포털시스템 상단 메뉴에서 “정보생활” 클린, [안전교육(서울)] 클릭하여 안전교육 페이지 접속(“크롬”으로 접속, 접속 오류 시 인터넷 설정에서 “팝업 차단 해제” 설정 필요)
-포털 아이디가 없는 경우, 국가연구안전관리본부 연구실안전교육시스템(https://edu.labs.go.kr/) 접속하여 수강 가능함. 
-외부기관에서 안전교육을 이수한 경우 별도의 등록절차를 통한 이수 가능
-미이수 시 불이익: 학부생(성적열람 제한), 대학원생(출입제한)

Industrial Organization 
Instructor: Prof. Nahm, Jae
(shnahm@korea.ac.kr ; tel. 3290 2221)
Office hours: By appointment
This course studies industry structures and firm strategic behaviors: how firms behave in different market structures, such as perfectly competitive, oligopoly, and monopoly markets. Using the basic tools of microeconomic theory and game theory, this course explores strategic interactions among firms and how their interactions affect market outcomes. 
The core topics of this course include 

(a) Industry Structure such as vertical and horizontal ones 
(b) Oligopoly Competition such as Bertrand and Cournot competition 
(c) Price Discrimination and pricing strategies 
(d) Complements, value net, and strategy; 
(e) Dynamic Optimization
(h) Merger Evaluation 
Economic analyses are employed in businesses (customer analysis, sales forecasting, financial planning), finance (analysis of factors that influence corporate profits and, therefore, stock prices), and public policy design and evaluation.  Students may, in the future, undertake their own economic analyses, or they would be “consumers,” who make important decisions on based on economics. 
We will provide lecture notes, PPT slides, and we will proceed our course based on these lecture notes (강의노트, 파워포인트 slide 위주로 수업이 진행될 것입니다). Lecture notes and homework assignments will be posted in the course web site. Please check the site regularly for new course materials before coming to lecture.
For Reference Book: Modern Industrial Organization, By Carlton and Perloff or Industrial Organization: Markets and Strategies, By Belleflamme, Paul and Martin Peitz 
Grades: Grades will be based on a weighted average of the following activities: Homework 10%, Midterm Examination 40%, Final Examination 40%, Class Participation 10%. 
Course Outline
1 Introduction to Industrial Organization
Review of Microeconomics 
2 Market Structure I
Perfectly Competitive Market
Monopoly and market power (Marginal this, marginal that)
Coase Conjecture
3 Pricing Policy I: Price Discrimination
Bundling; Two-part Tariff;
4 Pricing Policy II: Versioning/Screening
5 Market Structure II: Oligopoly
	Review of Game Theory
	Cournot, Bertrand Competition
	Collusion 
6 Market Analysis Applications 
Merger Analysis
7 Vertical Industry Structure
Double mark-up 
8 Externalities, incomplete contract and Organization
9 Dynamic Optimization

Office hours: by appointment
Prerequisites: None
Course Description and objectives
“Psychology is the Science of Mental Life, both of its phenomena and their conditions”
(William James, 1890)
심리기초Ⅰ은 인간의 마음과 행동을 과학적으로 이해하는 방법을 배우는 입문 과목입니다. 본 과목은 심리학을 상식이나 직관, 민간신념(folk psychology), 미신적 해석이 아닌 경험적 증거와 논리적 사고에 기반한 학문으로 접근하도록 훈련하는데 목적이 있습니다. 이 과목을 이수한 학생은 다음과 같은 목표를 달성할 수 있어야 합니다. 
생물학적, 인지적, 정신역동적 관점 등 인간 행동에 대한 기본적인 접근 방식을 학습한다. 
비판적 사고와 심리학 이론을 일상생활 및 다양한 사회 현상에 적용한다. 
심리학 및 뇌과학의 기본 용어에 익숙해진다.

Objectives:
This course will help you attain the following goals:
-  The ability to listen to and comprehend lectures in English and the skill to take comprehensible notes.
-  To be able to study from English course materials, such as books and journals.
-  Developing the confidence to converse in English in real life situations.

Professor: Darius Goodwin, MA Applied Linguistics
Email: dariusgoodwin@gmail.com 		Office: Room 709 – IFLS building
Course Delivery Method: This course will be taught on campus.
Required Equipment: A notebook computer or tablet with Wi-Fi for on campus class writing. Please bring it to every class.
Introduction to the Course
	Welcome to Academic English.  In this semester, you will learn valuable language and academic skills that will help you succeed at university, and in your professional careers. Academic English can be challenging, so please ask me if you need help at any time. I enjoy teaching and I want to help you do well. It is important that you feel comfortable in the class, and that you learn useful skills for your future. If you have questions at any time, please let me know. Asking me questions can be an effective way of gaining confidence and practicing your English too.
This syllabus has information about your course. The important information will also be explained clearly in the first week of class, so do not worry. (You can find a detailed schedule for the course on page 5 below. I will explain this later.)
STUDY METHOD
This course will use short lectures, individual tasks, pairwork, group discussion, writing using Google Docs, and presentations.
A key feature of this course is that your learning is supported at every stage.
You can work on some assessed tasks during class time, so you can ask for help to make sure you understand what you have to do. You can also ask questions conveniently at other times using Google Docs comment feature, or by coming to office hours.
You are given clear checklists for assessed tasks, so you understand exactly how you are graded. You are encouraged to ask questions about these checklists to ensure you can do your best.
You can build confidence by practicing writing, presentation and discussion skills in a friendly and comfortable atmosphere.
We will use Google Docs for writing assignments. I will help you make a shared Google folder with me, so I can give you feedback and answer your questions quickly.
II. COURSE OBJECTIVES: 
In Academic English, you will focus on developing academic writing, presentation and discussion skills.
At the end of the course, you will be able to:
write in academic style
organize and express your ideas clearly in paragraphs 
use APA formatting 
include ideas from academic sources using paraphrasing and quotations
write a title page and a reference page in APA
participate in academic discussions with more confidence
organize and give academic presentations with much more confidence

Please note that for academic English courses if a student has more than 3 non-officially excused absences, during the course there is a -1% penalty for each extra day they are absent. 
If you miss more than 8 classes, you automatically fail the course. Please ask me at any time if you are unsure about the rules. I am here to help explain the policies. Attending as many classes as possible makes it easier for you to follow the course and do well.
Lateness: If you arrive more than 3 minutes late, you receive a late mark. Every 3 late marks equals one class absence. You are responsible for telling the teacher at the end of the class if you arrived late. I may not have noticed you joined late. If you do not tell the teacher, you could be marked absent. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the official start of the class, you are marked absent.
Test Days: If you miss an official test day (e.g. Writing 2 - Midterm in-class Writing, Your Presentation, Academic Discussion, Final Quiz), you receive a significant grade penalty unless you can prove officially with documentation signed by a doctor (의사소견서 or 의사진단서, not 진료확인서) that there was a genuine medical emergency requiring urgent hospital treatment. The documentation must show that the medical emergency prevented you from taking the test. If you miss your presentation for any other reason, the highest score you can achieve is 14/20 for the rescheduled assessment. If you miss the discussion, the highest score you can achieve is 12/20. If you miss the final exam, the highest score you can receive is 12/18. If you miss Writing 2 - midterm in class writing, there is an automatic 5-point penalty. However, you should ask me early, and no later than 4 days before the assignment deadline, or you may not receive help in time. Please feel you can talk to me about any problems you have related to the course.  
Preparing & Submitting Assignments: On this course, all assignments must  be written in Google Docs only so I can see the document history. I need to see how you developed your work at every stage. If three or more words are together in your writing or are copied directly from another source this can be plagiarism. Any assignment that has significant (more than 25 words) plagiarism will receive a zero. If you need help with an assignment, please ask me before the deadline. Please do not copy. I will know.
The use of AI and other writing tools should be limited to grammar and style corrections, and not to generate full sentences or paragraphs. Submitting work that is partially or completely generated by AI writing tools will result in a grade of zero for the assignment.

2026년 1학기
교과목 개요
여러분은 소비자행동론 과목을 통해, 첫째, 소비자의 심리와 행동을 이해하고 설명하며 예측할 수 있는 이론과 방법을 학습하고, 둘째, 소비자행동과 관련된 현상으로부터 보편적이고 일반적인 원리와 이론을 도출하는 훈련을 하며, 셋째, 소비자행동과 마케팅전략의 연관성을 파악하고, 마지막으로, 소비자지향적 사고와 관점을 배양합니다.
교재
강의노트: 학교 LMS 강의자료실
이학식, 안광호, 하영원, 석관호, 소비자행동: 마케팅전략적 접근, 제8판, 집현재, 2024. 
출석 및 참여
수업 중 토론참여는 효과적인 학습을 위해 매우 중요한 요소이므로 수업내용의 예복습뿐만 아니라 여러분의 경험을 적극 토론에 반영해 주기 바랍니다.
출석 횟수는 성적 평가에 직접 반영되지 않지만, 총 수업시간의 3분의 1 이상을 결석한 학생에게는 성적을 부여하지 않는 것이 학교 규정입니다.
소비자행동 프로젝트(팀별)
- 이 과제의 목적은 소비자행동 과목에서 공부하는 개념과 이론, 방법을 실제 마케팅 문제에 적용하고 실습하는 데 있습니다. 
분석하고자 하는 기업, 제품, 그리고 브랜드를 선정합니다.
해당 브랜드가 수행하고 있는 마케팅활동을 파악합니다. 모든 마케팅활동을 포함하기보다는 일부 영역에 집중하는 것이 효과적입니다. 
소비자행동 지식을 사용하여 마케팅활동을 분석평가하고, 나아가 개선책을 제안합니다. 필요하면, 설문조사 등 1차 자료수집을 수행할 수 있습니다.
진행상황에 관해 간략한 진도 보고(목차와 계획)가 있을 수 있고, 학기말에 최종발표와 보고서 제출이 있습니다. 최종발표는 25분 이내, 최종보고서는 A4 문서15매 이내(본문 기준, 글자크기 10, 줄간격 1)로 준비합니다. 발표자료와 보고서는 교수에게 종이 인쇄본을 제출하고, PDF 파일을 LMS (프로젝트)에 올립니다.
평가기준은 분석의 정확성과 포괄성, 논리적 전개와 구성, 이해 용이성, 창의성 등과 발표의 매끄러움, 전문성, 주목도 등입니다.
팀별 과제는 ‘팀원 기여도 평가’를 실시해 이를 성적 산정에 반영할 예정입니다.

Course Description and Objectives
Credits: 3
With the proliferation of social media, alternative news sources and generative artificial intelligence, we are now living in a world that is saturated with information.  The ability to critically evaluate that mass of information is more important than ever.  This course will introduce students to some of the fundamental tools of critical thinking.  Depending on available time and student needs, topics to be covered could include identifying, analyzing, and evaluating arguments, clarity in language (definitions, ambiguity, vagueness, etc.), syllogisms, formal and informal fallacies, the role of rhetoric in critical thinking, deduction vs. induction, unstated premises and conclusions, and evaluating premises.  
Materials
A PDF with notes and worksheets will be provided at the beginning of semester.  You will need to have access to this document every class.  You can either print a copy at a local print shop if you prefer to work on paper, or you can access it on your tablet/laptop/notebook.
Other handouts will be provided in class and on the LMS
For in-class evaluations (the midterm exam and in-class article analysis 1 and 2), you must have a writing instrument.  Either pen or pencil is fine.
Grades
Assessment
Attendance
You may miss 2 classes without penalty.  For each subsequent absence you will lose 1% of your attendance grade.  Use this privilege wisely.
If you miss 7 classes for ANY reason (7 excused or unexcused absences) you will receive a grade of ‘F’ for the course.  
Documents for excused absences must be submitted to the university portal system. 
Be punctual.  Show up for class on time.  Three lates will be counted as one absence.  If you are 20 minutes late you will be marked absent.
It is your responsibility to make up for work that you missed during your absences and to find out what homework might have been assigned during the class you missed.  If you miss a class, assume that you missed something important and ask a classmate or me as soon as possible in order to catch up.
Class Rules and Other Comments
Cell Phones:  You are not allowed to use cell phones in class unless you are authorized by me to do so.  Unauthorized use of your cell phone in class will affect your participation score.
English Only:  Speak only English in the classroom.  Consistent failure to communicate in English during the class will also affect your participation score.
Academic Dishonesty and Plagiarism:  Plagiarism is using someone else’s words or ideas as if they were your own.  Assignments that are plagiarized will receive a score of zero.  
Office Hours: I intend to establish some regular office hours after the first week of classes.  In general, the best way to meet me is to make an appointment.

Overview | This course introduces the fundamental principles of electromagnetism and modern physics. Topics include electric fields, Gauss’s law, circuits, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, interference, diffraction, and an introduction to relativity and quantum physics. Emphasis is placed on conceptual understanding, analytical reasoning, and problem-solving through lectures and problem sets.
Who Should Take This Course | This course is designed for undergraduate students pursuing studies in physics, engineering, or other science-related fields.
Prerequisites (Recommended) | It is recommended that students have completed General Physics I.
Objectives 
General | By the end of the course, students will be able to:
Understand and apply the laws of electromagnetism, including Maxwell’s equations.
Analyze electric circuits using Kirchhoff’s laws and Ohm’s law.
Understand relativistic kinematics and basic principles of  quantum mechanics, such as the wave-particle duality.
Solve real-world problems involving electric and magnetic fields, and electromagnetic waves.
Strengthen critical and convergent thinking through interdisciplinary problem solving.

Course Description
This course introduces fundamental concepts of signals and systems, which is used widely in engineering in general. The signals and systems play a foundational role in telecommunication, computer visions, control theory, and robotics, which use various forms of signals (electric signals to electromagnetic waves). In this course, we will learn how to mathematically define signal spaces and systems, especially linear time-invariant systems. Students will learn how to use the Fourier transformation in continuous and discrete domains as well as periodic and non-periodic signals. 
Learning Resources, Technology & Texts
Main textbook (not required): Oppenheim, Alan V., and A. S. Willsky. Signals and Systems. Prentice Hall, 2nd edition. ISBN: 9781292025902.

Learning Outcomes
A student who successfully fulfills the course requirements will have demonstrated: 
An understanding of signal space.  
Knowledge of constructing a mathematical model of systems 
An ability to analyze system response for Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems using the frequency and time-domain representations. 
Knowledge of designing the filter to modulate the system outputs. 
These outcomes will be measured via assessments including homework assignments, exams, and 
projects.

COURSE NOTES
There is no set Textbook; all required materials will be provided by me. 
The course is designed to introduce you to the classroom and academic standards of an international, native speaking University English program. I will not, however, be grading you on such a standard. This difference will be made clear, especially with regard to the requirements for gradable elements. 
We will be reviewing your Midterm Assignments during Midterm week, and on a Friday before or after. This is a required part of the course. We will schedule these reviews in class. 
Some classes will need to be extended to 60/70 minutes to make up for classes lost to National Holidays/University Festivals, etc, as per University guidelines. 
All Classwork will be solo projects individually graded, with the exception of the Group Discussion Exam, which will be a Team Project individually graded.
Every student will be allowed two free absences during the semester, in large part to allow for isolations concerning Covid infections. Other mandated exceptions (e.g. Military Service Physicals) will be added to these two accepted absences. You must, however, strive to be on time. Any student who arrives more than 5 minutes late could potentially be listed as a late. 2 lates will equal an absence. Similarly, any student who arrives more than 20 mins late could be listed as “absent.” 
There are some adult protocols that I will require in class. For example, you cannot sleep, or eat, or do homework for other courses in class. Also, while you may use electronic devices to review material, you cannot use them for gameplay. We will make this clear in our early classes. 
Office hours are set for Monday and Wednesday, at 6pm, in IFLS Rm 728.

COURSE DESCRIPTION AND OBJECTIVES:
This course aims to develop students’ academic English proficiency and communicative competence required for university-level study. The course is conducted using academic content to strengthen students’ overall English ability applicable across a range of academic disciplines. Emphasis is placed on practical communication skills through a variety of task-based and interactive activities designed to help students use English effectively in academic and real-life contexts.
Students will also engage with a variety of academic texts to improve reading comprehension skills and to develop an understanding of English expressions related to their fields of study.
We will achieve these goals through a combination of practical activities, in-class assignments, and mini-lectures. This is a list of the core activities and skills we will focus on:
Discussion skills for academic purposes.
Research skills necessary for academic writing and discussion. 
Developing ideas for writing and discussion through conversation, discussion, brainstorming and freewriting.
Learning how to write a basic academic essay with citations, and how to avoid plagiarism.
Expanding upon your current level of academic vocabulary. 
Developing your public speaking skills/presentation skills.

ACTIVE PARTICIPATION is:

Examples of active participation include:
Volunteering to answer questions
Asking questions by raising your hand

Following classroom rules
REGULAR ATTENDANCE is required.
Please note that while you may miss up to 3 classes without penalty, missing 10 or more classes will result in an automatic failing grade, regardless of performance in other areas.
The semester consists of 16 weeks, and we must meet for a minimum of 15 weeks—this means we will meet 30 times in total.
Midterm and final exams (or exam-related assignments/quizzes) each count as one class session.
We are required to make up any missed classes to ensure we reach the 30 required meetings. This includes cancellations due to public holidays, teacher illness, or other disruptions.
My absence/lateness policy (5% of your overall grade): 
You are allowed 3 absences for any reason without penalty. Starting with the 4th absence, you will begin to lose attendance points. If you have a valid reason (see examples below), you must contact me and make arrangements to recover your lost points. 
Regardless of the reason, you are responsible for finding out what homework, quizzes, tests, announcements, or in-class work you missed—and you must complete the missed work. I understand that special situations may arise, but even in those cases, you are still responsible for making up missed work. Please talk to me or a classmate to find out what you missed. Important information—like deadline changes, handouts, or quiz details—is often given in class.
Being absent is not an excuse for turning in homework late or being unprepared for future classes. If you experience an emergency, I will be understanding—but you must speak with me personally to discuss the situation.
Officially excused absences (e.g., military check-ups, a family member’s funeral, etc.) must be supported by official documentation or must be registered online if required. Please make every effort to notify me in advance. If that's not possible, let me know as soon as you can afterward.

CLASSROOM MATERIALS
You will need access to Microsoft Word for the writing portion of our class. I do not accept HWP documents. There is no single book which can meet the needs of students whose English language levels and learning styles vary considerably. For this reason, we will use a combination of materials and handouts which I will upload to the LMS as needed.
CLASSROOM RULES AND FINAL COMMENTS
Important: a major goal of this class is to help you become a competent, independent learner. After completing this course, you should be able to continue developing your English through self-study and independent learning.
Participation: Often you will be expected to work in pairs or in small groups. Participation includes arriving on time, being prepared (bringing your book, notebook, handouts, and other required materials), listening attentively, interacting with your classmates and teacher, actively engaging in class activities, completing assignments thoroughly and on time, and asking questions when you don’t understand.
Speaking Korean: In most cases, speaking Korean in class is unnecessary. You will lose participation points if you speak Korean without permission. That said, I do allow Korean when helping classmates understand rules, grammar points, or my instructions—but you must ask for permission first.
Plagiarism: Plagiarism means presenting someone else’s ideas or work as your own. It is dishonest, unethical, and—even when unintentional—can negatively affect your grade. Accidental plagiarism is more understandable than intentional plagiarism, but both are serious. Most importantly, plagiarism prevents you from learning and growing as a student. We will discuss how to recognize and avoid plagiarism in this class.
AI (Artificial Intelligence): AI is a powerful tool and has many benefits, and we will occasionally use it as a learning tool in class. I allow the use of AI for some classroom activities, for research and preparation at home, and for any way that you feel it can be helpful in your English learning. However, you are not allowed to use AI programs during exams or quizzes—doing so is considered a form of academic dishonesty.

Your health, both mentally and physically, is extremely important. There are counseling services offered at Korea University free of charge, but few students take advantage of these services due to unnecessary fears. There’s a common misconception that people who seek counseling are “crazy.” In reality, most people who seek help are regular individuals dealing with common challenges, such as:
Stress

Anger management

Grief

The Counseling Center is a safe and confidential space where you can work through your problems. Unlike talking to a friend, a counselor is professionally trained to support your personal growth and help you deal with life's challenges. They can help you understand your situation more clearly and guide you toward solutions—so you can eventually manage things more confidently on your own. You are free to say whatever you want in counseling, without fear of judgment. You will never be pressured to talk about anything you're not ready to discuss. Reliable research shows that 70–90% of people who attend counseling feel better afterward. Don’t hesitate to seek support—you’re not alone, and help is available.

This syllabus has information about your course. The important information will also be explained clearly in the first week of class. (You can find a schedule for the course on page 5 below.)
STUDY METHOD
This course will use short lectures, individual tasks, pairwork, group discussion, writing in class using Google Docs, and presentations.
A key feature of this course is that your learning is supported at every stage.
You are given time to work on some assessed tasks during class, when you can ask for clarification to ensure you are on track. You can also ask questions conveniently at other times using Google Docs comment feature, or by coming to office hours.
You are given clear checklists for assessed tasks, so you understand exactly how you are graded. You are encouraged to ask questions about these checklists to ensure you can do your best.
A positive class atmosphere with support from your classmates ensures you enjoy learning, feel comfortable and can fulfill your academic potential. 
I will help you make a shared Google folder with me, so I can give you feedback and answer your questions quickly.
II. COURSE OBJECTIVES: 
In Academic English, you will focus on developing academic writing, presentation and discussion skills.
At the end of the course, you will be able to:
write a 4-paragraph research essay in APA style
identify credible academic sources
use AI ethically to help you produce assignments
lead discussions about academic topics related to your interests
give an engaging short academic presentation 
use Google Docs, Google Forms, & Folders to collaborate  
III.COURSE REQUIREMENTS & GRADING CONSIDERATIONS:
Grade equivalents:
A+        	95-100                 A           90-94                   B+        85-89 		B   80-84
C+        	75-79                   C           70-74                   D+        65-69    		D   60-64   	
F           	0-59
Note: Nobody needs to fail Academic English. With your hard and focused work, successful learning is guaranteed.  
Attendance Policy
Students are permitted a maximum of 3 absences in total each semester without grade penalty (or a maximum of 4 if they are all officially excused absences. Documentation for officially excused absences only must be submitted via the K.U. portal.)
Officially Excused Absences 
death in the family (government issued death certificate)
hospitalization (hospital document giving dates of hospitalization)
military service (send photo of document from military)
school trips with a letter from the faculty dean, or by tradition a document from the student council
menstrual pain (notification via portal)
covid diagnosis (notification via portal)
Please note that for academic English courses if a student has more than 3 non-officially excused absences, during the course there is a -1% penalty for each extra day they are absent. 
If you miss more than 8 classes, you automatically fail the course. Please ask me at any time if you are unsure about the rules. I am here to help explain the policies. Attending as many classes as possible makes it easier for you to follow the course and do well.
Lateness: If you arrive more than 3 minutes late, you receive a late mark. Every 3 late marks equals one class absence. You are responsible for telling the teacher at the end of the class if you arrived late. I may not have noticed you joined late. If you do not tell the teacher, you could be marked absent. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the official start of the class, you are marked absent.
Test Days: If you miss an official test day (e.g. Writing 2 - Midterm in-class Writing, Your Presentation, Final Quiz), you receive a significant grade penalty unless you can prove officially with documentation signed by a doctor (의사소견서 or 의사진단서, not 진료확인서) that there was a genuine medical emergency requiring urgent hospital treatment. The documentation must show that the medical emergency prevented you from taking the test. If you miss your presentation for any other reason, the highest score you can achieve is 20/30 for the rescheduled assessment. If you miss the final exam, the highest score you can receive is 7/13. If you miss Writing 2 - midterm in class writing, there is an automatic 5-point penalty. It is extremely important for your grade that you attend these test days. Please set multiple alarms, so that it is impossible to miss a test day. These rules need to be strict to ensure fairness. There can be 150 students, and it is logistically very difficult to reschedule tests.
Other Late or Missing Assignments: If you fail to complete an assignment by the specified deadline, the penalty to your total grade for the course is 0.5%. if submitted within the next 24 hours, 1% within 48 hours, 1.5% within 72 hours, 2% within 96 hours etc. until the points for that task reach 0. However, if you completed the task before the deadline, but forgot to move the file to your folder, move the file, and email me and there is no late penalty. 
Missing Presentation Slide Deadline: Students must submit their presentation slides (Google Slides only) by 9pm the night before their presentation or receive a 4-point penalty. This is necessary so slides can be graded before your presentation day.
Asking for Help: If you have any difficulty understanding a task, it is very important to ask me for help as soon as possible. You can ask during class, or use Google Doc comment feature, or by email. I can also arrange to help you on Zoom. However, you should ask me early, and no later than 4 days before the assignment deadline, or you may not receive help in time. Please feel you can talk to me about any problems you have related to the course. 
Preparing & Submitting Assignments: On this course, all assignments must  be written in Google Docs only so I can see the document history. I need to see how you developed your work at every stage. This helps to prove that it is your work and not AI. Failure to write assignments in Google docs will result in grade penalties. Students must submit assignments by moving the Google Doc to the shared folder. If you can see the file in the shared folder, you have successfully submitted your work. Google Docs keeps a record of when the file was completed or changed. This helps you show it is your work.
Grade Questions: Questions about scores received for assignments must be asked within 7 days of receiving the score. Please do not ask professors to give you a higher grade as there are strict university rules against this. However, if you think there may have been a miscalculation or you need further explanation to understand the score, please contact me immediately. I am very happy to meet you during my office hours if you need further explanation, or have questions about your score.
Professionalism: Bringing a notebook computer/tablet, always producing outstanding work, speaking in English as much as possible, encouraging others to speak in English, being enthusiastic and focused on learning, asking questions and frequently contributing ideas, no inappropriate use of cell phone, trying to use the language and skills we have studied, etc. 
Webcams: If we need to move online temporarily (very unlikely), all students will need a webcam with a working microphone. 
Participation: If a student is not participating in activities or is disruptive, it can reduce their grade. As this is a language class, participation and collaboration with students and the professor is especially important to achieve the course's learning goals successfully. If there is a problem, the student will receive an email warning first. If the problem reoccurs, a penalty of 2% will be applied for each incident. However, this is extremely rare in my experience, and has never happened at K.U. on any of my courses.
Cell phones: Generally, phones should be turned off. However, phones may be used for dictionary work and research. Naturally, Kakao and other social media should not be used during class as they can interfere with concentration and learning.
IV. OFFICE HOURS:
I have office hours every week. These will be announced in the first few days. These are great opportunities to ask me for help. I am also available at some other times if the office hours are not suitable. Please make an appointment by email. When you email me, can you always include your name, student number and class code. I look forward to seeing you either in my office (Room 709), or we can easily meet on Zoom.
V. PLAGIARISM: 
Copying some words/phrases or sentences from another person and claiming it as your own writing is not allowed.  Please do not copy. You should summarize and paraphrase others’ ideas and include a citation. I will teach you these important skills on the course. If three or more words are together in your writing or are copied directly from another source this can be plagiarism. Any assignment that has significant (more than 25 words) plagiarism will receive a zero. If you need help with an assignment, please ask me before the deadline. Please do not copy. I will know.
The use of AI and other writing tools should be limited to grammar and style corrections, and not to generate full sentences or paragraphs. Submitting work that is partially or completely generated by AI writing tools will result in a grade of zero for the assignment.
(It is important to note that AI writing tools cannot substitute for originality and critical analysis required for academic work.) As students write in Google Doc, I can review the file history to check that the assignment has been developed by you over time, and has not been copied and pasted from another source or A.I. This is why students must write their assignments in Google Docs. 
If AI is permitted to be used by the teacher for a specific class activity, they will inform you explicitly. Students should be careful to follow the instructions for AI use carefully. Please ask the teacher if you are unsure and feel free to discuss any concerns regarding the use of AI during office hours or email. 
VI. ANNOUNCEMENTS & ADDITIONAL COURSE INFORMATION
Please make sure you have your correct email address on the university system. During the semester and before the grades are finalized, there will be announcements. It is also important to keep checking your email, especially after the final assessments in case I need to contact you about your work. Also, after the final grades are announced, please contact me immediately if you think there may be an error with your score. There is a short period when this is possible, but after this period has finished it is not possible to make changes to scores.

Class Times:		Tu/Th, 10:30 – 11:45pm

Office hours: 		By appointment
E-mail:				sjcooper@korea.ac.kr
Text and Materials
Longman Academic Writing Series 4 – Essays (required text)
Supplemental handouts may also be provided on the LMS or in class.
Class Description 
This class is designed to improve students’ reading and writing abilities. Class time will be focused on discussing reading and writing skills, on reading and writing, as well as on critical thinking exercises.
This Course is for high-intermediate to advanced students, and is designed to enhance their basic reading and writing skills. The focus is on more advanced skills, such as making inferences, separating facts from opinions, as well as identifying bias, and extending these sophisticated reading skills to writing skills.
https://eled.korea.edu/eled_en/info/u_syllabus.do
Lessons will consist of a variety of activities including discussions, pair work, critical thinking exercises, writing practice, as well as peer review.  
Aims
Develop mastery and confidence when reading and writing in English
Improve ability to understand more nuanced meanings within a text
Use grammatically correct sentences when writing
Produce a well-organized and coherent 5 paragraph essay
Enjoy reading in English for study as well as for pleasure
Instructor’s expectations of students
Arrive on time and be prepared for class
Participate actively in every class and in all activities 
Be respectful of your classmates and the instructor 
Challenge one’s self whenever possible 
Ask questions when necessary 
Participation - Attendance Policy
Students arriving 5 or more minutes after the start of class will be marked ‘late.’ Students missing more than 15 minutes of a class will be marked ‘absent.’ Because the goal of this class is to improve reading and writing through discussion, critical thinking, and sharing ideas attendance and active participation are essential. As a result, student grades depend on attendance and any unexcused absences and lateness will count against a student’s participation grade.  
Participation
I am aware that studying reading and writing in English can bring unique challenges, however I strongly believe that the more effort we put in to our classes then the better the results will be. To this end I require all students to actively participate in each class, and each activity, and to push themselves at all times. This will not only help us to work well together in class, but it also allows students to take responsibility for their own learning.
Evaluation
	Participation – 30%
Homework/reading – 20% 
Assignments – 20%
Midterm – 10%
Final – 20 %
Assignment 1: Paragraph Writing and Peer Review: You will choose from several topics and prepare a 10 to 15 sentence paragraph, using the writing model from the textbook and following the steps in the writing process. Part of your assignment will also be to peer review your classmate’s writing, as this is an extremely useful skill to develop and a great way to practice recognising good writing.
Homework and reading: Homework given in class will mainly be reading, but also occasionally the editing and uploading of a final draft of a piece of written work from class. It is very important that all homework is completed on time, as without undertaking the reading you will not be able to participate actively in class discussions.
Midterm: Writing Assignment: You will write a summary of one chapter chosen from one of the required texts read in class. Summarising is an important skill that combines reading and writing skills. 
Assignment 2: Create an Outline for your final essay: A formal outline and essay plan will be created and submitted for review. This outline will form the basis for your final five paragraph essays, so it is an important chance to practice planning and preparing before you write. 
Final: Five Paragraph Essay: You will write an argumentative five-paragraph essay, incorporating what you have learned in class, and using the outline and plan created in the second assignment.
This syllabus is subject to change by the instructor to fit the needs of the students and/or achieve specific educational goals.

Course information
Course title: Korean Cultural Diplomacy
Course code: GKSS403-00
Course instructor: Minjae Zoh

Course Objectives
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Develop a critical and multidimensional understanding of South Korea’s cultural diplomacy within its global and historical contexts.
Analyze the use of culture, heritage, and media in constructing national identity and promoting soft power.
Evaluate the politics of representation, omission, and strategic narrative in South Korea’s international cultural outreach.
Strengthen practical academic skills in research, critical writing, oral presentation, and cross-cultural analysis through workshops and applied assignments.
Course Outline
Week 1: Introduction to <Korean Cultural Diplomacy>
Week 2: The background and formation of the United Nations
Week 3: The UNESCO Organization and its World Heritage Convention
Week 4: A discussion of the World Heritage Convention’s ‘Outstanding Universal Value’
Week 5: Museums as a place/space for cultural diplomacy
Week 6: South Korea’s conceptualization of national heritage and national culture
Week 7: Special Training: Academic Writing and Academic Presentations 
Week 8: Mid-term
Week 9: South Korea’s National Treasure and World Heritage
Week 10: South Korean Identity and Image (Activity and Presentations)
Week 11: The Popular and Influential Portrayal of South Korea via the Media
Week 12: The politically sensitive parts of South Korea’s heritage industry
Week 13: The (inter)national promotion of Hangul and Hangukmal
Week 14: Globalizing Korean Studies
Week 15: Round-up and Revision
Week 16: Final Exam
Assessment Methods
Student performance will be evaluated based on the following components:
Midterm Exam: 35%
Final Exam: 35%
Presentation: 20%
Participation: 10%
This assessment structure is designed to balance individual academic performance with collaborative learning and critical engagement throughout the semester.
Teaching Methods
This course will be conducted primarily through lectures, followed by class discussions and group projects. Students are encouraged to actively participate, share perspectives, and collaboratively develop ideas throughout the semester.

COURSE DESCRIPTION AND OBJECTIVES:
This course aims to develop students’ academic English proficiency and communicative competence required for university-level study. The course is conducted using academic content to strengthen students’ overall English ability applicable across a range of academic disciplines. Emphasis is placed on practical communication skills through a variety of task-based and interactive activities designed to help students use English effectively in academic and real-life contexts.
Students will also engage with a variety of academic texts to improve reading comprehension skills and to develop an understanding of English expressions related to their fields of study.
We will achieve these goals through a combination of practical activities, in-class assignments, and mini-lectures. The following are the core activities and skills we will focus on:
Discussion skills for academic purposes.
Research skills necessary for academic writing and discussion. 
Developing ideas for writing through discussion, brainstorming and freewriting.
Learning how to write a basic academic essay with citations, and how to avoid plagiarism.
Expanding your level of academic vocabulary. 
Developing your public speaking skills/presentation skills.
ASSESSMENT: 
Your final grade will be based upon a combination of the following: 
The standard scale for grading is as follows:
ACTIVE PARTICIPATION is:
Willingly taking part in all class activities
Showing interest and motivation to share your ideas, thoughts, feelings, and questions
Completing classwork on time
Examples of active participation include:
Volunteering to answer questions
Asking questions by raising your hand
Speaking actively in group work
Staying awake and attentive during class
Following classroom rules
REGULAR ATTENDANCE is required.
Please note that while you may miss up to 3 classes without penalty, missing 10 or more classes will result in an automatic failing grade for the course.
The semester consists of 16 weeks, and we must meet for a minimum of 15 weeks (30 class sessions in total).
Midterm and final exams (or exam-related assignments/quizzes) each count as one class session.
We are required to make up any missed classes to ensure we reach the 30 required meetings. This includes cancellations due to public holidays, teacher illness, or other disruptions.
My absence/lateness policy (5% of your overall grade): 
You are allowed 3 absences for any reason without penalty. Starting with the 4th absence, you will begin to lose attendance points. If you have a valid reason (see examples below), you must contact me and make arrangements to recover lost points. 
Regardless of the reason, you are responsible for finding out what homework, quizzes, tests, announcements, or in-class work you missed—and you must complete the missed work. I understand that special situations may arise. Even in special situations, you are still responsible for making up missed work. Please talk to me or a classmate to find out what you missed. Important information—like deadline changes, handouts, or quiz details—is often given in class.
Being absent is not an excuse for turning in homework late or being unprepared for future classes. If you experience an emergency, I will be understanding—but you must speak with me personally to discuss the situation.
Officially excused absences (e.g., military check-ups, a family member’s funeral, etc.) must be supported by official documentation or must be registered online if required. Please make every effort to notify me in advance whenever possible.
You are considered late to class if you are more than 5 minutes late. You can be late to class 3 times without penalty. The fourth time you are late will count for a loss of attendance points equivalent to one absence. 
ELECTRONIC EMAIL 
Always include the following information in the subject line of your email: 
Your full name, Your student ID number, Our class name (number)
When sending assignments or documents, always use Microsoft Word (.doc or .docx) — do not use HWP (Hangul Word Processor). Most foreign professors (including me) prefer and appreciate Microsoft Word files because they are more accessible and compatible.
My email address is: laramanuel@hotmail.com (do not write lala by accident)
CLASSROOM MATERIALS
You will need access to Microsoft Word for the writing portion of our class. I do not accept HWP documents. There is no single book that can meet the needs of students whose English language levels and learning styles vary considerably. For this reason, we will use a combination of materials and handouts which I will upload to the LMS as needed.
CLASSROOM RULES AND FINAL COMMENTS
Important: a major goal of this class is to help you become a competent, independent learner. After completing this course, you should be able to continue developing your English through self-study and independent learning.
Participation: Often you will be expected to work in pairs or in small groups. Participation includes arriving on time, being prepared (bringing your book, notebook, handouts, and other required materials), listening attentively, interacting with your classmates and teacher, actively engaging in class activities, completing assignments thoroughly and on time, and asking questions when you don’t understand.
Speaking Korean: In most cases, speaking Korean in class is unnecessary. You will lose participation points if you speak Korean without permission. That said, I do allow Korean when helping classmates understand rules, grammar points, or my instructions—but you must ask for permission first.
Plagiarism: Plagiarism means presenting someone else’s ideas or work as your own. It is dishonest, unethical, and—even when unintentional—can negatively affect your grade. Accidental plagiarism is more understandable than intentional plagiarism, but both are serious. Most importantly, plagiarism prevents you from learning and growing as a student. We will discuss how to recognize and avoid plagiarism in this class.
AI (Artificial Intelligence): AI is a powerful tool and has many benefits, and we will occasionally use it as a learning tool in class. I allow the use of AI for some classroom activities, for research and preparation at home, and in any way that you feel it can be helpful in your English learning. However, you are not allowed to use AI programs during exams or quizzes.  
Important Note: 
Sometimes the pressures of university life and/or personal matters can cause students to become distressed, which can have a negative impact upon their health. Your health, both mental and physical, is extremely important. There are counseling services offered at Korea University free of charge, but few students take advantage of these services due to unnecessary fears. There is a common misconception that people who seek counseling are “crazy.” In reality, most people who seek help are regular individuals dealing with common challenges, such as:
Stress
Self-esteem issues
Relationship problems (with partners, friends, or family)
Anger management
Bullying
Anxiety
Grief
Addictions (to TV, smartphones, gaming, eating, exercise, etc.)
Alcohol-related issues
Loneliness
Depression
Fears
ADHD
Emotional instability
The Counseling Center is a safe and confidential space where you can work through your problems. Unlike talking to a friend, a counselor is professionally trained to support your personal growth and help you deal with life's challenges. They can help you understand your situation more clearly and guide you toward solutions—so you can eventually manage things more confidently on your own. You are free to say whatever you want in counseling, without fear of judgment. You will never be pressured to talk about anything you're not ready to discuss. Research shows that 70–90% of people who attend counseling report feeling better afterward. Don’t hesitate to seek support—you’re not alone, and help is available.
